articleTitle: Tackling the Challenge of Small Sample Size: Effective Training by Integrating SNN and GNN
abstract: This complexity makes it more difficult to extract effective information and rules from small sample data. This article designs a method to address the challenge of small samples by integrating the advantages of SNN pulse neural network and GNN graph neural network. Using the time coding and threshold activation of SNN, it improves the excessive smoothing problem that exists in deep GNN. At the same time, it utilizes the advantages of GNN in image analysis to effectively capture and utilize complex relationships in structured data, and processes small sample graph structure data more effectively. Ultimately, it achieves the goal of effectively improving the difficulties of model training and generalization caused by small sample problems.

articleTitle: Disturbance Observer-Based Prescribed-Time Control for Flexible Rope Systems
abstract: This article addresses an issue of prescribed-time control (PTC) for flexible rope systems with disturbances. Initially, we introduce the prescribed-time disturbance observer (PTDO) to evaluate external perturbations, achieving zero error estimation within a specified time. Subsequently, utilizing the PTDO and the idea of feedback linearization, a PTC method is formulated to ensure that the elastic deformation velocity of systems converges to the origin within a specified time. It is proved by Lyapunov theory that the designed scheme not only guarantees the disturbances estimation and velocity stabilization within the specified time, but also presets the stabilization time through parameters assignment. Eventually, a numerical simulation is employed to demonstrate the feasibility and efficiency of the presented algorithm.

articleTitle: A Traffic Signal Control Method Based on Improved Deep Reinforcement Learning*
abstract: In order to solve the problem that the existing traffic signal control methods usually need to predefine the phase sequence or phase duration, a single intersection traffic signal control method based on improved deep reinforcement learning Double DQN (DDQN) was proposed. Firstly, a traffic signal control model based on deep reinforcement learning DDQN was constructed to optimize the estimated value of action-value function and the iterative process of target value. Secondly, the original one-dimensional action space was discretized into a three-dimensional action space composed of phase selection, phase duration and loss factor, and the next phase and phase green time to be executed were intelligently decided. Finally, a new loss function is designed based on the loss factor, which can dynamically adjust the loss weight of different actions according to the difference of importance. The simulation test is carried out based on the microscopic simulation platform SUMO. The experimental results show that, compared with the baseline method, the proposed method reduces the average waiting time by 28.1%, the average queue length by 29.7%, and the average number of parking vehicles by 18.8%.

articleTitle: A-MSCKF: An Improved MSCKF Algorithm Based on Adaptive Threshold Feature Points
abstract: When implementing robot localization using the traditional Multi-State Constraint Kalman Filter (MSCKF) algorithm, the frontend relies on optical flow methods to track feature points. However, this approach results in low-precision feature point matching and lacks robustness to changes in environmental lighting conditions. Considering the complex lighting variations in different environments during localization and tracking, this paper proposes the A-MSCKF algorithm. The frontend of this algorithm employs an adaptive threshold ORB (Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF) feature point extraction method, and the backend of the MSCKF algorithm is optimized. Experimental results show that the proposed improved method exhibits better stability and lower tracking errors compared to traditional approaches in trajectory tracking comparisons.

articleTitle: A Model Predictive Control Approach With Limited-Time Termination for Virtually Coupled Train Set
abstract: To improve the flexibility and efficiency of railway services, virtual coupling has been investigated widely. It forms multiple train units as a virtually coupled train set (VCTS), deploying advanced communication and control technologies instead of physical couplers. To operate VCTS as desired, all units should drive synchronously, while satisfying a safety constraint to regulate the following distance. Thus, model pre-dictive control approaches are a promising solution to achieve VCTS operation. However, the computation efficiency of MPC is a critical problem to be addressed, considering the limited capabilities of realistic on-board train computers. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a fast-safe MPC approach that can terminate in a limited time while generating a quasi-optimal and feasible controller. By adding barrier functions that are specifically transferred from constraints in VCTS operation, we formulate an augmented cost function for MPC. Then, a fast-safe solver is designed to analytically solve the optimal control problem in MPC, using the gradient of augmented cost function and adaptive updating steps. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach can yield controllers for VCTS in a limited time, while operating VCTS stably and guaranteeing constraint satisfaction.

articleTitle: Load Frequency Control of Multi-Area Power Systems based on Event-Triggered Control
abstract: This paper addresses load frequency control in multi-area power systems under Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks. It proposes an event-triggered control (ETC) strategy to reduce communication overhead and control costs. Sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>œ performance are derived. Specifically, a novel time-varying Lyapunov function (TVLF) is introduced, which requires less information about DoS duration, helping to alleviate the conservatism in stability analysis. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through a numerical case study involving a three-area power system.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Surrogate Model for Automobile Wheel Strength and Stiffness Based on Deep Learning
abstract: Structural strength and stiffness are critical factors in the design of automotive wheel spokes. In the context of conceptual design innovation, developing data-driven surrogate models for performance simulation is essential to meet requirements of rapid iterations. To address the issue of low accuracy caused by poorly distributed design samples, this paper proposes a method that combines the generation of high-quality samples with a deep regression model for surrogate modelling. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms its alternatives in terms of accuracy and efficiency, effectively providing support for innovative wheel spoke design.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Sliding Mode Control of QUAV Attitude System Based on Disturbance Observer
abstract: In this paper, the fixed-time stability of the attitude system of a quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle (QUAV) under external time-varying disturbance is investigated. A novel disturbance observer with state dependent variables as exponents is designed to estimate time-varying perturbations. Subsequently, a fixed - time controller is engineered to achieve fixed-time convergence of the QUAV's attitude system. The efficacy of the proposed algorithm is validated through numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Target-Reaching Control with Obstacle Avoidance Based Future Perception SAC for Unmanned Bicycle
abstract: A novel approach to control the balance and obstacle avoidance of unmanned bicycles using Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm enhanced with future state predictions is proposed in this paper. For reinforcement learning control of unmanned bicycles, inherent delayed reward poses a significant challenge. To address this issue, we introduce a Transformer-based time series prediction model combined with an autoencoder for dimensionality reduction. This prediction module provides the SAC algorithm with foresight into future states, improving decision-making capabilities. The proposed Future Perception-SAC (FP-SAC) framework integrates the state prediction module with the SAC algorithm, enhancing both sample efficiency and policy stability. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the FP-SAC algorithm outperforms the traditional SAC in terms of reward accumulation and balance maintenance and it can significantly improve the control performance of complex dynamic systems.

articleTitle: The Multi-UAV Path Planning for the Power Transmission Line Inspection
abstract: The power transmission line inspection is a key part of power system maintenance, and the safety and reliability of the power grid are closely related to the operation of transmission lines. To better plan the paths of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in large-scale inspection tasks, a novel two-stage algorithm is proposed in this work. Firstly, an improved K-means++ algorithm is proposed to assign the inspection tasks for multi-UAV. It considers the influence of the UAVs starting positions and improves the calculation of clustering centers. Then, the Q-learning based particle swarm optimization (QLPSO) algorithm is proposed to plan the inspection path for each UAV. It enhances the exploration of the particles by introducing the Q-leaning algorithm and the history information of the particles. Finally, the algorithm is tested on different-scaled inspection tasks. The results prove the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in multi-UAV power transmission line inspection tasks.

articleTitle: Research on Detection Method of Moldy Tobacco Leaf Raw Materials Based on Hyperspectral and Deep Learning
abstract: In this scholarly pursuit, hyperspectral imaging(HSI) technology was synergistically integrated with advanced deep learning techniques to detect mold contamination in tobacco leaves. The study involved the compilation of a comprehensive dataset of hyperspectral images, which included both mold-infested and healthy tobacco leaves. The spectral data underwent a rigorous preprocessing regime, commencing with Multivariate Scatter Correction (MSC) to mitigate the effects of scattering and followed by Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to isolate the most salient feature bands, culminating in the extraction of representative mean spectral profiles. Subsequently, an array of classification models was meticulously developed, including 1D convolutional neural networks (1DCNN), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM) algorithms. The empirical results conclusively demonstrated the 1DCNN model's superiority in classifying mold-related hyperspectral data, achieving a remarkable training accuracy of 100% and an exemplary testing accuracy of 99.75%. This performance not only surpassed that of traditional machine learning models but also showcased the 1DCNN model's heightened classification accuracy and robust generalization capabilities. These findings herald the potential for deep learning to revolutionize the analysis of complex hyperspectral data, offering innovative solutions to challenges that were previously insurmountable.

articleTitle: Differentially Private Consensus Under Quantized Communication with Dynamic Event-Triggered Mechanism
abstract: This study delves into the differentially private consensus problem in multi-agent systems (MASs), leveraging a dynamic event-triggered (DET) mechanism to ensure privacy-preserving consensus under a quantized communication setting. We develop a consensus algorithm for differential privacy communication that employs a uniform quantizer. This approach safeguards the agent's initial or present state against information leaks by relaying quantized data. To reduce the frequency of controller updates, a DET protocol, which is based on an auxiliary variable and local estimations, is implemented to control the data transmission. Subsequently, necessary criteria are established to guarantee mean square consensus performance when an unbounded quantizer is used. In conclusion, simulation examples are included to validate the results obtained.

articleTitle: SE-TDM: Squeeze-Excitation and Time Differencing Model for Precise Gesture Recognition through Spatio-Temporal Fusion of sEMG and IMU Signals
abstract: The integration of sEMG and IMU signals enables accurate gesture recognition, with broad applicability in manipulating prosthetics and human-machine interaction. However, previous fusion methods have predominantly focused on spatial information, often overlooking the crucial temporal information, resulting in inability to adequately portray gestures. This study introduces a novel deep learning method that uses spatio-temporal fusion neural network integrating both sEMG and IMU signals for gesture recognition. In the proposed method, two networks were utilized for the spatial and temporal fusion of sEMG and IMU signals, respectively. The spatial fusion network utilizes the attention mechanisms within the Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) module to assign varying weights to information. Meanwhile, the temporal fusion network leverages the signal differences across frames, enhancing both short-term and long-term variations to capture the signal temporal information. In order to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed model, an EMG armband was applied on the wrists of eight subjects to acquire the sEMG and IMU signals. The gesture recognition results indicated that the proposed method achieved a higher gesture recognition accuracy of 93.16±3.08<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, significantly outperformed four state-of-the-art methods (p < 0.05 revealed by ANOVA). This study contributes to offering innovative solutions to MPR in practical applications.

articleTitle: Adaptive Spike-Based Kalman Filter for Neural Decoding in Brain-Machine Interface
abstract: Brain-Machine Interface (BMI) assists paralyzed patients in restoring motor functions by controlling neuropros-thetic devices through intentions captured from brain activities. However, traditional spike-based neural signal decoding algorithms typically employ spike counting to estimate firing rates and rely on static functional relationships between neural activi-ties and movements, overlooking the facts that all information in a spike sequence is contained within the spike intervals and neural tuning dynamically varies over time. To address these challenges, this study introduces a novel decoding algorithm that combines spike-based Kalman filter and sequential Monte Carlo point process methods. The algorithm directly utilizes spike signals as observations through spike-based Kalman filter, effectively reducing the loss of information caused by traditional statistical methods in neural information processing. The sequential Monte Carlo point process method dynamically updates the parameters to accommodate the changes of tuning function caused by neural degradation. In simulation experiments, our algorithm demonstrates superior performance compared to the traditional spike-based filters, especially under conditions involving dynamic changes in neural tuning, thus providing a robust solution for long-term reliable BMI applications.

articleTitle: Pre-Trained Language Model - Based Real-Time Formation Lithology Identification Method for Drilling Process
abstract: Geological exploration is essential for economic and social progress, with lithology identification being a key technology that improves exploration precision and resource development efficiency. This paper presents a real-time identification method of formation lithology in drilling process based on pre-training language model, which is divided into three stages. In this first stage, the drilling data undergoes rigorous cleaning, feature selection, and normalization to eliminate noise and anomalies. In the second stage, key model inputs such as weight on bit (WOB), rate of penetration (ROP), rotation speed (RPM), torque, and pump volume (P) are identified through detailed drilling mechanism analysis. In the last stage, a real-time identification method of formation lithology in drilling process based on pre-training language model is proposed, which realizes high-precision real-time identification in drilling process. The effectiveness of the proposed method is proved by comparison with common methods.

articleTitle: A Kalman Filter Method for Train Operation State Estimation that Use Underdetermined Least Squares Estimation Model Error
abstract: In the problem of estimating the operating status of trains, achieving precise modeling is extremely challenging. Due to the complexity of the train operating environment and the inherent defects of the sensors, the model inevitably has some errors. Due to the lack of a priori information, these errors are difficult to be accurately derived, which affects the accuracy of the Kalman filtering method or even the results do not converge. To address this problem, we introduce an error variable into the system model, construct an error estimation equation, and propose undetermined least squares Kalman Filter (ULS-KF) algorithm. The undetermined least squares method is able to get the minimum paradigm solution for the underdetermined system of equations. By estimating the unknown error and incorporating it into the Kalman filtering process, the effect of modeling error on the estimation results is compensated and the accuracy of the filtering results is improved. Through simulation experiments, the results show the effectiveness of the method proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: HT-HAN: Hypergraph Attention Network Based on Hypergraph Transformation for Edge Classification
abstract: With the increasing number of graph data, traditional graph learning methods have encountered challenges in dealing with data with complex structure and high order relationships and in obtaining effective edge embeddings. In this paper, Hypergraph Transformation-based Hypergraph Attention Network (HT-HAN) is proposed to solve the edge classification problem in graph data. By introducing hypergraph transformation, we can obtain the hypergraph with the original edge as the node, and use the hypergraph attention mechanism to enhance the recognition ability of the model to the key information. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves significant performance improvement on multiple data sets.

articleTitle: Optimization of Support Vector Machine for Photovoltaic Array Fault Diagnosis Based on Sparrow Search Algorithm
abstract: Photovoltaic power generation system because of the use of energy green environmental protection has been widely concerned by the world, to ensure that the system operation with high efficiency is the premise that the system can operate normally, photovoltaic power generation system is installed in a bad environment, photovoltaic arrays often have a variety of failures, and the number of photovoltaic arrays in the system is large, it is difficult to determine the type of failure and maintenance in time. It seriously affects the efficiency of photovoltaic power generation system, so it is very important to study a method that can detect the failure of photovoltaic power generation system in real time. In this study, the output characteristic curves of various fault conditions were analyzed according to the output characteristic curves of photovoltaic cells, the characteristics that could be distinguished from other fault types were selected, and the fault characteristic values were collected. Then SSA-SVM is used to establish the fault diagnosis model of photovoltaic array, and combined with the simulation experimental data and the data of photovoltaic simulator, the validity of SSA-SVM method is verified. Through model design and algorithm improvement, SSA-SVM is applied to fault diagnosis of photovoltaic array. Compared with IGS-SVM and PSO-SVM, SSA-SVM algorithm has higher stability and shorter time.

articleTitle: Model-free fractional order differentiator based on modulating functions method
abstract: This paper aims to design a model-free fractional order differentiator based on the modulating functions method, which can non-asymptotically and robustly estimate fractional derivatives from discrete and noisy observation. In this paper, we adopt the idea of model approximation, and in this way, the problem of designing a differentiator is transformed into the parameter estimation problem for the approximation model. For this, a local approximation model with a short integration time is proposed. To enhance the integration effect, a moving window is introduced to increase the integration time. However, these two methods are indirect. To obtain the fractional derivative more conveniently, a direct model-free fractional differentiator is proposed. Finally, numerical simulation results are given to illustrate the efficiency and robustness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: MAPPO and Hungarian Algorithm Based Collaborative Decision-Making for UAV Air Combat
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of coordinating <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to shoot down <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> targets (N ≥M) through maneuvering decisions in a three-dimensional space without boundary constraints. The focus is on ensuring that all agents avoid collisions while employing collaborative strategies to efficiently neutralize the targets. A Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization combined with the Hungarian algorithm (MAPPO-H) is designed, integrating multi-agent reinforcement learning with a target allocation method. The Hungarian algorithm is utilized to address the target allocation problem, while MAPPO is utilized to implement the maneuver decision-making strategy. Firstly, we establish the aircraft motion model and define conditions for achieving victory in battle. Secondly, we frame the autonomous maneuver decision-making as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), delineating the state space, action space, and reward function using a target allocation algorithm rooted in the Hungarian method. We finally give a numerical simulation to verify the proposed algorithm and the conclusion that all agents can avoid collisions and successfully shoot down all targets.

articleTitle: Enhancing Binary Neural Network with Response Deep Supervision
abstract: In recent years, binary neural networks (BNNs) have achieved significant success in resource-constrained scenarios. However, compared to full-precision networks, BNNs tend to have lower accuracy, which negatively impacts their application on complex tasks. To address this, we propose a novel BNN-RDS (Binary Neural Network with Response Deep Supervision) algorithm based on self-distillation and response deep supervision techniques. Firstly, we extend the backbone structure by auxiliary classifiers to transform features extracted from intermediate layers into logits response outputs. Then we effectively supervise intermediate layers using response-based deep supervision methods. Additionally, we introduce residual feature extraction modules and fully connected layers to enhance information propagation efficiency through residual connections and feature reuse mechanisms. This allows the network to better capture fine details and contextual information in images. Finally, we analyze how teacher layer selection differs between full-precision networks and BNNs during self-distillation. We propose utilizing the most accurate auxiliary classifier as the teacher layer in self-distillation and it ensures mutual benefit among multiple shallow classifiers to avoid negative interactions. Experimental results on CIFAR-I0 and ImageNet datasets show that the BNN-RDS method enhances the performance of BNNs. Furthermore, experiments on plant pathology datasets validate its effectiveness for identifying plant leaf diseases in agricultural domains.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis and Fault-Tolerant Control of Networked Control Systems with Time Delay
abstract: This article addresses the challenges of fault diagnosis and fault-tolerant control in networked control systems, introducing an observation-based approach and a corresponding control strategy. The proposed method employs HBF neural networks for fault estimation, while integrating a control prediction generator (CPG) with a network delay compensation (NDC) mechanism. This combination allows for the prediction of future control inputs and the dynamic adjustment of network delays in real-time, thereby mitigating the adverse effects of delays. This seeks to enhance the system's performance and robustness amid time-varying delays and external disturbances. In the simulation process, state equations and output equations suitable for practical applications are designed, and the effects of actuator faults are considered. The simulation results demonstrate that the hyperbasis function (HBF) neural network can effectively estimate faults, and the CPG and NDC strategies can effectively compensate for the time-varying delay effects and keep the system running stably.

articleTitle: An Effective Heuristic Algorithm for the Two-Dimensional Variable-Size Bin Packing Problem with Circular Containers
abstract: This paper studies the two-dimensional variable-size bin packing problem with circular containers (2DVSBPPCC), a generalization of the well-known bin packing problem. The goal of this problem is to pack all the rectangular items into several bins and minimize the total cost of these bins. To solve this problem, we design a decoding procedure that converts a given sequence of items into a packing configuration and a swap operator that deals with infeasible containers. Based on this decoding procedure and this swap operator, we propose a highly efficient heuristic algorithm called the adaptive search algorithm. To evaluate the performance of the proposed adaptive search algorithm, we carry out experiments on numerous benchmark instances. The computational results show that the proposed algorithm is very efficient. Experimental analysis on the benchmark instances shows that the swap operator that exchanges a pair of containers plays an important role for the high performance of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Dynamic Optimization of Path-Constrained Switched Systems with Multiple Time-Delays
abstract: A dynamic optimization algorithm is designed for the optimal control problem of path-constrained switched systems with multiple time-delays. Firstly, the control vector parametrization technique is utilized to parameterize continuous control input into finite numbers of piecewise constant functions. Then, the gradient information of the objective function with respect to the decision variables (switching times and control input) is evaluated by solving an auxiliary costate system. Secondly, the dynamic optimization algorithm based on the gradient information is proposed to locate an optimal solution of the path-constrained switched systems with multiple time-delays, which satisfies the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions to a specific tolerance, meanwhile guaranteeing rigorous satisfaction of the path constraints. Thirdly, it is proved that the proposed algorithm terminates within finite iterations. Finally, the developed algorithm is validated through a numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Learning Allen-Cahn Equation Using Hard Constraint Representation
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries have the characteristics of high energy density, good safety, and long cycle life, so they have been widely used in consumer electronics, military, pure electric vehicles, and aerospace in recent years. Learning the electrochemical mechanism equations of lithium-ion batteries is vital for improving battery performance, designing new battery materials, and optimizing battery management systems. The traditional approach models the mechanism of ion migration, diffusion, and charge transfer inside the battery. However, mechanism modeling requires a complete understanding and knowledge of the electrochemical reactions inside the battery, which is very difficult in the research of lithium-ion batteries and even the next generation of new batteries. Therefore, in this paper, the electrochemical mechanistic equations of lithium-ion batteries are learned based on the physics-informed neural network (PINN), and the internal phase separation process of the battery described by the Allen-Cahn equation is used to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. PINN is a neural network embedded with a physical prior. It restricts the output of the neural network to satisfy the partial differential equations (PDEs) derived from the physical laws by regularizing the loss function. Specifically, this paper uses PINN to perform data-driven learning of 1D and 2D Allen-Cahn equations. It proposes a PINN based on hard constraints to represent the initial conditions (ICs) and boundary conditions (BCs). The Allen-Cahn equation learning results show the proposed approach possesses superior performance over the PINN with soft constraint representation. In addition, we further investigates the effect of the number of sampling points and the performance of different ICs and BCs.

articleTitle: A Subspace Gradient Descent Method for High-Dimensional Simulation-Based Optimization
abstract: High-dimensional simulation-based optimization problems are common and important in practice. Most of these problems have two key characteristics: (1) the objective function is unimodal, and (2) the factors influencing the objective function are far fewer than the number of dimensions. Gradient descent (GD) methods are well-suited for unimodal problems, but in high-dimensional cases, gradient estimation requires a large number of simulations, making it difficult to apply. This paper proposes a Subspace gradient descent (SubGD) method. First, a subspace is determined using historical data, ensuring that the gradient projection in this subspace closely aligns with the actual gradient. Then, the gradient projection in this subspace is estimated using the finite difference method (FDM). Finally, update the parameters by the estimated gradient projection in this subspace. Compared to the traditional GD methods directly using FDM for gradient estimation, SubGD significantly reduces the number of simulations. In our experiments on a 200-dimensional optimization problem and a 124-dimensional processor software parameter optimization problem, our method outperformed genetic algorithms, traditional GD methods, and Bayesian optimization methods.

articleTitle: Design of Nonlinear Global Finite-Time Observers with High Gain Technique
abstract: A kind of nonlinear observers with global finite time stability are proposed for nonlinear systems with non-Lipschitz nonlinearities. The designed nonlinear observers are constructed through high gain method. The global finite time stability is proved based on global asymptotical stability as well as local finite-time stability. The effectiveness of the designed observers is shown through simulation.

articleTitle: Optimization Method of Excitation System Parameters of Synchronous Condenser for Coordinated Voltage and Damping Support
abstract: Synchronous condensers can not only provide dynamic reactive power support but also improve the damping of power systems. This paper proposes a method to optimize the parameters of the excitation system of synchronous condenser for coordinated voltage and damping support. First, an objective function that considers both voltage and damping performance is established by combining the effective reactive current gain and the minimum damping ratio of electromechanical oscillations. Then, the optimization direction of the excitation system parameters of the synchronous condenser is determined based on parameter trajectory sensitivity and parameter perturbation damping increment. Additionally, to further improve the damping effect, the excitation system parameters of the generators strongly related to minimum damping ratio are also treated as optimization targets. Finally, a parameter iterative solution method is constructed using Power System Analysis Software Package (PSASP) combined with an improved Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. The simulation results validate the effectiveness and rationality of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Phased Optimal Experience Replay Method
abstract: In the field of reinforcement learning, experience replay buffers are frequently used. In previous work, most of the experience replay methods used uniform sampling or preferential sampling based on value of TD-errors. However, while these methods can improve data utilization and accelerate training speed, they still fall short in terms of rapid convergence. In this paper we develop a framework for best experience, so as to replay important transitions more frequently, and learn more efficiently. We implemented optimal experience replay in various state-of-the-art reinforcement learning algorithms, including both discrete and continuous action spaces. Experimental results show that using optimal experience replay can improve the performance of these algorithms.

articleTitle: Large Language Model-Assisted Parameter Prediction in Integrated Energy Systems
abstract: Accurate parameter predictions contribute to the operation optimization of integrated energy systems. Existing prediction methods have some limitations in fully capturing the complex temporal dependencies inherent in parameter patterns. To overcome such limitations, this paper investigates the problem of parameter prediction in integrated energy systems based on large language models (LLMs), which show the powerful logical reasoning capabilities when dealing with complex time series problems. To be specific, this paper utilizes Time-LLM framework to predict electric load, heat load, cold load, and photovoltaic generation. Note that the utilized framework facilitates the reprogramming of the LLMs for time series prediction while preserving the integrity of the backbone language models. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed prediction method can achieve higher accuracy by 5.7% to 83.6% compared with existing machine learning based benchmarks.

articleTitle: Design and Research of Arc Discharge Electromagnetic Radiation Detection Antenna
abstract: Arc fault could cause equipment damage, system instability, electromagnetic interference, and other problems, posing a potential threat to the reliability and safety of the power network and causing harm to the power system. This research aimed to design Archimedean spiral antenna and Hilbert fractal antenna to detect radio frequency electromagnetic signals generated by arc discharge. Through simulation and analysis, it was found that the sixth-order Hilbert fractal antenna had better emission coefficient characteristics and directivity, and was more in line with design requirements. Through optimized design, it was determined that the 6th-order Hilbert fractal antenna had the widest frequency band with a return loss of less than -5dB in the detection frequency band, which met the design requirements. The final size of the antenna was determined to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{90}\ \mathbf{mm} \times \mathbf{90} \mathbf{mm} \times \mathbf{1.6}\mathbf{mm}$</tex> to meet the design requirements for miniaturization and portability.

articleTitle: Image Encryption Algorithm Based on Matrix Semi-Tensor Product in DWT Domain
abstract: This paper proposed an image encryption method based on matrix semi-tensor product (STP) and discrete wavelet transform (DWT). Firstly, a two-dimensional chaotic system is utilized to produce random sequences. Secondly, the plaintext image is converted to wavelet coefficients based on discrete wavelet transform. Next, the wavelet coefficients are encrypted based on STP and chaotic sequences. Then the encrypted information in DWT domain are converted into space domain via inverse discrete wavelet transform (IDWT). At last, the image is diffused to obtain the encrypted image. The proposed method is highly secure against statistical attacks according to the security analysis, as the information entropy reaches 7.9971.

articleTitle: Robust Control on Coupling Effects of a Hovering Underwater Vehicle
abstract: This paper addresses a robust control solution to the coupling effects encountered by a hovering underwater vehicle. The coupling issues across different freedoms are treated as uncertainties. In this process, the nonlinear coupling model of the vehicle is first compensated into a linear coupling model using real experiments, and an uncertainty boundary is proposed to cover the coupled issues. Then, the non-zero elements on the non-diagonal part of inertia mass matrix, added mass matrix and damping matrix can be avoided in the control design process. A comparison is given between PID and the proposed robust controller.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Region Division and Leader-Follower Communication
abstract: The integration of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) into complex systems has paved new ways for collaborative problem-solving. However, traditional approaches to MARL frequently encounter the challenge of achieving ef-ficient communication among agents, essential for coordinated action. This paper introduces a region division and leader-follower(RDLF) communication algrithm with the MARL frame-work. RDLF divides the environment into several regions, each managed by a leader agent that coordinates the actions of fol-lower agents and handling inter-region communication. This hier-archical structure reduces unnecessary communication, enhancing learning efficiency. Experimental results in multi-particle en-vironments demonstrate RDLF's superiority over existing MARL algorithms, especially with increasing agent numbers. RDLF effectively addresses scalability and communication challenges in large-scale multi-agent systems, providing a robust foundation for its application in complex and dynamic environment.

articleTitle: The Application Method of Karush-Kuhn-Tucker Condition for Judging Boundary Extremum Points
abstract: The Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) condition is crucial in optimization algorithms as a basis for determining whether the optimum point is a boundary extremum point or not. This article proposes application methods for several situations encountered in numerical algorithms and provides the program flowchart. Before applying this condition, all of the redundant constraints among the working constraints must be removed. For the case where the number of effective constraints is greater than the dimension, all of the basic gradient groups must be checked. As long as the Lagrange multipliers of a group are all non negative, the optimum point satisfies the KKT condition. For the case where the number of effective constraints is less than the dimension number, it is necessary to take some equations to calculate the Lagrange multiplier, and then to take other equations to test the calculation result. The calculation steps of this application method are illustrated with examples. The solution idea to the optimization problems with equality constraints is proposed.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Group Consensus Control of Hybrid Multi-Agent Systems Based on Event-Triggering Strategy
abstract: In this paper, we study the group consensus problem of hybrid multi-agent systems (HMASs) with actuator faults under event-triggering conditions. Firstly, considering different starting times and a variety of fault types, an online observer is designed to accurately evaluate the impact of actuator faults. Then, a new distributed hybrid multi-agent group consensus fault-tolerant control protocol is proposed based on the neighbor multi-agent information of the location state when the event is triggered. The designed controller can effectively eliminate Zeno phenomenon, compensate the influence of fault on the system, and realize the consensus of the system group by providing appropriate event-triggering strategy. By using Lyapunov functional method, the sufficient conditions for stability of second-order multi-agent systems are given. Finally, a numerical example is presented to verify the correctness of the obtained results.

articleTitle: Research on a Current-Controlled Voltage Regulation Digital System for Online Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy of Space Fuel Cells
abstract: With the escalating demand for high-performance energy systems in spacecraft, Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs), characterized by their high power density and longevity, have emerged as a preferred option for space applications. Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) stands as a potent diagnostic tool for PEMFC malfunctions; however, conventional EIS measurements necessitate equipment such as electrochemical workstations, inhibiting their integration into spatial PEMFC systems. Addressing this challenge, this study devises a strategy that integrates the EIS measurement system with the DC/DC converter at the output end of space PEMFCs. A current-controlled voltage regulation method for online EIS measurements is proposed, employing a dual closed-loop control strategy to ensure the stability of the PEMFC output voltage during EIS assessments, thereby fulfilling the stringent stability requirements of operating voltages in space applications. The successful development and validation of a digital system for in-situ EIS measurements in PEMFCs not only underpin robust fault diagnostics for space fuel cells but also facilitate advancements in the stability and durability of PEMFC systems, thereby positively contributing to the progression of aerospace energy technologies.

articleTitle: Active Fault-Tolerant Control for Networked Nonlinear Systems under Sensor Fault
abstract: In this paper, a fault diagnosis and fault-tolerant control method based on a hyper basis function (HBF) neural network observer and state feedback predictive control is proposed for affine nonlinear systems operating under sensor fault conditions. The network-induced delay is modeled as round-trip time (RTT) delay, with additional consideration of sensor fault. Initially, an HBF neural network observer is developed to approximate the system state in real-time and detect sensor fault. Subsequently, effective fault-tolerant control is achieved through a state feedback predictive controller integrated with a network delay compensator. The results from the numerical simulations confirm the efficacy of the proposed method in handling sensor faults and network-induced delays.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Stabilizing Control for Nonlinear Systems With Uncontrollable Linearization and Unmodeled Dynamics
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of fixed-time stabilization for a class of nonlinear systems.Unlike existing results in the literature, the studied system accounts for uncontrollable unstable linearization and unmodeled dynamics, which may represent a broader class of nonlinear systems. Thanks to the changing supply rates for fixed-time input-to-state stability (FxT-ISS) system and the adding-one-power-integrator (AOPI) techniques, we propose a partial-state feedback control scheme that ensures system states converge to zero in fixed time. The settling time under this fixed-time control scheme depends solely on the control design parameters, independent of the initial conditions. Finally, numerical simulations validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Motion Control of Robot Jellyfish Based on Umbrella Structure Actuator
abstract: In order to meet the requirement for ensuring good stability of an underwater robot, this paper presents the design of a bionic robot jellyfish based on a novel umbrella-like slurry actuator. The jellyfish robot is composed of a sealing cover, a main support, a transmission device based on spur gear and crank mechanism, and an umbrella slurry actuator. Six evenly distributed circumferential actuators are utilized to propel the robot jellyfish forward by driving the slurry structure. Additionally, motion simulation analysis conducted on the umbrella drive using Solidworks demonstrates that the new drive is capable of achieving a higher level of propulsion. Finally, PID algorithm is employed to control the coding motor, and a system experiment platform is established to analyze the single slurry actuator. Therefore, it can be concluded that the proposed jellyfish robot in this paper has the capability to achieve stable underwater movement.

articleTitle: Tobacco Stem Object Detection Based on Improved YOLO
abstract: The threshing and redrying process is a crucial stage in cigarette production. During this stage, threshing equipment is used to separate the stems from the initially dried tobacco leaves, followed by the redrying of the leaves. Tobacco stems in the leaves affect various cigarette quality evaluation indices, making stem detection extremely important. In actual production, the methods used are mostly manual screening or winnowing equipment. Existing computer vision-based methods also require offline sampling and manual spreading for detection. The above methods are time-consuming and labor-intensive. Therefore, we propose a tobacco stem detection method based on an improved YOLO model, capable of directly detecting tobacco stems in the mixed materials on the production line without the need for offline sampling. This method, built on the YOLO framework, incorporates the SimAM attention module to make the network focus more on the tobacco stem regions. Additionally, it uses a texture enhancement module to extract concealed edge features of the stems, ultimately achieving a detection accuracy (AP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf>) of 83.6%. This method can effectively improve the detection efficiency of tobacco stems in the threshing and redrying process.

articleTitle: A Track Step Identification Algorithm for Medium and Low Speed Maglev Trains Based on Fuzzy Theory
abstract: The destabilizing effect of track steps on the levitation stability of medium and low speed maglev trains during running has long been a concern. Addressing the real-time identification of track step information is crucial for improving levitation stability of maglev trains. This study begins by analyzing the signal change characteristics of the triple air-gap sensor as the maglev train passes over track joints. Subsequently, fuzzy theory is employed to model the sensor's response to these track joints and divide it into several stages. Using a fuzzy logic system, optimal moments for sampling track step heights are determined, enabling real-time output of the most recent step height data. Simulation results indicate significant reductions in error and result delay. This method offers clear physical interpretations at each part and ensures manageable real-time identification errors and delays, making it suitable for track step identification and optimization control during medium and low speed maglev train running.

Author Keywords: medium and low speed maglev train

articleTitle: Chinese Vision-language Understanding based on Multimodal Pre-trained Models
abstract: The purpose of Chinese Vision-Language Understanding (CVLU) task is to enhance the capabilities of Chinese vision-language multimodal pre-trained models in vision-language multimodal modeling and understanding. The complex semantics and ambiguity of Chinese language result in varying performance levels of the general pre-trained models across different tasks. We verify the different performances of the general pre-trained model in processing vision-language information from different perspectives through four subtasks, including image-text retrieval, visual question answering, visual grounding and visual dialog. At the same time, to solve the above problems, we use task-specific datasets to fine-tune the general pre-trained model, enhancing its adaptability to various subtasks. The experimental results show that most of the evaluation metrics for the four subtasks have improved by over 10%, validating the efficacy of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Terahertz Metasurfaces Based on Different Coupling Regimes for Sensing
abstract: This study presents a comparative analysis of terahertz metasurfaces based on weak and strong coupling regimes, using electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and parity-time (PT) symmetry. We explore their theoretical behaviors and practical implementations for sensing applications, highlighting the nuanced interactions between terahertz waves and resonant structures. The simulations reveal that PT symmetry, exemplifying strong coupling, offers higher sensitivity but at the cost of reduced quality factor compared to EIT, which represents weak coupling. This trade-off underscores the complexities and necessity of optimizing terahertz metasurfaces for high-precision sensing, balancing sensitivity and quality factor. The insights gained advance understanding of coupling effects in terahertz metasurfaces, guiding future developments in terahertz sensing technology.

articleTitle: Aging Condition Monitoring for Aluminum Electrolytic Capacitor in Traction Rectifiers
abstract: The aluminum electrolytic capacitor (AEC) is one of the important components in traction systems, but it is prone to failure. In order to improve the reliability of the system, it is extremely essential to monitor the condition of the AEC. In this paper, an aging condition monitoring method based on magnitude-frequency response of the AEC is proposed. The capacitance value and the equivalent series resistance (ESR) value are selected to monitor the aging condition of the AEC, which can make the method highly reliable. The method only utilizes the existing components of the system, it does not require additional sensors and can be extended to other converter applications. Finally, a simulation experiment platform of the traction rectifier is constructed, and the robustness and effectiveness of the method are proved by the simulation results.

articleTitle: A Multimodal Complex Model for Measuring the Quality of Music Performance
abstract: While computational aesthetics evaluation has achieved success in various domains, the exploration of music performance remains an untouched area. Currently, subjective evaluation stands as the ultimate approach in music aesthetics research, yet it demands substantial human and material resources. Moreover, AI-generated music performances tend to be mechanical, monotonic, and devoid of beauty. To direct the creation of AI music performances and enhance the performance quality of human-being artists, this article introduces an objective beauty measurement method based on Birkhoff's aesthetic measure. The article's primary contributions are twofold: firstly, we present an objective aesthetic evaluation method tailored for music performance; secondly, we introduce ten fundamental music features and four aesthetic music features. Experimental results demonstrate that our method excels in performance assessment.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Spatial and Temporal Registration Algorithm Based on Unity Toolbox
abstract: Spatial and temporal registration are important issues in multi-sensor target tracking systems. This paper proposes a interpolation temporal registration method based on interactive multiple model (IMM) and adopts a spatial registration algorithm based on non-cooperative targets to improve the registration performance. Unity toolbox is used to build simulation scenarios for algorithms verification. Simulation results show that the methods we used have good performance in registration tasks.

articleTitle: Complex Fusion Structure Slow Dissociation Simulation Prediction Method
abstract: Human skeletal implants, as a category of critically important medical consumables, are designed to remain inside the body for long periods. Titanium or titanium alloys are commonly chosen as the primary construction materials. Recently, the academic community has explored an innovative approach to implant construction that uses titanium as the base framework and zinc as the filling material to create an interconnected composite structure. In this structure, zinc gradually dissolves over the lifetime of the implant, promoting bone growth into the pores formed after its dissolution. Given the continuous dissociation of zinc, the physical and chemical properties of the implant exhibit a slow and continuous change over its lifecycle. However, there is currently no effective method to precisely predict and assess the state changes of such complex structures over long periods of time. This study focuses on the typical application scenarios of human skeletal implants, and verifies the accuracy of short-term steady-state numerical calculation models through rigorous experimental methods. Based on this, we propose a complex fusion structure slow dissociation reverse simulation prediction method based on short-term steady-state calculation results. This method aims to simulate the steady-state performance of implants in the short term, and reverse deduce the structural changes and performance evolution caused by zinc dissociation during long-term use, thereby providing a more scientific basis and support for the design and evaluation of medical implants.

articleTitle: Optimal Output Power Tracking Method for MCR-WPT Based on DC/DC Converter
abstract: In this paper, a magnetically coupled resonant wireless power transmission system(MCR-WPT) output power tracking method is advanced to adress the challenge of decreasing output power of wireless power transmission systems due to the change of the distance. By first analyzing the output power of the system, an optimal reflection impedance is observed to maximize the output power. On this basis, a optimal output power tracking method is then proposed. This method performs the optimal matching of the reflected impedance by combining the adjustment of the DC/DC converter duty cycle and the proportion and integration (PI) control. It finally makes the magnetically resonant wireless power transmission system maintain the optimal output power even as the distance for transmission varies. Simulation, experiments are then conducted. The obtained results show that the maximum increase of the output power under simulation condition is almost 10.7% compared with the unregulated one when the transmission distance is in the range of 4–8 cm. Furthermore, the maximum increase in the output power under experimental conditions over unregulated is approximately 8.9%.

articleTitle: Position Control of Valve-Controlled Cylinder Based on CRL-DIARC
abstract: The control difficulties of electro-hydraulic system are high dynamic order, nonlinear model and uncertain model parameters. In order to achieve higher performance position control, it is necessary to design advanced nonlinear controller to ensure the control performance of the system. Aiming at the demand of high-precision position control of electro-hydraulic system particularly in scenarios with significant initial errors and complex disturbance, the state space equation of valve-controlled cylinder system is first established, and then the backstepping control framework is used to design the controller of the electro-hydraulic system. An exponential reaching law with constant velocity reaching compensation term sliding mode control method and integral sliding mode control method is used to construct the sliding surface and the direct/indirect adaptive robust control (DIARC) is used in each step of backstepping control, which developes DIARC with composite reaching law (CRL-DIARC). Finally, PID controller, DARC (direct adaptive robust control) controller, DIARC and CRL-DIARC controller are simulated and compared. The simulation results show that CRL-DIARC controller can effectively improve the position tracking performance of valve-controlled cylinders.

articleTitle: Integrating LSTM-Based Target Prediction with TD3 for Enhanced UAV Pursuit-Evasion
abstract: To address the pursuit-evasion problem of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), this paper proposes the TD3-TP algorithm framework. This framework integrates a target prediction network (TP Net) within the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm, enabling UAVs to autonomously pursue dynamic targets in an obstacle environment. The TP Net, constructed with a long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network that has memory units and time series data processing capabilities, predicts the future position of the target based on its historical trajectory. This integration allows the pursuing UAV to generate its current action strategy based on both the current and future states of the evader. Comparative experiments and ablation studies demonstrate that TD3 combined with TP Net enhances the success rates and efficiency of UAVs in pursuit-evasion scenarios, more effectively fulfilling the requirements for UAV pursuit tasks.

articleTitle: DA-MEF: A Multi-exposure Fusion Network via Detail Enhancement and Global Feature Attention
abstract: Multi-exposure image fusion (MEF) can produce high dynamic range (HDR) images with enhanced information and details from improperly exposed images. In recent years, MEF algorithms based on deep learning have shown good performance, but most of them have some defects because of the complex network and the neglect of unique features. In this work, we introduce a lightweight MEF method that synthesizes HDR images with high quality and efficiency. Specifically, we propose a comprehensive feature extraction block to accurately capture global information and local details. In this stage, we design a novel attention mechanism named GFA, which extracts valid features by comparing the similarities and differences between two inputs. Additionally, we introduce a detail enhancement fusion module that helps create HDR results with clear edges and rich details. To demonstrate the superiority of our approach, we conduct extensive experiments and compare our method with several cutting-edge techniques. Furthermore, we validate the effectiveness of the proposed modules through ablation experiments.

articleTitle: Asymptotic Sampling Behavior for a Class of Nonlinear Robot Systems in Multirate Case
abstract: The manuscript aims the stability of the two degree of freedom robot systems based on the corresponding discrete-time plant, which can generate from the sampling in the case of a new multirate input and hold. Furthermore, the asymptotic expression and stable conditions of discretization robot model and corresponding sampling zero dynamics are also desired. Moreover, the control strategy of the corresponding robot plant is acquired by using the sampling zero dynamic stable approach.

Author Keywords: a new multirate input and hold

articleTitle: An Improved RT-DETR Model for UAV-Based Power Line Inspection Under Various Weather Conditions
abstract: With the rapid advancement of deep learning, convolutional neural network-based target detection models have been effectively applied in UAV power inspection. However, the success of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) heavily relies on image augmentation and post-processing, both of which consume significant amounts of time in real-time object detection. This paper presents an end-to-end improved RT-DETR model that eliminates the post-processing module and introduces a reweighted L1 Loss to enhance the model's ability to learn small objects. Additionally, to improve the model's multi-scale feature fusion capability, we incorporate the GELAN module, combining CSPNet and ELAN models, allowing the network to more effectively propagate and aggregate feature information from different levels. Furthermore, to solve the shortage of power inspection datasets, we propose a Multi-Weather UAV Power Inspection dataset (MWUPI). Experimental results demonstrate that the improved RT-DETR model achieves high accuracy on this dataset while maintaining the fast detection speed of the original RT-DETR, meeting the performance requirements of real-time object detection. The codes for this study are publicly available at https://github.com/HantaoDing/Improved-RT-DETR-for-Power-Inspection.

articleTitle: Distributed Fixed-Time Coordinated Control for Multiple Electric Units in High-Speed Trains
abstract: This paper investigates a distributed fixed-time controller for electric multi units (EMU) of high-speed train (HST), which aims to ensure that each electric unit of the HST reaches a balanced state with consistent speed and the coupler force tending to be zero within a fixed time. To begin with, a multi-particle model of the HST is developed, incorporating nonlinear internal forces, uncertain resistances, and input saturation, based on the assumption that the HST is composed of EMU connected by elastic couplers. Then, after linearizing the train saturation function, a distributed coordinated controller is designed according to the fixed time control theory. Finally, the effectiveness of the controller is proved by simulation experiments. The research results provide an effective solution for the control of EMU in HSTs, which has important practical significance for improving the operational performance of HSTs.

articleTitle: On-orbit Inspection Scheduling Strategy with Multi-arm based on Hybrid NSGA-II and MOPSO Algorithm
abstract: Multiple operation point inspection task, as an integral part of the spacecraft on-orbit maintenance task, is of great significance to the life extension of the spacecraft. In this paper, a multi-manipulator scheduling method considering the motion performance of the manipulator at the operation point and the task space constraints between the manipulators is proposed to solve the scheduling problem of multi-manipulator performing multiple operation point inspection tasks. On the basis of constructing a multi-objective optimization model including manipulator motion performance, task execution time and load-balancing ratio, a hybrid NSGA-II and MOPSO algorithm is proposed by using the elitism of the NSGA-II algorithm and the local search ability of the MOPSO algorithm, and the coding form and iterative update strategy are improved for the discrete decision variables, and the effectiveness of the algorithm in task scheduling is verified by the simulated Pareto solution set.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Method for Rolling Bearings Based on SE-MSCNN-GRU with Adaptive Sample Length Adjustment
abstract: To address the issues of uneven data collection, inaccurate fault feature extraction, and insensitivity to important bearing features in real-world scenarios, this paper proposes a fault diagnosis method for rolling bearings based on Multi-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (MSCNN), Squeeze-and-Excitation Network (SE-Net), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) with adaptive sample length adjustment. Firstly, after performing Principal Component Analysis (PCA), we selected the maximum number of principal components that achieve a 99% variance explanation rate as the final dimensionality for reduction, thus standardizing the length of the samples. Then, MSCNN extracts local features from the signal, SE-Net enhances the network's focus on key information through ‘squeeze’ and ‘excitation’ operations, and the GRU module is responsible for extracting time series features. Finally, the CWRU bearing dataset was used as the experimental subject, and the SE-MSCNN-GRU model was compared with various other models. The experimental results show that the proposed method demonstrates its excellent performance in bearing fault diagnosis, which has large application potential and advantages.

articleTitle: Biomimetic Lateral Line Tactile Sensing Technology Based on Triboelectric Nanogenerator
abstract: Conventional underwater detection technologies (acoustic/optical) face challenges in turbid, dark and confined environments. The efficiency of underwater vehicles will suffer as a result. Inspired by the superficial neuromasts (SN) of the fish lateral line system, this paper develops a biomimetic lateral line tactile sensor (BLLTS) using triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) technology to provide a novel sensing modality for underwater vehicles. The sensor consists of a triboelectric sensing unit, a cap, a connecting rod, a cylindrical housing, a trigger and a silicone pad. The BLLTS is able to effectively detect the magnitude and frequency information of an external load through various forms of electrical signals. Meanwhile, the sensor maintains a stable signal output when it continuously receives external loads, proving itself to have good durability. The experimental results show that BLLTS has important advantages in assisting underwater vehicles to accomplish tasks such as underwater environment sensing.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Prediction for Hidden Degradation Process with Multiple Source Uncertainty
abstract: A remaining useful life (RUL) prediction algorithm considering temporal uncertainty, individual variability uncertainty, and unmodeled dynamic uncertainty is proposed for hidden degradation process with unmeasurable degradation index. First, the degradation model integrating multiple uncertainties is established. Then, the estimated distribution of degradation index and degradation model parameters are iteratively computed using the nonlinear filter. Finally, based on the real-time multiple uncertainties information, the probability density function (PDF) is adaptively updated, achieving the RUL prediction for hidden degradation process with the influence of multiple uncertainties.

articleTitle: Intelligent Scheduling Strategy with Bandwidth Feedback in Networked Control Systems
abstract: This paper proposes an intelligent scheduling strat-egy with bandwidth feedback. A network scheduler is designed to adjust the sampling period of each networked control loop based on its real-time control error. At a current scheduling period, the increment of the bandwidth feedback occupancy ratio is estimated by the dynamic control error of each networked control loop, and then a new bandwidth occupancy ratio within the next scheduling period is assigned to each loop based on the bandwidth constraint condition. After that, the sampling period is dynamically changed to adapt the quality of control and quality of service. To analyze the system stability, this variable sampling period networked control system is modeled as a dynamic interval discrete system with uncertain parameters. Its asymptotic stability is proved by the Lyapunov function and linear matrix inequality. Experimental results show that the scheduling strategy has the bandwidth feedback advantage, and the variable sampling period has the successive approximation ability for the time-varying reference input networked control system.

articleTitle: Attitude Takeover Control Using Cooperative Game Considering Time-Varying Angular Momentum
abstract: This article focuses on the failed spacecraft attitude takeover control problem by multiple micro-satellites. To tackle this problem, a wheel-level cooperative game considering time-varying angular momentum is proposed. First, the concept of the angular momentum margin factor is introduced to design an objective function for each reaction wheel, allowing torque output to vary according to each wheel's angular momentum level. Additionally, a cooperative game model is developed based on the dynamics constraints of the combined system. Furthermore, a particle swarm optimization-critic neural network is employed to find the Pareto optimal strategy for the cooperative game. Finally, Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can directly provide control moments for each reaction wheel based on the angular momentum margin without requiring control assignment. Compared to existing cooperative game control methods, this approach significantly reduces peak angular momentum, thereby enhancing control safety.

articleTitle: Simplified Fast Image Inpainting Method
abstract: Addressing the challenge of slow repair speed in inpainting small-scale damaged images, we proposed a streamlined, swift digital inpainting method, tailored specifically for images where damaged regions exhibit notable gray-level disparities from the original content. This method leverages the correlation between missing pixels and their neighboring, known image information. Specifically, it employs the values of four adjacent pixels to interpolate and fill in each missing pixel, iteratively traversing the damaged area until complete restoration is achieved. Both theoretical analysis and simulation outcomes underscore the efficiency gains of this simplified algorithm, which achieves time savings without compromising visual quality. Comparative experiments against FMM further validate its practical advantages and wide-ranging applicability.

articleTitle: Multi-Model Ensemble and Optimization for Baby Cry Analysis: Application of CNN and LSTM Methods
abstract: Baby crying is an important way for babies to express their needs and discomfort. Accurately analyzing their crying is of great significance to caregivers. This paper aims to solve the problem of baby crying analysis. It adopts a variety of data enhancement methods, uses LSTM and CNN deep learning models, and combines integrated ensemble and transfer learning methods to design and optimize the algorithm model. The experimental results show that the multi-model fusion and data enhancement methods effectively improve the accuracy and robustness of baby crying classification and analysis.

articleTitle: Fractional-Order Fixed-Time Control for a Quadrotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicle with Disturbances
abstract: This article investigates the issue of trajectory tracking for a quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle in the presence of disturbances. Firstly, in response to external disturbances, a fixed-time disturbance observer (FTDO) has been proposed that compensates for disturbances. Subsequently, a fixed-time terminal sliding mode surface is designed, and fractional-order theory is introduced to speed up the convergence and reduce the chattering. The results indicate that the aforementioned method can achieve precise tracking without overshoot under disturbances, and has good stability. Meanwhile, it can effectively suppress chattering and enhance system performance.

articleTitle: Apply the Sliding Mode Controller to the Generator-Side Converter of the Permanent Magnet Synchronous Wind Power System
abstract: In view of the characteristics of permanent magnet direct-drive wind power generation system, such as strong nonlinearity and multiple couplings, it is difficult for the traditional maximum power tracking control method to achieve accurate tracking and fast response to the optimal speed of the generator in the wind turbine. To mitigate this issue, we modify the traditional exponential reaching rate by introducing a variable exponential reaching rate, which is verified to satisfy the Lyapunov stability theorem, thereby enhancing the system's anti-interference capability. Four wind speed models are designed, the performance of the control is observed, the rationality and feasibility of the control design are judged, and finally the conclusion is that the sliding mode control method is superior to the traditional PI control by the MATLAB/Simulink simulation results, which can not only improve the robustness of the system, but also enable the system to realize the fast tracking of the motor speed under the action of different wind speeds, and improve the dynamic performance of the system.

Author Keywords: permanent magnet direct-drive wind power generation system

articleTitle: Siamese Network Tracking Algorithm Based on Multi-Scale Feature Fusion of Dual Attention Mechanism
abstract: Siamese network trackers have shown strong performance in the field of computer vision. However, relying solely on feature representations from the backbone network's final layer can cause tracking drift in complex scenarios. To address this issue, we propose a Siamese network tracking algorithm based on dual attention mechanisms and multi-scale feature fusion. This method leverages features from different layers of the backbone network, integrating deep semantic information with shallow spatial information through two multi-input attention mechanisms. This approach enhances the distinction between the target and the background, thereby enhancing the tracker's discriminative ability. Furthermore, a novel cascade of location prediction head is designed to accurately refine target localization. Experimental results on the VOT2019 and OTB2015 datasets indicate that the proposed method obtains satisfactory performance. On the VOT2019 dataset, the method achieved an accuracy of 60.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, an expected average overlap (EAO) of 34.1%, and a 14.20% improvement in robustness compared to the benchmark model, with a running speed of 48.2 FPS, surpassing the real-time threshold of 25 FPS.

articleTitle: A Novel Fault Diagnosis Method for Road Tunnel Ventilation Equipment Based on EEMD-SE Model
abstract: The operation status of ventilation equipment has a crucial impact on the safety of road tunnel traffic. In order to monitor the fault status of ventilation equipment, this paper determines the fault types and vibration signal data that need to be simulated according to the structural characteristics of axial fan, and puts forward a fault diagnostic model based on Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition-Squeeze and Excitation (EEMD-SE), which is based on the mechanism of ensemble empirical mode decomposition and attention. Fault diagnosis model, through the design and construction of the fan fault test bench to complete the fault simulation, while the collection and storage of vibration signals and various states of the fan data collection of empirical mode decomposition and analysis, the decomposed signal using the attention mechanism to further feature extraction and fault type discrimination, after verification of the model accuracy of up to 99.977%, has a good fault diagnosis, compared with other classical algorithms have a higher accuracy and accuracy, and the model has a higher accuracy and accuracy. The model is validated to be 99.977% accurate, with good fault diagnosis effect, compared with other classical algorithms with higher accuracy rate.

articleTitle: Multi-Target Tracking Algorithm Based on Improved ByteTrack
abstract: Aiming at the problems of target loss, slow speed and easy to be affected by noise in multi-target tracking algorithm, a multi-target tracking algorithm with improved ByteTrack algorithm is proposed. In terms of detectors, YOLOv8 is used to replace YOLOX, the number of C2f modules in Backbone structure is increased, and FasterNet modules and EMA attention mechanism are introduced to improve precision and reduce the number of parameters. CSPStage module of Neck part is redesigned to optimize the exchange of high-level semantic and low-level spatial information. The Wise-IoU loss function, which replaces CIoU, decreases the development of hazardous gradients. In the aspect of motion model, the noise adaptive Kalman filter is proposed, and the detection confidence is used to correct the noise and its prior probability, thus improve the tracking accuracy and stability. Experiments show that compared with the baseline algorithm, the detection indexes mAP0.5 and MAP0.5:0.95 of the improved algorithm are improved by 2.0% and 1.4% in MOT17 data set, and the tracking indexes MOTA and HOTA are improved by 0.64 and 2.74 in MOT20 data set, respectively. The indexes of the improved algorithm are all improved, which proves the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving the accuracy and stability of target detection and tracking.

articleTitle: Requirements of Risk Warning and Abductive for Power System Operation Based on Renewable Energy Accommodation Enhancement
abstract: With the acceleration of the construction of new power systems and the continuous expansion of the scale of the power grid, the access of flexible resources such as distributed renewable energy, virtual power plants and electric vehicles has made a large number of new adjustment objects appear on each side of the power grid load and storage, and the difficulty of cognitive analysis and adjustment of the power grid operation state has increased significantly. The traditional analysis model based on mechanism modeling is difficult to deal with the cognitive problem of multi-agent complex system. In view of the safe and stable operation of power grids in some regions after access to massive distributed flexible resources such as reverse transmission, overvoltage, and difficulty in peak regulation, it is urgent to study the refined cognition of power grid operation situation and the abductive technology of risk assessment based on probability statistical analysis and deep learning, so as to improve the cognition level and control ability of power grid risk. The power grid operation risk early warning and abduction technologies absorbed by renewable energy are further studied. The characteristics of abnormal situations are restored through the augmented matrix and abduction analysis is carried out, and the weak links of system operation and points causing risks are located to provide multi-dimensional cognitive information of power grid operation for subsequent optimization and dispatch.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Sliding Mode Control of the Slave Manipulator Based on Lagrange Equation
abstract: Minimally invasive surgical robot gets a lot of attention in the medical field because of their advantages such as fine stability, minimal trauma, and fast recovery. However, the large mass of the slave manipulator results in low positioning accuracy. To solve this problem, we design a fixed-time sliding mode controller which is by using Lagrangian dynamics equation. To begin with, the dynamic equation of the slave manipulator is established and the accuracy of the model is verified using Adams. Then, a novel non-singular fixed-time sliding mode controller based on the fixed-time stability theory is constructed by combining the dynamic model. The system stability is proved using the Lyapunov stability criterion. The performance of the controller can be clearly demonstrated that it is useful to cut down the influence of joints gravity and inertia on all of the active joints' moving accuracy of the slave manipulator of minimally invasive surgical robots and achieve faster convergence speed and good robustness.

articleTitle: A Multi-LIDAR SLAM Method Based on Hector-SLAM
