abstract: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping(SLAM) stands as the key technology facilitationg the realization of autonomous positioning and navigation in intelligent wheelchairs. Aiming at the problem that the field of view of an individual LIDAR mounted on the body of an intelligent wheelchair is susceptible to occlusion, we presents an improved Hector-SLAM method for simultaneous mapping using multiple laser data, which can simultaneously utilize laser data from multiple LIDARs mounted at varying angles for localization and mapping. By installing sensor devices and a main control panel on the body of an electric wheelchair and using it as an experimental platform, we show the method works effectively when the LIDAR's field of view is obstructed and enhances the accuracy of the map.

articleTitle: Design of Server Fault Diagnosis and Prediction Based on BMC
abstract: The server has become the central part of the information society, which means that the stable operation of the server is essential for people. Hence, the server fault diagnosis and prediction based on the baseboard management controller (BMC) is designed in this study to help administrators manage the server. The design scheme is divided into two phases according to the fault handling of the central processing unit (CPU). In the system startup phase, the basic input output system (BIOS) collects the errors in the system startup and sends them to BMC. In the running phase, the errors from the CPU, Memory, and PCIE are processed by the Reliability, Availability, and Serviceability (RAS) module but the errors from the NVME and PSU are handled by the registers. Hence, BMC obtains and handles the data by different methods. Then, the frequency reduction and DTF algorithms are adopted to maintain normal system status when BMC detects the alarm events. In summary, the novel design of fault diagnosis and prediction in this study contains a complete set of solutions for fault data collection, fault diagnosis, and fault prediction. Based on this, the design introduced by this paper can improve server management efficiency and reduce the probability of failure occurrence.

articleTitle: Entropy Investigation on Different Critical Properties of Spiking Neurons in Context-Dependent Learning Task
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) hold significant importance as a pivotal area of brain-inspired computing. Leveraging an SNN model of the rat hippocampus during the learning of content-related tasks, we examine the trends of coarse-grained entropy concerning the model's key parameters. To quantify this entropy, we adopt a method that maps binary spike sequences into a feature value space. Specifically, for each stimulus condition, the spike sequences of eight neurons are converted into eight corresponding feature values, upon which entropy is calculated by assessing the distribution of these values. We categorize the entropy values based on identical input stimuli and document the frequency of various input stimuli across 130 trials per training session. The entropy of all groups is then summed, weighted by their respective occurrence frequencies. By adjusting the values of the key parameters, we can trace the trends of entropy and derive specific findings. These insights offer invaluable guidance for setting our hyper-parameters.

articleTitle: A New Path Planning of Mobile Robot Based on Improved Ant Colony Algorithm
abstract: The paper thoroughly analyzes the shortcomings in the global path search process based on the traditional ACO algorithm. By integrating an improved ACO optimization approach with the A* algorithm, optimal paths can be efficiently generated for mobile robots navigating static environments. The enhanced ACO algorithm is capable of producing shorter paths with reduced turning points in a lesser number of iterations. Furthermore, a novel slope ACO algorithm is introduced to cater to more intricate terrains for optimal path exploration. The effectiveness of these two improved algorithms is validated through comparative simulations.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Load Prediction Based on CNN-BILSTM and XGBoost Combined Model
abstract: To address the issue of low prediction accuracy in single models due to the high volatility and redundancy of electric vehicle (EV) load data, this paper proposes a combined prediction method using CNN-BILSTM and XGBoost. The original electric vehicle (EV) load sequence is initially split into high-frequency and low-frequency components using adaptive noise complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition. The high-frequency components are processed by the CNN-BILSTM model, whereas the low-frequency components are handled by the XGBoost model. Hyperparameter optimization is refined using the improved Dung Beetle Optimization (DBO) algorithm. Experimental results indicate that this approach surpasses traditional methods in performance, including single CNN-BILSTM, CNN-GRU, and XGBoost models, in both prediction accuracy and speed.

articleTitle: Underwater Target Recognition with Sonar Images Based on Multiple Classifier Systems
abstract: Underwater target recognition(UTR) is an important task, where Multiple Classifier System (MCS) has been widely applied. By combining information from multiple sources or features, the improvement of target recognition accuracy can be expected. However, more classifiers in MCS do not necessarily bring better fusion results. In this paper, we focus on two key strategies to improve MCS performance: selecting diverse member classifiers and employing meta-learning methods for fusion. We develop multiple classifiers based on deep features derived from both hand-crafted features of sonar images and original sonar images. Beneficial diversity (BD) is employed to ensure diversity in classifier selection. To implement the fusion of member classifiers, meta-learning methods are used. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining diverse classifiers and the advantages of proposed meta-learning methods.

articleTitle: Temperature-Dependent Noise Analysis of Angular Accelerometer Using Cross-Correlation Method
abstract: Noise characteristics significantly affect the accuracy of the angular accelerometers and limit their application in various fields. According to the working principle, noises are affected by both internal mechanisms and external environments, especially temperature. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a method to identify the temperature-dependent noise model of the angular accelerometers. First, the output signals of the angular accelerometers are collected at different temperatures using the temperature chamber. Then, a cross-correlation method is applied to reduce the noise caused by the vibration of the temperature chamber and obtain the self-noise of the angular accelerometers. Moreover, the obtained noise data is analyzed by the Allan variance method to construct the noise model. Experiments are carried out on two angular accelerometers under ten different temperatures within their operation range. The results show that the proposed method can effectively identify the noise model, and the temperature characteristics of these angular accelerometers' noise are investigated.

articleTitle: Weak Feature Defect Detection of Insulators in Complex Images Based on Sequential Task Strategy
abstract: Detecting insulator defects from complex images poses a significant challenge using existing methods, especially for weak feature defects such as corrosion and notch. They exhibit limited spatial extent, complex morphology, and mutual interference. Therefore, this paper proposes a sequential task strategy for the detection of weak feature defects on insulators. Firstly, to address complex backgrounds, occlusions, and multi-scale issues, an insulator recognition method based on improved YOLOv5 is proposed, called feature refine fusion YOLOv5 (FRF-YOLOv5). This method realizes the accurate localization of insulators by introducing a spatially refined convolutional block attention module and a multi-scale feature fusion module. Then, DeepLabv3+ is cascaded, innovatively applied to the insulator defect detection, conducting pixel-level analysis on insulator re-gions and selectively replacing its backbone. Finally, the proposed method is validated. The results show it can effectively address the challenges of detecting insulator weak feature defects, and provide technical support for subsequent defect rating.

articleTitle: An Optimal Efficiency Online Planning for LEO/GEO Inter-Layer Link Establishment with Antenna Pointing Constraints
abstract: Addressing the online planning problem of LEO/GEO Inter-Layer Link (ILL) establishment with complex antenna pointing constraints, an iterative algorithm for constrained boundary equations is proposed, based on the antenna pointing constraints, attitude and orbit of satellites. Considering the longest connection time strategy, an optimal efficiency online planning algorithm for ILL establishment is proposed, which improves the search efficiency of access timetable, avoiding the duplicated links problem. The effectiveness of both the constrained boundary solution algorithm and the optimal efficiency online planning algorithm is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Two-phrase Optimization Based on Dijkstra and Artificial Potential Field Algorithms for Autonomous Vehicle Routing Problem
abstract: Path planning is one of the key technologies in autonomous driving. This paper attempts to combine global and local path planning by proposing the D&APF algorithm, which is based on Dijkstra's algorithm and the Artificial Potential Field method. This algorithm ensures both the safety and comfort of vehicle driving while achieving optimality and smoothness in path selection. Initially, the algorithm extracts nodes and their mutual distances from urban road data, employing Dijkstra's algorithm to select the optimal global path. Then, as the vehicle travels along the path, D&APF constructs a potential field based on real-time road obstacle conditions and employs an improved Artificial Potential Field method for local path planning. Meanwhile, D&APF optimized the attractive and repulsive forces for vehicles, overcoming the failures of traditional Artificial Potential Field methods in specific situations. The paper presents simulation experiments and algorithm comparison on local path planning, with results demonstrating that D&APF can achieve safety and smoothness in path planning along with obstacle avoidance, contributing to the research in the field of autonomous driving.

articleTitle: Research on Flexible Job Shop Scheduling based on an Improved Dung Beetle Optimization Algorithm
abstract: To tackle the challenges of job delivery times with buffer periods in actual orders, this study proposes an optimization strategy based on job weights, aimed at minimizing delivery times.A novel method has been developed for the conversion of job weights, which integrates the urgency associated with job delivery deadlines. This approach prioritizes the optimization of optional machine scheduling and the coordination of multi-process arrangements to mitigate waiting times in buffer zones. An Improved dung beetle optimization algorithm is designed specifically for the flexible job shop scheduling problem, targeting the minimization of delivery times. This approach utilizes a hybrid population initialization strategy to generate a high-quality initial population and incorporates a multipoint mutation strategy to enhance the diversity of transitions between individual positions and scheduling solutions, thereby improving accuracy in identifying optimal solutions. Additionally, a spiral search strategy is integrated to bolster local search capabilities. Comparative tests demonstrate that the improved algorithm significantly enhances both solving speed and accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on LiDAR Multi-Target Tracking Method Based on BEV Perspective
abstract: Multi-target tracking is one of the core technologies of perception in autonomous driving, but the current multi-target tracking related work has been carried out in the three-dimensional coordinate system, and the research direction of BEV perception is becoming more and more popular, and multi-target tracking from the perspective of BEV has gradually been paid attention to, so we use an improved JPDA algorithm from the perspective of BEV, use this algorithm to correlate the detection results of lidar and multi-target tracking, and add the multi-target tracking framework of Deepsort, and finally use the KITTI evaluation tool to evaluate the performance, and compare it with the three-dimensional point cloud tracking algorithms AB3DMOT, The results show that compared with the algorithm, the performance indicators are improved, and the tracking performance can still be good in the case of occlusion false detection, and the calculation speed is increased by more than 15% compared with the traditional JPDA algorithm under the same conditions.

articleTitle: A Novel Time-Driven Multiple Modes Division Based NCA Method for the AHU System Fault Detection
abstract: Fault detection is crucial for air handling unit (AHU) system's safe operation. The AHU operation represents a unique process with time-wise multiple mode characteristics and highly nonlinear characteristics. To address these challenges, a novel time-driven multiple modes division based neural component analysis (MNCA) method for the AHU system fault detection is proposed in our work. To figure out the time-wise multiple mode characteristics of the AHU system, the time-driven based multiple modes division method is adopted to precisely divide the entire process dataset into multiple operating modes along the time axis. To address the highly nonlinear and boost the efficiency of the fault detection, neural component analysis (NCA) fault detection models are established for each operating mode to nonlinearly extract the features with orthogonal properties. The effectiveness of the presented method is confirmed by results from the ASHRAE Research Project RP-1312 experimental datasets.

articleTitle: Sea Clutter Prediction Model Based On ICOA-ELM
abstract: To effectively detect targets in sea clutter, accurate prediction of sea clutter is particularly important. To this end, this paper proposes a sea clutter prediction model based on the Extreme Learning Machine (ELM)network optimized by the improved Crayfish Optimization Algorithm (COA). Firstly, because sea clutter has chaotic characteristics, the phase space reconstruction of sea clutter data is carried out, and the reconstructed data are input to the ELM network; secondly, the COA algorithm is improved to enhance its optimization searching ability, and the weight of the ELM network are optimized by using this algorithm; finally, the optimized ELM network is used to predict the sea clutter. From the experimental results, it is easy to find that compared with several other prediction models, the ICOA-ELM network has a higher prediction accuracy, which provides a new way to predict sea clutter effectively.

articleTitle: Design of Cruise Ship Engine Room Ventilation System Based on Asymmetric Variable Universe Fuzzy Control
abstract: There is a lot of residual heat and exhaust gases emitted as numerous heating devices work in the cruise ship engine rooms. It is necessary to design the cruise ship engine room ventilation system so that the devices and personnel can work normally. The main research contents of this paper are: (1) The computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation model of the cruise ship engine rooms is established according to the ship information. Simulation data can be obtained by this model. (2) Comparing multiple system identification methods, the differential evolutionary identification algorithm is determined to be the most suitable algorithm for the engine environment and then a more accurate model of the control object can be obtained. (3) The domain, membership function and fuzzy rules of asymmetric variable universe fuzzy control are designed. Compared with various control methods, asymmetric variable universe fuzzy has obvious advantages in tracking and reducing overshoot.

articleTitle: Consensus Analysis of the Leader-Follower Opinion Dynamics Model with Group Pressure
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel leader-follower opinion dynamics model with group pressure on the basis of the HK model. Different from most existing papers, we introduce both group pressure and opinion leaders into the model to examine the impact on opinion evolution within a social network. Then, by utilizing matrix theory and properties of scrambling matrices, we theoretically prove that all agents' opinions can achieve consensus. Finally, the results of this paper are verified by simulations and experiments. The results indicate that group pressure facilitates the formation of opinion consensus. It takes less time for opinions to reach consensus when the level of group pressure increases. Furthermore, opinion leaders significantly impact the evolution of followers' opinions, effectively guiding their formation in the leader-follower model. This novel model elucidates the “celebrity effect”.

articleTitle: Multi-Level Feature Extraction Point Cloud Registration Model Based on Cross-Attention Matrix
abstract: Three-dimensional point cloud technology is essential for intelligent robots, autonomous driving, and human-computer interaction. Due to the self-occlusion issue, a single scan cannot acquire complete point cloud data, requiring the integration of point cloud data scanned from different directions through rotational and translational transformations. For partial overlap point cloud registration, not every point in the source point cloud can find a corresponding relationship in the target point cloud, posing significant challenges and complexity to point cloud registration. This paper proposes a point cloud registration model based on multi-level feature extraction using a cross-attention matrix to address the issue of partial overlap in point cloud registration. The cross-attention matrix is introduced within the feature extraction network to mix contextual information between layers, seeking correspondences in the overlapping areas and optimizing the construction of matching features. To enhance the internal dependencies within the point cloud and maintain internal associations, a Transformer encoder is proposed to follow the graph convolution in each layer, and a complete Transformer is added after the final feature extraction to integrate overall feature contextual information, which can suppress the impact of noise on the registration effect. Experimental results show that on the ModelNet40 dataset, compared to other network models, the proposed model achieves higher precision in point cloud registration.

articleTitle: Architecture Selection Method Based on Densely Connected Neural Architecture Search
abstract: Designing the network structure in deep learning is time-consuming and trial-and-error. The purpose of neural architecture search is to let the machine search for a suitable network structure by itself. Currently, neural architecture search relaxes the search space to a continuous differentiable space, so we can use stochastic gradient descent for optimization. It significantly reduces the search time and dramatically improves the application value of neural architecture search. A densely connected neural architecture search is an improvement in neural architecture search. The input of each layer of its network consists of the outputs of all the layers before it. Moreover, the results of each layer of the network will be the output to all subsequent layers. Therefore, it can search out the subnet structure with better performance. We propose improvements to the densely connected neural architecture search algorithm, addressing the deficiencies in architecture selection and search strategies. We verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm through experiments.

articleTitle: State-Feedback Stabilization of Output-Constrained High-Order Nonlinear Feedforward Systems
abstract: In this paper, the state-feedback stabilization of high-order nonlinear feedforward systems with an asymmetric output constraint is investigated. By constructing scaling gain-based fractional nonlinear mappings, the sign function, a crucial coordinate transformation and integral Lyapunov functions, in-troducing adding a power integrator technique and a novel anal-ysis method, a continuous state-feedback controller is designed to eliminate the effects caused by upper-triangular nonlinearities and high powers. The performances of the closed-loop system can be proved, and the effectiveness of the control scheme can be demonstrated by a simulation example.

articleTitle: Observer-Based Adaptive Exponential Tracking of Port - Hamiltonian Systems via Contraction Method
abstract: This article proposes an observer-based adaptive exponential tracking control scheme for port-Hamiltonian systems (PHS) involving parameter uncertainty based on contraction method (CM). First, an exponential adaptive observer with Hamiltonian structure for uncertain generalized PHS is given based on the idea of augment plus feedback. Compared with the conventional observer design method, the proposed observer can maintain the structure of original system and simultaneously guarantees the completeness of the state's physical significance. Then, based on designed observer, we proposed an adaptive tracking control strategy by using the structure properties of the PHS and CM. Moreover, an analysis is provided of the relevant decay rate and how parameters affect tracking speed of system. Ultimately, simulation results demonstrated the effectiveness of proposed method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Variational Mode Decomposition for Bearing Fault Diagnosis
abstract: Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) can break down a signal into its intrinsic modes based on the frequency characteristics of the signal, but it suffers from the problem that the decomposition results are affected by preset parameters. This paper proposes an Adaptive Variational Mode Decomposition for Bearing Fault Diagnosis (EO-VMD) to solve the problem. Firstly, to achieve adaptability, composite evaluation index (CEI) is constructed to quantify the performance of different parameter combinations. Secondly, the EO uses the CEI as its fitness function to iteratively find the best solution for the Volume Mass Balance model as the best set of parameters for the VMD. To verify the adaptability and decomposition accuracy, a simulated signal and the Case Western Reserve University bearing fault dataset are tested and compared with Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD) and Genetic Algorithm-based VMD (GA-VMD). The results suggest that the EO-VMD algorithm can better extract the signal's effective components by adaptively selecting the number of modes and penalty parameters.

articleTitle: Finite Time Stability Analysis of Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Polynomial Positive Systems Based on Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Lyapunov Function
abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of finite time stabilization of interval type-2 (IT2) fuzzy polynomial positive systems. Stability analysis using interval type 2 (IT2) fuzzy co-positive Lyapunov function (FCLF) is performed to obtain stability and positivity conditions. Although the above IT2 FCLF can bring more relaxed effectiveness, it also will cause the non-convex problem more complicated. Hence, Converting non-convex conditions into convex conditions is the key to successfully design a controller. To achieve this goal, design of feedback control gain using matrix decomposition technique. Besides, the obtained results are very conservative if we ignore the information about the membership functions. In order to reduce the conservatism, the basic stability condition is relaxed by introducing the property that the sum of the derivatives of the membership functions(DMF) is zero, which can effectively enhance the relaxation of the analysis results. Finally, a sample simulation verifies the validity of the method.

articleTitle: Research on the Self-Powered Flexible Non-Contact Distance/Contact Pressure Dual-Mode Sensor for Manipulator Based on Triboelectric Nanogenerator
abstract: As industrial intelligence advances and the value of intelligent manipulators in numerous application domains grows, so do the demand for intelligent manipulator sensing systems. In this study, we propose a novel flexible dual-mode sensor (DP-TENG) based on a triboelectric nanogenerator that can sense contact pressure and target distance and may be used to precisely manipulate and grab intelligent manipulators. The DP-TENG is made up of a triboelectric layer made of MXene/Ecoflex nanocomposite and a liquid electrode made of carbon nanotube dispersion. It has outstanding charge storage performance. The gadget can detect the distance between it and its target within 15 cm, identify the contact force with the target within 16 N, and is exceptionally durable and stable. As a result, this flexible dual-mode sensor we propose will show a wide range of possibilities in the future in the practical application of intelligent manipulators.

articleTitle: Secondary Frequency Regulation Strategy for Energy Storage System Based on Expert Knowledge Guided DDPG
abstract: Traditional control methods find it difficult to effectively coordinate multiple frequency regulation resources to cope with the stochastic fluctuation problem caused by intermittent energy sources such as wind power and photovoltaic power generation connected to the grid. Therefore, this paper proposes a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) load frequency control algorithm based on expert knowledge guidance. Firstly, a system frequency response model including battery storage is constructed and the output control law of the energy storage system is designed. Then, the definitions of the state set, the action set and the reward function of a DDPG agent are given, the, and the framework of the DDPG algorithm based on expert knowledge guidance is designed. Lastly, the simulation results demonstrate that compared to PI control and conventional DDPG control, the control method suggested in this study has faster convergence, stronger frequency regulation performance, and better SOC maintenance.

articleTitle: An Optical Path Tracking Control Method for Robots Based on Laser Sensing
abstract: As technology advances, lasers play a crucial role in cutting-edge fields such as surveying, communication, and non-destructive testing. Nevertheless, the challenge of optical path deviation persists as a formidable hurdle during applications, necessitating prompt optical path tracking. To address this, this paper presents a novel approach: An optical path tracking control method for robots based on laser sensing, engineered to swiftly rectify laser optical path misalignments. Initially, a laser tracking control system anchored on a manipulator is devised and constructed, emulating real-world scenarios encountered in practical applications. Subsequently, the optical path reflection relationships of the system are scrutinized, employing laser sensing and PID control algorithms to maneuver the robotic arm for precise optical path tracking in both reflection and occlusion scenarios. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted to verify the performance of the system under low angular velocity conditions. The experimental results indicate that the system can quickly track optical path deviations at an angular velocity of 2 rad/s, with tracking errors controlled within approximately 0.2 mm. This performance meets the tracking requirements for various application scenarios in industrial production and aerospace.

articleTitle: A Configurable Architecture Design for Autonomous Flight Software
abstract: Some satellites are designed to be capable of autonomous flight in order to be intelligent. However, many autonomous flight events need to be designed because of the complexity of satellite system, which brings heavy software development workload. A configurable software development method is proposed in this paper, which designs the general process of autonomous flight events execution and the configurable sequence of sub-event execution. This method simplifies the software development logic and significantly improves the development efficiency of autonomous flight events. At the same time, if the autonomous flight events need to be modified on-board, this method simplifies the on-board maintenance by only modifying the configurable sub-event execution sequences.

articleTitle: Research on Pole Placement Control Based on EKF Missile Parameter Identification
abstract: This paper explores a method for accurately identifying the longitudinal characteristic parameters of a missile using an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) in the missile guidance system, followed by the application of a pole placement algorithm to optimize the control system. Firstly, the EKF algorithm eliminates observation and system noise to provide high-precision estimation and filtering of the missile's longitudinal motion states (such as position, velocity, and acceleration), thereby accurately understanding the current state of the missile. Subsequently, the pole placement algorithm adjusts the controller parameters according to the desired system dynamic characteristics, optimizing system stability and dynamic performance. This method achieved a remarkable improvement in the missile guidance system's performance, achieving a relative identification error of less than 4%, while ensuring the overload has a rapid rise time without overshoot.

articleTitle: System Summarization Based on Multimodal Language Model with Attention-Weighted Fusion
abstract: Power system briefings allow grid dispatchers to quickly understand the operating status of the power system and provide decision support, therefore the generation of power system briefings is of great importance to the stable operation of the power system. Although existing summary generation studies have made some progress, most of them have not focused on the power system domain, especially the utilization of visual information is insufficient. In order to fully utilize the multimodal information in power system, we propose a new multimodal summary generation model based on attention-weighted fusion in conjunction with BART pre-trained language model. In order to overcome the problem of scarcity of multimodal datasets in the power system domain, the power system briefing generation model is trained using a transfer learning approach, and the structure of forgetting gates is introduced to better capture the visual features. Extensive experiments and comparisons with state-of-the-art methods on multimodal datasets of power systems have validated the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Fault-Tolerant Control Method for the Quasi-Z-Source Hybrid Active Neutral-Point-Clamped Three-Level Inverter with Reduced Power Losses
abstract: Semiconductor device fault is one of the main fault types of power electronic converter, which leads to output current distortion and degrades the system performance. In this paper, an improved fault-tolerant control (FTC) method is proposed for the quasi-Z-source (QZS) hybrid active neutral-point-clamped (HANPC) three-level inverter. When the open-circuit fault (OCF) of semiconductor devices <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{a2}$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{a3}$</tex> occurs, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\mathrm{O}_{-}]$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[\mathbf{O}_{+}]$</tex> state cannot be obtained, and the modulation strategy can be changed to restore normal operation. Specifically, the space vector diagram (SVD) is divided into normal half-cycle and abnormal half-cycle. During the normal half period, the upper shoot-through (UST) and lower shoot-through (LST) states are utilized to achieve the boost function. Meanwhile, the full shoot-through (FST) state is employed in the abnormal half period. Based on the principle, Si IGBTs can maintain high-frequency switching action for only one-sixth of each switching cycle. Compared with the conventional FTC methods, the power losses by the FTC method are reduced by about 20% and 45% in non-boost and boost modes, respectively. Simulation results and power losses analysis are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of Control System for Four-Wheel Steering Omnidirectional Mobile Forklift
abstract: Forklifts play an increasingly critical role in modern logistics and transportation. This paper designs a control system for four-wheel steering omnidirectional mobile forklift. The system integrates the electrical system, control system, drive system, sensor system and human-computer interaction system, and designs a variety of assisted driving algorithms. Through software and hardware design, the control system of the four-wheel steering omnidirectional forklift is finally realized. After testing, all functions are normal, overcoming the shortcomings of traditional forklifts such as poor mobility and low work efficiency in narrow spaces, and achieving the expected goals.

articleTitle: Optimization of Wide-Baseline Stereo Matching Based on Multi-View Geometry
abstract: Stereo vision plays a crucial role in scientific expeditions and facility maintenance. However, fixed-baseline stereo vision lacks accuracy for long-distance measurements, while wide-baseline stereo vision encounters occlusion issues at short distances. In this study, a wide-baseline stereo matching based on multi-view geometric constraints is proposed. Initially, the camera poses of multiple wide-baseline images are estimated, followed by image rectification and depth estimation. Subsequently, the disparity searching is constrained using geometric relationships among the views, resulting in more precise depth maps. Experiments were conducted to verify the superiority of the proposed method. The results indicate that the proposed method achieves an RMSE as low as 0.15 meters, even with invalid depth points. Compared to traditional stereo vision methods, accuracy is improved by approximately 35%, and robustness is significantly enhanced. In the aircraft runway scenario, overall depth map accuracy is higher, and occluded areas are significantly reduced.

articleTitle: Learning-Based Defense Against Prediction-Based Displacement Attacks on Formation Control
abstract: Formation control is a widely performed task in multi-agent systems. However, agents under formation control are susceptible to attacks, and how to defend against the attack is important for system security. This paper aims to design a new method to protect the system from prediction-based displacement attack, which predicts the movement of agents, diverts them from their original tracks and drives them to a preset trap. The defense is challenging due to the robustness of the attacker's prediction mechanism. Also, undermining the attack can be costly and harm the system's performance. To address this issue, we first build obstacle-avoidance and formation control models of the holonomic and non-holonomic agents and specify the prediction-based attacks to limit the cases where the defense strategy can be effective. Then, we propose a learning-based defense strategy, which learns the prediction mechanism of the attackers. It modifies the control input based on self-adaptive fuzzy methods to reduce prediction accuracy and guarantee that the agents can reach the goal. Simulation results demonstrate that our method is better than the previous noise-based one at reducing the accuracy of the attacker's prediction.

articleTitle: GMM Weighted Pinball Loss Twin Support Vector Machine
abstract: General twin support vector machine with pinball loss function uses pinball loss function which produce noise insensitivity and resampling stability. However, Pin-GTSVM gives same weights to each sample points, including outliers, and outliers will disturb the generation of classification planes. To reduce this disturbance, we propose a weighted version of Pin-GTSVM called GMM weighted pinball twin support vector machine (Pin-GWTSVM). The weight matrix is introduced into the objective equation by Gaussian mixture model to reduce the interference of outliers, and additional regular terms are introduced to prevent overfitting based on the principle of structural risk minimization. Numerical experiments on several UCI benchmark datasets show that the proposed Pin-GWTSVM has better classification accuracy and generalization ability than Pin-SVM, TSVM and Pin-GTSVM.

articleTitle: A Knowledge-and-Data-Driven Modeling Approach for Mobile Payment Mode Recognition
abstract: Identifying different mobile payment modes based on cell phone signaling data in user movement is crucial for mobile payment scenario planning, payment risk assessment, and analyzing payment behavior patterns across multiple users. This paper proposes a novel knowledge-and-data-driven modeling approach to optimize the use of signaling data for mobile payment mode recognition. The approach integrates both unparsed signaling data and domain-specific URL- Key knowledge extracted from parsed signaling data that contains payment-related information. First, we develop a data-driven model for mobile payment event recognition, leveraging cell phone signaling data. Next, we establish a knowledge-driven model that utilizes domain URL- Key knowledge to identify mobile payment modes during user movement. These two models are then integrated using a composite coupling operator, and real data from a mobile telecommunication company located in Chongqing are used to calibrate and test our approach. Experimental results show that our approach significantly enhances both performance and efficiency.

articleTitle: Cross Attention Fusion Transformer Network for Urban Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
abstract: Urban remote sensing image segmentation algorithms have advanced significantly, but they still encounter challenges such as large scale variations, intra-class heterogeneity, inter-class homogeneity, and unbalanced foreground and background regions. In this paper, we propose a multi-scale feature mapping fusion based on transformer and CNN network for remote sensing image segmentation, called Cross Attention Fusion Transformer Network (CAFTNet). We adopt Swin Transformer-Base as an encoder to fuse the encoded features and decoded features by developing a cross-attention feature mapping fusion module to align the feature information for better modeling representation. In the decoder, we design an efficient convolution module to decode the fused features. We hope to obtain better segmentation results by unifying the spatial information of multi-scale features while reducing the semantic differences. The proposed method is conducted on two urban remote sensing datasets, including ISPRS Vaihingen and ISPRS Potsdam. Specifically, our method achieves 87.8% and 85.1 % mIoU on ISPRS Vaihingen and Potsdam datasets, respectively.

articleTitle: Self-Cutting T-LCL/LCC Constant-Current Constant-Voltage Wireless Power Transmission System
abstract: Due to its excellent power levels and efficiency characteristics over medium to short distances and a wide power range, Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) systems have become a primary research focus in the field of wireless energy transmission. The constant current/constant voltage output features of WPT systems are increasingly crucial in applications such as electric vehicles (EVs) and LED lighting. Most compensation networks in WPT systems are high-order resonance circuits. Within high-order resonance networks, various resonance network structures exist to achieve voltage and current outputs independent of the load. Analyzing these resonance network structures is crucial for achieving efficient constant voltage/constant current modes independent of the load. Addressing the charging characteristics of lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles, which involve constant current followed by constant voltage charging, this paper proposes a control method utilizing the T-LCL/LCC compensation network configuration to achieve constant current and constant voltage outputs at the same frequency in WPT systems. By employing a generic high-order resonance network modeling approach, simultaneous characteristics of voltage and current transfer independent of the load can be obtained. Furthermore, the study analyzes whether the system can operate at low power consumption after the receiver is open-circuited or short-circuited and after the charging process is complete.

articleTitle: Research on Transformer Nameplate Rivet Recognition Based on Improved RT-DETR
abstract: To solve the difficulties of heavy effort and low efficiency in traditional manual collecting of transformer nameplate information, a transformer nameplate rivet target detection algorithm based on improved RT-DETR is proposed. This algorithm utilizes Partial Convolution (PConv) to replace some conventional convolutions, enabling feature extraction from only selected channels of the feature map, thereby reducing computational redundancy. Additionally, structural re-parameterization techniques are introduced to perform multi-branch training and single-path inference on the feature map, further decreasing computational costs. To solve the problem of tiny objects' poor detection accuracy, a novel feature fusion network architecture, ASF-DETR, is introduced. According to experimental data, the enhanced approach reduces the number of Calculation and parameter quantity by 16.9% and 27.5%, respectively, while increasing detection accuracy by 1.4% when compared to the original DT-DETR model. This improvement ensures real-time performance while effectively enhancing detection accuracy and meeting the lightweight requirements for field deployment.

articleTitle: Pointer Meter Reading Under Noise Based on Virtual Data Generation
abstract: Using machine vision for meter reading significantly enhances the efficiency of industrial monitoring. However, meters in outdoor environment are often subject to the noise such as rain and fog, which affect the accuracy of meter readings. Additionally, the meter images and labels under noise are hard to obtain. To address these challenges, We propose a method for pointer meter reading under noise based on virtual data generation. Firstly, We utilize Unity to construct an industrial meter scene, which generates the images of meter under noise and theri labels. Secondly, we develop a U-Net network with an ASPP module, which expands the receptive field of network and enhances the ability of segmentation network to capture global semantic information under noise. Finally, the angular method is used to calculate the meter readings. Experimental results show that this method can effectively read meters under noise in outdoor environments.

articleTitle: MSSNet: LiDAR-Camera Extrinsic Calibration Based on Multi-Modal Semantic Similarity
abstract: LiDAR-camera extrinsic calibration plays a crucial role in multi-modal fusion perception and autonomous driving. Existing methods relying on specific calibration targets are time-consuming and unsuitable for online calibration. A LiDAR-camera extrinsic calibration method utilizing multi-modal semantic similarity (MSSNet) from point clouds and images is proposed in this paper. In particular, correlation volume which is updated with an optical flow estimate module is used to compute the similarity between images and point clouds using the multi-modal semantic information as input. Next, the final updated correlation volume is used to regress the calibration parameters. We present qualitative and quantitative analysis of experimental results on the KITTI odometry dataset, demonstrating the effectiveness of our method for LiDAR-camera extrinsic calibration. Our code will be available at: https://github.com/BUCT-IUSRC/Research__MSSNet.

articleTitle: Requirements of Power Grid Situation Cognition and Resilience Assessment in Extreme Scenarios
abstract: The increase in the number of regulators brings about the problem of high dimensional random variables to the cognition of power network operation state. The input parameter structure and data processing flow of the traditional model are clear and demanding, and the final analysis results are strongly dependent on the institutional model, which does not have the characteristics of model-free and adaptive, and it is difficult to deal with unstructured data or defective data. Through high-dimensional statistical analysis and artificial intelligence technology, the power grid operation state is finely simulated and predicted to improve the power system's adaptability to distributed resource fluctuations, promote the large-scale consumption of distributed new energy, and ensure the stable, reliable and economic operation of the power grid. Through the high dimensional statistical analysis, the high dimensional spatiotemporal big data with low information density is compressed into the low dimensional situation feature with high information density. For extreme scenarios and random fluctuations of massive flexible resources, specific signal tracking/analysis is carried out by adjusting test functions and control hyperparameters to realize specific event cognition, and quantitative assessment of power grid risk and its resilience..

articleTitle: Analysis on Orbit Defense and Control Strategy of USA Advanced Extremely High Frequency (AEHF) Satellite System
abstract: Advanced Extremely High Frequency (AEHF) is a new generation of strategic military satellite communication system of the United States. In order to meet the survivable, assured and crucial communication requirements during various levels of military conflict, the AEHF satellites are designed to work in the geosynchronous orbits with small inclinations, and take a series of strategies such as orbit plane isolation and orbit maneuver to improve the security defense capability of the satellite system. In this paper, the orbit defense and control strategy of the AEHF satellite system is analyzed according to Two-Line Element (TLE) published by North American Aerospace Defense Command (NORAD). Firstly, the AEHF satellites and their propulsion system configurations are introduced. Then, the TLE data format and the theoretical model of orbit analysis are presented. The orbit defense and control strategy of the AEHF satellite system is analyzed in detail, including inclination control, orbit plane isolation and orbit maneuver. Finally, the analysis conclusions of orbit defense and control strategy are summarized and the preliminary suggestions are provided for the construction of relevant systems in China.

articleTitle: ORB-SLAM3 Front-End Acceleration System Based on ZYNQ Platform
abstract: ORB-SLAM3, as a highly robust real-time positioning algorithm, can further enhance the platform's perception of the environment. However, when deployed on small embedded platforms, there are limitations in size, weight, and power, which face the problem of insufficient computing power of embedded platforms to serve SLAM algorithms in real-time. Therefore, this paper is based on the ZYNQ platform to accelerate the most time-consuming feature extraction in the ORB-SLAM3 front-end, in order to achieve real-time positioning of small embedded platforms. Specifically, the AR0144 binocular camera module is used to collect 640*400 color images in real time, which are converted into grayscale and sent to the FPGA acceleration module to obtain homogenized feature points. After verification, the FPGA acceleration algorithm has a relatively small loss of accuracy, with an average error of about 3.6mm compared to the trajectory running on the PC. Meanwhile, our work achieves a certain balance between running speed and power consumption compared to PC platforms and ZYNQ ARM.

articleTitle: Adaptive Path-Optimal High-Precision Rapid Maneuver Control Technology for Optical Imaging Satellites
abstract: With the increasing deployment of high-precision optical remote sensing and observation satellites across scientific research and commercial sectors, there is a growing demand for flexible imaging modes, strong maneuverability, agility, and high-precision, stable attitude control capabilities. Complex control algorithms hinder rapid attitude maneuvers. To address the problem of rapid attitude maneuver control for satellites with multiple observation tasks, this paper proposes an adaptive path-optimal attitude maneuver control algorithm. This method autonomously plans the attitude maneuver path according to the angular momentum and torque constraints of the actuators. It not only meets complex pointing constraints but also features fast maneuvering speed, simple structure, clear physical meaning, and easily adjustable parameters. Mathematical simulation results show that this algorithm can effectively achieve large-angle rapid maneuvers of flexible spacecraft, suppress vibrations of flexible attachments, ensure smooth and steady maneuvering processes, and demonstrate good robustness and anti-interference capabilities.

articleTitle: A Short-Term Traffic Flow Forecasting Model Based on OOA-BP Neural Network
abstract: Short-term traffic flow forecasting is the key to alleviating traffic congestion. Accurately forecasting the traffic flow of a certain road section within a short time can greatly improve the traffic efficiency, so this paper constructs a traffic flow forecasting model based on the Osprey Optimization Algorithm (OOA) optimized BP neural network (BPNN). To prevent the disadvantages of the BPNN, such as the randomness of weights and thresholds, which leads to the consumption of a large amount of training resources and reduced prediction accuracy during the prediction process, this paper adopts the OOA to optimize the BPNN. This method has strong global search and local search capabilities and fast convergence speed. Since it can accelerate the training speed of the BPNN and effectively solve the problem of the prediction model being trapped in a local optimum, the optimal solution can be found within a relatively short time. The experimental results show that under the same data set, OOA-BPNN model outperforms BPNN model, particle swarm optimization (PSO), genetic algorithm (GA) and other optimization models in terms of mean absolute error (MAE) and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE).

articleTitle: Noncontact Multi-Modal Biological Recognition Based on Three-Dimensional Integrated Learning
abstract: Single biometric recognition has become one of the most popular and promising method for personal verification. However, further work to improve safety and reliability needs to be carried out. The work shows a novel solution to create non-contact multi-modal biological recognition because of its high security and fast matching performance, which can be used in electronic currency trading, blockchain and other scenarios. The three-dimensional image acquisition method is designed. Subsequently, multi-layer image quality evaluation, maximum ROI extraction and two image enhancement methods are proposed. Next, the algorithm based on three-dimensional CNN is designed to solve the optimization problem. Finally, “single-line parallel matching mode” is constructed. In the experiments, the proposed method shows that the leading performance on precision (99.92<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) and processing speed (within 3ms) in comparison with other processing methods of single biometric recognition. Experimental results show that this new design is effective and feasible.

articleTitle: Exploration of Key Variables That Trigger Intelligent Emergent Behavior in ICSoS
abstract: Intelligent emergence is a key characteristic that dis-tinguishes Intelligent Complex Systems of Systems (ICSoS) from complex systems, yet it has long lacked in-depth explanation. Focusing on exploring the triggering mechanisms of intelligent emergence in ICSoS, we innovatively propose related conceptual definitions and basic assumptions, concentrating on two key variables “Component Connectivity” and “Component Intelligence Level”. We reveal that within ICSoS, there are key factors similar to targets, which exert a ripple effect on overall system performance. Numerical simulation results show that components in ICSoS with high connectivity exhibit stronger information transmission and collaboration capabilities, enabling them to effectively adapt to and respond to changes in the external environment. In contrast, components with low connectivity face issues such as obstructed information transmission and inefficient collaboration, making it difficult to respond effectively in complex environments in a timely manner. Additionally, a high Component Intelligence Level indicates that components possess greater perception, decision-making, and execution abilities, al-lowing for more effective interaction and collaboration with other components. Conversely, a low Component Intelligence Level may lead to limitations and deficiencies in the ICSoS's ability to cope with complex environments and tasks. Furthermore, the experiments also reveal that a high Component Intelligence Level is typically accompanied by a pursuit of high Component Connectivity, tending to establish more connections with other components to achieve higher levels of information sharing and collaboration.

articleTitle: High-Precision Tracking Control of Parallel Robots Using the Superhelix Algorithm
abstract: The increasing demand for precision in industrial automation has amplified the importance of accurate control in parallel robots, particularly given their high nonlinearity, complex coupling, and sensitivity to environmental disturbances. This paper presents a trajectory tracking control strategy leveraging a super-helix algorithm and an adaptive integral terminal sliding mode controller, specifically designed to address the challenges posed by inertial forces, frequent acceleration shifts, and external perturbations in high-speed Delta parallel robots. By deriving a comprehensive dynamics model and integrating the convergence law with sliding mode and super-helix techniques, the proposed method significantly enhances system robustness and dynamic responsiveness. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared to traditional approaches, this method markedly improves trajectory tracking precision, disturbance resistance, and vibration suppression, enhancing system performance by up to 98.65%. This controller not only ensures high tracking accuracy but also holds considerable promise for practical industrial applications.

articleTitle: A Deep Nonnegative Matrix Factorization Approach for Industrial Fault Diagnosis
abstract: Data-driven fault diagnosis represents a significant challenge in the realm of intelligent industry safety management. In practice, industrial data often encompasses a blend of various physical attributes, including the operating environment and fault location. Traditional models may struggle to enhance diagnostic performance due to their shallow architectures. To overcome this problem, we introduce Deep Nonnegative Matrix Factorization (DNMF), which employs a series of matrix factors to preserve the desirable structure of the process data. Specifically, DNMF systematically decomposes data into multiple hierarchical levels, allowing for the extraction of implicit features of industrial data. Our experimental results demonstrate that the DNMF model outperforms both shallow and deep methods while also requiring less computational time compared to deep structures.

articleTitle: Evaluation Method of Distributed Photovoltaic Primary Frequency Modulation Capability
abstract: In this paper, an evaluation method of distributed photovoltaic primary frequency regulation capability is proposed, which aims to cope with the challenges of power system inertia reduction and frequency fluctuation after distributed photovoltaic grid connection. Firstly, the output prediction is carried out by using the long short-term memory neural network combined with the control parameters, meteorological factors and historical data of distributed photovoltaic. Then, an evaluation system including three first-level indicators of frequency modulation power, frequency modulation dead time and margin capacity is constructed, and the entropy weight method and TOPSIS method are used to quantitatively evaluate the primary frequency modulation capability of distributed photovoltaic. Through the simulation system verification, the results show that the method can effectively evaluate the primary frequency modulation ability of distributed photovoltaic, which has important reference value for practical application.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Polynomial Positive Fuzzy System Controllers Based on Markov Transitions
abstract: This study explores polynomial Markov positive fuzzy systems, formulating controllers for these systems by examining the prerequisites for positivity and stochastic stability. Initially, polynomials are incorporated into the Markov positive fuzzy system to represent nonlinear elements better and enhance its capacity to model nonlinear systems. Concurrently, the study discusses the non-convex scenarios encountered in the stability analysis of the closed-loop system once the positive fuzzy system controller is integrated and confirms the stability of the Markov polynomial positive fuzzy system. Ultimately, the effectiveness of the proposed approaches is demonstrated through a numerical simulation example.

articleTitle: Nonlinearity Identification of Main Steam Control Valves in Thermal Power Plants Subject to Dynamic Behavior Variations
abstract: Nonlinear characteristics of main steam control valves play an important role in the frequency control performance of thermal power plants. Manual testing has traditionally been relied upon to evaluate the nonlinear characteristics, but this method interferes with the normal operation of thermal power plants. This paper proposes a novel method to identify nonlinear characteristics of main steam control valves subject to dynamic behavior variations by special data segments hidden in historical data. The special data segments solely contain static information, separating static nonlinear characteristics from dynamic behavior variations. Compared with the Hammerstein model identification method, the proposed method can more accurately establish a model for the nonlinear characteristics of main steam control valves. Industrial case studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Dual Time Scale Weighted Recursive Least Squares for IPMSM Parameter Identification with Inverter Nonlinearity
abstract: This research paper delves into the realm of parameter identification for Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (IPMSMs), with a particular focus on the influence of inverter nonlinearity. A novel online parameter estimation approach is presented, integrating the dual time scale (DTS) methodology with the weighted recursive least squares (WRLS) algorithm. The DTS framework strategically partitions motor parameters into two groups, tailored to their inherent dynamic characteristics, thereby significantly reducing computational complexity while ensuring system stability. Within this framework, the WRLS algorithm, deployed during system steady-state conditions, mitigates the risk of convergence to local extrema by adaptively assigning weights to parameters based on their confidence levels suppressing the effects of noise. Furthermore, the modeling process meticulously accounts for often-neglected VSI nonlinearities, such as dead time, switching time, and IGBT voltage drop, thereby enhancing the accuracy of the estimation model. Extensive simulations are conducted, analyzing the impact of VSI nonlinearity compensation and evaluating the efficacy of the proposed DTS-WRLS method. The outcomes underscore the superior performance of the proposed approach in enhancing parameter identification accuracy and stability.

articleTitle: Delving into the Intricate Connection: Individual Perspectives and Bi-Virus Transmission
abstract: This paper examines the intricate interplay between individual perspectives and bi-virus transmission in a city or country. The model under consideration involves two competing viruses, where the transmission of these viruses is affected by individuals' perceptions of the epidemic, and the actual transmission of the viruses also influences those perceptions. Based on an opinion-dependent reproduction number, we conduct a thorough theoretical examination of the developed model, focusing on the stability of various equilibrium states.

articleTitle: Design and Control of Rope-driven Flexible Manipulator with Variable Stiffness
abstract: Because of its flexible structure, the flexible manipulator can carry out operations through small and complex Spaces, but its bearing capacity is often low, which greatly affects the accuracy of its operations. In this paper, a novel rope-driven flexible manipulator structure with variable stiffness(RDFM-VS) is proposed, which is adjusted by the tension of the rope against the cross-axis bending pivot(CAFP) in the modular joint. The kinematic analysis of the flexible manipulator is carried out, and the corresponding mathematical model is established. Then the mechanical analysis of CAFP is carried out, the variable stiffness mechanism is expounded, and the relationship between the tension of the rope and the stiffness of the flexible manipulator is obtained. Finally, the prototype of the flexible manipulator system is made, and the feasibility and effectiveness of the designed flexible manipulator with variable stiffness and its control system are verified by experiments.

articleTitle: Enhanced Stationary Trend Analysis for Monitoring Nonstationary Industrial Processes
abstract: In industrial process monitoring, nonstationary characteristics of data often lead to low fault detection rate in traditional monitoring methods, compromising the stability and safety of industrial production. Traditional methods like cointegration analysis and stationary subspace analysis (SSA) are widely used but tend to lose critical fault features and do not adequately highlight incipient fault features within the monitored stationary components, limiting their effectiveness. To address these issues, this paper proposes an enhanced stationary trend analysis (ESTA) algorithm. ESTA decomposes nonstationary data into nonstationary common trends and stationary components using a common trend model. Unlike SSA, ESTA uses the Wasserstein distance to transform the optimization function into a matrix trace form during the separation of the stationary subspace, avoiding the complexities of logarithmic terms and reducing computational costs while enhancing robustness. ESTA effectively separates nonstationary common trends within the system, allowing the stationary components to reflect the true dynamic relationships among system variables and retain more fault features. The effectiveness of the proposed monitoring method is validated through a numerical case.

articleTitle: Parity Space-Based Sensor Fault Detection for Traction Rectifier in High-Speed Train
abstract: The issue of parity space-based sensor fault detection is solved for traction rectifier of high-speed train, effectively decoupling the effects of unknown initial states and control inputs. Unlike most existing results, process noise and measurement noise are classified as unknown disturbances, which are considered in the mixed logical dynamic model of the rectifier. Subsequently, a linear discrete time-varying dynamic model of rectifier is acquired including unknown disturbances, which is used to implement the fault detection algorithm. The evaluation function calculation of parity space-based fault detection is transformed into solving the minimization of a positive definite quadratic form. By designing observer to construct a new parity relationship, the recursive operation of the residual evaluation function is implemented to reduce the online calculation cost. Finally, an innovation reorganization and singular value decomposition aided parity space algorithm is given, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by the simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Output Feedback Control for Networked Switched Systems Under Multiple Attacks with Dynamic Event-Triggered Approach
abstract: This paper mainly studies the security control of networked switched systems in smart grid under multiple attacks. To reduce unnecessary data transmission, two dynamic event-triggered generators are deployed in the sensor-controller (S-C) channel and controller-actuator (C-A) channel, respectively. In the concerned system, both S-C channel and C-A channel suffer from denial-of-service (DoS) attacks and replay attacks. In addition, a multiple attack model and an output feedback controller considering dynamic event trigger are constructed. Sufficient conditions to ensure the mean square exponential stable of networked switched systems are derived. Moreover, we provide the desired design method of observer-based output feedback controller. Finally, an example of switched system which includes two subsystems is utilized to demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed method.

articleTitle: Bi-Level Optimization of the Integrated Energy System with Flexible Thermoelectric Ratio Adjustment
abstract: This paper introduces an optimization scheduling model for integrated energy systems that incorporates flexible thermoelectric ratio adjustment to address issues such as limited regulation capacity and energy supply-demand mismatches found in traditional systems. By employing energy storage devices and supplementary combustion waste heat boilers, the thermoelectric ratio can be adjusted flexibly. Additionally, it introduces demand-side response based on time-of-use electricity pricing for optimization scheduling, implements optimization strategies through bi-level optimization, verifies the model's feasibility and practical value, and achieves cost savings of approximately 6.8255%. This paper holds significant theoretical importance in advancing the development of integrated energy systems and in alleviating pressure on power grids.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based Target Interception for USVs with Experimental Validation
abstract: Intercepting hostile targets in complex scenarios is a crucial task for unmanned surface vehicles (USVs). This paper proposes an interception algorithm based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and tests it in a real-world environment. This work establishes a DRL framework in a virtual environment based on the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG). A simplified state and a composite reward function are designed for the tasks involving multiple objectives, while the attacker is navigated using an artificial potential field (APF). The proposed policy shows an interception success rate of over 99% against evading attackers in the simulation environment. By constructing an interception hardware architecture based on Matlab and high-precision motion capture system, we transferred the policy from virtual to real environments. With the incorporation of randomly varied hydrodynamic parameters, the defender achieved rapid interception under complex disturbances. The interception and obstacle avoidance algorithm in this paper performs well in both simulation and real-world environments.

articleTitle: An Improved Variational Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Initial Center Frequency for Bearing Fault Feature Extraction
abstract: Variational mode decomposition (VMD) is extensively utilized in the field of industrial signal processing due to its superior anti-mixing and denoising capabilities. However, in practice, the performance of VMD is significantly influenced by the initial center frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega^{1}$</tex>. An improper setting of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega^{1}$</tex> can significantly reduce the stability of decomposition, resulting in the loss or masking of feature information by noise. To address the above issue, an improved VMD algorithm is proposed in this work. Our algorithm redefines <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega^{1}$</tex> based on the narrowband characteristics of intrinsic mode function (IMF). Under the new definition, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega^{1}$</tex> can be adaptively adjusted based on the signal spectrum processed by Wiener filtering. This adjustment significantly enhances the flexibility and anti-mixing performance of the original VMD. To validate our proposed method, comparative experiments were conducted using two sets of fault data from Case Western Reserve University (CWRU). The results demonstrate that our method is more effective and superior in extracting fault features.

articleTitle: 3D Guidance for Maneuvering Targets with Terminal Angle Constraints: An Incremental Nonsingular Terminal Sliding Mode Approach
abstract: In this paper, a three-dimensional guidance law is proposed against maneuvering targets with considering terminal angle constraints. First, dynamics of the line-of-sight (LOS) angle are derived, thereby facilitating the guidance law design. Second, a novel incremental nonsingular terminal sliding mode (INTSM) guidance law is designed by combining the incremental nonlinear dynamic inversion technique with the nonsingular terminal sliding mode (NTSM) control design. Different from the conventional NTSM guidance law, the effects of external disturbances caused by maneuvering targets are significantly reduced by employing the incremental control strategy, thus chattering can be suppressed. Finally, a series of simulation studies illustrate the superiority of the proposed INTSM guidance law.

articleTitle: LCTrack: Leveraging Convolutional Neural Network and Transformer for Visual Tracking
abstract: In recent years, with the support of Transformers' ability to integrate information from the target region and search region, the performance of relevant trackers has dynamically improved. However, these Transformers methods that capture global information about the tracking target often overlook local information, which significantly affects the performance of the corresponding trackers. To address this issue, we propose a novel tracking framework that uses both convolutional neural networks (CNN) and Transformers for visual tracking, called LCTracker. Our main contributions are as follows: 1) We integrate a new tracking framework that combines local information extraction from CNNs and global information extraction from Transformers; 2) We incorporate a multi-layer Transformer aggregation module; 3) We implement cross-attention between CNN feature maps and Transformer attention maps. Additionally, extensive experiments demonstrate that our LCTracker can effectively handle challenges such as fast motion, background clutter, and low resolution, showing significant advantages in these areas. Impressively, LCTracker achieved leading performance in three tracking benchmark tests and significantly outperformed SOTA results.

articleTitle: Robust Tracking Control of UPQC with Integrated Harmonic Estimation and Compensation: An Iterative Observer Approach
abstract: Due to the widespread use of renewable energy sources and non-linear loads in power electronics, the level of harmonic injection throughout the power system is showing a significant increase. In this context, the unified power quality conditioner (UPQC) has attracted much attention due to its excellent dynamic voltage restorer and active power filter functions. The UPQC is capable of effectively coping with a wide range of power quality problems including supply voltage dips, voltage fluctuations and flickers, voltage imbalances, harmonic currents and reactive currents. However, it is noted that most of the existing harmonic estimation methods for grid systems embedded with UPQC adopt the idea of multi-observer parallel estimation, which poses a challenge to the limited hardware computational and storage resources of the controller. For this reason, this study gives an efficient iterative observer method, which determines the harmonic order one by one in an iterative manner at each moment and gradually accumulates the estimators of the corresponding order. Based on this disposition, this paper designs a robust tracking controller with integrated harmonic estimation and compensation. Finally, simulation studies demonstrate that the propose method can accurately estimate the harmonics of the UPQC system and can significantly improve the efficiency of the harmonic estimation and compensation process.

articleTitle: Construction and Application of Virtual Light Scene for Solar Greenhouse Groups
abstract: A general framework was proposed in this study to promote the modernization and intelligent development of solar greenhouse production. The method defines a virtual lighting model composed of three basic functions: sensing, modeling, and application. Based on this universal framework for greenhouse light simulation, it can comprehensively cover various light environment, operating conditions, and planting scenarios. This study enables the quantification and visualization of the 3D spatial heterogeneity of light environments within greenhouse structures and crop canopies, providing scientific evidence for precise control in greenhouse planning, covering material selection, and optimization of planting strategies.

articleTitle: UAV Trajectory Planning for Wireless Data Acquisition: A Bernstein-Polynomial Approach
abstract: Wireless data acquisition, characterized by its flex-ibility and low cost, is optimized by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV s) due to their efficiency and versatility. In this paper, we propose a Bernstein-polynomial approach for the UAV wireless data acquisition problem. Firstly, we propose a trajectory gener-ation algorithm that can generate flight trajectory based on the UAV's take-off and landing points and the positions of the sensors. Secondly, we investigate the flight trajectory and communication performance to prove that the UAV wireless data acquisition system's maximum data transmission rate has a non-zero lower bound. Finally, the results from simulations indicate that the pro-posed trajectory planning approach can generate flight trajectory with shorter lengths and smoother curvatures than spline curves, and the theoretical analysis provides reasonable lower bound for the maximum data transmission rate.

articleTitle: A Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Multiple AGVs Scheduling in Automated Container Terminals
abstract: The equipment scheduling method of automated container terminals is gradually evolving towards intelligence and automation. In this paper, a novel multi-agent deep reinforcement learning algorithm called Coupling Deep Q-network (C-DQN) is proposed to address the automated guided vehicles (AGV) scheduling problem. Specifically, the sparse reward problem of the proposed algorithm model is solved by a mask. The convergence of the model is accelerated by changing the greedy rate with a fixed step size. The shape of samples in the experience replay buffer is also improved through the methods of the centralized training and decentralized execution. Furthermore, the scheduling conflict problem caused by the cooperative game is reduced, and the overall efficiency of the scheduling task is also improved. Finally, the scenario of multi-AGV scheduling is designed to verify the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed C-DQN algorithm.

articleTitle: MRF-SegFormer : A Magnetic Leakage Defect Segmentation Network Based on Segformer
abstract: Traditional segmentation networks have low Accuracy in segmenting defects in magnetic flux leakage images, and are prone to small defects being missed. This has a significant impact on evaluating the degree of defect harm using the results of magnetic flux leakage image defect segmentation. This article proposes a high-precision decoder based on cross feature fusion, which is more suitable for magnetic flux leakage defect detection, on the basis of the SegFormer network, to replace the traditional multi-layer perception (MLP) decoder. The experiment TA results show that the model increases the MIoU value of the traditional MLP decoder from 88.21% to 89.63% with a small number of additional parameters

articleTitle: KPNDepth: Depth Estimation of Lane Images Under Complex Rainy Environment
abstract: Recent advancements in deep neural networks have improved depth estimation in clear, daytime driving scenarios. However, existing methods struggle with rainy conditions due to rain streaks and fog, which distort depth estimation. This paper introduces a novel dual-layer convolutional kernel prediction network for lane depth estimation in rainy environments. It predicts two sets of kernels to mitigate depth loss and rain streak artifacts. To address the scarcity of real rainy lane data, an image synthesis algorithm, RCFLane, is presented, creating a synthetic dataset called RainKITTI. Experiments show the framework's effectiveness in complex rainy conditions.

articleTitle: The Design and Implementation of the Embedded Sleep Ecosystem
abstract: In recent years, sleep disorders have become a major stubborn illness affecting people's physical and mental health. Traditional treatment methods have problems such as single direction, low efficiency, and cumbersome processes. In response to this problem, this paper designs and develops a sleep ecosystem. This system combines traditional medicine with modern intelligent technology and conducts all-round and multi-faceted three-dimensional treatment for insomnia patients through 7.83Hz Schumann waves, fragrances containing sleep-aid drugs, 720nm red light, and the sounds of insects and birds. The sleep ecosystem is based on the single chip microcomputer, including the Schuman wave generator module, fragrance eruption module, 720nm red light module, sound module and other components, respectively from the electromagnetic wave, smell, vision, hearing and other aspects of human sleep intervention and treatment. Develop a mobile APP, which can send control commands such as switching, timing off, timing eruption, volume size and music selection to the sleep instrument. The practical application test shows that the system has achieved the expected function, can regulate the sleep atmosphere and improve the sleep quality.
