articleTitle: Transformer-Based Sequence Modeling with Action Discretization for Robotic Grasping
abstract: The powerful representational and sequential modeling capabilities of Transformer have been validated in various fields such as natural language processing. However, how to better address sequential decision-making problems like robotic grasping through the Transformer architecture and achieve autonomous control of robotic grasping remains a longstanding challenge. Models that directly output continuous decision actions for robotic arms often rely on mean squared error (MSE) loss for training, which is unable to effectively handle the randomness and diversity of actions. This limitation leads to the generation of relatively singular actions in certain grasping scenarios, reducing the success rate of grasping. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Transformer-based method for discretizing robotic arm actions, where actions are discretized by dimension to enable autoregressive modeling. Experimental results demonstrate that this method effectively improves the grasping performance of robotic arms in simulation environments.

articleTitle: Refinement Based on Contour Alignment for Monocular 6D Object Pose Estimation
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel refinement technique for object pose estimation. We perform the extraction of the Contour of Interest (CoI) from both the visible mask and the complete mask. Following this, we utilize both the Col and the contour rendered by the initial pose to optimize the pose. Our fundamental insight is that contour alignment serves as an essential criterion for accurately estimating the pose, while also facilitating the generation of gradients for pose optimization. Notably, our method diverges from the render-and-compare approach by solely requiring the rendering of the segmentation, without the need for training a new refinement network. This distinctive aspect eliminates the time-consuming nature associated with the refinement process. To validate the effectiveness of our proposed technique, we conduct a comprehensive evaluation on benchmark datasets, namely YCB-V and IC-BIN. The code can be found at https://github.com/lyltc1/ContourAlignment.

articleTitle: Modeling Markov Decision Process Elements Leveraging Language Models for Offline Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Offline multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has attracted considerable attention for its capability to learn distributed policies from offline datasets, eliminating the need for costly exploratory interactions or accurate environmental models. However, the absence of real-time interactions can result in inaccuracies when learning Markov Decision Process (MDP) elements, thereby affecting sample efficiency. Drawing inspiration from the relational learning capabilities of language models, we propose leveraging these models to implicitly capture MDP elements, such as global state representations. This paper introduces the state language model (SLM) framework, a sequence-to-sequence approach that implicitly learns global state representations from offline data. The SLM framework enables agents to infer global-like information by modeling implicit relationships between local observations and the global state, without relying on predefined communication protocols. A feedback mechanism further refines state predictions, ensuring both scalability and accuracy. Extensive experiments on offline MARL benchmarks demonstrate that SLM can be seamlessly integrated into existing algorithms, significantly enhancing their performance.

articleTitle: Asymptotic Observers for Nonlinear Feedforward Systems
abstract: In this paper, an approach is provided of asymptotic observer design problem for a kind of nonlinear feedforward systems. The nonlinear terms of the considered feedforward systems are with output dependent conditions. The observer is designed with high gain. The asymptotical stability of the error system is proved based on the Lyapunov stability theory.

articleTitle: Formation Control of a Group of Quadrotor Aircraft Based on Nash Equilibrium
abstract: In this paper, a control method based on Nash equilibrium is proposed for the formation control of a group of quadrotor aircraft. Firstly, the dynamics and kinematics models of the quadrotor aircraft are established. Then, according to the kinematics and dynamics model of the quadrotor aircraft, the decision variable of the quadrotor aircraft is selected and the objective function of the quadrotor aircraft is designed. By analyzing the objective function of quadrotor aircraft, the Nash equilibrium solution of multi-quadrotor aircraft system is obtained. Finally, the feasibility and superiority of the proposed control method are verified by simulation experiment and comparative test.

articleTitle: Long-Tailed Classification with Fused Latent Features and Contrast Learning
abstract: In the real world, datasets usually show a long-tailed distribution. This presents a challenge to learning a robust feature extractor. Therefore, many recent studies have introduced contrast learning to learn better representations, but direct transfer does not adapt well to long-tail scenarios, and traditional contrast learning methods do not make full use of the information between features in a batch. To solve this, we modeled class condition distribution using Gaussian Mixture distribution with class Prototypes and Batch data(GM-PB}, which is more suitable for long tail scenario and can boost the model performance. The generalization of GM-PB is proved by deducing the upper bound of the generalization error. Then we propose a feature aggregation method for KNN graphs constructed using logits. In this way, model can capture the relation-level information between features, and get more robust features of tail category. We did intensive experiment on common long-tailed datasets, and the results show that our proposed model is superior to recent methods.

articleTitle: Neural Network-Based Load Swing Angle Tracking Control for Underactuated Ship-Mounted Cranes
abstract: As a typical marine engineering equipment, ship-mounted crane systems play a crucial role in meeting the demands of maritime cargo transportation and other engineering operations. However, due to their underactuated characteristics and the uncertain marine environment, particularly the disturbances caused by waves and wind leading to continuous variations in the ship's roll angle, these systems face a series of control challenges. To address these issues, this paper proposes A sliding mode control approach leveraging neural networks to achieve stable tracking of the load swing angle with respect to the ship's roll angle. Specifically, a suitable sliding mode surface is designed to effectively control both the actuated and underactuated state variables. Concurrently, a neural network is constructed, and appropriate update rules are proposed to effectively compensate for the unmatched disturbances caused by wave-induced ship motions and the uncertainties in the ship-mounted crane system. Based on the proposed control method, the trolley can quickly reach its preset position, and the load swing angle can dynamically track the ship's roll angle, achieving load swing suppression in the global coordinate system. Through rigorous analysis using Lyapunov techniques, the asymptotic stability of the predefined sliding mode surface and state variables is theoretically proven. Finally, a series of simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and strong robustness of the proposed neural network-based sliding mode controller.

articleTitle: Short-term Trajectory Prediction of USV Based on Multi-source Data
abstract: In recent years, research on Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV) trajectory prediction has gained attention due to its potential to reduce voyage time and eliminate collision hazards in maritime transportation. Deep learning, particularly Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory Network (LSTM), has shown promise in this field. CNN is effective at extracting spatial features from time series data, while LSTM is adept at handling long-term dependencies. The combination of these models can enhance prediction efficiency and accuracy. This paper puts forward a data-driven deep learning approach to USV trajectory prediction, utilizing a CNN+LSTM model. Tests conducted with simulated unmanned vessel data from three trajectories revealed a reduction in RMSE errors by 60.08% and 37.15% in comparison to LSTM and CNN methods, respectively, which indicates that this model can fully consider the influence of external environmental factors on the system and verifies the effectiveness of the USV trajectory prediction model.

articleTitle: LSCC-Net: Convolutional Neural Network for Coated Corn Seed Variety Recognition
abstract: To achieve the recognition of coated corn seed varieties and address the issue of high complexity in deep learning models, which makes them difficult to adapt to hardware devices with limited computing power, this paper proposes a lightweight convolutional neural network method for recognizing coated corn seed varieties, named LSCC-Net. A dual-path structure DFE Block is proposed as the feature extraction module of LSCC-Net, enabling efficient extraction of feature information with a small number of parameters. Experimental results show that the LSCC-Net model achieves an accuracy of 97.9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> on the coated corn seed dataset with only 0.16M parameters. The LSCC-Net algorithm is characterized by its lightweight nature and high accuracy, making it suitable for deployment on hardware devices with limited computing power. It provides a theoretical foundation for the automated detection of corn seeds.

articleTitle: Composition of Cascading Failure in Physical Power System Triggered by Cyber-Attack
abstract: The interconnection between cyber and physical systems in power networks tightens the bond between the electrical grid and cyber systems. However, this integration also exposes cyber physical power systems to numerous threats. Therefore, it is essential to study the mechanisms behind cascading failures in these systems that can be caused by cyber-attack. This paper provides a comprehensive examination of the model that comprises both the physical power and the cyber systems within cyber physical power systems. Secondly, employing complex network theory, we construct the topo-logical structures of both the physical power system and the cyber system. Additionally, we introduce an enhanced traffic model tailored for the physical power system. Subsequently, our research into cascading failures within and between the physical and cyber systems, triggered by cyber-attack, leads us to propose a model for the evolution and spread of such failures. We also categorize the different types of failures that can occur within the physical power system.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Reconstruction of Potato Plants Based on Improved Neural Radiation Field Theory
abstract: Intelligent and reliable access to high-quality crop phenotypic big data, which can be achieved by three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction of crop plants, will greatly promote the research in digital breeding. However, efficient achievement of satisfactory accuracy in 3D construction has remained challenging. To address this, we developed a dataset preprocessing algorithm (referred to as Laplacian) as well as an efficient and effective 3D reconstruction algorithm (referred to as NGP). As a case study, the Laplacian algorithm was tested on video datasets sampled from potato plants. Results showed that 3D reconstruction algorithms including NGP as well as classical algorithm Colmap delivered higher PSNR (1.08%-1.62% increase) and SSIM (0.34%-0.74% increase) on optimized datasets than raw datasets, implying the effectiveness of the Laplacian algorithm. Comparing NGP and Colmap on the same (raw and optimized) datasets showed that NGP delivered significantly better in PSNR and SSIM. In the meanwhile, the tests showed that in terms of reconstruction speed, NGP reconstructs 10.2 times faster than Colmap when the number of iterations was set as 20000. The strategy proposed in this study provides a novel solution for achieving efficient, low-cost and high-precision 3D reconstruction of field crops, which paves the path for intelligent and reliable phenotyping.

articleTitle: Open Vocabulary SAR Object Detection with Denoising and Scaled Box Loss
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has important applications in military, geology and other fields due to its high resolution and all-day, all-weather operation. However, the inherent speckle noise of SAR images seriously restricts the effectiveness of detection algorithms. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an open vocabulary SAR object detection model that combines a denoising network and an open vocabulary detection model, named Denoise GroundingDINO (DGD). We add a denoising network AGSDNet before image encoder to remove speckle noise in SAR images and propose a new box loss function called Scaled SCA (SSCA) Loss to improve the model accuracy. Experimental results show that the DGD model has achieved excellent performance on the SSDD, HRSID and SARDet-lOOK (part) datasets, verifying the superior ability of the DGD model in the field of SAR object detection.

articleTitle: Lightweight Similar Object Detection Method Based on Improved RT-DETR
abstract: The lack of feature information in similar object detection tasks generally leads to high false detection rates and large model sizes. To deal with such an issue, in this paper, a lightweight similar detection (LS-DETR) model is proposed to enhance detection accuracy and maintain detection speed. It utilizes the lightweight network architecture generalized efficient layer aggregation network (ELAN) as the main feature extraction backbone network, ensuring high accuracy while maintaining network lightweightness and speed. Furthermore, by combining cross-stage partial (CSP) networks with diverse branch blocks (DBB) and introducing the ELAN, the DBB-CSP-ELAN module is constructed to enhance the network's multi-scale feature extraction capability and reduce model computation. Experimental results on a solid color puzzle dataset demonstrate that, compared to the original real-time detection transformer (RT-DETR) model, LS-DETR achieves an improvement of 4.7% in mAP, a reduction of 53.5% in flops, and a decrease of 53.1% in model size. Compared to other mainstream algorithms, the improved method exhibits significant advantages in terms of model accuracy, size, and computational complexity, meeting the requirements of lightweight similar object detection tasks.

articleTitle: Deep Koopman Embeddings for Unidirectional Phase-Resolved Wave Prediction
abstract: The phase-resolved wave prediction is of vital im-portance for improving safety in ocean engineering. However, it is a challenge for traditional physical methods to predict wave elevation accurately and efficiently at the same time. In this work, we develop a phase-resolved wave prediction model based on combined deep learning and the Koopman theory. The model can calculate in real-time while ensuring prediction accuracy. In addition, the model can predict wave elevation under the sea state 4, demonstrating certain generalization performance.

articleTitle: A Multilevel Deep Fusion Framework for FeO Content Prediction in Sintering Process
abstract: Iron ore sintering is a critical procedure in steel production, and the content of ferrous oxide (FeO) in the finished sinter directly reflects sintering quality. This key indicator is commonly obtained by data-driven soft sensor modeling technology. However, existing methods struggle to fully utilize the multisource and heterogeneous characteristics of the sintering dataset, and this may limit the improvement of FeO prediction accuracy. To address this issue, this paper proposes a multilevel deep fusion framework (MDFF) for detecting FeO content in the sintering process. This novel framework integrates a multilevel fusion of multisource heterogeneous data, i.e., data-level, feature-level, and decision-level. First, shallow features are extracted from images based on expert experience for data-level fusion. Then, multiscale encoding network and shared representation learning network are used for feature extraction and fusion. Finally, the prediction results of shared representations and modality-specific features are combined at the decision level to realize real-time sensing of FeO content. The proposed MDFF fully exploits the intrinsic correlations between multisource information at multiple levels, and experimental results on real sintering datasets further prove its accuracy and stability.

articleTitle: An Image Selection Strategy Based on Swin Transformer and CWT for Robotic Grinding Monitoring
abstract: This paper proposes an image selection strategy (ST-CISS) based on Swin Transformer (ST) and continuous wavelet transform (CWT), with the aim of efficiently screening out high-quality image datasets and providing high-quality samples for equipment wear detection during robot grinding. The method first generates multiple datasets through CWT transformation with different parameter combinations and records the corresponding transformation time. Subsequently, an image dataset quality evaluation index based on the correlation coefficient is proposed, and an ST model for robot grinding fault diagnosis is developed. Finally, the optimal image dataset is selected by considering the transformation time, quality evaluation index, and classification accuracy. The experimental results demonstrate that the ST-CISS method effectively selects high-quality datasets and provides efficient data processing and training methods for grinding robot fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Predefined Time Attitude Control for Quadrotor UAV with Output Constraints and Input Saturation
abstract: In this paper, we examine the predefined time flight control of a quadrotor UAV with output constraints and input saturation. The attitude tracking error of UAV is constrained by the tan-type barrier Lyapunov function. The undesirable effects of the saturated input limitations are addressed by introducing an auxiliary system. Then a predefined time tracking control strategy is designed and the stability of the scheme is analyzed. Eventually, the simulation results show the method allows the angular tracking error to converge to the specified range in a predefined time.

articleTitle: Research on Infrared Target Detection Technology Applied to Nighttime Scenarios
abstract: During nighttime driving, it is common to encounter situations where the headlights of oncoming vehicles are too bright, posing a challenge to the driver's vision and reaction time, thereby increasing the risk of traffic accidents. Infrared target detection technology, by capturing the thermal radiation of vehicles and pedestrians, provides an effective method to improve nighttime driving vision. In this paper, a new lightweight deep learning object detection network, YOLO-GC, is proposed. First, Constructing the necessary dataset for this study has addressed the issue of limited infrared datasets, providing a solid data foundation for the training and evaluation of the model. Second, the backbone model of YOLOv5, CSPDarknet53, was replaced with the GhostNet network, reducing the computational load and model size while maintaining high accuracy at lower computational complexity. Finally, an attention mechanism was introduced to focus on key areas of the image, specifically on regions with significant temperature changes in infrared images, enhancing the accuracy of object detection. Experimental results show that the improved network achieves a recognition accuracy of 94.2% for vehicles and pedestrians, an improvement of 3.9% compared to the original network.

articleTitle: Requirement and Practice of Supply Chain Information Monitoring and Operation Planning for Large Energy Enterprises
abstract: In recent years, with the accelerated innovation of Internet, big data, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, blockchain and other technologies, and increasingly integrated into the whole process of economic and social development and energy, the digital economy has developed rapidly, with a wide range of radiation and unprecedented influence, and is becoming a key force in reconstructing global factor resources and reshaping the global economic structure. Change the global competition pattern. In this context, it is urgent for energy enterprises to carry out innovation, efficiency and power changes. It is of great significance to promote the development of energy enterprises in the direction of integration, intelligence and efficiency based on information transformation and big data science and technology as a powerful means. The energy industry needs to change the development mode driven by extensive investment and high-density investment, continuously improve the synergy efficiency of total factor production, improve the ability of intelligent scheduling and risk perception, and realize the high-quality and rapid development of the whole industry. Under the background of digital transformation, the core business support of energy enterprises extends to the direction of integration and coordination, the operation mode changes from “planned scheduling” to “real-time scheduling”, and the management means changes from “online” to “intelligent” to ensure the integrated and high-quality operation of energy enterprises.

articleTitle: SDPS-M2CAN: Improving Predictive Performance of Photometric Stereo Networks on Broad Spectrum Reflective Surfaces with Minor Indentations or Bumps
abstract: Photometric stereo is a method used to estimate surface normals of objects, commonly employed in detecting surface defects on industrial products. To enhance the detection of surface features on smoother and more continuous industrial components, this study improves the learning-based photometric stereo approach, SDPS-Net, resulting in the model SDPS-M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>CAN. Firstly, we introduce the Multi-scale Channel Attention Module (MCAB) to optimize the extraction of photometric stereo features, allowing the model to effectively adaptively extract useful features across multiple scales. Secondly, in the upsampling network, we employ a multi-scale feature fusion strategy based on maxpooling to fully utilize photometric stereo features at different scales, thereby enhancing the prediction capability of surface normals. Finally, by incorporating the ResNet architecture to simplify the model training process and expanding the network channels, we further improve prediction accuracy. Quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate that our enhanced model outperforms the original SDPS-Net in predicting concave-convex areas and normals near edges of smooth and continuous broad-spectrum reflective materials, achieving more accurate overall normal predictions.

articleTitle: QVT-Based SysML v2 Model Version Difference Transformation
abstract: In order to address the issue of model version incompatibility in supporting the implementation of Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) with SysML v2, this paper first elucidates a feasible engineering modelling method based on the SysML v2 specification. Subsequently, leveraging model transformation concepts, a v2 model version conversion method based on the QVT Relations Language is proposed. Various potential compatibility scenarios and implementation paths are meticulously analysed. On this foundation, a design scheme for program modules ensuring version full transitivity is presented. Finally, the proposed methods and programs are validated through case studies involving version conversion under two different scenarios. The results indicate that the proposed approach effectively resolves SysML v2 model version compatibility issues arising from changes in syntax or semantic patterns.

articleTitle: Unmanned Forklift Path Planning Method Based on Improved Hybrid A* Algorithm
abstract: Unmanned forklifts are an important part of the current intelligent logistics system, and their path planning problems directly affect the efficiency and safety of the logistics system. This paper improves the hybrid A* algorithm for the path planning problem of single-wheel steering unmanned forklift. First, the path planning problem of a single-wheel steering unmanned forklift was modeled and its kinematic constraints were analyzed. Then, the basic mechanism of the hybrid A* algorithm was analyzed, and the map environment evaluation index was proposed, and the motion step size of the hybrid A* algorithm was improved accordingly. This allows the algorithm to have different movement steps under different obstacle densities, which enhances the algorithm's adaptability to the environment. Finally, the feasibility of the path generated by the improved hybrid A* algorithm was verified through simulation experiments, and multiple sets of tests proved that the improved algorithm significantly reduced the expansion nodes and improved the algorithm performance.

articleTitle: Extended H∞ Estimation Based Longitudinal Control of Vehicle Platoons with Disturbances
abstract: This study focuses on a longitudinal control method for vehicle platoon system with multiple disturbances, including matched lumped disturbance such as external disturbance and parameter inaccessible, as well as mismatched disturbance where the acceleration of the preceding vehicle is unavailable. To this end, the extended H∞ observer is proposed to estimate the disturbances under measurement noise. Derived from the estimation results, a composite controller integrating state feedback and disturbance compensation is developed, ensuring individual and string stability. Finally, illustrating the proposed methods effectiveness and feasibility with numerical simulations.

articleTitle: A Novel Method to Improve the Accuracy of Low-Cost Gyroscope-Based Attitude Estimation by Fusing Angular Acceleration Sensors
abstract: Gyroscope-based attitude estimation system has the problem of attitude drift under long-term operation conditions, which is particularly obvious on low-cost gyroscopes. As a new type of inertial sensor, the angular acceleration sensor can directly sense the angular acceleration of the carrier. The error characteristics and the mechanism by which an angular acceleration sensor is sensitive to changes in attitude are different from those of a gyroscope. Therefore, it is a feasible solution to use angular acceleration data to provide error correction for the gyroscope, thereby improving the accuracy of attitude estimation. In this paper, a novel method is proposed to improve the attitude estimation accuracy of low-cost gyroscope by fusing angular acceleration sensors. Based on the data characteristics of two inertial sensors, two different state variables and corresponding observation variables are designed, and the information fusion of the two sensors is realized through Kalman filtering. A synchronous data acquisition device was designed to conduct experimental verification. The experimental results show that the proposed method can improve the attitude estimation accuracy of low-cost gyroscopes under long-term operation conditions.

articleTitle: Feature Hybrid Reconstruction Network for Few-Shot Action Recognition
abstract: The primary challenge in few-shot learning lies in acquiring generic characteristics from a limited number of labeled samples. Recent approaches in few-shot action recognition have achieved remarkable performance through the acquisition of discriminative features from each video during episodic training., as well as the implementation of diverse multi-feature fusion techniques. However, these methods often overlook the fact that the knowledge obtained from each episode may not be relevant in subsequent iterations, leading to potential failures in matching misaligned samples. In order to address these limitations, we propose a Feature Hybrid Reconstruction Network (FHRN) comprising a spatial reinforcement layer, a hybrid reconstruction module, and a prototypical matching strategy to effectively leverage spatial and temporal information. The FHRN adopts an agnostic approach to learn task-specific representations through the reconstruction process. Moreover, the set matching strategy enables precise identification of corresponding video frames across different videos. Experimental evaluations are conducted on various datasets including UCF10l, HMDB51, SSv2, and Kineticsl00. Our proposed FHRN method yields results that are comparable to, and in some cases surpass, those achieved by most state-of-the-art techniques.

articleTitle: Based on AHP Evaluation Model and Neural Network Backbone to Achieve Specialized and Integrated Talent Training
abstract: Based on the talent training mode that combines innovation and entrepreneurship with professional education in applied undergraduate colleges, this paper provides a talent training mode with three complete education, three spiral theory and three methods of scientific evaluation system for cultivating high-quality talents with innovative thinking and practical ability. Among them, the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) evaluation model is adopted, determine the weight value of elements in the talent training mode, and pay more attention to the important elements. Based on talent training mode, CNN-MHSA-LSTM model is constructed by using convolutional neural network, attention mechanism and recurrent neural network to predict students' academic performance in professional courses and public courses. To evaluate the students' process performance and predict whether they can pass the final grade. By comparing the courses of different nature, the prediction accuracy is above 86<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, which can realize the grade warning better.

articleTitle: Semi-Supervised Curriculum Learning for Ultra-Wide-Angle Fundus Optic Disc Segmentation
abstract: Segmentation of the optic disc in ultra-wide-angle fundus images could aid in detection and diagnosis of diabetic kidney disease and diabetic retinopathy. Due to the wide field of view, large image size, and small targets of ultra-wide-angle fundus images, it's hard to annotate them. In this case, semi-supervised methods could solve this problem. However, standalone semi-supervised training does not take into account the differences between samples. We developed a new semi-supervised training method incorporating curriculum learning, where the model initially trains on easier samples and gradually progresses to more hard ones. This strategy could avoid the pos-sible negative impact of the unlabeled samples in early stages in training and strengthen model's robustness and serves as a plug-and-play approach and is adaptable to existing semi-supervised semantic segmentation methods. More concretely, we design a difficulty measurer to estimate the training difficulty of samples from the perspective of the entire dataset and a pace controller to control training time and duration of different samples according to their training difficulty. The experiment result shows the method we proposed could improves the performance.

articleTitle: Predefined Time Trajectory Tracking Control of Underactuated Autonomous Underwater Vehicle*
abstract: In this paper, the problem of underactuated autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) trajectory tracking control with predefined time convergence is investigated. A novel predefined-time control strategy is proposed to eliminate the singularity and reduce the computational complexity, whose convergence time can be preset by setting the time parameter, and the system state can be converged to zero within the predefined time. A predefined time backstepping controller is designed for AUV trajectory tracking control. Theoretical analysis shows that the upper limit of the convergence time is only determined by a constant, which reduces the complexity of parameter tuning compared to existing finite/fixed time control methods. The effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method are verified through further simulation studies.

articleTitle: Development of a Compact Optical Layout for a Miniature Fluorescence Spectrometer: In-Situ Detection of Organic Pollutants in Aquatic Environment
abstract: In recent years, the increasing presence of emerging organic pollutants in rivers, lakes, and other aquatic environments has posed significant threats to human health and ecological safety. Current monitoring technologies for these pollutants face several challenges, including the high cost of equipment and the scarcity of trained professionals. Furthermore, existing portable fluorescence sensors are limited by inadequate data, unsuitability for in-situ water environments, and the ability to detect only specific pollutants. This paper proposes a novel design for an in-situ miniature fluorescence spectrometer, utilizing a compact optical layout to monitor organic pollutants in water. The design features a high-power UV LED combined with a lens group to enhance the fluorescence excitation effect of low-concentration organic pollutants. The system components are integrated into a compact layout centered around a flow cell, significantly reducing the device's size. In experimental validation, vitamin B was used as a model organic pollutant to test the prototype's detection capabilities. Within the concentration range of 1 − 100 μg/L, the fluorescence intensity exhibited a strong linear correlation with the vitamin B concentration, achieving an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value of 0.9945, comparable to that of commercial spectrometers. This portable device demonstrates excellent performance in detecting organic matter and offers significant advantages for in-situ monitoring applications, making it well-suited for real-time pollutant detection in rivers, lakes, and other aquatic environments.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Occupational Pneumoconiosis Based on Adaptive Feature Fusion and Multi-Class Loss Function
abstract: Pneumoconiosis, as the most prevalent and severe occupational disease in China, is categorized into four stages based on the area of small shadows in lungs. Previous diagnostic methods have limited accuracy for identifying different stages due to complex and diverse lesions of pneumoconiosis, as well as the difficulty of collecting rich X-ray images of patients. To address the issues, a novel diagnostic method based on adaptive feature fusion and multi-class loss function is proposed. First, the prototype network is introduced to establish a diagnostic model under the insufficient images, with the purpose of distinguishing the disease stage by the distance between the features of various samples. Following that, the multi-channel and multi-level feature fusion modules are proposed, respectively. These modules incorporate a gate-based adaptive selection mechanism to efficiently integrate the most important features from different channels and levels. Finally, the multi-class loss function is designed to train the diagnostic model of pneumoconiosis. The experimental results on a self-built dataset of chest X-ray radiographs demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms ten comparative methods in terms of comprehensive performance.

articleTitle: Adaptive RBFNN-Based Fast Fixed-Time Backstepping Control for Robotic Manipulators
abstract: This article explores the time-varying trajectory tracking control for robotic manipulators with uncertainties. Initially, we propose a novel fixed-time backstepping control algorithm. This innovation allows the system to achieve fixed-time convergence more rapidly. Considering that the manipulator system are affected by disturbance and model uncertainty, we adopt an adaptive radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) to compensate for the lumped disturbance. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by simulation. Compared to existing methods, this approach shows a more rapid convergence rate and superior convergence performance.

articleTitle: Requirement and Practice of Coal Supply Balance and Energy Dispatching Risk Analysis for Large Energy Enterprises
abstract: Among the various forms of energy involved by energy enterprises, coal plays an important role, and the coal industry shoulders the heavy responsibility of ensuring the safe and stable supply of coal throughout the country. The coal industry and the whole energy industry are mutually integrated, interdependent and influenced, so it is difficult to draw a clear boundary. Among them, coal-fired power enterprises are the most typical, and the upstream and downstream industries of coal-fired power enterprises have high correlation, which makes the integrated operation chain closely connected and has unique competitive advantages in operation efficiency and cost. At the same time, however, the biggest potential risks of coal-fired power enterprises are high correlation between upstream and downstream industries, small fault-tolerant space and strong system rigidity, which makes enterprises have many management coordination problems and risk early warning problems in the production and operation process. In order to deal with the above problems, further expand the industrial advantages of energy enterprises, eliminate production and operation risks and improve comprehensive operation efficiency, it is necessary to give full play to the overall competitive advantage of integrated operation mode. Based on the construction of digital supply chain, the research and application of key technologies of coal-electricity integrated intelligent dispatching and joint early warning in large energy enterprises will be carried out to further improve comprehensive productivity and ensure integrated and efficient operation.

articleTitle: Robust Path Planning for Quadruped Robots in Dynamic and Challenging Environment
abstract: This paper proposes a path planning method for quadruped robots that combines an improved Jump Point Search (JPS) algorithm with the Artificial Potential Field (APF) method. Existing global path planning methods are unable to avoid dynamic obstacles while ensuring an optimal route. Local planning methods, such as APF, encounter issues like unreachable goals and local optima. To address these challenges, we propose a hybrid method that combines the globally-oriented JPS algorithm with the locally-oriented APF approach. To enable dynamic obstacle avoidance while maintaining a relatively optimal path, thus making it more suitable for real-world environments. We rigorously prove the stability of this fusion algorithm. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Parameter Identification of Multi-motor Driving Cutterhead System Model in Tunnel Boring Machine using Prediction Error Method
abstract: In this paper, parameter identification of multi-motor driving cutterhead system model in tunnel boring machine (TBM) using prediction error method (PEM). A state-space linear dynamics model of the cutter system is established based on the first principle by analyzing the working process of the induction motor, coupling, reduction gearbox and spur gear. Then, the parameters of the model are identified using the PEM by considering the constraints of the model parameters. Finally, the identified model is fitted to the test, which shows that the identified model can fit the test data better. We can find that the parameters identified by the PEM method have a good fitting degree and a small mean square error.

articleTitle: Adaptive Neural Zeta-Backstepping Tracking Control of Rigid Spacecraft with Predefined Damping Ratios
abstract: An important issue of attitude tracking of rigid spacecraft when exists inertial uncertainty and external perturbations is studied in this work. Different from the traditional backstepping method, a novel adaptive neural network zeta-backstepping method is proposed, which can realize the predefined adjustment of the system damping ratio through selecting specific controller parameters according to designed rules. At the same time, a second-order Lyapunov function method is introduced in order that system stability is guaranteed. With prescribed damping ratio, the system attitude tracking error will converge to a tiny region close to a state of equilibrium. Finally, simulation results prove the validity of the put-forward control strategy.

articleTitle: Exponential and Finite-Time Consensus of Multiagent Systems via Curve Suppression Method
abstract: This article investigates the exponential and finite-time leader-following consensus of first and second order multi-agent systems (MASs). Unlike the finite-time Lyapunov method, the curve suppression method based on the exponential and linear suppression functions is respectively designed to achieve the exponential and finite-time leader-following consensus of MASs. Especially, the distributed controllers are designed to reduce communication between MASs, where does not require the design of complex fractional-order controllers to achieve finite-time consensus. Furthermore, the first-order consensus is extended to the second-order consensus by defining a new system state including position and velocity. Finally, the effectiveness of the suggested approach is verified through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Dynamic Execution Path Analysis of the Linux Kernel on ACRN
abstract: With the expansion of safety-critical system requirements and increasing system complexity, safety-critical systems built on the Linux kernel and hypervisors such as ACRN are becoming essential in the safety-critical field. The Linux dynamic execution path refers to the changes in the function execution path in the Linux system call, reflecting the inherent uncertainty of the Linux kernel. We collect data on the Linux dynamic execution path based on Ftrace and find that lock contention and process preemption are the primary sources of uncertainty in the Linux dynamic execution path. By comparing the data of the ACRN environment and the native Linux environment, we find that introducing the ACRN hypervisor can reduce the diversity of the Linux dynamic execution path to a certain extent and improve the determinism of the Linux kernel. This contribution can provide data and method support for designing and implementing complex real-time systems.

articleTitle: Improved DQN for Path Planning with Classified High-value Prioritized Experience Replay
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low sample utilization and slow convergence speed when robots use the DQN algorithm for path planning, an improved DQN algorithm based on classification high-value prioritized experience replay (CHV-PER-DQN) is proposed. First, a dual experience pool is set up to categorize and store experience samples based on immediate reward values. Second, design a high-value prioritized sampling method that combines the state-action value function of the samples with the TD error as a measure of prioritized sampling. Finally, the high-value prioritized experience sampling method and the random uniform sampling method are used to draw experience samples from the two experience pools according to the proportion, respectively, to improve the sampling utilization rate and reduce the impact of the long time-consumption of the traditional prioritized experience replay (PER). Simulation results show that the CHV-PER-DQN algorithm can realize faster convergence speed and better path planning effect than the traditional DQN algorithm and PER-DQN algorithm.

articleTitle: A Layered Essential Visibility Graph Approach for Energy-Efficient UAV 3D Path Planning
abstract: This paper presents a visibility-based path planning algorithm for energy-constrained unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) Our algorithm constructs a layered essential visibility graph that accounts for environmental conditions, followed by the development of a modified heuristic function that balances time and energy consumption. The energy consumption model is formulated based on the dynamic characteristics of the UAV. Simulations in various environmental complexities demonstrate that the proposed path planning algorithm can efficiently generate paths with optimal energy and time consumption in a short computational period.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Cigarette Packaging Defect Detection Method Based on Multi-Scale Feature Matching
abstract: During the cigarette packaging printing process, defects can occur due to environmental changes, printing machine malfunctions, or human errors. Currently, visual inspection by humans is commonly used in production, but this method is inefficient and highly subjective. Most existing defect detection methods based on computer vision require extensive manual annotation. However, due to the uncertainty in defect types, forms, and sizes, as well as the limited availability of defect samples, these methods struggle to meet the requirements for supervised detection. Therefore, we propose an unsupervised defect detection method for cigarette packaging based on multi-scale feature matching. This method only requires normal images during the training phase. By providing a pre-trained image classification network as the teacher network, knowledge across multiple scales is extracted through an attention module into a student network with the same structure but without pre-training, to learn the feature distribution of normal images. During the testing phase, when an image with a defect passes through the network, it will produce a multi-scale feature distribution different from that of normal images. The difference between the abnormal and normal feature distributions is then analyzed to detect and localize defects. This method achieved an average detection and localization accuracy of 98.1 % (PRO), outperforming existing unsupervised defect detection methods and providing robust support for the automated inspection of cigarette packaging.

articleTitle: A GRU-based Automatic Weighting Factors Optimization Strategy for PMSM
abstract: The performance of model predictive control (MPC) in permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) still remains a challenging problem due to the large torque ripple in lower speed. The cost function in conventional MPC generally use fixed weighting factors, which is not easy to adapt different operation scenario and keep balance between torque ripple suppression and current tracking accuracy. To address this issue, a gated recurrent units (GRU) network based weighting factors automated-regulation strategy is proposed for the MPC in PMSM. Through offline training, the weighting factors in MPC are tuned in real time and the current tracking accuracy as well as torque ripple in different conditions are ensured, which is superior to the conventional fixed weighting factors-based MPC. Finally, some simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Integrated Prediction of Unfavorable Geology in Main Tunnel Considering the Geological Conditions of Parallel Tunnel
abstract: Currently, the advanced geological prediction for the main tunnel from the parallel tunnel often employs parallel deduction of detection conclusions, which faces issues such as a lack of diverse geological exploration information, a lack of analysis of geological structures and poor accuracy. In this paper, an integrated prediction method for unfavorable geology in main tunnel considering the geological conditions of parallel tunnel is proposed, which consists of three stages. In the first stage, based on the forecast mileage range and tunnel excavation conditions, the process is divided into four specific cases. In the second stage, it deduces the geology of the main tunnel along the orientation of rock strata occurrence or joint to parallel tunnel and selects the results of the rock strata occurrence or joint deduction according to the distance of the deduction. In the last stage, it deduces the geological conditions of parallel tunnel face and the integration of geophysical and drilling information for predictive conclusions based on the four specific cases. The proposed method offers higher prediction accuracy for rock mass integrity and surrounding rock grades compared to parallel deduction method.

articleTitle: Research on Improving the Accuracy of Force Sensor Through Hole Array Design
abstract: With the rapid development of modern industrial automation and intelligence, the demand for higher precision in force sensors has steadily increased. This paper addresses the issue of insufficient accuracy in traditional resistive strain gauge sensors by proposing a novel hole array sensor structure designed to enhance stress concentration effects, thereby improving force measurement accuracy. By conducting a theoretical analysis of the stress distribution on the surface of the hole-containing structure, a hole array structure was developed to effectively increase stress concentration. Comparative experiments were conducted to evaluate the differences in force measurement performance between sensors with and without the hole array structure. The experimental results show that the newly designed sensor improves basic accuracy by tenfold compared to traditional sensors, with significant improvements in both nonlinearity and hysteresis by an order of magnitude.

articleTitle: Research on High-Precision Thrust Control Methods for Vertical Short Takeoff and Landing Aircraft
abstract: Vertical/Short Takeoff and Landing (V/STOL) aircraft are crucial aviation assets, combining the flexibility of helicopters with the speed of fixed-wing aircraft. However, during hovering and vertical landing modes, these aircraft rely on the propulsion system to directly control their attitude, demanding high responsiveness and precision in thrust control-requirements that traditional speed controllers struggle to meet. This study adopts a direct thrust control architecture, designing an onboard adaptive model to estimate engine thrust and a thrust controller to directly manage thrust. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed model achieves high accuracy, with errors as low as 0.0004% even under engine degradation. The direct thrust controller also significantly outperforms traditional speed controllers, offering faster response times and zero steady-state error. These results underscore the effectiveness of advanced thrust control in enhancing the stability and performance of V/STOL aircraft.

articleTitle: Knowledge-Driven Target Trajectory Prediction Method for BVR Air Game Mission
abstract: Aiming at the high-precision real-time prediction requirements of target trajectory prediction in beyond-visual-range (BVR) air game mission, this paper proposes a method driven by aeronautical domain knowledge of BVR game missions. The target historical intentions and maneuvers are identified based on 2 different time windows respectively. Considering that the target's intention in the BVR game missions does not change drastically in a short time, the future maneuvers are predicted based on the historical intentions and maneuver identification results, and then the predicted future maneuver information is used to assist in realizing target trajectory prediction by long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network. The proposed method was tested based on BVR game mission data collected in a highly realistic simulation environment. The results showed that the method has high prediction accuracy and real-time performance.

articleTitle: Research on Post Weld Heat Treatment Control System for Ultra Large Carbon Steel Workpieces Based on Fuzzy PID
abstract: Aiming at the problems existing in the traditional post-weld heat treatment method, a large-scale heat processor is designed and fuzzy PID temperature control is introduced to improve the system's self-adaptive capability. The heater is designed for ultra-large carbon steel workpieces, and the temperature of the cylinder is raised to a specific temperature by the electromagnetic field generated by the induction current, which utilizes a good high-temperature environment to reduce the residual stresses inside the material. Through COMSOL finite element simulation combined with theoretical calculations, the parameters obtained are optimized, and the appropriate induction current and frequency are selected. Through simulation and analysis, the temperature change of the cylinder can be observed more intuitively, and the calculation error can be reduced to achieve the technological requirements of post-weld heat treatment.

articleTitle: Demagnetization Prediction Method of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Digital Twin Model
abstract: For the issue of local irreversible demagnetization faults in the permanent magnet of the PMSM (permanent magnet synchronous motor) affected by factors such as high temperature and high current. A method for predicting the demagnetization trend of permanent magnets based on digital twins has been proposed. Firstly, establish a digital twin geometric model based on motor parameters; Secondly, based on the finite element analysis method, a digital twin behavior and rule model is constructed, and a composite model of CNN (convolutional neural network),LSTM( long short-term memory neural network), and self attention mechanism is introduced into the digital twin model to achieve the prediction of the demagnetization trend of permanent magnets; Finally, the effectiveness of the method is validated using the experimental dataset. The experimental results show that compared with traditional digital twin technologies such as CNN,LSTM and so on, the prediction method proposed in this study significantly improves prediction accuracy and speed.

articleTitle: Fusion Filtering for Networked Stochastic Systems with Deception Attacks, Correlated Noises and Quantization Error
abstract: In this paper, the state fusion estimation problem for a set of networked stochastic uncertain systems subjected to network attacks and quantization error is concerned. The multiplicative noises in the state equation and the observation equations are correlated at the same instant. The additive noises are correlated simultaneously. The quantized measurements may encounter random deception attacks during the transmission process between sensors and estimators. To obtain the available measurement data, the centralized and distributed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\chi^{2}$</tex> detectors are employed in different fusion framework to distinguish whether the system is attacked. Based on the detection results, an improved two-segment centralized fusion filter is proposed. Furthermore, a distributed weighted fusion filter with good reliability is addressed. The simulation example verifies the effectiveness of the proposed results.

articleTitle: Optimal Control of Influent Water Quality Disturbance in Wastewater Treatment Aeration Process
abstract: The instability of the contaminants in the influent water quality will affect the precision of the dissolving-oxygen control in the effluent process. Therefore, this paper carries out an in-depth study of this problem. Firstly, the correlation between each influent water quality and dissolved oxygen consumption in the aeration process is derived by analysing the influence of influent water quality on dissolved oxygen consumption; secondly, an optimisation model associating dissolved oxygen consumption and influent water quality in the aeration process is designed by adopting the optimisation prediction method of influent water quality in order to obtain the most optimal control strategy of the aeration process; lastly, the radial basis neural network regulation of the influent water quality interference optimisation Finally, the control of a proportional-integral-derivative (WQO-RBF -PID) controller optimised for influent water quality disturbances is implemented in a benchmark simulation model. The test results illustrate that the method can effectively suppress the influence of influent water quality on dissolved oxygen control and improve the dissolved oxygen control effect during the aeration process.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Moving Characteristics of Pedestrians and Non-Motorized Vehicles on a One-Way Road Based on Actual Videos
abstract: When non-motorized vehicles and people travel on one-way roadways, traffic mobility and safety become significant concerns. When combined with constrained road space, the stark disparity between pedestrian walking speeds and non-motorized vehicle riding speeds can quickly result in gridlock and accidents. To better understand the behavioral traits of pedestrians and non-motorized vehicles on one-way roads, this article examines the interaction between pedestrians and these vehicles in mixed traffic flow. It was discovered that whether or not pedestrians are moving in groups impacts their speed. Pedestrians travel more freely and are more widely dispersed in the vertical highway direction. Still, non-motorized vehicles are more inclined to travel on the middle and right side of the road. Large disparities exist in the overtaking process of non-motorized vehicles due to variances in the safe spacing needs and speeds of bikers and pedestrians. It is feasible to support the sustainable development and enhancement of the transportation system by monitoring and evaluating the actions of walkers and non-motorized vehicles. This will enable traffic control authorities and urban planners to get helpful recommendations and direction.

articleTitle: Histogram Equalization Based Infrared Image Enhancement with FCOWA-ER
abstract: The temperature of the target and the surrounding environment are often close and the detection distance is long, resulting in the contrast between the target and the background is not obvious and the texture information is poor for infrared images. To solve these problems, a histogram equalization method of infrared image fusion based on uncertainty reasoning is proposed in this paper. After noise suppression and texture enhancement, considering the characteristics of different histogram equalization methods, this paper uses Fuzzy-Cautious Ordered Weighted Averaging and Evidential Reasoning (FCOWA-ER) method to jointly use three histogram equalization methods which are Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE), Dynamic Quadrants Histogram Equalization Plateau Limit (DQHEPL) and Plateau Histogram Equalization (PHE). Experimental results show that compared with the single histogram equalization method, the proposed evidence theory fusion histogram equalization method has better performance on the infrared dataset.

articleTitle: Research on Ship Recognition Based on Adaptive Image Enhancement and Defogging
abstract: An adaptive image enhancement defogging ship recognition method is proposed to detect ships navigating on heavy foggy weather. This method is applicable to different image sources, including gray scale transform from radar echo data and video image captured by cameras. The adaptive image enhancement methend is applied to the acquired foggy image, which includes image preprocessing, logarithmic transformation enhancement, gamma transform enhancement, and the ACE algorithm for fusion defogging. The purpose is to highlight the features of the ship target. The defogged images will be handled by filtering, grey scale transformation and Canny edge detection, and the ship will be recognized using HOG and SVM. The results indicate that the method can not only produce a defogging image, but also recognize the ship more clearly, and does not need a large number of data sets for training. At the same time, the method has a wide range of applicability, faster processing speed, and able to deal with different sources of image data, which provides technical support for the monitoring of ships and safety management.

articleTitle: Neural Network Control for Fuel Cell Boost Converter Based on Particle Swarm Optimization
abstract: The stable control of disturbance rejection in direct current-direct current (DC-DC) boost converters is critical for fuel cells to meet load demands. However, uncertainties and disturbances can negatively impact the output performance of these converters. To address this challenge, an adaptive neural network control strategy utilizing adaptive particle swarm optimization (APSO) is proposed. First, the uncertainties introduced by variations in the inductor, capacitor, input voltage, and load are estimated using neural network observers. Next, a control scheme that integrates the APSO algorithm is introduced to improve the convergence of the output voltage in the DC-DC boost converter. Finally, quantitative analyses confirm the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy in enhancing the performance of the output system.

articleTitle: LFC Strategy of Power System with Hybrid Regulation Resources: A Multi-Agent-Based Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
abstract: As renewable energy sources become increasingly prevalent, relying solely on conventional generators for load frequency control (LFC) in power systems proves to be neither cost-effective nor practical. Consequently, a variety of regulation resources (called hybrid regulation resources) will be integrated into the LFC. The heterogeneous characteristics of hybrid regulation resources pose a significant challenge to the LFC strategy design. In this context, this paper proposes a novel LFC strategy based on the multi-agent twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (MATD3) algorithm. We establish a mathematical model of the power system with hybrid regulation resources to create a reinforcement learning environment. Furthermore, we formulate a reward function consisting of the area control error (ACE) and the frequency deviation according to the control objectives of the LFC. Given that the hybrid regulation resources exhibit both continuous and discrete properties, a rounding function discretizes these actions tailored for the resources with discrete properties. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through simulation and comparison.

Author Keywords: multi-agent twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient

articleTitle: Reliability-Aware and Cost-Efficient Planning Methods for Hydrogen-Based Multi-Energy Systems in Off-Grid Mode
abstract: Hydrogen-based multi-energy systems (HMESs) contribute to addressing the environmental and energy issues faced by many nations. When designing an HMES with higher reliability and lower system cost, system planning should be conducted beforehand. In this paper, we investigate an optimal planning problem for HMESs in off-grid mode under multi-source uncertainties. Specifically, we first formulate a multi-objective stochastic programming problem related to system cost and reliability. Then, we design a planning method for the considered HMES based on the third-generation non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-III) and a rule-based scheme. Finally, simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Compared with several benchmarks, the proposed method can offer a better Pareto frontier (i.e., higher reliability and lower total cost can be implemented simultaneously).

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Control for Robotic Arms with Uncertain Input Gain
abstract: Robotic manipulators encounter challenges such as modeling errors, external disturbances, and uncertain input gain during trajectory tracking control. This paper presents a control strategy for a single-link robotic manipulator to enhance tracking precision and speed. First, the uncertain input gain and external disturbances are transformed into an equivalent disturbance through a mathematical formulation. Next, a disturbance observer is designed to estimate this equivalent disturbance, which is incorporated into the control framework to achieve precise trajectory tracking. Finally, the stability of the system is validated through Lyapunov function analysis. Simulations and comparative experiments in MATLAB/Simulink demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves high-precision trajectory tracking, confirming its effectiveness.

articleTitle: DMD3QN: Dual Model Combined Driving Based on Dueling Double Deep Q-Network
abstract: Fast computation, low latency, and high accuracy are required for autonomous vehicles (AVs) to reach the end in uncertain environments safely. Therefore, high dimensional input data from sensors must be processed efficiently to reduce the state space dimensionality and improve operational efficiency. Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) can better ensure an efficient exploration and learning process for each intelligence. Based on this, we propose a Dual-Model Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (DMD3QN) autonomous driving system, which uses D3QN to train braking and driving models separately to combine the driving tasks, enabling the vehicle to localize objects and make braking and driving actions accordingly more accurately. In addition, to reduce the state space, we utilize depth cameras and segmentation cameras for object detection, distance estimation, and image processing. We used the CARLA simulator to conduct 20 test episodes on four routes with uncertain environments, achieving success rates of 95%, 95%, 100%, and 90%, which demonstrates the superiority of our proposed system.

articleTitle: Adaptive Neural Sliding Mode Based Control of Robot Manipulators with Disturbance Observer
abstract: For robotic manipulator systems experiencing uncertainties and external disturbances, an integral nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode control (INFTSMC) approach is introduced, incorporating an adaptive sliding mode disturbance observer (ASMDO). To relax the constraints on the design of the robotic arm disturbance observer, an adaptive method is added to estimate the upper bound of the disturbances. The fixed-time stability of the proposed ASMDO is analyzed theoretically. Secondly, radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) is utilized to estimate the system uncertainty. Subsequently, by combining the proposed observer with the RBFNN, the INFTSMC is structured around an integral nonsingular fast terminal sliding surface. The stability and finite-time convergence of the full system are then demonstrated through Lyapunov theory, and simulation outcomes confirm the proposed method's effectiveness.

Author Keywords: integral nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode control

articleTitle: Diffusion Modeling and Transformer Knowledge Distillation Techniques for Time Series Imputation
abstract: In recent years, big data analysis has gained popularity, but data are often missing during collection, storage, etc., which affects the effectiveness of data analysis. Therefore, this paper proposes a Time Series Imputation method based on Diffusion model and Knowledge Distillation (TSI-DIKD). The diffusion model imputation missing values in time series and is combined with a Transformer structure to capture the intricate dependencies present in the time series data. Knowledge distillation is also used in the reverse process of the diffusion model to improve imputation accuracy. We conducted experiments on healthcare and environmental data to compare the performance of the model with different percentages of missing values. The results show that our model outperforms other models on all three evaluation metrics.

articleTitle: Voltage Stability Analysis of Distribution Network Considering Massive Electric Vehicle Charging Load
abstract: In order to assess the impact of large-scale integration of electric vehicles (EVs) into the distribution grid on its stability, a modeling approach is employed based on EV user behavior and charging characteristics. Different charging modes, namely conventional charging, fast charging, and battery replacement charging, are modeled, taking into account voltage stability indicators. The charging power of EVs is analyzed under these three scenarios, considering user behavior and charging characteristics. Additionally, a particle swarm optimization algorithm is employed in simulations to study the voltage stability of EVs during different time periods in the charging process. By integrating the above factors, the impact curve of EV charging load on the distribution grid is obtained. This analysis method not only validates the feasibility of the voltage stability analysis approach but also assesses the influence of EV charging load on various nodes in the distribution grid.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Observer Based Motion Vector Control for Air Cushion Vehicle with Drift Phenomenon
abstract: Considering the influence of drift phenomenon, a finite-time robust vector control method is proposed for air cushion vehicle (ACV). The nonlinear vector model included the dynamics of course and total speed is established. To obtain the robustness for uncertainties, finite-time observer is designed based on a nonlinear vector model. By the well combining with finite-time theory, finite-time robust vector controller is designed. Controller can make ACV track desired moving speed and direction well although the big drift phenomenon and uncertainties exist. Designed controller guarantees that tracking errors of motion vectors will diminish to zero within a limited number of steps. Its efficacy and superiority are confirmed through simulation results.

articleTitle: Research on Thrust Characteristics and Optimization of Thrust Ripple of Coreless Superconducting Linear Synchronous Motor
abstract: As a special form of linear motor, coreless superconducting linear synchronous motor (SCLSM) has the advantages of small thrust ripple and high control precision. Because of the structure of the primary without iron core, the thrust ripple caused by the end effect and the cogging effect is eliminated, but the thrust ripple caused by the primary winding discontinuity still exists. Based on three-dimensional electromagnetic field modeling and Maxwell tensor method, a three-dimensional electromagnetic force calculation method of coreless SCLSM is proposed. The thrust characteristics of the motor are analyzed, and a thrust ripple optimization method is proposed, which can effectively reduce thrust ripple caused by the discontinuity of the primary winding.

articleTitle: Robust $H_{\infty}$ Control and Smooth Transition of Thrust Closed-Loop and Inlet Unstart for Scramjet
abstract: To meet the performance requirements of fast and accurate control for the scramjet control system, this study utilizes a control-oriented model based on small perturbation dynamics. The main thrust closed-loop control and inlet unstart protection control systems are designed based on the robust <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> control algorithm. A soft switching method is employed to achieve smooth transitions between the two control modes, reducing control signal fluctuations during controller switching. Simulation results demonstrate that the designed controllers exhibit excellent control performance, enabling overshoot-free control of the scramjet. Compared to a direct switching system, the control system with soft switching achieves smooth and non-disruptive transitions, effectively suppressing control oscillations caused by switching processes, and ensuring the control effectiveness and operational safety of the engine.

articleTitle: Risk-Driven Security Strategy Decision-Making for High-Speed Train Control and Monitoring System
abstract: With the extensive application of technologies like Ethernet and integrated control in high-speed trains, onboard networks encounter mounting security challenges, making the assurance of their secure and stable operation a pressing issue. Since train onboard control and monitoring systems require high reliability and continuous stability, implementing security strategies can compromise system functionality, resources, and costs. Therefore, this paper presents a risk-driven method for decision-making on security strategies, examining how to select suitable security measures that minimize security risks while maximizing security benefits. A risk assessment approach is proposed, which accounts for the propagation of attack impacts based on system topology and functional features. Finally, a network simulation system is established, referencing the topology and functional specifications of the CR300AF Fuxing EMU, and experimental outcomes confirm a close alignment between the analysis results and actual train operations.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Topology-Unshared and Occlusion-Robust Network for Skeleton-Based Action Recognition
abstract: This paper introduces an advanced hybrid network architecture that integrates Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) with Transformer models to enhance human action recognition in complex scenarios, particularly in environments with frequent occlusions, such as power stations. We developed a dynamic topology modeling approach with channel-specific unshared weights that adaptively refine the feature matrices and improve recognition accuracy. Our results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid network outperforms traditional models, especially in handling occluded or incomplete skeletal data. We further validated the effectiveness of our model against a range of standard skeleton-based recognition methods, show-casing significant improvements in accuracy. The hybrid model proves particularly adept at maintaining high accuracy even in challenging conditions with substantial occlusions, aligning with the operational realities of power production facilities. This study not only advances the field of action recognition with its robust approach to occlusions but also sets a new benchmark for the practical application of deep learning technologies in industrial settings, ensuring enhanced operational safety and efficiency.

articleTitle: Model-Free Dynamic Event-Triggered Load Frequency Control for Multi-Area Interconnected Power Systems
abstract: This article studies the load frequency control problem for unknown interconnected multi-area power systems, where data dropouts occur in both forward and feedback channels. A dynamic linearization data model is established for these systems. Furthermore, a dynamic event-triggered mechanism is proposed to relieve the communication burden. An input-based data dropout compensation scheme is proposed to reduce the damage caused by random data dropouts on system stability. Finally, the validities of the above methods are verified through simulation studies.

articleTitle: Adaptive Finite-Time Control for Nonlinear Time-Delay Systems with Output Constraints
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive finite-time control strategy is proposed for non-strict feedback nonlinear systems to solve the time-delay and output constraint problems. It introduces a fuzzy adaptive update law to compensate for the time-delay and uses the barrier Lyapunov function (BLF) to handle the output constraints in both constrained and unconstrained systems. The method integrates adaptive backstepping and fuzzy logic systems to manage non-strict feedback challenges. The controller designed by this method ensures that the output tracking error of the system converges to the origin in finite time even under the influence of time-delay and also meets the output constraints. Simulation examples confirm the effectiveness of this proposed approach, demonstrating its capabilities with respect to time-delay and output constraints.

articleTitle: Design of a Secure Industrial Data Interaction System Based on International Data Space and Optimized KP-ABE Algorithm
abstract: In order to tackle the challenges of data interaction security and trustworthiness in industrial environments, this paper proposes and implements an industrial data interaction system that integrates the International Data Space (IDS) framework with an improved KP-ABE security encryption technique. The system employs an edge gateway as the application platform. It enhances data protection by incorporating a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE), creating a secure data exchange platform that ensures reliable participant interactions, facilitates data sharing, and maximizes data value. The results of the tests demonstrate that this system can effectively protect and manage industrial data interactions, providing a robust solution for industrial data exchange.

articleTitle: Optimization of Under-Voltage Starting Performance of PMSM Based on Improved Voltage-Loop Quasi-Z-Source Inverter
abstract: Low-voltage servo systems often use batteries for power. As the battery continues to discharge, the DC bus voltage of the inverter circuit gradually decreases. Before triggering the undervoltage shutdown protection, a derating method is generally used in engineering under undervoltage conditions. At this time, back electromotive force saturation occurs, and the starting current and torque are limited, leading to a decline in starting performance and a slower overall system response speed. To address this issue, a new control strategy is proposed, which combines the Quasi-Z-source network with the traditional low-voltage servo driver. Additionally, the rate of change of the phase current amplitude of the permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) is introduced into the voltage loop control circuit of the Quasi-Z-source network as a compensation amount, forming a positive feedback voltage loop control structure. This improves the DC bus voltage and its dynamic response performance, increases the motor starting current and starting torque, thereby improving the starting performance of the system under undervoltage conditions. The effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified through MATLAB/Simulink simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: Auxiliary Model Based Maximum Likelihood Least Squares Iterative Estimation Algorithm for Bilinear Systems with Colored Noises
abstract: This paper mainly considers the parameter estimation of bilinear output-error systems with colored noises. According to the auxiliary model identification idea, the unmeasurable inner variables (true outputs) in the system model are replaced with the output of an auxiliary model, and an auxiliary model based maximum likelihood least squares iterative algorithm is studied to estimate the parameters of bilinear output-error systems. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm is effective for identifying the bilinear output-error systems.

articleTitle: Safe Formation Control For Micro-UAV Using Control Barrier Functions
abstract: The formation control for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has become a key research focus in the past two decades. This paper studies the issues of formation tracking and safety control for micro-UAV swarms.
