A distributed finite-time formation control method based on an adaptive super-twisting algorithm is designed, ensuring that micro- UAVs can quickly converge to the desired formation within a finite time. Meanwhile, a safety formation control method based on control barrier functions is developed to address collision and obstacle avoidance during formation maintenance. The effectiveness and superiority of the proposed methods are validated through both simulation and real-world micro-UAV experiments in obstacle environments.

articleTitle: Initial Population Optimization Sparrow Search Algorithm for Warehouse AGV Path Planning
abstract: To address the excessive randomness in the initial population that may lead to suboptimal first-generation solutions in the storage system path planning using the Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA), this paper propose the Initial Population Optimized Sparrow Search Algorithm (IPOSSA). IPOSSA utilizes the good point set method to distribute initial population values uniformly within the permissible range, thereby bringing the first-generation solution closer to the optimal value. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of this approach, showing that IPOSSA shortens the average optimal path by 5.89% compared to SSA, converges more quickly, and mitigates the tendency to fall into local optima. Overall, the improved method demonstrates significant effectiveness.

articleTitle: Observer-Based Sliding Mode Control for Interconnected Systems Under Constrained Bit Rate: Weighted Try-Once-Discard Scheme
abstract: This paper investigates the observer-based sliding mode control (SMC) problem for interconnected systems under the constrained bit rate and weighted try-once-discard (WTOD) protocol. The bandwidth of the digital communication network is measured by the bit rate. With limited network bandwidth, a WTOD protocol is introduced to reduce the length of the transmitted sensor data to reduce the bit rate consumption and improve the decoded accuracy. The selected data components under the WTOD protocol are compressed and transmitted to the observer side by the designed encoding-decoding mechanism. Then, an observer-based SMC strategy is developed under a decoded output-based observer and a normal sliding surface. Some sufficient conditions are provided to ensure that the closed-loop system is exponentially ultimately bounded (EUB) while the system trajectories can be driven into a specific sliding domain. Finally, a two-area power system is exploited to validate the effectiveness of the developed control algorithm.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning with Model Predictive Control for Coordinated Operation of Power Plant
abstract: To address the challenges of rapid and accurate regulation of power generation load due to significant model nonlinearity, strong inertia, and substantial variable coupling in the load control process of boiler and turbine units in coal-fired power plants, this paper proposes a control policy that combines model predictive control with reinforcement learning based on a multi-operating condition model. By making real-time adjustments according to the operating state, the policy corrects model predictive control towards optimal control, thereby achieving optimal variable load control of a coal-fired power unit. A case study of a typical 300MW power plant in China demonstrates the superior control performance of the proposed method compared to traditional predictive control models.

articleTitle: Time-Varying Distributed Neurodynamic Algorithm to Fixed-Time Economic Dispatch with Event-Triggered Communication Over Directed Graphs
abstract: This paper proposes a distributed fixed-time neuro-dynamic algorithm with time-varying coefficients over directed communication networks, based on an event-triggered strategy. Following that, it is shown that the algorithm converges to an economic dispatch problem (EDP) optimum solution, and an upper bound on the convergence time that is independent of the initial conditions is given. Meanwhile, the proof of the exclusion of Zeno behavior is also given in detail. Finally, an EDP numerical simulation example is provided to verify the superiority of the proposed algorithm and the effectiveness of the event-triggered strategy.

articleTitle: Predictive Cruise Control with Velocity Profile Online Optimization for Energy Efficiency
abstract: Factors such as road gradient, driving style, and traffic conditions all significantly impact the energy consumption performance of heavy trucks. Predictive Cruise Control (PCC) algorithm, which based on Model Predictive Control (MPC), can utilize the upcoming road gradient to achieve energy-efficient driving by controlling the truck's longitudinal speed. However, as a type of cruise control, PCC regulates longitudinal speed within a certain range, which limits its ability to fully exploit the energy-saving potential brought by speed variations. Dynamic Programming (DP) can compute the globally optimal vehicle speed for energy-efficient driving using pre-obtained map information. However, it requires significant computational resources and cannot be used in real-time online scenarios. This paper utilizes the powerful fitting capability of neural networks to enable online use of the DP algorithm. It utilizes the suggested vehicle speed output by the network to guide the PCC algorithm in speed tracking, thereby significantly enhancing energy efficiency. The proposed method has been compared with the Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) algorithm and the original PCC algorithm. Simulation results show that this method achieves superior energy efficiency: compared to the ACC algorithm, it improves energy savings by 14% to 18%, and compared to the original PCC, it improves energy savings by 6 % to 8 %.

articleTitle: Inverse Hysteresis Compensation and Quasi-Sliding Mode Control of Micro-hand System
abstract: Micro-hand is a kind of pneumatic soft robot, which has light weight and high flexibility is widely used in various fields. However, due to the inevitable hysteresis effect in rubber materials, the stability and accuracy of the system are affected, which puts higher demands on the control system. In this paper, inverse hysteresis compensation for hysteresis effect which is represented by generalized Prandtl-Ishlinskii model is discussed and robust right coprime factorization control and quasi-sliding mode control are combined to ensure the robust stability and the tracking performance of the system. Finally, the simulations of tracking performance are carried out.

articleTitle: Multi-Reservoir Scheduling Optimization with Cooperative Game Based on Coalition Formation Method
abstract: The optimization of reservoir operations is vital for rational water resource allocation, ensuring a stable supply for industrial, agricultural, and domestic purposes, and mitigating the risks of floods and droughts. This study approaches reservoir cooperation by considering stakeholder coordination and balancing individual interests with overall system benefits. It constructs a corresponding game model using the coalition formation (CF) method from multi-agent systems (MAS) and provides an optimal coalition formation strategy for multi-reservoir water resource allocation based on the genetic algorithm (GA). The results demonstrate that this method can reduce water supply costs while meeting the water demands of all stakeholders. Additionally, it effectively addresses the issues of water resource waste and low allocation efficiency in the Puyang River basin reservoirs of Pujiang County.

articleTitle: Online Continual Learning Based Real-Time Dynamic Digital Twin Model in Industrial Systems
abstract: Digital twin (DT), as a new digital technology, has been widely used to improve the ability of industrial applications such as monitoring and fault diagnosis, by generating high-fidelity models of physical objects. However, existing DT models of industrial equipment cannot dynamically update with changing environments, particularly when it comes to utilizing real-time data streams. In this paper, we propose an edge-based DT framework in industrial systems. For dynamically updating the DT model of the equipment with real-time data streams, we design an online continual learning (OCL) based on DT update method. Meanwhile, an algorithm based on online experience replay (OER) is proposed to address the catastrophic forgetting problem of the proposed DT update method. Numerical results show the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization Method for Crane Scheduling in Steelmaking Workshop
abstract: In the steelmaking workshop, crane scheduling is a crucial logistics challenge affecting production efficiency and resource utilization. This study addresses the multi-machine, multi-task crane scheduling problem in steelmaking workshops by examining the associated temporal and spatial constraints. A multi-objective optimization model is formulated with the goals of minimizing total transport distance, passive transport distance, and waiting time. The model includes rules for resolving crane conflicts and employs the NSGA-II algorithm to identify the Pareto optimal front. Subsequently, an ideal point method is utilized to achieve balanced scheduling solutions. Finally, the proposed approach is validated using actual production data collected from the site. Experimental results show that proposed model effectively addresses crane scheduling problem, offering decision-makers high-quality scheduling solutions.

articleTitle: Active Disturbance Rejection Control for Random Signal Tracking in Electro-Optical Tracking Systems Based on Random Sensitivity Function
abstract: The target trajectory tracked by the electro-optical tracking system (ETS) is often accompanied by randomness, while the tracking effect of the active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) on the random signal in it lacks a targeted evaluation index. To address this problem, a random sensitivity function evaluation indicator based on the framework of ADRC is introduced. The random sensitivity function is introduced according to the two-degree-freedom structure of ADRC, and three frequency-domain indicators are utilized to describe the steady state performance and dynamic performance of the ADRC in the ETS in the tracking process of random reference signals. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed indicators are verified using simulation analysis.

articleTitle: Wood Surface Discoloration Defect Detection Based on Improved HRNet
abstract: Discoloration defect detection is a significant task in the wood industry for ensuring the appearance and quality of wooden products. However, discoloration defect detection still faces some challenges due to the low contrast, blurred boundary, and slender shape of discoloration defects. To overcome these challenges, we propose a multi-branch feature encoding HRNet(MFE-HRNet) for wood surface discoloration defect detection. The network maintains high-resolution features and builds a parallel multi-resolution architecture to prevent the dilution of low-contrast discoloration defect features. Through repeated cross-fusion of multi-scale features, the network enhances the global representation of blurry features. In order to effectively preserve the detail features of the defect edge, a multi-branch feature encoding module (MFEM) is proposed as the encoding layer of the network. In the MFEM, multiple branches concurrently extract features, generating feature maps with complementary characteristics, thereby enhancing the ability of network to recognize fine details of defects. Experimental results verify the effectiveness of our method in detecting discoloration defects on wood surface.

articleTitle: Low-Rank Compression of CNN Models Based on Efficient Rank Parameter Learning
abstract: Tensor decomposition is an important method for compressing convolutional neural network (CNN) models. However, in the decomposition process, it is necessary to configure appropriate rank parameters for each convolutional kernel tensor. Addressing the difficulty in setting ranks, we propose a low-rank optimization algorithm, which defines a cost function based on information entropy. By solving the constructed optimization problems, the low-rank structure and rank parameters of each convolutional kernel tensor can be learned automatically, such that efficiently achieving global scope automatic configuration of rank parameters while ensuring model accuracy. By testing various CNN models on different datasets, the results show that the proposed low-rank optimization algorithm can obtain all rank parameters in a single training process, and the average accuracy loss of the decomposed model does not exceed 1%.

articleTitle: $H_{i}/H_{\infty}$ Optimization Based Fault Detection for Traction Rectifier in High-Speed Train
abstract: The traction rectifier plays an important role in safe operation of high-speed trains. Any occurrence of unexpected faults in the traction rectifier may result in safety deterioration to high-speed trains. In this paper, an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{i}/H_{\infty}$</tex> optimization based method is used to achieve fault detection of the traction rectifier affected by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l_{2}$</tex>-norm bounded multi-source disturbances. First, the rectifier with potential faults is described as a linear discrete time-varying system model. The residual is generated by applying an observer-based fault detection filter (FDF). Then, an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{i}/H_{\infty}$</tex> optimization criteria is introduced by using the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{-}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> sensitivity indices. Based on this, the design of FDF can be reformulated as an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{i}/H_{\infty}$</tex> optimization problem. A feasible solution of the post-filter and observer gain matrix is given in terms of Riccati recursions. Consequently, the sensitivity of residual to faults and robustness of residual against disturbances can be improved. Finally, a simulation is carried out to demonstrate the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Simulation Platform for Closed Systems
abstract: This study introduces a closed ecological system simulation platform, designed to model the natural ecological cycle within a controlled environment. The paper presents the various types of components within the ecosystem, the methods for mathematical modeling of each component, and the flow of materials between components. It provides a detailed introduction to the design and implementation of the simulation platform, especially the design of the simulation timing sequence. The simulation results from this platform can realistically reflect the overall material flow of the system and its changes over time.

articleTitle: A Controllable Editing Closed-Loop 3D Gaussian Autonomous Driving Sensor Simulator
abstract: With the development of Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) and 3D Gaussian techniques, significant progress has been made in autonomous driving sensor simulation. However, current data-driven sensor simulations are limited to the re-production of autonomous driving scenes, with restricted scene editing capabilities. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a 3D Gaussian-based closed-loop controllable editing sensor simulator for the joint simulation and planning of sensors. The simulator reconstructs a road network model aligned with the 3D Gaussian model, enabling the planning of background vehicle trajectories within the scene and facilitating scene editing. This paper introduces a technique for the simultaneous construction of the road network and 3D Gaussian model, automating the creation of both. Evaluation results validate that the proposed method can automatically construct high-precision rendered camera sensors and aligned road networks, demonstrating its potential for application in large-scale scenarios.

articleTitle: Research on Motor Control of Steer-by-Wire for Intelligent Vehicles Based on Flood-PID Algorithm
abstract: To improve the control performance of the steering-by-wire system, an improved flood PID control algorithm for the steering motor is proposed.First, by analysing the structure and dynamic characteristics of the wire-rope steering system, a mathematical model of the steering system and motor is developed. Then, A PID controller is then designed to target steering motor angle to achieve precise steering angle control.By incorporating human learning mechanisms to boost population diversity in the flood optimization algorithm, a refined flood-PID steering motor control algorithm was developed. Finally, the results were confirmed experimentally on the steer-by-wire test bench using a combined simulation with the CarSim software and MATLAB/Simulink.Simulation results and bench tests indicate that the enhanced flood-PID control algorithm presented in this paper effectively adapts to system changes and disturbances, achieving precise motor angle control and enhancing the steering system's reliability.

articleTitle: Design Framework of Active Disturbance Rejection Control with System Model
abstract: Although Active Disturbance Rejection Control is a control algorithm that does not rely on the object model, its design philosophy does not exclude the use of models. This paper proposes a model-based ADRC design framework. Firstly, a generalized object with an approximately integral cascaded structure is constructed using the model. Then, the ADRC system design is completed based on the generalized object. This framework fully utilizes the model information without altering the original ADRC structure while assisting in the parameter tuning of the controller. Based on this framework, this paper discusses three different scenarios: known transfer function model, linear state-space model, and nonlinear model. Furthermore, simulation and physical experiments are conducted on a typical two-tank water level system to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Multi-Granularity Supervised Contrastive Framework for Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Aero-Engines
abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) predictions are critical to the safe operation of aero-engines. Currently, the RUL prediction task is mainly a regression paradigm with only mean square error as the loss function and lacks research on feature space structure, the latter of which has shown excellent performance in a large number of studies. This paper develops a multi-granularity supervised contrastive (MGSC) framework from plain intuition that samples with the same RUL label should be aligned in the feature space, and address the problems of too large minibatch size and unbalanced samples in the implementation. The RUL prediction with MGSC is implemented on using the proposed multi-phase training strategy. This paper also demonstrates a simple and scalable basic network structure and validates the proposed MGSC strategy on the CMPASS dataset using a convolutional long short-term memory network as a baseline, which effectively improves the accuracy of RUL prediction.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Control of Articulated Roller With Sideslip Effect
abstract: In order to reduce the operation difficulty of operators in complex working conditions and improve compaction efficiency, unmanned road rollers have become a favorable solution. When compaction is carried out on rough and uneven road surfaces, the fuselage will inevitably have a side slip problem. In order to reduce the impact of sideslip on the vehicle performance, the nonlinear mathematical model and dynamic error model of articulated roller with sideslip angle are established in this paper. The nonlinear system is linearized by feedback linearization, and a tracking controller is designed to eliminate the trajectory tracking error of actual path and reference path. Through MATLAB/Simulink simulation verification, the results show that the feedback linearization processing method proposed in this paper can effectively solve the sideslip problem caused by vehicle fuselage offset, thus proving the feasibility and effectiveness of the scheme.

articleTitle: Ballistic Characteristics and Control Authority of a High-Spin Projectile with Tail Control Mechanism
abstract: To minimize collateral damage and improve the long-range accuracy of artillery munitions. One strategy is to install low-cost guidance kits to enable uncontrolled munitions to have corrective capabilities. The projectile is often stabilized by a high spin rate, which induces complex dynamic characteristics and increases the difficulty of adding control mechanisms. This paper focuses on a high-spin projectile with a tail control concept, investigates the guided boattail control mechanism, and formulates a generalized dynamic model for pulse control. Numerical simulation of the ballistic characteristics of the tail control of high-spin projectiles and analysis of the influence of control input parameters on control authority. The results show that the tail control mechanism corrected the center-of-mass motion of the projectile while generating complex angular motion. The impulse size and activation time of the pulse control significantly impact the control authority and the total angle of attack amplitude. The control input parameters can be adjusted to improve ballistic characteristics and increase control authority while ensuring stable flight of the proj ectile.

articleTitle: A Bayesian Optimization Approach via Iteratively Least Squares for High-Dimensional Black-Box Systems' Design Space Exploration
abstract: The design space exploration in black-box systems, which lack complete mechanistic models, has wide applications in scientific and industrial research. Bayesian optimization(BO) can obtain high-quality solutions with limited evaluations, which is particularly suitable for expensive black-box optimization problems. However, existing research indicates that BO meth-ods face challenges in high-dimensional black-box optimization problems. A BO algorithm based on iterative least squares(ILS) dimensionality reduction is proposed to reduce the impact of the dimensionality in high-dimensional black-box function opti-mization with low-dimensional effective subspace. The algorithm first performs dimensionality reduction by a limited dataset, iteratively conducting least squares fitting, and obtains important parameters through weight analysis of the combination with the smallest error. Subsequently, it applies Bayesian optimization only for the important parameters, while other parameters are set to the optimal values obtained from the primal dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to directly USE BO with MACE acquisition function, an advanced BO method, this method performs better in high-dimensional black-box functions with the same number of evaluations.

articleTitle: ScenE Similarity Recognition with Integrated High-Dimensional Point Cloud Features
abstract: To enhance the scene understanding capability of inspection robots in dynamic environments, this paper proposes a system for calculating scene similarity based on point cloud data to comprehend the connections between two scenes. The point cloud data is acquired through ORB-SLAM2 and integrated with YOLOv5 to exclude dynamic interference, ensuring the precise capture of scene data. The similarity calculation system downsamples the input point cloud, uses the Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm for preprocessing and alignment of the point clouds, and adapts to variable observation conditions through point cloud enhancement techniques. Feature extraction employs self-attention mechanisms and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for dimensionality enhancement to capture the details of the points, and finally calculates the similarity of the feature vectors using random evaluation metrics. Experimental results show that in the TUM dataset and actual scene tests, the similarity of data collected multiple times in the same scene exceeds 90%, while the similarity in different scenes is below 70%.

articleTitle: Prescribed Performance Trajectory Tracking Control for an Underwater Vehicle-Manipulator System with FPTPPF
abstract: The problem of prescribed performance control for an underwater vehicle-manipulator system (UVMS) is investigated. Firstly, we design a predefined time control strategy that enables the system to achieve convergence within a predefined time. Secondly, considering the transportation and grasping work to be performed by the UVMS and to overcome the weaknesses of the existing predetermined performance functions, this project proposes to design an improved flexible predefined time-prescribed performance function (FPTPPF). Then, to ensure that the tracking error has a small overshoot, a control framework of an error transformation function with FPTPPF is employed, which achieves good tracking performance. And a new filter is designed to avoid the “complexity explosion” problem of the backstepping algorithm. Finally, the Lyapunov stability theory is used to prove the predetermined time stability of the closed-loop system, and the effectiveness of the control strategy is verified via numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Soft Variable Structure Controller Design for Descriptor Delta Operator Sampled Systems
abstract: For descriptor Delta operator sampled systems under the condition of complete controllability, a novel soft variable structure controller is designed in the paper. First, the system model is established according to the characteristics of the discretization method by Delta operator. Then, in terms of controller selection strategy, soft variable structure control (SVSC) with small chattering and fast reaching speed are considered. And then, the characteristics of SVSC under continuous time systems and discrete time systems are quite different, and the classical formula under continuous systems could make countless sub-controllers switch smoothly in a short time. This has different control characteristics from discrete time system where SVSC structure changes only at the sampling instants. Furthermore, the design of soft variable structure controller for descriptor Delta operator sampled systems, which makes the system reflect the characteristics of rapid convergence in the dynamic process. Finally, the proposed controller is simulated to show the feasibility and effectiveness of the control strategy.

articleTitle: The Shape Perception Method for Space Continuum Robot Based on Structure-Sensor Integration
abstract: Continuum robots are widely used in spacecraft interior detection and dangerous environment detection due to their multiple degrees of freedom and adaptability to narrow spaces. However, the shape perception problem of continuum robots seriously affects their closed-loop control and precise operation capabilities. This paper proposes a shape perception method based on a structural sensing integrated module, which helps to achieve high-precision shape perception of space continuum robots. First, the structural sensing integrated module is designed and its kinematics model is analyzed. Second, the data obtained by the sensor are processed by Kalman filtering, and a multiple keypoint error compensation method based on the BP neural network model is proposed. Next, a shape perception method based on Bezier curves is introduced, and a shape fitting accuracy evaluation index considering global information is designed. Then, an experiment is carried out on a shape perception test platform to verify the shape perception method of the continuum robot based on the BP neural network, and the experiments showed that its average relative distance error is less than 2.5%. Finally, slit crossing and docking tests are carried out on the space continuum robot, and the arrival accuracy is better than 3.5mm, which demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed shape perception method and its potential application in actual space missions.

articleTitle: ST-DCAN: Spatio-Temporal Dual Compression Attention Network for Traffic Prediction
abstract: With the rapid expansion of urban scale, the demand for precise traffic prediction is increasing. While existing traffic prediction models often incorporate complex components, their marginal benefits are diminishing. Additionally, these models struggle to extract generalized patterns among global nodes and segments, which impacts their performance. In response to these challenges, we introduce a transformer-based model, the Spatio-temporal Dual Compression Attention Network (ST-DCAN), which integrates a unified attention mechanism on input patches. Our approach reduces computational complexity from exponential to linear levels, enhances the extraction of both temporal and spatial information, and achieves state-of-the-art performance across three real-world traffic forecasting datasets with optimal computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Backstepping-Based Interception Control for an Underactuated ASV with Experimental Validation
abstract: This article puts forward an interception control system designed specifically for an Autonomous Surface Vehicle (ASV). The prime goal of this system is to capture a moving target whose speed may vary, even when there are unknown external disturbances such as waves, wind, and stream currents. By applying the sophisticated backstepping method, it can guarantee that the relative speed between the interceptor ASV and the target globally gets close to a neighborhood of the desired value. The effectiveness of this interception control approach has been thoroughly verified through simulations as well as practical experimental tests.

articleTitle: A Method for Surface Defect Detection of Tempered Glass Based on Polarization Characteristics and Unsupervised Learning
abstract: Self-detonation of tempered glass due to defects has always been a major problem in its engineering applications, and in the actual defect detection, it is susceptible to the interference of dust on tempered glass. In this paper, combining the different polarization characteristics of defects and dust, we design a polarization system combining polarizer and 1/4 wave plate to collect images, combined with deep learning for detection and differentiation. However, in the actual detection process, the samples of tempered glass with defects are relatively rare, and the probability density of abnormalities is low, typically resulting in a long-tailed distribution of normal and abnormal data. The lack of abnormal sample data leads to a low detection rate of defects by supervised learning methods, which can't satisfy the actual industrial inspection needs. Therefore, this paper proposes an unsupervised learning method based on FastFlow to solve the problem of insufficient abnormal samples. Finally, the experiments show that the unsupervised learning method based on polarization characteristics and FastFlow proposed in this paper effectively detects defects and distinguishes dust and the recall rate of defects reaches 96.1%, and the false detection rate is only 3.1%, which realizes the intelligent detection of tempered glass defects and meets the requirements of the industrial inspection of tempered glass.

articleTitle: A Dataset Production for Fault Diagnosis of Mining Induction Motors
abstract: Induction motors in coal mines face tough conditions, leading to more frequent breakdowns than regular motors. These failures increase maintenance costs and hinder safe mining operations. This paper examines the YB3 series explosion-proof motors, common in coal mines, and introduces a fault modeling approach using Maxwell software to analyze induction motor faults. Finite element simulations calculate stator currents under various conditions, creating datasets for stator-rotor faults in mining motors. The dataset's utility is validated by comparing fault characteristic simulation results with calculated outcomes, offering data support for fault detection and diagnosis in mining induction motors.

articleTitle: Study of a Combined Thrust-Torque Calibration Equipment with Uncertainty Evaluation
abstract: An innovative design approach is proposed for combined thrust-torque calibration equipment with an evaluation of its uncertainty. The combined thrust-torque calibration has been implemented in the control of the rotation rate drive-torque load braking mode, along with a new thrust-loading system design at a fixed rotation rate. In contrast to the conventional static calibration method, the proposed design method is more suitable for practical use in the shaft rotation. Uncertainty indices demonstrated the advancement of calibration equipment through uncertainty sources analysis and experiments.

articleTitle: Carbon Emission Evaluation Method for Distribution Networks Based on Entropy Method
abstract: As one of the main sources of carbon emission, the power industry's carbon emission evaluation and management become particularly important. In this paper, a carbon emission evaluation index system for distribution network considering carbon emission and low carbon benefit is proposed to improve the accuracy of carbon emission data and the reliability of evaluation results. Firstly, the carbon emission flow (CEF) model is established. Then, the carbon emission evaluation index system of distribution network is constructed in two dimensions of carbon emission and low carbon benefit. In addition, the determination method and evaluation method of index weight are also studied, and the scientificity and rationality of the method are verified by IEEE 33-node examples.

articleTitle: Motor Fault Diagnosis Under Complex Working Conditions Based on Signal Fusion and CA-CNN
abstract: Accurate fault diagnosis plays a key role in the safe and efficient operation of electrical motors. Aiming at multiclass motor fault diagnosis under complex working conditions, a signal fusion-based fault diagnosis framework is proposed. Measurement parameters from different sensors are first transformed by wavelet denoising and fast Fourier transform (FFT). Then, multiple parameters spectrum and working condition information are integrated and converted into high-dimension matrices. Finally, a channel-attention-based convolution neural network (CA-CNN) is proposed to extract fault patterns from a reconstructed matrix and output diagnosis results. Experiment results on both simulated and experimental datasets verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Study of Double Degree of Freedom Solar Arrays Control for Inclined-orbit Spacecraft
abstract: The spacecraft is powered by solar arrays. Solar arrays control problem for Inclined-orbit spacecraft, which has double degree freedom, is investigated in this paper. By analyzing the variation law of solar height angle, a double degree of freedom solar arrays control algorithm is designed, and the earth-oriented mode and attitude bias mode are studied respectively. Finally, by analyzing the data from the simulation test on the ground and the in-orbit test, it can be concluded that the proposed method is simple and feasible, and can ensure that the accuracy of solar panels orientation towards the sun remains within the allowable range for an extended period. In addition, the approach presented in this work can serve as a guide for the overall design of inclined orbit spacecraft aimed for an extended lifetime.

articleTitle: Knowledge Distillation Framework of Pre-Trained Language Models Combined with Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning
abstract: The development of pre-trained language models(PLMs) has increased the size of models, increasing the demand for computing resources and data when fine-tuning downstream tasks, and challenging deployment in resource-limited environments. In order to alleviate this demand, this paper proposes a knowledge distillation(KD) framework of PLMs combined with parameter efficient fine-tuning(PEFT). By introducing PEFT into both teacher fine-tuning and specific task distillation, the framework reduces computational costs without significantly compromising model performance. The experimental results show that in the GLUE benchmark test, the performance of the student model trained by the distillation framework on multiple NLU tasks is comparable to or even better than that of the teacher, and it shows higher efficiency and robustness in resource utilization.

articleTitle: Research on Temperature Control of Welding Wire Heating System Based on Smith Prediction
abstract: Aiming at the moisture attached to the surface of the wire after the copper plating process, an inductor is designed to dry the moisture on the wire by induction heating. The heating power supply of the inductor adopts medium-frequency induction heating power supply. After designing the model of the inductor, the theoretical calculation of each workpiece parameter is used to obtain the corresponding heating frequency, coil current, power supply configuration and other parameters, and then the COMSOL finite element software simulation method is used to numerically simulate the working state of each part and simulate the role of magnetic-thermal coupling, which concludes that it meets the design requirements and obtains a better effect in the industry. On this basis, this project proposes a new optimal design method of induction heating system based on Smith predictive PID, and through the comparative study with the control model without Smith predictive PID, it is found that this method can not only reduce the overshooting amount of induction heating, but also effectively improve its stable operation state, and it can satisfy the heating and drying requirements for the welding wires after copper plating.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Capacity Optimization for Integrated Energy Systems Considering Green Certificate Trading
abstract: Environmental pollution and energy crisis are becoming more and more serious all over the world, and the integrated energy system (IES) with renewable energy as the core is the key to energy conservation and emission reduction. Capacity optimization is the premise of efficient operation of the IES. Therefore, this paper focuses on solving the problem of capacity optimization of the IES considering green certificate trading. Firstly, the green certificate trading model is introduced. On this basis, the capacity optimization model of IES considering green certificate trading is proposed. Second, the basic architecture of the IES was constructed, and a detailed mathematical model was established for the main equipment of the system. Thirdly, the capacity optimization problem of the IES is studied and analyzed, and the model is solved by using the fast non-dominant ranking genetic algorithm with elite strategy with the optimal system economy and environmental friendliness as the objective function. Finally, a case analysis is carried out in combination with the data of a campus to verify the effectiveness of the model.

articleTitle: Depth Quality Enhancement and Feature Shrinking Guided RGB-D Salient Object Detection
abstract: Nowadays, depth cameras are equipped on many mobile devices, meanwhile RGB-D based salient object detection methods have made significant progress based on deep neural networks. However, poor quality depth images are not avoidable, which can certainly degrade the performance of current salient object detection method. Therefore, it is worthwhile to mitigate the impact of low-quality depth images while maintaining a lightweight model. This paper proposes a depth quality enhancement(DQE) and feature shrinking(FS) guided salient object detection network, named DEFSNet, which consists of RGB and depth streams based on MobileNet-V3 and depthwise separable convolution. The model also includes a Dice coefficient-based depth quality judgment(DQJ) mechanism to assign weights to each depth feature and a depth feature enhancement (DFE) structure to improve low-quality depth images. Finally, a feature shrinking structure is designed to fuse multi-scale features and output the saliency prediction map. Experimental results show that, compared to state-of-the-art salient object detection models, the proposed model achieves higher detection accuracy with a smaller number of parameters.

articleTitle: The Equipment Preventive Maintenance Strategy of Two-stage Spot Inspection Considering Different Detection Effects
abstract: For equipment deterioration state from light to heavy progressive characteristics, based on the theory of three-stage delay time, the preventive maintenance strategy of two-stage point inspection equipment considering different detection effects is proposed. In the first stage, the equipment is detected at period T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>. When the equipment is in a mild defect state, the detection is not perfect. If the equipment is found in a mild defect state, imperfect preventive maintenance will be carried out. If a device is found to be in a serious defect state, preventive replacement is required. When the equipment life reaches the threshold MT<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, there is still no failure or replacement, then the detection period is shortened to T2. In this stage, the equipment will be replaced regardless of whether it is in mild or serious defect. During the detection interval, if an unexpected fault occurs, the device shall be replaced. Considering all situations, T1, T2 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> were optimized with the aim of minimizing the maintenance cost per unit time. Compared with the equal-period detection model and the non-threshold model, the proposed two-stage spot-inspection strategy can always reduce the unit time maintenance cost more effectively, which verifies the effectiveness of the model.

articleTitle: Design and Verification of Reactor-Following-Load Coordinated Control Strategy for Modular High Temperature Gas-Cooled Reactor
abstract: A coordinated control strategy of “Reactor-Following-Load” for modular high temperature gas-cooled reactor HTR-PM600S is proposed, which can balance energy supply and demand between nuclear steam supply system and industrial heat supply system by maintaining main steam pressure. Simulation results based on the Simscape dynamical model verify that the control strategy can effectively control the pressure of the main steam pipe and perform the load-following.

articleTitle: A CMT-Based Approach for Skin Lesion Segmentation
abstract: The problem of skin lesion segmentation is addressed in this paper. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have be applied to deal with the image segmentation problem. However, the CNN-based image segmentation techniques may suffer from the problems of poor generalization and difficulty in capturing long-distance dependencies. In another hand, Transformer has the advantage of a flexible structure, but its ability to learn positional encoding of pixels in an image is often limited when facing fewer medical images. In this paper, a CNNs meets Transformer (CMT)-based approach is proposed for the skin lesion segmentation. The proposed approach's performance is scrutinized and juxtaposed against CNN-based methodologies (e.g., the InceptionNet-based, the ResNet-based, and the DenseNet-based) via extensive experiments on the ISIC2018 dataset. Compared to CNN-based methods, the results reveal that the proposed CMT-based approach enhances the skin lesion segmentation accuracy by a margin exceeding 8%.

articleTitle: Research on Improved SIFT Algorithm Based on Optimal Transmission Theory
abstract: The traditional SIFT algorithm is known for its time-consuming nature due to the high-dimensional feature descriptor and the weak anti-noise ability of matching resulting from a single matching strategy. In this paper, an improved SIFT feature matching algorithm based on optimal transmission theory is proposed. Firstly, PCA is utilized to reduce the dimension of the extracted descriptor, optimizing its structure and enhancing matching efficiency. Secondly, in order to address sensitivity to noise, a change in the matching strategy is implemented using iterative calculation of Sinkhorn distance as the distance metric and applying optimal transmission theory to establish matching relationships between descriptors. This reduces noise influence while improving stability and accuracy in image processing. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm enhances matching accuracy across different scenarios, achieving over 90% accuracy while reducing processing time and effectively improving performance.

articleTitle: An Evolutionary Game with Memory-Based Reputation in Networked Populations
abstract: The networked evolutionary game theory investigates the emergence of cooperative behaviors in the real world possible. Many reputation-based studies have made significant progress. However, reputation is easily forgotten in the real world, and only the reputation of loyal individuals remains. Therefore, in this paper, we focus on a reputation updating mechanism based on forgetting and explore how it influences the emergence and maintenance of cooperative behavior in complex networks. We creatively introduce a behavior threshold that influences the memory of reputation. In the simulation, we show the evolution of cooperation density over time, discuss the influence of behavior threshold on cooperation density, and further show the evolution of cooperators and defectors over time under different thresholds, which helps us understand the formation of cooperation. Results show that the mechanism we propose helps to overcome social dilemmas.

articleTitle: Enhancing Few-Shot Plant Disease Classification with Diffusion Model
abstract: Plant diseases significantly threaten global agriculture, impacting crop yield and quality, thus affecting food security and economic stability. Traditional detection methods, reliant on expert knowledge and manual inspection, are time-consuming and error-prone. Few-shot classification methods, including meta-learning, transfer learning, and data augmentation, have gained attention. Meta-learning adapts models quickly across tasks but requires substantial computational resources. Transfer learning enhances related task performance, reducing data needs but risking negative transfer. Traditional data augmentation, like image flipping and rotation, offers limited effectiveness. We propose an advanced generative model-based plant disease data augmentation method using Stable Diffusion models to generate high-quality synthetic data, integrated with ControlNet and Embbedings for precise control, and fine-tuned by Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). This method overcomes traditional limitations by generating diverse, high-quality samples, enhancing dataset diversity and model generalization, thereby facilitating robust and accurate plant disease detection model development.

articleTitle: Adaptive Consensus Control of Nonlinear Multiagent Systems Based on Event-Triggered Mechanism Under Dos Attacks
abstract: The issue of nonlinear multiagent systems consensus control has attained more and more attention with the development of network technology. To handle such require-ments, a multiagent systems fuzzy adaptive control scheme under denial-of-service attacks (DoS attacks) and sensor attacks by using dynamic event-triggered mechanism which reduces network communication burden is proposed. Firstly, Fuzzy-Logic System(FLS) is used to approximate the unknown nonlinear part of the systems. Secondly, because of the sensor attacks, all states and the real outputs can't be measured, a distributed states observer by utilizing the disturbed output is designed to deal with the problem. Finally, combining with the backstepping scheme and through theoretical derivation and simulation results based on the second-order system model, the control scheme which aims to ensure the output consistency of the leader-less multi-agent system without Zeno behavior is verified.

articleTitle: Research on Real-Time Welding Spot Extraction Algorithm for Welding Seam Tracking
abstract: The precision of weld point extraction is significantly influenced by disturbances such as arc light and splattering during welding processes. This paper proposes a real-time weld point extraction algorithm designed for weld seam tracking using binocular laser vision. Initially, to capture laser stripes during welding, we utilize the Yolov8 deep learning framework integrated with the lightweight HGNetv2 network backbone. The Neck section incorporates the FDPN (Focusing Diffusion Pyramid Network) to enhance feature detection accuracy. Introducing the InnerIoU bounding box loss in the loss function accelerates model convergence, resulting in a 1.9% improvement in stripe instance segmentation accuracy and achieving an inference speed of 172 FPS. After extracting laser stripes, image processing is applied to identify the coordinates of weld points from the left view. Spatial 3D coordinates of weld points are determined using left-right camera disparity, enabling real-time extraction of weld point 3D coordinates. Experimental validation confirms welding errors within 0.9 mm and a tracking speed of 33 FPS, meeting the real-time weld seam tracking requirements.

articleTitle: CoFMD-BiLSTM: A Wind and Photovoltaic Power Prediction Method Based on Feature Mode Decomposition and Cooperative Learning Strategy
abstract: With the increasing penetration of new energy sources such as wind and solar, accurate source-side power forecasting helps power system dispatchers to obtain new energy pre-output plans and improve the power system's new energy consumption capacity through the coordination of multiple power generation resources. The wind and photovoltaic power data are characterized by large fluctuations, strong nonlinearity, instability, and strong time dependence, etc. Through “Decomposition-Prediction”, the original sequence is decomposed into a number of sub-sequences, which reduces the volatility and randomness of the original sequence, and has been widely used in wind and photovoltaic power prediction. In order to solve the problem that traditional decomposition algorithms have insufficient decomposition capability to extract data features in a targeted and effective way, we propose a wind and photovoltaic power prediction method based on Feature Mode Decomposition and Cooperative Learning Strategy: the CoFMD-BiLSTM model. A novel emerging decomposition algorithm, Feature Mode Decomposition (FMD), originally applied in fault detection, is introduced. By designing a Cooperative Learning Strategy to learn and fit the decomposition sequence information obtained from the FMD decomposition covering different features, which is fed into the BiLSTM model to obtain the wind and light power predictions. The actual operation data of Sotavento Galicia (sg) wind farm in Spain and TuoZhuo photovoltaic farm in Yunnan, China are used. Compared with the two models, VMD-BiLSTM and BiLSTM, the validation results show that the wind and solar power prediction method based on the CoFMD-BiLSTM model can effectively improve the accuracy of wind and solar power prediction.

articleTitle: Optimization Method on Single Radiation Source and INS Localization of UAV by Geometric Projection
abstract: To achieve self-positioning of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) during motion, this paper proposes a geometric projection method for UAV flight along a straight line, from which the yaw angle is derived. Subsequently, the nonlinear least squares (NLS) method is employed to optimize the pseudo-measurement of the yaw after clutter elimination, followed by an error analysis. The simulation results show that the optimized pseudo-measurement is superior to the unoptimized pseudo-measurement in terms of error convergence speed and ultimate error, and verifies the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Predictive Maneuver for UAV Air Combat Confrontation Based on Game Theory
abstract: This paper presents a game theory-based decision-making algorithm for air combat maneuvers. The Dubins minimum achievable distance is introduced to replace the Euclidean distance, and situation assessment function is reconstructed as the utility function of the game model, providing a more accurate basis for maneuver decisions. To effectively handle different opponents UAVs, their autonomous maneuvering capabilities are graded, and corresponding strategies are formulated to enhance tactical flexibility. Meanwhile, the model predictive control method is used to optimize the real-time maneuver decisions based on the anticipated battlefield dynamics. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Adaptive Task Allocation for Multi-UAV Systems Using a Novel Dynamic Distributed Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Efficient Distributed Performance Impact (DEDPI) algorithm for optimizing task allocation in multi-UAV systems operating in dynamic environments. The algorithm overcomes the limitations of existing approaches, specifically the suboptimal solutions of dynamic task algorithms and the computational inefficiencies of extending static algorithms to dynamic contexts, by dynamically adjusting task queues and employing a novel objective function to enhance resource allocation and responsiveness. Experimental results demonstrate that DEDPI significantly increases the number of completed tasks while reducing the average task execution cost, providing an effective solution for real-time, mission-critical UAV operations.

articleTitle: A Novel Two-Stage Robot Grasping Detection Method
abstract: Selecting predefined targets for grasping based on diverse requirements in actual environments is a critical issue in the field of robotic grasping. To address this problem, this paper propose a novel two-step cascading method. First, we propose a lightweight target detection backbone GhostNetV2S, which replaces the standard convolution with Ghost convolution to enable real-time detection of the region of interest in the RGB image. Then, the RGB image and the depth image are cropped with the region of interest as the center to reduce the interference between the object and the background. Finally, The cropped images are input into generative residual convolutional neural network to determine the optimal grasping position of the target. We conduct qualitative and quantitative comparative experiments on the Cornell and VMRD datasets. Simultaneously, we conduct a robot grasping experiment in a real-world scenario, and the success rate of robot grasping reaches 97%, experimentally verifying the reliability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Intelligent Track Association Method Based on Deep and Composite Features
abstract: Track-to-track association plays an important role in multi-sensor tracking and fusion system. The correct rate of association will directly influence the accuracy of tracking in multi-sensor system. However, when the number of targets increases, using only traditional motion features could lead to a decrease in the correct rate of association due to their insufficient representation capability. In this paper, the fuzzy based track association is improved by using deep features of tracks extracted by neural network and motion model probability obtained with Interactive Multi-Model (IMM). A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is constructed with residual structure to extract deep features of tracks, and the fuzzy association factors is redesigned by deep features and model probability in this paper. The effectiveness of the proposed method is illustrated by various simulation scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method has better performances compared with traditional methods.

articleTitle: A Student Classroom Behavior Detection System Based on Improved YOLOv10
abstract: The detection and analysis of students' classroom behavior is of great significance for schools to understand students' classroom learning status, classroom teaching evaluation and promote the improvement of teaching quality. Different classroom seat layouts and smaller targets away from cameras will seriously affect the effectiveness of detection. To solve these problems, this paper proposes a student classroom behavior detection system based on the improved YOLOv10. Firstly, we constructed a multi-view student behavior dataset with different seat layouts for model learning and training. Secondly, the backbone network of the YOLOv10 model was modified by replacing the C2f and C2fCIB modules with the Dynamic Snake Convolution module, which can adaptively adjust the shape and size of the convolution kernel during the convolution process, thereby better capturing the features of small targets or fine structures. The experimental results show that the improved YOLOv10 algorithm achieved a mAP@O.S of 87.1 %, and increased the mAP by 3% compared to the original YOLOv10. Lastly, the system also implemented a user interface (UI) that visually reflects the students' behavior status. The evaluation outcomes showed that the proposed system can detect and count student behaviors in the classroom with acceptable results in changing scenarios.

articleTitle: An Improved Data Mapping Method and Sensitivity Analysis for Roadside LiDAR
abstract: LiDAR technology is gaining significance in the transportation sector because of its ability to gather detailed 3D traffic data. Unlike conventional sensors, LiDAR provides highresolution micro-traffic information, independent of lighting conditions. However, the absence of an effective mapping technique has hindered its broader adoption. This study introduces a novel data mapping approach for roadside LiDAR sensors, leveraging GIS-related software. The process involves collecting reference points using both GIS tools and the LiDAR sensor, followed by three key steps: matching reference points, calculating the transformation matrix, and performing data mapping. Post-mapping, a sensitivity analysis was conducted to optimize the number and placement of reference points. Realworld data validation revealed a 0.138m discrepancy between the GPS-measured and calculated points. Additionally, a comparative analysis with another mapping method showed an average deviation of 2.21m per frame of data, which contained 37,832 LiDAR points.

articleTitle: Link Prediction by a Node Pair Similarity Based Method with Unknown Number of Missing Links
abstract: This paper considers the problem of link prediction in networks with unknown number of missing links in a partial observation. We first estimate the number of missing links by solving an optimization problem, in which the objective function is to maximize the clustering coefficient of a network, subject to a Kullback-Leibler divergence constraint. Then based on this estimation, we propose an optimization approach to identify the potential missing links. The proposed approach uses both the node similarities and links in the observation and calculates the existence likelihood of missing links based on node pair similarities. Experiments in synthetic networks verify the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Based SOC Equalization Control Strategy for Distributed Battery Energy Storage System
abstract: In the battery energy management system, it is important to maintain the consistency of state of charge (SOC). In this paper, a multi-agent based SOC equalization control strategy is proposed for power regulation in distributed battery energy storage system (BESS). Each agent is independently controlled and only exchanges data with neighboring agents, which greatly reducing computation and improving the fault tolerance and scalability. To improve the efficiency of SOC equalization, an optimization method considering energy loss and equalization time is presented. Simulation results show that the multi-agent based SOC equalization control strategy proposed in this paper can reduce the energy loss and equalization time, and effectively cope with some system failures.

articleTitle: Hydroponic Cultivation Control System Based on Multi-Sensor Parameter Inputs
abstract: Hydroponic cultivation technology, as an advanced soilless growing method, has been widely applied in modern agriculture in recent years. To enhance the automation level and cultivation efficiency of hydroponic systems, this paper designs and implements a hydroponic cultivation control system based on multi-sensor parameter inputs. The system integrates various sensors, such as temperature sensors, humidity sensors, pH sensors, and electrical conductivity sensors, to monitor the parameters of the hydroponic environment in real-time and performs dynamic adjustments through intelligent control algorithms. The goal is to achieve real-time monitoring and adjustment of key parameters in the hydroponic environment, thereby improving the automation level and production efficiency of the hydroponic system and ultimately increasing crop yields.

articleTitle: INR-ECGAN: An Enhanced Conditional GAN with Implicit Neural Representation for SAR-to-Optical Image Translation
abstract: The SAR-to-Optical image translation task helps solve the interpretability of SAR images and has attracted much attention from researchers in recent years. Although existing methods based on conditional generative adversarial network (CGAN) have shown appealing potential for this task, the optical images generated by them still suffer from blurred details and color distortion. To this end, a novel enhanced CGAN with implic-it neural representation (INR-ECGAN) is proposed in this paper. Specifically, the proposed method utilizes convolutional residual blocks to encode the semantic features of SAR images at multiple scales. Then, a pyramid pooling module is employed to mine the global information of deep semantic features. Subsequently, an implicit decoder is designed to fuse the multi-scale semantic and global features and estimate a continuous function mapping from the fused features to the optical images. Finally, a discriminator that can simultaneously distinguish the generated and real optical images at multiple scales is adopted to improve the translation performance. Extensive experiments on public datasets have demonstrated the superiority of INR-ECGAN. The code will be available at https://github.com/lyltbafwIINR-ECGAN.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Migratory Bird Optimization Algorithm for solving the Large-Scale Flow Shop Scheduling Problem
abstract: The flow-shop scheduling problem (FSP) is significant in modern industry, with increasing complexity and computation time as the scheduling scale grows. To address this, this paper integrates the Migratory Bird Optimization (MBO) algorithm with the Simulated Annealing (SA) algorithm. This hybrid approach leverages MBO's robust global search and SA's effectiveness in avoiding local optima. The hybrid MBO algorithm aims to minimize makespan, supporting automated, intelligent, and unmanned production in core workshops. Parts of the Taillard benchmark are used to verify the proposed SAMBO algorithm's performance, comparing it with the memetic and hybrid genetic algorithms. Experimental results show that SAMBO better saves processing time.

articleTitle: A Robust Cubature Kalman Filter for INS/CNS Integrated Navigation with Measurement Outliers
abstract: To tackle the reduced filtering efficacy in INS/CNS integrated navigation systems faced with measurement outliers, this study introduces a robust cubature Kalman filter (RCKF) that employs hypothesis testing to boost the CKF's resilience to these outliers. Within the RCKF framework, a chi-square test (HT) along with an enhanced sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) are employed for online estimation and adjustment of the measurement noise covariance. Simulation experiments confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Data-Enhanced Multi-Objective Optimization for Hot Rolling Load Distribution
abstract: This paper addresses the multi-objective load distribution optimization problem in the rolling process, concerning three optimization targets of balancing rolling force margin, minimizing total rolling power, and ensuring desirable strip shape. In addition to exit thickness, bending force and roll shift position are also incorporated as decisive variables, both exerting significant influence on strip shape. Notably, while a data-driven model trained by neural networks predicts the final strip crown, the strip crown during rolling is determined using a simplified mathematical model. Such an optimization model considers a more comprehensive range of influences compared with previous studies, making it more realistic and accurate. Besides, the NSGA-II algorithm is employed to identify the Pareto optimal set. Through simulation using real product data from a domestic steel company, the effectiveness and practical applicability of the proposed approach are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Model Adversarial Attack and Defense Based on Network Reorganization
abstract: To address the tradeoff issues in adversarial training of deep neural networks, where enhancing one performance metric often compromises another; the gradual decrease in model robustness in the later stages of training; or the sudden drop in robustness after a specific training stage, etc. This article mainly starts from two perspectives: modifying the network architecture and applying improved adversarial training methods. By adding the CBAM dual attention mechanism and DropBlock regularization technology to the existing wide residual network WideResNet_22_10, the accuracy and robustness of the model are improved to a certain extent. Experimental results demonstrate that TRADES, an enhanced adversarial training approach, surpasses conventional methods in strengthening model resilience against powerful adversarial attacks.

articleTitle: GPNet: Point Cloud Semantic Segmentation Network for Off-Road Scenes
abstract: Semantic segmentation of point clouds plays a critical role in autonomous driving as it enables the processing of lidar-obtained data to achieve environmental perception. While significant progress has been made in the semantic segmentation of point clouds in urban traffic environments, research on off-road scenes has been limited due to a lack of datasets. In this paper, we present a semantic segmentation model for point clouds, tailored to address the unique challenges of off-road environments. Given the characteristics of off-road scenes, such as indistinct boundaries, uneven terrain, irregular features, and relatively few occlusions, our model utilizes a projection method to segment point cloud data into Bird's Eye View (BEV) and extracts adjacent features through adaptive graph convolution to compensate for lost information during projection. Our model achieves high performance on Rellis-3D and SemanticKITTI datasets.

articleTitle: Deep Longitudinal Dynamic Model for Electric Semi-Trailer Trucks with Varying Load
abstract: For the autonomous driving of semi-trailer trucks, the main challenge is the model uncertainty caused by the vehicle structure complexity and working condition variation. This paper concentrates on the longitudinal dynamic modeling problem, which describes the longitudinal motion characteristics of a varying load semi-trailer truck. A deep neural network based method is proposed to deal with the underfitting problem of conventional empirical modeling methods. The model is designed according to the physical structure, including driving and braking subsystems, using engine and braking throttle signals as input. The output of subsystems are integrated to predict the acceleration and velocity. This model is time-varying w.r.t. vehicle states, which are encoded as the network features to describe the coupling effect between lateral and longitudinal dynamics. Different working load is considered explicitly by the mass ratio in the model and is simultaneously identified in the training and inference process. Experimental results are provided to show the effectiveness of the proposed model using real driving data.

articleTitle: Research on Temperature Control System Based on Cheetah Optimization Fuzzy PID Algorithm
abstract: With the rapid development of industrial automation and intelligent control technology, temperature control systems have been deployed in many fields, such as process control, biomedical engineering and electric drives. However, the performance of traditional PID controllers is often far from acceptable when running in temperature control systems with high nonlinearity and complexity. To fix this problem, this paper first proposes a thermal network modeling and refinement method based on the Cauer model. Based on this model, this paper creates a fuzzy PID control method based on the Cheetah optimization algorithm to improve the robustness and response speed of the temperature control system. The simulation results show that the step response curve of the system with the CO-fuzzy PID controller reaches the stable state in 0.64 seconds, while the traditional PID controller takes 1.14 seconds. Moreover, the overshoot of the CO-fuzzy PID controller is far less than that of the traditional PID controller. Therefore, with such good dynamic and static characteristics, the CO-fuzzy PID controller in this paper is believed to have a wide range of applications and be particularly suitable for industrial areas requiring accurate temperature control.

articleTitle: A Self-Attention Enhanced Method for Non-Invasive Breast Cancer Grading on Magnetic Resonance Imaging
abstract: Breast cancer represents the most prevalent malig-nancy and the leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women globally. Current grading systems rely on conventional pathological criteria necessitating invasive procedures for tissue or cellular acquisition, which are labor-intensive, subjective, and invasive. This paper introduces a non-invasive end-to-end deep learning framework for breast cancer grading. It marks the inau-gural attempt to deploy deep learning methodologies on breast cancer magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), providing evidence for imaging biomarkers of breast cancer. Addressing the fine-grained and multi-scale lesions inherent in datasets, we propose a feature fusion approach based on self-attention mechanisms. Experimental results validate the feasibility of exploring breast cancer biomarkers on MRI through deep learning methodologies, with the novel feature fusion strategy enhancing the extraction of salient pixel information and augmenting classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of Time-Varying Compound Control System for Hypersonic Vehicle
abstract: Aiming at aerodynamic parameters variation of hypersonic vehicle during flight, a time-varying composite control system is proposed. The composite control system consists of an aerodynamic system generated by pneumatic rudder and a thrust system generated by the engine. In the aerodynamic system, a controller is designed by the linear quadratic regulator. When aerodynamic rudder is unable to continuously generate control force and torque, a lateral thrust is added to the system. A sliding mode theory is used to design the controller of compound control system with lateral thrust. To reduce the chattering phenomenon and ensure the system stability, fuzzy control is introduced. Finally, the effectiveness of designed time-varying composite controllers and the stability of the system are verified by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Disturbance Observer-Based Hysteretic Quantized Fuzzy Control for Nonlinear Parabolic PDE System
abstract: This paper investigates the disturbance observer-based hysteretic quantized fuzzy control for nonlinear parabolic partial differential equation (PDE) system with disturbances. The system contains two types of disturbances, one is bounded disturbance from outside, and the other is generated along with the control input and can be depicted by the ordinary differential equation (ODE). We initially adopt the Galerkin technique to separate the PDE system into fast subsystem and slow subsystem, and the slow subsystem can describe the main dynamics properties of the system. Then, we obtain a fuzzy system by the Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy technique. Next, we design the disturbance observer based on the external ODE system. On this basis, a hysteresis quantized controller is designed to be semi-globally uniformly ultimately bounded. Finally, a simulation example shows the effectiveness.

articleTitle: Finger Vein Recognition Algorithm Based on MobileNet and ConvNeXt
abstract: Finger vein recognition is an emerging biometric technology with broad application prospects in the field of security. It has the advantages of high anti-counterfeiting, high security and ease of use. However, current finger vein recognition algorithms still have limited accuracy due to incomplete feature extraction. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a finger vein recognition algorithm based on the MobileNet and ConvNeXt network (M-Cnet). M-Cnet uses ConvNeXt to extract the overall features of the finger vein image, and uses MobileNet to extract the local detail features of the image. Finally, the overall features and local features are weighted and fused, and the recognition classification is performed on this basis. The experimental results show that M-Cnet can effectively extract finger vein features with high recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: VDA-YOLOv8 An Improved YOLOv8 Network Model for Vehicle Detection
abstract: Vehicle detection is of great significance to intelligent transportation systems and autonomous driving. However, due to many complex uncertainties associated with real traffic scenarios, such as bad weather, occlusion, motion blur and illuminance differences achieving precise and real-time vehicle detection continues to be a challenging task. To minimize the impact of uncertainties in real-world environments and enhance both the real-time and accuracy of vehicle detection, this paper proposes the VDA-YOLOv8 network model. First, the structural re-parameterization technique is employed to build a C2f-DBB module, which combine the Diverse Branch Block with the C2f to reinforce the feature extraction ability of the network. In addition, Bi-Level Routing Attention is introduced to help the model locate the interest region and suppress useless information. Finally, P2 detection layer is added to make the model more effective in detecting and locating small targets. Our algorithm improves the precision by 3.5%, mAP50 by 4.3%. The detection speed reaches 108.69 FPS. Our algorithm reaches better balance between accuracy and speed compared with other algorithms.

articleTitle: Identification and Decoding Technology of EEG Under Complex Visual Stimuli Using Clustering Ensemble
abstract: Accurate target recognition in complex backgrounds is the primary key step for aircraft to achieve sensitive perception and control. Traditional computer vision based object recognition technology is difficult to fully meet practical application needs for complex and open flight environment scenarios such as camouflage and variants. Its recognition accuracy and other performance are still far lower than manual interpretation. This article innovatively proposes an analysis method for identifying and decoding EEG signals under complex visual stimuli based on clustering ensemble. Firstly, this paper design the method for collecting and preprocessing EEG under visual stimulation obtain effective EEG information that can be represented in relevant visual stimuli; Further research was conducted on the time-domain and time-frequency feature extraction techniques for EEG signals to obtain EEG feature information with effective discriminative power under different stimulation; Finally, a clustering model for multi domain and multi-scale EEG mixed features was constructed, and a clustering ensemble model construction method for multiple subjects was designed to achieve strong generalization EEG identification and decoding across subjects under visual stimuli, thereby realizing perceptual recognition of relevant visual stimuli. The experimental results in this paper indicate that the proposed approach can precisely identify the target of interest in the image, promote the quantitative analysis of human brain signal representation models under visual stimuli, and promote the development of new brain inspired target recognition technologies.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control Strategy of Virtual Inertia Based on Particle Swarm Optimization
abstract: With the widespread application of renewable energy, optimizing grid frequency stability has become particularly important. This paper proposes a coordinated control strategy for virtual inertia based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) to improve the frequency response in photovoltaic grid-connected systems. By simulating the characteristics of synchronous machines and combining high-pass filters and the PSO algorithm, this study develops a new control framework that dynamically adjusts virtual inertia. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy significantly optimizes the frequency recovery process and reduces frequency fluctuations caused by sudden load changes. Moreover, compared to traditional methods, the strategy proposed in this paper not only maintains system stability but also reduces voltage fluctuations, thereby proving its potential application in modern power grids.

articleTitle: Design of Multifunctional Health Management Desktop Robot
abstract: With the increasing use of computers for learning, office work, and scientific research, health issues such as cervical spine disease, lumbar disc herniation, and muscle degeneration (in the legs and buttocks) are becoming more common due to prolonged sitting or poor posture. In response to this situation, we have designed a multifunctional health management desktop robot that utilizes machine vision technology to analyze human posture and facial micro-expressions in real time. The robot provides real-time voice reminders and visual relaxation exercise solutions on the screen when it detects poor posture, such as slouching, prolonged sitting, or signs of fatigue during work. Additionally, the robot is equipped with a range of software features, including a Pomodoro timer and weather forecasting, to further enhance the user's work efficiency. This innovative approach aims to promote health and productivity in a modern work environment dominated by sedentary activities.
