articleTitle: Collaborative Active and Reactive Power Control Based on Distributed Event Triggered Heavy Ball Method
abstract: With the increasing integration of distributed energy into distribution networks, the demand for advanced voltage control is increasing. This paper introduces a novel approach for coordinating real and reactive power in distributed power systems, employing the decentralized event-triggered heavy ball algorithm. This strategy allows the power system to maintain voltage stability and frequency maintenance within an integrated framework. In this article, we employ the distributed event-triggered heavy ball technique, which integrates the dual-based heavy ball approach into the conventional dual iteration process by introducing supplementary momentum components to expedite the convergence rate. Meanwhile, event triggering conditions are designed on the bivariate to modify the control scheme and further reduce communication burden. The use of linearized models as a basis provides convergence results for the design process and theoretical examination of controllers. The control strategy proposed in this article can efficiently reduce communication expenses and expedite the convergence rate.

articleTitle: Robust Extended Kalman Filter for Nonlinear Singular System
abstract: In this paper, for the stochastic singular systems with nonlinear measurement, a robust extended Kalman filtering algorithm is proposed. The original singular system is transformed into a standard system through the application of the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) method and the state augmented approach. The nonlinear measurement is handled using the Taylor series expansion method, where the higher-order terms of the linearization error are represented by norm-bounded uncertainties. Further, a time-varying filter is designed by defining a new augmented system and introducing the variance constraint method, which ensures the upper bound of the filtering error covariance. Finally, to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed filtering algorithm, a simulation example is provided.

articleTitle: Point Cloud Registration Method Based on Bidirectional Search and Curvature Information
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of registering unorganized point clouds without prior information and proposes a robust automatic point cloud registration method. This method is designed to overcome the sensitivity of the classical Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm to initial poses and its tendency to get trapped in local optima. The algorithm utilizes local information to filter feature points and construct feature descriptors, and then combines with the Random Sample Consensus (RANSAC) algorithm for coarse point cloud registration. The classical ICP algorithm is improved by using bidirectional search and constraints based on distance and curvature to obtain correct correspondences, achieving precise point cloud registration. Experimental results of point cloud registration demonstrate that this algorithm has significant advantages in terms of robustness and registration accuracy.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Control for Triple Inverted Pendulum Based on Three-Step Method
abstract: In order to enhance the stabilization control performance of the triple inverted pendulum system, a nonlinear controller based on the three-step method is proposed. Firstly, the state space model of the triple inverted pendulum is established. Secondly, the stabilization control law is derived in according with three-step method, that is, homeostatic-like control, reference dynamic feed-forward control and Error feedback control. Finally, the stability of the closed-loop system is proved by the Lyapunov stability theory. Simulation results show that the proposed control strategy has shorter settling time and smaller overshooting and control input, compared with the LQR algorithm optimized by PSO-AFSA and the Robust H∞based on LMI.

articleTitle: Research on Control Method of Free-floating Platform for Microgravity Experiment
abstract: For the Free-floating Platform for Microgravity Experiment (FPME), this paper explores the optimal control problem for microgravity level within a specified duration. The paper proposes a control strategy of “the outer body of FPME ideally follows the inner body, while the inner body plans and follows the optimal motion trajectory for microgravity level.” Firstly, a high-precision dynamic model of China's Space Station (CSS), the outer body, and the inner body is established to lay the foundation for trajectory planning and controller design. Then, the inner body uses the convex optimization method to plan and follow the optimal motion trajectory for microgravity level. An active disturbance rejection controller is used in the outer body of FPME to avoid collision and reduce the influence of disturbance on the microgravity level of the inner body. Simulations show that the control strategy can plan and track the optimal trajectory of microgravity level according to the experiment duration and has good vibration isolation effect.

articleTitle: LSTD: Stable Triangle Descriptor of Line Keypoints for Loop Closing in 3D Lidar SLAM
abstract: Loop closing is a crucial module in simultaneous localization and mapping(SLAM), enabling the identification of revisited locations and facilitating trajectory correction. However, the high dimensionality, sparsity, and susceptibility to occlusions of LiDAR-generated point clouds pose significant challenges for this task. We propose Stable Triangle Descriptor of Line Keypoints(LSTD), which extracts texture-rich line features as keypoints and constructs stable triangular features. This descriptor encapsulates both geometric and spatial characteristics, and remains resilient to changes in LiDAR viewing angles, thereby enhancing loop closing capabilities. We devise a voting-based scheme for descriptor matching and leverage the circumscribed circle feature of triangles to enable efficient loop closure detection. Comparative evaluations on the KITTI dataset demonstrate the improvements offered by our approach. Furthermore, we integrate the algorithm into LiDAR SLAM and validate its efficacy on the KITTI dataset as well as our own dataset, showcasing its ability to accurately identify loops and refine the system's trajectory and point cloud map.

articleTitle: An Effective Heuristic Algorithm for the Two-Dimensional Orthogonal Packing Problem
abstract: This paper investigates the classic two-dimensional orthogonal packing problem (2DOPP), which aims to determine whether a set of rectangular items can be packed orthogonally into a given rectangular container. To address this problem, we introduce a new scoring rule for evaluating the positions of rectangular items and design a skyline-based decoding procedure. Moreover, based on this decoding procedure, we propose a randomized local search method to rapidly improve the solution quality. We assess the performance of the local search algorithm by applying it to a set of benchmark instances, which were extensively used in the literature. The computational results demonstrate that the decoding procedure can quickly generate a packing configuration and that the proposed local search algorithm is highly effective. Experimental analysis shows that the scoring function plays a crucial role for the high performance of proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Fault Estimation for Nonlinear Stochastic Systems with Imprecise Time-Varying Noise Statistics
abstract: In this paper, the issue of fault estimation is investi-gated for nonlinear stochastic systems subjected to inexact noise covariance matrices. Due to the system's nonlinear characteristics and the unknown noise covariance matrix, designing the fault estimator and estimating state probability density function (PDF) are highly challenging. Initially, an augmentation vector is introduced, which incorporates both system state and sensor fault information, and a nonlinear augmented system is constructed. Subsequently, an enhanced fault estimation method is developed for nonlinear systems, integrating the variational Bayesian in-ference technique with a particle approximation approach. The method utilizes a particle filter, where the weights of the particles are computed iteratively to approximate the posterior probability density of the state. Furthermore, unlike other intricate fault estimators, the proposed method can adaptively estimate the unknown noise covariance matrix during the filtering process. Ultimately, through numerical simulations and experiments, the proposed method's validity and feasibility are confirmed. It demonstrates superior estimation accuracy compared to conventional fault estimation methods.

articleTitle: Attention-Based Variational Encoding Regression Method of Predicting Engine Remaining Useful Life
abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction result for turbofan engine is critical to aircraft safety, however, the complex operation conditions and high-dimensional monitoring data seriously affect the prediction performance. To address the problems, this article presents an attention-based variational encoding regression model. The proposed method adopted variational auto-encoder whose total loss function jointly considers the reconstruction error and the prediction error for improving the feature exaction ability and prediction performance. furthermore, bi-directional gated recurrent unit (Bi-GRU) neural network and attention mechanism are adopted to exact and focus on the important hidden features effectively. Experiments based on four datasets are conducted to assess the effectiveness of the model, compared to other methods, this method can achieve superior performance.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based Dynamics Control of Biped Reconfigurable Robots for Standing Balancing Tasks
abstract: This paper presents a standing balance control scheme for biped reconfigurable robots (BRRs) via neuro-dynamic programming (NDP) method. First, a global dynamic model of BRRs is established, in which the torso model is approximated by utilizing the virtual model control (VMC). Then, the cost function is developed including the system state, control law, and the coupling torque between the torso and legs, to construct the optimal standing balance control framework. On the basis of NDP algorithm, the near-optimal standing balance control strategy is developed by designing the critic-only neural network to solve the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation. Then, the tracking error of closed-loop BRRs is proved to be uniformly ultimately bounded. Finally, a series of experimental studies are carried out on the self-designed hyper-redundant BRRs experimental platform to show the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Water Quality Prediction in Wastewater Treatment Process Using Lasso Echo State Network
abstract: Aiming at the effluent water quality prediction in the wastewater treatment process (WWTP), a lasso echo state network (LESN) is proposed. LESN uses the lasso regularization method instead of linear regression to learn the output weights, the coordinate descent method is used to train LESN. The simulations confirm that LESN can well handle the collinearity problem compared with other ESN models. Effluent water quality prediction is well done, LESN has higher prediction accuracy and generalization ability.

articleTitle: CameraLink Interface Design Based on 3.5x Frequency Encoded Clock
abstract: Based on the EG4D20 FPGA chip of AnLogic Falcon series, this paper builds an image transmission platform with CameraLink interface, and proposes a CameraLink interface design scheme with low clock frequency requirements. Compared with the traditional implementation of the CameraLink interface of the LVDS transmitter chip, this design reduces power consumption and cost. Compared with the existing FPGA-based CameraLink interface IP, the proposed solution successfully optimizes the 7 -octave encoded clock to a 3.5-octave encoded clock, which increases the consumption of logic resources, but greatly reduces the clock frequency requirements of the CameraLink interface and the power consumption of the interface on the FPGA. The paper tests the pixel clock frequency of 85MHz, the prior art requires a 595MHz coded clock, and the design scheme only needs a 297.5MHz coded clock, and the power consumption of the former is 0.111W after the test of AnLogic power analysis tool, while the power consumption of the design scheme is 0.08W, and the power consumption is reduced by 27.9%.

articleTitle: Neural Network-Based Funnel Adaptive Surge Motion Tracking Control of Autonomous Underwater Vehicle with Unknown Deadzone
abstract: This paper investigates the asymptotic state tracking control with guaranteed transient performance for the surge motion of autonomous underwater vehicles with unknown input deadzone. A neural network-based funnel adaptive controller is designed based on Lyapunov theory, with funnel control strategy used to guarantee tracking performance. Neural network is used to approximate uncertainty. Robust strategy is adopted for the compensation of input deadzone. To reduce the design complexity, a differentiator is constructed to estimate the time derivative of virtual control law. The control algorithm can not only guarantee asymptotic state tracking, but also transient performance. The simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on Top-Down Collaborative Product Design Method
abstract: This paper introduces a top-down collaborative design methodology rooted in the concept of initiating product development from a holistic perspective, encompassing overall scheme planning, layout design, and subsystem refinement, down to detailed component engineering. This approach transcends software platform constraints and harmoniously integrates with the R&D workflows prevalent across industries, especially in large-scale, interdisciplinary product development endeavors. The core of our proposal revolves around a skeleton model-based framework that encompasses the establishment of a collaborative platform, outlining a top-down collaborative design strategy, and facilitating parallel design efforts across departments. This ensures that product conception stems from a unified vision, with seamless intent communication and efficient multi-disciplinary labor division, ultimately culminating in a comprehensive digital prototype equipped with models suitable for advanced applications like finite element analysis and motion simulation, fostering innovation and efficiency in the entire design lifecycle.

articleTitle: From ByteTrack to MCMOT: A Study of Multi-Category-Multi-Objective Tracking Methods
abstract: This paper investigates the multi-category multi-target tracking problem, focuses on online multi-target tracking methods, analyzes the advantages and disadvantages of existing methods, and proposes an improved algorithm, MCMOT, based on ByteTrack.MCMOT solves ByteTrack's deficiencies in complex environments by introducing four improvement strategies: closed-loop lifecycle management, motion state classification processing, refined priority matching, and interactive multi-model motion prediction. Experimental results show that MCMOT outperforms ByteTrack in terms of tracking accuracy, precision, persistence and frame rate.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Controller Design of a Pneumatic Muscle Joint System with Dead-Zone Input
abstract: In this paper, an event-triggered adaptive controller is designed by backstepping techniques for a pneumatic muscle joint system with dead-zone input. In addition to unknown dead-zone parameters, unknown system parameters and unknown nonlinear terms caused by the unknown modelling error and external disturbance are also considered. We proved that for any signal, the error between the signal obtained by the trigger signal after dead-zone transformation and the signal obtained by direct dead-zone transformation is bounded by an unknown constant. This error and the error generated by the linear approximation of the dead-zone are handled together as a disturbance-like term. These uncertainties will be compensated for by estimating the upper bound of the disturbance-like term. It is shown that the proposed event-triggered adaptive controller can ensure all signals in the closed-loop system bounded and the tracking error can converges to zero. Finally, simulation studies are used to verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Cascaded ESO and BLF Based Multi-Task Priority Controller for Redundant Robots with Null Space Compliance
abstract: In this study, we address multi-task priority trajectory tracking and null space compliance control for redundant robots, which lack joint velocity and torque sensors, under substantial external disturbances. A cascaded ESO and BLF-based multi-task priority controller is proposed, which can make the robot still keep the position state of each task within the prescribed performance range under the condition of strong external disturbances. First, The cascaded ESO is utilized to estimate joint velocities and compensate for system uncertainties. Then, a trajectory tracking controller for high-priority tasks based on BLF and the null space compliance controller with the lowest priority are designed. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in comparison to alternatives.

articleTitle: Simultaneous 2D and 3D Lane Detection Algorithm Based on Multi-Granularity Lane Attention
abstract: Lane detection is a crucial step in the perception task of autonomous vehicle driving. However, to the best of our knowledge, there is little literature to simultaneously obtain the two-dimensional coordinates of lane in the image coordinate system and the three-dimensional coordinates in the vehicle coordinate system from the front view road image. In this paper, we propose Lane-MGA: an end-to-end 2D and 3D lane joint detection network model, which aimes to promote the effective detection of both through mutual supervision of 2D lane and 3D lane. In addition, we propose a multi-granularity lane attention mechanism, which aggregates the spatial features and channel features of lane at different granularities. The experimental results verify the effectiveness of Lane-MGA.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Torsional Vibrating Systems with Delayed Vibration Absorbers
abstract: It is universally acknowledged that using delayed vibration absorbers can effectively reduce vibrations in torsional vibrating systems. When the absorbers are adopted, choosing appropriate gains of absorbers and delays is extremely important. In this paper, the stability analysis of torsional vibrating systems with delayed vibration absorbers is studied. Based on the Lyapunov-Krasovskii method and integral inequality techniques, stability conditions for the torsional vibrating systems with the delayed vibration absorbers are obtained. According to the conditions, the relationship among the gains, the delays and the stability of the systems are shown. It means that the conditions can be used to adjust the gains and the delays effectively. At last, a case study is given to show the effectiveness of the obtained conditions.

articleTitle: Meta-reinforcement Learning Task Planning Based on Improved Curriculum Learning Sampling
abstract: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML), have shown a good generalization performance in solving task planning problems. Most of the existing meta-reinforcement learning(meta-rl) algorithms learn meta-policies by randomly sampling tasks. However, this sampling strategy can only adapt to simple tasks, and have insufficient ability to generalize to difficult and new tasks. To address these problems, the Improved curriculum learning-MAML (ICL-MAML) framework is designed, which the task sampling strategy based on improved curriculum learning is applied for sampling the tasks. This method improves the convergence ability of meta strategies for difficult tasks and their generalization ability for new tasks. At the same time, it alleviates the problem of catastrophic forgetting. Experiments in the meta-world environment show that ICL-MAML has a significant improvement in training and testing success rates, and uses less training time compared to random sampling task strategy.

articleTitle: Research on Frame and Table Recognition Based on CAD Drawings
abstract: In the process of drawing architectural drawings with AutoCAD software, enterprises will produce a large number of CAD drawings in DWG format. The tables of these CAD drawings contain rich textual information. These text information constitute the key data base of enterprise systematic management drawings. At present, the systematic management of drawing data needs to collect these sheet data, but the sheet data collection mainly depends on manual input, which leads to high error rate of data collection, huge workload, long compilation cycle and low work efficiency. The purpose of this paper is to discuss how to deal with these tables efficiently. Firstly, based on Revit secondary development, the frame recognition algorithm is proposed, which confirms the inner and outer frame by finding the largest rectangle and the second largest rectangle. In addition, the Teigha class library is used to extract text, so as to extract key data, so as to promote the collection, reuse and systematic management of product data. Through the processing of drawing frames and forms, it lays a good foundation for subsequent component identification. The method proposed in this paper has strong versatility and adaptability, and can basically realize the recognition of CAD drawing frame and form, and extract form text, and achieve higher accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Experimental Comparsion Between NeRFs and 3D Gaussian Splatting for Underwater 3D Reconstruction
abstract: In the last two decades, research on the field of visual-based 3D reconstruction has undergone a significant evolution especially in the area of deep learning. Typically Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) are used for representations in high-fidelity view synthesis and have made rapid development. However, such techniques have not been fully evaluated in challenging conditions, such as the underwater domain while it is vital to human ocean exploration, archaeology, oil and gas industry and mine countermeasure missions. In this paper, we compare the performance of NeRFs and 3DGS techniques in the underwater reconstruction on the dataset QDLake-UW, collected at QianDao Lake Underwater by ourselves on different conditions.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Enhancement Model for Brightness Equalization of Small Celestial Body
abstract: The economic and scientific value that small celestial bodies (SCBs) offer humanity are the main motivations for close exploration of these bodies. However, optical autonomous navigation becomes challenging due to the light variation caused by the rapid spin of SCBs. In this paper, we therefore propose a brightness equalization method, which consists of an Illumination Components Estimation Module (ICEM), a Brightness Self-Calibration Module (BSCM), and a Brightness Equalization Curve Optimization Module (BECOM). First, the adjustment factor and illumination components are estimated separately by BECOM and ICEM. These factors are input into the brightness equalization curve to remap the illumination components and further achieve brightness equalization of SCBs images. Next, we designed BSCM to calibrate the illumination components further. Considering the high coupling between the illumination and reflection components in SCBs images, we estimate the illumination components multiple times by the modules above. The input for each estimation is the output of the previous one, enabling weight sharing in a cascaded learning process, reducing the model parameters and accelerating network inference speed. Finally, we conducted extensive experiments on SCBs images, the results confirm the superiority and effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on the Schedulable Potential of Aggregated Electric Vehicle Clusters in Virtual Power Plants
abstract: In the process of virtual power plant(VPP) construction, electric vehicle, as a typical distributed resource, has strong flexibility, which makes their participation in the optimization and regulation of power system more uncertain. According to this problem, we studies the schedulable potential of electrical vehicle (EV) clusters within VPP. First of all, an optimization control strategy model for a VPP which includes EVs is proposed. By maximizing the profit of VPP, the model guides EVs charging and discharging behaviors during different periods to achieve peak shaving and valley filling, optimize resource utilization efficiency, and maximize VPP revenue through electricity sales to distributed power grid. Secondly, after fully considering the optimization control strategy of the VPP, an EV schedulable potential model is established to fully exploit and utilize the schedulable potential of EVs, thereby optimizing VPP operation strategies. Finally, through simulation examples, the impact of different depths of charging and discharging on the schedulable potential of EVs is simulated. The overall potential of EVs is found to be considerable, which verifies the effectiveness of the proposed optimization control strategy in evaluating the schedulable potential of EVs.

articleTitle: Estimation of Lithium-ion Batteries State of SOC Based on Borges Difference Structural Adaptive Gated Recurrent Unit Networks
abstract: A gated recurrent unit (GRU) network based on Borges difference is proposed, which is called B-GRU network. The B-GRU network aims to solve the limitation that the integer-order GRU network lacks sufficient flexibility in adjusting the proportion of updated information and forgotten information. The B-GRU network is specifically applied to the state of charge (SOC) estimation of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). By introducing Borges difference into the GRU network structure and combining with strict order interval analysis, the convergence of the improved B-GRU network is guaranteed. The optimization of the network is achieved by adjusting the order rules in the B-GRU network. The experimental results show that the proposed B-GRU network effectively improves the SOC estimation accuracy of LIBs.

articleTitle: Temperature Control Method for Batch Reactors Based on Adaptive Delay Compensation
abstract: To address the instability issue caused by time-delay and nonlinear characteristics of intermittent reactions in batch reactors, a temperature control method for batch reactors based on adaptive delay compensation was proposed. By integrating the chemical reaction mechanism inside the reactor with graphical analysis and actual production data, a time-varying second-order delayed transfer function model for the reactor is established. The adaptive rate for controlling the time-varying delayed system is designed based on the control error between the actual controlled object and the nominal model. Furthermore, standard Smith predictor is employed to compensate for the delay in the error term. When applied to temperature control in batch reactors, experimental results demonstrate that this method effectively reduces the temperature control errors caused by time-varying delays, significantly accelerates the convergence speed and diminishes the oscillation amplitude of the temperature curve.

articleTitle: Prefabricated Pizza Defect Detection Algorithm Based on CNN and Transformer
abstract: Accurate and efficient defect detection is of great significance in the field of prefabricated food quality inspection to ensure product quality and improve production efficiency. This article proposes a CNN Transformer model for defect detection in prefabricated pizza images. This method extracts three sets of pizza features by establishing a new color, texture, and shape feature extraction model, and uses three parallel convolutional neural networks for feature extraction. The extracted features are projected and input into a Transformer model combined with position encoding for processing. The projection section proposes a convolutional nonlinear projection method to improve the quality of projection. The position encoding part proposes a combination of sine cosine and learnable position encoding algorithms, utilizing the global position information provided by sine cosine position encoding and the adaptive adjustment ability of learnable position encoding to enhance the feature representation ability of the model. The Transformer encoder effectively captures long-range dependencies in the input sequence through multi-layer self-attention mechanisms and feedforward neural networks. Adaptive feature fusion integrates encoded features to achieve accurate classification of pizza defects.

articleTitle: SAR Images Change Detection Based on Maximum Classifier Difference with Multiscale Multilevel Features
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images can still be effective under harsh weather and lighting conditions, but the presence of scattering noise and the lack of labeled sufficient datasets have severely impacted the development of change detection (CD) methods and limited the performance of CD models. In order to solve the above problems and make full use of the existing labeled data, we propose a CD model based on the maximum classifier difference of multi-scale features. Firstly, we extract multiscale features directly from the original images and fuse them, after which the multiscale features are fed into a Siamese network for multilevel feature extraction, followed by fusion of the multilevel features for use in subsequent CD. The extracted features are then fed into the classification module and subjected to maximum classifier variance processing. While ensuring the performance of the model on the source domain dataset, the parameters of the two classifiers are updated so that the difference between their results on the target domain dataset increases, and then the parameters of the feature extractor are updated so that the difference between the results of the two classifiers on the target domain dataset decreases. Repeating the above process can achieve a reduction in the difference between the source and target domain datasets, so that the model can make full use of the labeled data and can perform well on the unlabeled data as well. We conducted comparative experiments on four publicly available SAR datasets, and the experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and sophistication of the method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Neural Control of Robotic Manipulators with Adaptive Disturbance Compensation
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive neural network control approach for robotic manipulators to enhance trajectory tracking accuracy in the face of unknown system dynamics and external disturbances. The proposed method designs an adaptive compensation term to deal with the total disturbance from neural network approximation errors and unknown bounded disturbances without requiring prior knowledge of their magnitudes. The proposed scheme is validated through Lyapunov stability theory, ensuring the uniform ultimate boundedness of the system and the high-performance tracking control. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme in achieving robust tracking performance under bounded unknown disturbances.

articleTitle: Research on Railway Operational Accidents Analysis Method Based on Knowledge Graph
abstract: The occurrence of railway operational accidents is caused by various interrelated hazards. Through topological analysis of the characteristics and correlation of these hazards, targeted accident prevention strategies can be developed. In this paper, a new knowledge graph-based railway operational accidents analysis approach is proposed, aiming to reveal the potential rules of accidents by analyzing a large number of accident data. The novelty of this work lies in defining new topological indicators that are tailored for multidimensional network analysis, and facilitate the evaluation of hazards from multiple perspectives. In addition, a targeted accident analysis process is designed based on topological indicators. The analysis method is helpful to formulate the general prevention strategy for the hazard, so as to provide the basis for ensuring the safety of railway operation. This paper uses railway operational accidents in the UK as a case study. The results indicate that this method can discover the key hazards influencing the occurrence of accidents and provide targeted preventive measures.

articleTitle: Small Intestine Tumor CT Image Segmentation Method Based on Self-Supervised Learning
abstract: In order to solve the problem of small amount of labeled data and low segmentation accuracy of CT images of small intestinal tumors, a self-supervised learning-based image segmentation model BT-RC-UNet is proposed. Firstly, depth-separable convolution, residual structure, and CBAM attention mechanism are introduced into U-Net to better retain the integrity of the input information and learn the feature representations of small intestinal tumors; secondly, the encoder network is pretrained based on the redundancy-reducing of the Barlow Twins method, the encoder network of the improved U-N et model is pre-trained using the feature representation of CT images of small bowel tumors in an unsupervised manner; finally, the improved U-Net model is fine-tuned using the limited labeled data in the actual segmentation task, so as to extract the more effective features of the original image and refine the image segmentation effect. The experimental results show that the Dice coefficient of the model reaches 87.01%, the Jaccard similarity coefficient and the Hausdorff distance reach 67.60% and 11.2170, respectively, and the indexes such as recall are improved relative to those of the U-Net model, which can effectively realize the accurate segmentation of the lesion region of the CT image of the small intestinal tumor.

articleTitle: Screen-shooting Resilient Watermarking Based on Invertible Neural Network
abstract: As an invisible mark embedded in multimedia objects, the original watermark is only utilized for copyright protection and authentication in digital domain, but nowadays it has been applied as an invisible QR code for human-machine information exchange. This kind of physical watermarking will undergo a re-imaging process, which introduces noise and distortion that are different from the digital watermarking. How to effectively improve its invisibility and robustness is a new challenge. Facing the challenges, this paper proposes a novel end-to-end screen-shooting resilient watermarking framework that seamlessly integrates an invertible neural network into an encoder-noise layer-decoder scheme. A two-stage training strategy and some elaborately designed loss functions are used to make the algorithm be stable and robust. Extensive experiments show that the proposed scheme outperforms existing algorithms in terms of robustness and invisibility. In most of the real screen-shooting experiments, the BER of our watermarking scheme is below 1% when its capacity reaches up to 196 bits. Meanwhile, the visual quality of the watermarked image still has a PSNR of 37.65dB and an SSIM of 0.9803.

articleTitle: Modeling and Optimization of an Integrated Energy System for Combined Cooling, Heating, and Power
abstract: Energy crisis and environmental pollution are two important issues related to the development of human society, which are of great concern to countries around the world. In order to accelerate the realization of the dual-carbon goal, improve energy utilization efficiency and reduce carbon emissions, the key energy supply equipment Cold, Heat and Power (CCHP) system is selected to construct an integrated energy system model. The changes in the overall operation mode and efficiency of the park after the introduction of this equipment are investigated using the improved Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II (NSGA-II). The results show that the CCHP equipment can realize the multi-energy complementarity and energy gradient utilization of the energy upper side equipment through its strong coupling characteristics; it can be seen that the introduction of the CCHP can greatly improve the operation efficiency of the integrated energy system, reduce the operation cost while relatively controlling the release of carbon emissions, and improve the overall efficiency of the systemt.

articleTitle: Leader-Following Consensus Control for Multi-Agent Systems Under DoS Attacks and Average Dwell Time Switching Topology
abstract: This article studies the leader-following consensus problem of multi-agent systems (MASs) in the presence of denial-of-service (DoS) attacks and switching topology. The problem that all edges of one follower are blocked under each attack is considered in this work. By using the multiple Lyapunov functions approach and average dwell time switching technique, a piecewise consensus protocol is designed. Sufficient conditions are established for the consensus of linear MAS. Moreover, the lower bound of average dwell time of the switching topology is determined under DoS attacks. Finally, we provided simulations to validate our theoretical finding.

articleTitle: Weld Seam Differentiation and Welding Torch Attitude Determination Based on Point Cloud Data
abstract: With the development of robotics technology, robotic arm welding tends to be more and more automatic and intelligent. To address the difficulty in determining the welding torch attitude caused by the uncertainty in the geometry and position information of the workpiec, a method for calculating the welding torch attitude based on the point cloud information of the workpiece is proposed. Firstly, the vector used to determine the welding torch attitude is identified based on the workpiece point cloud information. Then the attitude of the welding torch coordinate system relative to the world coordinate system is calculated from the vector. In addition, the method distinguishes between various types of weld seams and accurately determines the corresponding welding torch attitude. Finally, we conducted experiments on a bucket workpiece containing various types of weld seams, which successfully verified the adaptability and effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Output Constraint Control of Electro-Hydraulic Servo System Based on Extended Sliding Mode Observer
abstract: To address the output state constraint issue of electro - hydraulic servo systems, an adaptive output constraint control strategy based on an extended sliding mode observer (AOCESMO) has been put forward. To further cope with unmeasurable signals and external disturbances, an extended sliding mode observer (ESMO) is established by integrating the design of adaptive nonlinear feedback tracking control, thereby improving its transient performance. For electro-hydraulic servo systems with output limits, a barrier Lyapunov function (BLF) is developed, ensuring that the tracking error remains within the predetermined range. In controller design, this paper estimates and compensates for the derivative term of the adaptive law in real time, and proves the bounded tracking performance of the system through theoretical analysis, in order to keep the system's tracking inaccuracy within a predetermined range. The efficacy of the suggested high-performance control method is confirmed by a number of comparison simulation findings.

articleTitle: Encoding-Decoding-Based Recursive Filtering for Nonlinear Systems Subject to Multiple Missing Measurements
abstract: This paper investigates the recursive filtering (RF) problem for a class of time-varying nonlinear systems with an encoding-decoding mechanism. Multiple missing measurements (MMMs) phenomena are considered in the data transmission process, which is mainly caused by the transient failure of the sensor or external interference. A set of reciprocally independent Bernoulli random variables with uncertain probabilities are used to characterise the stochastic occurrence of MMMs. In wireless communication networks, a dynamic-quantization-based encoding-decoding mechanism is introduced to encrypt the measurements, safeguarding important data from potential theft. The connection between the real measurement and the decoded output is established through a bounded uncertainty. The purpose of this paper is to devise a RF algorithm for the considered phenomenon. Meanwhile, the filtering error covariance matrix is minimized by calculating the appropriate filtering gain. Finally, the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed filtering algorithm are verified by a simulation example.

articleTitle: A Gender Recognition Method for Chinese Mitten Crab in Low Light Environment Based on Machine Vision
abstract: The acquisition of gender information of Chinese mitten crabs is crucial for survival rate assessment and biomass estimation. Machine vision is commonly used for the automatic gender recognition of Chinese mitten crabs, but the low light conditions caused by deeper containers reduce the accuracy of existing algorithms. To improve the accuracy of gender recognition of Chinese mitten crabs in low light environments, this study incorporates the GAM into the backbone of YOLOv7, improving the capability to distinguish gender-specific features. A lightweight upsampling operator, CARAFE, replaces the original upsampling module, expanding the model's receptive field and better aggregating global information. Using Focal-Clo U to mitigate the impact of low-quality prediction boxes, enabling the model to better optimize high-quality ones. By constructing an image dataset of Chinese mitten crabs in low-light environments to validate the model's performance, experimental results demonstrate that the average precision of the model established in this study is 0.870, 10.6% higher than the most update algorithm GMNet-YOLOv4, effectively performing the classification task of Chinese mitten crabs in low-light environments.

articleTitle: Modeling and evaluation design of heterogeneous media networks considering quality of experience
abstract: Aiming at social media platforms with different commercial scenarios, especially for “cloud gaming”, this paper proposes a modeling and analysis framework for heterogeneous media networks considering quality of experience, which addresses the challenges of quantifying human impacts. Through standardized definitions of humans and equipment, man-machine information transmission is classified formally. Then, the evaluation of quality of experience for entities and media networks are defined. Finally, a case study about analysis and optimization for media network in the scenario of “cloud gaming” is derived. Different simulation results and the experiment's comparison imply the applicability and effectiveness of the framework proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Impulsive Control of Heterogeneous Multi-agent Systems with Saturation Constraint and Time Delay
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of leader-following consensus in heterogeneous multi-agent systems (HMAS) with input saturation and communication delay. Given the practical differences between leader and follower dimensions, we design virtual leaders to address this problem by allowing actual leaders and followers to communicate with virtual leaders separately, thus enabling indirect communication between actual leaders and followers. Additionally, the control protocol proposed in this paper takes into account the effects of input saturation and time delay that exist in real communication. At last, a simulation example is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the designed control protocol.

articleTitle: Quantized Control of semi-Markovian Jumping Bilinear Systems with Fractional Brownian Motions and Saturation Actuators
abstract: Utilizing the quantized control method, the analysis of the finite-time stochastic boundedness for semi-Markovian jumping bilinear systems driven by fractional Brownian motions with saturation actuators is investigated in this paper. Semi-Markov process is introduced to describe switching modes of bilinear systems. In order to obtain an improved stochastic boundedness condition based on fractional Brownian motions, a new type of double-integral Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional is constructed related to the Hurst index to deal with fractional Brownian motions, then the finite-time stochastic boundedness of the closed-loop bilinear system are studied. Last a numerical example are given and simulated to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Disturbance Rejection Study and Validation of the Control Law for the Guide Vane of Variable Geometry Low Pressure Turbine
abstract: During the aeroengine operation, the airflow with the high temperature and pressure acts on the guide vanes of the low pressure turbine (LPT). The guide vanes are subjected to high pneumatic loads. The pneumatic load is transmitted to the adjustment mechanism of the guide vanes. The pneumatic load varies greatly under different operation conditions. Therefore, the adjustment mechanism of the guide vanes has the requirements of the fast response, the low overshoot and zero static error and strong disturbance rejection ability. In this study, permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM) are used as the actuators. This study adopts the scheme with multiple PMSMs and the linkage ring. Three drive motors regulate the rotation angle of the guide vanes. Three load motors simulate the pneumatic load disturbance. The drive motors and load motors are arranged crosswise in the circumferential homogeneous manner on the linkage ring, with neighbouring motors spaced 60° apart. The active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) is used instead of the traditional three-loop control structure of angle-speed-current to enhance the disturbance rejection ability of the actuators. The improved synchronization control method with variable deviation coupling is applied to ensure the synchronization of the drive motors. The hardware in the loop (HIL) experimental system is built to verify the feasibility and the real-time performance of the ADRC algorithm. It is verified that the adjustment mechanism of the guide vanes has the fast response speed and the high precision. It can follow the command angle in time. The ADRC and synchronization control algorithms can significantly enhance the disturbance rejection ability and the synchronization respectively. The study provides the technical support for the performance enhancement of the variable geometry turbine (VGT).

articleTitle: Bearing Fault Diagnosis in Noisy Environment Based on Continuous Wavelet Transform and Convolutional Attention Fusion Network
abstract: Accurate diagnosis of bearing faults in noisy environments is crucial for the safe operation of equipment under real working conditions. This paper introduces an innovative approach to bearing fault identification using continuous wavelet transform and a bidirectional fusion multi-scale convolutional attention network (BiMCAN). First, the original signal is processed using continuous wavelet transform to generate a timefrequency image. Then, the proposed multiscale convolutional SimMSC module and an improved Swin Transformer serve as the backbone network for feature extraction, with BiFPN used for multiscale feature fusion. Experiments conducted on the CWRU bearing dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other diagnostic methods in terms of diagnostic performance under strong noise and varying working conditions.

articleTitle: Improved Antiskid Braking Control Algorithm and System Design for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
abstract: To satisfy landing and braking operations for un-manned aerial vehicle, an improved antiskid braking control algorithm and system that fits working characteristics is proposed together with key technical problems. Firstly, system identification and principle are introduced. Secondly, landing gear and braking apparatus of aerial vehicle are analyzed and modeled based on structural features. Electromechanical actuator active suspension force control method is used for high-precision tracking. Multi-gate threshold PD-PBM anti-sliding algorithm fused with a compensation factor for balanced adjustment is proposed to improve braking performance. Finally, proposed algorithm is verified based on single-wheel co-simulation platform and multi-wheel flight dynamics real-time view software platform.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Approximation of Gene Regulatory Networks Using Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition
abstract: This paper addresses the data-driven modeling problem of a class of gene regulatory networks. Utilizing the Koopman operator theory, the study applies the extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) method to linearize a high-dimensional nonlinear biochemical network model, and extends the state model establishment without input to the model establishment with input. Finally, the control signal obtained by the model predictive control (MPC) method is used to converge the state of the original nonlinear model. The results show that the data-driven method applied in this study can effectively establish the linearized model of the nonlinear system and make the subsequent linear control feasible.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Fault-Tolerant Control for Lateral Stability of Steer-by-Wire Vehicles
abstract: This paper presents a hierarchical fault-tolerant control system design to enhance the lateral stability of steer-by-wire vehicles. The control system can be divided into two layers. The upper layer focuses on designing a controller that determines the desired front steering angle from driver's command to improve lateral stability. The lower layer includes a steering controller that ensures the execution of the desired steering angle from the upper layer. However, the tracking errors of lower layer controller can lead to actuator faults in the upper controller. To address this, we propose a fault-tolerant control strategy for the upper layer. Theoretical analysis and simulation results using Simulink/Carsim demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control system in maintaining lateral stability under external disturbance input.

articleTitle: Fog Traffic Image Simulation Optimization Algorithm Based on Unet++
abstract: This study aims to improve the challenge of achieving accurate target detection accuracy under fog conditions. Aiming at the scarcity of foggy data sets, we propose a fog traffic image simulation optimization algorithm based on UNet++. The algorithm consists of several steps: the relative depth map is generated by the self-supervised monomeric depth estimation network, and then the absolute depth map is initially derived by applying dense geometric constraints for scale recovery. Secondly, the Unet ++ image segmentation network is used to segment the sky region of the original image and optimize the initial absolute depth map. Then, the visibility of the simulated image is defined and the transmittance map is generated. Then dark channel maps are used to distinguish sky regions and estimate atmospheric light values. Finally, atmospheric scattering model is used to generate fog simulation images under specific visibility conditions. The experimental results show that compared with before optimization, the optimized fog simulation algorithm without reference image quality evaluation score is significantly improved. This suggests that its non-structural similarity (NSS) features are closer to those of natural fog. The fog simulation method proposed in this paper can realize clear image conversion under natural environment, and solve the problem of lack of fog image data set and incomplete visibility data.

articleTitle: Design and Kinematics Analysis of an Index Finger Exoskeleton with Elastic Actuator
abstract: Rehabilitation training is vital to patient's recovery after stroke surgery. However, due to the inability to effectively absorb and buffer external shocks, rigid exoskeletons are more likely to cause damage to the patient's joints and muscles. In this paper, the index finger exoskeleton with elastic actuator (IFEEA) is studied. First, the IFEEA is designed to realize the flexion-extension (F/E) movements of MCP joint of index finger. Second, the kinematic model of IFEEA is analyzed. Finally, the motion experiment was carried out. The experimental results show that the IFEEA has good spatial motion ability and great potential in future applications.

articleTitle: An Innovative Dual Closed-Loop Control Strategy for Peak Stability of High-Frequency Fatigue Testing Machine
abstract: The high frequency fatigue testing machine employs the principle of electromagnetic resonance and is specifically designed to evaluate the tensile and compressive fatigue performance of metals under various force values. However, the main challenge faced by this tester in the later stages of the experiment is the problem of controlling the accuracy of the vibration peaks when the stiffness of the specimen varies. To solve this problem, an innovative dual closed-loop control strategy is proposed in this paper, which is based on phase and force feedback mechanisms. While utilizing the incremental PID algorithm to accurately control the force value, the excitation frequency is adjusted in real time to match the intrinsic frequency of the system by analyzing the phase angle relationship between the frequency of the excitation force and the resonance frequency using the successive approximation method suitable for the actual situation, which ensures the stability of the vibration peak value during the whole experimental process. The control scheme is modeled and simulated by MATLAB/Simulink, and the results show that the scheme can effectively track the intrinsic frequency of the system and maintain the stability of the peak value in the whole experimental process, which significantly improves the control accuracy and reliability of the testing machine and reduces the power consumption.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Line-of-Sight Guidance Law for Path Following of AUV
abstract: Line-of-Sight (LOS) guidance law is widely used for path following of autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) due to its simplicity and effectiveness. However, LOS guidance law has a contradiction between rapidity and overshoot, as well as a steady-state error caused by waves, wind and ocean currents. This paper proposes an adaptive LOS (ALOS) guidance law that can balance rapidity and overshoot while compensating for sideslip angle. The proposed algorithm uses adaptive parameter based on the cross-track error to real-time adjust the look-ahead distance and adaptively calculate a reasonable desired heading angle. An adaptive integral state is designed based on the adaptive parameter to compensate the impact of sideslip angle and then calculate the desired heading angle. Through stability analysis, it is proven that ALOS has uniform semiglobal exponential stability (USGES) at the balancing point. Finally, lake trials results shows that ALOS effectively suppressed overshoot and compensated for disturbance of waves, wind and ocean currents while reducing lateral cross-track error by 52.3% in similar converge speed with LOS. ALOS can effectively improve robustness of control and enhance path following performance of AUV.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control of Decomposition Furnace Based on Equivalent-Input-Disturbances
abstract: In the cement production process, the decomposer outlet temperature control faces challenges such as large time delay and multiple disturbances. A general control system cannot handle time delay and disturbances effectively at the same time. Therefore, in this paper, we consider the problem of disturbances in time-delay systems and suppress the disturbances present in the outlet temperature control of the decomposer by combining equivalent-input-disturbance (EID) and Model Predictive Control (MPC), where EID can estimate the disturbances and apply them to the input channels of the system, which do not require any information about the disturbances. Finally simulations are carried out in the catabolizer system and the results indicate that this system is able to suppress the perturbations effectively in time delay systems.

articleTitle: SLAM Method of Mine Inspection Robot based on Stereo Vision and IMU
abstract: In view of the poor robustness And poor accuracy of single sensor SLAM technology in the complex surroundings of coal mine, A global localization method based on multi-sensor fusion of IMU and stereo vision is proposed. Firstly, the ORB feature were extracted and matched, and the FAST keypoints were extracted by adaptive threshold to improve the quantity and quality of feature points. The quadtree method was used to realize the uniformity of point feature extraction and overcome the problem of feature stacking redundancy. Then, the direction consistency check and RANSAC algorithm are used to remove the mismatching of feature points. Finally, the tight coupling optimization mechanism was used to fuse the sensor data, and the loop closure detection module is configured to increase the overall positioning accuracy. According to the experimental results in the EuRoc public data set, compared with ORBSLAM2, a single stereo vision sensor, the absolute positioning accuracy increased by 36.49% on average, and compared with VinsFusion based on visual-inertial fusion, the absolute positioning accuracy is improved by 87.21% on average. It effectively improves the robustness and positioning accuracy of the coal mine inspection robot.

articleTitle: Prediction of Joint Angles for Human Elbow Motion Based on sEMG
abstract: In the field of intelligent rehabilitation, the primary reliance is on rehabilitation robots, which often struggle to continuously respond to a patient's movement intentions in real-time and with accuracy. To improve the level of human-robot interaction (HRI) and provide personalized rehabilitation exercises with active patient participation, this study developed a joint angle prediction model using surface electromyography (sEMG). Initially, six healthy subjects were selected, and devices for sEMG and angle acquisition were employed to synchronize the collection of sEMG and elbow joint angle data for each participant. Subsequently, the preprocessed data were input into the designed Transformer-based joint angle prediction model. Finally, the performance of the Transformer-based model was compared with that of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) and Convolutional Neural Network-Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM) models. Experimental results indicate that the Transformer-based joint angle prediction model outperforms its counterparts, achieving a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of less than 0.065, thereby suggesting its potential for future applications.

articleTitle: Chattering-Free Sliding Mode Control Based Sampled-Data Consensus for Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Systems with Disturbances
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges of achieving consensus in heterogeneous multi-agent systems (HMAS) by examining the effects of sampled-data based external disturbances and interactions. For each agent, a reference trajectory is defined, and the consensus problem is analyzed from two perspectives: consensus among reference trajectories and the tracking needs of each agent. To effectively handle external disturbances, the tracking control laws incorporate a sliding mode control approach. The proposed protocol integrates reference trajectory methods, sampled-data control, and sliding mode strategies. Notably, this protocol allows HMAS to achieve asymptotic consensus while minimizing chattering. Finally, a simulation example is provided to validate the protocol's effectiveness.

articleTitle: SpecuPro: An Integrated Method for Refined Specular Reflection Removal in Endoscopic Images
abstract: The quality of endoscopic images is inevitably affected by varying degrees of specular reflections, which increases diagnostic difficulty. Although various methods for detecting and removing specular reflections have been proposed, most of the methods face challenges in achieving optimal segmentation accuracy and often perform poorly in restoring large reflective areas. In response, we introduce a method, SpecuPro, that integrates refined segmentation and restoration techniques for improved performance. Specular reflection regions are segmented by the proposed lightweight UNet variant, DSUNet++, while images are restored using an enhanced Criminisi algorithm. We evaluated our method using the publicly available real endoscopic dataset CVC-ClinicDB and compared it with methods from previous research. Quantitative metrics and qualitative visual results demonstrated that our method outperforms the existing methods in accurately segmenting specular reflections within a reasonable time frame and effectively inpainting large highlight areas.

articleTitle: Iced Power Line Image Enhancement Method Based on Improved Retinex-Homomorphic Filter
abstract: In order to address issues related to complex backgrounds and poor contrast of transmission line icing image, a line icing image enhancement method is proposed in this paper, which based on improved Retinex-homomorphic filtering. To begin with, to address the issues of uneven brightness and unsatisfactory enhancement effect of traditional homomorphic filtering algorithm, a new filtering function is constructed as the filtering function of improved homomorphic filtering, and the image's high-frequency and low-frequency components are individually processed using the filtering function. Then, to address the edge blurring problem of the traditional Retinex algorithm, the Laplace operator is used to sharpen the edge of the image, and the sharpened image is used as the guided image of the guided filter, and then the guided filter is applied to replace the Gaussian low-pass filter in the conventional Retinex algorithm. Finally, the improved homomorphic filtering and the improved Retinex processing results are fused to obtain the final enhanced image. Experimental results indicate that, in comparison to the traditional algorithm, the enhanced algorithm can significantly improve the line icing image, and is superior to the traditional algorithm in terms of objective evaluation index and subjective visual effect.

articleTitle: Transit Search Optimized Least Squares Support Vector Machine for the State of Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: The State of Health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries is a critical parameter that mirrors the performance of their health monitoring systems. To achieve accurate prediction of SOH, we propose a novel prediction model. The model combines the advantages of variational mode decomposition (VMD) and transit search optimization-least squares support vector machine (TSOA-LSSVM). The constant-current charging time (CCCT), constant-current discharging time (CCDT), and Constant voltage charging time(CVCT) with Internal resistance(IR) are extracted as health indicators (HIs), and the correlations between HIs and SOH are evaluated by using Spearman correlation coefficient (spearman) respectively. With the VMD method, the most correlated HI is decomposed into multiple intrinsic modal functions (IMFs), and each IMF is fitted by the LSSVM. TSOA is used to obtain the most appropriate hyperparameters. The efficacy of the newly developed VMD-TSOA-LSSVM model is assessed by utilizing battery aging data sourced from the Center for Advanced Life Cycle Engineering (CALCE). Its performance is then compared to that of the solo LSSVM, the VMD-LSSVM, and the VMD-TSOA-SVM methods. The laboratory outcomes demonstrate that the VMD-TSOA-LSSVM model outperforms other models in prediction and has better robustness and generalization ability.

articleTitle: Enhanced Fault Characteristics Information Based Canonical Variate Analysis for Detecting the AHU's Faults
abstract: As an indispensable component of air-conditioning system, the air handling unit (AHU) always exhibits the issue of inconspicuous fault characteristics information and strong time-wise dynamics. To address these challenges, the enhanced fault characteristics information based canonical variate analysis (EFBCVA) monitoring strategy is developed in this paper. Firstly, to obtain the enhanced fault characteristics information, the normal dataset is deducted from the test dataset and multiple batches normal datasets are subtracted from each other to obtain multiple training differential datasets, which together compose the three-dimensional training differential dataset. Then, the three-dimensional training differential dataset is rearranged into a variable-wise two-dimensional differential matrix. Finally, to manage the time-wise dynamic attributes, the CVA is utilized to capture the slowly evolving driving forces during the AHU's operation. The experimental results on the ASHRAE RP-1312 datasets show significant enhancements achieved by our proposed EFBCVA based monitoring operation approach.

articleTitle: Vehicle Detection Method Based on Improved YOLOv8 in RGB-infrared Aerial Images
abstract: In recent years, RGB-infrared object detection in aerial images has received much attention. This is because there are complementary properties in the two modalities that can mitigate the adverse effects of single modality's own limitations. However, there are still challenges in detecting objects in low-light and occlusion conditions. The common occlusion in aerial images is non-object occlusion. Existing methods usually focus on the design of modal feature fusion strategies and do not specifically deal with the occlusion phenomenon. To solve this problem, a data augment method is proposed, which mixes the object with the surrounding background to simulate the actual occlusion situation, increases the proportion of occlusion samples in the dataset. In addition, for better feature capture, a cross-modal object detection network based on the improved YOLOv8 network is proposed. In the detection network, a multi-modal feature fusion module is designed, which can adaptively select channel features and suppress redundant features so as to fuse features from different sensor images more effectively. The method is evaluated on the DroneVehicle dataset, and experimental results show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance.

articleTitle: A UUV Traversal and Obstacle Avoidance Search Algorithm Based on Adaptive Ocean Current Direction
abstract: Adopting appropriate traversal path planning algorithms can effectively solve the problem of UUV task area coverage search. Autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles have their own underactuated characteristics, and when they are subjected to underwater ocean currents, especially in the direction of cross flow, the accuracy of the autonomous unmanned aerial vehicle's tracking path will be greatly reduced. In response to the above issues, this article proposes a simple and convenient unmanned autonomous vehicle coverage traversal obstacle avoidance search algorithm that can adapt to the direction of ocean currents, providing engineering practical value for the high airworthiness and high followability of search paths. The numerical simulation results show that, the coverage traversal method proposed in this article can enable autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles to mainly plan in a collinear manner with ocean currents, reducing the length of the cross flow direction path and improving the accuracy of tracking paths.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fractional Order Sliding Mode Fault-Tolerant Control for Uncertain Manipulators With Intermittent Actuator Faults
abstract: It is both challenging and meaningful to investigate the control issue for uncertain manipulators with intermittent actuator faults. To solve this problem, an adaptive fractional sliding mode fault-tolerant control scheme is proposed. Within this scheme, a projection operator is used to change the adaptive parameters in controller and a piecewise continuous Lyapunov function is proposed to prove the closed-loop stability. It proves that the boundedness of all closed-loop signals are guaranteed in the case of intermittent actuator faults (IAFs) and the control goal is achieved. Furthermore, when the jump amplitude of the unknown fault parameters is smaller and the time interval between two consecutive actuator faults is longer, the tracking error is smaller. Finally, simulation studies are done to verify the feasibility of the developed control scheme.

articleTitle: Multi-Source Information Fusion Based Motor Fault Diagnosis via Deep Discriminative Residual Adaptation
abstract: Asynchronous motors play a key role in industrial equipment. To cope with the challenge of incomplete fault information due to a single signal, and the problem of missing target domain labels. this paper proposes a method that combines multi-source information fusion with an improved domain adaptation approach. First, an autoencoder is used to extract features from the collected vibration, current and temperature signals. The extracted features are concatenated and fused at the channel level. Then, a deep feature extraction network is designed by combining efficient channel attention and deep residual network, which can accurately and efficiently extract deep features from multi-source information. Finally, an improved domain adaptation mechanism is proposed, which significantly enhances the learning of discriminative features between two different domains. In addition, by incorporating the I -Softmax loss, the constructed Deep Discriminative Residual Adaptive Network exhibits stronger classification capabilities. The superiority and feasibility of the proposed method is verified by comparing several methods under the sample of asynchronous motor without labeling the target domain.

articleTitle: Improved Non-Singular Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control and Disturbance Observer for PMSM
abstract: This paper proposes a non-singular fast terminal sliding mode control and non-singular fast terminal sliding mode disturbance observer compound control strategy for permanent magnet synchronous motor. Firstly, by introducing a new reaching law, the imbalance issue between chattering and convergence speed in the conventional reaching law is solved. To further enhance the system's capacity to restrain disturbances, a non-singular fast terminal sliding mode disturbance observer is proposed to estimate the disturbance value and provide feedback to the speed controller. The non-singular fast terminal sliding mode disturbance observer reduces sliding mode chattering and enhances observer response speed compared to sliding mode disturbance observer. Simulation consequences demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Voltage Control Strategy of Active Distribution Network Considering Reactive Power Margin of Photovoltaic Inverter
abstract: Aiming at the problem of voltage fluctuation caused by large-scale distributed photovoltaic access to distribution network, this paper proposes a voltage control strategy for active distribution network considering reactive power margin of photovoltaic inverter. Firstly, based on the voltage sensitivity matrix, the interaction mechanism between distributed photovoltaic power control and node voltage change is clarified in detail, so as to determine the compensation priority of each node. Secondly, considering the capacity and load characteristics of photovoltaic inverters, the reactive power regulation margin index of distributed photovoltaic distribution network is proposed, and the voltage control model is established based on the regulation margin index and node compensation priority. Then, the particle swarm optimization algorithm of precoding technology is used to solve the problem efficiently, so as to obtain better voltage control effect of distribution network. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by the simulation of the modified IEEE33 node.

articleTitle: Tracking Control on Closed-Loop-Identification UAV with Constrained Attitude Angle Based on Barrier Lyapunov Function
abstract: In this paper, the trajectory tracking problem of the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) is considered. Firstly, different from the accurate models adopted in most of existed works, we consider a concise and effective model in which the inertia link delay phenomenon is considered, and an adaptive backstepping controller is designed to handle the model uncertainty. Further-more, considering the fact that the attitude angle of UAV should be limited within a set of range for safety in real flight. To handle this problem, a barrier Lyapunov function (BLF) based adaptive controller is also proposed to achieve the trajectory tracking task while constrains the attitude angles within a set range. Both simulation and experiment results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Quasi-Z-Source Inverters for High Voltage Gain Ratio Scenarios
abstract: Due to the limitations of the conventional qZSI in terms of boost capability, capacitor voltage stress, and input inductor current ripple, this paper proposes a novel high-gain qZSI with a unique boost structure instead of the boost inductor used in the original quasi-Z source topology. This new high-gain qZSI not only exhibits enhanced DC-side boosting capabilities compared to the previously proposed qZSI topology but also mitigates capacitive voltage stress while reducing input inductor current ripple. Consequently, it significantly diminishes the rate of input inductor current ripple and thereby improves both output waveform quality and system stability. The theoretical analysis along with simulation and experimental results validate the feasibility and superiority of this new high-gain qZSI topology.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered State Estimation for USV System with Correlated Noises and Packet Losses
abstract: This article focuses on the problem of Unmanned Surface Vehicle (USV) system operating in network environments with noise correlation and packet drop occurrences. An innovative event-triggered state estimation method is considered to effectively reduce the impact of noise correlation and packet dropout. The event-triggered state estimator incorporates both a triggering threshold and a correlation coefficient, enabling an optimized balance between transmission frequency and estimation accuracy. Within the proposed framework, the covariance of the prior estimation error is assured to remain bounded. Ultimately, a mock-up of the USV prototype is provided to confirm the pertinent findings.

articleTitle: Semi-Process Noise Distillation for Continual Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Models
abstract: Generative diffusion models have made significant improvements in the image, audio, and video domains. However, existing diffusion models suffer from a critical challenge: after being trained on new datasets, they tend to forget how to generate images of the previous datasets domain. We name it as catastrophic forgetting of diffusion models. To address this challenge, we propose the NDE-Diff, a method that supports diffusion models trained in continual learning scenarios. The NDE-Diff contains semi-process noise distillation and memory augmented continual mixture of experts. Unlike conventional images replay distillation, our method distills the memory of the previous diffusion model with Gaussian noise during the intermediate denoising process. The memory augmented continual mixture of experts further increases the memory capacity of the diffusion model and introduces a task-guided routing network, effectively activating the utilization rate of the experts. Comprehensive experimental results demonstrate that our NDE-Diff significantly reduces training time compared to joint training and achieves state-of-the-art results on continual learning datasets.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Control of a Dynamic Positioning Vessel with Thruster Faults Based on Improved Adaptive Control Allocation
abstract: This paper proposes an improved adaptive control allocation-based fault-tolerant control (IACA-FTC) scheme to address partial or complete thruster faults for a dynamic positioning (DP) vessel. First, an adaptive control allocation algorithm is developed to perform online adaptive reconstruction of the configuration matrix for the faulty propulsion system, aiming to minimize deviations in control allocation given the current propulsion capacity. Second, a differential term is incorporated into the adaptive updating law to mitigate thrust jitter during the adaptive process. The analysis, based on Lyapunov stability theory, demonstrates that all error signals in the control allocation closed-loop system are uniformly ultimately bounded. Finally, simulated comparison experiments based on the DP vessel thruster faults scenario indicate that the designed IACA-FTC method can effectively handle partial and complete thruster failures and improve the fault tolerance capabilities of the vessel during operation. This advancement is significant for improving the safety and reliability of dynamic positioning vessels.

articleTitle: Interval Prediction of Air Conditioning Load Based on Quantile Regression BiTCN-BiGRU-Attention Model*
abstract: Aiming at the characteristics of load instability and large volatility in the process of air conditioning operation, to better improve the prediction accuracy of air conditioning load and quantization the uncertainty of prediction results, this paper proposed an improved neural network model composed of Bidirectional Temporal Convolutional Network based on Attention mechanism (BiTCN) and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU). Quantile Regression (QR) was applied to realize interval prediction of air conditioning load. The model was trained and tested adopted measured data from an office and a machine room in both summer and winter. The results showed that the average MAPE and R2 of the prediction model were 2.3% and 0.980, respectively, while the average PICP (Prediction Interval Coverage Probability) and PIMWP (Prediction Interval based Mean Width Percentage) were 0.965 and 0.213, respectively. It was verified that the proposed method had a good prediction effect on both point prediction and interval prediction of air conditioning load.

articleTitle: A More Lightweight and Accurate Object Detection Network for UAV Aerial Images
abstract: Object detection technology plays an important role in the application of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). There are many small targets, multiscale targets, and noise interference of complex environments in UAV aerial images, which often lead to false and missing detection. To solve the above problems and reduce the computational burden in practical application, this paper proposes a more lightweight and accurate object detection network based on YOLOv8 for UAV aerial images.
