We redesign an efficient feature extraction network based on MobileViT, which can simultaneously extract global and local information in complex backgrounds, and learn better feature representations with less computational cost. Besides, a feature fusion named DSCFF that can fully interact the semantic information with the spatial information is proposed, enhancing the detection ability of various scales, especially small targets. Finally, we perform the lightweight design of the decoupled head to reduce the increased computation due to the decoupled structure. Experiments on the VisDrone2019-DET dataset indicate the proposed method raises mAP50 by 2.2% and 2.4% on the validation set and test-dev set respectively, while its parameters and computation are reduced by 6.1 M and 4.3 G respectively. The experimental results on the DOTA-v1.0 dataset further prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Backstepping Sliding Mode Control for Double-Pendulum Tower Cranes
abstract: Most of the previous studies on tower cranes simplified the payload as a single-pendulum model, neglecting the double-pendulum effect when the hook mass approaches the payload mass. In this study, a dynamics of tower cranes considering double pendulum effect is developed on the basis of Euler-Lagrange technique. An adaptive backstepping sliding mode control (ABSMC) algorithm is presented to achieve precise positioning and eliminating oscillations. Simulation results validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Optimization of Desulfurization Control System for Thermal Power Plant Based on Improved Model Predictive Control
abstract: Thermal power plants produce large quantities of SO2 and other toxic gases during power generation, which cause serious pollution to the atmosphere and ecological environment. How to better control the desulfurization process to improve and optimize the emission of harmful gases has become a difficult point in the thermal system, this paper uses a control scheme based on the model predictive control (MPC) algorithm and improves it. Firstly, the model of the desulfurization system was established through system identification. Secondly, the MPC algorithm was used to optimize the pH value of absorber tower slurry and the outlet net flue gas SO2 concentration. Finally it was compared with the PID algorithm in the Matlad platform. From the experimental results, it can be concluded that the MPC algorithm can eliminate pH oscillations in order to reduce SO2 emissions and improve the blindness of human control operations. The improved MPC algorithm reduced the outlet net flue gas SO2 concentration by 8% compared to the MPC algorithm.

Author Keywords: outlet net flue gas SO2 concentration control

articleTitle: Strict Lyapunov Functions for Time-Optimal Sliding Mode Control Algorithm
abstract: Strict Lyapunov functions, with a negative definite derivative, for the time-optimal sliding mode control (TOSMC) algorithm with perturbations, are provided. Here, we present a new nonlinear feedback control technique that combines the classic “bang-bang” time-optimal control (TOC) with methods for sliding-mode control. This approach can achieve robust TOC for double-integral plants under perturbations. A family of switching lines with different slopes is introduced to obtain the desired fast response for those plants with a simple and robust control algorithm. The proposed Lyapunov functions ascertain finite time stability, provide an estimate of the convergence time, and give the upper bound of perturbations for ensuring robustness. Test scenarios demonstrated the system behaviour associated with this proposed TOSMC algorithm.

articleTitle: GS-U-Net-An Catalyst Image Segmentation Model
abstract: The GS-U-Net presented in this study is a lightweight deep-learning model designed to improve the characterization of nanoparticles using transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The GS-U-Net is an innovative adaptation of the U-Net architecture featuring a VGG16-based encoder with a squeeze excitation (SE) attention mechanism and a GhostBottleneck module for enhanced feature extraction. The decoder part also integrates the SE mechanism and utilizes Ghost Convolution (GhostConv) instead of the standard convolution, which improves detection accuracy and reduces computational requirements. The performance of the model is evaluated by its Mean Intersection Union (MIOU) score, which improves from 89.71% to 90.07%. In addition, the parameter size of the model was drastically reduced from 24.892MB to 15.563MB, which significantly reduces the computational load and increases the detection speed. The improvement in efficiency and accuracy of the model helps to advance nanoparticle characterization research.

articleTitle: Capacity Maximization Based Multi-Resource Assignment for IRS-Assisted Cognitive SWIPT with Nonlinear Energy Harvesting
abstract: In this paper, capacity maximization based multi-resource assignment strategy is proposed for intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-assisted cognitive simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) with nonlinear energy harvesting in overlay spectrum sharing scenario. The maximum cognitive SWIPT sum capacity is set as the optimization target, which is subject to secondary transmitter (ST) power control, cognitive SWIPT user nonlinear energy harvesting and the modulus of IRS reflection coefficient element constraints. The multi-resource assignment strategy is investigated via the resolution of this nonlinear non-convex optimization problem with multi-variable coupling. Alternating optimization (AO) is implemented to obtain optimal subcarrier power and optimum IRS phase shift vector. Firstly, IRS phase shift vector is fixed, then the Lagrange duality is applied to search optimal subcarrier and power. Once the optimal subcarrier and power are obtained, IRS phase shift vector is derived via successive convex approximation (SCA) approach. Simulation results indicated that, the proposed scheme effectively allocates multi-resource such as subcarrier power and IRS reflective beamforming vector. The maximum sum capacity can be achieved in IRS-assisted cognitive SWIPT with practical nonlinear energy harvesting case.

IEEE Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer

articleTitle: An Improved A* Algorithm for Ocean-Going Vessels to Avoid Dynamic Time-Varying Obstacle Areas
abstract: At present, ocean-going vessels typically rely on static and dynamic environmental information obtained from meteorological forecasts for path planning. However, there is no optimal global path planning algorithm that can balance the computational speed and avoiding of dynamic obstacles. A brief overview of the commonly used A* algorithm and other popular path planning algorithms is given in the paper, and an improved A* algorithm is proposed. By employing the Probabilistic Roadmap Method (PRM) for mapping, the proposed algorithm enhances the capability to handle continuous spaces and increases flexibility in path planning. Furthermore, during the search process, the algorithm incorporates an assessment of the suitability of points to be explored at subsequent steps, enabling ocean-going vessels to rapidly plan the shortest path that avoids dynamic time-varying obstacle areas.

articleTitle: Speed Profile Optimization for High-Speed Maglev Trains Considering the Constraint of Auxiliary Stopping Area
abstract: Auxiliary stopping areas play a crucial role in maintaining the safety and reliability of high-speed maglev train operations. In this paper, a multi-objective speed profile optimization model for high-speed maglev trains is established based on kinetic equations, considering the objectives of energy conservation, punctuality, parking accuracy, and speed limits of auxiliary stopping areas. To overcome the shortcomings of MOP-SO, particularly its limitations in solution quality, low iteration efficiency and inclination towards local optima, a refined multi-objective particle swarm optimization (RMOPSO) algorithm is introduced. Simulation results indicate that RMOPSO remarkably enhances both solution quality and iteration efficiency.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Control for Nonlinear Networked Cascade Control Systems with State Delay
abstract: This paper focuses on the event-triggered control problem of nonlinear continuous network cascade control systems (NCCSs) with network delay and state delay. Firstly, to markedly enhance transmission efficiency in the network environment, an event-triggered mechanism is introduced, and a nonlinear NCCS model is constructed by taking into account the influence of nonlinear disturbance and double time delays in the system. Secondly, by constructing Lyapunov generalized functions and with the help of known theorems, the sufficient condition for system stability is provided. Then, the design of the two state feedback controllers is accomplished using the LMI toolbox in Matlab. Finally, the feasibility of the method is confirmed in a simulation example of a thermal power plant, which demonstrates good performance.

articleTitle: An Event-Triggered Adaptive Tracking Controller for Nonlinear Systems With Pure-Feedback Form
abstract: This paper is concerned with the adaptive event-triggered tracking control (AETC) problem for nonlinear systems with pure-feedback form (NSPF). Firstly, this paper uses adaptive estimate and mean value theorem (MVT) to overcome unknown constant parameter and non-affine input burden. In addition, a transformation based on monotonically decreasing positive continuous function is introduced, which can be used to deal with uncertain virtual control coefficient (UVCC) arising from the decoupling of pure-feedback systems. Finally, the event-triggered threshold is used to implement the switching of the value-triggered strategy.

articleTitle: Human Activity Detection Algorithm Based on TSACT Model
abstract: Human activity recognition technology based on WiFi has attracted considerable attention in health monitoring and medical treatment due to its characteristics, including the absence of additional equipment, strong privacy protection, and comprehensive coverage area. However, due to the high complexity involved in WiFi signal detection and human activity, the recognition rate of human activity based on WiFi signal detection is not ideal. To effectively explore the mapping relationship between WiFi signal variations and human activity, this paper proposes a TSACT model(Combined Time and Space Domain Information for Human Activity Detection). The TSACT model recognizes that CSI signals encompass both temporal and spatial feature information, and relying on information from only one dimension may result in the omission of critical data, thereby affecting the final activity recognition rate. Therefore, TSACT integrates temporal and spatial characteristics to identify human activities. In the conclusion of the paper, the recognition rates of human activities using temporal features, spatial features, and the TSACT model are compared. The proposed scheme achieves a higher recognition rate.

articleTitle: Saliency-Guided and Feature Fusion with Transformer for Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation
abstract: We propose a saliency-guided Transformer-based weakly supervised semantic segmentation network to address the issues of limited target range and unclear boundaries in the localization of target regions in current weakly supervised semantic segmentation networks. Firstly, by adjusting the weights of attention heads, the model can more completely cover the tar-get area when generating class activation maps. Simultaneously, a saliency-guided self-attention fusion module is introduced to provide more reliable boundary information for the generated class activation maps. To further enhance the performance of weakly supervised semantic segmentation, an online gradient clipping mechanism is designed to effectively filter redundant gradient information by setting appropriate thresholds. Finally, class activation map generation and semantic segmentation ex-periments were conducted on the Pascal VOC dataset, resulting in more complete class activation maps. By obtaining more comprehensive class activation maps, we address the issue of in-sufficient supervision information in weakly supervised semantic segmentation, thereby improving the model's accuracy.

articleTitle: A Two-Stage Coverage Path Planning Compliant with the Kinematic Constraints of USVs
abstract: The existence of omitted areas is unacceptable in coverage missions such as maritime search and military reconnaissance. Therefore, it is crucial to plan a path that can guarantee the full coverage of the mission area and conform to the kinematic characteristics of Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs). To achieve this objective, this paper proposes a two-stage coverage path planning algorithm aimed at optimizing coverage paths of underactuated USVs. In the first stage, the USV is modeled as a particle to facilitate path planning, and an improved Direction Highest Priority First (DHPF) coverage path planning algorithm is proposed to minimize collision risks for USVs during turns near obstacles. In the second stage, two kinematic constraints, turning radius, and safety distance, are incorporated into the USV model, and a multi-strategy switching framework is devised to tackle planning challenges associated with different types of paths. Specifically, an improved Hybrid A-star path planning algorithm with a variable step size is proposed to minimize both the path length and search time, and a backward mechanism is introduced to ensure full coverage of the area when forward turning conditions of the USV cannot be satisfied. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed coverage path planning algorithm.

articleTitle: A Communication Adaptation Method for New Power Load Management System Based on Game Theory and GMARCOS
abstract: In the context of low-carbon economic development, new power load management system businesses exhibit increasingly differentiated and diversified communication technology performance requirements. Selecting appropriate communication technologies that meet the requirements of businesses is crucial to establishing a safe, reliable, and economical new power load management system. Firstly, this paper comprehensively considers performance factors such as bandwidth and latency to construct an adaptability evaluation system. Secondly, a comprehensive weighting method based on game theory is proposed to weigh the evaluation indicators, incorporating expert experience and the inherent laws of the data. Finally, the Measurement of Alternatives and Ranking according to Compromise Solution (MARCOS) method improved by grey relational analysis is used for the adaptability ranking decision of communication technology. A numerical example shows that the proposed evaluation system and adaptation method offer a robust theoretical framework and practical solution for selecting communication technology for the business of the new power load management system.

articleTitle: Controller Design for a Class of Nonlinear Discrete Networked Cascade Control Systems With State Delay and Network-Induced Delay
abstract: This research investigates nonlinear discrete network cascade control systems, focusing on the challenges posed by network-induced delays and state delays. First, a discrete NCCS model was developed, incorporating a commonly used nonlinear system into the NCCS framework, resulting in a new model. The new model fully accounts for both network and state delays, and two state feedback controllers were designed using linear matrix inequality techniques. An actual case is provided to demonstrate the efficacy of the suggested cooperative design method.

articleTitle: Bird Species Recognition by Integrating EfficientNet-B0 Deep Learning Architecture and Broad Learning System
abstract: Accurate identification and classification of bird species are crucial for advancing research and conservation efforts, enhancing our understanding of population dynamics, and implementing targeted conservation strategies. Despite its importance, this task is challenging due to the wide variation in bird appearances and environmental noise, which can lead to poor generalization and increased complexity. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel bird species recognition method, EN-BLS, which integrates the EfficientNet-B0 deep learning architecture with a broad learning system. EfficientNet-B0 is used as the backbone network for feature extraction from bird images, with the final feature map layer serving as input for the broad learning system. The resulting hybrid model, EN-BLS, is designed for bird species classification. The model's performance is evaluated using the Birds 525 Species dataset, the latest publicly available benchmark dataset with the highest number of categories collected from diverse real-world environments. Experimental results show that EN-BLS achieves a recognition accuracy of 93.79<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> with lower computational complexity compared to existing methods, demonstrating its effectiveness for bird species diversity monitoring and conservation efforts.

articleTitle: Human Hand Trajectory Prediction Using RNN Enhanced with KAN and Horizontal Vertical Exponential Gated Unit
abstract: Human motion prediction is a significant and challenging problem in the field of machine intelligence and a crucial component for achieving effective human-robot interaction. Robots need to accurately predict human future movements to safely plan their own trajectories, thereby cooperating effectively with humans. This paper proposes a framework for trajectory prediction based on an improved RNN neural network, combining the KAN network and Horizontal-Vertical Exponential Gating Units (HVEGU). This framework is specifically designed for human-robot interaction in medical dispensing scenarios, particularly when data representation capabilities are limited or hand motion trajectories are complex. We evaluate performance based on the average prediction error at each prediction step. Experimental results demonstrate that the KGRNN framework excels in predicting hand movements in medical dispensing scenarios. It maintains a low average error, around 7 cm. Compared to popular non-Transformer methods like LSTM, RNNIK-MKF, and WITRAN, KGRNN shows significant error reduction across various step lengths, with a maximum reduction of 26.67%. These findings indicate that our proposed KGRNN framework performs excellently in handling human-robot interaction tasks involving complex trajectories in medical dispensing scenarios.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Cooperative Guidance Against Aerial Target for Unpowered Glide Vehicle
abstract: This paper investigates the spatial-temporal guidance problem for multiple unpowered High-speed Glid Vehicles (HGV). First, a 3D vector guidance law is given by extending the traditional 2D guidance law to 3D scenario, in which the terminal angle constraint and time-coordination of multiple HGVs are satisfied. Then, the time-to-go estimation problem considering moving target for HGV without active velocity control is addressed by numerical integration, and from which predictive intercepting point (PIP) is gained, thus the problem of intercepting a moving target simultaneously is simplified as guiding multiple HGVs to hit a fixed point along different directions at same time. Taking into account that aerial target can evade threats through terminal maneuvering, an extended state observer is used to estimate the acceleration of target. Accordingly, a sliding mode terminal guidance law designed in the framework of Line-of-Sight (LOS), which is different from the previous guidance law, is used to compensate the disturbance caused by the maneuvering target. Unlike similar existing results, the proposed guidance strategy for HGV can satisfy spatial-temporal constraints when the target is moving or maneuvering, and the guidance law designed in this paper is appropriate for unpowered vehicles without constant velocity. Numerical simulations are provided to show the effectiveness of the proposed cooperative guidance law.

articleTitle: A Trusted Multiview SAR Target Recognition Algorithm for Seaward Targets Based on Pseudo View Enhancement
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) is widely used in the fields of strategic exploration and ocean surveillance due to its all-day, all-weather wide-area search and detection capability.SAR images are sensitive to the imaging azimuth, and the SAR images of the same ship target in different azimuths have certain differences, and the multi-azimuth SAR image sequence contains rich classification and identification information. Aiming at the problem that environmental interference and data corruption affect the reliability of multi-view integration and final decision, this paper proposes a credible multi-view ship target recognition algorithm based on pseudo-view enhancement, which achieves high recognition accuracy under interference conditions, small datasets, and variations in the number of input images, respectively. The experimental results show that the recognition accuracy of this method is better than other target recognition on most of the datasets and has a certain degree of robustness.

articleTitle: BFD-DDPM: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models for Bearing Fault Diagnosis
abstract: Rotating machinery fault diagnosis is of paramount importance in industrial production. In this field, the proposed generation model breaks through the restriction of machine learning on the completeness of sample set in the process of model training. While Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have shown potential in this domain, their susceptibility to training collapse due to stringent parameter selection remains a concern. In addressing these challenges, we propose BFD-DDPM, a novel bearing fault diagnosis grounded in the principles of unsupervised learning via the diffusion model. Utilizing the Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM) - an enhanced generative model, normal samples of mechanical vibration signals are studied in an unsupervised manner to capture their prevalent distribution in a latent space. Subsequently, equipment fault diagnosis is achieved by locating the nearest generated data of test samples within this space via denoising diffusion, utilizing the Manhattan distance metric. Compared to unsupervised learning-based fault diagnosis methods, this paper demonstrates the advantages of DDPM in terms of accuracy and the robustness of parameter selection.

articleTitle: A Construction Method of a Network-Type Index System for Air Combat System Effectiveness Evaluation Based on Association Rules Mining
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the traditional tree-type and cluster-type index systems do not fully meet the requirements of complex air combat effectiveness evaluation under the background of system combat, a method of constructing network-type index system is proposed. Firstly, through the analysis of the index hierarchies of typical complex air combat systems, the capability hierarchy indexes with network characteristics are selected as the research object. Then, FP-Growth algorithm is used to mine the association rules among indexes and compared with Apriori algorithm in the difference of run time. Then, the lift is introduced to quantitatively describe the influence relationship among the indexes and the air combat effectiveness evaluation network-type index system is constructed. The feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Prescribed-Time Bipartite Consensus of High-order Multi-Agent Systems Based on Barried Lyapunov Function
abstract: This study addresses the prescribed-time bipartite consensus problem of higher-order heterogeneous multi-agent systems (HMASs). Firstly, a bipartite consensus protocol is designed to enable all agents to achieve bipartite consensus. Secondly, based on the barrier lyapunov function (BLF), a prescribed-time algorithm is developed to ensure that bipartite consensus among all agents is reached within a prescribed-time. The convergence time of this algorithm is independent of initial conditions and parameters. Concurrently, the consensus error is constrained to satisfy predefined conditions. The effectiveness of the proposed control method is ultimately validated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Estimation of Peanut Seedling Emergence Rate of Peanut Based on Deep Learning and Drone Imagery
abstract: Obtaining the number of peanut seedlings and seedling emergence rate in a timely and accurate manner is of great significance for yield prediction. However, current labor survey methods of peanut seedling have problems with backward means, time-consuming and inefficient. In this study, peanut seedlings collected from various peanut germplasm resources and subjected to different management conditions during 2022–2023 were used as the research subjects. Visible light images of the peanut fields, captured by unmanned aerial platforms, served as the data source. A deep learning method was employed to construct a training model for detecting peanut seedlings. The results show that the model trained based on the YOLOv5-1 algorithm performs best in peanut seedling number recognition, with a precision of 98.34% in the validation set, a recall rate of 96.09%, and an average precision (AP) mean of 97.98%. The model shows good applicability in complex field environments and can quickly and accurately detect the number of peanut seedlings during the peanut seedling stage, which provides a technical reference for peanut seedling counting and yield estimation in the field.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Filters-Based Adaptive Heading Tracking Control of Marine Vehicles Subject to Asymmetric Dead-Zone Output
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive control method using an improved nonlinear filter is designed for the heading tracking problem of marine vehicles with asymmetric dead-zone output under stochastic noise. Firstly, a smooth approximation model is introduced to address the non-differentiable phenomena caused by dead-zone output in the control process. Then, the unknown nonlinearity in the marine vehicles model is approximated by a fuzzy logic system (FLS), and FLS properties are utilized for relevant deduction. Afterwards, an improved nonlinear filter technique is proposed to avoid the issue of explosion of complexity (EOC) encountered in the backstepping method. Subsequently, the boundness of all signals in the closed-loop system in probability is proved using the stochastic Lyapunov method. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through the provided simulation results.

articleTitle: Improving Transmission Efficiency and Reliability for UAV Networks Based on Loongson Embedded System
abstract: This paper introduces the QUIC(Quick UDP Internet Connection) protocol into UAV(Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) networks with the aim of enhancing transmission efficiency and reliability for UAV networks on Loongson embedded system. It briefly outlines the principles and characteristics of QUIC, substantiates the feasibility of porting QUIC to Loongson embedded system, which can serve as control unit of UAV networks, and sets up a semi-physical network emulation platform to comparatively test the performance of QUIC against TCP(Transmission Control Protocol) and UDP(User Datagram Protocol) in networking environments. The results show that QUIC is approximately 61.82% faster than TCP under normal conditions and about 13.8 times faster under extreme conditions. Additionally, QUIC is 88.7% more reliable than UDP in the tested channel environment, indicating that QUIC is a more ideal transport layer protocol for UAV networks.

articleTitle: An Inception-GRU-SE Based Method for Arrhythmia Diagnostic
abstract: To address the challenge that a single network is insufficient for extracting comprehensive features from ECG data, we propose an Inception-GRU-SE-based diagnostic model for ECG signal classification. This model aims to enhance the efficiency of ECG screening while alleviating the workload of healthcare professionals by classifying ECG signals into seven distinct categories. The research primarily focuses on the following aspects: merging datasets of raw electrocardiogram (ECG) signals, standardizing ECG data using the Z-score method, annotating ECG signal labels, and subsequently thoroughly evaluating the proposed model using the processed ECG data. Experimental results show a significant improvement in ECG classification accuracy with the proposed model, achieving 99.13% accuracy on the test dataset compared to existing approaches.

articleTitle: Phase Angle Measurement System for Energy Meter Composed of Multiple Single-Phase Measuring Chips
abstract: Traditional three-phase electric energy meters adopt the current transformer sampling method, which is susceptible to constant magnetic field interference and easy DC saturation, while the manganese-copper sampling method can well solve the problem of anti-DC component of the electric energy meter. When disturbed by a magnetic field, the energy error jumps, Therefore the all-manganese-copper sampling scheme used on the three-phase electric energy meter mainly faces the problems of electrical isolation of the three-phase metering circuit and the problem of asynchronous sampling of the three-phase signal. This paper introduces a phase angle measurement system composed of multiple single-phase metering chips, including the structure and working principle. It uses the synchronous zero-crossing sampling method to achieve high-precision phase angle measurement, reverse phase sequence analysis and unbalance judgment under three-phase electricity, which has high industrial practical value. Experiments are carried out on the stereotype of the phase angle measurement system. The results have shown that the phase angle runout are all within 0.5°.

articleTitle: Loadformer: Power Load Forecasting Based on Transformer
abstract: Load forecasting is essential for the efficient operation and planning of power systems. Accurate load prediction enables utility companies to ensure reliable electricity supply, optimize generation and distribution resources, and reduce operational costs. However, the nonlinearity and uncertainty of grid load pose significant challenges to accurate load prediction. To address these issues, a Transformer-based forecasting model, named Loadformer, is proposed to achieve highly accurate load forecasting. Firstly, the sliding window strategy is introduced to divide the historical load data into different patches, which can not only reduce the input sequence length to the model, but also enable the model to learn temporal information at multiple scales. Subsequently, an improved Transformer encoder is employed to capture the rich nonlinear relationships within the historical load data, and a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) is used to directly perform multi-step forecasting. Finally, comparative experiments and ablation studies reveal that Loadformer exhibits superior accuracy and robustness in load forecasting.

articleTitle: Obstacle Avoidance Path Planning and Trajectory Tracking of Unmanned Logistics Vehicle Based on MPC
abstract: To address the obstacle avoidance challenges faced by unmanned logistics vehicles during trajectory tracking, this paper presents a hierarchical control approach that integrates obstacle avoidance path planning and trajectory tracking, utilizing model predictive control (MPC). Firstly, an upper-layer obstacle avoidance path planning controller is designed using the vehicle kinematics model. The artificial potential field function is incorporated to represent the collision risk based on the relative states of obstacles and the vehicle. Secondly, a lower-layer trajectory tracking controller is developed based on the vehicle dynamics model, utilizing MPC to ensure accurate tracking of the obstacle avoidance path. Finally, a CarSim-Simulink cosimulation platform is established to evaluate and validate the performance of obstacle avoidance path planning and trajectory tracking across two different scenarios and three vehicle speed levels. The simulation results demonstrate that, compared to the classical MPC, the proposed hierarchical controller reduces lateral acceleration amplitude by 26.18% when avoiding a single obstacle and by 18.56% when navigating multiple obstacles. This indicates that the proposed approach achieves superior obstacle avoidance and trajectory tracking performance compared to the classical MPC controller.

articleTitle: Adaptive Backstepping Control for a Class of Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems with Time-Varying Actuator Faults
abstract: This paper considers the tracking control design for a class of uncertain second-order nonlinear multi-agent systems. To eliminate the adverse effects of the unknown time-varying actuator faults, we propose a novel filter-based distributed fault-tolerant control scheme by utilizing the adaptation technology and backstepping control method. Then we prove that the developed approach not only achieves fault tolerance ability effectively but also guarantees the tracking performance well. Finally, the simulation results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Cooling Load of Central Air Conditioning System for Cruise Ship
abstract: Taking cruise ships as the research object, this study establishes models of the main types of cabins and public areas on cruise ships using the TRNSYS simulation platform. Apply the corresponding dynamic meteorological parameters on the cruise route to the established model and output hourly load data of summer cruise ships. The Pearson correlation analysis method is used to determine input variables and obtain the original dataset. Various representative intelligent algorithms are selected for training and prediction. The results show that the Random Forest algorithm performs best, providing a reference for subsequent energy-saving operation and fault diagnosis of cruise ship air conditioning systems.

articleTitle: Blood Cell Detection: Enhanced YOLOv9 Algorithm
abstract: Blood cell examination is a vital diagnostic tool in medicine, yet traditional methods suffer from low efficiency and accuracy due to overlapping cells, varying sizes, and high densities. To address these challenges, we present an enhanced version of the real-time object detection algorithm YOLOv9, incorporating a novel AKELAN4 module for improved blood cell recognition. Unlike previous approaches, AKELAN4 uniquely integrates Adaptive Kernel Convolution (AKConv) with Inverted Residual Multi-Branch Attention (IRMB), enabling simultaneous dynamic kernel shape adjustments and multi-scale feature extraction. This synergistic combination excels in detecting early-stage abnormalities and irregular shapes. To optimize model efficiency, we introduce the DySample sampling operator and Space-to-depth Convolution (SPDConv) module, reducing redundant calculations and enhancing feature learning efficiency. Our improved YOLOv9 algorithm achieved state-of-the-art performance on the Blood Cell Classification Dataset (BCCD), with 87.2% precision and 93.4% mean average precision, outperforming the recent YOLO-BC model by +6.3% and +3.4%, respectively. This work marks a significant advancement in blood cell detection research, with potential clinical applications.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control Analysis of Horizontal Cable-Driven Rehabilitation Robot
abstract: Addressing the current problem that the lower limbs of patients in the early stages of rehabilitation affect the effect of rehabilitation training due to muscle weakness, this paper proposes a modeling and control strategy for the new horizontal cable-driven rehabilitation robot (HCDRR). Firstly, the kinematic model of lower limb is established to derive the mapping relationship between the joint angle and the trajectory of the moving platform. The relationship between the change of cable length and the trajectory of the ankle joint of the lower limb is derived by the spatially closed vector method. Secondly, the dual-space dynamics model about the human lower limb workspace and the cable space is established, and the cable tension is optimized to ensure that the cable is always under tension. Finally, a dual-space adaptive neural network sliding mode control strategy is proposed to address the problems of modeling errors and uncertain disturbances in horizontal cable-driven rehabilitation systems. Taking the rehabilitation action of hip and knee flexion as an example for experimental verification, the results show that the proposed control algorithm can achieve high-precision trajectory tracking.

articleTitle: Research on Trajectory Tracking Control of Robots in Narrow Spaces Based on Disturbance Compensation
abstract: The precise tracking of planned paths in narrow spaces has always been a research hotspot and challenge in the field of robotics. This paper proposes a model predictive control framework based on active disturbance compensation, aiming to address the interference issues caused by robot inertia and sideslip in narrow spaces. We introduce a disturbance observer to estimate disturbances and utilize a spatial decomposition method for active compensation. An MPC optimization problem is established and solved to achieve precise tracking control. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted in narrow spaces, and the results demonstrate that the improved MPC algorithm significantly outperforms the traditional MPC algorithm in terms of control performance.

articleTitle: Nussbaum-Based Adaptive Neural Fractional-Order Sliding-Mode Fault-Tolerant Control of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
abstract: To realize the tracking control of fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) with actuator fault, an adaptive neural network (NN) fractional-order (FO) sliding-mode fault-tolerant control (FTC) method is proposed. The Nussbaum function is employed to handle the loss-of-effectiveness fault, and the adaptive method is combined with radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) to learn the bias fault. Furthermore, FO sliding-mode mechanism is designed to heighten the robustness. The Lyapunov method is employed to prove the stability of FTC system. Finally, simulation results are provided to show the effectiveness of the designed control method.

articleTitle: Interactive Multi-Trajectory SLAM for Large-Scale Mapping
abstract: Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) has shown significant success in constructing environmental map. However, as the scale of the environment expands, the accuracy and global consistency of these maps tend to decrease. In response to this challenge, we introduce an interactive multi-trajectory SLAM framework designed for large-scale mapping, with the aim of enhancing both the quality and scale of the generated maps. This framework optimizes a pose graph comprising initial constraints generated by an automatic SLAM process, supplemented by additional map merging and correction constraints created by users via a graphical user interface (GUI). We propose a human-assisted inter-trajectory loop closing technique for manually adding map merging constraints. Evaluation results confirm the efficacy of our proposed framework in achieving a large-scale, consistent environmental map with minimal human effort. Furthermore, it demonstrates robustness for large-scale incremental mapping.

articleTitle: A Polynomial Approximation Algorithm for the Adaptive Control of High-Speed Train
abstract: The paper investigates the approximation of the complex additional resistance encountered during high-speed train operations and proposes the adaptive driving strategy of high-speed train which adopts polynomial approximation. By analyzing the forces acting on the train, the study employs a polynomial approximation method to adaptively adjust the polynomial variables, enabling real-time modeling and compensation of the unknown additional resistance. Simulation results show that this method effectively handles unknown additional resistance in complex operating environments, improving control accuracy and system stability. The velocity error and displacement error are reduced to the order of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${10}^{-3}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${10}^{-2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Research on Missing Value Compensation of Skiing Data Based on Neural Networks in Optical 3D Motion Capture
abstract: It is necessary to adopt an human action capture system to capture and analyze the movement posture of athletes. However, it cannot cover all experimental areas during the collection process as the camera's perspective, resulting in missing marker points in the collected data, which is inconvenient for later analysis of sports data. This research focuses on the missing value completion of skiing data based on the neural networks in optical 3D motion capture. Specifically, the Qualisys motion capture system is utilized to collect the skiing data of athlete by wearing 17 key points. In the case of a missing key point in skiing data, all the collected key point data is randomly masked with one key point, and part of it is used as the training set and the reset part as the validation set. Then, the fully connected neural network and ResNet are combined to train and compensate the collected data. Finally, the compensation results are verified by real data, which is of great significance for analyzing the sports posture.

articleTitle: Combining Centralized and Decentralized Federated Learning: An Integrated Framework
abstract: Centralized federated learning (CFL) can lead to communication bottleneck because of bottlenecks, and decentralized federated learning (DFL) may cause the training trapped in the local optimum due to the lack of global views. In this paper, we propose an integrated framework of federated learning that combines the advantages of CFL and DFL. First, we design an algorithm by periodically performing global aggregation, neighbor consensus and local stochastic gradient descent (SGD). Second, we prove the convergence of the designed algorithm and analyze the effect of two stages (global aggregation and neighbor consensus) on the convergence. Finally, experiment results based on the CIFAR-10 dataset show that the integrated federated learning (IFL) accelerates the convergence and has higher accuracy compared to CFL and DFL.

articleTitle: Robust Output Voltage Tracking with Prescribed Performance for Single-Phase UPS Inverters
abstract: This paper deals with the robust output voltage tracking problem with prescribed performance for single-phase voltage source uninterruptible power supply inverters. We construct two linear internal models to reproduce the steady-state information, based on which we transform our problem into the robust stabilization problem with prescribed performance of an augmented system. Then, we incorporate a novel error transformation into the existing framework for the robust output regulation problem to design a stabilization controller, based on which we synthesize our control law to make the tracking error converge to zero asymptotically while always satisfying the prescribed performance.

articleTitle: Full Focus Imaging of Concrete Ultrasonic Array Based on Semi Sparse Matrix
abstract: The versatility, excellent durability, plasticity, and relatively economical production cost of concrete make it the primary material choice in today's construction and infrastructure fields. The interior of concrete is composed of cement slurry, mortar, aggregates, voids, bubbles, possible steel bars, and additives, which make ultrasonic energy easily attenuated in concrete. In this paper, the finite element model of concrete is established by comsol simulation, and the signal received by the probe is preprocessed. In order to avoid noise errors, the signal is transformed by Hilbert. Aiming at the problems of large data scale and long computation time of full-focus imaging algorithm, a semi-sparse matrix full-focus imaging algorithm is studied. The full-focus imaging of full matrix, half matrix and sparse array matrix is compared. The simulation results show that the semi-sparse matrix full-focus imaging algorithm can effectively reduce the computational load, reduce the imaging time, achieve higher signal-to-noise ratio, and reduce the defect sidelobe by controlling the number of transmitting array elements.

articleTitle: An Interpretable GWO-LSTM-SA Model for Crystal Diameter Prediction in Czochralski Process
abstract: The growth process of Czochralski silicon single crystal (Cz-SSC) has problems such as high nonlinearity and time-varying working conditions, making it difficult to develop a precise crystal diameter model through first principles. To address this problem, an interpretable long short-term memory network model (LSTM-SA) based on self-attention is proposed and used to predict crystal diameter. Firstly, the maximum mutual information coefficient (MIC) for selecting the characteristic variables related to the crystal diameter is used. Secondly, the SA mechanism is integrated into the LSTM network, which helps the model automatically learn and focus on the time periods and key variable information that have a significant impact on the prediction of the crystal diameter index. Then, the network parameters of the LSTM are optimized using the gray wolf optimization (GWO) algorithm to achieve the best prediction. Finally, using SHAP algorithm to complete the interpretability of crystal diameter prediction results, to quantitatively obtain the contribution and direction of different characteristic variables to the prediction results. Based on the actual industrial data, an interpretable prediction model GWO-LSTM-SA for crystal diameter was established. The experimental results show that the proposed method provides accurate predictions and interpretable results compared to other conventional models.

articleTitle: A Novel SIR Model-Based Public Opinion Propagation and Optimal Control
abstract: A strategy for optimal control is introduced to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SI_{1}I_{2}R$</tex> public opinion propagation model. This incorporates the enhanced epidemic model along with real-world public opinion propagation characteristics. This paper primarily focuses on identifying the right method to steer public opinion trends. Initially, The basic reproduction number of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SI_{1}I_{2}R$</tex> model is calculated using the next-generation matrix method, which can determine whether rumors will prevail. Subsequently, to construct a harmonious network environment, control variables are introduced to formulate an optimal control problem. The controllability of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$SI_{1}I_{2}R$</tex> model with control terms is analyzed, and the minimum value principle is employed to develop an optimal control strategy. Finally, we deduce that false information can be controlled by executing effective control measures. Moreover, the control cost can be minimized. The validity and efficiency of our approaches are demonstrated through comprehensive simulation examples.

articleTitle: Design of Stress Point Detection System for Tempered Glass Based on Contact Image Sensor Optical Image
abstract: As large-format tempered glass is widely used in construction-related industries, higher requirements are placed on its safety testing. Based on the optical principles and imaging characteristics of Contact Image Sensor (CIS), this paper proposes a design scheme for a large-format glass inspection system based on CIS camera, and builds an experimental test platform based on it. The platform has the ability to test tempered glass with a width of 1.8m. For tempered glass covered with 1/4 polarizing film, The experimental results show that the best stress spot imaging effect can be achieved when the focus height is 26.5±0.5mm and the exposure is 10.5us. Compared with the existing image acquisition system based on Charge-coupled Device (CCD) camera, the accuracy of defect recognition is improved from 92.84% to 98.76%.

articleTitle: Motion Control for Hydraulic Steel Grab Excavator Based on Contour Compensation
abstract: Hydraulic steel grab excavators are widely used in steel handling tasks. However, due to nonlinear characteristics, large inertia, and hydraulic circuit coupling, achieving precise contour control is challenging, making steel grabbing and unloading tasks more complex. To address this issue, this paper proposes a contour compensation-based motion control method for hydraulic steel grab excavators. By analyzing the contour error characteristics across different operational stages, we design a contour compensation method to achieve precise trajectory tracking control of the end-actuator. Experimental results show that the proposed method limits the maximum tracking error in the horizontal direction within 3.72 cm, with an average error of 1.04 cm during the entire steel-grabbing process. Compared to traditional PID control, the proposed method reduces the maximum tracking error and average error by 76% and 66%, respectively, demonstrating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Bipartite Consensus for General Second-Order Systems with Communication Delay
abstract: This paper discusses bipartite consensus and bipartite tracking consensus for general second-order multi-agent systems (MASs) under signed digraphs in the presence of communication delay. In light of the reduced-order observer, distributed output feedback controls are applied to general second-order MASs. Utilizing the tree-type transformation, knowledge related to graph theory, and characteristic equation analysis, certain conditions are determined for bipartite consensus and bipartite tracking consensus under communication delay. Finally, practical examples and simulations are included to confirm the theoretical findings.

articleTitle: Design of Intelligent Physiotherapy Room Temperature Control System Based on GA-Fuzzy-PID
abstract: In recent years, as the pressure of young and middle-aged people's study and work gradually increases, the demand for physiotherapy products gradually increases. In this paper, a graphene far-infrared intelligent physiotherapy room is designed. Aiming at the nonlinearity and large hysteresis of the temperature control system of the intelligent physiotherapy room, a control strategy based on genetic algorithm optimized fuzzy PID is proposed. First, the least squares method is used to determine the system model parameters. Then the PID model and the fuzzy adaptive PID model are established through Simulink. Finally, the fuzzy rules and PID control parameters are optimized using the genetic algorithm, and the fuzzy adaptive PID model optimized by the genetic algorithm is established. The simulation results indicate that the intelligent physiotherapy room temperature control system based on GA-Fuzzy-PID demonstrates significantly reduced overshoot, quicker response time, and enhanced resistance to interference compared to traditional PID and fuzzy adaptive PID controllers.

articleTitle: Multiple Static Target Hunting Based on the RRT and OSPA Distance
abstract: This paper considers multiple static target hunting control and path planning using multi-agents. The whole hunting process can be classified into two stages. The first is cruising stage, where the agents move in a certain formation to approach the multiple static targets. Once the agents enter into certain ranges around the targets, the agents will switch into the second stage of hunting. In these two stages, it is required to consider several issues: the agent controlling, path planning, and task allocation. Specifically, the traditional multi-agent controlling algorithm, rapidly-exploring random tree (RRT), and optimal sub-pattern assignment (OSPA) are respectively used in the process. Simulation experiment shows that the path planning and hunting algorithm can efficiently realize the formation movement and multiple static targets hunting.

articleTitle: An Improved A* Algorithm for 3D Path Planning of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
abstract: In this paper, A 3D path planning method of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) based on improved A* algorithm was proposed. The focus of the method is to assign dynamic weight functions to heuristic functions of the algorithm, and the change of dynamic weight functions can affect the proportion of heuristic functions, so as to achieve the purpose of reassigning search speed and search precision, and thus improve the overall time of path planning. The distance factor is constructed by the distance between the current point, the starting point and the target point, and is used as the variable of the dynamic weight function. In addition, the B-spline algorithm is introduced to deal with the path points generated by the improved A* algorithm, so that the path is continuous and smooth. Through the experimental simulation, the increase rate of operation time of the improved algorithm can reach 53.81%, which proves the effectiveness of this optimization method.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model and Adaptive Neural Network Flight Control of Wing-in Ground-Effect Vehicle
abstract: Based on the analysis of the initial design tasks for ground-effect vehicles, this paper utilizes the Vortex Lattice Method (VLM) in conjunction with the image method to establish a simplified, partially linearized multi-parameter mathematical model of the aerodynamic characteristics of ground-effect vehicles. Furthermore, considering the presence of various disturbances such as gusts and waves on the sea surface, an Active Disturbance Rejection Controller (ADRC) based on an Adaptive Radial Basis Function Neural Network (ARBFNN) has been designed for ground-effect vehicles. The adaptive RBFNN replaces the traditional Extended State Observer (ESO) in the estimation of disturbances and compensates them into the control inputs. Simulink simulation results demonstrate that this approach effectively addresses the issue of inaccurate disturbance estimation in traditional ADRC due to the fixed parameters of the ESO.

Author Keywords: Adaptive Radial Basis Function Neural Network

articleTitle: An IGD+ Indicator-Based Metric for Interactive Evolutionary Multi-Objective Optimization Algorithms
abstract: Interactive evolutionary multi-objective optimization algorithms have received widespread research. The goal of these algorithms is to iteratively involve decision makers(DM) in the solution process, by providing preference information, the solution is guided to regions of interest. However, most indicators are designed to assess how well algorithms approximate the entire Pareto optimal front. In order to assess the quality of the preferred solution sets obtained by interactive algorithms, this paper introduces a novel performance indicator based on the modified inverted generational distance (IGD<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>). The indicator is examined using interactive evolutionary methods and demonstrating its capability to evaluate the performance of interactive algorithms.

articleTitle: Hybrid-Based Relightable 3D-Aware Generative Model
abstract: Lighting-based 3D-aware generative networks have a multitude of applications in computer vision and graphics. However, the problem of generalization remains unresolved. In this paper, we propose a novel hybrid disentangled method for lighting control. We introduce a lighting control module into the pretrained model that disentangles illumination from geometry and appearance in the latent space. For the intermediate illumination components, a physically-based illumination model is employed to explicitly represent the lighting, thereby generating relit images through physically-based rendering. To reduce the computational cost associated with the physically-based illumination model, we use a neural bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF). Our method enhances generalization capability without requiring additional supervision of intermediate components. We have experimented with the method on the FFHQ dataset and have outperformed the current method in terms of lighting accuracy.

articleTitle: Online Identification of Servo System Mechanical Model Using Dynamic Weighted Recursive Instrumental Variable Least Squares
abstract: During the prolonged operation of servo systems, various factors such as equipment aging and variations in working conditions, inevitably cause the model parameters to deviate, leading to a degradation in control system performance. To ensure that the servo control system maintains superior dynamic performance under uncertain conditions, it must possess the ability to monitor the system model in real-time and adaptively adjust the controller parameters. For this purpose, accurate identification of the key parameters in the system model serves as the foundation for optimizing the performance of the speed or position loop. To address this challenge, the present study employs a discretized mechanical motion equation of the servo system based on zero-order hold, while fully considering the impact of viscous friction coefficients and load torques on the identification results. By applying the Dynamic Weighted Recursive Instrumental Variable Least Squares method to the discrete-time model, this study successfully achieves the concurrent identification of dominant mechanical model parameters. To validate the effectiveness and practicability of the proposed identification method, detailed simulation was conducted in the MATLAB environment, and then experimental verification was performed on an STM32-based servomotor test-bench. Both simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the identification method presented in this study possesses high accuracy and good real-time performance, capable of reflecting changes in system parameters in real-time, providing strong technical support for parameter self-tuning in servo control systems.

articleTitle: Optimal Formation Control for Mobile Robots Under Prescribed Performance Constraints via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This study introduces an optimal control algorithm for the formation of mobile robots, addressing collision avoidance and adhering to specified performance constraints. The desired formation geometry is established within a leader-follower architecture, where each robot follows an intermediate leader while maintaining a desired distance. Limited communication range and collision avoidance are considered to ensure the safe operation of the formation system. Boundary functions defined as time-varying exponential functions are employed to manage transient performance of formation errors. To ensure transient and steady-state performance of formation errors, we propose a design technique of optimal formation control with prescribed performance. A reinforcement learning algorithm based on an actor-critic strategy is introduced to achieve optimal formation control and specified tracking accuracy simultaneously. Through stability analysis, it is demonstrated that the proposed optimal controller ensures the uniform ultimate stability of the formation system, while meeting the specified performance criteria. The effectiveness of the presented control algorithm is illustrated through experiment results.

articleTitle: SparallaxMPC: High-Speed Model Predictive Control Solver with High Sparsity and Parallelism
abstract: Model Predictive Control (MPC) is one of the most popular methods used in control problem. However, MPC is computationally demanding with limited use of sparse and parallel implementations. We present SparallaxMPC, a high-speed MPC solver with parallel and sparse representation. Our approach is based on sparse matrix representation and leverages the structure of the MPC problem for efficiency. We demonstrate the effectiveness of SparallaxMPC by benchmarking it against the state-of-the-art solver CasADi, achieving more than a 3x acceleration.

articleTitle: Path-Constrained Dynamic Optimization of Rougher Flotation Process
abstract: Concentrate grade directly affects the profit of rougher flotation process, and a dynamic optimization problem should be proposed with practical constraints to optimize the concentrate grade. In this paper, a nonlinear dynamic model of two-phase kinetic rougher flotation process is first constructed. Then, a dynamic optimization problem is presented whose objective function is the overall error between reference and actual concentrate grades, subject to path constraints and other functional constraints on feed flow, pulp level, concentrate grade, and tail grade. Furthermore, the optimization problem is solved to locate optimal control input with rigorous satisfaction of path constraints and other constraints by adapting a new dynamic optimization method. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed approach is verified by a numerical experiment of a rougher flotation process.

articleTitle: Design of a Multi-Step Predictive Control Alum Dosing System Based on GRU Neural Networks*
abstract: This paper proposes a predictive control alum dosing system based on a data-driven approach. Considering the highly nonlinear, uncertain, and time-varying parameters in the coagulation and sedimentation process of water treatment plants, a multi-step predictive control algorithm (GRU-MPC) is designed. This algorithm uses current and previous alum dosing amounts and effluent turbidity data to predict effluent turbidity over multiple future time steps. The approach includes: constructing a multi-step predictive neural network model, designing an objective function to minimize the difference between effluent turbidity and the target value while reducing the fluctuation of alum dosing amounts, optimizing the objective function using a sequential quadratic programming algorithm, and applying the optimal alum dosing amounts for real-time control. Simulation results show that the GRU-based multi-step predictive control method can effectively enhance the stability and resource utilization efficiency of the water quality control system.

articleTitle: A Complementary Augmentation Algorithm for Remotely Sensed Data Based on Radiometer Distortion Phenomenon
abstract: For the problem of distortion and loss of radiometer observation time series data, LSTM-based Seq2Seq network is used to augment and supplement the contours, and CNN network and RNN network are used as comparison items. Firstly, the basic principles network is introduced respectively; secondly, the microwave remote sensing data in Harbin are used to conduct data augmentation experiments, and finally the relevant conclusions are analyzed.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Guidance Law for Multiple Missiles with Impact Angle Constraint Against Maneuvering Target
abstract: For the problem of coordinated interception of maneuvering targets by multiple missiles in three-dimensional space, this paper proposed a consensual control method based on the theory of fixed-time convergence. The method combines the generalized consensus error and Integral sliding mode control to effectively deal with the target acceleration interference and realize the convergence of the Time-to-go of the formation members in fixed time. In the direction normal to the line of sight, a fixed-time non-singular fast terminal sliding control approach is designed to solve the terminal-guidance problem with an impact angle constraint, and the convergence of the system is proved by Lyapunov stability theory. It is verified by simulation that the algorithm demonstrates fastness and accuracy in three-dimensional cooperative interception, which can make the system converge in fixed time for both the time-to-go time and the line-of-sight angle.

articleTitle: Multi-AGV Task Allocation Strategy Based on Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Efficient task allocation for multiple automated guided vehicles (AGVs) in factory environments is one of the key issues in intelligent manufacturing. This study constructs a mathematical model with the goal of minimizing the total running time between delivery tasks, and optimizes it through an improved particle swarm optimization algorithm. The model first calculates the distance matrix from AGV to priority tasks, formulates a distance based priority task allocation scheme, and initializes particle positions. In addition, the model introduces a penalty term for task allocation balance in the evaluation function of the algorithm to reduce the inefficiency caused by imbalanced allocation. Through simulation experiments on 30 sets of tasks and 5 AGVs, it has been proven that the algorithm can effectively reduce the total running time when processing priority tasks, thus verifying the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: A Non-Calibration Nonlinear Errors Correction Method for Phase-Shifting Patterns
abstract: To reduce phase errors caused by nonlinear responses in the measurement system, we propose a non-calibration correction method for nonlinear errors in phase-shifting patterns. First, the captured grating fringes are transformed using a Fourier transform to convert the images from the gray scale to the frequency domain. The first harmonic frequency is then determined using an appropriate method. Second, the appropriate filter cutoff frequency is calculated by combining the phase-shift algorithm's sensitivity to different harmonics with frequency response curves. Low-pass filtering is then performed on the phase-shift patterns to suppress high frequencies caused by nonlinear responses, thus reducing phase errors in the actual measurement process. Finally, the standard plane and other irregularly shaped objects were reconstructed using the proposed method and other techniques. Measurement errors under different conditions were then compared. Experimental results show that the proposed method significantly suppresses gamma nonlinear responses and achieves high measurement accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: An Efficient Sampling and Search Method Based on Risk Framework in Highly Dynamic Scenarios
abstract: It is still a challenge to quickly plan a high-quality path that is collision-free and kinematically feasible in a highly dynamic environment with dense dynamic obstacles. Traditional risk-based motion planning algorithms solve the planning problem in the environment of human-machine coexistence by considering the risk of collision with dynamic and static obstacles. Although these algorithms solve the security problems of planning, they have problems such as too many iterations and low quality of planning paths. Therefore, combined with the Artificial Potential Field method (APF), this paper introduces an efficient sampling method into the risk-based motion planning algorithm to guide the growth of random trees to the feasible region, effectively reduce the redundant nodes of random trees, and improve the quality of planning trajectories. Finally, simulation experiments are carried out in different highly dynamic hybrid scenarios, and the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by comparing with Risk-RRT and Multi-Risk-RRT.

articleTitle: Observer-Based Sliding Mode Control Triggered by CPS Events Under Periodic Denial of Service Attacks
abstract: This study examines the resilience of linear CPSs under periodic DoS attacks using a triggering mechanism. The model and assumptions are first outlined, followed by a communication strategy designed to reduce network traffic. Details of the DoS attack model, including attack and dormancy periods, are presented. A state observer and sliding mode controller are developed to counteract DoS effects. Using stability proof techniques, the system's asymptotic stability and performance are demonstrated. Key steps for controller design and stability analysis are provided. The triggering mechanism is also analyzed to confirm the absence of Zeno behavior in practical scenarios, ensuring the strategy's feasibility and reliability.

articleTitle: Graph Attention Network-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Traffic Signal Priority Control
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is widely applied to the problem of adaptive traffic signal control (ATSC). This paper presents an efficient RL algorithm to address ATSC issues. We adopt the decentralized multi-agent advantage actor-critic (A2C) algorithm, where distributed control methods introduce new challenges: the environment becomes partially observable for each local agent. To tackle this issue, we incorporate spatial infor-mation from neighboring agents using graph attention networks (GAT) to learn collaborative control strategies. Additionally, to better adapt to real-world road environments, we propose a hybrid reward function model. This model ensures the traffic efficiency for social vehicles while emphasizing the priority of emergency vehicles (EMV), thereby reducing their travel time. We numerically evaluate the proposed method in a simulated environment containing 25 intersections. Experimental results demonstrate that the approach presented in this paper has significant advantages compared to similar algorithms applied to multi-agent ATSC.

articleTitle: Balance Control of Unmanned Motorcycle Without Self-Balancing Auxiliary Device Based on LADRC
abstract: Motorcycles, renowned for their ease of operation and superior passability, have emerged as a primary mode of transportation in numerous regions.However, their inherent difficulty in maintaining stability at rest or at low speeds is a problem that needs to be studied in depth, especially in the field of driverless motorcycles. To address this challenge and facilitate autonomous motorcycle operation, this study meticu-lously designed a comprehensive data acquisition and control system. In addition, the lateral force in the driving process of the unmanned motorcycle is studied in detail, and the rolling dynamics model of the unmanned motorcycle is established. By using this model, a linear active disturbance rejection con-troller(LADRC) is designed. By controlling the steering angular speed of the handlebars, the autonomous motorcycle can still control stably under the condition of changing driving conditions without self-balancing auxiliary device. To validate the efficacy of our proposed control scheme, rigorous simulations were conducted, demonstrating its potential. Subsequently, real-world experiments on an outdoor grass field further substantiated the feasibility of our data acquisition and control system, as well as the robustness of the controller under varied environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Event-triggered Adaptive Control of Switched Nonlinear Cyber-physical Systems
abstract: The event-triggered control problem of switched nonlinear cyber-physical systems (CPSs) is investigated under average dwell time (ADT). A new dynamic gain is proposed, which can effectively compensate for the unknown growth rate and measurement sensitivity. Then, a switched observer integrated with a novel dynamic gain is designed and an event-triggered output feedback controller is developed, which can effectively mitigate the communication burden. Finally, it is proved that all the closed-loop signals are bounded and all system states converge to the origin. Accordingly, the effectiveness of the presented scheme is verified through the simulation of switched RLC circuit system.

articleTitle: Enhancements in Data Querying: Applying MMR-Integrated In-Context Learning to LLM-based Text-to-SQL
abstract: In the modern business ecosystem, informed decision-making relies heavily on effective data utilization. To enable more intuitive and efficient data access, Text-to-SQL technologies serve as a crucial bridge. This paper introduces an improvement by integrating the Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) with In-Context Learning (ICL) to improve the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in generating SQL queries. This research focuses on strategically deploying MMR within ICL frameworks, optimizing prompt construction by balancing relevance and diversity of examples. This method was rigorously tested on datasets from domains such as tobacco and automotive marketing, as well as the cross-domain SPIDER benchmark. Results demonstrate that the proposed method excels in both domain-specific and complex questions.

articleTitle: YOLOv8-Sea: An Efficient Object Detection Network for Sea Surface Scenarios
abstract: Object detection in sea surface scenarios is a key task for unmanned surface vehicles (UAVs) to achieve autonomous navigation. This task usually needs to overcome difficulties such as different target scales, complex sea surface background and small targets at a long distance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes YOLOv8-Sea, a sea surface scene-oriented object detection network based on YOLOv8s. Our network introduces the Star-c2f module to improve the network's high-dimensional and nonlinear feature transformation capabilities; the Global-to-Local Spatial Aggregation (GLSA) module to enhance the network's ability in extracting object features from complex backgrounds; and the introduction of Inner-IoU loss to achieve faster and more efficient regression loss. By conducting experiments on a self-made sea surface object detection dataset, the experimental results show that our proposed network is 3.4% more accurate than the original YOLOv8s, and mAP@.5:95 is 2.5% better than the baseline model.

articleTitle: Distributed Event-Triggered Voltage Secondary Control Strategy for Microgrids Considering Load Forecasting
abstract: Voltage regulation in microgrids (MGs) is increasingly challenging due to the integration of renewable energy sources and load variability. This paper presents a distributed event-triggered voltage secondary control strategy for MGs, incorporating load forecasting using semi-Markov theory. By predicting load variations, the proposed method utilizes an event-triggered communication mechanism to adjust the voltage of distributed generation units, effectively solving voltage regulation issues caused by line impedance mismatches and load fluctuations. Lyapunov stability theory is employed to prove the stability of the event-triggered system with semi-Markov switching topology. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed control strategy significantly reduces communication frequency while maintaining voltage at its rated value, even under varying load conditions. This approach enhances the reliability and efficiency of MG operations, demonstrating its practical applicability in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: An Analytical Impulse Thrust Strategy in Spacecraft Pursuit-Evasion Games with Mass Variation and Perception Frequency
abstract: The domain of astrodynamics is witnessing a surge in scholarly interest, particularly concerning the spacecraft pursuit-evasion games. This treatise introduces an analytical methodology designed to deduce the optimal impulsive thrust game-theoretic strategies for spacecraft, considering both mass variation and the sensory limitations inherent in systems. The methodology commences by computationally delineating the relative reachable domain difference from a spatial geometry standpoint. Then, each spacecraft computes a threat index predicated on its perceptive faculties and the prevailing engagement geometry, then it strategically deploys thrust to precipitously diminish this index. The efficacy of the proposed analytical technique is corroborated by the simulation experiment. Given the analytical nature of the computations entailed, the approach holds significant promise for on-board application.

articleTitle: Auto-Regressive with Exogenous Input Modelling Based Model Predictive Control of Cement Grate Cooler
abstract: In the cement production process, the speed of grate coolers directly affects the residence time and cooling effect of cement clinker. Its effective control is of great significance to ensuring cement quality. But the adjustment of grate speed is a complex process, involving moderate cooling air, uniform clinker thickness, regulated output and other constraints. In this study, an Auto-Regressive with exogenous input (ARX) grate cooler prediction model is developed using a data-driven approach based on a company's cement production line, a model predictive control (MPC) approach is employed for the purpose of optimising the speed of the grate cooler based on the ARX model. The results demonstrate that the method of MPC exhibits greater stability than the method of PID, and that MPC technology has good efficacy and superiority in the adjustment of grate speed.

articleTitle: DDQN-Based Path Planning for Mining Cave Robots
abstract: This study aims to address the path planning problem in complex mining cave environments, with DDQN chosen as the algorithm for path planning. Firstly, we provide a detailed introduction to Q-learning, DQN, and DDQN. Subsequently, we introduce the DDQN algorithm into the field of path planning and explore its potential in solving path planning problems in unknown environments such as complex mining caves. In order to overcome the limitations of traditional DDQN algorithms in path planning, we propose an improved DDQN algorithm by introducing techniques such as experience replay, target network update, and exploration strategy optimization, thereby enhancing the effectiveness of path planning. Following this, we conduct a series of simulation experiments to compare the performance of traditional DDQN algorithms with that of the improved DDQN algorithms in various scenarios. The experimental results demonstrate that the improved DDQN algorithm exhibits faster convergence, more stable performance, and higher reward values in path planning, confirming its effectiveness and superiority in complex environments.

articleTitle: Prescribed-Time Average Consensus of Integrator-Type Multi-Agent Systems With Bounded Time-Varying Gain
abstract: This paper studies the prescribed-time average consensus of integrator-type multi-agent systems (ITMASs) with a bounded time-varying gain. A switching controller including a time-based generator (TBG) gain term and a fractional power term of consensus error is first designed for each agent. In the switching controller, the controller with the TBG gain controls the disagreement among all agents to an adjustable range within an arbitrary pre-assigned time. Then the controller comprising the fractional power of the consensus error controls the consensus error converges to zero in a pre-allocated time. By using the boundedness of TBG gain and finite time control theory, the ITMASs realize the prescribed-time average consensus and avoid numerical implementation problem.
