A simulation example verifies the validity of the developed switching controller.

articleTitle: Observer-Based Non-Fragile Intermittent Control for VSC-MTDC Under Non-Ideal Communication Channel
abstract: Multi-terminal direct current transmission (MTDC) systems, which rely on voltage source converters (VSC), have emerged as the premier solution for connecting offshore wind farms across vast distances. Nevertheless, the integration of VSC and MTDC with offshore wind farms is susceptible to various in-terferences and network security hazards. One significant threat is the Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks, capable of disrupting measurement signals and inducing instability within the VSC-MTDC systems. Therefore, ensuring the seamless observation of system measurement signals is imperative. To tackle this challenge, this paper introduces a semi-aperiodic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{DoS}$</tex> attack model and develops a non-fragile observer with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> stability. Our proposed approach establishes two sufficient conditions leveraging the time-varying Lyapunov function, and its efficacy is corroborated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Multi-Terrain Adaptive Control for Knee Exoskeletons: Development and Experimental Evaluation
abstract: Lower limb augmented exoskeletons (LLAE) could potentially be used in some domains (e.g. logistics) to enhance human walking ability. For walking with LLAE on different terrains, precise and flexible control strategies of LLAE are required to achieve smooth and natural motion transitions. However, previous control algorithms for LLAE are mainly developed for flat terrains, so the LLAE cannot be effectively used in work environments with other terrains such as slopes and stairs. Therefore, a multi-terrain adaptive assist algorithm based on parametric dynamic motion primitives (PDMPs), which can adaptively adjust assist torques according to terrain types, was developed in this paper to solve the above problems. The algorithm obtains the mapping relationship between the assistance sub-model and terrain slope for each terrain by polynomial fitting, thus modelling the multi-terrain adaptive assist algorithm based on PDMPs. The model is evaluated using a generalized validation method and the results show that the peak error in torques prediction of the model is less than 5%. To further validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, it was verified on a homemade LLAE and the experimental results showed that the proposed multi-terrain adaptive assist algorithm was able to reduce the human body's motion consumption by about 5%, which can facilitate the exoskeleton system to achieve the human-exoskeleton cooperative control.

articleTitle: Dynamic Event-Triggering Control for Discrete Time Singular Perturbed Switched Systems
abstract: This paper is concerned with the practical control for discrete time singular perturbed switched systems via the dynamic event triggering mechanism. The quasi-time parameter matrices are introduced into the novel Lyapunov function and much freedom degree is added into the stability analysis. And then, less conservative stabilization criteria are achieved to design sampling controllers with quasi-time gains. At last, a numerical simulation example is given to illustrate the effectiveness of results.

articleTitle: NFIM: A Neural Frequency Interpolation Model for Grid Load Time Series Forecasting
abstract: The grid load forecasting plays a crucial role in the steady operation management of smart grid system. However., the drastic and irregular fluctuations of grid load make the accurate forecasting difficult to achieve, and most of the existing models are unable to learn the complex data patterns of load data. In this work, we propose a novel framework named Neural Frequency Interpolation Model (NFIM) to tackle these challenges. NFIM is composed of 3 stacks, with each stack using a pooling layer and a multilayer perceptron (MLP) to extract feature representations from the input sequence, which are then decoded by different basis decoder modules. Such a structure helps the model learn the deep patterns of grid load data, such as pattern in frequency domain and multi-scale resolution, thereby achieving high-performance forecasting. Extensive experimental results on real-world dataset verifies that our model outperforms state-of-art deep learning models on grid load forecasting tasks.

articleTitle: Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation Network Based on Feature Decoupling and Pixel Aggregation
abstract: Image-level annotated weakly supervised semantic segmentation has garnered considerable attention because of its efficient annotation process and remarkable scalability. Most studies typically generate pseudo labels by leveraging class activation maps produced by classification networks, which are then used to train segmentation models. However, conventional class activation maps tend to focus on only parts of the foreground objects and are prone to encroaching into background regions, thus limiting segmentation performance. To address these issues, this paper proposes a weakly supervised semantic segmentation Network based on feature Decoupling and pixel Aggregation (DANet). The network consists of a decoupling branch and an aggregation branch. The decoupling branch, by disentangling foreground-background features, compels the model to concentrate on stable target representations while ignoring background noise. This effectively eliminates false associations between foreground and background, thereby addressing the co-occurrence problem. Meanwhile, the aggregation branch delves into global contextual information through a pixel aggregation module, generating more comprehensive class activation maps, which in turn yield improved segmentation performance. Benefiting from the synergy of the two branches, the network demonstrates advanced performance on the PASCAL VOC 2012 and MS COCO 2014 datasets.

articleTitle: Disturbance-Rejection Control of Motor Position Servo Systems with Experimental Evaluation
abstract: In this paper, a position servo controller is designed for motor position servo control, incorporating equivalent-input-disturbance (EID) compensation and a finite-time control law. This approach effectively suppresses unknown disturbances and ensures high-precision tracking of reference inputs. The disturbance estimate is then fed back to the control input to establish an anti-disturbance position servo controller. This controller is compared with a controller based on finite-time extended state observer. Finally, simulations and experiments verify that the proposed method can achieve fast and accurate positioning, demonstrating strong robustness against external disturbances and uncertainties.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Flexible Manipulator based on Lattice Structure
abstract: In this paper, a flexible manipulator based on lattice structure is proposed, which can realize multiple bending motions through the arrangement and combination of lattice units. To explore the deformation characteristics of this flexible manipulator, the mathematical model of the deformation for the manipulator is established through the assumption of piece wise constant curvature. Furthermore, the manipulator model is simulated to obtain the end trajectory or the maximum bending bangle of the manipulator by the UG software. Finally, the design's accuracy and effectiveness are validated through a comparative analysis of the experiment and simulation. The results shows that the designed manipulator present excellent flexible properties, offering a novel approach to the design of flexible manipulators.

articleTitle: Improved Model-Free Adaptive Control of Continuous Stirred Tank Reactor
abstract: In this paper, we present a model-free adaptive control method based on PID for a complex CSTR device in the chemical industry, which has strong nonlinearity and low mathematical modelling accuracy. This method extends the traditional MFAC method with PID controller and thus effectively improves the efficiency of the PID control system. In the simulation research, the control performance of the proposed PID - MFAC approach is contrasted with that of the traditional MFAC method. The outcomes demonstrate that the PID - MFAC approach has a more favorable control impact on CSTR, and its control performance surpasses that of the traditional MFAC method when a step -like disturbance occurs, signifying that the PID - MFAC approach has stronger anti - interference capacity.

articleTitle: Design of Automatic Painting System for Steam Turbine Stator Assembly Surface
abstract: In view of the current problems such as low manual painting efficiency, different sizes and shapes of each set of assemblies, and lack of actual assembly drawings, this paper completes the depth information acquisition and three-dimensional reconstruction of large workpieces by means of the combination of vision and robot, as well as the automatic planning of the painting path on the assembly surface of the steam turbine stator, and constructs a set of automatic painting system suitable for large surface products similar to large workpieces such as steam turbines, so as to realize the automatic painting operation on the assembly surface of the steam turbine stator.

articleTitle: Optimal Control of Multi-Rate Systems Using Inverse Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The goal of this study is to design an optimal tracking controller for multi-rate systems using inverse reinforcement learning (RL). The multi-rate nature of sampling and control periods in controlled devices complicates the implementation of optimal control methods. In this study, the objective performance functions are assumed to be unknown. Under this condition, we first derive an equivalent discrete-time system using the lifting technique. Then, an online model-free inverse RL algorithm is developed to learn both the optimal control policy and the unknown performance objective function for the tracking control of the lifted system. Finally, theoretical analysis and simulation examples demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed algorithms.

articleTitle: MS-GATformer:Multi-Scale Hybrid Prediction Based on GAT-iTransformer
abstract: In multivariate time series, data at any time is often not only correlated with historical values, but also with the values of the other parameters. However, most of the existing methods are one-sided, focusing only on the correlation in time dimension or between parameters when processing multivariate time series, and unable to fully extract features of time series data. In addition, for the time series data under different observation scales, the trend and periodic change also show different states, reflecting the internal characteristics of the data itself. It is important to extract the intrinsic features of time series data at different observation scales. This paper proposes to use multi-window pooling to decompose the trend and period of complex time series data, then use convolution layers of different sizes to obtain the trend and period components of different scales, and finally extract the trend and period components of different scales based on the spatiotemporal feature extraction module integrated by graph attention neural network and iTransformer. To obtain the time series trend and periodic change characteristics at different granularities, the effect of the proposed model is demonstrated through some data sets.

articleTitle: Optimization Scheduling of Virtual Power Plants with Electric Vehicles Based on Moth-Flame Optimization Algorithm
abstract: In recent years, distributed renewable energy generation has been vigorously developed to address energy crises, environmental pollution, and other issues. However, distributed renewable energy generation exhibits strong randomness and volatility. This paper constructs a dual-layer optimization scheduling model for virtual power plants (VPP) with electric vehicles (EVs), designs operational strategies for VPP integrating EV, and optimizes the output of each component using the moth-flame optimization algorithm. The moth-flame optimization algorithm demonstrates excellent search performance and robustness, suitable for solving complex real-world engineering problems. Simulation results indicate that coordinating output between EVs and controllable power sources can compensate for deviations in renewable energy output, reduce the grid impact caused by standalone EV grid integration, and enhance the supply reliability of virtual power plants.

articleTitle: A Laser Centerline Extraction Method for 3D Reconstruction of Throttle Valves
abstract: In the process of 3D measurement and reconstruction using line-structured light, the most critical step is the extraction of the laser stripe centerline, as its extraction accuracy has a decisive impact on subsequent measurement precision. Due to its metallic reflectivity, the throttle valve can cause the laser stripe to lose its original Gaussian characteristics, thereby reducing extraction accuracy. This paper proposes a method for extracting the stripe centerline specifically for the 3D measurement of throttle valves. First, the method preprocesses the grayscale image using filtering to smooth the image and reduce interference from noise and speckles. Next, the image is binarized to reduce its complexity. Then, edge detection is used to extract the stripe contour. Subsequently, the light stripe contours are extracted through edge detection, and the centerline of the laser stripe is extracted using the gray level centroid method for the detected laser stripe contours. The comparison results yield that the proposed method improves the speed and accuracy of stripe center extraction compared to traditional grayscale centroid methods, meeting the requirements for real-time 3D reconstruction and ensuring the precision and real-time performance of 3D measurement and reconstruction.

articleTitle: Analysis of Motion Intention Prediction Based on Human Gait Data
abstract: In the research of lower limb rehabilitation robotics, accurate prediction of human motion intention plays a key role in achieving active robot control, providing personalised rehabilitation programmes and enhancing training effects. Although there have been more studies on motion intention recognition methods based on physiological signals (e.g. EMG and EEG signals), there is still a relative lack of research on continuous motion estimation at multiple joint angles. To address this, a multi-objective gait prediction model is developed to simultaneously estimate the motion trajectories of the bilateral hip and knee joints. This model integrates joint position data obtained from the NOKOV motion capture system with a hybrid architecture combining convolutional neural networks (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks. Experimental results demonstrate the model's capability to accurately predict joint motion trajectories, providing robust data support for the active control of lower limb rehabilitation robots, and highlighting its potential for practical implementation in rehabilitation training protocols.

articleTitle: Robust Subband Adaptive Filtering Algorithm Based on Fair Estimator
abstract: This paper tackles the challenge of identifying sparse systems in environments with impulsive noise and proposes the FNSAF algorithm, which combines the Fair estimator with normalized subband adaptive filter (NSAF) algorithm and exhibits high robustness to impulsive noise. To enhance the flexibility of the FNSAF algorithm and enable it to adaptively balance the trade-off between rapid convergence as well as low steady-state MSD, we propose the adaptive threshold FNSAF algorithm (AF-NSAF). In this algorithm, the threshold parameter of the Fair function is updated in real time, allowing for better handling of complex noise environments. Additionally, based on energy conservation argument, stability conditions for both AF-NSAF and NSAF algorithms are provided, along with the computational complexity for the algorithms used in the experiments. Ultimately, computer simulations in impulsive noise scenarios validate the effectiveness of our algorithms for sparse system identification.

articleTitle: A Metapopulation Seir Model with Asymptomatic Individuals Based On Human Mobility Patterns
abstract: In the post-pandemic era, new variants of COVID-19 continue to emerge and spread within communities across various regions, underscoring the importance of epidemic control and prevention. However, previous research has largely overlooked migration behaviors and individual awareness. In this paper, we propose a Susceptible-Exposed-Asymptomatic-Symptomatic-Recovered (SEI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sup>I<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup>R) model with a self-protection mechanism that simulates the impact of awareness in the metapopulation network. The proposed model incorporates analytical expressions for each state, derived from human mobility patterns using the microscopic Markov chain approach (MMCA). Simulation results highlight the significant influence of initial mobility rates and population size on disease transmission. We present an example of a real transportation network for metapopulations to illustrate its effectiveness in depicting epidemic dynamics.

articleTitle: Multi-Algorithm Fusion Framework for Trajectory Prediction of Human Upper Limb Motion
abstract: To achieve the accuracy and security controlling of human-robot collaborative in the medical laboratory, a multi-algorithm fusion framework for human upper limb trajectory prediction is proposed. The main idea can be described as follows. A fusion strategy for integrating three algorithms including partial time series classification, representative trajectory, and polynomial fitting that can recognize human behavior and provide trajectory prediction is given. It can improve the accuracy of human-robot cooperation. The framework is divided into the online phase and the offline phase. The offline phase is designed to learn the parameters required by the predictive model from the task data directly, and the fusion method combines different algorithms; In the online phase, based on partial trajectory classification, polynomial fitting algorithms and representative trajectory algorithms have been used to predict the trajectory within a given time node. We discuss its accuracy in simulations. Furthermore, the framework was evaluated on a well-designed human upper limb dataset that collects the videos of humans-robot collaboration in a real scenario. The results show that our method could predict human trajectories better than the state-of-the-art forecasting algorithms.

articleTitle: Heart Rate Estimation Algorithm for Radar Signals Based on Resnet18 and MobileViT
abstract: Non-invasive heart rate monitoring technology using millimeter wave radar offers high comfort, high convenience, and wide applicability to different user groups. However, current heart rate monitoring algorithms are likely to be affected by environmental noise, DC offset, and respiratory harmonics, which can compromise result accuracy. To address these issues, this paper proposes a radar signal heart rate estimation algorithm based on Resnet18 and MobileViT. In the phase preprocessing stage, techniques such as phase difference calculation, interpolation smoothing, and wavelet threshold denoising are employed on the phase signal. During the heart rate estimation stage, the Resnet18 and MobileViT networks are utilized to process the phase signal. Experimental analysis indicate improved heart rate estimation accuracy with the proposed method..

articleTitle: Voltage Sag State Estimation based on Hybrid Neural Network using One Dimensional CNN and GRU
abstract: Voltage Sag State Estimation (VSSE) based on voltage information collected by monitoring devices at limited nodes in the distribution network can identify weak links in the power grid, evaluate economic costs, verify corresponding responsible parties, and take corresponding solutions for voltage sag suppression. Therefore, in this paper, a combined deep learning method using one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Networks and Gated Recurrent Unit is adopted for VSSE solution. Here, the high-dimensional features in the voltage sag monitoring information are extracted via one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Networks, and then the temporal features is further learned through Gated Recurrent Unit. Finally, the voltage sag state, that is, the voltage sag amplitude range of all other nodes without monitoring devices installed, is obtained. Based on this method, it is not necessary for physical model or any other prior conditions, such as system parameters, operating mode, and so on. The effectiveness of the proposed method is also verified via IEEE 33 system, and the VSSE accuracy can reach 98.32 % under the premise of three monitoring points.

articleTitle: Improving Load Frequency Control in Power Systems with Energy Storage Devices via FOPID Controllers
abstract: Power systems play a crucial role in providing sustainable energy across various sectors, including critical applications such as military equipment. However, optimizing their stability to meet modern energy demands presents a considerable challenge. This paper introduces a novel methodology aimed at improving the stability of a three-zone hydroelectric power system. The approach involves the integration of fractional-order proportional integral derivative (FOPID) controllers and energy storage devices (ESDs), supported by an improved whale optimization algorithm (WOA). The proposed method demon-strates significant efficacy, notably reducing frequency overshoot by 82.2%, from -0.1437 Hz (ISFS) to -0.0256 Hz in Zone 1. This innovative approach offers several advantages, including rapid response times and seamless convergence, thereby leading to improved stability in load frequency control.

Author Keywords: Fractional order proportional integral derivative controllers

articleTitle: Formalization of the Cauchy Convergence Criterion for Sequences in Coq
abstract: The Cauchy Convergence Criterion is a fundamental theory in mathematical analysis. It has a wide range of applications, including sequences, functions, integrals, series, and the completeness of real numbers. Recently, significant progress has been made in the formalization of mathematical theorems, accompanied by strong advocacy for trustworthy mathematics, the strengthening of fundamental mathematical theories has become increasingly important. As a cornerstone of Limit Theory, formalizing the Cauchy Convergence Criterion holds significant importance. This paper utilizes the computer-assisted proof tool Coq, based on the Morse-Kelley (MK) axiomatic set theory formalization system, and employs the real number model provided in Zorich's “Mathematical Analysis” to complete the formal proof of the Cauchy Convergence Criterion for sequences. Through this formal proof, we have established a basis for the formalization of MK-based limit theory and calculus in Coq.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach to Resolve Velocity Aliasing in Blood Flow Velocity Measurement
abstract: The detection of hemodynamic parameters is crucial for early diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases. Traditional non-parametric methods for blood flow velocity measurement have drawbacks such as poor measurement precision and limitations imposed by the Nyquist limit. The recently presented one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1DCNN) method improves precision but suffers from significant fluctuations and suppression of reverse blood flow signals. To address these issues, this paper proposes a dual-branch convolutional neural network (DBCNN) method combined with singular value decomposition (SVD) for blood flow velocity measurement. Initially, SVD filtering was applied to simulated echo signals to remove substantial clutter. The filtered data was then processed by the DBCNN model for secondary filtering and blood flow velocity measurement. This model comprises two branches that estimate blood flow velocity magnitude and direction, enabling vector blood flow estimation and color imaging. Ultimately, the DBCNN model accurately estimated blood flow velocities within 1.2 times the Nyquist speed range, improving the performance of velocimetry and imaging. Compared to the SVD method using correlation algorithm and the 1DCNN model, the DBCNN model reduces the normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) for blood flow velocity profiles by an average of 32.61% and 19.7%, respectively.

articleTitle: LSTM with AhI-Model Based Kalman Filter for Lithium-ion Battery State of Charge Estimation
abstract: Accurate state of charge (SOC) estimation of lithium-ion battery in battery management system (BMS) is important for the safety and reliability of electronic devices and electric vehicles. This paper proposes a LSTM-extended Kalman filter based on AhI-model (LSTM-EA), which constrains SOC result from LSTM with an AhI-model based Kalman filter. AhI-model is based on Ampere-hour integration method and requires simpler structure to obtain estimated SOC with higher accuracy and robustness. In the experiments, the public datasets from the Center for Advanced Life Cycle Engineering (CALCE) are used to validate the SOC estimation performance. The mean absolute error (MAE) and maximum error of the proposed method are less than 2.51% and 8.82% respectively.

articleTitle: Depth-Supervised Neural Radiance Fields for Accurate Novel View Synthesis
abstract: We present Depth-NeRF as a promising solution to address the limitations of Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF). NeRF effectively encodes scenes into neural representations, allowing for the photo-realistic rendering of novel views. However, it falls short in capturing surface geometry, restricting its rendering capabilities to surface colors alone. For overcoming these limitations, we have undertaken substantial modifications to the NeRF network architecture and strategically incorporated depth information to guide its optimization. This method ensures that the ray termination distribution conforms to the scene's geometric properties, thereby producing renderings with improved precision and accuracy. Compared to NeRF, our method achieves a substantial improvement in rendering quality, while simultaneously reducing the RMSE between the rendered and actual scene depth. These improvements unequivocally demonstrate our approach's superior ability to capture the scene's geometric information.

articleTitle: Knowledge Distillation-Based Federated Fine-Tuning Under Resource Constraints
abstract: Model fine-tuning is an effective machine learning method that allows pre-trained models to adapt to different downstream tasks. However, in the context of federated learning, it is not realistic to directly fine-tune the pre-trained model due to the storage, computation, and communication resources constraints of user devices. The communication overhead of traditional federated learning increases with the size of the model. In addition, sharing locally trained models may pose a risk of privacy leakage. To address the aforementioned issues, we propose knowledge distillation-based federated fine-tuning. We use LoRA, a parameter efficient fine-tuning method, to reduce user storage overhead during local training epoch. We implement model-free federated learning using knowledge distillation, eliminating the impact of LoRA model dimensions on communication volume. Our algorithm effectively avoids the high communication overhead caused by multiple exchanges of pre-trained model parameters, while protecting user privacy. The experimental results on the image classification dataset SVHN and CIFAR10 demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on Parameter Optimization of Levitation Controller for Fast Maglev Train
abstract: Maglev train as an efficient mode of transportation, the high performance operation of its levitation system is the key to achieve stable transportation, engineering applications and commercial operations generally use PID controllers to achieve stable levitation of the levitation system. However, the traditional PID controller is difficult to adapt to the complex and changing operating conditions. In order to solve this problem, this paper mainly investigates a parameter optimization method of PID controller based on Non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II). Firstly, a single-point levitation model is analyzed and established with the Changsha Maglev train as the object. On this basis, the methods of deterministic, robust and stochastic performance evaluation are analyzed and the NSGA-II control structure framework and algorithm are designed. Finally, through simulation and comparison with the particle swarm algorithm, it is shown that the optimization of the PID controller parameters using the NSGA-II algorithm can better improve the robustness of the levitation system as well as the anti-interference ability.

articleTitle: Research on Geomembrane Leakage Detection Method Based on Quadruped Robot
abstract: Aiming at the problem of leakage detection of seepage control geomembranes in landfills, a fully autonomous dipole method detection system based on a quadruped robot equipped with a dipole sensor is designed. The feasibility and superiority of using a quadruped robot are analyzed on the basis of the detection principle of the dipole method. Due to the problems existing in the process of upgrading the artificial static detection to autonomous dynamic detection, a dynamic detection method based on a quadruped robot is designed while the structure construction of the dipole method on the quadruped robot is completed. The experimental results show that the efficiency of geomembrane leakage detection can be improved with detection system method employed in this paper.

articleTitle: Attitude Estimation Based on Angular Accelerometer in High Dynamic Environments
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of attitude estimation drift in high dynamic environments by proposing an attitude algorithm based on angular accelerometer. The system configuration includes an angular accelerometer, a linear accelerometer, and a magnetometer. A mathematical model using the rotation matrix as the state variable is developed, and the invariant unscented Kalman filter is employed for attitude estimation. Through simulation experiments, the accuracy of the proposed algorithm is compared with a traditional gyro-only method. Results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm offers superior performance in high dynamic scenarios, significantly enhancing system bandwidth and reducing error drift. This research contributes to improving precision in high dynamic attitude estimation applications.

articleTitle: A Noble EEG Classification Method Using Wavelet Scattering of Feature Extraction for Mental Attention State Detection
abstract: The mental attention state directly affects an individual's learning ability. It is important for teachers to understand a student's mental attention state in real teaching. Although many experts have started relevant research on mental attention state recognition, the classification algorithms proposed by these studies can only be limited to a specific field, lacking applicability to common application scenarios. Additionally, the number of mental attention states that can be classified is generally dominated by 2 or 3 categories. Therefore, this paper proposes a general algorithm for mental attention state classification by using electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. First, a wavelet scattering network is introduced to obtain the wavelet scattering features matrix of a specific time segment EEG signal. Feature vectors are obtained by statistical analysis of the wavelet scattering features matrix. The classification model is an ensemble bagged tree; 75% of the feature vectors are used for training the model, while 25% are used as the test set. The experimental results of three open datasets show that the proposed method can better achieve EEG mental attention state classification, with recognition accuracy rates of 99.99%, 100%, and 88.43% in 3, 4, and 5 categories, respectively. Compared with other literature methods, this method has the advantage of high recognition accuracy and reduces the time required for recognition.

articleTitle: A Gesture Recognition Method Based on Improved YOLOv8 Detection
abstract: Aiming at the existing hand gesture estimation algorithms with large computation and poor real-time performance, this paper proposes an improved YOLOv8 algorithm for hand recognition, which combines the improved YOLOv8 detection algorithm for the detection of the hand and combines it with gesture analysis to realize gesture recognition. The improved algorithm not only reduces the amount of floating-point arithmetic, but also increases the accuracy and robustness of detection. In the gesture detection part, the traditional YOLOv8 algorithm is improved by firstly adding the p6 detection head, secondly replacing the CBS module with RFSE module, and thirdly replacing the C2f module with CFE module. The gesture analysis part is performed by training the yolov8 classification model for gesture recognition. The test results of the improved model in TV-Hand and COCO-Hand datasets confirm the effectiveness of the improved YOLOv8 algorithm in this paper, which improves the accuracy by 2.3% and reduces the computational volume by 13.5% compared to the original YOLOv8n, and the correct rates of gesture recognition are all over 90%, and the improved algorithm, which ensures the lightweight and at the same time realizes the further enhancement of accuracy The improved algorithm can realize further improvement of accuracy while ensuring lightweight, and the application prospect is broader.

articleTitle: Unilateral Payoff Control is Infeasible in Network Attack-Defense Interactions
abstract: Network resilience generally refers to the ability of a network to maintain normal operation in the face of various failures and disturbances, which has many applications in social, financial, communication, and transportation systems. There is a large amount of research on designing strategies to disrupt the network from the perspective of attack and to protect the network from the defense standpoint. However, attacks and defenses in the real world often occur simultaneously and repeatedly. The study of network resilience should not be limited to the structural characteristics but should consider the functional characteristics of the network. We develop a general game-theoretic framework to study attack-defense repeated interactions on complex net-works and examine the possibility of achieving precise control over the payoffs of attackers and defenders. Our findings reveal that neither the attacker nor the defender can unilaterally control their own payoff, the opponent's payoff, or any linear combination thereof. This work highlights the limitations of unilateral payoff control in real-world interaction scenarios, a consideration often overlooked in numerous theoretical studies.

articleTitle: Dual-Branch Speech Enhancement Network for Noise-Robust Automatic Speech Recognition
abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) has achieved remarkable successes thanks to the end-to-end deep neural networks, but it is still challenging in the noisy and reverberation environments. The joint training of front-end speech enhancement (SE) and speech recognition system becomes a popular solution to the noise-robust ASR. However, the speech distortion problem arisen due to excessive information suppression by the SE module. To address this issue, in this paper, a novel dual-branch SE (DBSE) module is proposed as the front-end of the ASR system for joint training. Particularly, the two branches extract the clean speeches using different ways: one branch directly extracts clean speeches and the other branch utilizes spectral subtraction method. The final denoising speech signals are obtained by combining the outputs from both branches. In this way, the oversuppressed information can be compensated from each other. The two-stage joint training strategy is adopted for the noise-robust ASR model where the proposed DBSE is first pretrained by multitask reconstruction loss, and then the DBSE and ASR model is jointly trained using the speech recognition based loss function. Comparisons with several state-of-the-art ASR algorithms on benchmark dataset are conducted, and the results demonstrate the superior performance of our proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Normalizing Flow Learning Based Restoration for Low-Light Images with Massive Zero-Element Pixels
abstract: The low-light image enhancement task learns the mapping of low-light images to normal images by training paired or unpaired images, but it does not restore the missing areas composed of massive zero-element pixels(ZEP). In this paper, we propose a normalizing flow learning based restoration for low-light images with massive zero-element pixels(LLI-MZEP), named ZMAR-SNFlow, which is composed of a zero-element mask attention based Restormer (ZMAR) encoder and a strengthened normalizing flow (SNFlow). A new attention mechanism, zero-element mask attention (ZMA) is proposed in mask-based Transformer blocks to repair missing regions. Existing image restoration methods are trained with multiple loss functions, but we use a single negative log-likelihood loss for training, so that SNFlow can learn the conditional distribution of high-light images. Experimental results on three benchmark datasets show that the proposed ZMAR-SNFlow method can achieve state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance in low-light image restoration tasks.

articleTitle: AFPN Based YOLOX for Rotation Object Detection in Remote Sensing Image
abstract: Rotation Object Detection in Remote Sensing Image is a big challenge, as it has different sizes and orientations. In this paper, we proposed an AFPN and YOLOX based Rotation Object Detection method, named AFPN-RYOLOX. In the AFPN-RYOLOX, an angle prediction branch added into the detection head of YOLOX and revised the loss function to incorporate Kullback-Leibler Divergence (KLD) loss firstly, which enhanced loss continuity and ensuring scale invariance. Then, the Asymptotic Feature Pyramid Network (AFPN) is integrated in the neck layer of YOLOX, which boosts the network's capability to extract features and decreases the number of model parameters through a dual-phase adaptive spatial fusion process. Through compare with other SOTA method, the proposed AFPN-RYOLOX achieved superior performances on DOTA and HRSC2016 datasets.

articleTitle: Short-Term Wind Power Prediction Based on DTW-BiLSTM Modeling
abstract: Wind power forecasting plays a critical role in wind farm planning, operations, maintenance, and market trading. It improves the efficiency of wind energy production, minimizes system uncertainties, and provides a solid foundation for evaluating the economic viability of wind power and integrating renewable energy into the grid. However, the complex, non-linear nature of wind power data makes it challenging to capture the relationships within time series.To address these challenges, this study introduces a DTW-BiLSTM approach for short-term wind power forecasting. This method first captures the non-linear dependencies in the time series data through clustering, then extracts temporal features for each cluster. To enhance the accuracy and efficiency of forecasting, the dataset is normalized, and similar days are grouped using a sliding window technique. A BiLSTM model is then employed to fully capture the temporal correlations within the wind power data. To evaluate the effectiveness of this approach, the model was compared against LSTM, TCN, and CNN using performance metrics such as MAE, MSE, and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The results show that the proposed method outperforms the alternatives, offering more accurate and reliable predictions for wind power forecasting.

articleTitle: A Novel Photovoltaic Maximum Power Point Tracking Control Method Under Partial Shading Conditions
abstract: To enhance the power generation efficiency of photovoltaic (PV) systems, it is essential to ensure stable operation at the global maximum power point (MPP). This paper investigates the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) technique for PV systems and proposes an advanced MPPT technique based on the multi-subgroup parallel optimization algorithm with shuffled frog leaping algorithm (MSPO-SFLA), which integrates the improved particle swarm optimization algorithm with the shuffled frog leaping algorithm. The proposed MPPT technique not only enhances the accuracy and stability of MPP tracking but also effectively addresses the issue of traditional frog leaping algorithms falling into local optima under partial shading conditions (PSC). To validate the efficacy of the proposed method, a simulation model was developed in MATLAB. The simulation results demonstrate that this method significantly improves the operational efficiency of PV power generation systems, contributing to the advancement of the renewable energy sector and the progress of clean energy technology. Compared to traditional algorithms, this method exhibits clear advantages in achieving MPPT for PV power generation systems.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation based Defect Detection Algorithm for Ceramic Substrates
abstract: Semantic segmentation, an important technique, has been widely applied in defect detection and recognition in automated systems. However, it still faces challenges such as high parameter count and inaccurate defect boundary localization. To address these issues, this paper proposes a lightweight semantic segmentation algorithm for defect detection based on DeepLabV3+. Firstly, we utilize a lightweight network, MobileNetV3, to extract defect features from ceramic substrates. Secondly, we employ a parallelized approach with multiple layers of dilated separable convolutions to further extract deep features, which not only reduces the parameter count but also expands the effective receptive field. Lastly, we fuse the deep features, which incorporate essential channel features, with shallow features, and subsequently upsample the fused features using bilinear interpolation to generate the final segmentation predictions. Experimental results, when applied to defect detection in ceramic substrates, demonstrate that the improved model achieves higher segmentation accuracy, utilizes fewer parameters, and improves defect boundary localization capability.

articleTitle: Decentralized Impulsive Control for Stochastic Systems Interconnected over Graphs*
abstract: This article is concerned with stability analysis and decentralized impulsive control problems for a class of interconnected stochastic systems (ISSs). The ISSs is a class of large scale systems with numbers of subunits interconnected over graphs and each subunit may subject to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\it Ito}$</tex> -type noise disturbances. We first presented the related stability criteria for ISSs by using the stochastic multi-Lyapunov function. Secondly, an impulsive state feedback controller is designed to neutralize the stochastic disturbances and some instabilities caused by the interconnection among subsystems, at the same time the impulsive controller can guarantee that the closed-loop system have an ideal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> performance. At last, numerical simulations are established to prove the validity of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Multi-Motor Coordinated Propulsion Based on Improved Virtual Spindle Control
abstract: The multi-motor propulsion system of autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) is characterized by easy operation, good start-up and acceleration performance, and stable power supply. Aiming at the problem that the multi-motor propulsion system is susceptible to rotational speed desynchronization caused by external environmental perturbations and changes in its own parameters during the undersea exploration mission under complex current waters. design of a super-helical backstepping integral sliding film control strategy based on virtual spindle control. Firstly, according to the structure of multi-motor control system, the virtual spindle control idea is combined with weighted average deviation coupling compensation to compensate the multi-motor speed. Finally, the simulation results show that the synchronization performance, stability and dynamic response performance of the improved multi-motor coordinated propulsion control scheme are significantly improved.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Trajectory Optimization of Collaborative Robots Based on improved NSGA-III
abstract: In industrial production, collaborative robots require joint trajectories to meet multiple optimization objectives such as time, energy consumption, smoothness, and safety, to ensure the collaboration with humans. Therefore, this paper addresses the multi-objective trajectory optimization problem for collaborative robots, focusing on achieving the optimal time, energy efficiency, and smoothness. A method based on the NSGA-III is proposed to improve the issues of slow algorithm convergence and susceptibility to local optimal solutions. Firstly, to meet the requirement of smooth continuity of robot joint trajectories, seventh-order B-spline curves are used for planning to ensure the continuity and stability of robot motion. Secondly, considering the constraints of joint trajectories and robot kine-matics, emphasis is placed on the work efficiency, lifespan, energy consumption, and motion impact of the robot, proposing multiple optimization objectives including minimizing time, optimizing energy, and minimizing the motion impact. Finally, based on the characteristics of multi-objectives and the definition of the Pareto optimal solution set, the improved NSGA-III is utilized to solve the multi-objective trajectory optimization model. We further avoid the problem of the original algorithm prematurely falling into the local optima. Experimental results show that the optimized robot joint trajectories have shorter running time, lower energy consumption, and reduced motion impact. The continuity and smoothness of joint velocities, accelerations, and impact trajectories provide strong assurance for the stability and lifespan of robot motion.

articleTitle: Neural-Network-Based Adaptive Prescribed Finite Time Control for a Class of Second-Order Nonlinear Singularly Perturbed Systems
abstract: This article studies prescribed finite time control (PFTC) subject for a class of second-order nonlinear singularly perturbed systems (SPSs). An adaptive prescribed finite time stability strategy based on neural network (NN) is designed for SPSs. The key to successfully designing this strategy lies in introducing a crucial coordinate transformation during design procedures of the controller. This strategy not only ensures stability of the system but also guarantees that the convergence time of the system neither depends on the initial conditions nor on the design parameters. Meanwhile, this designed strategy is not based on a finite time interval, but rather on an infinite time interval. In the end, a simulation example is given to confirm benefits of designed strategy.

articleTitle: Target Intention Recognition Based on Multi-Type Information Fusion and DS Ensemble Classification in Aerial Combat
abstract: Aerial combat target intention recognition is a critical component of combat situational awareness, providing essential support for combat decision-making. Due to the robust learning capabilities of neural networks, neural network-based methods for target intention recognition have garnered significant research attention. However, existing methods often overlook the heterogeneity of information types, the latent information in future dynamic behaviors, and exhibit a lack of reliability in complex combat scenarios. To address these issues, this paper proposes a neural network model that integrates multi-type information fusion and Dempster-Shafer (DS) ensemble classification for aerial combat target intention recognition. The proposed model first performs classification based on data attributes and incorporates a prediction module, a neural network module, and an attention mechanism for the expansion, extraction, and fusion of feature information. Additionally, the model constructs an ensemble classifier grounded in ensemble learning principles and integrates the classification results using DS evidence theory to enhance reliability. The superiority and effectiveness of the proposed method are validated through comprehensive comparison and ablation experiments.

articleTitle: Security Event-Trigger Mechanism-based Diffusion Kalman Filter for Wireless Sensor Networks under Cyber-Attack
abstract: This paper studies the problem of state estimation in wireless sensor networks affected by false data injection attack. An event-triggered mechanism-based diffusion Kalman filter algorithm is proposed to solve this problem. Firstly, an event-triggered mechanism based on saturation function is designed to reduce the sampling rate of nodes and clipping abnormal measurements. To maintain the stability of node estimation and prevent the diffusion of contaminated data between nodes, a data transmission mechanism based on local outlier factor is designed to control the data exchange between nodes. Simulation results show that the designed algorithm improves the estimation performance in the case of false data injection attack, the communication rate between nodes and the transmission of contaminated data are reduced.

articleTitle: Mapping of Pipeline Networks Using ROS and Inertial Navigation Technology
abstract: In many cities, buried underground water supply pipelines have become outdated, and their maps have been lost, causing significant difficulties in the daily maintenance and upkeep of these pipelines. To address this issue, this paper focuses on developing a pipeline mapping system based on the ROS platform, utilizing a pipeline robot. The pipeline robot is designed with a structure mimicking an aquatic snake and is equipped with a high-definition camera, multiple sensors, and functionalities such as driving and illumination, allowing it to operate under pressure within the water supply network. The robot's pose and pipeline trajectory are obtained using its onboard 6-axis attitude sensors and odometry wheels. Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) is employed to fuse the 6-axis sensor data to determine the pose, and the same method is used to combine the odometry wheel and IMU data to obtain the robot's trajectory, which is then rendered into a pipeline map. A section of the underground water supply network in a certain area of Beijing was selected as the practical scenario. The rendered map was compared with the actual map, resulting in a comprehensive error of less than 1.5%, demonstrating certain practical engineering value.

articleTitle: Identification of Aerodynamic Coupling During Vertical Takeoff and Landing of Tilt-rotor Aircraft
abstract: The aerodynamic coupling between the rotor, wing, and ground is highly complex during the vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) process of a tilt-rotor aircraft, which severely affects flight stability. In this paper, a novel multi-input single-output feature model considering phase lag is first proposed to characterize the aerodynamic coupling mechanism during vertical takeoff and landing of the tilt-rotor aircraft. Based on that, a complete identification scheme for the rotor/wing/ground coupling of the tilt-rotor aircraft is proposed to derive the coupling law. Model comparison and performance verification based on flight tests are conducted to verify the accuracy of the model. The results demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed method in identifying complex aerodynamic coupling during vertical takeoff and landing of the tilt-rotor aircraft.

articleTitle: Straight-Line Autonomous Walking for Quadrupedal Robots
abstract: The autonomous walking of quadrupedal robots is currently realized mainly through perception, map building, localization, and planning. It also requires expensive hardware such as LIDAR, cameras, Graphics Processing Units(GPU) and so on. The pose of a quadruped robot is mainly estimated from the fusion of an inertial measurement unit(IMU) and kinematics. The integration aspect of the algorithm makes the pose estimation subject to time drift, and the control accuracy of the single-joint motors also affects the accuracy of the pose estimation. In addition, a study shows that the world's top quadrupedal straight-line walking more than 20m or so can be clearly seen lateral offset, its path is not straight, there is a tendency to change to the arc. To address the above issues, we propose a straight-line autonomous walking motion control method based on the position information estimated by IMU and kinematics of a quadruped robotic dog platform, using the coordinate point of the initial position of the autonomous straight-line walking function initiated as the reference system.The quadruped robot developed by Unitree B2 was selected as the experimental platform. The experimental results show that by using a two-dimension plane of joint control and the start point reference system, the method proposed in this paper realizes the autonomous straight-line walking, which enables the quadrupedal robotic dog to ensure that the position is on a straight-line in a Cartesian coordinates coordinate system, and that the heading of the quadruped is in the same direction as that of the straight-line. This improves the system straight-line autonomous walking accuracy, reduces the hardware cost, and reduces the algorithm cost.

articleTitle: Adaptive Control for a Class of Strict Feedback Nonlinear Systems Under Replay and Actuator Attacks
abstract: In this study, controller design and resilience analysis are investigated for a class of strict feedback nonlinear systems subjected to replay and actuator attacks. To maintain the stability of the system under these hybrid attacks, an adaptive controller is designed to mitigate their negative effects. In addition, the resilience of the proposed control strategy is analyzed using Lyapunov stability theory, and an upper bound on the duration of replay attacks is derived. Finally, the effectiveness of the approach is validated through simulations of a single-link robotic arm system.

articleTitle: Distributed MPC for Nonlinear Networked Vehicle Platoon System with Communication Delays
abstract: This paper investigates the platoon control problem for nonlinear networked vehicle systems, while taking into account the communication delay. The nonlinear system is linearly discretized and a linear distributed controller is designed using the distributed model predictive control (DMPC) method, while another controller is designed based on the fusion state estimation method. In the designed controllers, the linear distributed controller controls the stable operation of the platoon, and the fusion state estimation controller helps to solve the problem of missing state values of neighboring nodes caused by communication delay. Finally, simulation verifies the effectiveness of the algorithm and the stability of the vehicle platoon under the communication delay environment.

articleTitle: Drag-Free Control Verification Based on a Combined Ground Simulator
abstract: This paper proposes a method to verify the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) controller of the drag-free control system in space gravitational wave detection based on a ground-based semi-physical drag-free simulator. The ground-based simulator for drag-free simulation is innovatively designed referred to the drag-free satellite with two test masses (TMs). The dynamics scaling laws used for the design of the ground simulator between the space prototype and the ground system are derived by using the Pi theorem. The control scaling laws of LQR are analyzed based on the idea of energy equivalence. The simulation results indicate that the two systems exhibit similar closed-loop dynamic behavior.

articleTitle: Cloud Removal in Remote Sensing Images Using Attention-Guided Dual-Stream U-Net with SAR
abstract: Remote sensing (RS) images are widely used for ecological and environmental monitoring. However, cloud cover often hinders direct acquisition of continuous, unobstructed RS images, which makes reconstruct clear RS images necessary. Traditional algorithms, however, struggle to fully exploit the information of multi-source data and face registration errors during fusion process. To solve these issues, we propose an attention-guided dual-stream U-Net encoding method by fusing cloud-covered optical images and SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) images in this work. The method employs dual-stream encoding for cloud-covered images and SAR images during the encoding phase, utilizing max pooling for down-sampling. Subsequently, we utilize a cross-attention block-guided fusion module for model integration, effectively harnessing the information from multi-source data and alleviating the minor misalignment between SAR and cloud-covered optical images. Finally, the designed decoder decodes the data, using Deconvolution for up-sampling, and ultimately outputs a cloud-free optical image. Compared to two mainstream SAR-guided optical image cloud removal methods, our proposed method significantly improves image restoration quality with about 0.5 reduction in RMSE.

articleTitle: Unified Design Method of Filters for Different Measurement Phases in Space Relative Navigation Tasks
abstract: In spacecraft relative navigation, as the relative distance changes, the output varies with different measurement devices. For traditional filtering methods, different filters need to be switched when the measurement output changes, which reduces the computational efficiency. Considering this problem, a simplified converted measurement Kalman filter (SCMKF) is designed to construct a unified filter. The proposed unified filter simplifies the calculation of the measurement noise covariance matrix, based on the analysis on the factors affecting measurement noise and the accuracy of measurement device. Compared to the traditional filter, the proposed unified filter decreases the computational complexity significantly on the premise of ensuring the calculation accuracy.

articleTitle: Interconnection and Damping Assignment Passivity-Based Control for Underactuated Overhead Cranes with Frictions
abstract: Due to its underactuated characteristics, the control difficulty of underactuated overhead cranes is greatly increased. In this paper, a control scheme based on interconnection and damping assignment passivity-based control method is proposed. First of all, in order to simplify the controller design, the overhead crane system is linearized at the origin. Then, a design technique is applied to interconnection and damping assignment passivity-based control method, which can simplify the partial differential equation of the potential energy. Finally, a controller is designed by using interconnection and damping assignment passivity-based control method. By designing an elegant controller, the swing of payload is suppressed and the trolley is adjusted to the desired destination of the overhead crane system. Via zero dynamics and Lyapunov stability theorems, the stability analysis is rigorously provided. Some simulation results are provided to prove the applicability of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Trust Evaluation Mechanism of Terminal Device in Industrial Edge Computing Environment
abstract: Edge computing has been widely introduced into industrial networks, which not only provides low-latency and high-bandwidth network communication capabilities for industrial networks, but also provides a huge number of interfaces for terminal devices to access industrial networks. Therefore, how to ensure the terminal devices in the industrial edge computing environment are trustworthy is a challenge that needs to be solved urgently presently. In order to solve the problem that legitimate terminal devices may send untrustworthy data during network operation, a trust evaluation mechanism based on comprehensive trust evaluation was designed in this paper. The mechanism primarily calculates the trust value based on the integrity of terminal device data and categorizes trust level, thereby realizing sustainable monitoring of the security status of terminal devices under industrial edge computing environment and guaranteeing the accuracy of the trust value of the terminal device is realized. On this basis, the mechanism was validated and analyzed through a test platform. The results verified that the proposed trusted access mechanism has both stable feasibility and good reliability.

articleTitle: Design of Nearly Linear Phase IIR Fractional Order Digital Differentiators using Iterative Convex Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a methodology for the design of IIR fractional-order digital differentiators with near-linear phase properties. The primary objective is to minimize the maximum phase deviation from the ideal linear phase, subject to constraints on stability and relative magnitude response deviations. This design incorporates group delay as an optimization variable, leading to a nonconvex optimization problem. To resolve this, we propose an Iterative Convex Optimization algorithm that reformulates the nonconvex problem into a series of convex subproblems utilizing a Gauss-Newton strategy. Simulation experiments have substantiated the superiority of the proposed differentiator compared to methods in the field, demonstrating significantly reduced relative magnitude deviations and maximum phase errors.

articleTitle: Self-Contrastive Learning Fault Diagnosis Network for Signal Imaging: A Case Study
abstract: The deep convolution method based on MSDP signal imaging has been proven to be an effective means of monitoring the robot grinding process. This method has very high requirements on the quality of imaging and requires a lot of computing resources. This paper proposes an image self-contrastive learning network that can effectively extract fault information from low-pixel fuzzy images and achieve efficient and accurate condition monitoring. The network first calculates the correlation distance matrix between two identical modified symmetrized dot pattern (MSDP) images and uses the generated similarity labels to calculate the contrast loss to extract the embedded features of the image. Finally, the classification network is trained using the cross entropy loss to achieve the classification of fault images. The method was verified on a robotic grinding platform to significantly reduce the calculation time while maintaining the recognition accuracy, which provides reliable technical support for the real-time monitoring of the robotic grinding process.

articleTitle: Delta Operator Sliding Mode Speed Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
abstract: Aiming at the problems of large system oscillation and slow response speed of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) based on sliding mode control (SMC) scheme with conventional reaching law, a novel sliding mode controller is designed by Delta operator discrete reaching law. First, fal function is introduced, and Delta operator is used to discretize the system of PMSM. Then, a sliding mode controller for PMSM is designed using Delta operator discrete reaching law, and its stability is proved. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed Delta operator discretization method in PMSM systems. Compared with conventional sliding mode controllers based on exponential reaching law, the proposed controller in this paper has smaller overshoot, faster response speed, and better performance.

articleTitle: Depth Completion Algorithm Based on Panoptic Segmentation Assistance
abstract: The depth completion task aims to solve the problem of sparse or missing depth values caused by the sensor itself or the external environment. This paper proposes an RGB camera/LiDAR fusion algorithm based on image-guided depth information completion. Initially, sparse radar point clouds are converted into sparse depth maps, followed by the application of an image segmentation algorithm to the RGB images to generate Boolean masks. Guided by these masks, the study employs a depth completion algorithm based on morphological filtering to densify the sparse depth maps into dense depth maps, thus creating fusion information. The advanced nature of the proposed image-guided depth inflation algorithm in maintaining edge depth discontinuities was validated through testing on the KITTI depth completion dataset. This algorithm effectively preserves depth information at image edges, reducing the root mean square error and mean absolute error by 2.3% and 1.2%, respectively, compared to non-image-guided methods. Back-projection experiments shows that this method can enhance the quality of 3D reconstruction.

articleTitle: An Optimized Three-Phase Three-Level VSVPWM Modulation Algorithm
abstract: The fluctuation of NP is a distinctive issue specific to 3L NPC inverters, which can have adverse effects on power quality and even result in inverter failure. This paper focuses on the three-level inverter and aims to establish a mathematical model to study the performance advantages and disadvantages of SVPWM, VSVPWM modulation algorithms, and NPP fluctuation problems. Then, the NP active control method based on the distribution factor is proposed, aiming to rectify the initial imbalance in capacitor voltage by adjusting the action time of positive and negative virtual small vectors. The corresponding model for simulation verification and hardware-in-the-loop experiment was established using MATLAB/Simulink and HIL. Experimental results demonstrate the favorable effect of the proposed algorithm on the active control of NP voltage.

articleTitle: 3D Mesh Generation Model of Human Body Based on Monocular Image and 2D Pose
abstract: In this paper, we propose a model designed to generate a single human 3D mesh from monocular images and 2D human poses, even in highly occluded environments. The model employs a well-established 2D pose detector to capture the 2D pose information of the human body. Additionally, our proposed AFF module extracts robust features in occluded conditions. The model's regressor, leveraging both 2D and 3D joint features, allows it to focus on the target person's positional region while estimating depth information to distinguish the person from other objects. Ultimately, the model regresses the parameters of a parametric human body model. We validate the proposed method on public benchmark datasets, which qualitatively and quantitatively demonstrate its robustness in recovering 3D human body meshes in occluded environments.

articleTitle: SID-YOLOv5: Improved Object Detection Algorithm for Sea Surface Scenes
abstract: Accurate detection of objects on the sea surface is a crucial aspect of intelligent perception for smart ships. To tackle the challenges of difficult small object detection., poor detection accuracy., and low real-time performance in sea surface scenes, we propose a target detection algorithm called SID-YOLOv5, which incorporates the sliding window mechanism, involution operator, and decoupled detection heads. To train and evaluate the performance of the proposed method, we construct a dataset for sea surface scene object detection and conduct experiments to compare and verify the effectiveness of the proposed method against existing algorithms.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Resilient Estimator for Nonlinear Cyber-Physical Systems Under DoS Attacks
abstract: This paper tackles the challenge of state estimation in nonlinear cyber-physical systems under Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks. To address this, it proposes a novel event-triggered resilient estimator, offering enhanced resistance against such disruptions. Firstly, to account for DoS attacks, a random attack model is established. This model paves the way for a dynamic event-triggered mechanism, which reduces network load by strategically decreasing the transmission rate of measurement data. Next, this paper tackles the challenge of recursively solving coupled Riccati-like difference equations. Through this approach, an estimation gain is obtained that minimizes the upper bound (UB) on the estimation error covariance. Leveraging random analytic theory, the paper rigorously proves that the estimation error is probabilistically bounded. This theoretical foundation is then validated by a example showcasing the proposed estimator's performance.

articleTitle: Design of Flight Path Angle Rate Control Based on Active Disturbance Rejection Control for Manual Landing System
abstract: This paper proposes a direct lift manual landing system based on active disturbance rejection control (ADRC-DLC). The system employs ADRC as the control strategy and is divided into three channels: the stabilator channel, the flap channel, and the throttle channel. These channels are responsible for flight path angle rate adjustment, angle of attack maintenance, and speed stabilization, respectively, allowing the pilot to directly control the flight path angle rate and guide the carrier aircraft onto the proper glide path for landing. Additionally, a direct lift decoupling module based on balanced pitch rate is designed to dynamically allocate the deflection of the flaps and stabilators, achieving decoupling of the flight path and attitude angles and enhancing landing precision. The effectiveness of the proposed control system is evaluated through simulations, demonstrating its strong control performance.

articleTitle: MCUNet:Multi-Level Feature and Uncertainty-Guided Lung Nodule Segmentation
abstract: Lung cancer ranks among the top causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and precise segmentation of lung nodules is essential for early detection and diagnosis. However, the low contrast of small nodules often makes them difficult to distinguish from noise and other structures in medical images, posing a significant challenge for accurate segmentation. This paper presents a novel lung nodule segmentation network, the Multi-Level Feature and Uncertainty-Guided Lung Nodule Segmentation Network (MCU-Net). MCU-Net includes a Multi-Level Dense Feature Extraction Module, an Uncertainty-Aware Module, and a Feature-Aware Attention Module to enhance the accuracy and robustness of lung nodule segmentation. By combining multi-scale feature extraction and uncertainty-aware learning, the proposed network achieves superior performance on the LIDC-IDRI dataset, with an average Dice score of 86.16

articleTitle: Adaptive Event-Triggered Tracking Control for Discrete-Time Markov Jump Systems with Time-Varying Delay
abstract: This study explores the strategy of adaptive event-triggered tracking control in the discrete-time linear Markov jump systems time-varying delay parameter. Firstly, this study proposed an adaptive event-triggered strategy to improve the effectiveness of communication. Secondly, by applying the Lya-punov stability theorem and the matrix inequality approach, relevant conditions are derived to ensure the system is satis-fying stochastic stability and extended dissipativity. Thirdly, to accomplish the intended tracking performance, the controller gains are determined by the linear matrix inequality techniques. Ultimately, the proposed controller design method is validated through a numerical example, which effectively demonstrates its performance.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Output Feedback Consensus Control for High-Order Nonlinear Multiagent Systems
abstract: This paper is concerned with the consensus control problem of a class of high-order nonlinear multiagent systems. First, two kinds of fixed-time (FixT) observers are introduced to estimate the leader's state and the the follower's unmeasurable states. Then, a FixT output feedback consensus control strategy is proposed by virtue of the FixT observers and the homogeneous method. Finally, a numerical example is presented to show the effectiveness of the designed FixT control algorithm.

articleTitle: Distributed Optimization for Multi-Agent Systems Under Disturbances with Quantization and Event-Triggered Communication
abstract: This paper studies the distributed optimization problem for multi-agent systems with dynamic event-triggered communication. We investigate the comprehensive effects of the logarithmic quantization and the external disturbances on the distributed optimization problems. It is proved that the event-triggered algorithm practically converges if the design parameter-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex> are chosen properly. Based on the event-triggered condition, we prove that there is no Zeno phenomenon. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm is illustrated through a simulation example.

articleTitle: GAN-Based Fusion of Infrared and Visible Images in Dark Light Environments
abstract: In low light conditions, the fused image generated by fusion of infrared and visible images is dark and lacks detailed texture information, resulting in low target detection accuracy, based on which a target detection network for fusion of infrared and visible images in low light conditions is proposed. Firstly, the dark light perception network is designed to enhance the brightness of the dark light image; secondly, the feature extraction module of the image fusion network introduces the gradient residual dense block to strengthen the ability of the image fusion network to extract the depth features and finegrained detail features of the source image; subsequently, the loss function incorporates the intensity loss and the structural similarity loss to enhance the ability of the image fusion network to extract the pixel intensities and the structural texture details of the source image; Finally, the optimal solution of the fusion network for target detection is achieved by joint training of the image fusion network and the target detection network. The experimental results show that the fusion network in the paper improves the mutual information, average gradient, visual fidelity, gradient-based fusion performance, and structural similarity by 0.142, 0.135, 0.043, 0.067, and 0.082 compared to the other network models, and improves the average precision mean and accuracy by 2.6% and 2.5%, respectively, in the YOLOV8 detection network.

articleTitle: New Results on Proportional Plus Derivative Feedback Control for Singular Takagi-Sugeno Fuzzy Systems Based on Observer Design
abstract: This paper presents new insights into the design of a proportional plus derivative (PD) feedback controller for singular Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy systems based on observer design. By introducing certain free-weighting matrices and employing Lyapunov theory, sufficient conditions for ensuring the stability of the closed-loop system are provided in the form of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). To solve for the controller and observer parameters, an iterative algorithm-based solution approach is proposed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through a simulation example.

articleTitle: An Evaluation System for Multi-Machine Cooperative Operation of Weeding Robots Based on Fuzzy Combination Weight
abstract: This paper proposes a matter-element evaluation model to address the low-efficiency issue in the multi-machine cooperative operation system of weeding robots. The model transforms the weeding robot's multi-machine cooperative operation system into an indicator system with five first-level indicators: working environment, safety, path planning, energy consumption, and weeding situation. Each first-level indicator has several second-level indicators. Each second-level indicator is weighted with a combination of the order relation analysis method and the CRITIC method. The combination weighting is then used to determine the weight of the evaluation indicator of the weeding robot's multi-machine cooperative operation, while the extension evaluation is used to assess the robot's multi-machine cooperative operation level and identify the factors that influence its efficiency. In this work, the weeding situation was simulated, and the data were evaluated to determine the important elements influencing the efficiency of each weeding robot group's multi-machine cooperative operation. This model can provide valuable insights and strategies for evaluating and optimizing multi-agent collaborative activity.

articleTitle: Visual SLAM Loop Closure Detection Algorithm Based on LightGlue
abstract: In the traditional field of closed-loop detection, the method of manually designing features dominates. However, this method is highly susceptible to environmental variations, leading to fluctuations and inaccuracies in detection results. To overcome this limitation and improve the accuracy and robustness of loop closure detection, a method based on LightGlue is proposed. First, the SuperPoint network model is used to extract image features, obtaining a series of keypoints and corresponding descriptors. These feature information are then input into LightGlue for feature matching, generating an assignment matrix that reflects the correspondence between feature points. Finally, by calculating the similarity of the matching results, the algorithm can accurately identify the loop closure relationship between images. To validate the effectiveness of this algorithm, experiments were conducted on two widely used public datasets, NewCollege and CityCentre. Compared with other advanced loop closure detection benchmark algorithms, this algorithm demonstrates higher accuracy while maintaining a certain recall rate, showing stronger robustness and stability, and meets the basic requirements of loop closure detection.

articleTitle: Long-Term Prediction for Harmful Gas Concentration Based on RevIN-KANformer Model
abstract: Advance prediction of hazardous gases can help monitor trends in air quality and take effective preventive and control measures in advance.In short-term prediction, it is necessary to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the prediction results. And in long-term prediction, it is also crucial to accurately predict the changes of the sequence trend. This paper proposes a RevIN-KANformer model based on the reversible instance normalization method (RevIN), Transformer and KAN for long-term prediction of harmful gas concentrations in the air.
