The model effectively combines the Transformer and KAN models through an encoder-decoder structure, while the input and output sequences are normalized and denormalized by RevIN method to ensure optimal long-term prediction performance.The experimental results show that RMSE and MAE of the model proposed in this paper are reduced by at least 16% and 9% compared with the baseline model, which provides an effective method for the long-term prediction of harmful gas concentration.

articleTitle: Adaptive Event-Triggered Partially Mode-Dependent Filtering for Delayed Markov Jump Systems
abstract: This article investigates the partially mode-dependent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> filtering problem for delayed Markov jump systems. With the help of a Bernoulli random variable, a partially mode-dependent filter is proposed, which ensures the stochastic stability and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> performance of the error system. Furthermore, an adaptive event-triggered scheme is adopted in order to save communication network resources. By employing a novel Lyapunov functional and an Abel lemma-based inequality, the filter design algorithm is proposed. An example is given to verification the usefulness of the proposed design methodology.

articleTitle: Data-Driven MPC for Uncertain High-Order Fully Actuated Systems
abstract: This study combines machine learning with Model Predictive Control (MPC) to regulate the High-Order Fully Actuated (HOFA) nonlinear systems with disturbances. By exploiting the full-actuation characteristic of the HOFA system, we neatly eliminate the nonlinearity of the system, thus circumventing the complex computation of uncertainty propagation in nonlinear stochastic MPC. To address the disturbances, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) precisely identifies principal components, while Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) assesses probability distributions and uncertainty bounds. Furthermore, we apply stricter state constraints and define terminal sets to ensure the recursive feasibility of the method theoretically. Lastly, a numerical example is simulated to confirm the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Model Predictive Control for Perturbed Nonlinear Systems via a Non-Squared Integrand Objective Function*
abstract: This paper studies a dual-mode predictive control scheme based on an event-triggered approach. Firstly, a non-squared integrand objective function is adopted to construct the finite-horizon optimization problem. By analyzing the recursive feasibility on this type of optimization problems and its corresponding system stability, a triggering condition including three criteria is introduced into the considered system and constructed to reduce the solving times on optimization problems. Moreover, prediction horizon is not constant and computed at each triggering instant such that prediction horizon decays as the system operates. By this means, the solving complexity of optimization problems is reduced further. By considering the effect of disturbances, the maximum upper deviation on the actual and predicted trajectories under same control input signals is estimated and Zeno behavior of this event-triggered strategy is excluded. Then, both the feasibility and stability of this control mechanism are verified where disturbance is the only factor that matters. Finally, the correctness and superiority of this control strategy are verified based on a vehicle-damp-spring system.

articleTitle: Natural Sit-to-Stand Control of a Musculoskeletal Model with Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Reward Shaping
abstract: Understanding the neuromuscular control mechanisms underlying the human sit-to-stand (STS) movement, a fundamental daily activity, is crucial for enhancing the physical capabilities of older adults and advancing applications in robotics and exoskeletons. This paper introduces a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approach with reward shaping to replicate natural human STS movements using a lower limb musculoskeletal model with three degrees of freedom and nine muscles. We used proximal policy optimization (PPO) with two behavior-guided reward shaping functions,: one focused on joint angle changes (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">joint</inf>) and the other on head height changes (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">head</inf>), each tailored to the model's capabilities and the movement's objectives. To assess the effectiveness of our control method, we collected kinematic and kinetic data of human STS movements, allowing for a comparison of joint angles between the musculoskeletal model and human subjects. Both reward conditions demonstrated a strong correlation with experimental data, with the R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">head</inf> reward achieving a correlation of 0.9 and faster convergence compared to R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oint</inf>. Additionally, R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">head</inf>more accurately captured human joint dynamics, enhancing the realism of the simulated movements, while R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">joint</inf> proved more effective in reducing energy consumption. These findings highlight the potential of DRL with reward shaping to generate realistic and efficient movement patterns, paving the way for future applications in robotics and assistive technologies.

articleTitle: Phenotyping the Seedling Vigor in Winter Wheat Based on Multispectral Images
abstract: Seedling vigor is a crucial determinant of crop establishment and yield in winter wheat. Traditional phenotyping methods are often laborintensive and time-consuming. This study explores the use of multispectral imaging to assess seedling vigor in winter wheat, providing a rapid, non-destructive alternative. In this research, winter wheat seedlings of AN1589, AN188, AN98 and JM22 were imaged at seedling stages using a multispectral camera during 2023–2024 wheat season. Key vegetation indices were extracted and analyzed. These indices were then correlated with traditional measurements of seedling vigor, including leaf area index (LAI), ground biomass (GB), and specific leaf area (SLA). The results demonstrated strong correlations between the multispectral vegetation indices and traditional vigor traits, validating the effectiveness of multispectral imaging for phenotyping seedling vigor. This approach offers a high-throughput, accurate method for assessing seedling vigor, which can facilitate breeding programs and precision agriculture practices aimed at improving winter wheat productivity.

articleTitle: Robust Tracking Control for Uncertain Micro-Hand Actuator with Dead-Zone and Hysteresis
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of uncertain Micro manipulation with dead-zone and uncertain backlash models based on robust right coprime factorization (RRCF). Firstly, the conventional dead-zone model and common backlash model existing in soft robotic arms are introduced, along with the model of inflatable rubber tube actuators. Secondly, a robust controller is designed to ensure the system's stability. Thirdly, a combination of RRCF-based approach and integral-sliding mode approach is employed for tracking, significantly reducing the time and improving the tracking performance. Finally, the performance and feasibility of this method are tested through simulation.

articleTitle: Adaptive Asymptotic Tracking Control of Strict-Feedback Nonlinear Parameterized Systems
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive control tactic is designed for a class of nonlinear systems with nonconvex parameterization by using the backstepping method. During the backstepping control process, an improved nonlinear filter with a compensation term is introduced to deal with the repetitive differentiation problem of the designed virtual controllers, which removes the boundary layer error simultaneously. The nonconvex pa-rameterized terms are discussed in light of the extensions of explicit realizability assumptions. Under the constructed control algorithms, the bound ness of all signals in the closed-loop system is proved, and the tracking error can reach 0 as time approaches to infinity. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through a simulation example.

articleTitle: Model Reference Adaptive Impedance Control Method Based on Online Environment Stiffness Identification
abstract: A force control method combining model reference adaptive control and impedance control is studied for the work environment of physical interaction with unknown and time-varying environmental stiffness. The updating law of adaptive gains is derived to improve the applicability of the system to different environments. The uncertainty is compensated by a radial basis function neural network. The variable forgetting factor recursive least squares method is used to identify the environmental stiffness, optimize the controller output with the identification results, and reduce the force response overshoot. The stability of the system is proved by means of the Lyapunov stability theorem. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by simulation results.

Author Keywords: variable forgetting factor recursive least squares

articleTitle: Fault Detection Algorithm Based on Complex Evidential Reasoning Considering Information Reliability
abstract: In the existing fault detection algorithms based on evidence theory, the basic belief assignment method usually only focuses on the uncertainty of information, which does not consider the impact of information reliability on the fault decision-making performance. To solve the above problems, a fault detection algorithm based on complex evidential reasoning considering information reliability is proposed. Initially, the Gaussian membership function is used to establish attribute models under different basic hypotheses. The matching degree between the feature data and the attribute model is used to express the support for different hypotheses. Subsequently, the static reliability of the information source is calculated based on the similarity between different hypotheses under the attribute model, and the dynamic reliability is obtained by the distance between the feature data and the reference point of the attribute model. Furthermore, a novel basic belief assignment method is introduced to generate complex evidence in the complex domain. Lastly, complex evidence fusion from different information sources is achieved to obtain the final fault detection result. The advantage of the proposed algorithm is that it takes into account both the reliability and uncertainty of the information sources. The feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm are verified through the fault detection experiment of aviation electromagnetic relay.

articleTitle: Adaptive Hybrid Vision and Force Control for Dual-Arm Robotic Assembly Tasks
abstract: In the field of industrial automation, achieving precise force-controlled assembly remains a critical yet challenging task, particularly for traditional position-based robotic systems. This paper introduces an adaptive hybrid visual-force control approach that significantly enhances the precision and reliability of robotic assembly tasks within complex industrial environments. The proposed system integrates advanced visual recognition using the YOLOv8 algorithm for accurate part detection, coupled with force-controlled manipulation via a dual-arm robotic manipulator for dexterous handling. An adaptive-gain based visual servo control is employed during the assembly process to ensure rapid and accurate positioning, while a force exploration strategy mitigates visual positioning errors, guaranteeing high assembly precision. Additionally, the system features a novel implementation of fuzzy impedance control, which stabilizes the assembly force, resulting in smoother and safer operations. Experimental validation demonstrates that the system achieves a positioning accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm \mathbf{0.5}\ \mathbf{mm}$</tex> and a force control precision of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm \mathbf{1}\ \mathbf{N}$</tex>, confirming the effectiveness in executing complex assembly tasks.

articleTitle: Real-Time Agricultural Pest Detection Enhanced via Hybrid Distillation Framework
abstract: We propose an improved version of the YOLOv8 model that enhances real-time agricultural pest detection performance by integrating feature distillation and relation distillation. Feature distillation focuses on transferring intermediate feature maps from the teacher model to the student model, enriching the student's intermediate representation capabilities. Additionally, relation distillation maintains the relative relationships between feature channels, further boosting the model's generalization ability and detection accuracy. In this process, the teacher model constructs a relationship graph between feature channels and conveys this structural information to the student model. This approach not only emphasizes the semantic information of the intermediate features but also incorporates the geometric relationships between channel-level features, enabling the student model to better understand and preserve the inherent structure of the data. Experimental results on the large-scale agricultural pest dataset IP102 demonstrate that this model significantly improves detection accuracy and robustness compared to the traditional YOLOv8 model. The strategy of combining feature and relation distillation showcases its practicality and potential for wide application in agricultural pest detection tasks.

articleTitle: A Fact-Based Approach to Define Static and Dynamic Knowledge in Expert System
abstract: In this paper, we describe a method for expressing knowledge in expert systems and provide solutions to knowledge representation and internal coupling of knowledge. The term “fact” discussed in the background includes ordinary fact that depicts static system features, and composite fact that depicts dynamic features. The ordinary and composite facts constitute the fundamental elements of expert system production rule. The complex fact is capable of simulating temporal logic semantic, that it enhances expert system knowledge base by adding extensible patterns, therefore, it provides effective tools to extend expert system functionality. Meanwhile, we give an efficient pattern matching method for the inference engine based on this knowledge representation. When dealing with a target system with high complexity and frequent state changes, in comparison to the traditional expert system solution, the fact-based expert system features a simpler infrastructure and more efficient inference pattern matching. In practice, the real-time fault diagnosis expert system we implemented using this method has the basic capabilities of the model checker, and can automatically and effectively match fault patterns in the system state space.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Policy Network Reinforcement Learning for UAV Swarm Confrontation
abstract: UAV swarms confrontation is becoming increasingly important in the field of military security, however, learning effective cooperative strategies for heterogeneous UAV swarms confrontation remains a major challenge. In this paper, we address the heterogeneous UAV swarms confrontation problem by developing the UAV swarms collaborative state space reconstruction mechanism. This mechanism reconstructs the UAV's own state space by using the relative state information to depict the collaborative relationship between the UAV swarms. Then, within the Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) deep reinforcement learning framework, we propose a heterogeneous policy network local parameter sharing MAPPO algorithm. This algorithm addresses the differences in heterogeneous agent state spaces and action decision spaces by designing heterogeneous policy networks for different types of agents and optimizing the policy network parameters using the local parameter sharing mechanism. Finally, with a simulation environment for reconnaissance-attack heterogeneous UAV swarms, experiments comparing the proposed method with existing multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: Multi Classification Online Monitoring of Photovoltaic Array Fault Diagnosis Algorithm
abstract: With the rapid development of photovoltaic power generation, the fault of photovoltaic array is receiving increasing attention. In response to this issue, proposes an online monitoring photovoltaic array fault diagnosis algorithm based on Support Vector Machines. Firstly, collect the voltage and current of the photovoltaic array for feature extraction. Next, the extracted feature data is normalized and input into a SVM to train the classifier and identify and judge the faults that occur. In the experiment, simulation datasets were used for testing, and online detection and verification were conducted on the real datasets generated by the actual prototype. The results showed that this method can effectively diagnose photovoltaic array faults, with high accuracy and reliability. The online detection photovoltaic array fault diagnosis method based on support vector machine proposed in this paper has high fault detection rate and accuracy, which can provide technical support and guarantee for the maintenance and management of photovoltaic power generation system.

articleTitle: Road Surface Condition Recognition Based on Visual Information Fusion
abstract: To address the problem of lower classification accuracy in current road surface condition recognition methods for both daytime and nighttime, this paper proposes an end-to-end deep learning model. Which integrates RGB and Near Infrared (NIR) dual-channel visual information for autonomous road surface condition classification. The collected image data is first augmented to mitigate the effects of model overfitting. A lightweight network based on ConvNeXt-Tiny is designed to extract basic features from RGB and NIR images, respectively. A feature fusion module based on Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) is designed to fuse hierarchical features, which are then classified together with the basic features using fully connected layers. Comparative experiments with MBFN and ablative studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed network model and feature fusion module.

articleTitle: Multi-Feature Fusion Recognition Method Based on Information Entropy and Classification Decision Tree
abstract: Aiming at the characteristics of radar network measurement data, such as incomplete information and large uncertainty, a feature layer fusion recognition algorithm based on information entropy decision tree classification is proposed. The algorithm does not need training samples, adopts the way of construction-side classification, selects the attribute with the least information entropy as the classification attribute to classify the measured data, and realizes the recognition of the target. The simulation results show that the algorithm can make full use of the feature information of the measured data, and is a simple and effective feature layer fusion recognition algorithm.

articleTitle: Semi-supervised Learning with GAN for Semantic Segmentation of Wood Defect Image
abstract: Automatic defect detection on wood surface is essential for ensuring product quality. Semantic segmentation methods have shown outstanding performance in wood defect detection. However, it is costly to acquire correct pixel-level labels of wood surface defects due to the complicated characteristics. To mitigate the cost of acquiring high-quality datasets, this study proposes a semi-supervised defect detection approach based on generative adversarial networks, which contains a generator and a discriminator. The generator is utilized to generate pixel-level segmentation results of wood defect images. To improve the segmentation performance, the discriminator learns against the generator by judging the goodness of the prediction results and generates supervised signals for the prediction results of unlabeled images. With this learning model, the proposed method can enhance segmentation performance using unlabeled images and alleviate the burden of data annotation. We validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach on a collected dataset of wood defects. Experimental results demonstrate the remarkable performance of our method even when utilizing only a small amount of annotated data.

articleTitle: A Genetic Algorithms for Optimizing Structural Brain Network Across Cognitive Tasks
abstract: The topology of structural brain networks is critical for information transmission and processing across brain regions, enabling the brain to flexibly perform diverse cognitive tasks through functional segregation and integration. While the architecture of brain networks continuously evolves and optimizes under the influence of factors such as wiring costs, it remains unclear whether cognitive tasks also impact this process. We formulate objective functions that integrate cognitive tasks with wiring cost factors and employ a genetic algorithm to iteratively optimize brain network structures. Our findings indicate that the optimized brain network structures driven by cognitive tasks closely resemble actual structural brain networks. Compared to optimizations considering individual cognitive tasks, the multi-task optimized brain network demonstrates greater similarity and topological alignment with structural brain networks. These results suggest that the formation of brain structural networks may incorporate the influence of multiple cognitive tasks, offering new insights into the close relationship between cognitive functions and brain structure.

articleTitle: Support Vector Machine Based Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance Strategy for First-Order Consistent Formation Control
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of dynamic obstacle avoidance in wheeled mobile robots by developing a classifier grounded in multi-agent consensus theory, leveraging support vector machines to enhance obstacle avoidance efficiency. Firstly, the current main methods of dynamic obstacle avoidance were introduced. Based on the existing consensus algorithm, support vector machine was selected as the dynamic obstacle avoidance method. Subsequently, specific attackers are designated to target both the leader and the follower, followed by simulations of the formation system to derive significant conclusions. That is, support vector machine can have good performance in multi-agent obstacle avoidance, which proves the feasibility and effectiveness of support vector machine in multi-agent dynamic obstacle avoidance. The simulation results show that in the limit case, that is, when the dynamic obstacle avoidance target continuously attacks the formation, the consensus formation system can still maintain the formation and recover to the original formation.

articleTitle: Integral Sliding Mode Control of LCL Single Phase Photovoltaic Grid-Connected System Based on Sliding Mode Observer
abstract: In this research, we introduce an integral sliding mode control (ISMC) approach designed to improve the robustness of systems against parameter variations and external disturbances, thereby enhancing dynamic performance. For DC/AC converters, we developed an ISMC method with a sliding mode observer (SMO) to address the inherent resonance caused by LCL filters and reduce the negative impact of their parameter changes. The SMO, equipped with an adaptive switching function, estimates the inverter-side current and capacitor voltage of the LCL filter. This control strategy not only strengthens the system's resilience to parameter changes but also significantly decreases system chattering. Matlab/Simulink simulation results indicate that the proposed approach effectively mitigates various disturbances, ensuring the reliable operation of photovoltaic microgrids.

articleTitle: Parallel CNN-Transformer Dual-Branch Hybrid Tracker
abstract: Currently, object tracking methods are increasingly adopting Transformer-based models to replace the earlier convolutional neural networks (CNNs). While these methods have achieved performance improvements, they tend to overlook the importance of local feature details in visual tasks due to the global modeling nature of Transformers. In this paper, we propose a parallel CNN-Transformer dual-branch hybrid tracking model (PCTTrack). By designing a feature fusion module with various attention mechanisms and an improved prediction head, the model effectively leverages both local and global information advantages. Experiments show that our method achieves competitive results on multiple object tracking datasets. For instance, it achieves an AO of 75.5 on the GOT-10K dataset. Compared to the single Transformer branch, the hybrid model improves the AUC on LaSOT by 3.8% and the AO on GOT-10K by 2.6%. Additionally, through visualizing the outputs of different model structures, we validate the effectiveness of the dual-branch fusion model.

articleTitle: GPP Estimation of a Grassland Ecosystem Based on Photosynthesis-Hydrology Coordination Optimization
abstract: Accurate estimation of gross primary production (GPP, ecosystem level photosynthesis) is critical for monitoring terrestrial ecosystems. However, most of the current models used for GPP estimation are with many unknown parameters and rarely include the effects of soil water stress due to the covariation of soil moisture and air humidity. In addition, grasslands, as the most widely distributed ecosystems in the world, have simple ecosystem structure and are easily affected by soil drought. Therefore, in this paper, we applied photosynthesis-hydrology coordination optimization theory and soil water potential based on soil moisture effect to develop a combined model (PH model) for GPP estimation of grassland ecosystems and used the US-Var grassland ecosystem, one of the FLUXNET sites from January to July 2004 (the driest period in recent years) as an example to validate the model. The results show that the model can effectively track the measured GPP during soil drought period and is better than the result from another commonly used photosynthesis coordination model (Pmodel) which does not consider the effect of soil drought. Further, we can infer the vegetation photosynthetic capacity parameters including the maximum carboxylation capacity (V cmax) and the maximum electron-transport capacity (Jmax) under the effect of soil drought. The result also shows that if soil drought is not considered, the photosynthetic capacity parameters of vegetation will be overestimated. These results provide evidence for the application of photosynthesis-hydrology coordination theory in the assessment of ecosystem carbon cycle under the intensified climate changes.

articleTitle: Optimization of High-Speed Train Driver Gesture Recognition Using Self-Supervised Learning and Stream State-Tying
abstract: During train operations, drivers need to maintain a fixed driving posture for extended periods, and due to the monotonous train operating environment, it can lead to a decline in the quality of the driver's work, thereby posing potential safety hazards. According to the high-speed train driver standards, executing prescribed gestures is a crucial aspect of their driving operations. Detecting driver gestures allows for the effective assessment of the driver's operational status and quality, thereby ensuring train operation safety. Traditional manual inspection methods are inefficient and inadequate for meeting actual needs. Existing gesture recognition algorithms suffer from low detection accuracy and require extensive manual annotation of training data. With the development of intelligent railways, building a high-precision, labor-reducing train driver gesture recognition model has become an industry necessity. This paper proposes a three-stage train driver gesture recognition algorithm based on the aforementioned situation. In the first stage, the self-supervised learning (SSL) method MoCo contrastive learning is used to extract vector features from known gesture categories. In the second stage, flow state binding is utilized to jointly model multiple synchronized data streams of gesture direction, position, and angle for gesture category recognition. In the third stage, a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) is used to generate additional gesture samples for training, addressing the complexity and diversity of recognition environments. The proposed method aims to improve gesture recognition accuracy, reduce manual annotation workload, and enhance gesture recognition accuracy in different environments.

articleTitle: An Internal Environment Anomaly Detection System for Secondary Water Supply Pump Houses Based on the Improved PatchCore Algorithm
abstract: With the growing public awareness regarding tap water safety, the secondary water supply pump room, acting as the final checkpoint before water enters homes, plays a crucial role in ensuring a safe internal environment. However, pump rooms face challenges such as disordered spatial distribution and a shortage of maintenance staff, leading to significant difficulties and costs in maintenance and supervision. This paper introduces an anomaly detection system for the internal environment of secondary water supply pump rooms, based on an enhanced PatchCore algorithm. The system is designed to alleviate the burden and costs associated with manual monitoring by providing continuous 24-hour anomaly detection through automated equipment. It incorporates 5G communication and edge computing technologies within edge-end devices, showcasing superior capabilities in data transmission speed, detection efficiency, information security, and intelligent processing. On the software front, the system employs an improved PatchCore algorithm that has been trained and tested on a dataset constructed from real-world scenarios of secondary water supply pump rooms, achieving an AUROC metric of up to 0.996 and an inference speed of 23.6ms per image. Anomaly information from the pump rooms is transmitted to an IOT platform, email, and server for remote access by personnel. This research offers an effective solution for the intelligent monitoring of pump rooms and provides valuable practical insights for safeguarding the security and reliability of secondary water supply systems.

articleTitle: Single-Pixel Detection Based Tracking of Multiple Moving Objects Using Window Geometric Moment
abstract: Fast localization and tracking of multi-targets is of great significance in many fields such as guidance, area surveillance, and unmanned aerial vehicle detection, etc. Benefiting from the unique mechanism of single-pixel imaging, a single-pixel detection based tracking method with windowed geometrical moment detection is proposed to achieve fast multiple objects tracking. Fourier slice pattern is utilized to obtain a one-dimensional projection of the scene and design the window function, which is combined with zero-order geometric moment patterns to obtain the region of the multi-target at first. In the subsequent frame tracking, the window function of each target is combined with the three geometric moments patterns to obtain the center of mass position, and the window function is updated to realize the matching correlation, and the sampling rate can be as low as 0.0034%, which greatly reduces the sampling time to achieve fast tracking. With a modulated frame rate of 20kHz, tracking can be done at frame rates up to 2200 Hz. While the window overlaps, the window transformation, and multi-directional Fourier slice segmentation method are designed to solve the tracking error. A background subtraction method is applied in complex backgrounds. The simulations of a scene with a spatial resolution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$512 \times 512$</tex> pixels are performed, and the results show that the proposed method tracks the localization of three targets with an error of less than one pixel in both horizontal and vertical directions.

articleTitle: Modeling and Prescribed Performance Attitude Control of Transport Aircraft
abstract: The attitude control problem of the transport air-craft under state constraints is investigated in this paper. Firstly, a 6-degree-of-freedom(DOF) model of the transport aircraft is established, and an aerodynamic parameter interpolation table is created using wind tunnel test data. The aircraft's aerodynamic parameters are identified using an improved Simulated Annealing-Particle Swarm Optimization(SA-PSO) algorithm, which providing a basis for control law design. Then, the prescribed performance control theory is introduced. A prescribed performance function is established to constrain the dynamic and steady-state performance of the aircraft system. The aircraft's attitude angle output error is transformed into an unconstrained space and an attitude controller is designed using the backstepping control method based on the transformed error. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted to validate the performance of the proposed prescribed performance back-stepping attitude controller(PPBC). The simulation results show that the aircraft model with PPBC controller can effectively track the desired signal and maintain the error within the prescribed performance boundary.

articleTitle: Estimating Finger Joint Angles from Surface Electromyography Using Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: This study proposes a novel method to improve the accuracy of finger joint angle estimation based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and surface electromyography (sEMG). sEMG, a complex biological signal measuring muscle electrical activity, plays a crucial role in controlling prosthetic devices for amputees. To address the challenge of accurately simulating continuous multi-finger movements in intelligent prosthetics, we introduce a CNN-based approach that improves joint angle prediction. Key innovations include the simultaneous estimation of five joint angles using a CNN regression model and the extraction of two time-domain and one frequency-domain features from sEMG signals. The method was validated using forearm sEMG data from eight channels and finger joint movement angles from six subjects performing nine distinct finger movements. The proposed method achieved high accuracy, with R2 values of 0.802, 0.805, 0.904, 0.931, and 0.899 for estimating the five finger joint angles, demonstrating its potential for enhancing multi-finger movement control in prosthetic hands.

articleTitle: Enhanced YOLOv8 Method for Real-Time Detection of Complex Fabric Defects
abstract: Detecting fabric defects in the context of diverse fabrics, textures, and colors has always been a significant and challenging problem. Additionally, the scarcity of datasets in industrial applications limits the generalization and robustness of models, particularly in detecting small defects. To address these issues, this paper proposes an improved YOLOv8 method for textile defect detection. First, a weighted feature fusion method is used to enhance the network's focus on critical information, effectively addressing challenges in detecting small defects. To further improve detection performance, we introduce the DGSCSP feature fusion module, which integrates multi-level feature information, reduces redundancy from irrelevant data, and decreases computational complexity. Furthermore, the original bounding box loss function is replaced with an angle loss function to improve training stability. Finally, reparameterization techniques are applied to enhance model performance without increasing inference costs, maintaining the same model architecture. Experimental results on the Tianchi fabric dataset, detecting 24 defect types, show that the proposed algorithm achieves 92.2% precision, 82.8% recall, and 90.5% mAP50, with an inference time of only 2.2 milliseconds. These results demonstrate the exceptional performance and efficiency of the proposed algorithm in textile defect detection.

articleTitle: A Style-Pooling Vision Transformer for Underwater Object Classification Based on Audio-Visual Image Fusion
abstract: To enhance underwater object classification performance, we propose an audio-visual image fusion method using Vision Transformers (ViTs) equipped with style pooling-based recalibration modules (SPRMs). Our network termed as Fusion-ViT consists of two branches: one for audio image input and the other for visual image input. Each ViT branch incorporates a SPRM to improve feature representation. After feature extraction from both branches, the outputs are fused using channel-wise addition and then fed into a linear classifier for classification. We evaluate FusionViT on a custom underwater object dataset comprising paired audio and visual images. Extensive comparative and ablation experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our audio-visual image fusion classification method. Notably, FusionViT achieves superior accuracy compared to methods that do not incorporate audio-visual fusion, all while maintaining a comparable model size. This underscores the advantages of fusing heterogeneous features for improved image classification. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first ViT architecture to achieve this.

articleTitle: Research on the Control of Large Flexibility Spacecraft Based on Time-Delay Link
abstract: For satellites with low-frequency, strongly coupled flexible attachments, the impact of time-delay links on the stability of the control system is particularly evident [1]. For satellites that need large dynamic maneuver tracking, the impact of time-delay links on the control system's attitude accuracy is particularly evident as well. This paper focuses on the time-delay link in the control of large flexible spacecraft, designs several different control strategies in combination with different on-orbit working condition modes, and ensures the on-orbit attitude accuracy of the spacecraft.

articleTitle: Wheelchair Tai Chi Teaching System Based on Real-Time Vision Motion Capture
abstract: In the field of rehabilitation, Tai Chi is highly recognized for its gentle movements and promotion of body coordination. This paper presents the design and development of a mixed-reality teaching system for wheelchair Tai Chi based on the Kinect camera and Unity3D development platform. To address visualization issues, the system includes standard motion animations of an instructor and uses real-time motion capture technology to reconstruct users' movements in 3D, enhancing the efficiency and engagement of wheelchair Tai Chi instruction. To evaluate users' movements, the system employs a frame-by-frame comparison method based on angles and an action sequence scoring method using a sliding window and backtracking algorithm.

articleTitle: Reflected Impedance Based Maximum Output Power Monitoring for MCR- WPT
abstract: This paper proposes a magnetically coupled resonant wireless power transmission maximum output power monitoring method based on reflected impedance allowing to solve the problem of large fluctuation of system output power due to the uncertainty of the position of the receiving coils in the conventional wireless power transmission system. The expression of the reflected impedance of the transmitting loop function of the transmission distance is first derived according to Kirchhoff's voltage law. The relationship between the reflected impedance and the maximum output power is then obtained. Afterwards, a simulation model is developed using Simplorer and Maxwell. When the position of the receiving coils changes, the transmitting coils are adjusted to the optimal transmission position by monitoring the reflected impedance, which allows the system to maintain the maximum output power. Furthermore, an experimental model of wireless power transmission is developed. Several experiments are conducted at different distances between the two coils. The proposed reflected impedance monitoring method can make the system always function at the maximum output power.

articleTitle: MADDPG Based Radar Interference Resource Allocation Decision
abstract: For the problem of jamming penetration under the one-to-many scenario with jammer, a real-time radar interference resource allocation method based on the Multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) algorithm is proposed. This method describes the interference resource allocation model as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), and designed the state space, action space and reward function for interference resource allocation problem. The jammer is divided into three heterogeneous agents, each responsible for selecting jamming targets, jamming patterns, and jamming power, respectively. These three agents coordinate to enhance the convergence ability of the high-dimensional action space algorithm. Simulation results indicate that the jamming resource allocation method designed in this paper provides better jamming effects on radar positions, higher stability, and effectively improves the operational performance of the jammer.

articleTitle: An Effective Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Gyroscope Control Method Based on ESOPI-PLL
abstract: In the design of nuclear magnetic resonance gyroscopes, the closed-loop control of the excitation magnetic field is crucial. Among various control methods, the phase-locked loop (PLL) is widely used to enhance the dynamic characteristics and stability of the gyroscope. This research employs the Second-Order Generalized Integrator (SOGI) as the phase detector, with the loop filter utilizing PI control. However, the system, being of type 2, cannot track acceleration signals without a static error. To address this limitation, we propose a loop filter design based on an Extended State Observer (ESO) integrated with PI control, effectively transforming the system into ESOPI-PLL, which is a type of Type3-PLL. Compared to the traditional SOGI-PLL system, simulation results demonstrate that our proposed scheme extends the gyroscope range to 2000 °/s, with a bandwidth of 30Hz, and achieves zero static error tracking. This advancement presents significant application potential for nuclear magnetic resonance gyroscopes.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach for Aerodynamic Characteristics Identification Based on Time-Frequency Analysis
abstract: With the increasingly wide range of flight altitude and velocity, the complexity and uncertainty of aircraft dynamic characteristics become prominent. The difference between aerodynamic data obtained according to wind-tunnel testing or computational fluid dynamics and actual aerodynamic characteristics becomes increasingly significant, resulting in the inability to schedule control gains. Deep learning is used to identify the actual aerodynamic characteristics of the aircraft and adjust control gains in real time. First of all, aerodynamic characteristic uncertainties and inconsistencies are modeled by varying the aerodynamic data used for control system design. The digital simulation is carried out under different aerodynamic modes and types of overload commands. Then, classify the aerodynamic characteristics according to the gain margin. Secondly, continuous wavelet transform is used to obtain time-frequency images of angular velocity, control surface deflection, overload, and overload command. Finally, convolutional neural networks are trained to extract time-frequency image features and identify the type of aerodynamic characteristics. The simulation results show that the accuracy of online identification reaches 96.3%.

articleTitle: Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection in Medical Images Using Conditional Denoising Diffusion Models and Data Augmentation
abstract: Zero-shot anomaly detection holds significant importance in medical image analysis, particularly when newly emerging anomaly categories are absent from the training set. Traditional methods often perform poorly due to their inability to effectively classify and locate anomalous regions. In this study, we propose a method that combines the Denoising Diffusion Anomaly Detection (DDAD) model with data augmentation strategies for zero-shot anomaly detection in medical images. Prior to data training, we employ various data augmentation techniques, such as contrast enhancement, sharpening, rotation, and translation, to increase data diversity and enhance the model's ability to learn image features. This improves the model's generalization capability and robustness. Experimental validation on medical image datasets demonstrates that our method exhibits superior performance in zero-shot anomaly detection tasks, significantly outperforming the current state-of-the-art models. Our experiments on the BMAD benchmark for medical anomaly detection demonstrate significant improvements in zero-shot anomaly detection for the Brain, Liver, and RESC datasets. Specifically, the AUROC for anomaly classification increased by 1.67%, 16.56%, and 13.09%, respectively, while the AUROC for anomaly localization improved by 4.13%, 0.65%, and 5.85%, respectively,

articleTitle: BFMF-Net: Bimodal Feature Multiscale Fusion Network for Multilayer Steel Bar Intersection Detection
abstract: At present, steel bar binding robots solve the problems of large amounts of work and worker safety in steel bar binding projects, and the detection of steel bar binding intersections has become a research point. To solve the problems of wrong detection and unsatisfactory detection accuracy of intersections in the lower non-bound layer due to the multi-layer structure of rebar and the complex environment at the site, this paper proposes a bimodal feature multiscale fusion network, BFMF-Net. To better fuse the RGB and depth map features, a bimodal feature fusion module, BFFM, and a multiscale fusion module, MFM, are proposed. To validate the effectiveness of the network, the validation results on the val dataset and the test dataset of the constructed bimodal multilayer steel binding dataset Bi-MSB indicate that, relative to the results of the base algorithm for detecting the intersections on the RGB alone, the detection accuracies of the proposed network are improved by 0.005 and 0.027, respectively, and the robustness to complex environments is also significantly improved.

articleTitle: Digital Predictive V2C Peak Controlled Buck Converter With Current Observer
abstract: To solve issues of increased cost, noise, and delay caused by current sensors in traditional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V^{2}C$</tex> control, a digital predictive <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V^{2}C$</tex> peak control algorithm with the current observer is proposed. Firstly, based on the geometric characteristics of inductor current and output voltage ripples, the peak and valley values of inner loop feedback voltage are stable within the same switching cycle, which effectively eliminates the subharmonic oscillation that occurs under trailing-edge modulation. The control voltage of the inner loop can be followed by inner loop feedback voltage within two switching cycles. Secondly, a current observer is constructed based on the ripple characteristics of the inductor current, which estimates the inductor current according to the input voltage, output voltage, and duty cycle. Furthermore, the discrete-time nonlinear model of the Buck converter system under the proposed algorithm is derived, and the critical equivalent series resistance (ESR) value for system stability is calculated using Jacobian matrices. Simulink simulation results demonstrate the correctness of the theoretical derivation of the critical capacitor ESR. With low capacitor ESR <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(20\mathrm{m}\Omega)$</tex>, the converter system with the proposed algorithm remains stable and exhibits good dynamic response performance, while <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V^{2}$</tex> peak control occurs low-frequency oscillation. Compared with voltage-mode control, the dynamic response time for load change is reduced by 55.56%, and for line voltage change is reduced by 66.67%.

articleTitle: Adaptive Disturbance Rejection Control Design for Quadrotor UAV Based on High-Order Fully Actuated System Method
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive disturbance rejection control design for quadrotors based on a high-order fully actuated (HOFA) system approach. To achieve the tracking of a preset reference trajectory under turbulence disturbances, the established 4-DOF quadrotor nonlinear systems is transformed into three HOFA subsystems using an improved HOFA method. An adaptive disturbance rejection controller is designed, and an augmented error model is constructed. The gradient descent method is used to obtain the corresponding adaptive law, which dynamically updates the parameters of the adaptive disturbance rejection controller. Simulations verify that, under the action of this controller, the quadrotor system exhibits good stability, disturbance suppression, and output asymptotic tracking capability.

articleTitle: Stability of Probabilistic Boolean Networks*
abstract: This paper studies the fix-point stability and set stability of Probabilistic Boolean networks based on its corresponding discrete Markov chain. Through the state classification of the corresponding Markov chain, necessary and sufficient conditions for the fix-point stability and set stability of Probabilistic Boolean networks are given seperately. And the method to find the largest invariant subset of Probabilistic Boolean networks is provided. Finally, numericial examples are given to illustrate the obtained theoretical results.

articleTitle: FDI Attacks Detection and Reliable Prediction for Lithium-Ion Battery Based on Encrypted Koopman Prediction Method
abstract: This paper proposes a method for detecting attacks and reliable prediction based on encrypted Koopman prediction method in the scenario where batteries are subject to FDI (False Data Injection) attacks. On the one hand, this method accurately detects whether the lithium-ion battery system has been subjected to FDI attacks. On the other hand, even in the event of FDI attacks, reliable prediction of the lithium-ion battery system output is achieved through the use of encryption and pre-set signal methods. The paper provides ample numerical comparisons to demonstrate the effectiveness of these results.

articleTitle: Enhancement and Analysis of Transient Stability of VSC with Anti-Windup Augmented Phase-Locked Loop
abstract: Maintaining stability of grid-following VSC during severe grid faults remains an open problem, where phase locked loop (PLL) plays a critical role. Previous research on PLL and transient stability either introduces time delays which degrades the system dynamics, or is computationally expensive. In this paper, an improved SRF -PLL configuration with an anti-windup compensator is proposed to improve the transient stability of the grid-following VSC. Based on the linearized model of PLL, an optimization problem is formulated to determine the parameters of the anti-windup compensator. Simulation results illustrated that the proposed PLL can tremendously enhance the transient stability of grid-following VSC compared with the existing PLLs.

articleTitle: RDB-YOLO: A Lightweight and High-Precision Steel Surface Defects Detection Method
abstract: Most deep learning-based target detection algorithms have low speed and accuracy for detecting defects on steel surfaces, which fails to meet the requirements of industrial sites. To tackle this important issue, we propose a lightweight network structure based on YOLOv5n. Firstly, Receptive Field Enhancement (RFE) is introduced into the backbone network for compensation for loss of accuracy caused by light changes and environmental noise interference. Secondly, Deformable Convolution network (DCN) is utilized to improve performance of the network to fit defects of different shapes. Thirdly, Bi-Ievel Routing Attention mechanism (BRA) is embedded into the neck to improve detection performance in small targets. Experimental data from the NED -DET dataset indicates that the Mean Average Precision (mAP) of the improved algorithm is 82.1 %, which is 5.1 % higher than that of the benchmark model, and the detection rate is 60.4 frame/s. Compared with other mainstream object detection algorithms, our algorithm has higher accuracy, lighter weight parameters and can achieve efficient steel surface defect detection under the premise of maintaining a certain detection speed.

articleTitle: Application of Knowledge Distilled Neural Network to Railway Overhead Line Fault Diagnosis
abstract: This research has applied the teacher-student model of knowledge distillation (KD) technique to compress artificial neural networks (ANN) and Densely Connected Convolutional Networks (DenseNet) for efficiently examining railway overhead line's footage and diagnosing its operational health. The feature extraction process is optimized by a Satisfied Learning Transfer (STL) strategy; the KD+STL combination refines the ‘dark knowledge’ in the teacher model and updates the student model through a proactive feedback mechanism, leading to higher diagnostic accuracy. Furthermore, to keep the model simple with a practicable number of parameters while minimizing the loss of performance, the benefits of adopting differential KD and attention-based probabilistic factor knowledge distillation assisted KD (APF-KD) are discussed. The footage is segmented and compressed, and the results of different KDs algorithms are presented for comparison and recommendations.

articleTitle: Time Delayed Bilateral Teleoperation Using a Novel Wave Variable Architecture with Position Compensation
abstract: The communication delay is a critical concern within teleoperation systems due to the significant impact on system stability. The passivity-based wave variable approach can guarantee the stability of the teleoperation systems, but wave reflection may occur, which seriously distorts the operator. Moreover, serious position drift may occur when the communication delay varies over time. Considering the above issues, this paper proposes a novel wave variable approach to reduce wave reflection by removing the force terms present in the forward wave. Furthermore, an energy reservoir is designed to compensate the forward wave, which is used to deal with the aforementioned position drift problem and maintain the passivity of system under time-varying delay. Simulation is provided to demonstrate that the proposed approach can guarantee the stability of the teleoperation system while its transparency can be also obviously improved.

articleTitle: Research on the Temperature Control System of TP347 Induction Heating Based on Fuzzy Neural PID
abstract: TP347 material is widely used in the fields of oil and natural gas transportation due to its characteristics, and its unique working environment leads to the extremely high requirements for thermal stabilization of TP347 material pipes. In this paper, a heating power supply for TP347 material pipes is designed, and fuzzy neural PID regulation is introduced to control the heater in a nonlinear way, and then the calculation is verified by COMSOL finite element simulation. The correctness of the calculated parameters is then verified by COMSOL finite element simulation.

articleTitle: An Improved Mobile Phone Screen Defect Detection Based on Multi-Level Feature Fusion
abstract: With the growing demand for cell phone products, the quality of cell phone screens has become increasingly crucial. Accurate detection of mobile phone screen glass (MPSG) defects is of utmost importance. However, traditional manual and machine vision methods of detection suffer from low accuracy and slow speed. In this paper, a novel MPSG detection method that addresses the limitations of existing detection methods. The proposed method utilizes a YOLOv8 model with multilevel feature fusion necks. We develop a cutting-edge solution to address the issue of defect scale imbalance. Our High-level Screening-feature Fusion Pyramid-Path Aggregation Network (HS-FPN-PAN) enables seamless integration of features at multiple levels, resulting in enhanced performance. The model utilizes high-level features as weights, effectively filters low-level feature information using the channel attention module, and integrates the filtered information with high-level features to enhance the model's feature expression capability. Additionally, we implement the variability convolution module to enhance the neck's capability in extracting irregular shapes. This module is designed to be lightweight, ensuring optimal performance. Our experiments demonstrate that the enhanced YOLOv8 model exhibits superior detection accuracy and inference speed, providing strong evidence for the effectiveness of the proposed model in this paper.

articleTitle: Optimal Tracking Performance of Networked Control Systems Under DoS and its Applications
abstract: This paper investigates the optimal tracking performance (OTP) of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) discrete networked control systems (NCSs) under the influence of Denial of Service (DoS) attack, channel noise, and bandwidth constraints. The channel noise is assumed to be additive Gaussian white noise (AWGN). Due to the randomness of DoS attack, a Bernoulli distribution is used for DoS modeling. Utilizing frequency domain analysis methods, coprime factorization, all-pass decomposition, and Youla parameterization, an explicit expression for the optimal tracking performance (OTP) of the system under the two-degree-of-freedom (TDOF) controller is derived. The analysis indicates that non-minimum phase (NMP) zeros, unstable poles (UPs), DoS attack, and network constraints affect the OTP of NCSs. Finally, the theoretical results are validated through simulations of MIMO NCS and vehicle control system.

articleTitle: Pose Measurement and TCF Calibration for Automatic Cabin Docking
abstract: Cabin docking is a fundamental process in aircraft and rocket manufacturing, where cabins are mounted on robots to complete the docking process. Tool Control Frame (TCF) calibration, which involves calibrating the relative pose matrix between the docking cabin and the robot end, is a critical step in ensuring the accuracy of cabin docking. In this paper, we propose automatic pose measurement and TCF calibration methods for cabin docking. First, cabin pose measurement is performed using a coded structured light sensor to capture point clouds. A two-stage model-based point cloud registration method is introduced to enhance robustness and accuracy. Second, robotic TCF calibration is carried out by solving the AX=XB equation. The proposed calibration method introduces an auxiliary frame and designs three pairs of robot poses to improve calibration accuracy. Finally, experiments verify that the proposed methods exhibit high accuracy in pose measurement and TCF calibration, successfully enabling automatic docking.

articleTitle: Predictive Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control for Air Conditioning Supply Air Temperature Based on GWO
abstract: Variable air volume (VAV) air conditioning systems for supply air temperature control involve multiple devices and ducts, characterized by significant time delays and susceptibility to internal and external disturbances. To address these challenges, a control approach combining a linear active disturbance rejection controller (LADRC) with a Smith predictor (SP) is designed, termed predictive linear active disturbance rejection control (SPLADRC), aimed at compensating for delays and enhancing disturbance rejection capabilities. To further improve control performance, controller parameters are optimized using the grey wolf optimization (GWO) algorithm and compared with several common control methods. Simulation results demonstrate that the SPLADRC optimized by the grey wolf optimization algorithm achieves better tracking and robustness, showing promising potential for practical applications.

articleTitle: Water Content Control in Tobacco Leaf Loose and Moisture Regain Process based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: In this paper, the control problem of outlet moisture content is investigated for the tobacco leaf loosening and moisture regain process. Unlike existing strategies that heavily depend on manual expertise for adjusting water addition and hot air temperature, a novel control framework is proposed in this work. This framework integrates an optimal outlet moisture content control method and a traditional Proportion-Integral-Differential (PID) control loop, thereby reducing the dependence on manual intervention. Specifically, the hot air temperature and water addition flow rate are dynamically adjusted using the soft actor-critic (SAC) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed method can maintain the outlet moisture content with a steady-state precision of 0.1%.

Author Keywords: tobacco leaf loose and moisture regain process

articleTitle: SMA-LSTM Soft Sensor Based on Bayesian Optimization in Irregular Sampled Time Sequence of Industrial Processes
abstract: In modern industrial processes, soft sensor technology is used to predict quality parameters that are difficult to measure directly. Due to the complex dynamic relationships inherent in industrial process data series, time series models are often employed for predicting these quality parameters. However, most existing time series prediction models can only handle regular sampled data. Unfortunately, this condition dose not always hold true in real industrial environments. To address this issue, a sampling interval multi-attention LSTM (SMA-LSTM) model is proposed in this paper to handle with potentially irregular sampling conditions. Specifically, a set of attention mechanisms is applied to assess the impact of the sampling interval on the three gating signals. Interval information between sampling points is introduced into the network to adaptively adjust the model's estimation of the dynamic relationships between samples. Additionally, Bayesian optimization is employed to tune the hyperparameters of the network, making it easier to find reasonable parameters in different industrial processes. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed SMA-LSTM is more effective than other time series prediction algorithms.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Data Reconciliation and Gross Error Detection in Olefin Plants by the Expectation Maximization Algorithm Based on Gaussian Mixture Distributions
abstract: Ethylene and its derivatives play an important role in the development of the petrochemical industry, and olefin plants for obtaining ethylene by steam cracking technology are widely used around the world. However, there are many variables involved in the hot section of the plant, and the flow connection relationships are complex. Therefore, when the measurement data contains many gross errors, it is difficult to eliminate the gross errors and obtain accurate data reconciliation results at the same time. However, Gaussian mixture distribution models have independent parameters to characterize gross errors, so they are able to detect multiple gross errors and achieve good reconciliation results, and the expectation maximization(EM) algorithm can efficiently derive each parameter and update the estimates of the parameters iteratively in the model. In this paper, it is proved experimentally that this method can be well used to solve the data reconciliation and gross error detection problems in the hot section of olefin plant.

articleTitle: Data-Driven and Internal Model Control for Optimal Output Regulation of Linear Systems with an Assured Convergence Rate
abstract: This paper addresses an optimal output regulation problem with a requirement on convergence rate for linear time-invariant systems with unknown system dynamics. First, an internal model is introduced to transform the problem into a dynamic optimization problem. Then, a new virtual system is designed to replace the original system and internal model. By collecting the data from the virtual system, a novel data-driven learning algorithm is proposed, which not only learns the optimal control policy but also guarantees the convergence rate of the tracking error to be no slower than a predefined convergence rate. Finally, an illustrative example is presented to validate the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Research on Prediction of Track Irregularity in Maglev Transportation System Based on BP Network
abstract: As a rail transportation tool, the track condition is always an important factor affecting the safe operation of maglev trains. Based on the analysis of the influence of track irregularity on the state of the maglev train suspension system, this paper makes a preliminary prediction and estimation of the impact caused by track irregularity by using the train operation state data provided by the state comprehensive monitoring system. Through the modeling and simulation of the maglev train suspension system, the influences of various track irregularity conditions on the state of the maglev train suspension system are analyzed and compared. By monitoring the changes of the suspension gap and suspension current when the train passes the same position of the track multiple times, and using the prediction method based on the recursive synthetic BP network, the fluctuation amplitude of the suspension gap when the train passes this position of the track in the future is predicted, and then the safety impact of the track irregularity at this location is evaluated.

articleTitle: Prediction of Office Building Air Conditioning Cooling Load Based on the CEEMDAN-TPA-LSTMModel
abstract: Accurate prediction of air conditioning cooling load is fundamental to optimizing energy-efficient operation of air conditioning systems. In this paper, we propose a combined forecasting model, CEEMDAN-TPA-LSTM, based on Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN), Temporal Attention (TPA), and Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTM). Initially, cooling load data for the summer three months were simulated using EnergyPlus software, and correlation analysis was performed between cooling load data and meteorological information to select the most relevant external features for cooling load prediction. Subsequently, the CEEMDAN algorithm was employed to decompose the original cooling load data, resulting in several Intrinsic Mode Function (IMF) sequences and residual sequences. Finally, the LSTM model with an attention mechanism was utilized to predict each signal component, and the combination of these components yielded the predicted cooling load data. The ultimate prediction results demonstrate that the CEEMDAN-TPA-LSTM combined forecasting model outperforms other models such as GRU, LSTM, and TPA-LSTM, providing robust support for energy optimization of air conditioning systems.

articleTitle: Flexible Rigid Coupling Soft Pneumatic Actuators with Customizable Shape
abstract: By designing and manufacturing different internal air chambers, soft pneumatic actuators can achieve a variety of movements, such as bending, twisting, and stretching. The flexibility of actuators can be improved by designing shape-customizable pneumatic actuators. In this paper, we propose a programmable design that enables mechanical programming and shape customization of pneumatic actuators by flexibly and selectively placing rigid constraint structures. Specifically, the shape-customizable soft actuator designed in this paper consists of a bending soft actuator and a rigid constraint structure. Under the coupling effect of the rigid-flexible structure, some areas of the soft actuator are constrained and cannot be bent, while other areas can bend. Through the constraint effect of the rigid constraint structure on the deformation of the soft actuator, the customization of the shape of the soft actuator after deformation is realized. In addition, we also studied the influence of the size of the rigid constraint structure on the deformation results of the actuator. The shape-programmable soft pneumatic actuators can be used in application scenarios with specific requirements on the shape of the actuator.

articleTitle: Detection of False Data Injection Attacks: An Extending Dimension Data Modification Scheme
abstract: To achieve the detection of a typical stealthy false data injection attacks in two-channel, this paper presents a data modification scheme for extending the dimension of the measured value from the view of a defender. Before the sensory measurement data is transmitted to the communication network, the dimension of the data is expanded to change the system knowledge required by attacker to launch stealthy false data injection attacks. The dimension reducing processing of the measurement data transferred to the controller, causes a bias of the state estimation between attacker and defender to achieve the detection of attack. With the expanding-reducing processing of the data modification scheme, the defender can still detect residual discrepancies from the attacked measurement data and trigger an anomaly detector alarm, even though system knowledge modified by the data is obtained by the attacker. Finally, the effectiveness and realizability of the proposed data modification scheme are verified by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Research on the Modeling and Optimization of Mutual Inductance in Dynamic Wireless Charging Systems for Electric Vehicles
abstract: The interaction of mutual inductance between coils is pivotal in dynamic wireless charging for electric vehicles, profoundly shaping power transmission performance throughout the charging process. This paper proposes a mutual inductance calculation model that accounts for the driving state of vehicles, aiming to effectively address the current challenges in dynamic wireless vehicle charging. Firstly, the rectangular coil is chosen as the focus of study for its enhanced stability against drifting. Subsequently, a novel mutual inductance calculation model is developed by integrating the Neumann formula with the Biot-Savart law. The optimal coil parameters are designed by backpropagation (BP) neural network and genetic algorithm, and the influence of different bias on mutual inductance is discussed by simulation. Finally, an experimental infrastructure is established tailored for dynamic wireless charging systems intended for vehicles. This platform is designed to authenticate the precision and efficacy of the proposed computational model under real-world operational conditions.

articleTitle: HATSC-YOLOv10:Improved YOLOv10 for Satellite Remote Sensing Images of Small Object Detection
abstract: When dealing with small object detection in satellite remote sensing images, the state-of-the-art object detection model YOLOv10 often suffers from the difficulty of extracting enough local detail features of small objects. In this paper, a novel and improved YOLOv10 network based on hybrid attention transformer (HAT) as well as spatial and channel reconstruction convolution (SCconv) is proposed, which is named HATSC-YOLOv10. A brand new HATSC module, which takes full use of HAT and SCconv to extract and refine more efficient high-level features, is designed and integrated with original YOLOv10 network so as to strengthen its capability of feature extraction towards small objects. What's more, the normalized Gaussian Wasserstein Distance (NWD) metric is used to calculate the similarity between two bounding boxes instead of the complete intersection over union (CIoU) metric used in the loss function of original YOLOv10, in order to make the whole network be insensitive to the positional deviation of small objects. Experimental results on DOTA remote sensing dataset show satisfactory performance of the proposed HATSC-YOLOv10 on small object detection in satellite remote sensing images. Compared with original YOLOv10 network, HATSC-YOLOv10 shows an increase of 2.61%, 2.09%, 2.3%, and 1.68% in precision, recall, mAP50, and mAP50-95 respectively.

articleTitle: Adaptive Event-Trigged Control for Intelligent Connected Vehicles Systems with Collision Avoidance
abstract: This study proposes a robust adaptive neural network asymptotic tracking control for a third-order heterogeneous vehicle platoon system with input saturation. In order to reduce the waste of communication resources and unnecessary data transmission, an event triggering mechanism is constructed. An auxiliary design system-integrated control scheme is devised to tackle the input saturation issue, and utilizing the radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) to approximate the unspecified nonlinear function. Combining the auxiliary system and triggering mechanism, an adaptive NN asymptotic tracking control scheme is developed. Through the barrier Lyapunov functions, the developed control scheme ensures the spacing error asymptotically converges to zero, and both string and individual stabilities can be proved. In addition, the collisions can be avoided. Comprehensive numerical simulations validate the efficacy of the proposed control approach. Finally, numerical simulations validate the effectiveness of our control approach.

articleTitle: Pneumatic Valve Position Control of Third-order LADRC Based on RBF Neural Network
abstract: Pneumatic control valves are used extensively in industrial processes. Due to the valve's nonlinear characteristics and the impact of time-varying disturbances, the PID control strategy struggles to achieve the desired levels of precision and robustness in control systems. This paper introduces a control scheme combining a third-order Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Controller (LADRC) with a Radial Basis Function (RBF) neural network. Firstly, the third-order transfer function model of the pneumatic control valve is established. Then a third-order LADRC is designed, and the Jacobian information of the valve position is recognized online by RBF neural network to realize the online tuning of the control parameters. Finally, the results of simulation and experimental show that the proposed method boasts excellent anti-interference capability and superior control precision.

articleTitle: Simulation and Material Removal Modeling of Abrasive Air Jet Erosion
abstract: Abrasive jets are commonly employed to remove damaged organic coatings. To ensure surface processing quality and enhance the predictability of abrasive jet erosion, it is crucial to quantitatively analyze the erosion process and establish an erosion model. An abrasive air jet experimental platform was designed, and erosion simulation analysis revealed that the primary factors influencing the erosion rate are abrasive velocity and jet angle. An orthogonal central composite experiment featuring 5 factors and 4 levels was devised, and a fitting model was constructed based on the experimental results. As jet pressure and abrasive mesh size increase, material removal also rises; however, an increase in jet angle and workpiece movement speed results in reduced material removal. Meanwhile, with an increase in jet distance, material removal initially rises and then falls, peaking at approximately 40mm. By comparing experimental and predicted values, the maximum absolute deviation was 9.61mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and the average deviation was 3.92mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, demonstrating that the model effectively captures how various process parameters influence material removal, confirming its efficacy.

articleTitle: Bipartite Consensus Algorithm Under Second-Order Multi-Agent Systems with Matrix Weight-Based Network
abstract: Currently, the research on consensus in second-order scalar-weighted multi-agent systems has made significant progress. However, when describing complex problems, scalar weighted networks are difficult to accurately represent the coupling relationships between these problems. The dimensional expansion offered by matrix-weighted networks facilitates the description and analysis of complex issues. Currently, there is still limited research on second-order matrix-weighted networks. In this paper, a novel control protocol is designed using the backstepping method, enabling second-order matrix-weighted networks to achieve bipartite consensus. The impact of the Laplacian's null space on the network's bipartite consensus results is analyzed, and numerical simulations are conducted to validate the conclusions presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Bipartite Consensus of Multi-Agent Systems via Adaptive Dynamic Event-Triggered Control
abstract: This paper investigates the bipartite consensus problem for leader-following multi-agent systems over the signed undirected graph. An adaptive dynamic event-triggered strategy is developed for achieving bipartite consensus with relative information among agents. Specifically, by including adaptive techniques, the design of control protocols frees from the dependence on global network information. Then, due to the relative information we introduced, also no global coordinate frame is needed. Furthermore, the triggering condition in this study can be dynamically evolved by adding an internal variable, hence prolonging the duration between consecutive events. The proposed protocol is proved to asymptotically reach the bipartite consensus while excluding Zeno behavior. The effectiveness of our method is demonstrated through a numerical example.

articleTitle: ISDA-QBAS Net: A Novel CNN Optimization and Data Enhancement Model for Pneumonia Diagnosis
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) excel in medical image analysis through iterative weight learning and updating. Traditional random weight initialization can result in low accuracy, prolonged convergence, or training failure due to extreme parameter values. This paper introduces the Quantum Beetle Antennae Search (QBAS) algorithm, a bionic optimization method. To address the limitations of the Chest X-ray (CXR) dataset, the Implicit Semantic Data Enhancement (ISDA) algorithm is proposed, which semantically augments the dataset without manual intervention. The combined QBAS-ISDA net further optimizes CNN performance.
