Exper-iments on the CXR dataset show the QBAS net achieves 91.3% accuracy, while the QBAS-ISDA net reaches 91.8%, surpassing the baseline's 72.6%. The QBAS algorithm also outperforms other bionic optimization methods like Beetle Antennae Search (BAS), Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO).

articleTitle: Resistant Q-Learning for Path Planning of Mobile Robot in Complex Environment
abstract: This study proposes a Resistant Q-Learning (RQL) algorithm to address the problems of low efficiency and slow convergence when mobile robots perform optimal path planning in unknown complex environments. The algorithm learns by utilizing the estimation deviation of the Q-values in Q-Learning. According to the number of updates of the Q-values estimation, the estimation deviation and learning rate are dynamically adjusted. By comparing this algorithm to Q-learning, the adapt-ability and convergence speed are greatly improved. The RQL algorithm is implemented on a mobile robot for path planning, and related experiments are conducted on simulated maps. The effectiveness and utility of the RQL are demonstrated by the simulation results.

articleTitle: DC-Link Voltage Control of Voltage Source Converters via a Fully Actuated System Approach
abstract: In practical applications, the DC-link voltage regu-lation performance of the three-phase voltage-source converter (VSC) is an important index. However, it is affected by load disturbances and parameter uncertainties. To tackle this problem, this paper introduces a robust control strategy for the VSC based on a fully actuated system. Initially, we develop the fully actuated VSC model, incorporating load disturbances and parameter uncertainties as lumped disturbances. Utilizing this model, a finite-time observer and a state feedback controller are then successively designed to ensure rapid and accurate DC-link voltage control while improving disturbance rejection. Both simulation and experimental results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Notably, this strategy has a single-loop structure, which facilitates its implementation.

articleTitle: Driver-Centric Predictive Risk Map Modeling via Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: In the field of autonomous vehicles, extensive research on risk assessment has been carried out to improve road safety. Nevertheless, in scenarios of assisted driving, particularly scenarios of human-machine co-driving, the establishment of driver-centric risk assessment models remains a challenge. The absence of consideration for human drivers may lead to a reduction in trust within the human-AI team and give rise to conflicts between humans and machines. This study presents a Driver-centric Predictive Risk Map (DPRM) model that combines the driver model with the AI risk assessment model through deep successor reinforcement learning. The proposed risk map not only takes into account future risks associated with driver behavior but also adapts to drivers with different driving styles.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Output Regulation for Linear $2 \times 2$ Hyperbolic System with Boundary Unmatched Disturbance
abstract: This paper investigates the sliding-mode output regulation problem of linear <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> hyperbolic PDE systems. The disturbances to which the system is subjected contains two types: modellable and unmatched disturbances. For modellable disturbance, the geometric design technique is employed to design compensator to compensate for the disturbance. For unmatched disturbance, the sliding-mode control technique is leveraged to constrain a particular system state to the sliding-mode surface, and thus eliminating the adverse impact of unmatched disturbances. We address the tracking control problem under these two types of disturbances on the basis of the existing work that only considers modellable disturbance. The comparative simulation verifies the effectiveness and advance of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Robust Data-Driven Attitude Control for the Hovering Flight of Aerial Manipulator
abstract: Coupling disturbances, caused by onboard manipu-lator's motion, would bring non-negligible influence to unmanned aerial vehicle. To tackle this problem, this paper introduces an adaptive data-driven attitude architecture that includes dynamic modeling and controller design to achieve the hovering flight of the aerial manipulator. In the modeling part, only input-output data of system is required to identify the dynamics, which reduces the complexity effectively compared to traditional modeling method. In the controller part, a robust attitude control law is designed utilizing identified model to resist coupling disturbances, wherein the disturbances are not supposed to be estimated by additional methods, such as observers. Moreover, the stability of the attitude control system is validated through the Lyapunov criterion. Furthermore, comparative simulations are carried out to showcase the effectiveness of the proposed method. Finally, real-world experiments are tested using our self-built platform. Experimental results demonstrate our method could improve the coupling disturbances suppressing capability effectively.

articleTitle: Multi-Robot Formation Obstacle Avoidance Based on Virtual Robots and Improved Artificial Potential Fields
abstract: Aiming at the problem of multi-robot formation control to avoid obstacles, a formation obstacle avoidance algorithm based on virtual robot layer and improved artificial potential field is proposed. First, for information management, a member management mechanism based on the virtual swarm head is designed to realize information sharing and navigator designation. Second, the artificial potential field method is improved to establish the internal potential field of robots and the potential field of obstacles to ensure the obstacle avoidance of multiple robots in the formation process and the collision avoidance among members; finally, simulation experiments are designed, and it is finally proved that the method can effectively solve the obstacle avoidance and collision avoidance problems of the multi-robot system in the formation process.

articleTitle: DSMT: RGB-D Dual-Stream Multi-Task Model for Multi-Granularity Semantic Understanding
abstract: Understanding semantic information of objects and scenes from images is an important part of mobile robot perception, providing a visual foundation for its operation in complex environments. This paper proposes a dual-stream multi-task (DSMT) model for realizing three different granularities of semantic understanding simultaneously: object detection, semantic segmentation, and scene classification. By integrating RGB images with geometric information from depth images, our model mitigates the deterioration of feature extraction that typically arise due to similar object textures and ambient lighting variations. Specifically, a Coordinate Attention Fusion Module (CAFM) is designed to mutually refine RGB and depth features. Subsequently, a Dynamic Task Awareness Module (DTAM) is developed to enable dynamic perception at various levels of granularity. Additionally, an RGB-D multi-task dataset in the context of warehouse logistics is constructed, and our model is validated using this dataset. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Code will be available at: https://github.com/BUCT-IUSRC/ResearchDSMT.

articleTitle: Adaptive Finite-Time Control for CPSs Under False Data Injection and Actuator Faults
abstract: This article presents a novel adaptive control scheme for nonlinear Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) with uncertainty under False Data Injection Attacks (FDIAs) and actuator faults. By simultaneously considering the time-varying gain before the state variable in the strict-feedback system state equations and dual-channel injection attacks, the CPS is modeled. Based on which, the exponentially-decay parameters are proposed and the Nussbaum function is introduced to construct a novel finite-time adaptive fuzzy controller. In the end, the feasibility of the proposed scheme is verified through numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Image Realism Enhancement Method Based on Improved Neural Neighbor Style Transfer
abstract: Object detection technology is a very important technique that relies on a large amount of data for training. However, obtaining sufficient data for specific detection targets can be challenging. In cases where data are limited, it is necessary to increase the number of datasets using various methods. We propose an improved algorithm based on the Neural Neighbor Style Transfer (NNST) algorithm to better adapt to the task of realistic style transfer. Through comparative experiments, we find that image realism could be enhanced when the alpha value is 0.75 and content loss, color correction, and high pixel output are used. Additionally, we design a more effective feature extraction network called SE-VGG19. Compared to the original VGG16, SE-VGG19 can improve the network's ability to perceive style and extract features, making the generated images match the target style better while preserving the original content features. Furthermore, we suggest using the center cosine distance instead of the original Euclidean distance for loss measurement. After comparison and verification, our method has been proven to improve image realism compared to the original algorithm greatly.

articleTitle: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for RUL Prediction
abstract: With the complexity and intelligence of industrial equipment continue to increase, Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) of such equipment have become increasingly important, with the accurate prediction of Remaining Useful Life (RUL) emerging as a critical industry need. This paper proposes an RUL prediction method that integrates the Attention-Mamba network with a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) framework. The Mamba network, as an efficient sequence modeling structure, is capable of capturing temporal dependencies. By incorporating the Attention mechanism, the Mamba network can effectively identify key features and changing trends in the operational state of the equipment, highlighting these features through weight allocation to enhance prediction accuracy. Furthermore, we introduce the PINN framework into the model to further improve its predictive performance. We validate the superiority of this method using the C-MAPSS dataset. The proposed approach enhances the accuracy of RUL predictions and provides robust support for intelligent maintenance and reliability management of industrial equipment.

articleTitle: Gravity Anomaly Extraction Method Based on Wavelet Transform and Kalman Filtering
abstract: In standard Kalman filtering (KF), the fixed measurement noise does not accurately describe the gravity anomaly model under undulating flight conditions, leading to a decrease in measurement accuracy. To address this challenge, we propose a Kalman filtering method for gravity anomaly extraction based on wavelet transform noise estimation (WKF), which effectively tracks the measurement noise of the system. The proposed method is validated using measurement data collected under undulating flight conditions. The results show that the WKF method improves the repeatability of two undulating flight lines from 2.49 mGal and 2.63 mGal to 1.0 mGal and 2.10 mGal, respectively, and improves the repeatability of all repeat lines from 1.44 mGal to 0.96 mGal.

articleTitle: DeepONet-Based Bank Angle Profiles Design for Mars Entry with Actuator Constraints
abstract: The determination of the bank angle profile is crucial for Mars atmospheric entry guidance. A significant limitation of existing bank angle profile construction methods is their neglect of the dynamic process of the bank angle. This paper introduces a novel parameterized bank angle profile construction method using deep operator networks (Deep-ONet). Initially, a design strategy for parameterized bank angle profiles, considering the dynamic characteristics of the bank angle, is presented. The bank angle profile is then modeled as an operator dependent on specific parameters. The DeepONet, which is tailor-made for learning operators, is utilized to construct parameterized bank angle profiles of unknown analytical forms. To handle rapid changes in the bank angle, Fourier feature layers are incorporated into the network to encode the time inputs. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed network can effectively approximate the desired bank angle profile. In the guidance design, using the proposed network-based parameterized bank angle profile can effectively reduce the deviation between the predicted and actual flight states.

articleTitle: Discussion on Function Definitions and Related Axioms Within the Coq Proof Assistant
abstract: Axiomatic set theory forms the foundation of modern mathematics, and the Morse-Kelley axiomatic set theory system is more convenient for applications compared to the ZFC system and the NBG system. This text is based on the Morse-Kelley axiomatic set theory. It defines the intersection and union of members in a way that differs from the naive set theory. It then further explores the relevant definitions of functions as well as the axiom of substitution and the axiom of amalgamation, establishing a more comprehensive machine-assisted proof system. Function is one of the fundamental concept in set theory, and the formalization of function provides great convenience for the subsequent establishment of axiomatic systems for real numbers and exponent operations. The entire formalization process in this paper has been verified by Coq and run successfully on computer, with the proof process having standardization and reliability.

articleTitle: Design and Research of Real-Time Perception for Intelligent Power-Assisted Bicycles Based on Fuzzy Control
abstract: This paper introduces an electric-assist bicycle equipped with a power management system that utilizes fuzzy control technology. The system dynamically adjusts motor assistance power based on real-time parameters such as cycling speed, cadence, and road gradient. A Mamdani-based fuzzy logic controller is used to modulate the output of the lithium battery. The primary goal is to improve safety and comfort during cycling while minimizing rider muscular fatigue. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed power management approach significantly enhances the comfort and safety of urban cycling.

articleTitle: Optimal Trajectory Planning and Control of Manipulator Based on Model Predictive and Inversive Control
abstract: Aiming at the problem of optimal trajectory planning and tracking control of manipulators, this paper proposes a trajectory planning and control algorithm based on model predictive and inversive control(MPIC). The MPIC method designs the controller based on the controllability of the system, predicts the future state according to the system's current state when the control quantity is 0, and uses the generalized inverse solution to make the future state error 0. The method sets the total amount of work done by non-conservative forces of the system during motion as an objective function, and the optimal trajectories of each manipulator joint are obtained by the differential evolutionary algorithm and spline interpolation. The MPIC method is used to design the tracking controller, which realizes the trajectory planning and tracking control of the 2-dof manipulator and verifies the feasibility and effectiveness of the technique through MATLAB simulation.

articleTitle: Load Frequency Control of Power Systems Under Cyber Attacks: A Memory-Based Event-Triggered Method
abstract: The load frequency control problem of multi-area power systems under external disturbances and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks is addressed in this paper. A cache module is introduced to design a memory-based event-triggered scheme based on state information and attack parameter, and the subsystems of the system during the dormant and active periods of DoS attack are established respectively. An input compensation strategy is adopted to obtain the exponential stabilization and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>performance criteria based on the Lyapunov method, and the co-design of event-triggering parameter and the controller gain is proposed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by an example of a three-region power system.

articleTitle: Relationship between the Long-Term Practice of Tai Chi Stance with Neural Patterns of the Brain: An Exploratory Study
abstract: Research has shown that practicing Tai Chi can alleviate brain tension and enhance the activity of the autonomic nervous system in the human body. However, there is limited research on the effects of Tai Chi Stance on brain function. This study aims to analyze the electroencephalogram (EEG) characteristics of long-term Tai Chi Zhuang practitioners and investigate the changes in brain dynamic neural patterns during different stages of Tai Chi Stance, together with the differences between long-term practitioners and a control group. In this study, we first analyzed the changes in EEG spectral characteristics during different stages of Tai Chi Stance practice of long-term practitioners. We found that the alpha (8–13 Hz) power significantly increased during the stance, indicating a state of deep relaxation during the Tai Chi practice. The experimental group also exhibited significant changes in brain functional network parameters in the alpha band during the stance, including increased clustering coefficient and global efficiency. Finally, inter-group differences in EEG characteristic parameters were analyzed between the experimental group and control group. The results showed significant differences in relative power and functional connectivity in the alpha band between the two groups, indicating that long-term Tai Chi Stance practice can effectively enhance brain network efficiency and improve information integration capabilities. This study provides scientific evidence for Tai Chi Stance training to enhance brain health.

articleTitle: Efficient Circuit Diagram Retrieval via Graph Representation
abstract: In the field of electronic engineering, the retrieval of circuit diagrams has become an area of considerable research interest. This is attributed to the critical role it plays in consulting legacy electronic designs and in the identification of design plagiarism. Existing image retrieval techniques, which are proficient in managing natural images, typically involve the conversion of images into feature vectors and retrieve similar images according to the closeness of these vectors. However, these methods encounter limitations when adapted to the more specialized and complex domain of circuit diagrams. This paper introduces an innovative approach to the retrieval of circuit diagrams through the use of a graph representation of these diagrams. This novel approach effectively transforms the retrieval task into a graph retrieval problem. The methodology proposed in this paper is comprised of two main components: A recognition algorithm for circuit diagrams designed to accurately extract the components and the topological structure of the circuit and a retrieval strategy based on graph similarity. This methodology is pioneering in its use of graph representation for circuit diagram retrieval, incorporating topological features that are often not considered by conventional image retrieval methods. The experimental results presented in this paper validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Design of a Nested Observer for Composite Disturbances Based on Characteristic Extraction
abstract: To address composite disturbances in the system, this paper proposes a disturbance rejection method. The considered disturbances include both regular and irregular components. First, by extracting the characteristics of the frequency components, a frequency compensation observer(FCO) is designed to fully utilize the disturbance characteristics, processing only the regular disturbances. Next, the remaining irregular components and the errors of the regular disturbances are estimated and compensated using a nonlinear extended state observer (NESO). In the proposed method, the multi-loops are independent of each other, which reduces the computational complexity to a large extend. The two types of observers form a nested structure, handling disturbances more targetedly, making the method more suitable for addressing composite disturbances in the system.Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through simulations.

articleTitle: Differentially Private Synthesis for Cooperative Output Regulation of Discrete-Time Linear Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: This work investigates the differentially private algorithm for the cooperative output regulation problem when the reference signal is constant. A distributed control strategy is developed that ensures individual privacy by adding random noises to the exchanged information. Moreover, a set of time-varying gains is formulated to ease the condition that the imposed noise must decrease exponentially to zero. Furthermore, a method is proposed to design the control gains to ensure that multi-agent systems maintain a specified differential privacy index. Lastly, a numerical example is presented to demonstrate the practical effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Automatic Pusher Robot Remote Monitoring System
abstract: In the traditional pasture, the manual way of pushing back the feed has the problems of low efficiency and large labour cost, and the introduction of automatic pusher robots can effectively improve this drawback. However, due to the complexity of the pasture environment, the problem of remote monitoring and operation of the automatic pusher robot is inconvenient. In order to address this problem, this paper designs and develops a remote monitoring system for the automatic pusher robot in the pasture, which realises the real-time monitoring of the position, speed, power and other operating states of the automatic pusher robot, as well as the remote control functions of the robot's working path selection, operation control and other remote control functions. Practical application tests show that the monitoring system can effectively manage multi-location and multi-user pusher robots, improve the efficiency of automatic pusher robots, reduce the cost, and increase the efficiency of the pasture.

articleTitle: Dynamic Learning from Neural PID Output-Feedback Control for a Lower Limb Exoskeleton Rehabilitation Robot
abstract: With the intensification of population aging and the increasing number of patients with lower limb dysfunction, the research and precise control of lower limb rehabilitation robots have become increasingly important. In this study, a sitting and lying lower limb exoskeleton robot model is developed based on the CoppeliaSim platform. For the nonlinear system of a two-degree-of-freedom single-leg robot with uncertainty, an improved PID control method based on deterministic learning is proposed. Under the condition of persistent excitation, this control method accurately identifies the unknown dynamic characteristics of the system by introducing a neural network, ensuring precise control of lower limb movements. Learning-based PID controllers are constructed using the gained knowledge to achieve fast, smooth tracking and greatly improve the safety of rehabilitation control. The results of simulation experiments show that the proposed control strategy in this paper is effective.

articleTitle: A Novel Fault Diagnosis Method for Multimode Hot Rolling Process Based on MGU and BLS
abstract: Owing to changes in raw materials, set points, external environment, and other factors. Hot rolling process (HRP) typically has multiple operating conditions. When the operating conditions change, the performance of the fault diagnosis model may deteriorate. Therefore, effective multimode fault diagnosis technology is an effective way to guarantee the safe operation of industrial systems, and it is also a research hotspot and difficulty in fault diagnosis technology. In this paper, we propose a novel fault diagnosis method for multimode HRP by integrating minimal gated unit (MGU) and broad Learning system (BLS). First, MGU is used to extract the dynamic features of process data. Then, the dynamic features are introduced to the BLS model for fault classification. A case study on the multimode HRP illustrates that the proposed method achieves superior fault diagnosis performance compared to traditional MGU and BLS.

articleTitle: Finite-Dimensional Observer-Based Model Predictive Controller for Heat Equation in Silicon Single Crystal Growth Process with Time Delay
abstract: The growth process of the Czochralski (CZ) sili-con single crystal (SSC) involves complex phase changes and interactions between multiple fields. Heat, as the fundamental driving force of crystal growth, plays a crucial role in SSC. The growth process of CZ SSC involves complex phase changes and interactions between multiple fields, resulting in large time delays in temperature control. This paper introduces a finite-dimensional control approach founded on the low-dimensional discreteness of output feedback. The spectral decomposition method is used to establish a Luenberger-type observer for a one-dimensional heat conduction distributed parameter system. Only measurable spatiotemporal outputs are used to design a feasible controller, which solves the problems of system instability caused by output time lag during crystal growth. The final experiment verifies the feasibility of the control design.

articleTitle: ChangeAD: Enhanced Remote Sensing Change Detection via Bi-Temporal Alignment and Differential Feature Integration
abstract: Remote sensing change detection (RSCD) aims to identify semantic changes in bi-temporal images, with broad applications in disaster assessment, urban expansion analysis, and other fields. With advancements in computer vision, deep learning-based methods have significantly improved the performance of RSCD tasks. However, existing approaches primarily focus on feature representation, overlooking the interaction between bi-temporal features, which leads to suboptimal performance when dealing with imaging condition disparities (such as seasonal changes, lighting variations, and image distortions). To address these limitations, we introduce ChangeAD, a novel framework that leverages Bi-temporal Alignment (BTA) to align bi-temporal features, mitigating false changes caused by imaging condition differences. We further integrate Differential Feature Integration (DFI) and Cross-level Feature Integration (CFI) modules to extract and integrate a differential feature pyramid. This approach utilizes the integrated differential feature maps, rich in semantic and edge contour information, to address the identification challenges posed by complex details and texture features in high-resolution images. Experimental evaluations on the LEVIR-CD and S2-Looking datasets demonstrate that ChangeAD achieves F1 scores of 78.6% and 83.6%, respectively, showcasing its effectiveness in handling the complexities of high-resolution remote sensing Images.

articleTitle: Transformer-based Diffusion Model for Single Image Deblurring
abstract: A Transformer-based diffusion model for single image deblurring is proposed in this paper, which combines diffusion model and transformer block. Specifically, the blurred image is first used as a condition to guide the diffusion model to reverse restore and generate deblurred clean background image. Secondly, a U-shape Spatially Gate Transformer Net for Noise Estimation(USGTN-NE) is proposed, which utilizes blurred image and noisy states to estimate the distribution of noise. Introducing Spatially Adaptive Feature Modulation(SAFM) into the network to capture multi-scale and global information, combined with gate mechanisms to enhance the network's noise prediction capability. The experimental results show that the PSNR index and SSIM index of our proposal are higher than those of other competitors. The subjective quality has also been improved, and the restored images are visually closer to the real situation.

articleTitle: Research on UAV-Assisted Computation Offloading Based on PER-SAC
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are becoming more popular in Mobile Edge Computing (MEC). However, UAVs face problems such as high task processing delay, high energy consumption, and the lack of fairness in service during the service process. This paper investigates a UAV-assisted mobile edge computing system which uses the reinforcement learning algorithm to minimize the task processing delay and the energy consumption of the UAV while maximizing the fairness of the user service. Firstly, a Markov decision process is formulated for this system. Then, the SAC algorithm is improved by employing the prioritized experience replay method based on instantaneous rewards and TD errors, and the PER-SAC algorithm is employed to tackle this problem. The simulation demonstrate that the proposed algorithm converges rapidly and outperforms other algorithms.

articleTitle: Dolphin 1 Ship Trajectory Prediction based on Ivy-multi-output Least Squares Support Vector Regression
abstract: Trajectory prediction for ships plays a crucial role in intelligent ship route planning and collision avoidance. The Dolphin 1 ship is the first digital twin intelligent ship of China and is developed by Harbin engineering university. To design a trajectory prediction model for the Dolphin 1 ship, this paper employs the multi-output least squares support vector regression (MLSSVR) method. The Ivy algorithm is also used to find the optimal hyper-parameters for MLSSVR. The performance of the established trajectory prediction model is validated using real-measured trajectory data. The experimental results demonstrate the generalizability and prediction accuracy of MLSSVR.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Sparrow Search Algorithm and CNN-BiLSTM Neural Network for Predicting Air Conditioning Cooling Load*
abstract: It is difficult to predict air conditioning load accurately because of the nonlinear and time-varying characteristics of air conditioning load data. In this paper, a hybrid enhanced sparrow search algorithm (SSA) called HESSA was proposed, which integrated tent chaotic map, mirror reverse learning, butterfly optimization algorithm (BOA) and Cauchy mutation strategy, aiming to improve the global search capability and convergence speed. The HESSA-CNN-BiLSTM model was obtained by optimizing the hyperparameters of the CNN-BiLSTM (convolutional neural network combined with bidirectional long short-term memory neural network) model with HESSA. The experimental results indicated that, in the air conditioning cooling load prediction for different types of buildings in a specific area of Shandong Province, the RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and R2 of the HESSA-CNN-BiLSTM model were as follows: 0.04RT, 0.03RT, 0.71%, and 0.99 for office building; 0.014RT, 0.0053RT, 0.74%, and 0.98 for commercial building. Compared with the CNN-BiLSTM model and the BiLSTM model, the proposed HESSA-CNN-BiLSTM model exhibited higher prediction accuracy and generalization capability.

Author Keywords: prediction of air conditioning cooling load

articleTitle: MAS-Based Decentralized Coordinated Control Strategy for Multiple Renewable Energy Sources
abstract: This paper suggests a multi-agent system (MAS)-based distributed coordinated control strategy for improving the grid voltage. Specifically, in the lower layer, it is devised as a decentralized control with dual-loop control through inverters for each renewable energy source, involving droop control-based outer-loop power controller and fractional order proportionalintegral-derivative (FOPID)-based inner-loop current and voltage controllers. In the upper layer, it is aiming at achieving proportional power sharing and voltage consensus among all ERs by distributed coordinated control method. For this control manner, each coordinated control unit only requires system information about itself and neighbouring units. Simulation results prove the validity of the suggested strategy.

articleTitle: Optimal Traffic-Power Flow of Transportation-Microgrid Coupled System Based on Spatiotemporal Coupling
abstract: The growing adoption of electric vehicles and dynamic wireless charging has strengthened the spatiotemporal interconnection between the transportation network (TN) and the microgrid (MG). This paper presents an optimal traffic-power flow (OTPF) model for the transportation-microgrid coupled system (TMCS) to enhance the coordination of its operations. The OTPF model is transformed into bi-level programming, with the optimal power flow model of MGs at the upper level and the dynamic traffic assignment model of the TN at the lower level. The upper level is a mixed-integer second-order cone programming, while the lower level is formulated as a dynamic user equilibrium. A fixed-point algorithm is developed to tackle this bi-level programming. Case studies show that the OTPF model of the TMCS can be efficiently solved to capture the spatiotemporal variations of traffic flow and power flow.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Enhanced Anomaly Localization for Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: Cybersecurity incidents such as network attacks can trigger anomalies in industrial cyber-physical systems (ICPS), leading to disastrous consequences. Accurate localization of these anomalies help in execution of precise security response measures, preventing further escalation and spread of the impact. This paper proposes a digital twin-enhanced anomaly localization (DTEAL) approach for ICPS. This DTEAL approach includes three interconnected modules: a digital twin model and a prediction compensation module, as well as an anomaly state localization module. The first module utilizes a digital twin model to predict the state of the ICPS processes and generate extended space states. Next, the prediction compensation module combines the extended data to compensate for deviations. The final state prediction results are then used to locate the anomaly state. Experimental studies conducted on a petrochemical fractionation unit simulation testbed demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Improved Hyperbolic Sine and Cosine Optimizer that Fuses Golden Sine Algorithm and Tent Chaos Mapping
abstract: In view of the problems of the Sinh Cosh Optimizer (SCHO), such as uneven initial position, slow convergence and poor search accuracy, This paper presents an improved SCHO that combines the Golden Sine Algorithm(Gold-SA) and the Tent chaotic mapping (GTSCHO). First, the Tent chaotic mapping was used to replace the traditional random number initialization of the population, which improved the diversity of the population. Then, the Golden sine algorithm is added to the position updating process, which makes the algorithm's search and development have a better balance, and the optimization accuracy is improved. Through 13 benchmark test functions, the simulation and comparison test results show that: Compared with SCHO, the improved GTSCHO has better convergence speed, searching ability and stability.

articleTitle: Research on SMC - ADRC Strategy of Dual Three-Phase PMSM
abstract: A dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) model using vector control based on a Sliding Mode Control-Active Disturbance Rejection Control (SMC-ADRC) strategy is constructed and simulated according to its mathematical model in the d-q-axis coordinate system. Simulation results demonstrate that the dual-loop SMCADRC control method significantly outperforms traditional PI control and standalone ADRC strategies in several key areas, such as improved tracking performance, faster response speed and enhanced anti-Interference capability, reducing the impact of noise or load changes on motor performance.

articleTitle: Robust Model Predictive Control with Predefined Performance for Spacecraft Rendezvous
abstract: Safety is paramount for the rendezvous mission of spacecraft. A key quantitative indicator of safety is achieving zero overshoot control during the rendezvous. This paper proposes a model predictive control (MPC) method with performance constraints. These performance constraints are represented as state constraints within the MPC optimization problem. The boundaries forming these constraints are exponentially convergent, time-varying functions, theoretically ensuring zero over-shoot in the system output. Additionally, this paper introduces a function-adaptive law to estimate and compensate for unknown disturbances in the aerospace environment, thereby enhancing the control accuracy of spacecraft rendezvous. The paper provides a theoretical analysis of the recursive feasibility and stability of the designed MPC and verifies the controller's effectiveness through a set of simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Estimation Using Optimized Extension Based Multiple Conversion Approach with Generalized Conversion for Target Tracking
abstract: For estimation, minimum mean square error is one of the most widely accepted criteria. The optimal MMSE estimate is the posterior mean. For linear Gaussian systems, the posterior mean can be calculated easily. For nonlinear problems, it is hard to be obtained, although the posterior distribution can be solved by the joint distribution of the estimand and its measurement. Aim at this, the multiple conversion approach (MCA) uses several predesigned hypothesized distributions to match the true joint distribution. To match the truth better, the recently proposed optimized conversion extension (OCE) approach introduces one more distribution into the MCA. It has also proven that the MCA using the OCE outperforms the original one. However, practical nonlinear estimation problems are diverse. For a nonlinear problem, obtaining such an estimator which outperforms the existing estimators is hard. In this paper, considering the effectiveness of the recently proposed generalized conversion based filter (GCF) for conversions with high dimensions, we introduce it within the OCE framework. It is proven that the obtained new estimator called OCE-G can outperform the MCA using the original OCE and match the truth more sufficiently. Finally, a filtering algorithm using the OCE-G based on the interacting multiple conversion is proposed for dynamic problems. Compared with several popular nonlinear filters, a bearing-only filtering problem is used and simulated to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach and algorithm.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control for Nonlinear Singularly Perturbed System Based on Linearization Method
abstract: A new model predictive control design method based on state feedback linearization is proposed for a class of nonlinear singularly perturbed system. Firstly, the system is decomposed into slow subsystem and fast subsystem by singularly perturbed theory. Secondly, the decomposed system is transformed into a linear system by feedback linearization. Then the model predictive controller is derived by predictive control theory, such that the quadratic performance index achieved minimum value. This controller design method selects different quadratic performance indicators for fast and slow subsystems respectively and avoids solving complex nonlinear equations. Finally, simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method and the states of the closed-loop system are convergent.

articleTitle: Research on UAV Path Planning Based on Particle Swarm Optimization and Soft Actor-Critic
abstract: This study proposes a groundbreaking path planning method in UAV path planning in complex 3D environment, I-PSO-SAC, which seamlessly integrates Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) reinforcement learning algorithm to address these intricate challenges. The innovative approach leverages PSO-SAC to initially generate feasible paths, followed by advanced interpolation sampling techniques to refine and optimize the path quality. Experimental results show that I-PSO-SAC improves the convergence speed by 42.57% compared to the traditional SAC algorithm in static scenarios and 51.01% in dynamic scenarios. In addition, the method significantly improves the smoothness of paths, outperforming other deep reinforcement learning algorithms.

articleTitle: A Simulation Research Method for Data Injection Attacks on DC Microgrids
abstract: By using Typhoon HIL simulator, a simulation research method of data injection attack against secondary control DC microgrid is established, which reveals the important influence of the attack function on the effectiveness and covertness of the attack. Firstly, a decentralized four-node DC microgrid system using TCP/IP Modbus protocol for communication is built in Typhoon HIL simulator, then, a microgrid security testing experimental platform based on the man-in-the-middle attack as a network attack method is built in Kali Linux system, which can carry out timed single-and multi-links data injection attacks and replay attack on the above four-node DC microgrid. The paper designs a variety of data injection attack schemes to study the impact of data injection attacks on voltage and current control in this DC microgrid, including single-link attack, multi-link composite attack, and replay attack using different attack functions. By controlling the main parameters of the attack function, the amplitude of the fluctuation of the output voltage generated by the attack can be controlled, which can produce a more covert and effective attack effect.

articleTitle: A Method for Establishing a “Life-Like Health Check Quantification System” Based on a Multi-Task State GNC Subsystem with Identical Configuration
abstract: The health check system for living organisms assesses the overall health status of an organism by independently diagnosing key indicators of its multi-functional organs and finally synthesizing these diagnoses into a comprehensive health value. The GNC subsystem (Guidance, Navigation, and Control subsystem) serves as the core of satellite platform and mission control, incorporating various attitude sensors, orbit measurers, attitude control actuators, and orbit control actuators. Together with GNC software algorithms for attitude, orbit, navigation, and guidance functions, these components are orchestrated by the on-board computer, the “brain” of the system, to accomplish various on-orbit control tasks. The operational status of both hardware configurations and software functions collectively affects the overall health of the GNC subsystem. This paper proposes a method for constructing a “life-like health check quantification system” tailored for GNC subsystems with identical hardware configurations and multi-task capabilities. The method involves decomposing the GNC subsystem into “organ-like” modules, conducting independent diagnoses on each module, and finally deriving an overall health score for the entire subsystem using a priori health quantification algorithms. This health check system holds promising applications for the on-orbit maintenance of formation-flying satellite constellations equipped with GNC systems of similar configurations and multi-task states [1] [2].

articleTitle: An Enhanced Path Tracking Control Method for Unmanned Surface Vehicles Using Combined Reinforcement Learning DDPG Algorithm and MPC
abstract: To address the problem of path tracking control for the USVs in highly dynamic environments, we propose a trajectory tracking control algorithm based on DDPG and MPC. DDPG's Actor network generates preliminary control actions, optimized by MPC for final control. LSTM networks process sequence data for Actor and Critic networks. Future state predictions are stored in a “Prediction Pool” to enhance Critic training and accelerate convergence. The outcome of the simulations demonstrates that the introduced algorithmic approach exhibits efficient convergence in terms of path-tracking precision, significantly reducing path error and heading error, demonstrating considerable potential for practical applications.

articleTitle: High Intensity and Uniform Magnetic Field Sensor for Trenchless Underground Cable Detection
abstract: To solve the problems of insufficient magnetic field density and uneven magnetic field distribution when trenchless detection of underground cables is performed. This paper designs a high intensity and uniform magnetic field sensor for trenchless underground cable detection, which involves high-precision excitation schemes and interference-resistant sensor physical structures. The excitation scheme is a low-frequency triangular wave, and the physical structure of the sensor is a round coil sensor. This paper compares the magnetic field excitation capabilities of round, rectangular, and diamond-shaped coils. Simulation results show that the round coil produce stronger magnetic field strength at the same location. To quantify the uniformity of the magnetic field, this paper proposes three evaluation metrics for different spatial locations. To solve the problem of non-uniform magnetic field strength, this paper tests five different excitation signals for each of the three coils. The experimental results show that the round coil with low-frequency triangular wave excitation produces a high magnetic field strength and better uniformity.

articleTitle: Predefined-Time Synchronization for Variable-Order Fractional Chaotic Systems via Smooth Control
abstract: This brief proposes a predefined-time synchronization smooth controller for a class of variable-order fractional chaotic systems (VOFCS) with uncertainties and external disturbances. Firstly, a novel predefined-time strategy is designed, which will not only guarantee the upper-bound time function independent of initial values of the system but also be more explicit than the conventional upper-bound time function. Then, a smooth controller is proposed, which can effectively restrict the chattering phenomenon compared with conventional control methods. Furthermore, by using the generalized Lyapunov stability criterion, a condition for the stabilization of the VOFCS under the predefined-time smooth control is established. Finally, two different chaotic systems are taken to illustrate that the VOFCS can be synchronized in predefined-time based on smooth control, thus better avoiding chattering and enhancing the synchronization convergence rate of the VOFCS. The proposed control strategy can be applied to variable-order chaotic systems, commensurate and incommensurate systems.

articleTitle: Compressed CNN for Atrial Fibrillation Detection on Wearable Devices
abstract: Monitoring patients' electrocardiograms (ECG) with smart wearable devices for real-time detection of atrial fibrillation (AF) can significantly improve healthcare outcomes. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are highly effective in detecting such anomalous heartbeats, yet their high computational complexity poses challenges for deployment on resource-constrained platforms. In this work, we present an efficient approach to deploying lightweight CNN-based AF detection models on wearable devices. We developed an advanced classification net-work based on MobileNetV2, trained and validated on the ECG dataset from the Intelligent Embedded System Design Contest at ICMC. To improve model generalization, we applied GAN-based data augmentation techniques. Additionally, to optimize the model's size, we employed a combined CNN compression approach that incorporates Dependency Graph Pruning and Quantization-Aware Training. Inference experiments conducted on the Loongson 2K0500 development board highlighted the superior performance of our approach. The proposed method enabled real-time inference with a low latency of 9.67 ms and a compact model size of 41.1 KB, while maintaining a high accuracy of 96.52 %. These results demonstrate that our CNN compression scheme is exceptionally well-suited for deploying AF detection models on resource-constraint wearable devices.

articleTitle: Enhancing Privacy in Microgrid Operations: A State Decomposition Approach for Consensus-Based Distributed Economic Dispatch over Directed Networks
abstract: The dual objectives of privacy protection and optimization scheduling are of paramount importance in economic dispatch for smart microgrids. This study presents a privacy-preserving consensus algorithm that employs state decomposition to tackle the privacy leakage challenges associated with distributed economic dispatch in smart microgrids. By decomposing state variables into internal and external sub-states, the algorithm selectively transmits partial data, effectively preventing information leakage. Compared with traditional methods such as noise injection and encryption, the proposed algorithm offers lower computational complexity while maintaining rapid convergence. Privacy analysis demonstrates the robustness of the algorithm against both internal and external eavesdroppers, ensuring the security of sensitive information. The results from numerical simulations affirm the algorithm's efficacy. This approach is applicable to ED problems in smart microgrids with privacy protection requirements, providing a novel solution for secure and efficient microgrid operation.

articleTitle: Dynamic Hybrid Temporal Attention With Attention on Attention for the Capacity Vehicle Routing Problem
abstract: With the increasing utilization of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) in recent studies to solve vehicle routing problem, it has been observed that these models mainly adopt an encoder and decoder structure. However, the time and space features embedded in encoder and decoder are not fully considered. To address these limitations, we propose a dynamic hybrid temporal attention (DHTA) model that incorporates an attention on attention (AOA) mechanism to tackle the capacity vehicle routing problem. A noted feature of DHTA is its utilization of a multidimensional attention mechanism based on AOA within encoder, along with a temporal pointer decoder that dynamically focus on the decision-making information. Experimental results demonstrate that our model exhibits superior performance compared to state-of-the-art DRL-based models and several traditional heuristic algorithms.

articleTitle: Early Indoor Fire Warning Algorithm Based on INRBO-XGBoost and Fuzzy Inference
abstract: Given the current limitations of computer vision technology in detecting early smoldering fires and the challenges posed by traditional single chemical sensors in distinguishing alarms amidst disturbances, we propose a multi-sensor fusion fire warning algorithm. This algorithm integrates an improved Newton-Raphson Based Optimizer (INRBO) with an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm and fuzzy inference theory. Initially, the mix opposition-based learning (MOBL) method is employed to enhance the NRBO algorithm, increasing population diversity and avoiding local optima. The improved NRBO optimizer is then used for hyperparameter tuning of the XGBoost algorithm, accelerating model convergence and improving prediction accuracy. Finally, fuzzy inference theory is applied to integrate the predicted fire probabilities, yielding optimal control decisions. Compared to the PSO-XGBoost, XGBoost, and GA-BP models, the root mean square error (RMSE) of the INRBO-XGBoost model is reduced by 24.43%, 39.10%, and 32.95%, respectively. The warning accuracy for various types and regions of fires, including plastic smoldering fires, electronic equipment smoldering fires, and cotton fabric smoldering fires, exceeds 99.11%.

articleTitle: Traffic Sign Detection Based on Improved YOLOv5-S
abstract: This paper proposes an improved YOLOv5-S traffic sign detection model to address the issues of missed and false detections in existing traffic sign detection models in complex backgrounds. Firstly, a small-sized detection layer was added to enhance the model's utilization of detailed shallow feature information; Secondly, a C3-Res2Block module that integrates multi-scale information is proposed to improve the network's multi-scale perception ability and better adapt to targets and scenes of different sizes, thereby improving recognition accuracy and robustness; Once again, introduce the CBMA attention mechanism to focus on key information and enhance the feature expression ability of traffic signs; Finally, to address the challenge of localizing small targets in loss calculation, the NWD(Normalized Wasserstein Distance) loss function was introduced. Experiments confirm the improved model's efficacy in mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95, it achieved 85.2% and 64.0% respectively, while achieving a detection speed of up to 108FPS, meeting the real-time and reliable detection requirements.

articleTitle: Contrastive Clustering Learning for Few-shot Image Classification
abstract: The objective of Unsupervised Few-Shot Learning (UFSL) is to obtain high-level representations using a limited amount of unlabeled data. However, in the actual process of feature extraction, the model merely focuses on a single focal point, failing to adequately exploit the rich information within the samples. In order to solve this issue, we propose a framework of Multi-Focal Semantic Access (MFSA). Our approach, during the training process, leverages both contrastive learning and deep clustering perspectives to better identify intra-instance and inter-instance semantic disparities, thus capturing multiple focal points of the samples. Specifically, contrastive learning generates instance-level prototypes to emphasize inter-instance differences, thereby enhancing the generalization capability of representations. Deep clustering uses random partitions to dynamically generate powerful clustering-level prototypes to focus on intra-instance differences, effectively mitigating the loss of intra-instance semantic information. Through the joint action of contrastive learning and deep clustering, MFSA effectively enhances the ability of extracting comprehensive representations for fuzzy scene tasks. Extensive experiments conducted on the miniImageNet dataset have demonstrated the superiority of MFSA. This is because, by focusing on multiple focal point of images to extract comprehensive representations, can effectively classify images in complex scenes.

articleTitle: Anorectal Surgery Navigation System Based on Bursa Seven-Parameter Model and Optical Mixed Reality
abstract: In traditional closed anorectal surgery, surgeons first need to locate the position of the anal point on the patient's body using information provided by the imaging screen. Subsequently, they make an incision along the anal margin, and insert surgical forceps into the anal muscles to locate the blind end of the rectum, thus performing anorectoplasty. The difficulty of this procedure lies in the fact that surgeons need to identify the anal point and anal margin of the patient through MRI images before surgery, then construct an anal canal during the surgery. In order to optimize these process, this paper proposes a closed anorectal surgery navigation system based on the Bursa seven-parameter model and optical mixed reality. The system establishes a spatial mapping relationship between virtual models and real objects to achieve virtual-to-real registration and assist surgeons accurately performing closed anorectal surgery.

articleTitle: The Improvement of Data Selection Method in Data-Driven Model Predictive Control of Uncertain Systems
abstract: Data quality is pivotal for the performance of data-driven model predictive control systems. While traditional data processing methods, such as cleaning and enrichment, are necessary, they do not always improve the controller performance. To tackle this problem, this paper introduces a new data selection method specifically designed for data-driven model predictive control. It includes a controller performance evaluation approach that assesses the quality of the current data, enabling the controller to select a set of informative data elements that enhance its performance. Additionally, a sliding window mechanism is implemented to compare current data against historical data, preventing the loss of significant patterns or trends. A simulation example illustrates the effectiveness of the proposed data selection method.

articleTitle: Deceptive Pollination Process - Modeling Based on Individual Agents
abstract: This study explores the interactions between deceptive plants and pollinators using Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) to overcome the limitations of traditional mathematical models. By treating plants and pollinators as independent agents with defined behaviors and incorporating deep reinforcement learning, agents adapt to environmental changes and optimize strategies. Simulated experiments reveal the dynamic evolution of these interactions, highlighting competition and cooperation patterns. The findings show that ABM effectively simulates the interactions between deceptive plants and pollinators, providing valuable insights and analytical tools for understanding complex ecological interactions and evolution.

articleTitle: Adaptive Neural Network Algorithm with Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Neural network algorithm (NNA) is a new type of population-based meta-heuristic algorithm, which is inspired by artificial neural networks. NNA is a result of the deep integration of artificial neural networks and metaheuristic algorithms. Benefiting from the unique structure of artificial neural networks, NNA shows excellent optimization performance. However, NNA has the disadvantages of slow convergence speed and easy trapping in local optimal solutions when solving complex multimodal optimization problems. To enhance the global search ability of NNA and expand the application of artificial neural networks in the field of metaheuristic algorithms, this paper proposes a new variant of NNA, namely adaptive neural network algorithm with reinforcement learning (ANNA). The core components of ANNA are the designed bias factor based on reinforcement learning and multiple learning transfer mechanism. To investigate the performance of ANNA, ANNA is employed to solve the challenging CEC 2014 test suite. Experimental results prove the validity of the improved strategies and excellent performance of ANNA in solving complex multi-modal optimization problems.

articleTitle: M/M/c Queueing Model with Variable Matching Rate
abstract: In recent years, with the development of the service industry, the queuing problem of improving the effectiveness of resource allocation to reduce the waiting time of customers has become more prominent. Existing researches mainly focus on the fixed matching rate model, and lack the in-depth exploration of the variable matching rate in real service scenarios. This paper constructs an M/M/c model of variable matching rate, considering the impact of various factors on the customer arrival rate and service rate in practical service contexts. Innovatively, we propose a variable matching rate formula applicable when the number of customers exceeds the number of service stations, addressing the gaps in the current research. By constructing a two-dimensional Markov quasi-birth-and-death process and generator matrix, it establishes an infinite-dimensional steady-state probability equation to calculate system performance metrics. Finally, a reasonable range of matching rates is determined by simulation, and system metrics are compared between fixed and variable matching rate M/M/c models.

articleTitle: A Modified Cellular Automata Model for Crowd Evacuation Considering Pedestrian Fallen and Helping Behavior
abstract: The phenomenon of falls occurs from time to time during the evacuation process, and once a fall occurs, it is very easy for casualties to occur. Therefore, the cause of pedestrian falls is analyzed from the angle of micromechanics, the mechanism of pedestrian falls is established, and the effect of falls on pedestrian evacuation is discussed. Based on the cellular automaton, a pedestrian evacuation model is established which considers the static field, dynamic field, and wall field. According to the differences between people, the passers-by are divided into two categories: enthusiastic and indifferent. The former helps fallen pedestrians, the latter is indifferent to fallen pedestrians. The impact of helping behavior and various pedestrian personalities on evacuation is studied. The distinction between pedestrians fleeing along and away from the wall is also explored. The findings indicate that helping behavior can prevent falls in a row. People who are impatient or apathetic will add to the congestion and have a negative impact on evacuation efficiency. The best method of evacuation is for the crowd to move evenly through the corridors.

articleTitle: CDMG:Combing DeBERTa-v2 Model with Globalpointer for Chinese Text Level Event Extraction
abstract: Extracting event information from professional texts is a prerequisite for intelligence decision-making system or intelligence personnel to conduct intelligence analysis and decision-making. In the past, event extraction from professional texts mainly relied on human reading and event extraction. Since entering the era of big data, millions of professional texts of interest to intelligence personnel are generated every day. And it's basically impossible to extract information about events from these texts by relying on people alone. In this case. We first use the pre-trained Chinese DeBERTa-v2 model for text coding and word segmentation. Secondly, gobalpointer technology is used to predict and extract event arguments, and Adam optimizer is used for optimization. Finally, a Chinese text level event extraction framework for the professional field is constructed by dividing argument into events through complete subgraph recognition technology. In this way, the event information of the text in the professional field can be extracted, so as to improve the application efficiency of text intelligence in the professional field and promote the application of artificial intelligence technology in the professional intelligence field.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Fixed-Time Tracking for Multi-Agent Systems with Directed Topologies and Communication Noises
abstract: This paper is concentrated on the study of fixed-time consensus problem of nonlinear multi-agent systems (NMASs) with stochastic disturbance under directed topologies. First, a novel event-triggered control (ETC) protocol is designed to realize the fixed-time consensus (FTC) of NMASs with stochastic disturbance. Compared with the existing results, the proposed ETC schemes can make NMASs with communication noises achieve the consensus tracking within a fixed time, is applicable for the detail-balanced directed, and is capable of requiring only intermittent communication. Then, some sufficient conditions are presented to guarantee the FTC. In addition, it is proved that no Zeno behavior exhibits by the ETC control protocols. Finally, a simulation case is supplied to validate the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Optimizing Bounding Box Regression in Complex Backgrounds
abstract: In the context of electrical power operation sites, the automated and accurate detection of whether workers are properly equipped with safety gear, such as safety clothing, helmets, and safety ropes for high-altitude operations, is crucial for ensuring the safety of personnel. Traditional object detection models often struggle to accurately identify these critical pieces of safety equipment in complex environments, due to variable object sizes, overlapping objects, and substantial background noise. To specifically address these challenges, we propose a novel loss function-Enhanced Alignment Intersection over Union (EAIoU) loss. This loss function is designed to enhance the model's ability to discriminate between closely spaced and overlapping safety gear in real-time, significantly improving robustness against scale variations and complex backgrounds. In experiments based on the YOLOv8s architecture, our model achieved a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 92.1 % on a dataset specific to electrical power operations, markedly outperforming traditional IoU loss functions. Additionally, EAIoU demonstrated improved performance on the COCO dataset, indicating its generalization capability across various complex scenarios. This research not only enhances the accuracy and real-time performance of safety equipment detection at electric power operation sites but also opens new avenues for advanced object detection technology in complex, multi-object environments.

articleTitle: 4D-CRNN Model of EEG Motor Imagery with Attention Module
abstract: EEG signals are often used to classify motor imagery in the field of brain-computer interface research. Deep learning is used in EEG signal classification to focus on extracting features, selecting features, and classifying them. Taking the frequency, spatial and temporal features of the signal into account at the same time, in the 4D-CRNN model, motor imagery can be classified from EEG signals based on its characteristics. The model achieved good results in this area. As a part of the experiment, attention module has been introduced into the model, resulting in a partially improved model effect.

articleTitle: Global-Local Adaptive Attention-Based U-Net for Single Image Deblurring
abstract: Image deblurring is a classical ill-posed problem aimed at recovering a clear image from a blurred one. The recent application of Transformers to image restoration tasks has significantly improved performance, thanks to their powerful long-range dependency modeling capabilities. However, the high computational cost of self-attention mechanisms limits their practical use. Additionally, the training cost for Transformer models is considerable. To address the issues of high computational cost and training cost, this paper proposes a novel Global Local Attention (GLA) mechanism that combines global and local adaptive attention. The mechanism uses 1D adaptive pooling operations to capture global context information, while fixed-size 1D pooling with different kernel sizes (7 and 11) is used to capture local details, effectively addressing both long-range dependencies and fine-grained information. Furthermore, a larger receptive field is crucial for effective image deblurring. To this end, we introduce a Feature Enhancement Module (FEM) with an expansive convolutional kernel size that serves as a bottleneck layer to further improve recovery quality. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed model achieves competitive performance on several benchmark datasets, advancing the field of image restoration.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Based Tool Wear State Recognition with Domain-Integrated Multi-Residual Network
abstract: Cutting tools are vital in industry, but they wear out with use and will affect the quality of the workpiece if not replaced in a timely manner, so determining the tool's wear status is very important to the cutting process. Current wear state identification models rely on large, reliable datasets, which are challenging in the real world. This study presents an approach using digital twins and domain adaptation. The digital twin model generates sufficient simulated data, supported by a domain-integrated multi-residual network (DIMRN), to extract key wear features from real and simulated data. Mapping these features through fully connected layers allows accurate tool wear state identification. The results confirm effective wear state identification and enhance digital decision-making in smart manufacturing.

articleTitle: Model-Based Remaining Useful Life Prediction of PEMFC Using EMD and ARIMA
abstract: The remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is vital to the heath management of Proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC). However, it is challenging for RUL prediction due to the multiple complex factors such as PEM degradation, bipolar corrosion or diffusion layer collapse etc. In this paper, a model-based RUL prediction method is proposed with particle filter (PF), empirical mode decomposition (EMD) and ARIMA. First, a semi-empirical model is used as the state equation for the PF. The parameters of the semi-empirical model are determined based on the polarization curves of the PEMFC with the PSO. For the acquisition of observation values of the PF, the voltage curves of stacks are decomposed by EMD, and then ARIMA is used to predict intrinsic mode functions (IMFs). The PF makes iterative prediction from the starting point to obtain the RUL of the PEMFC. The simulation results show that the proposed method has an improved prediction accuracy with the RUL prediction errors as low as 1.54%.

articleTitle: Research on Recognition and Control Technology of Coal Mine Inclined Shaft Running Cars
abstract: The phenomenon of coal mine running cars is a common type of accident in inclined shaft transportation. Early prediction and active control of running cars are of utmost importance in improving the level of running car protection. This article applies a radar system to the recognition of inclined shaft running cars, obtaining real-time mining and industrial information, automatically detecting whether the locomotive has stall, overspeed and other situations, and assisting the running car protection device to intercept it in the first time. The signal-to-noise ratio of the three target echoes measured by the radar is not less than 20dB, and the filtering algorithm can meet the speed measurement requirements, verifying the feasibility of the running car recognition method. In the aspect of active control, matrix based interlocking control strategy is adopted, and intuitive control strategy is obtained by using the multi section division method of running lines, which simplifies the interlocking logic relationship, realizes the intelligent dispatching of all track trains, and verifies the feasibility and progressiveness of the control of rail transport vehicles.

articleTitle: Time-varying Formation Control for Multiple Omni-WMRs Based on ROS
abstract: The present study introduces a time-varying formation control algorithm designed for multiple omni-directional mobile robots (Omni-WMRs). The algorithm employs a leader-follower strategy, which tackles the challenge of time-varying consistency in multi-robot formation control within complex environments by devising a communication topology and an error control method that ensure consistency. To validate this algorithm, a multi-robot experimental platform based on ROS was designed and constructed, utilizing its modularity and scalability to facilitate dynamic adjustments and efficient cooperation within the multi-robot system. Experimental results show that the control algorithm and experimental platform can achieve precise target trajectory tracking and flexible formation control in complex environments, maintaining consistency errors within acceptable ranges, and demonstrating efficiency and stability in practical applications.

articleTitle: Vibration Isolation and Control of Variable Stiffness Fast Steering Mirror Based on Extended State Observer and Sliding Mode Control
abstract: Fast steering mirror (FSM) play a crucial role in the precise control of light beams in electro-optical tracking systems. When FSMs are mounted on vehicular motion platforms, conventional passive isolation systems often fail to meet the stringent isolation requirements of FSM. To address this issue, this paper proposes a method that combines the advantages of passive isolation and active control to enhance the isolation and control performance of FSM. The proposed approach employs a variable stiffness negative stiffness mechanism (NSM) to reduce the stiffness of the FSM, thereby improving isolation performance. An extended state observer (ESO) is used to observe and compensate for total disturbances, and a sliding mode controller (SMC) is designed to enhance the rapidity of the FSM's response and improve disturbance rejection characteristics. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method effectively suppresses disturbances under road step disturbances. The addition of NSM enhances the vibration isolation and control performance of FSM, while the inclusion of ESO further improves the disturbance rejection capability of FSM.

articleTitle: EEG Based Sleep Staging Analysis of BECTS Subjects
abstract: Spike-wave index (SWI) in electroencephalograms (EEGs) of different sleep stages is an important criterion for the diagnosis and prognosis evaluation of benign childhood epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (BECTS). Accurate sleep staging thus becomes a prerequisite for statistical SWI analysis in different sleep stages of BECTS subjects. In this study, a novel BECTS sleep staging method based on multi-domain EEG features and statistical significance analysis has been developed. Particularly, 29 features from single-channel signal are taken for EEG characterization and statistical methods are adopted to describe the mechanisms underlying the variation in sleep in different types of subjects. Analysis on 11 BECTS and 7 normal subjects reveals that the proposed method can achieve 86 % and 86.7% F1 score, 87.2% and 92.7% kappa for BECTS and normal subjects, respectively.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Observer-Based Adaptive Fuzzy Control of Uncertain Multi-agent Systems
abstract: This study provides an observer-based event-triggered adaptive fuzzy backstepping control technique aimed at achieving a leader-following consensus consensus for uncertain second-order multi-agent systems (MASs). Fuzzy logic systems are utilized to approximate unknown nonlinear functions, and state observers utilized are to estimate unavailable states. More-over, the feasibility of the proposed event-triggered mechanism with relative threshold is verified in order to reduce transmission frequency while simultaneously ensuring that tracking error converges to a small neighborhood near zero. Ultimately, simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the developed controller.

articleTitle: Forecasting Spring Frost Frequency Based on Time Series Decomposition Model and Machine Learning
abstract: Spring frost can significantly impact agriculture. Predicting the occurrence frequency of spring frosts is crucial for reducing agricultural economic losses and ensuring food security. To reduce noise interference and improve prediction accuracy, we propose a time series decomposition model to extract the trend features of spring frost frequencies in the Northern Hemisphere, the primary agriculture planting region in the world, from 1948 to 2016. Based on the extracted trend features, we utilized random forest and deep neural network models to forecast future occurrence frequencies of spring frost in the Northern Hemisphere. The results show that spring frost frequencies will continue to increase in some Northern Hemisphere regions in the future.

articleTitle: Human Intention Based Fuzzy Variable Admittance Control for a Walking Aid
abstract: With the aging of society, walking aids have increasingly attracted attention. Achieving compliant interaction between humans and walking aids plays a crucial role in this context. Accordingly, this paper proposes a novel human intention-based fuzzy variable admittance control strategy. The controller uses human-robot interaction (HRI) force and velocity as fuzzy control inputs, adaptively adjusting the parameters of the admittance model to match different movement phases. By effectively estimating human intention, the controller adjusts the walking aid's speed to synchronize with the user's movements, reducing horizontal interaction forces and operator effort, thereby enhancing the compliance and smoothness of HRI. The controller's effectiveness and its practicality in assisting human ambulation have been validated through experiments.

articleTitle: Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Based on Patch-Transformer Model
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power generation occupies an increasing proportion in the new energy power generation system. Accurate prediction of PV power is crucial for ensuring the stable operation of the power grid and enhancing the reliability of dispatch operations. However, traditional neural network models perform poorly in predicting the fluctuations in PV power out, leading to an inability to effectively anticipate and manage instability in the power grid. This paper introduces a PV power prediction model based on the innovative Patch-Transformer architecture. By integrating Patch and Transformer algorithms, the model significantly enhances scalability, perception, and generalization capabilities. The performance of model has been rigorously evaluated in spring, summer, autumn, and winter, with the prediction accuracies for PV power generation over the next seven days being 0.9995, 0.9994, 0.9996, and 0.9986, respectively. These results underscore the model's robustness and its potential to significantly improve power prediction in the renewable energy sector, promising enhanced grid reliability.

articleTitle: State/parameter Observer Design for a Single-rod Electrohydraulic Manipulator
abstract: This paper considers a nonlinear state and parameter estimation problem of single-rod electrohydraulic manipulator with unknown parameter. Compared to the translational mass with single-rod hydraulic actuator or manipulators driven by electrical motors, electrohydraulic manipulator possesses a richer nonlinear dynamics. An observer design approach is applied to the state and parameter estimation problem of the single-rod electrohydraulic manipulator system. The proposed results are also illustrated by numerical simulation experiment.

articleTitle: Binocular Pupil Detection Based on Adaptive Gabor Filter
abstract: In modern medicine, clinical examination of the pupil is fundamental in ophthalmology. The results of these examinations are crucial for assessing the severity of certain diseases, guiding the development of new medical devices and medications, and determining the suitability of specific medical procedures. However, existing circular detection operators and threshold segmentation algorithms are affected by disturbances such as eyelashes and shadows, leading to poor detection accuracy. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a method for pupil diameter detection based on adaptive Gabor filtering. The method first utilizes unequal weight centroid method to roughly locate the center of the pupil. Subsequently, adaptive Gabor filter is applied to reduce noise and segment the pupil region. The image is then binarized, and a neighbor tracing algorithm is employed to search for the pupil contour. Finally, ellipse fitting is performed to obtain the pupil diameter parameter.
