By analyzing these characteristics, the specific location of the sound source is accurately determined.

articleTitle: Multirate Signal based Fault Diagnosis of Hydraulic Systems with Residual Shrinkage Separable Convolutional Network
abstract: For the multi-rate problem of data caused by different sampling rates of sensors in the hydraulic system, the multi-rate data is difficult to be directly input into a single neural network for inference training because of the difficulty of aligning its time dimension. Therefore, this paper proposes a diagnostic framework for hydraulic systems based on multi-rate signals. A residual shrinkage separable convolutional network is utilized to capture the fault characteristics of the system's high-rate data and the network has fewer parameters compared with the traditional convolution, and combined with a statistical feature module, the time and frequency domain features of the low-rate data are extracted. Secondly, a multi-rate feature fusion module based on gated attention mechanism is designed to capture the fault features at different levels, and the adaptive weighting mechanism is used to aggregate the feature information at different levels and obtain the fusion features. The experimental results show that the framework can still obtain high diagnostic accuracy in the more extreme case of data sampling rate imbalance ratio of 1: 100, and the average fault recognition accuracy also reaches 99.55% and 99.55% in the diagnosis of complex faults such as pumps and accumulators, respectively.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Based Bearing Fault Diagnosis with Convergent Attention
abstract: Rolling bearings are crucial in various rotating machinery, playing a key role in maintaining safety and reliability in industrial operations. Deep learning-based fault diagnosis approaches typically depend on training datasets containing samples for all possible fault scenarios, which may not be readily accessible in certain industrial settings. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a visual perception model for diagnosing bearing faults using aggregated attention and digital twins. Initially, a digital twin model of the bearing is developed to simulate its vibration characteristics and produce vibration data representing different health conditions. Second, the vibration signals of the bearing are transformed into time-frequency diagrams, allowing the model to automatically learn important features, as well as local and global features, across different time and frequency scales through the aggregation of attention. These features are then input into the network for classification. Finally, after reducing the distribution gap between virtual and real data within the feature space, real data is then utilized to validate the effectiveness of the training model based on virtual data. Experimental results show that the digital twin-based approach provides high accuracy in diagnosing bearing faults and can effectively simulate and identify various fault types.

articleTitle: ViMPose: Human Pose Estimation Based on Vision Mamba
abstract: Recently, state space models (SSM) based on efficient hardware-aware design, such as the Mamba deep learning model, have demonstrated exceptional efficacy in visual feature recognition functions. However, few studies have explored the potential of this novel architecture for pose estimation tasks. In this paper, we propose ViMPose, a baseline model for human pose estimation based on Vision Mamba. We demonstrate the model's excellent performance in pose estimation from multiple aspects, including model simplicity, inference speed, and lightweight parameters. Specifically, ViMPose employs a new backbone with bidirectional Mamba blocks to extract features from given human instances and uses a lightweight decoder for human pose estimation. Employing the scalable capacity and lightweight nature of Vision Mamba, ViMPose achieves high recognition accuracy with fewer parameters, striking a new balance between real-time efficiency and performance. Furthermore, ViMPose exhibits lower memory usage when processing high-resolution image inputs. Findings of the COCO dataset experiments highlight the ViMPose model's effectiveness and considerable promise for human pose estimation tasks.

articleTitle: Electrocardiogram Classification Based on Spatial-Channel Networks and Optimization Algorithms
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are one of the leading causes of death globally, and the electrocardiogram (ECG) serves as a primary diagnostic tool, making automated ECG classification of significant clinical importance. Although previous studies have extensively utilized various neural network models for feature extraction and classification of ECG signals, these methods often face challenges such as insufficient accuracy, high computational demands, and lengthy processing times. This study aims to design a new arrhythmia classification framework that achieves high accuracy and low cost in diagnosing arrhythmias. We introduced Spatial and Channel-wise Convolutional (SCC) attention into Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN), resulting in the SCC-TCN model, which significantly enhances classification accuracy and reduces computational costs. Additionally, by incorporating a stochastic walking mechanism, we improved the Rime optimization algorithm(RIME), effectively enhancing its performance. We also utilized the improved RIME algorithm to optimize the hyperparameters of the Spatial and Channel-wise Temporal Convolutional Networks(SCC-TCN) model, further improving its classification performance. Testing on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Dataset (MITAD) and the MIT-BIH Supraven-tricular Arrhythmia Dataset (SVDB) demonstrated that our method achieves classification accuracies of 99.40 % and 97.82%, respectively, validating the practical value of this approach.

articleTitle: BCFN: Bi-Directional Consistent Fusion Network for 6D Object Pose Estimation
abstract: In this work, we introduce BCFN, a Bi-directional Consistent Fusion Network designed for 6D pose estimation from a single RGB-D image. Our goal is to fully leverage the appearance information from the RGB image and the geometric information from the depth image. Previous studies have primarily utilized fused depth data to guide learning, overlooking the RGB branch. The core insight of our approach is to use both the RGB and depth branches to supervise the network. We have developed a dual-branch network that integrates appearance and geometric information. Subsequently, we propose pixel-level and vertex-level losses for each branch, respectively. Moreover, we introduce a consistent loss to enhance the network's convergence. We demonstrate the superiority of our method through experiments conducted on the LM-O dataset.

articleTitle: Q-Learning-Based Predictive Control for Capacity Adjustment in Reconfigurable Job-Shops
abstract: Nowadays, companies are faced with challenges to produce a variety of products with a satisfactory productivity in the presence of unpredictable demand fluctuation that may seriously disturb the work plan and lead to performance deterioration. Capacity adjustment is an effective strategy which typically achieved by labour-oriented approaches. In this paper, we consider a machinery-based capacity adjustment via reconfig-urable machine tools (RMTs) to regulate work in process (WIP) for performance improvement. Yet, the referred optimization and control concerning RMTs allocation are intractable. To this end, we propose an intelligent predictive control scheme that combines genetic algorithm (GA) and Q-Iearning. In this case, the complex and possible frequent reconfiguration derived from RMTs can be firstly well predicted and accordingly decreased, while guaranteeing a desirable production control performance. Also, the computational complexity of the rolling reconfiguration optimization problems can be significantly reduced. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated in a multi-product multi-workstation job shop system.

articleTitle: Aerodynamic Modeling and Aerodynamic Parameter Identification for High-Speed Aircraft
abstract: The aerodynamic parameters modeling and identification method of high-speed aircraft are studied in this paper. Firstly, the dynamic characteristics and aerodynamic performance of high-speed aircraft are investigated to establish the aerodynamic parameters theoretical model. Then, this paper provides a neural network approximating method for the aero-dynamic parameters model by using the off-line flight data to mitigate the impact of modeling error. The input of the neural network can be determined according to the theoretical model of aerodynamic parameters. Moreover, based on the estimation result of neural network, the least squares method is used to identify the aerodynamic parameters relying on the states of high-speed aircraft. The purpose of this paper is to improve the accuracy and performance of the aerodynamic parameters identification of high-speed aircraft. Finally, the approximation effectiveness of neural network and the identification effect of aerodynamic parameters for high-speed aircraft are verified by the fight simulation experiment.

articleTitle: Running Velocity Planning and Tracking Control of Forging Manipulator Lifting Mechanism
abstract: This paper focuses on the issues of mechanical shaking during operation and velocity tracking for the parallel lifting mechanism of forging manipulators, and investigates the planning of velocity and design of the velocity tracking controller of the manipulator. Firstly, an electro-hydraulic servo model for the lifting mechanism is presented. Secondly, a velocity planning method based on segmented operation distances is adopted, then the optimized asymmetric S-type velocity curves are proposed in order to realize smooth and shortest-time operation under different process requirements. Furthermore, a sliding mode velocity tracking controller is designed. Simulations demonstrate that the velocity planning method presented in this paper can effectively address the issues of shaking and time minimization during operation, and the output of system can track the ideal velocity curve well under the sliding model tracking controller.

articleTitle: Sar Image Classification Based on Spiking Neural Network with Different Coding Methods
abstract: Deep learning methods are widely used in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image recognition and have achieved high recognition accuracy on some public datasets. However, the existing deep learning methods do not really form a cognitive level of understanding and are highly susceptible to spoofing attacks by external noise. Spiking neural network (SNN) contains the inherent spatiotemporal dynamics of biological neurons and has strong robustness. SAR image recognition task is accomplished based on SNN model using different coding methods in this paper, and the effects of different coding methods on SNN model are analysed in detail through different degrees of interference samples. Firstly, Poisson coding and direct coding methods are adopted to achieve spiking coding of SAR images. Then different SNN models are constructed for SAR image recognition based on different coding methods. Surrogate gradient method is then employed to solve the problem of non-differentiable spiking sequences, which effectively achieves the end-to-end training of SNN. Finally, efficient SAR image recognition is achieved based on the constructed SNN models. And the salt-and-pepper (S&P) noise samples and fast gradient sign method (FGSM) adversarial samples are produced to test the SNN models, which are used to compare and analyse the effects of different coding methods on the model performance. In this paper, the model is validated using the public dataset MSTAR. The experimental results show that Poisson coding is more likely to improve the robustness of the SNN model, and direct coding is more conducive to improve the recognition accuracy of the SNN model, which provides valuable insights for the design of SNN models in the future.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation Network for Small-Body Rock Based on Improved DeepLabv3+
abstract: To address the issues of complex calculations, large memory consumption, and insufficient segmentation of small rock fragments and edge detection in traditional rock image segmentation algorithms, we propose an improved small-body rock segmentation algorithm based on DeepLabv3+. To cut down on computations and use, this method leverages the lighter MobileNetV2 network as its backbone. The HDC module is used in place of the original dilated convolution in ASPP in order to mitigate the gridding impact. The network's ability to fuse and extract features at various sizes is further improved by the addition of the Coordinate Attention (CA) and Channel Feature Pyramid (CFP) modules. The suggested approach obtains a 95.88% accuracy rate for small-body rock picture segmentation, with a MPA of 80.28% and a MIOU of 71.43%, according to experiments conducted on simulated datasets.

articleTitle: Efficient Human-Robot Safety Framework Based on Human Hand Trajectory Prediction and Path Replanning
abstract: To achieve safe and efficient human-robot interaction(HRI), it is essential to predict how operators will move during the execution of tasks by both humans and robots. Existing research in human-robot interaction often focuses solely on human hand predictions, frequently overlooking the significance of robotic arm movements in maintaining safety. Addressing safety concerns in dynamic and unstructured environments, this paper introduces a Predictive Obstacle-Aware Rapidly-exploring Random Trees Connect(POA-RRT-Connect) approach. This method utilizes a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) to predict human motion over forthcoming intervals. Based on these predictions, the results are forwarded to the robotic arm's collision detection algorithm, which checks for potential collisions and plans an optimal collision-free path if none are detected. Experimental results show that compared to our proposed method, the Lazy RRT algorithm reduces planning time by approximately 71.19%, and by about 72.82% when compared to the RRTextend algorithm. In terms of path efficiency, it saves approximately 36.87% of the path length compared to our proposed method, and about 7% compared to RRT*. Consequently, the method proposed in this paper is capable of identifying an optimal collision-free path within a shorter timeframe for human-robot interaction tasks.

articleTitle: Optimal Control of Constrained Trajectory Optimization Problem of UAV with Limited Sensing
abstract: Optimal control of constrained unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) trajectory optimization problem is one of the frontiers and hotspots of UAV research. The various constraints generated by physical limitations and obstacles in the environment increase the difficulties of solving the trajectory optimization problem, especially when the limited sensing ability is taken into consideration. This paper presents the receding horizon optimization method to obtain optimal control for the UAV with limited sensing range in a complex environment with obstacles. To improve efficiency, a path constraint processing method is proposed to reduce the number of constraints in the nonlinear programming problem (NLP). The proposed main structure and detailed algorithm are also given. The numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method compared with the classical Gauss pseudospectral method.

articleTitle: Research on Water Cooling Plate Simulation System Based on Finite Element
abstract: The power devices of power electronic converters generate a lot of heat during operation, and effective heat dissipation and cooling are crucial for their reliable operation. As a typical heat dissipation module, the water-cooling plate has good heat dissipation performance, but its geometric shape and physical field are complex. The number and structure of the plates, the number and arrangement of cooling pipes, the flow velocity and material of the coolant, and the ambient temperature will affect the heat dissipation capacity. Manually modifying model parameters and repeating simulation steps are not only require a lot of work but also prone to errors. The finite element method (FEM) is used to design the heat dissipation module for converter simulation, which both has high engineering value for the design and operation of the converter. Based on the finite element method, this paper designs a water-cooling plate simulation system. The system is jointly developed using COMSOL and MATLAB software, and the design of modules including software environment configuration, software writing and thermal simulation is completed. After setting the parameters, the system can automatically establish a geometric model, and set material parameters and physical fields, then divide the grid and solve the model. Finally, data visualization is completed to achieve rapid construction and analysis of water-cooling plate simulation. The operation results prove the effectiveness of the simulation system. The system designed in this paper can improve the simulation efficiency of water cooling plate design and can be extended to the design and simulation of other cooling modules, which has highly great promotion value.

articleTitle: Bi-level Optimization Configuration of Integrated Energy Systems for Combined Cooling, Heating, and Power Based on Shared Energy Storage Aggregators
abstract: In the context of “dual carbon” goals, traditional energy systems are no longer sufficient to meet sustainable development needs. Therefore, a two-level scheduling strategy is proposed that considers both economic and environmental performance to enhance the power system structure, promote the utilization of various renewable energy sources, and improve energy conversion efficiency. Firstly, a new shared energy storage aggregation mechanism, aimed at coordinating the operation and profit mechanisms of shared energy storage units, is introduced. Subsequently, the battery sharing scheme is then applied to the integrated energy system, and a two-layer planning model is established based on different time scales. The upper-level model targets annual investment and operation & maintenance (O&M) costs, while the lower-level model focuses on optimizing daily operation and maintenance costs. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed bi-Ievel optimization model is validated through specific numerical examples.

articleTitle: Optimizing Autonomous Navigation Scheme for Smart Vehicle Platform
abstract: Smart vehicle platform, as a kind of mobile robot, have important research and application value. In this paper, we study an intelligent vehicle control system with an Android terminal as the core control unit. Our research focuses on environment perception, environmental modelling and path decision making. We designed and implemented an intelligent vehicle control system with real-time control and path planning functions. The system demonstrates the potential of smart vehicle platform in in the field of mobile robotics applications. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Research on the Expansion Algorithm of Leakage Magnetic Flux Defect Image Dataset for Long-Distance Oil and Gas Pipelines Based on DCGAN-Res-CBAM
abstract: The deep convolutional generative adversarial network (DCGAN) faces issues such as poor image quality, unstable model framework, and slow convergence during data augmentation. To address these challenges, an improved DCGAN model for pipeline leakage magnetic flux defect image generation is proposed. This model incorporates residual networks and attention mechanisms into the DCGAN framework to enhance the model's feature extraction capabilities. Experimental results demonstrate that the quality of pipeline leakage magnetic flux defect images generated by the given model is superior to those generated by DCGAN, WGAN, CGAN, and SAGAN. The average Frechet Inception Distance (FID) score achieved is 11 6.17, with the minimum FID score reaching 84.94. The proposed model can stably generate higher quality pipeline leakage magnetic flux defect images, providing an effective approach for expanding the tire defect sample dataset. This contributes to effectively solving the small sample problem faced by the development of deep learning in the field of defect detection.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Dimension Measurement System for Industrial Part Inspection
abstract: This paper develops a deep learning-based system for the dimension measurement of industrial parts. The system employs a general self-supervised image segmentation network to perform dichotomous image segmentation (DIS) on the parts, effectively extracting binary images of the target components from complex backgrounds without requiring preprocessing steps such as filtering or denoising. Following segmentation, contour detection, and dimension measurement are executed. The system utilizes a CMOS area scan camera and was tested on a computer equipped with a GTX1050 graphics card. The tests, conducted on two typical thrust ball bearing components (i.e., the ball retainer and the shaft ring) - yielded ten measurements per part. Comparison with a vernier caliper as the reference standard reveals that under normal operating conditions, the maximum standard deviation is 0.007 mm and the maximum absolute error is 0.017 mm.

articleTitle: Adaptive Architecture of Baseboard Management Controller Based on Different Projects
abstract: In this study, a novel architecture of baseboard management controller (BMC) based on intelligent platform management interface (IPMI) is discussed for the questions that the code of BMC needs to be modified, adjusted, adapted, and complied over and over again when the different demands from the different projects and platforms need to be developed. In the novel architecture, the abilities of BMC are modularized and integrated by the optimizations of the software, and the different projects are distinguished by the design of the hardware. Then, the driver adaptation layer is built by the PRJ file. According to the driver adaptation layer, the functions can be selected in the PRJ file and the exclusive BMC image that meets the customized demands can be compiled and booted up according to the PRJ file, the code base, the Board ID, the Customer ID, and the SKU ID. Based on the novel architecture, the implementation plan and practical case are also introduced to prove the feasibility. In summary, the novel architecture can improve code development efficiency, code reusing, and code maintainability, and accommodate many exclusive images for different projects only by a set of codes.

articleTitle: Distributed Fixed-Time Optimal Control of First-Order Stochastic Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: The present paper focuses on the distributed fixed-time optimization control issue within multi-agent systems under the influence of random noise interference. Through the introduction of a power-integral feedback distributed nonlinear optimal controller, along with the application of random Lyapunov stability theory and convex optimization techniques, it's guaranteed that even in the presence of random disturbances, the system can attain global convergence within a fixed time. The simulation results verify the accuracy of the theoretical outcomes.

articleTitle: Design of Software for Batch Extracting and Merging Document Pages Based on Character Matching
abstract: In some cases, it is necessary to extract specific pages from a large number of PDF files for subsequent processing. For example, extracting cover and signature pages from a large number of documents makes it easier for people to sign on them. Ordinary PDF file processing software, such as Adobe Acrobat, requires users to operate the software to open each PDF file one by one, browse the entire text, find specific pages, extract and save them, which is extremely time-comsuming. This article uses Python and commonly used PDF processing libraries to design a software for batch PDF specific pages extraction. This software extracts specific pages of multiple files by detecting keywords on the file page, and has an interface that facilitates multiple parameter settings and observation of processing progress.

articleTitle: Biosafety Management System for Pig Farms Based on Deep Learning and Internet of Things Technology
abstract: African swine fever has had a significant impact on China's pig farms. At present, there is no safe and effective vaccine for African swine fever, and the most effective way to combat it is to establish stringent and safe biological prevention and control measures. This paper proposes a regulatory system based on deep learning and the Internet of Things to minimize the damage caused by African swine fever by supervising personnel, vehicles, and pigs on farms and prompting farm staff to adopt a strict elimination philosophy. In this paper, to address the lack of site-specific datasets for large-scale farms, a large amount of data was collected using cameras in pig farms and selfconstructed farm environment datasets. To deploy the object detection network on the Jetson Nano, the YOLOv5s network is improved and trained in this paper to obtain the optimal weighting parameters. It was found that the improved YOLOv5s network achieved 89.6%, 96.4%, and 92.6% detection accuracy for detecting people, vehicles, and pigs respectively in the pig farm environment, which is 3.2%, 1.6%, and 2.7% higher than the recognition accuracy of the original YOLOv5s network respectively. In addition, this paper implements an intelligent biosafety management system in pig farms by building an Internet of Things database and constructing front-end web pages to receive and display abnormal information reported by the Jetson Nano.

articleTitle: An Effective Model Predictive Control with Self-Optimizing Deep Belief Network
abstract: Model predictive control (MPC) is an effective control based on the state prediction and rolling optimization. However, the system states are from the predictive model, and these existing predictive models fail to give the accurate modeling and prediction results of system states. In this paper, we propose an effective model predictive control with self-optimizing deep belief network (MPC-SODBN). First, a self-optimizing deep belief network (SODBN-EL) is designed based on the event-triggered learning to improve the performance of modeling and predicting system states. Second, we design a loss function that consists of the output of SODBN-EL and the control law. The optimal control law sequence can be obtained based on the loss function. Finally, the simulation experiments on the nonlinear system modeling and control show that the MPC-SODBN is effective and efficient.

articleTitle: HA-SpMM: A Hybrid Feature-Based Adaptive SpMM Algorithm on GPU
abstract: Sparse Matrix-Matrix Multiplication (SpMM) plays a key role in practical applications such as machine learning and neural networks. With the rapid development of parallel computing, accelerating SpMM on GPUs has become a current research focus. However, existing acceleration methods have not simultaneously considered the effects of matrix sparsity and GPU hardware parameters. In this article, we propose an efficient adaptive SpMM algorithm called HASpMM, which can automatically select suitable storage formats and load-balancing algorithms based on the hybrid feature of matrix sparsity and GPU hardware parameters. We first use CSR or COO format to store the matrix, and then we implement the load-balancing SpMM algorithm. Finally, we design a novel framework based on the hybrid feature to select the optimal storage format and SpMM algorithm for matrices. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method. On all matrices in the Suite Sparse Matrix Collection, our method performs better than state-of-the-art SpMV methods (i.e. cuSPARSE SpMM, ASpT, GE-SpMM, and HPSpMM) on more than half of the matrices.

articleTitle: State of Health Estimation of Lithium-ion Batteries Based on TiDE
abstract: Given the widespread use of lithium-ion batteries, accurately forecasting their State of Health (SOH) is crucial for ensuring the secure and reliable operation of equipment. The local capacity regeneration during battery degradation can undermine prediction accuracy. This research introduces an MDT-FOA+TiDE approach for predicting SOH in lithium-ion batteries using multidimensional time series data. Initially, capacity and various feature data from the degradation process were collected and health indicators were derived. Features with high correlation to capacity were integrated into multidimensional time series. Subsequently, the Time-series Dense Encoder (TiDE) model was employed for training and prediction, while the Fox Optimization Algorithm (FOA) was used for model optimization. Experimental results using the NASA dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms SVR and LSTM models that utilize univariate data and MDT-TiDE model without FOA optimization.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Pass IIR Digital Differentiator with Approximately Equal Ripple Group-Delay based on Iterative Reweighting Method
abstract: In minimax phase error infinite impulse response filters, the group-delay error is typically much larger at the passband edges than elsewhere. In this article, we propose an iterative reweighted minimax phase error algorithm for designing low-pass infinite impulse response digital filters with approximately constant group-delay. A revised Gauss-Newton strategy with variable step size is used to solve the minimax phase error problem with a weight function, and the revised envelope of the group-delay error is used to update the weight function of the phase error. Under the premise of meeting the requirements for passband and stopband magnitude error, an approximately equal ripple passband group-delay is obtained. Three design examples demonstrate the validity of the proposed iterative reweighting method.

articleTitle: Human Skeleton-based Action Recognition Algorithm Based on Improved PoseC3D
abstract: In response to the limitations of existing skeleton-based action recognition algorithms that rely on 3D convolutional networks for modeling long-range dependencies, this paper proposes an enhanced human skeleton action recognition algorithm based on an improved version of PoseC3D. First, the human skeleton sequence is converted into a 3D heatmap stack as an input to the network; second, a plug-and-play 3D attention mechanism module is introduced to enhance the ability of the network to perceive critical information; and finally, a bi-directional long and short-term memory network is combined to deal with long-term dependencies, the ability of the network to capture temporal features is enhanced, especially the change of complex actions over time in the successive skeleton sequences. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 97.3% (X-View) and 90.4% (X-Set) on the NTU-RGB+D60 and NTU-RGB+D120 datasets, respectively. These results represent an improvement of 1.8% and 0.3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> over the baseline algorithm, PoseC3D, thereby validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

Author Keywords: bi-directional long and short-term memory network

articleTitle: YOLOv8-IRD: Infrared Road Small Object Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv8
abstract: Aiming at the problem that existing model had multiple parameters while showed unsatisfactory recognition accuracy and inaccurate localization in small objects recognition task on infrared roads, this paper proposes a improved YOLOv8-based model for detecting infrared small road objects: YOLOv8-IRD (IRD, Infrared Road Detection). Firstly, to improve the performance of model in object detection while reducing computational complexity, we remove the detection head of size 20×20 and adding a detection head of size 160×160. Secondly, we introduce the Efficient Multi-scale Attention (EMA) for improving the object detection head, addressing the issue of poor localization of small objects. Thirdly, we leverage the RepViT block (RVB) to improve the backbone network, ensuring both lightweight characteristics and robust feature extraction capabilities. Finally, we employ the lightweight upsample module Dysample to alleviate the problem of detail loss during feature map upsampling. The proposed YOLOv8-IRD is evaluated on the FLIR dataset, compared with YOLOv8s and other advanced methods. Experiments show that our approach improves mAP50 by 4.43% and mAP50:95 by 3.30%. Compared to baseline YOLOv8s, the model parameters of YOLOv8-IRD decrease by 46.1%.

articleTitle: Adaptively Corrected Vicsek Model Using Fuzzy Logic
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the effect of fuzzy correction value on the self-propelled agents. In variable correction Vicsek model proposed by George et al., the correction value is constant, which leads to the collective motion with either poor anti-interference or slow response speed. Whereas, in this study, the agents can dynamically adjust the correction value according to the state of their surrounding neighbors. According to different neighbor states, the correction value of an agent can be linguistically described into IF-THEN rules. Utilizing fuzzy logic, the correction value is dynamically updated according to the synchronization degree of the neighbors of agent, the difference angle between the agent direction and the synchronization direction of its neighbors, and the current correction value. The modified Vicsek model with fuzzy correction value is called fuzzy adaptive correction Vicsek model. Simulation experiments have been carried out for the fuzzy adaptive correction Vicsek model, the variable correction Vicsek model, and the Vicsek model under different conditions and experiment results demonstrate that the proposed fuzzy adaptive correction Vicsek model has better ability of resisting disturbance and response speed of agents is significantly improved.

articleTitle: A Video Surveillance System Based on Single-Mode Fiber for Energy and Signal Co-Transmission
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative video surveillance system that utilizes single-mode fiber for the simultaneous transmission of energy and information. Traditional surveillance systems relying on electrical cables pose safety risks and operational challenges, particularly in hazardous and remote environments. The proposed system leverages power-over-fiber (PoF) technology, using a single-mode fiber to co-transmit high-power laser energy and video signals. This approach overcomes the limitations of multimode fibers, such as signal loss and modal dispersion, and enables long-distance transmission up to 10 kilometers. At the remote end, the energy is converted into electrical power by a photovoltaic converter, ensuring the operation of surveillance equipment. The system also incorporates low-power micro-controller (MCU) and a lossless compression algorithm to enhance video transmission efficiency, achieving a frame rate of 16–17 frames per second at a resolution of 320×240. Experimental results demonstrate the system's effectiveness in delivering stable energy supply and high-quality video transmission, making it suitable for use in special environments with stringent safety and operational requirements.

articleTitle: Utilizing ESP Mesh Ad-hoc Networking for Home-Based Planting Facility
abstract: Due to the lack of a low-cost plant cultivator with low difficulty of use for home application scenarios, in this paper, we propose an ESP Mesh Ad-hoc Networking-based home gardening facility design, which aims to achieve efficient plant cultivation in the home environment through intelligent and networked technologies. The system combines intelligent control, low cost, and high adaptability to address the challenges of space constraints, unstable climate conditions, and lack of professional horticultural knowledge that are common in home gardening. By presetting a variety of common plant and vegetable cultivation modes, the system enables users to easily operate and manage the system, making it particularly suitable for home application scenarios. Adopting ESP Mesh networking technology, the system realizes a modular distribution design and relies on wireless connection between functional modules, reducing installation complexity and cost. The design not only adapts to changing climatic conditions, but also optimizes the plant growth environment through intelligent control to improve plant growth efficiency and yield. However, the stability of this design in extreme environments has yet to be verified. Moreover, there are only automated planting methods for a few common plants, and more plants are planned to be covered in the future. In summary, this paper details the hardware and software architecture of the system and explores its potential for domestic and agricultural applications. The great value of the system in enhancing urban greening, improving air quality and promoting smart agriculture is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A Class of Perimeter Defense Strategy via Relative Time and Maximum Matching
abstract: This paper studies a class of perimeter defense problems for large-scale multi-robot systems. A perimeter defense strategy is designed via relative time calculations and maximum matching methods. The strategy is simple, effective, and easy to implement for large-scale perimeter defense problems. Some simulations are made to verify the effectiveness of the strategy.

articleTitle: Research on Visual Fault Diagnosis Technology for Power Transformers Based on Diffusion Model Sample Augmentation
abstract: The issue of insufficient sample size is a key factor restricting the effectiveness of deep learning techniques in the field of visual fault diagnosis for power transformers. To address this, we propose a visual fault diagnosis technology for power transformers based on diffusion model sample augmentation. This method first fine-tunes the diffusion model using LoRA to generate visual fault samples for transformers, thereby expanding the dataset. Subsequently, the diagnostic model is improved to better adapt to the complexity of transformer fault samples, aiming to enhance diagnostic accuracy. The enhanced diagnostic performance of the model is evaluated using an assessment system composed of accuracy, F1 score, and a confusion matrix. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method has good diagnostic effectiveness for visible faults in transformers.

articleTitle: A Novel Lightweight Model for Underwater Small Object Detection
abstract: Underwater object detection is widely used in underwater resource exploration and fisheries management. However, the complex underwater environment and limited computational resources pose significant challenges for accurate and efficient object detection. To address these challenges, a lightweight and efficient underwater object detection model, YOLO-SBL, is proposed in this paper. First, a novel SDGSConv convolution is introduced to mitigate the loss of fine-grained information caused by strided convolutions. Second, inspired by the Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (BiFPN) approach, the weighted fusion of features at different scales is achieved. Finally, a lightweight shared detail enhancement detection head (LSDED) is proposed, which enhances feature extraction capabilities while reducing the number of parameters. On the UPRC2020 dataset, YOLO-SBL achieves a mAP@0.5 of 84.1%, improving by 1.4% over the original YOLOv8n model. The parameter count of the model is reduced by 20%, and the FPS increases from 240 to 249. On the NVIDIA Jetson TX2 edge device, the inference speed was reduced from 65 milliseconds to 51 milliseconds, meeting real-time requirements.

articleTitle: Loop Detection Method Based on Multi-Frame Background Point Distance Histogram Encoding
abstract: Loop closure detection is a crucial component in Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) for constructing high-precision maps, as it can eliminate cumulative errors generated during the operation of SLAM systems. To address the shortcomings of traditional loop closure detection methods in reverse loop closure detection, we propose a method based on multi-frame background points. Firstly, we segment the current point cloud into regions and identify the farthest point as the background point. Then, we encode the relative distance relationships of all background points into histograms. Finally, by comparing the scores of the current histogram with those of candidate histograms, as well as the scores from the previous five frames, we determine whether a loop closure has occurred. We conducted comparative experiments on the KITTI dataset, which is widely used in the autonomous driving field, against various loop closure detection algorithms. The results demonstrate that our method effectively identifies loop closures while ensuring real-time performance.

articleTitle: A Parallelized Framework for Human Action Recognition and Prediction Based on Graph Neural Networks
abstract: With the rapid development of intelligent technology, human action recognition and prediction have important applications in fields such as video surveillance, security, human-computer interaction. However, current approaches to human action recognition and prediction often involve separate training processes, which can lead to error propagation from the recognition module to the prediction module, increasing prediction errors. To address this, this paper proposes a parallelized framework based on graph neural networks (PRP), consisting of a backbone network, action recognition head, and action prediction head. First, features are extracted through graph convolutional layers in the backbone network; then, the action recognition head outputs the action category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hat{y}$</tex>; finally, the action prediction head uses <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hat{y}$</tex> as prior information to predict future action sequences. Joint optimization enhances the model's learning capability and reduces error accumulation. Experimental results demonstrate that the PRP model significantly outperforms comparison algorithms and holds broader application prospects.

articleTitle: Gear Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Transfer Learning
abstract: Transfer learning offers a novel approach to address complex feature processing and human factors in traditional gearbox fault diagnosis. First, one-dimensional vibration signals are decomposed into IMF components via Empirical Mode Decomposition and Hilbert transform, with prominent components selected to form a 2D image sample set. The pre-trained model is fine-tuned and combined with a support vector machine optimized using Particle Swarm Optimization for classification. Experimental results show an average classification accuracy of 98.54% with a small sample size, fast convergence, low computational requirements, and strong adaptability to various scenarios with personalized outputs.

articleTitle: Lightweight SAR Image Ship Target Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv8
abstract: To address the issue of high model complexity in ship target detection algorithms for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images, which makes deployment on embedded devices difficult, a lightweight ship target detection algorithm based on YOLOv8 is proposed. First, a feature aggregation module is proposed to reconstruct the neck network. Second, deformable convolution and spatial channel reconstruction modules are introduced into the C2f module of the backbone. Finally, a lightweight shared convolution detection head is designed. Experimental results show that the improved algorithm reduces the number of parameters by 23.5% and the computational load by 23% compared to the original YOLOv8 algorithm, while achieving increases in mAP50 of 1.4% and 0.6% on the HRSID and SSDD datasets, respectively, which achieves the balance between algorithmic complexity and detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on Modeling and Control Method for PMLSM Considering Asymmetric Mutual Inductance
abstract: Due to end effects and segmented structure, permanent magnet linear synchronous motor (PMLSM) inevitably suffers from three-phase mutual inductance asymmetry and can cause harmonic disturbances in the current loop. In this article, it is analyzed through theoretical modeling that asymmetry in the abc axis can lead to 2-folder fundamental frequency disturbances in the dq-axis inductance. Based on this, the inhibitory effect of incremental prediction models on mutual inductance asymmetric disturbances was analyzed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method in suppressing current harmonics and thrust fluctuations was verified through Simulink numerical simulation models. Simulation results showed that the second harmonic was reduced by 52.89% compared with the PI method, and 25.92% compared with the deadbeat predictive current control (DPCC) method.

articleTitle: Research on Stabilization of Finite State Machine Under Function Perturbation Based on STP
abstract: This paper investigates the stabilization of finite state machines (FSMs) under function perturbations. First, by using the semi-tensor product (STP) of matrices, we derive an algebraic expression for the FSM under function perturbations. Next, based on this algebraic form, a necessary and sufficient criterion is derived, which can be used to judge whether a perturbed FSM is stabilizable to an equilibrium state. Furthermore, an algorithm for stabilizing perturbed FSMs is developed. Finally, an illustrative exmaple is provided to show the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Cooperative Optimal Operation of Multi-Microgrids Based on Two-Staged Robustness
abstract: A two-stage robust optimization model with a min-max-min structure is developed to depict the uncertainty and lower the microgrid's operation cost through the operation method of multi-microgrid cooperation in order to address problems like significant uncertainty disturbances and high operating costs faced by individual microgrid operations. The two-stage robust optimization model for multi-microgrid collaboration is addressed by a column-and-constraint generation alternating direction multiplier approach. The suggested approach can balance the system's economy, privacy, and resilience, as demonstrated by the example results.

articleTitle: Dynamic Learning from Adaptive Neural Control of Nonlinear Non-Minimum Phase Systems
abstract: This study proposes a dynamic learning control scheme for a class of nonlinear non-minimum phase systems with unknown nonlinear terms. To deal with the unstable internal dynamics, the system is transformed into a serial-connected form. After the transformation, the internal dynamics are directly driven by control input signals, while the output dynamics are driven by the internal dynamics. Adaptive neural control is initially proposed for nonlinear non-minimum phase systems based on neural function approximation. This approach ensures that the system output and internal dynamics converge to a small neighborhood of the reference signal and the expected stable response, respectively. Moreover, the neural estimated weights converge to a small neighborhood of the ideal weights based on the dynamic learning theory. The converged constant weights are used to develop a learning controller that enhances the control performance. A cart with an inverted pendulum is simulated to demonstrate the effectiveness of the developed scheme.

articleTitle: Path Planning Based on Improved A * Algorithm
abstract: In order to solve the problem of collision or path pl anning failure when using the traditional A* algorithm to plan paths in environments with complex obstacles, this paper propo ses an improved A* algorithm. This algorithm designs an adjus table weight factor to realize the dynamic adjustment mechanis m of the heuristic function and improve the robot's search effic iency and path quality by optimizing the node selection strateg y. Experimental results show that in a variety of different map environments, the improved A* algorithm can reduce the path length by 28.14 % and the planning time by 48.41 % on averag e compared to the standard A* algorithm. The search efficienc y and path planning quality verify the effectiveness of the algor ithm.

articleTitle: Electromotive Force Calculation and Analysis of an Inductive Displacement Sensor Based on ANSYS Maxwell
abstract: In order to improve the performance of the inductive displacement sensor, ANSYS Maxwell was used to compute and analyze the induced EMF(electromotive force) produced by the sensor in this paper. First, the theoretical analysis and simulation models of the inductive displacement sensor which mainly includes permanent magnet and PCB induction coil were established. Then, the model settings in ANSYS Maxwell for studying the magnitude and characteristics of the induced EMF were carried out, and the simulation results were compared with the analytical calculation results. Lastly, it was investigated how important parameters affected the mapping relationship between the change in position to be measured and the induced EMF. The findings demonstrate that the size and composition of the permanent magnet, the length of the air gap, the coil's form and number of turns, and other parameters have a significant impact on the induced EMF produced by the sensor. Furthermore, the results of the analytical calculations and the simulation results are essentially in agreement, demonstrating the accuracy of the suggested approach.

articleTitle: Formalization of Natural Deduction System in Proposition Calculus
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence research, the relationship between mathematical logic and arti-ficial intelligence is becoming increasingly close. Mathematical logic is one of the cornerstones of artificial intelligence. At present, consolidating the theoretical foundation of artificial intelligence will provide guarantees for the development of artificial intelligence technology. Proposition calculus is the most fundamental in mathematical logic, with two types: axiom sys-tems and natural deduction systems. Axiom systems start from axioms, while natural deduction systems start from reasoning rules, and the derivation process tends to natural ideas. This article establishes a natural deduction formal system for propo-sitional calculus using the theorem prover Coq, and verifies the equivalence between natural deduction systems and axiom systems.

articleTitle: Class-Agnostic Dual-Branch Network for Few-Shot SAR Target Recognition
abstract: To address potential bottlenecks in cross-domain transfer for few-shot SAR target recognition, we overcome the limitations of source domain category attributes and propose a model named Class-Agnostic Dual-branch ProtoNet (CADP-Net). In this network, the global and local branches are designed to extract global and local features of the image, respectively, which are then mapped to a more discriminative space through a multi-layer perceptron. The dual-branch network is trained using moving exponential averaging under the consistency constraint of classification prediction. This approach can generalize a universal recognition strategy regardless of the target's category attributes, reduce intra-class distances, and increase inter-class distances. As a result, it enhances the ability to learn transferable representations in cross-domain few-shot tasks for SAR images. Experiments on the MSTAR dataset effectively validate our method.

articleTitle: DGL-YOLOv8 a Lightweight Yarn Detection Algorithm
abstract: Yarn, being a fundamental raw material in fabric manufacturing, directly influences the quality of the final product. To address potential challenges that may occur at various stages of yarn production, in this paper, we propose a lightweight and efficient recognition algorithm based on YOLOv8n, named DGL-YOLOv8. First, we enhanced the lightweight convolution DWConv by incorporating the MLCA attention mechanism to strengthen the connection between channel and spatial information. Then, we introduced the GhostModule lightweight module to refine the C2f structure, replacing the standard convolution layers with dynamic convolution layers. This allows the model to better capture features of objects at different scales. Finally, in the detection head, we adopted the concept of shared parameters, replacing the bulky three Detect modules of the original model with a single shared convolution, further reducing the model's parameters and computational cost. According to the experimental data, DGL-YOLOv8 achieved an mAP0.5 value of 90.1%, an improvement of 0.5% over YOLOv8n. The parameter count is 0.95M, and the computational load is 3.3 GFLOPs, representing reductions of 68% and 59%, respectively, compared to the base model. The results demonstrate that the improved model greatly increases the effectiveness of real-time object detection in complex environments, providing an effective solution for yarn production monitoring.

articleTitle: A Fault Diagnosis Method for NPC Three-Level Inverters Based on VMD-SE and SMA-SVM
abstract: To tackle the challenges of low accuracy and high computational complexity in diagnosing open-circuit faults for NPC three-level inverters, this paper introduces a novel fault diagnosis approach that integrates Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), Sample Entropy (SE), and an enhanced Slime Mold Algorithm (SMA) optimized Support Vector Machine (SVM). The method begins by decomposing the fault current signal using VMD and calculating the SE to identify fault characteristics. Next, it employs a correlation coefficient to filter out invalid Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs). Finally, an improved SMA is applied to optimize the SVM for accurate fault classification and identification. Simulation results show that this method outperforms traditional techniques in terms of effectiveness and accuracy.

articleTitle: Speed Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Improved Nonlinear Disturbance Observer
abstract: To improve the precision and anti-disturbance capability of the speed regulation system of permanent magnet synchronous motors, a new control approach based on a nonlinear disturbance observer is introduced. Adopting a dual-loop control strategy, the traditional PI control in the speed loop is replaced by second-order nonlinear disturbance observer control, while PI control is retained in the current loop. In order to enhance the control performance of the permanent magnet synchronous motor, the nonlinear function fal() in the disturbance observer control is replaced by the smoother gfal() function. Additionally, to improve the system's adaptability and responsiveness, fuzzy control is utilized to online adjust the crucial parameters in the nonlinear error feedback control law. Simulation results demonstrate that significantly enhance both the response rate and the capability to counteract disturbances of the motor's speed.

articleTitle: IUS-MAAC: Multi-Agent Attention-Critic for Task Offloading in Integrated User-Server Mobile Edge Computing
abstract: In recent years, the rapid development of computation-intensive mobile applications has posed significant challenges to the computational capabilities of user devices. In response to these challenges, Mobile Edge Computing (MEC), as an emerging technology, effectively alleviates the computational pressure on user devices. Task offloading, as the core mechanism of MEC, has become a focal point in current research. Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has demonstrated its unique advantages in handling task offloading. However, current DRL-based task offloading methods primarily focus on the user level, considering factors such as limited battery life and computing capacity, thereby neglecting server performance. These methods often assume that servers have sufficient computational power and storage resources. Additionally, traditional DRL performs well in handling discrete or continuous actions but still faces challenges when dealing with hybrid action spaces. Based on these, the paper proposes a novel Integrated User-Server Multi-Agent Attention-Critic (IUS-MAAC) algorithm for MEC task offloading. This takes into account various constraints during the task offloading process and demonstrates better performance in handling hybrid spaces compared to existing Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) and heuristic algorithms. Based on our verification, the results show that the proposed algorithm has better convergence and improves the overall reward value by approximately 9.3% compared to other state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Dynamic Event-Triggered Filtering of Semi-Markov Jump System with Time-Varying Delay
abstract: This paper explores dynamic event-triggered filtering for a class of semi-Markov jump systems with time-varying delays. Utilizing the semi-Markov kernel, we analyze these systems and design a dynamic event-triggering mechanism to alleviate communication pressure. A Lyapunov function is constructed with a guaranteed negative trigger threshold. After a period of dwell time, the system undergoes mode transitions. By ensuring that the Lyapunov function decays during this process, we derive a set of sufficient conditions for the existence of the filter under the dynamic event-triggering mechanism. Finally, a numerical example is provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Disturbance Rejection Control of Overhead Cranes Based on Neural Network
abstract: A neural network-based online optimization algorithm for double linear active disturbance rejection control is proposed to address the problems of large load swing and long convergence time of overhead cranes in the lifting process. Firstly, a double linear active disturbance rejection controller (DLADRC) is designed by adding the control of load swing angle to the conventional linear active disturbance rejection controller (LADRC). Then, a neural network double linear active disturbance rejection controller (NN-DLADRC) is designed by combining the DLADRC with a neural network, which realizes the online tuning of the controller bandwidth and the observer bandwidth. In addition, considering the actual working environment of the crane, simulations were performed under a variety of working conditions and disturbances. The proposed control strategy enhances the adaptability of the crane under different working conditions and disturbances, and realizes the accurate positioning of the trolley and the swing suppression of the load. The effectiveness and superiority of the proposed control strategy is verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Design of an Integrated Detection and Monitoring System for Confined Space Operations
abstract: Confined spaces refer to enclosed or semi-enclosed areas where poisonous, harmful, or combustible gases may accumulate due to poor ventilation. Working in such spaces can easily lead to personal injuries, including oxygen deficiency, asphyxiation, and poisoning. Nuclear power enterprises are characterized by dense confined space equipment, frequent confined space operations, and significant operational risks. To address these issues and ensure operator safety in confined spaces, this paper designs an integrated detection and monitoring system that integrates both environmental and operator monitoring sensors. Specifically, real-time monitoring of personnel is accomplished using multi-channel audio and video transmission technology. Additionally, a gas monitoring and wireless relay system using industrial gas detection sensors is designed to assess the safety of the environment. A wearable personnel status monitoring sub-system is also adopted to ensure operator safety by monitoring their physiological indicators. Finally, a behavior recognition algorithm is designed to achieve real-time detection of operator behavior to assist supervisors in assessing the safety conditions of operators. Experimental analyses of network performance, program functionality, and algorithm effectiveness are conducted to verify the feasibility of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Wave Equation-Based PD Control for Course Deployment of Unmanned Surface Vehicles
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of course de-ployment for multiple unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) based on the nonlinear wave equation derived from the Norrbin model. The proposed method, different from other existing course con-trollers, can accurately estimate unknown external disturbances and rapidly achieve the course deployment of multiple USVs. Firstly, the Norrbin model of unmanned ship is transformed into a second-order nonlinear wave equation error model by introducing course angle error, so that the deviation between the actual course angle and the expected course angle can be converging depending on the relative course angle information of each ship under the influence of disturbance. Secondly, based on the constructed disturbance observer, a course PD controller with anti-interference capability is designed, which can accurately estimate the disturbance and realize the course deployment from different initial course angle to the expected course angle for each ship in the large-scale unmanned ship cluster. Then, the sufficient linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) condition is derived by using the Lyapunov theory, and the stability of course deployment control of the multi-USV is demonstrated. Finally, a numerical simulation is conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Adaptive Formation Control of USVs- UAVs Heterogeneous Systems With Visibility Constraints in Obstacle Environments
abstract: This paper presents a heterogeneous formation control algorithm for unmanned surface vessels (USVs) and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in obstacle environments. The control algorithm guides the followers to track their leaders and forms a desired formation. To simplify the design process, the dynamics models of underactuated USVs and quadrotor UAVs are described to be unified. Time-varying performance functions are applied to ensure that field-of-view constraints and collision avoidance requirements are met, and to guarantee the tracking errors to converge within a controllable range at the specified speed. Additionally, an artificial potential function is designed to ensure obstacle avoidance in obstacle environments. Finally, simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed formation control algorithm.

articleTitle: Multi-level Enhanced Contrastive Learning for the Prediction of Learning Effectiveness in MOOCs
abstract: With the development of Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) platforms, accurately predicting student learning outcomes has become particularly important. To address the limitation of representation learning caused by sparse supervision signals, contrastive learning is introduced as a powerful method, utilizing self-supervised signals between training samples to learn better representations. However, existing self-supervised contrastive learning methods heavily rely on historical performance and behavioral data, overlooking semantic information, cognitive states, and emotional responses. To address the above limitations, we propose a Multi-Level Enhanced Contrastive Learning framework (MECL), which aims to redefine the self-supervised learning process from the perspectives of label perception and structural reconstruction. and learn better representations by exploiting self-supervised signals between training samples. Specifically, we treat the parameters of the classifier as augmented samples associated with different labels, injecting label information into the feature space to obtain enhanced views. In addition, to balance the robustness and generalization ability of learning representations, we designed a structural enhancement mechanism to guide the model in reconstructing multiple feature representations. The experimental results on a real-world MOOC platform dataset demonstrate that the model outperforms the best existing methods in terms of prediction accuracy and generalization across different courses, providing new insights for educational interventions and personalized learning path design.

articleTitle: Research on Motion Planning Method for Robotic Arm Under Obstacles
abstract: To solve the problem of the motion planning algorithm of a robotic arm, such as long search time, uneven planning path and large mechanical vibration during movement, this paper proposes a motion planning method for a robotic arm under obstacles. First, an improved Informed-RRT* algorithm is proposed for path planning. Based on the traditional Informed-RRT* algorithm, the bidirectional search strategy is introduced to reduce the randomness of search and improve the sampling efficiency. In the path growth stage, the adaptive step size strategy is adopted and the step size is dynamically adjusted according to the expanding trend of the search tree, so the local optimization can be avoid and the path search time can be reduced. Second, the 3-5-3 segmented polynomial interpolation method is used in trajectory planning. The purpose is to smooth the path and optimize the motion trajectory. Thus, the angular velocity of each joint of the manipulator is smooth and continuous, and the impact of the manipulator movement is reduced. In the experiment, the improved Informed-RRT* algorithm is compared with the traditional algorithm under the obstacle environment. The experiment results show that, compared with traditional path planning algorithms, the proposed method has shorter path length, fewer path branches and faster computation time. Compared with the traditional trajectory planning algorithm, the proposed method has faster response speed and smaller mechanical vibration.

articleTitle: Security Indirect Adaptive Iterative Learning Control for Nonlinear Systems with Fading Channel Under DoS Attacks
abstract: This paper investigates the security data-driven control problem for repetitive nonlinear systems with fading channels under denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. Firstly, under the influence of fading channels, a novel data-driven indirect adaptive iterative learning control (iAILC) algorithm is designed to idealize system tracking results. The adaptive mechanism is introduced to construct the adaptive set-point tuning law, thereby regulating the learning gain instantaneously. Secondly, double dynamic linearization method is deployed to simplify the system model, wherein the considered system is transferred to linear parametric model related to data. Then, considering the stochastic DoS attacks act on the fading output, compensation mechanism is developed by historical data, which eases the effect of DoS attacks accordingly. Finally, simulation results validate the efficiency of the presented control method.

articleTitle: Label Self-Correction Intelligent Diagnosis Method and Embedded System for Axle Box Bearings of High-Speed Trains
abstract: Label noise is inevitable when manually annotating monitoring data for the axle box bearings of high-speed trains. This issue can cause deep learning-based diagnosis models to overfit on false-labeled samples, thereby reducing the models' diagnostic accuracy. To address this problem, this article presents an intelligent diagnosis method that is resistant to label noise for the axle box bearings of high-speed trains. The proposed method consists of two modules. Firstly, the module leverages the strengths of different networks to independently extract features from dual perspectives. Subsequently, it filters noise labels through model interaction and ingeniously employs a correction model to rectify incorrectly labeled samples. Then, the proposed method is embedded within a hardware-based system, primarily constructed with a microprocessor. Both the method and the system have been validated through diagnostic cases of axle box bearings. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can significantly improve the accuracy of the diagnostic models, and the hardware-based system is capable of successfully displaying signals from faulty bearings and providing real-time diagnostics, thereby further enhancing the reliability and efficiency of the diagnostic process.

articleTitle: Data-Driven-Based Bipartite Tracking Consensus Control for Networked Agent Systems via Adaptive Policy Iteration
abstract: In this paper, the optimal bipartite tracking consensus control problem of networked agent systems is addressed. Theoretically, a data-driven control scheme based on adaptive policy iteration (API) is designed to enable all followers in a cooperative-competitive network to achieve bipartite tracking for the leader. Firstly, the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation of this optimal tracking consensus control problem is obtained based on the Bellman optimality principle. Secondly, an API algorithm with the adaptive escape mechanism is designed to achieve the solution of the HJB equation while reducing the iteration resource consumption. Then, the optimal value function and optimal control input are solved online based on neural networks. Finally, a simulation example is given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed data-driven-based bipartite tracking consensus control scheme.

articleTitle: Robust Divergence Learning for Missing-Modality Segmentation
abstract: Multimodal Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) provides essential complementary information for analyzing brain tumor subregions. While methods using four common MRI modalities for automatic segmentation have shown success, they often face challenges with missing modalities due to image quality issues, inconsistent protocols, allergic reactions, or cost factors. Thus, developing a segmentation paradigm that handles missing modalities is clinically valuable. A novel single-modality parallel processing network framework based on Hölder divergence and mutual information is introduced. Each modality is independently input into a shared network backbone for parallel processing, preserving unique information. Additionally, a dynamic sharing framework is introduced that adjusts network parameters based on modality availability. A Hölder divergence and mutual information-based loss functions are used for evaluating discrepancies between predictions and labels. Extensive testing on the BraTS 2018 and BraTS 2020 datasets demonstrates that our method outperforms existing techniques in handling missing modalities and validates each component's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Low-Carbon Regional Integrated Energy Optimization Scheduling Considering Two-Stage Power-to-Gas
abstract: Under the background of the “dual carbon” goals, in order to improve the energy efficiency of the Regional Integrated Energy System (RIES) and promote the consumption of new energy, further reducing the carbon emission level of RIES; on the basis of considering the consumption issue of wind power, a two-stage power-to-gas (P2G) device is adopted, and hydrogen fuel cell energy storage is incorporated to facilitate the consumption of abundant wind energy during nighttime. Secondly, variable efficiency operation characteristics are adopted to improve the energy utilization efficiency of each device. Finally, under the guidance of the carbon market, a reward-penalty ladder carbon trading mechanism is introduced to limit the system's carbon emissions. Based on this, an operation target is established to minimize energy procurement costs, carbon trading costs, system operation and maintenance costs, and wind power output costs. The CPLEX solver is used for solving, and different scenarios are set up to analyze and demonstrate the model's effectiveness in terms of economy, environmental protection, and other aspects.

articleTitle: Enhancing Context-Dependent Learning in Spiking Neural Networks Through Symmetric STDP and Synaptic Scaling
abstract: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) are heralded for their biological plausibility and efficiency in processing spatiotemporal data. However, maintaining robust learning in noisy environments remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a novel model that integrates symmetric spike-timing-dependent plasticity (sym-STDP) with synaptic scaling mechanisms to enhance context-dependent learning in SNNs. By dynamically adjusting the synaptic weights and incorporating synaptic scaling, our model achieves superior learning accuracy and robustness to noise. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms traditional STDP models, achieving higher learning efficiency and adaptability in varying conditions. These findings underscore the potential of our model for advancing the application of SNNs in real-world, dynamic environments.

articleTitle: An Improved WQMIX with Dual-Network and Dynamic Weights for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: In the domain of cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), QMIX is a key algorithm that facilitates effective collaboration among multiple agents by enforcing monotonicity constraints on the joint Q-values. However, this assumption of monotonicity may limit the algorithm's capacity to explore more complex strategies. As an extension of QMIX, WQMIX attempts to relax these constraints by incorporating a weight scheme, aimed at enhancing the algorithm's flexibility and efficiency when handling complex multi-agent interactions. Nevertheless, its weight design is overly simplistic and fails to fully leverage potential performance. This paper introduces an improved version of WQMIX, termed Dual-Network and Dynamic Weights QMIX (DDWQMIX), which employs a dynamic weights strategy to more flexibly adapt to changes in the environment and optimize the learning process. Additionally, DDWQMIX integrates a dual-network structure, updating targets based on the smaller Q-values produced by the two networks, thus allowing for a more accurate estimation of joint Q-values and ensuring that optimal actions are not missed. Experiments conducted in the starcraft multi-agent challenge (SMAC) environment demonstrate that DDWQMIX outperforms traditional VDN, QMIX and WQMIX in multi-agent cooperative tasks, particularly in more complex scenarios.

articleTitle: High-Speed Maglev Train Speed Measurement and Positioning Technology Research Overview
abstract: The paper provides a comprehensive review of the current state and development trends of speed measurement and positioning technology for High-Speed Maglev Trains (HSMT). It first elaborates on the importance and characteristics of maglev train speed measurement and positioning technology, including strong coupling, high real-time performance, high precision, and technological diversity. Then, it thoroughly analyzes a variety of speed measurement and positioning technologies, including inductive loop, tooth slot detection, Pulse Width Modulation (PWM), Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), fiber optic measurement, Doppler radar, laser scanning, and Radio Frequency Identification (RFID), and discusses their advantages and limitations in practical applications. The paper also introduces some new research developments in technology, such as Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) based fiber optic positioning measurement technology and improved Doppler radar speed measurement technology. In the future, speed measurement and positioning technology will place greater emphasis on the integration and innovation of technologies. By leveraging multi-sensor data fusion, it will achieve higher precision and robustness in positioning, providing support for engineering applications.

articleTitle: Dynamic Multi-Channel Access in Heterogeneous Industrial Wireless Sensor Networks: A MADRL Approach
abstract: Industrial Wireless Sensor Network (IWSN) is one of the key technologies for future industrial automation and intelligent manufacturing. With the increase in the number of wireless network devices, the coexistence of wireless networks becomes a challenge. Dynamic multi-channel access in IWSN is critical for optimizing spectrum utilization and ensuring real-time data freshness. This paper proposes a Model-free Actor-Critic based Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MADRL) approach to address the challenges posed by heterogeneous network environments. The method aims to improve spectrum efficiency and packet freshness by dynamically selecting channels for transmission, considering the Age of Information (AoI) metric. Key contributions include a novel multi-agent framework tailored for heterogeneous networks, harnessing MADRL to enhance spectrum utilization and reduce transmission delays. Simulation results demonstrate significant improvements in throughput and AoI management compared to conventional methods.

articleTitle: Fast and Stable UAV Exploration With Incorporating Localization Uncertainty
abstract: The high maneuverability and freedom of un-manned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to swiftly explore complex and unknown environments while establishing corresponding maps is a typical application of UAVs. However, existing methods mainly focus on enhancing exploration efficiency while over-looking the impact of localization on quality and stability. This study introduces a rapid and robust frontier-based au-tonomous exploration method for UAVs, which incorporates localization uncertainty into the framework. This integration ensures coverage of more information-rich areas during fron-tier exploration, thereby reducing mileage drift and preventing localization failures, thus enhancing the exploration robustness. Extensive simulation experiments are conducted, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method compared to the state-of-the-art approach. To foster future research, we make the code in this work publicly available for any researcher at https://github.com/Joosool/FSUE.git.

articleTitle: Filtered Iterative Learning Control of the Time-Delay Flexible Manipulator System with Slowly Varying Tracking Trajectory
abstract: In this paper, the filtered iterative learning control (FT-ILC) problem of a time-delay flexible manipulator system with variable tracking trajectory is studied. In practice, the system may be affected by random noise, which can reduce the control accuracy. In order to reduce the influence of noise on the system, this paper designs a filtered iterative learning law. At the same time, considering that the desired trajectory of the system is not fixed, but slowly changing, the learning law is extended to this situation. Through the compression mapping principle, the convergence of the time-delay flexible manipulator system is demonstrated. Finally, the numerical simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A Cognitive Tracking Method Based on Evaluation and Feedback
