abstract: In complex tracking problems with multiple targets, the cognitive tracking method can adjust the algorithm with feedback by analysing tracking results, and obtain more accurate estimation results than conventional tracking methods. With the aid of historical results, we design an online evaluation variable to achieve feedback. We dynamically adjust the association threshold through the evaluation results to improve the association accuracy, and with the help of historical tracks and measurements, we implement the CNN-based clutter statistics and trajectory management method, which provides a more accurate discrimination of clutter and newborn targets. For individual targets, we analyse the environmental information through the time series of the LSTM network to obtain a more accurate estimation of noise covariance and achieve a high-precision adaptive filter. They constitute a complete cognitive tracking method based on the feedback. Simulations in single-target and multi-target tracking scenarios are carried out respectively to demonstrate the enhancement effect of feedback on the tracking method by comparing with methods such as IMM, and ablation experiments are conducted to illustrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Automatic UAV Inspection of Hydropower Station Diversion Pipelines Using Robust Cylinder-Like Fitting for Incomplete Point Clouds
abstract: This study presents a solution for UAV navigation within hydropower station diversion pipelines, introducing a robust cylinder-like fitting algorithm for incomplete point clouds (RCFIC) alongside a UAV state estimation algorithm. The RCFIC algorithm efficiently fits incomplete point clouds to cylinder-like structures using 3D lidar and IMU sensors. It preprocesses the point cloud data, slices it equidistantly along the centerline of the previous frame, and applies the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm to fit ellipses to the cutting plane points. A line or curve is then fitted to the centers of these ellipses. Using this cylinder-like model and various sensors, the UAV's target point, speed, and yaw are estimated based on geometric relationships. Field tests conducted at a hydropower station validated the algorithm. In both horizontal and oblique straight segments, the RCFIC algorithm achieved over 90% fitting accuracy, while it successfully maintained alignment with the pipeline's centerline in curved segments, demonstrating the method's robustness and precision. This approach enables reliable, automated inspection of diversion pipelines.

articleTitle: Application of Cloud-Edge Based Digital Twin in Robotic Arm Scanning of Aircraft Fuselage Panels
abstract: This paper investigates the Industry 4.0 upgrade of the aircraft fuselage panel workstation. Faced with diverse computational and transmission requirements of various business data at the workstation, this study proposes a combined cloud-edge transmission and computing architecture. Additionally, the research includes the planning of viewpoints for robotic scanning of aircraft fuselage panels and introduces a predetermined viewpoint trajectory method based on digital twin technology, effectively addressing the issues related to scanning quality. The practical application at this workstation has significantly enhanced both the scanning quality of the aircraft fuselage panels and the data processing capabilities.

articleTitle: CSTFnet: Cross-Scale Spatiotemporal Predictive Framework for Seasonal Prediction of Sea Surface Temperature
abstract: Sea surface temperature (SST) is critical for climate prediction, environmental monitoring, disaster warning, and various other oceanographic applications. SST prediction traditionally relies on numerical simulations, which effectively consider dynamical evolutions with explicit physical interpretations, but suffer from numerous challenges, such as limited timeliness and intensive computational demands. Recent advancements in deep learning have demonstrated its capability to capture spatiotemporal information through automatic feature representation learning, however the high-dimensional spatiotemporal correlation in ocean data, particularly the dependencies across different scales, remains inadequately explored. To fill this gap, this study proposes a cross-scale spatiotemporal fusion prediction network for seasonal prediction. Specifically, we explore the latent relationships within ocean spatiotemporal processes by tensor decomposition to derive mapping results across different scales. The fusion learning of the mapping results is achieved through dilated convolutional long short-term memory networks to achieve seasonal prediction of spatiotemporal process information. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed model over existing state-of-the-art methods in medium- to long-term predictions.

articleTitle: PatchCLIP: Enhencing CLIP with Pair-Images for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection
abstract: The vision-language model CLIP has profoundly transformed the filed of zero-shot anomaly detection. Recent studies acquire anomaly maps by aligning images with normal and abonormal prompts. However, CLIP does not effectively interpret text prompts in the context of anomaly detection. As a result, relying solely on text prompts is insufficient, making visual cues are particularly crucial. In this paper, we propose PatchClip for zero-shot anomaly detection, integrating both text-image feature matching and image-image matching. We concurrently process two images, treating each as the visual prompt for the other, and combine their respective text-image matching scores. We conduct extensive experiments on anomaly detection benchmarks, demonstrating superior performance compared to previous methods. The code will be open soon.

articleTitle: Digital Twin System Design for Rice Supply Chain Based on Identity Resolution
abstract: Aiming at the problems of insufficient informatization and intelligence in the grain, oil, and food industries, the difficulty of monitoring the data of the long whole supply chain, and the lack of informatization talents, this paper takes the rice supply chain as a typical object and organically integrates the industrial Internet logo resolution technology and digital twin technology together. By establishing a digital bridge between the physical object and the information system, proposing a digital twin architecture containing the physical layer, the network layer and the twin layer, forming a data circulation and sharing foundation based on the industrial Internet, clarifying the key model of the twin architecture, proposing a functional module design concept based on the scene control system and the three-dimensional visualization platform, and focusing on the practical training evaluation model based on a one-dimensional convolutional neural network, which provides the ability to provide a basic hands-on training platform for scientific research on the quality and safety of the entire supply chain of food, oil and foodstuffs, the digital upgrading of the industry, and the training of talents in marking and resolving.

articleTitle: MMD-DCGAN: A Robust Approach for Missing Data Imputation in Manufacturing Processes
abstract: Data quality is a critical factor in enhancing the intelligence of process industries. Incomplete or corrupted data can significantly affect the performance of industrial soft-sensing models. The paper proposes an improved Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Network (DCGAN) model, enhanced with Lipschitz continuity and Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD), for the imputation of missing data. The proposed MMD-DCGAN model addresses common issues in traditional GANs, such as mode collapse, unstable training, and high computational costs. The model is validated using both synthetic benchmark data and real-world wastewater treatment data, demonstrating its superior performance in generating accurate and consistent data. The experimental results indicate that the MMD-DCGAN model reduces the imputation error by 10% for benchmark data and 15% for real-world data, proving its effectiveness and practical application potential in industrial scenarios.

articleTitle: Improved Hybrid Gaussian Process Regression Model for State-of-Health Estimation of Li-ion Batteries
abstract: Accurate State-of-health (SOH) estimation con-tributes to the healthy and stable operation of the Li-ion batteries. This paper proposes an improved hybrid Gaussian process regression (GPR) method incorporating physical information for the high-accuracy estimation of battery SOH. The estimation process considers the effects of temperature, discharge rate, and depth of discharge (DOD) on the battery health, and the relevant features of the electrode degradation process are extracted for battery SOH estimation. The kernel function of GPR comprehensively considers the mechanical characteristics of battery degradation and can effectively track the battery degra-dation process. The validation experiments were conducted on the A123 LFP/Graphite battery dataset. Sufficient comparative experiments have validated the accuracy and robustness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Methods for Collaborative Combat Capabilities Analysis: An Overview
abstract: Collaborative combat is the foundational organizational form of intelligent, informatized, and systematic combat. With the rapid development of unmanned combat system, collaborative combat becomes the trend of future combat forms. Based on the network information sharing, the key elements to decide the victory or defeat of war are no longer limited to the advanced level of individual platforms, but also depends on the collaboration level among the components of the system. Thus, analyzing the system's collaborative capabilities is a core aspect of current combat assessment and optimization. Owing to the fog of war, the analysis of collaborative combat capabilities is not only limited by the acquisition of data and the complexity of the combat system, but is also influenced by the heterogeneity, hierarchy, coupling, dynamics, and multi-domain characteristics of the collaborative relationships between equipment, making it difficult to obtain an analytical method that considers various dimensions. We comb through the main research methods used for collaborative combat capability analysis, categorizing the research methods into four perspectives: analysis based on network structure, modeling and simulation, capability aggregation, and hybrid approaches. Furthermore, we provide a forward-looking perspective on the future trajectory of collaborative combat capability analysis. This overview can serve as a theoretical and technical foundation for research into countermeasures for systemic confrontation.

articleTitle: Research on Anti-Swing Strategies for Bridge Cranes
abstract: A study is conducted on the LH5T-13.5M electric crane, focusing on the swing characteristics of the load during steel coil lifting operations and the displacement issue of the crane. Initially, the system model is formulated using the Lagrange dynamic equations, translating the practical challenges into a solvable mathematical framework and deriving the transfer function of interest. Subsequently, the development of three control strategies is elucidated, formulated on the basis of the established model: a conventional PID control system, a fuzzy PID control system, and an adaptive proportional factor fuzzy neural PID controller. These systems are simulated and validated using Simulink. A comparative experimental setup is employed to evaluate performance. The results show that when the step input signal is 1, the maximum absolute load swing Angle of the traditional PID, fuzzy PID and adaptive scale factor fuzzy neural PID controller are 0.185°, 0.054° and 0.049° respectively for the working condition 1 experiment. The percentage overshoot corresponding to the wheelbarrow is 37.1%, 40.0%, and 30.5%, respectively. The findings indicate that the introduced fuzzy neural PID controller, equipped with an adaptive scaling factor, exhibits superior stability and effectiveness in maintaining the crane's operation within the optimal range of parameters.

articleTitle: A Building Integrated Energy System Scheduling Strategy Considering Wind and Photovoltaic Output Correlation Based on Improved Information Gap Decision Theory
abstract: The Building Integrated Energy System (BIES) is a useful approach to realise low-carbon buildings. In order to constrain the building carbon emissions and cope with the uncertainty of renewable energy and loads within the building, a scheduling strategy for the BIES in accordance with the improved Information Gap Decision Theory (IGDT) is proposed. Firstly, the wind and photovoltaic output correlation constraints are introduced on the energy supply side, and combined with the multi-type demand response of cooling, heating and electricity on the load side, the deterministic low-carbon dispatch model is designed to minimize both the daily operating costs for building users and the associated carbon emissions costs. Secondly, considering the uncertainty at both ends of the building source and load, the improved IGDT is used to describe the uncertainty variables, and the risk aversion model is constructed to explore the scheduling scheme under different risk attitudes of the BIES, which provides guidance for the dynamic operation of the system. Finally, the efficiency of the suggested strategy in terms of cost-saving, low carbon and flexibility is verified by the arithmetic simulation results.

articleTitle: A Robust Substation Indoor Personnel Action Recognition Network and Online Framework
abstract: It is crucial for operation safety that substation staff work indoors as required. Therefore, it is necessary to monitor the behavior of workers to reduce the occurrence of dangerous practices. Work in substations often involves interaction with equipment, leading to frequent occlusions that challenge the robustness of action recognition models. Additionally, monitor typically needs to be performed online, requiring the extraction of action segments from the live video stream for label classification. We have established a dataset specifically for the recognition of certain actions about indoor personnel in substations. A special processing method for skeletons is adopted and the recognition network is improved, which surpasses the accuracy of conventional Graph Convolutional Networks and significantly outperforms them in terms of robustness. Furthermore, we have proposed three online action detection frameworks according to the actual recognition scenarios in substations, balancing both inference accuracy and efficiency. Experiments conducted on our self dataset have verified the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: DyHeadNet: Insulator Defect Detection with a DYnamic Detection Head Combining Lightweight and Attention Mechanism
abstract: Considering the existing challenges in insulator defect detection, including the challenge of identifying small target defects, the limited capacity to handle complex background interference, and the low level of detection precision, this paper proposes a DyHeadNet model based on YOLOv8 for insulator defect detection. Initially, GSConv is implemented to substitute traditional convolution within the network, aiming to decrease the volume of model parameters. Following that, an efficient module named C2f-Faster is crafted to additional reduce the model's footprint. Subsequently, a novel dynamic monitoring head, DyHead, leveraging the attention mechanism, is introduced to enhance the detection capabilities for small defects. Ultimately, to precisely regulate the geometric characteristics of bounding boxes, the original model's CIOU loss function has been substituted with the MPDIoU loss function. Extensive experiments have been conducted utilizing the Insulator Defect Dataset (IDID). The outcomes demonstrate that DyHeadNet achieves an mAP@0.5 of 96.0%. In contrast to YOLOv8n, there is a 4.8% enhancement in detection precision, while the model's parameter count and computational load are decreased by 0.5 M and 0.8 G, respectively. When pitted against state-of-the-art methods like DSA-Net and Insu-Yolo,DyHeadNet excels at identifying small targets and coping with intricate backgrounds, all while maintaining a minimal computational expense.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning Control for AUV-Tow-Load Systems Under Safety-Critical Condition
abstract: In this paper, an safety-critical reinforcement learning control solution is developed for cable subsystems of autonomous underwater vehicle-tow-load systems with unmodeled dynamics. To achieve predetermined tracking performance guarantees, a nonlinear mapping is designed to transform the system dynamics into a new one complemented by predefined boundary functions. Based on this, a system identifier is constructed to provide online estimates for the controller, which releases the demand of exact modeling of cable subsystems. By employing experience reply technique, an update law is designed for a single critic neural network, where activation functions involved with system dynamics and reference trajectory is employed, allowing for an enhanced robustness of the closed loop using released persistent of excitation (PE) condition. Numerical simulation is provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed control algorithm.

articleTitle: Leveraging Siamese Framework for Enhanced Contextual Feature Learning in Traffic Forecasting
abstract: As smart city systems become increasingly complex and urban road networks become more interconnected, traditional predictive models are gradually losing their ability to handle the intricate information among contextual data, such as traffic flow and weather data, due to their inability to learn the holistic features of the entire dataset. These data not only require consideration of contextual relationships but also an understanding of the overall characteristics of the data, which traditional models typically fail to achieve. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel deep learning architecture: SimFormer. This architecture leverages the advantages of both the Siamese network and Transformer architectures, mapping complex time series into high-dimensional space to better capture their contextual features. Concurrently, the Transformer encoder's focus on capturing global temporal dynamics ensures that global features are preserved and utilized in subsequent prediction tasks. We evaluate this innovative architecture on multiple real-world datasets using two different performance metrics, and it consistently outperforms traditional models.

articleTitle: An Algorithm for Key Object Point Cloud Extraction Suitable for Subway Tunnels
abstract: In subway tunnel environments where GPS signals cannot be received, autonomous train positioning faces significant challenges. To address this issue, this paper proposes an algorithm that integrates multiple point cloud processing techniques in tunnel scenarios to extract key objects and calculate distances, aiming to utilize critical objects within the tunnel for assisted positioning. Specifically, the algorithm combines techniques such as point cloud filtering, clustering, and plane segmentation. Initially, radar point cloud data is preprocessed using the coordinates and intensity information to remove noise points while retaining essential data. Statistical filtering methods are then applied to further refine the point cloud by setting appropriate parameters to eliminate outliers and enhance data quality. Subsequently, the filtered point cloud data undergoes plane segmentation, where threshold parameters are set to segment the data into multiple planes. Post segmentation, the Minimum Bounding Box (MBB) algorithm is employed to obtain the volume of the smallest bounding box for each plane. These processing steps enable assessment of whether the extracted planes meet requirements, followed by distance calculation using the centroids of compliant planes. Using data recorded from a hardware platform installed on a city subway, the algorithm extracts point clouds of landmark objects within the tunnel and calculates their real distances relative to the train. Experimental results demonstrate that the algorithm effectively extracts landmark point clouds in tunnel environments, thereby enhancing the accuracy of train positioning. This validates the feasibility and effectiveness of the approach in practical applications. The study provides a novel solution for autonomous train positioning in subway tunnels where GPS signals are unavailable.

articleTitle: TGRL: A Trajectory-Guided Reinforcement Learning Approach for Robust Autonomous Racing
abstract: This paper presents a trajectory-guided reinforcement learning (TGRL) approach aimed at enhancing the robustness of autonomous racing by addressing model mismatch issues. Our proposed framework effectively mitigates these challenges by combining the heuristic strengths of reinforcement learning with the reliability of classical optimal planning methods. In this framework, the agent receives rewards based on the alignment of its actions with those selected by a classical planner that follows the optimal trajectory. Experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly improves generalization capabilities and robustness across various tracks, consistently outperforming baseline models under both normal and adverse conditions.

articleTitle: Robust Control of Feeding Speed in Coal Seam Drilling Process Considering Borehole Friction
abstract: During the coal seam drilling process, the drill string is subject to compressive deformation, compounded by unpredictable variations in formation hardness and borehole wall friction, leading to challenges in maintaining a stable feeding speed. This paper presents a novel approach by introducing uncertain parameters to describe the effects of formation hardness and borehole wall friction. Drill string axial movement model is modeled as a polyhedral system based on a lumped parameter representation. To meet industrial performance requirements, we design a robust <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> controller to achieve consistent feeding speed control. Our simulation results demonstrate the controller's effectiveness in ensuring system stability despite fluctuations in formation hardness and drill string friction.

articleTitle: Coverage Path Planning of Heterogeneous Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Based on Dual-Stage Genetic Algorithm
abstract: To address the increasing complexity of modern autonomous applications, heterogeneous unmanned aerial vehicles(UAVs) with solid robustness and high parallelism have emerged to compensate for the limited capabilities and insufficient performance of single UAVs. In this study, we propose a dual-stage genetic algorithm to solve cooperative coverage path planning in complex boundary regions, specifically in the context of cooperative coverage search by heterogeneous UAVs. First, considering that UAVs have different flight attitudes and sensor performances, the complex boundary region is uniformly discretized. A regional coverage path planning model is established and solved using a linear programming formulation. Next, a two-layer coding mechanism represents the region allocation results and coverage path sequences. A density clustering strategy is used to generate the initial solution, and a dual-stage alternating optimization strategy is utilized to enhance the performance of the solution set, providing the optimal point-to-point flight paths between the regions for each UAV. The coverage paths are generated through the decoding scheme. Finally, the performance of the proposed method is evaluated experimentally in terms of execution time, task completion time, and deviation ratio.

articleTitle: Neuro-Adaptive Cooperative Tracking Control for Nonlinear Multiagent Systems Against DoS Attacks
abstract: This paper studies the issue of adaptive cooperative tracking control for MASs in the presence of DoS attacks. The agents' communication structure is characterized by directed links, ensuring that at least one leader maintains a directed route to every follower despite the presence of attacks. Initially, a distributed observer is designed to enable each follower to precisely estimate the leader's information. Furthermore, the study utilizes the average dwell time method in conjunction with adaptive backstepping strategies to create a secure consensus controller, ensuring that the tracking error has asymptotically approached zero. Additionally, the detrimental effects of DoS attacks have been fully addressed and neutralized. Ultimately, simulation outcomes have validated the effectiveness of the proposed approach for achieving adaptive asymptotic tracking control.

articleTitle: Distributed Constrained Optimization with Uncoordinated Step Sizes: A Case Study on Ethylene Plant
abstract: This paper investigates an uncoordinated step sizes distributed optimization algorithm based on an undirected topology network structure, which can handle distributed optimization problems with inequality constraints and heterogeneity (losing the global clock) by only communicating with neighboring nodes. Firstly, an “Adapt-Then-Combine Distributed Inexact Gradient tracking subject to Inequality Constraints (ATC-DIGing-IC)” algorithm is proposed for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>-strongly convex and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l$</tex>-smooth objective functions. Using the “Adapt-Then-Combine (ATC)” framework and the gradient information tracking structure, the flexibility and fastness of the algorithm can be guaranteed under the uncoordinated step size. Then, a parameter projection technique is introduced to handle the inequality constraints without introducing additional auxiliary variables. Subsequently, the convergence results of the algorithm and the bounds on the uncoordinated step sizes are theoretically analyzed. Finally, the algorithm is applied to a plant-wide separation production process of an ethylene plant, and the experimental results show that the proposed algorithm requires a shorter optimization time than the existing methods.

articleTitle: Optimization of Train Operation Strategy for Single-track Freight Railway Based on Cooperative Game Theory
abstract: Single-track railways play an important role in freight railway networks. The increasing demand for transportation cannot be met by the current railway capacity. Due to the single-track railway having only one track in the section, potential conflicts exist in trains. In view of this, the same dwell time at each intermediate station is adopted in conventional operation strategies. To improve line utilization, cooperative game theory is employed to addresses the optimization of the dwell time and departure interval of trains. Specifically, a cooperative operation model is constructed to minimize the game cost which is composed of the departure interval at starting station, total dwell time and running time of trains. The Shapley theorem is applied to allocate the operational time among the trains. An improved coyote optimization algorithm (ICOA) is designed to obtain the operation strategy. Finally, a case study is conducted on a single-track freight railway in China to verify the effectiveness of operation strategy.

Author Keywords: cooperative game and improved coyote optimization algorithm

articleTitle: Performance Guaranteed Composite Adaptive Neural Consensus Control for Uncertain Multiagent Systems
abstract: This article studies performance guaranteed composite adaptive neural consensus control problem of uncertain multiagent systems over a directed graph. First, a piecewise function is adopted to characterize fixed-time prescribed performance (FPP), and barrier functions are constructed to achieve the prescribed system performance. Next, hybrid echo state networks (HESNs) are constructed and employed to approximate unknown nonlinear dynamics. To realize smooth and fast learning, adaptive neural predictors are designed, and the predictor errors are fused with barrier functions or virtual control errors to design composite adaptive weights update laws of HESNs. Then, a novel FPP composite adaptive consensus control strategy is proposed. It ensures prescribed tracking performance and high-precision NN approximation performance. Finally, the availability of the proposed strategy is confirmed through simulation studies.

articleTitle: Advanced Detrending and Denoising of Industrial Oscillation Data Utilizing CiSSA
abstract: Oscillation is a significant indication of the deterioration of control system performance and needs to be carefully monitored to ensure safe and stable process operations. However, industrial processes are often prone to noisy artifacts and nonstationary trends, resulting in low signal-to-noise ratios. In order to tackle this problem, this study introduces a novel framework for enhanced trend removal and noise reduction, which is featured by the following steps:(i) The circulant singular spectrum analysis (CiSSA) is used to decompose oscillation data into several reconstructed components (RCs). (ii) The estimated power spectral density (PSD) of these RCs is then smoothed using the Savitzky-Golay filter (SGF) to eliminate noise and identify the RCs corresponding to oscillatory components. (iii) These identified RCs are subsequently reconstructed to produce purified oscillatory data. The effectiveness of the suggested approach is validated using simulations and real-world industrial case studies. The findings indicate that the method notably enhances the quality of oscillatory data.

articleTitle: Neural Network-Based Model Predictive Control with Active Disturbance Rejection for Quadrotor Systems
abstract: Rejecting external disturbances and addressing model uncertainties are critical objectives in control system design. In this paper, we propose a neural network-based model predictive control with active disturbance rejection (NNADR-MPC) strategy for quadrotor systems. This approach utilizes neural networks to learn model uncertainties and designs a neural network-based disturbance observer (DO) to achieve active disturbance rejection control. In combination with model predictive control, the system can rapidly adapt to and handle disturbances caused by partially known suspended loads on a quadrotor during trajectory tracking tasks in the presence of model uncertainty. The designed observer has bounded input bounded output (BIBO) stability guarantees. A comparative study is conducted with existing anti-interference methods for quadrotors under suspended load disturbances. The results show that the proposed control strategy can effectively estimate the disturbance and improve the tracking effect of the quadrotor on the reference trajectory.

articleTitle: Siamese Neural Network-Based Quality-Related Abnormality Detection for Sintering Process
abstract: The sintering process serves as a crucial pretreatment unit in ironmaking, supplying the primary raw materials for the blast furnace. Accurately and real-time estimating the quality of the final sintered ore holds significant importance. Nonetheless, the sintering process data is marred by complexities such as nonlinearity, nonstationarity, non-Gaussianity, and dynamic behaviors, which complicate the application of traditional fault detection methods. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach employing Siamese neural networks for quality-related abnormality detection (SNN-QAD) for the sintering process, focusing specifically on detecting abnormalities in the ferrous oxide (FeO) content of sintered ore. Siamese neural networks are initially used to isolate quality-related stationary features, adeptly navigating the data's nonlinear properties. The Wasserstein distance is then applied to gauge the dissimilarity between distributions, tackling the non-Gaussian distribution challenge. These stationary features are subsequently leveraged as input for a regression model, with the FeO content acting as the output variable, to facilitate training. Hotelling's <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{T}^{2})$</tex> statistic is employed to identify deviations and pinpoint fault occurrences. The paper culminates with the experimental validation of our method using actual sintering process data.

articleTitle: Obstacle avoidance parking based on improved deep reinforcement learning SAC algorithm
abstract: Recent research uses neural-network-based approaches to generate time-optimized parking trajectories in linear time. However, the generalization of these neural networks in different parking lot scenarios is not fully considered and relies on high-quality data. To address these issues, this paper proposes an improved soft actor critic (SA C)-based parking trajectory planning method to achieve fast convergence and high success rate. A trajectory data-based reward function and an experience replay sampling strategy are designed simultaneously improve the learning efficiency. Meanwhile, the Flatten-T Swish Plus (FTSPlus) activation function is firstly introduced into the SAC's neural network structure to enhance the convergence capabilities. The simulation results show that compared with traditional SAC methods, the success rate has been greatly improved and convergence rate has also been improved by more than 60%. Furthermore, it has the good model generalization ability while maintaining collision-free traj ectories.

articleTitle: GASIL-SAC: A Novel Reinforcement Learning Algorithm for Mapless Navigation of Wheeled Mobile Robots
abstract: Efficient and safe mapless navigation in unknown environments is critical for deploying mobile robots in diverse real-world scenarios. However, existing methods based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and imitation learning (IL) often suffer from low sample efficiency and distribution mismatch, respectively. In this paper, we propose GASIL-SAC, a novel reinforcement learning algorithm that combines Generative Adversarial Self-Imitation Learning (GASIL) with Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) for mapless navigation of wheeled mobile robots. To address the issue of overfitting to limited expert data, we introduce a diversity-prioritized positive memory buffer to collect the agent's past good trajectories, ensuring a diverse set of expert demonstrations. We trained a mapless motion planner using the GASIL-SAC algorithm in a 2D simulation environment and conducted comprehensive comparisons with planners based on SAC and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithms. The results demonstrate that GASIL-SAC achieves stable performance more rapidly and generalizes better to previously unseen scenarios, highlighting its effectiveness for mapless navigation tasks.

articleTitle: Extracting and Predicting of Industrial Quality Knowledge with Relation Attention Networks
abstract: Actual industrial production is often accompanied by a large number of miscellaneous production data, but these data can not be fully used. This paper provides an idea for mining the potential value of data from industrial production by using data association analysis and knowledge embedding model. Firstly, to get the correlation degree between features from the production data, the grey correlation analysis method is adopted. Then, the product quality correlation degree knowledge graph is formed based on heterogeneous relation attention networks. Furthermore, the unknown quality knowledge is derived by using the knowledge embedding model. Finally, the validity of the applied method is verified with the specified data set.

articleTitle: Autonomous Navigation Algorithm for GEO Satellites During Hall Thruster Trajectory Control in All-Time
abstract: This paper mainly studies the autonomous navigation and orbit propagation algorithm of the Hall electric propulsion as the thrust control device for geostationary orbit satellites during the thrust control period. Compared with low-altitude satellites, high-altitude satellites generally have relatively poor GNSS velocity measurement accuracy during thrust control, as well as small thrust generated by the Hall electric propulsion, and the tachometer on the large-inertia, large-mass satellite cannot accurately measure the thrust control acceleration, resulting in a decline in the original autonomous navigation accuracy during thrust control. This paper proposes a joint autonomous navigation algorithm for the Hall electric propulsion during thrust control using the EKF and local optimal filtering. The EKF filter suppresses the measurement white noise of the GNSS positioning data, and then the local optimal filter estimates the Hall electric propulsion acceleration and feeds it back to the EKF filter algorithm in real time to improve the navigation accuracy of the Hall electric propulsion during operation. Simulation results show that the joint autonomous navigation algorithm based on the above filtering method can accurately estimate the size of the Hall electric propulsion acceleration, and can effectively improve the autonomous navigation accuracy during continuous small thrust control.

articleTitle: Real-Time Traffic Management of High-Speed Trains: A Novel Approach Combining Optimization with Machine Learning
abstract: The real-time traffic control of high-speed trains (HSTs) is an important task in railway networks to reduce the delay time of trains in case of unexpected disruptions. Traditional approaches are based on mixed-integer programming (MILP) formulations to be solved by optimization methods such as branch-and-bound (B&B), which however require a very long time in real-world problems. Our study introduces a novel methodology that employs machine learning (ML) techniques to accelerate the optimization of MILPs. Specifically, our approach develops a feedforward network, which can be trained off-line, to predict the optimal MILP parameter configurations for the control of HSTs. Additionally, we develop a differential evolution (DE) algorithm, which fine-tunes these parameters in response to dynamic conditions. We conduct numerical experiments based on the real-world data of Beijing-Zhangjiakou high-speed railway (BZHR). The results demonstrate that our ML-accelerated approach significantly outperforms traditional optimization methods, improving the solution performance by 21.47%.

articleTitle: DBTE-CAM: Fault Diagnosis for the Chiller Based on Dual-Branch Transformer Encoder
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the characteristic parameters of the chiller fault operation data are coupled and the timing features are difficult to extract, a fault diagnosis model named DBTE-CAM is proposed in this paper. The model combines an ensemble feature selection strategy, a dual-branch Transformer encoder, and a cross-attention mechanism. Firstly, an ensemble feature selection method based on sequence forward search is adopted, combining the minimal-redundancy-maximal-relevance (mRMR) algorithm and the random forest algorithm, to obtain the most indicative and discriminative fault-relevant features. Then, utilizing a dual-branch Transformer encoder structure for feature encoding, taking into account the timing dependence of single variables and the correlation between feature variables. Finally, the feature information from the two branches is fused by the cross-attention mechanism, and the fault diagnosis is performed by the Softmax classifier. The experimental data from ASHRAE RP-1043 is used to verify the effectiveness of the diagnostic framework. The experimental results show that the model can accurately identify faults in chiller units, with a diagnostic accuracy of 98.34% on the dataset of fault level L1 (the lowest severity). Compared with CNN, LSTM and other mainstream fault diagnosis models, it achieves better diagnostic results.

articleTitle: A Two-Layer Ensemble Deep Learning Model for Acoustic Seabed Sediment Classification
abstract: Seabed sediment information is widely utilized in marine exploration and management. Recent breakthroughs of sonar technology and data processing method have spurred the development of automated seabed sediment classification techniques. However, the variability and complexity of sonar data present a series of challenges that must be addressed before acoustic sediment classification technology can be practically applied. Traditional methods for classifying seabed sediments often struggle with the complexity and variability of acoustic data, leading to misclassification and instability in sediment type predictions. To address these challenges, we develop a robust ensemble framework that integrates several deep learning models, to leverage the strengths of each model. Experiments conducted on real sonar datasets demonstrate that the ensemble deep learning model outperforms any individual model and traditional ensemble learning model, achieving higher accuracy and better generalization. These results also highlight the potential of ensemble deep learning in tackling the intricacies of practical seabed sediment classification.

articleTitle: SLAM Based on Visual Semantics and Laser Fusion
abstract: As one of the main sensors of SLAM mapping, LiDAR has been widely studied and used because of its high precision and stable performance. However, in degraded environments where geometric features such as corridors or movement along single-sided walls are scarce, it is difficult for LiDAR to obtain sufficient feature information, resulting in reduced mapping accuracy. Therefore, a SLAM mapping method based on visual semantics and laser fusion is proposed. This method not only realizes SLAM mapping through LiDAR, but also uses visual deep learning algorithm to extract the semantic information of objects, and determines the relative position of the target by combining the depth data of the depth camera. Finally, the target position is mapped to the world coordinate system through coordinate conversion, and the target semantic annotation is realized in the map. The experimental results show that this method not only improves the accuracy of map construction and enriches the semantic information of the map, but also has high reliability of target location, which can meet the actual needs, make up for the shortcomings of LiDAR in the environment with scarce features, and improve the scene understanding and classification ability of the system.

articleTitle: Global Path Planning for Amphibious Robots Based on Improved Q-Learning
abstract: Aiming at the problems of excessive energy consumption, slow convergence speed and long running time of amphibious robots in 3D environment, this paper presents an optimized path planning method using improved Q-learning for amphibious robots. The algorithm combines the Dyna framework with Q-learning, which integrates modelling, learning and planning to boost the algorithm's rate of convergence. Meanwhile, the artificial potential field method is introduced to initialize the Q-value by using the potential value of the environment as the search inspiration information to improve the convergence speed. The dynamic exploration factor is introduced to make the algorithm quickly adapt to the environmental changes and improve optimization efficiency. Finally, considering the different energy consumption of movement in different environments, the reward function is crafted to facilitate the amphibious robot to choose an optimal path with the lowest energy consumption. According to the simulation results, the optimized algorithm accelerates the convergence speed, improves the learning efficiency, reduces the energy consumption, and enables the amphibious robot to quickly find a non-colliding trajectory with low energy consumption.

articleTitle: Unmanned Ship Path Planning Based on Improved Genetic Algorithm
abstract: In order to solve the problems of excessive steering angle and high collision risk when intelligent ships plan paths in restricted waters such as inland waterways, port space and strait channels, this paper proposes a path planning algorithm based on improved genetic algorithm. This method designs a restricted random initialization method to generate an initial population to generate multiple collision-free paths, improves the quality of the initial population, and designs adaptive crossover and mutation operators to improve the convergence ability of the algorithm. For multi-objective optimization problems, the Pareto-binary tournament selection operator is used. According to the shortest path, the best smoothness and the safest path, half of the population is selected for crossover and mutation. The security operator is used to keep the path outside the safe distance. Taking the shortest path and the optimal smoothness as the fitness function, the unmanned ship path planning system is established. The deletion operator is used to delete the redundant path points, and the security operator is further used to regenerate the path points that are not kept outside the safe distance.

articleTitle: An Improved Prescribed-Time Privacy-Preserving Average Consensus Algorithm for First-Order Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Privacy issues, communication constraints and convergence performance are key factors for expanding applications of multi-agent systems, but considering the above three factors simultaneously has not been well addressed. In order to extend the practical application scenarios and fill such gaps, the paper proposes an improved prescribed-time privacy-preserving consensus method based on event-triggered mechanism. Unlike the traditional privacy protection scheme, proposed method adopts a decentralized (executed separately by every agent), time-varying transformation to encrypt the information. Agents encode their true states in virtue of independent key before transmitting them, which makes the agents' internal states indecipherable from others. On this basis, the prescribed-time theory is introduced to achieve convergence at any specified time within the range allowed by the actuator performance. In addition, event-triggered mechanism can effectively relieve the actuator pressure caused by frequent updates and reduce computational resource consumption. Finally, the validity of theoretical results is verified by numerical simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Image-Based Detection of the Fineness Modulus of Manufactured Sand
abstract: With the improvement of economic levels, the quantity and scale of buildings continue to increase, enhancing the importance of manufactured sand. Fineness modulus is the most important indicator for measuring the performance of manufactured sand. However, current methods for detecting the fineness modulus are time-consuming, labor-intensive, and costly. To address these problems, this paper proposes a method based on an instance segmentation model in deep learning, revealing for the first time the relationship between the fineness modulus and image features, and establishes a regression model based on this relationship. Additionally, a manufactured sand fineness modulus detection system is designed in this paper, thereby achieving automated detection of the fineness modulus of manufactured sand, saving labor and reducing detection costs.

articleTitle: Few-shot Pose-free View Synthesis with 3D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Recent advancements in Novel View Synthesis using neural radiance fields and 3D Gaussian splatting have demon-strated promising results. However, these methods conventionally rely on accurate initial poses and point clouds from the model of structure from motion, which poses challenges in sparse input views. To addressing these drawbacks, we introduces an novel method for view synthesis based on 3D Gaussian splatting. Our approach operates on sparse input views without the prerequisite of pose priors, achieving reconstruction and real-time rendering of novel perspectives. For the deficiency of camera poses and point cloud, we employ an end- to-end deep learning model to recover the 3D structure from a few of 2D images to initialize the 3D Gaussian point cloud. In addressing the issue with few-shot, we utilize the differentiable rasterization module to render depth map and apply regulation on it. Additionally, we incorporate supervision between input views by interpolating to generate novel perspectives during training. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method significantly enhances the capabilities of 3D Gaussian splatting for novel view synthesis in sparse views and without the necessity of camera pose priors.

articleTitle: Research on Adaptive Model Pooling Method for Data Stream Anomaly Detection Based on Variational Auto-Encoder
abstract: Abnormal detection is vital for fault warning in industrial production and safety in daily life. However, the challenge of constantly evolving data streams, influenced by external factors and performance degradation, presents a significant hurdle in this regard. Unfortunately, existing anomaly detection methods are unable to cope with these issues effectively. The models are unable to adapt to data streams with constantly changing distributions, which results in poor anomaly detection performance. To address this problem, this paper proposes VAE-ARCUS, an adaptive model pooling online abnormal detection method based on variational autoencoders. This is achieved by modifying the original autoencoder model, which is implemented within the ARCUS framework, into a variational autoencoder. This enables the model to achieve greater accuracy and to grasp the characteristics of the data distribution more effectively, thus alleviating the issues associated with the overfitting of the base autoencoder model to noisy data. Finally, experimental results conducted on six high-dimensional and concept drift datasets show that the model outperforms other autoencoder-based models and common stream anomaly detection methods in detecting anomalies and generalizing the model's capabilities.

articleTitle: An EMU Bogie Defect Detection Method Based on Similarity Comparison
abstract: With the rapid growth in the number of high-speed railway Electric Multiple Units (EMUs), ensuring their safe operation and efficient maintenance becomes crucial. Due to the scarcity of defect samples, the data-driven deep learning methods are not applicable in this scenario. This study proposes a non-data-driven defect detection strategy based on similarity comparison, aiming to improve the intelligence level of EMU maintenance. Firstly, the Improved Deformable DETR model with embedded prior knowledge of labels, is employed for the accurate detection of train bogie components, obtaining 2D bounding boxes. Then an initial defect diagnosis is performed by comparing the test component's image to a reference image using Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), and enhanced by Support Vector Machine (SVM) analysis. Furthermore, point cloud data comparison with standard point clouds via the Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm pinpoints defects like looseness and loss. In addition, complex defects such as the loss of large parts and deformed foreign objects at random locations are detected by overall registration of the entire point cloud to be detected and the standard point cloud, Z-axis difference analysis and clustering. In order to solve the time-consuming problem of overall registration, twostage-ICP is proposed to improve efficiency. By combining the above methods, this study can comprehensively detect defects such as looseness, loss and deformation of EMU components, providing a strong guarantee for the safe operation of EMU.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Driven One-Step Fastening in Robotic Flexible Printed Circuit Assembly
abstract: Nowadays, robots are widely used in various assembly tasks in industry. However, in the assembly task of tiny parts such as mobile phone flexible printed circuit (FPC), it is often necessary to conduct multi-step analysis of multi-modal information such as visual and tactile information to achieve the final fastening of mobile phone FPC. And because the robot has errors in perceiving tactile information, the resulting multi-step fastening strategy is not reliable enough, which makes it difficult for the robot to improve the fastening accuracy and success rate of mobile phone FPC. To this end, this work proposes a digital twin (DT) driven one-step fastening method for mobile phone FPC based on adaptive gradient. The contributions mainly include the following. First, in order to reduce the perception error of real tactile information, we proposed a tactile perception method in a DT environment. In addition to obtaining real tactile data through tactile sensors in a real environment, virtual tactile data is also obtained by simulating the deformation of the soft cable using the material point method (MPM) in a virtual environment. Secondly, in order to achieve the one-step strategy for fastening mobile phone FPC, we proposed an adaptive gradient prediction model based on virtual and real tactile images. By comparing the virtual and real tactile image sequences in the DT environment, adaptive gradient calculation is performed, and the adjustment strategy sequences are input into the LSTM network to predict the adjustment strategy at the fastening moment, thereby achieving fast and efficient fastening of mobile phone FPC, effectively improving the execution efficiency of the robotic arm and the synthetic power of the mobile phone FPC fastening. The experiments were carried out on the actual assembly platform of the Redmi Note 11 mobile phone. With the number of failed trails limited, our approach significantly outperforms vision-only and DT-free approaches.

articleTitle: Building Intrinsically Interpretable Deep Neural Networks: A Survey
abstract: Deep neural network has achieved remarkable success in fields such as image classification and object detection, sometimes even outperforming humans, but the black-box nature of deep neural networks limits their application in areas where the reasons for decisions need to be known. The increasing demand for more transparent and reliable models has led to the emergence of explainable machine learning, and more and more researchers have turned their attention to the interpretability of deep neural networks in an attempt to explore the inference process of the model by investigating the black-box properties of the network. Based on the different stages of explanation generation, we can broadly classify interpretable neural networks into two categories: post-hoc interpretable models and intrinsically interpretable models. In recent years, there have been numerous researches on interpretable neural networks, but nevertheless, there is still a lack of a unified classification and summary of the construction of intrinsically interpretable networks. In this paper, we review several typical approaches to building intrinsically interpretable neural networks in the field of image classification that have proposed in recent years, classify them according to the way they achieve interpretability, and summarize the strengths and weaknesses of each type of approach. Furthermore, we provide an outlook on future developments in this field.

articleTitle: A Novel Bearing Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Deep Incremental Learning
abstract: In the face of continuous dynamic changes in working conditions, the static deep learning bearing fault diagnosis model gradually loses its effectiveness. To this end, a novel bearing fault diagnosis method based on deep incremental learning is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a one-dimensional signal is converted into a two-dimensional image by Gramian angle field (GAF) to realize the extraction of global features of the input signal. The image is dimensionally transformed and input into a selectable classification network, which can improve the robustness and generalization ability of the model. Secondly, a parameter importance estimation method based on the change of loss value is designed. It can effectively alleviate the catastrophic forgetting problem in incremental learning caused by inaccurate estimation of the importance of the parameters of old working conditions. Then, the gradient clipping method using Huber regularization eliminates the gradient explosion induced by the quadratic terms in the regularization process. Finally, the validity of the method was verified with a dataset from the bearing data center of Case Western Reserve University. The results show that when dealing with incremental faults, the method can achieve diagnostic accuracies of 97.75% and 98.25% on different classification networks, respectively. And it can well overcome the stability-plasticity dilemma.

articleTitle: Large-Scale EV Charging Using Genetic Algorithm with Greedy Constraint Repair Mechanism
abstract: In this paper, we propose an efficient approach based on genetic algorithms for scheduling the charging of large-scale electric vehicles (EVs) under various constraints. This problem is typically framed as an integer linear programming (ILP) issue, akin to other assignment problems. Two critical and unresolved challenges in EV charging are minimizing the total charging cost (Objective 1) and meeting both customer and grid constraints (Objective 2). To address Objective 1, we introduce the fitness function defined in Eq (3) to evaluate charging costs. The population evolves towards minimizing these costs until the termination condition is met. For Objective 2, we propose a swap operation that ensures time and state-of-charge (SOC) constraints are maintained throughout the repair process. Additionally, we present customized repair operators to address power limit constraints and three-phase imbalance constraints. In comparison to two widely used solvers, CBC and Surro-gateopt, our method demonstrates superior performance. CBC struggles with more than 1500 EVs, leading to extended computation times, while Surrogateopt encounters resource limitations with over 50 EVs. Our approach, however, is capable of finding near-optimal solutions for larger-scale EV problems on the same computer, with greater efficiency than these solvers. Moreover, our proposed algorithm exhibits nearly linear computational complexity, enabling it to handle large-scale constraint problems effectively.

articleTitle: A Gap Inference Neural Network for Efficient Collision Detection in Robotic Arm Path Planning
abstract: With the widespread application of robots in industrial manufacturing and service sectors, the safety and efficiency of path planning in complex dynamic environments have become increasingly important. Collision detection is an essential step in path planning, yet traditional methods based on geometric models or physical simulations often face challenges such as low computational efficiency and inadequate adaptability to complex dynamic environments. In this paper, we propose a Gap Inference Network (GIN) for efficient collision detection in robotic arm path planning. This network aims to enhance the efficiency of collision detection during path planning in complex and dynamic environments. We employ a voxelization strategy to partition the robotic arm's workspace into uniformly distributed cubic units, and we collect an extensive dataset of gaps between the robotic arm and all cubic units corresponding to various joint configurations. The GIN is trained to learn the complex nonlinear mapping between the joint configurations and The Gap Field of all cubic units relative to the robotic arm. This enables rapid batch inference of The Gap Field for any given robotic arm joint configuration, significantly improving collision detection efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that the GIN achieves an average collision prediction accuracy of 92.23 % and an average non-collision prediction accuracy of 98.44%, markedly enhancing the efficiency of collision detection.

articleTitle: Lightweight Infrared Maritime Target Detection Algorithm Based on Fusion Shuffling Convolutional Attention
abstract: Infrared maritime target detection is fundamental in maritime rescue and maritime security fields. We collected an infrared maritime target dataset and found that the texture details of infrared images are blurry, leading to poor detection performance by algorithms. To address this, we propose a lightweight infrared maritime target detection algorithm based on fusion shuffling convolutional attention. This algorithm employs the lightweight network EfficientformerV2 as the backbone for feature extraction, reducing model parameters while ensuring feature extraction capability. Additionally, the algorithm introduces the Dysample upsampler to efficiently restore the resolution of infrared image features with minimal computational cost, mitigating the accuracy loss caused by lightweighting. Finally, we propose the lightweight mixed attention mechanism called fusion shuffling convolutional attention, which effectively extracts spatial and channel features of images with only a slight increase in parameters. Experiments were conducted using our self-collected infrared maritime target dataset to train the model. Results show that, compared to RT-DETR, our algorithm's mAP@0.5 increased by 1.2%, reaching 87.5%, while the number of parameters and computational cost decreased by 63% and 71.4%, respectively. The improved algorithm enhances detection performance while significantly reducing parameters and computational cost.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Multivariate Long-Term Time Series Robust Forecasting Model with Distinguishable Variable Identifier
abstract: Recently, in the field of multivariate long-term series prediction, Linear models have benefited from the training strategy of Channel Independence, outperforming most previous Transformer-based models and questioning the ability of the attention mechanism to capture time dependence. To regain the Transformer's dominance, we have further improved the Patch-based Transformer model, but some articles point out that the model designed based on Channel Independence has the defect of spatial indistinguishability. In order to solve this problem, our Variable Identifier, embedding corresponding to a specific variable, is specially designed for the Transformer model to give it the ability to distinguish among different variables. The Variable Identifier we have learned can also roughly describe the similarity between variables. In addition, to enhance the model's resistance to data noise interference and prevent overfitting, we incorporate a novel loss function that combines the advantages of both Mean Squared Error and Mean Absolute Error loss functions. In order to further improve the model's performance but not add extra computation, we try to design a multi-scale CNN structure inspired by computer vision. Finally, our model outperforms recently proposed linear models and previous Transformer-based models, and our extensive experiments on widely used open-source datasets show a maximum 4.4% relative improvement over state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Simulation and Transfer of Physical Image Features Based on Recurrent Generative Adversarial Networks
abstract: Training machine learning models in virtual environments often fails to generalize effectively to real-world applications. The discrepancy between simulated and real environments results in suboptimal performance of the learned models. Various approaches have been proposed to address this “simulation-to-reality gap,” including refining training images within simulations or randomizing virtual environments to narrow the disparity. A CycleGAN model is used to convert simulated images into real ones for correction, but this method remains task-agnostic and does not preserve task-specific information, which can negatively affect task performance. Critical features, particularly those directly related to the task, may be lost during translation, which can compromise task success. To address this issue, conditional information is introduced during the image transformation process to ensure that task-relevant features, such as location data, are retained. This method makes the transformation task-aware rather than task-agnostic. Additionally, skip connections are implemented to mitigate blurring in the generated images. The proposed method has been trained on a custom dataset from a laboratory environment and validated on a robotic arm. This approach significantly improves the accuracy of image conversion tasks and enhances the efficiency of sim-to-real image translation.

articleTitle: Knowledge Graph Completion for Industrial Robots Based on Graph Attention Network
abstract: The current state of the knowledge graph for industrial robots is confronted with several significant challenges. One issue is the insufficient fault data of industrial robots, which results in an inadequate number of nodes and edges in the knowledge graph and a pervasive problem of data sparsity. Additionally, industrial robots encompass a wide array of diverse and complex fault types, leading to intricate correlations and interactions among different fault types. In response to these challenges, this study proposes a method called BAKGAT for complementing the knowledge graph of industrial robot faults. BAKGAT leverages the semantic understanding and feature extraction capabilities of BERT, in conjunction with the multi-hop neighbor node information aggregation proficiency of KBGAT, thereby enhancing node and relation representation and capturing complex semantic relationship information more effectively. Furthermore, BAKGAT introduces an attention attenuation mechanism to mitigate the impact of distant nodes and amplify the attention weight of neighboring nodes, thereby facilitating the more precise capture of local structural information. To validate the efficacy of the proposed method, a series of comparative experiments was performed on two benchmark datasets, WN18RR and FB15k-237, as well as the industrial robot fault dataset IRF9K. The experimental results demonstrated that BAKGAT surpasses the performance of the baseline models, highlighting its superior effectiveness in addressing sparse and heterogeneous data.

articleTitle: CMBSR: Contrastive Multi-Behavior Social Recommendation via Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Most of the traditional recommendation algorithms are based on single-behavior interaction, ignoring the multiple-interaction behaviors displayed by users in reality. In the real world, there is far more than one type of interaction between users and items. For example, in e-commerce platforms, users may perform various operations such as collecting, adding a shopping cart, and purchasing, which reflect users' different intentions and preferences for items. At the same time, multi-behavior recommendations still seriously suffer from the problem of limited supervision signals. This paper proposes a Contrastive Multi-Behavior Social Recommendation model named CMBSR to solve the above problems. Based on multi-behavior social rec-ommendation algorithm, we add three comparison mechanisms: multi-behavior comparison, user social interaction comparison and item knowledge comparison, which make full use of multi-behavior information, social information and item knowledge to capture user complex preferences and behavior patterns. Experimental results show that CMBSR performs significantly better than other advanced algorithms on multiple datasets. Especially on the Tmall dataset, CMBSR achieves a 4.958% and 5.923% performance improvement on HR@10 and NDCG@10 compared with the sub-optimal result, respectively.

articleTitle: Finite-time Prescribed Performance Cooperative Control of Multiple Unmanned Aerial Vehicles under Actuator Faults
abstract: This paper proposes a finite-time prescribed performance fault-tolerant cooperative control method for multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) encountering actuator faults. First, the model of the UAV is transformed into a control-oriented model, and the actuator faults are considered in the study. Then, an adaptive adjustment signal is introduced into prescribed performance function to enhance the robustness, thereby improving its control performance. Moreover, a finite-time radial basis function neural network disturbance observer is constructed to deal with the unknown nonlinear terms caused by faults. Finally, simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

Author Keywords: radial basis function neural network disturbance observer

articleTitle: EDFFF: Ensemble Distillation Framework based on Fourier Features
abstract: Domain generalization enables the model to extrapolate its learning to an unfamiliar test distribution, showcasing its ability to adapt and apply knowledge across diverse domains. Deep convolutional neural networks have significantly improved the generalization ability of models due to their enhanced fitting capabilities and deep feature extraction abilities. Current domain generalization models are still susceptible to irrelevant factors and do not effectively address the correlation shift caused by these factors or the diversity shift caused by style differences. To tackle these issues, we propose an Ensemble Distillation Framework based on Fourier Features (EDFFF). This framework utilizes features learned by teacher models through distillation learning to train student models. Specifically, phase reconstruction is employed to retain main body information while amplitude mixing is used to mitigate style differences between domains during the data manipulation. Furthermore, ensemble teacher models learn from images augmented by different augmentation strategies, emphasizing the heterogeneity of features learned by the student model from these ensemble teacher models. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EDFFF achieves superior accuracy on both correlation shift datasets and diversity shift datasets.

articleTitle: Reliability Assessment of Islanded Microgrids Considering Generation-Load Uncertainty
abstract: Due to the volatility and uncertainty of renewable energy, as well as the constantly changing load demand, the reliability assessment of islanded microgrids faces significant challenges. To address this issue, this paper proposes a reliability assessment method for islanded microgrids considering source-load uncertainties. Firstly, an uncertainty model of the islanded microgrid system is established: the “failure-repair” time series model is used to simulate the life process of the micro gas turbine unit; the “normal-deficiency-shutdown” time series model combined with wind and photovoltaic prediction errors is used to simulate the uncertainty of wind and solar power; a load uncertainty model considering load prediction errors is established; a storage charge-discharge model considering energy storage life is established. Secondly, the CNN-BILSTM-MATT (Convolutional Neural Network - Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory Multi-head Attention) hybrid model optimized by the RIME algorithm is used to predict wind, solar, and load; combined with the Adaptive Bandwidth Kernel Density Estimation (ABKDE) method, interval prediction of wind and solar power is realized. Then, within the wind and solar prediction interval, Monte Carlo sampling is used to obtain the actual power of the simulated wind and solar output; finally, combined with the predicted power load data, conventional generators, and energy storage status, the reliability index of the microgrid is calculated.

articleTitle: Digital Twin-assisted Gearbox Fault Diagnosis Framework using Hybrid Adversarial Domain Discriminative Networks
abstract: In industrial applications, fault diagnosis of gear-boxes is critical for ensuring the reliability and safe operation of machinery and equipment. However, data-driven fault diagnosis techniques rely heavily on high-quality labeled data for training, which is often difficult to obtain in real industrial scenarios. To address this challenge, this paper presents a digital twin fault diagnosis framework. First, the digital twin technique is utilized to build a virtual model of a gearbox that generates sufficient labeled fault data. Second, we develop a hybrid adversarial domain discriminative network, which incorporates a spatial channel reconstruction convolution module instead of a conventional residual network to enhance the model's feature extraction capabilities. Additionally, we propose a dynamic weighted joint distribution adaptation method to improve domain confusion capability, minimizing the granularity of features between the two types of data. Finally, the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed method are validated through experiments.

articleTitle: Cabin Temperature and Humidity Comfort Control for Electric Vehicles in High Temperature and Humidity Environment
abstract: With the gradual increase of the market share of electric vehicles, their endurance mileage in extreme temperature environment has become the most concerned indicator for consumers and the comfort control of the cabin is directly related to the battery range. In order to further improve the energy efficiency level of the whole vehicle, this paper introduces a hybrid hierarchical and centralized Model Predictive Control(MPC) that balances energy consumption with temperature and humidity control, enabling precise regulation of the temperature and humidity within the vehicle cabin. Firstly, dynamic equations for the cabin temperature and humidity are established based on the automotive air-conditioning simulation model CoolSim, and the model parameters are obtained through linear regression fitting. Secondly, a sensitivity relationship between the air-conditioning system and vehicle speed is established through statistical analysis, so that an expression for the energy consumption of the air-conditioning system as a function of vehicle speed is derived. Finally, the hybird control algorithm is employed to achieve coordinated control of temperature, humidity, and energy consumption within the air-conditioning system. The simulation results show that the hybrid control algorithm is effective and can reduce the energy consumption of the air conditioning system on the premise of ensuring the comfort of cabin temperature and humidity.

articleTitle: Trajectory Planning for Unmanned Surface Vessels in Confined Waters
abstract: This paper presents a novel trajectory planning method for unmanned surface vessels (USVs) operating in confined waters. The proposed approach formulates the planning problem as an optimal control problem, considering the vessel's dynamics and environmental constraints. Obstacle avoidance is formulated as a separation problem using the hyperplane separation theorem, while collision avoidance with boundaries is modeled as a containment problem using smooth, differentiable constraints. This formulation allows for efficient solving using gradient-based optimization algorithms. A geometry-based method for initializing auxiliary variables is introduced to improve computational performance. The method is validated through a simulated case study of USV docking in a confined port with static and dynamic obstacles. Results demonstrate the ability to generate optimal, collision-free trajectories that satisfy dynamic constraints and navigate complex environments.

articleTitle: Improved Adaptive-Gain Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Control of Transmission Line Inspection UAVs
abstract: This paper presents an improved adaptive-gain super-twisting sliding mode control method for transmission line inspection unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to track desired trajectories in the presence of external disturbances. A cascaded control structure is designed to compute the desired accelerations using the proposed controller, which are then utilized to determine the desired orientation and angular rates. By dynamically adjusting the gains in the controllers, the chattering problem is effectively suppressed, and the system's transient performance and robustness are significantly enhanced. Furthermore, using Lyapunov function theory, the finite-time stability of the system is rigorously proven. Finally, simulation studies demonstrate the effectiveness and superior performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Deep Spatial-Spectral Multi-Resolution Attention Residual Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification
abstract: Due to its modular design and robust feature extraction capabilities, deep learning has emerged as one of the essential tools in hyperspectral image classification. However, effectively extracting deeper-level features and improving the ability to analyze spatial-spectral information simultaneously remain challenging problems. In response to these issues, a deep spatial-spectral multi-resolution attention residual network is proposed, comprising two critical components: a multi-level transfer fusion residual network and a spatial-spectral multi-resolution fusion attention residual network. By employing different residual blocks, the multi-level transfer fusion residual network can effectively promote interactions between feature information and obtain deeper features. Furthermore, the spatial-spectral multi-resolution fusion attention residual network can adaptively extract and integrate spatial-spectral joint features and multi-resolution features comprehensively from hyperspectral data. The performance was evaluated against other methods on the Pavia University hyperspectral dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that the network proposed in this paper exhibits promising classification performance.

articleTitle: Diagnosing Oral Mucosal Diseases Using Deep Learning
abstract: Oral Potentially Malignant Disorders (OPMD) contain a variety of diseases with complex pathological features, most of which are associated with systemic diseases and have a high risk of malignant transformation, making diagnosis challenging. In this regard, we adopted rapidly developing artificial intelligence methods in recent years, using deep learning for feature extraction and multi-task research on images of oral mucosal diseases. Concerning the severity of oral mucosal diseases, we employed a Swin Transformer-based classification model for the classification of benign diseases, OPMD, and oral cancer, achieving an accuracy of 94.2% and a precision of 95.0%. Further research explored the instance segmentation algorithm based on Mask2Former, comparing it with classic segmentation algorithm to achieve automated segmentation of oral mucosal inflammatory lesions. The study shows that deep learning methods can effectively discriminate the severity of oral mucosal disease images and segment lesion areas, providing solid research foundation for intelligent assisted diagnosis.

articleTitle: Alarm Monitoring for Condensate System in Thermal Power Plants Based on Bayesian Estimation
