abstract: In a thermal power plant, there are numerous pieces of equipment and hundreds of process variables involved, making it difficult for the monitoring system to track all variables simultaneously. Operators determine the key variables that best reflect the condition of the system or equipment based on their experiential knowledge, then analyze data from normal conditions and build a model to obtain estimated values of variables, and the process may be evaluated by the estimation error. This paper employs an AutoRegressive Moving Average model with exogenous variables(ARMAX) to model historical data, yielding more accurate estimated values of variables and designing alarm thresholds. The Bayesian method is used to assess the reliability of estimated alarm thresholds. Used existing Bayesian methods assume a continuous uniform prior distribution, this method introduces a beta distribution to consider more information of prior knowledge. When a new observed data available, the parameters of the Bayesian method can be updated to adapt to the slow change of the operating environment. Practical industrial cases demonstrate the reliability of this method.

articleTitle: PE-SSD: Improved SSD for Small Object Detection
abstract: With the flourishing development of deep learning, object detection technology has achieved encouraging results. However, small objects remain a major challenge in the field of object detection due to their lack of texture and contextual information caused by their small size. Despite such fact, we observed that their edges typically exhibit high contrast in relation to the background. Specifically, we innovatively employ a Laplacian image pyramid incorporated with feature enhancement modules rather than the traditional image pyramid, with the aim of more effectively capturing image details and edge information, given that the Laplacian pyramid has the ability to retain such information within its lower levels. Furthermore, we introduce attention mechanisms to optimize the feature fusion process, thus improving the utilization efficiency of multi-scale features. Taking SSD as the baseline, we propose a novel method called PE-SSD, which integrates the advantages of featureized Laplacian pyramid. Experimental results show that our method achieves higher accuracy in detecting small objects compared to traditional SSD. For inputs of size 512 × 512, the extensive experiments on the VisDrone2019 dataset demonstrates that our method achieves an average precision of 15.4%, surpassing traditional SSD networks by 1.2%. Specifically, The mAP_s score reaches 6.6%, which is 0.4% higher than the baseline network, indicating the effectiveness of our method in the field of small object detection.

articleTitle: ConvMFP-A Convolution-based Multi-source Fusion Prediction Network for Precipitation Nowcasting
abstract: Precipitation nowcasting is very important in coping with extreme weather conditions, but the prediction accuracy of traditional precipitation prediction methods is difficult to improve, and it is impossible to predict problems such as convective initiation. Therefore, this paper proposes a convolution-based multi-source fusion precipitation prediction network (ConvMFP) based on radar echo and satellite cloud image data. The model adopts the encoder-fusion-decoder network structure, combined with the spatial channel attention mechanism, and effectively integrates multi-source features, in order to achieve accurate prediction of severe convective weather system within one hour. Experiments on meteorological datasets in the Yangtze River Delta region show that compared with the traditional optical flow-based methods and some well-known deep learning methods (ConvLSTM, TrajGRU, PredRNN++, RainFormer and SimVP), the accuracy of precipitation prediction is significantly improved, especially in dealing with the prediction problems in the initial generation stage of precipitation.

articleTitle: Optimizing Speech Recognition Models with Effective Confidence Calibrations
abstract: In the domain of speech recognition, deep learning models have achieved tremendous success. Despite the increasing predictive performance of these models, there has been limited focus on uncertainty estimation and calibration, leading to unreliable confidence. To address this challenge, we employed Sparse Gaussian Process Attention (SGPA), which performs Bayesian inference directly within the output space of the Multi-Head Attention (MHA) blocks in Transformers to calibrate its uncertainty. This method replaces the scaled dot-product operation with an effective symmetric kernel and utilizes Sparse Gaussian Process (SGP) techniques to approximate the posterior distribution of the MHA outputs. Experimental results in speech recognition tasks demonstrate that models incorporating SGPA not only maintain their predictive accuracy but also significantly enhance the reliability of their output confidence.

articleTitle: A Physical Information Neural Network (PINN)-Based Model for Soft Measurement of 3D Temperature Field in Aluminium Electrolysers
abstract: Aluminium electrolysers, as the core equipment for aluminium electrolysis, have an internal three-dimensional temperature distribution that directly reflects their working condition and impacts both production quality and safety. Traditional measurement methods and soft measurement techniques are inadequate, and research on high-dimensional data, such as 3D temperature fields, still needs enhancement. In this paper, we propose a PINN-based soft measurement model for the 3D temperature field of aluminium electrolysers. This model uses the operating current and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{x},\ \boldsymbol{y},\ \boldsymbol{z}$</tex> coordinates as inputs to the PINN, and outputs the temperatures at the corresponding positions. The prediction error is less than 1%, and the prediction time is reduced by six orders of magnitude compared to finite element simulations, meeting the requirements for real-time online prediction in engineering applications.

articleTitle: Adaptive Integral Sliding Mode Control with Gaussian Processes for AUVs
abstract: This paper proposes a novel adaptive integral sliding mode control (ISMC) scheme for robust trajectory tracking of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) utilizing Gaussian process (GP) regression. By incorporating GPs into the ISMC framework, the proposed control strategy exhibits robustness against significant system uncertainties and aggressive desired trajectories. The GP posterior means offer high-probability uncertainty compensation, while the posterior variances enable adaptive tuning of controller gains and learning rates. A novel adaptive gain law is introduced to prevent excessive gain growth and nonsmooth control actions near the sliding manifold. Lyapunov stability analysis guarantees that the tracking errors of the proposed scheme converge to an arbitrarily small bound within a specific probability. Simulation results demonstrate the superior transient tracking performance of the proposed method compared to both the standard GP-ISMC without gain adaptation and the adaptive GP-ISMC using standard monotonically increasing adaptive laws.

articleTitle: PathFinder-Based Simulation Study on Passenger Evacuation in Subway Stations During Floods
abstract: When floods backflow into subway stations, passenger movement is severely obstructed, and the safety of lives and property cannot be guaranteed. This paper establishes a simulation system for passenger evacuation movements in subway stations during floods using Fluent and PathFinder software. The impact of flood intrusion on passenger evacuation behavior in subway stations is studied, with a focus on analyzing the effects of the initial intrusion velocity of flood at the inlet, the number of inlets, and the number of passengers on the evacuation efficiency. The simulation results indicate that real-time changes in flood flow velocity and water depth during the invasion process of the flood significantly affect passenger evacuation time. The greater the initial intrusion velocity of flood and the more inlets there are, the higher the risk of instability for passengers during evacuation and the lower the evacuation efficiency. High passenger flow during evacuation can easily lead to congestion, which is detrimental to the evacuation process. Studying the characteristics of passenger evacuation in subway stations under flood scenarios could positively promote both evacuation efficiency and safety.

articleTitle: Anomaly Diagnosis of Catalytic Cracking Process Based on Autoencoder and Causal Model
abstract: The regeneration process of catalytic cracking reactions is the core process of refining and chemical enterprises, which localized anomalies can propagate in cascade, leading to severe consequences. Accurate anomaly diagnosis is crucial for identifying root causes and establishing a basis for implementing refined protective measures to prevent the further propagation of anomalies. Based on this, the paper proposes a method for abnormal detection of root causes in the regeneration process of catalytic cracking reactions. In this method, the Diagonal State Space Autoencoder (DS2AE) is utilized to detect abnormal process variables. In addition, the Maximum Information Coefficient and Time-Delayed Transfer Entropy-based causal analysis method (MIC-TDTE) is employed to construct causal models among variables. Finally, causal graphs are traversed to trace the propagation paths of anomalies, thereby detecting the root causes of anomalies. The proposed method is applied to a dataset of abnormal working conditions constructed from a catalytic cracking process simulation system, demonstrating the effectiveness of the approach.

articleTitle: Robust Robot Control Policy Learning Based on Gaussian Mixture Variational Autoencoders
abstract: Reinforcement learning methods have demonstrated advanced capabilities in training neural network controllers for specific tasks. In the industrial domain, where model discrepancies and state disturbances occur, robot control strategies must exhibit adaptability. Existing studies, such as Generative Motor Reflexes (GMR), employ Variational Autoencoders (VAE) to approximate the latent variable space distribution to a standard normal distribution. However, this method, while straightforward, offers limited capability in representing data. The Gaussian Mixture Variational Autoencoder (GMVAE) algorithm leverages a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) as the prior distribution for data generation, enhancing the representation of the original state distribution. To increase the robustness of the trained neural network controllers against unknown states, we utilize GMVAE to represent the original state space, subsequently learning the mapping from latent variables to actions. We further accelerate the policy search process by integrating state representation learning with Guided Policy Search (GPS) methods. Our method was evaluated on robotic reaching tasks. Experimental results validate the robustness of our method against state perturbations.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Method for Detecting Defects Under Urban Utility Tunnels
abstract: Urban Utility Tunnel (UUT) is susceptible to defects throughout its service life due to various factors, such as material aging, soil load, and adverse conditions. These defects deteriorate the tunnel's load-bearing capability and compromise the integrity of pipeline facilities. Hence, there is an urgent need for an effective method to detect UUT defects. In this study, we propose an Enhanced U-Net model called EU-Net, which leverages ResNet34 as the feature extraction backbone in place of the base U-Net. This substitution significantly enhances both global and local feature extraction capabilities. Additionally, we introduce a spatial attention module to establish meaningful relationships between defect pixels at different distances, thereby reinforcing important information. To tackle the challenge of limited samples and prevent overfitting, we employ a data augmentation method to increase dataset diversity. Compared to the conventional U-Net model, our improved U-Net achieves a notable 13.7% increase in Fl-score, a 10.1% increase in Mean Intersection of Union (MIoU), faster detection speed, and improved accuracy. These results convincingly demonstrate the effectiveness and practicality of our proposed method in real-world UUT defect identification tasks.

articleTitle: Research on Global Path Planning in Air-Ground Collaborative Robotic Systems Based on the ORB-SLAM3 Algorithm
abstract: The air-ground collaborative robotic system has garnered significant attention due to its potential applications in complex scenarios such as search and rescue and extraterrestrial exploration. However, existing research encounters substantial challenges related to efficient and reliable path planning in large scale environments. In this study, we explore the creation of maps in unknown environments without GPS by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to assist unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) in rapid and advanced global path planning. Our approach begins with a UAV equipped with a camera, using the ORB-SLAM3 algorithm to generate a sparse point cloud map. Next, we apply the Statistical Outlier Removal (SOR) algorithm to filter out point cloud noise. To obtain a map of navigable paths, we employ the Random Sample Consensus (RANSAC) algorithm to extract the point cloud information representing the traversable ground. Finally, the processed 3D point cloud map is converted into a 2D grid map, resulting in an obstacle map suitable for UGV global path planning. Additionally, we employ the A* algorithm for path planning, considering critical factors such as path width and gradient. The proposed system demonstrates significant application potential in unknown environment exploration. UAVs can pre-scan unfamiliar terrains to facilitate efficient UGV navigation. The results indicate that our integrated method significantly enhances the efficiency and reliability of path planning in collaborative robotic systems.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Optimization Based Dispatching of Source-Grid-Load-Storage with Demand Response
abstract: The integrated model of source-grid-load-storage (SGLS) significantly enhances the flexibility and controllability of the power system by integrating the elements of generation, transmission, distribution, consumption, and storage. However, traditional dispatching methods encounter numerous challenges, such as the instability and intermittency of renewable energy supply, along with the optimal utilization of storage systems. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a particle swarm optimization (PSO) based dispatching algorithm for SGLS system considering multi-load demand response (DR). First, cost models of the SGLS system are established as the optimization objectives. Second, the PSO algorithm is utilized to optimize the output of wind turbines, photovoltaics, storage, and load adjustments, thereby achieving system cost savings and efficient utilization of renewable energy. Third, multiple dispatching rules are proposed to further minimize the system cost by comprehensively considering actual operating conditions. Comparative results substantiate the effectiveness of the presented dispatching algorithm.

articleTitle: The Construction of a Multi-Modal Dermatology Database and Secondary Clustering Analysis of Rosacea
abstract: The primary objective of this study is to develop a comprehensive dermatological database enriched with extensive clinical information and to automatically assign pseudo-labels to dermoscopic images using deep clustering technology, thereby enhancing the efficiency of diagnostic processes and reducing the burden on medical resources. Although deep clustering effectively aggregates similar cases, the precision of the resulting categories does not yet meet clinical demands. To address this, we implemented a secondary clustering analysis using a minimal amount of precisely labeled data for weakly supervised learning, further refining disease classification. For example, the classification of acne was significantly improved by secondary clustering, which precisely distinguished rosacea from initial clustering categories. This method not only optimized disease classification outcomes but also laid a solid foundation for in-depth research and clinical applications in dermatology. Moving forward, we plan to expand the database, incorporate more types of clinical data, and explore advanced deep learning techniques to enhance the accuracy of clustering and classification, further supporting the diagnosis and treatment of skin diseases.

articleTitle: Quantitative Damage Diagnosis Method under Vibration Conditions Based on Two-Dimensional Gaussian Model with Phase Synchronization Damage Index
abstract: In civil, mechanical, and aerospace engineering, structures are subjected to complex high-frequency vibrational loads during operation. Diagnosing structural damage under these conditions is essential for ensuring safe operation. This paper tackles the challenges in monitoring the structural health of guided wave structures during operation and proposes a damage diagnosis method based on two-dimensional Gaussian model. First, this paper examines the impact of various vibration conditions on guided wave signals and introduces a new damage index-the phase synchronization damage index. This index, together with the spatial phase damage index, constitutes a two-dimensional feature sample set. Using this feature sample set, the optimal number of samples is determined, and both a baseline Gaussian model and a dynamic monitoring Gaussian model are established. The weighted sum of multi-path distance metrics is then employed as a quantitative damage index for diagnosis. Experiments were conducted on aluminum alloy plate structures with varying degrees of crack damage under different vibration conditions. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can quantitatively monitor damage under different vibration conditions, achieving high accuracy in estimating the degree of damage.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Backstepping Trajectory Tracking Control for a Quadcopter with Experimental Validation
abstract: This paper addresses the nonlinear control problem for a quadcopter. The proposed control strategy ensures effective trajectory tracking with ultimately bounded errors. A nonlinear controller employing a backstepping framework is designed to stabilize the quadcopter with damping effects. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate the controller's capability to maintain stability and accurately follow reference trajectory, validating the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling Strategy for Intelligent Building Cooperation Game Considering Generalized Energy Storage
abstract: A cooperative game optimization scheduling strategy for intelligent building clusters considering generalized energy storage is proposed to address the difficulties in optimizing scheduling due to the wide variety of equipment types in current intelligent buildings, as well as the low utilization and high cost caused by configuring energy storage separately. Firstly, electric vehicles with flexible energy storage characteristics and ice storage air conditioning are introduced. Then, a generalized shared energy storage model is constructed using cooperative game theory. The coordinated optimization of energy consumption in intelligent building clusters is achieved in the form of building cooperative alliances. The energy flow is uniformly regulated through the energy storage sharing platform. Finally, a low-carbon operation model of the building comprehensive energy system is established with the goal of minimizing comprehensive operating costs.

articleTitle: Trajectory Control of Multi-Axis Robotic Arms Based on Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
abstract: Multi-axis robotic arms are extensively utilized in intelligent manufacturing scenarios, with trajectory control in flexible scenarios constituting a primary challenge. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) represent advanced methods that integrate physical laws with data-driven approaches. Despite their outstanding performance in integrating theory and data, research on their application for controlling robotic arms in complex scenarios remains limited. This paper establishes a nonlinear dynamic model based on the physical relationships between the axes of robotic arms. In the absence of prior data, Sobol sequence random sampling is employed to generate data, which are subsequently trained using PINNs. Considering system noise, the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) is utilized to predict the next state in noisy environments, and Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) is implemented to control the robotic arm for trajectory tracking, achieving real-time control. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed Discrete Physics-Informed Predictive Control (DPIPC) method exhibits smaller position and velocity errors with less fluctuation compared to the method in the reference, indicating superior control capabilities.

articleTitle: Sensorless Algorithm of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Linear Motor Based on Super- Twisting Sliding Mode Observer with New Adaptive Strategy
abstract: An innovative adaptive strategy is applied to the super-twisting sliding mode observer (STSMO) for permanent magnet synchronous linear motors (PMSLM), addressing the issue of significant nonlinear variations in the observed back electromotive force (back-EMF) amplitude during uniform acceleration when using a fixed-parameter STSMO. The stability of the proposed method and the reasons behind the nonlinear behavior of the STSMO under fixed parameters are analyzed. A normalized orthogonal phase-locked loop (PLL) is employed to extract velocity and position. Simulation results demonstrate that the back-EMF observed by the new adaptive algorithm during uniform acceleration closely aligns with theoretical values, and the sensorless algorithm exhibits excellent tracking performance.

articleTitle: Enhancing Category-Level 6D Object Pose Estimation with a Point Cloud Completion and Deformation Network
abstract: Category-level pose estimation aims to estimate the rotation, translation and size of unseen instances in specified categories. This task becomes challenging due to intra-class variation and the intricate nature of estimating dense correspondences between instance cloud and NOCS point cloud. In this paper, we propose a patch-seeds-based point cloud completion and deformation network to address these challenges. Our method leverages patch seeds to complete instance point cloud and deform categorical shape prior, enabling us to estimate complete instance point cloud in both camera space and normalized space. Subsequently, we employ the ICP algorithm to directly register the estimated point cloud and derive the pose. This method not only robustly cope with intra-class variations, but also avoids the complex and dense correspondences between instance point cloud and NOCS point cloud by directly estimating the network. Our designed network adopts a multi-stage point cloud completion and deformation strategy, where each stage progressively refines the accuracy of the point cloud reconstruction. We conducted extensive experiments on a recognized category-level 6D attitude estimation benchmark, and the experimental results showed that our proposed method significantly improved the accuracy of attitude estimation compared to previous methods.

articleTitle: A Portable and Open-Source Potentiostat for Continuous Electrochemical Analysis
abstract: This manuscript demonstrates a portable and open-source potentiostat for continuous electrochemical analysis to promote electrochemical analysis technology from the laboratory to the consumer electronics market. This innovative potentiostat comprises a smartphone application (APP) and an application-specified printed circuit. The smartphone APP serves as a user interface, facilitating data reception, inputting instructions, and providing real-time experimental data visualization. The application-specified printed circuit acts as an intermediary, responsible for storing and processing analog signals acquired from the electrochemical electrodes while establishing seamless communication with the smartphone APP. This potentiostat offers a function of chronoamperometry techniques, featuring a broad current and voltage range of 0.1 μA to 2000 μA and ±10 V, respectively. This chronoamperometry technique covers the majority of scenarios of electrochemical detection. Resistance and electrochemical measurements showcase its performance, which closely rivals that of benchtop commercial potentiostats. It is an open-source platform and aims to better support electrochemical researchers by reducing the repetitive effort required for circuit development, enabling them to focus more on creative electrochemical research.

articleTitle: A New Trajectory Optimization Design Method of Smart Morphing Aircraft
abstract: With the gradual maturity of materials science, computer science and artificial intelligence technology, the development of smart morphing aircraft that can make deformation decisions quickly and independently according to target requirements like birds, and meet various flight tasks with the best aerodynamic layout has become a common goal of the current engineering and academic fields. By integrating intelligent materials and intelligent algorithms, morphing aircraft can independently optimize their deformation based on environmental perception, thereby enhancing their overall performance and trajectory optimization throughout various flight phases. Due to the significant changes in their structure, establishing an accurate mathematical model becomes challenging, rendering traditional control methods inadequate for achieving intelligent control over flight trajectories. Consequently, a novel intelligent trajectory optimization design method based on the reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm, is proposed to address this issue. This method allows for innovative trials on supersonic or hypersonic cruise missiles and aircrafts, which can be better adapted to various stages from launch to accelerated climb, to cruise flight and final target attack by changing the aerodynamic configuration. It is believed that the preliminary exploration of this research can provide new inspiration for intelligent decision control and flight performance optimization of future aircraft.

articleTitle: Cross-dimensional Principal Component Analysis-A New Dimensionality Reduction Method
abstract: cross-dimensional principal component analysis (CD-PCA). It is based on the semi-tensor product of matrices theory (STP), where a new projection rule is introduced to reduce dimensionality of high-dimensional data in various linear spaces. Compared to principal component analysis (PCA) and its variants, which typically discard some principal components related to small eigenvalues for the purpose of dimensionality reduction, the methodology of CD-PCA can unite all principal components to form new components of lower dimensions. A comparitive anaylsis is conducted to characterize the potential relation of PCA and CD-PCA, which not only reveals the principle of the CD-PCA algorithms but also provides a deep insight on its properties and capabilities, ensuring its suitability for dimensionality reduction and feature extraction. Extensive experiments on classification and clustering verify the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: Collaborative Optimization of Semiconductor Manufacturing Production and Opportunistic Maintenance Scheduling based on QMIX
abstract: Minimizing production delays due to equipment maintenance is crucial in the semiconductor industry, driven by high costs and competitive pressures. This paper introduces opportunistic maintenance (OM) to optimize equipment utilization and reliability in semiconductor manufacturing. OM strategically schedules maintenance actions based on buffer utilization and predicted failure times to minimize operational disruptions and maintenance costs. Recognizing the limitations of traditional mathematical programming in handling the complexities of real-world production systems, this paper presents an integrated decision-making framework tailored for intelligent semiconductor workshops. Central to this approach is the QMIX algorithm operating under the CTDE (Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution) paradigm. This enables joint training of policies while supporting independent decision-making during execution. The framework leverages independent policies assigned to each machine group, coordinated through a decision collaboration module to synchronize outputs with real-time workshop states, thereby optimizing production and maintenance scheduling. This methodology enhances performance in dynamic environments with limited local observations, thereby advancing operational efficiency in semiconductor manufacturing.

articleTitle: An Embedded Temporal Information Graph Network for Traffic Accident Anticipation
abstract: Early anticipation of traffic accidents from dashboard cameras (dashcams) videos can play an important role in enhancing road safety and enabling autonomous driving. However, the drastic changes in perspective, the complexity of traffic scenes, and the scarcity of data pose significant challenges to this task. In this paper, we propose an embedded temporal information graph network for early traffic accident anticipation. It extracts the spatio-temporal features of the object and utilizes the interaction between objects in the same frame and adjacent frames, taking into account all objects between adjacent frames to make accurate predictions as early as possible. Experimental results on widely used DAD and CCD datasets demonstrate that our model can achieve state-of-the-art performance compared with previous accident anticipation methods.

articleTitle: Structured Joint Sparse Discriminative Dictionary Learning for Image Classification
abstract: In order to improve the image classification performance of dictionary learning, this article develops a structured joint sparse discriminative dictionary learning (SJSDDL). In contrast to the Fisher Discriminative Dictionary Learning (FDDL), we propose introducing an additional low-rank shared subspace in the original dictionary and conducting the joint sparse coding for dictionary coefficients. Overall, the introduced low-rank atoms are beneficial for alleviating the entanglement relationship in similar samples from different classes, which facilitates the coefficient discrimination term to distinguish the data categories. Extraordinarily, by imposing the joint constraints of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell_{2,0^{-}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell_1$</tex>-norms on the coefficients, the resulting joint sparse coding allows the associated dictionary subspaces to overlap partially, thereby constructing the class-specific sub-dictionaries with appropriate dimensions. The structured sparse coding and the flexible dictionary construction strategy endow the proposed method with better discriminability. The utilized optimization techniques involve the FISTA for sparse coding and the ADMM for dictionary update. The improved classification performance of SJSDDL is illustrated by the experimental results on widely used image datasets.

articleTitle: Robot Safe Planning in Dynamic Environments Based on MPC Using Control Barrier Function
abstract: Implementing obstacle avoidance in dynamic environments is a challenging problem for robots. Model predictive control (MPC) is a popular strategy for dealing with this type of problem, and recent work mainly uses control barrier function (CBF) as hard constraints to ensure that the system state remains in the safe set. However, in crowded scenarios, effective solutions may not be obtained due to infeasibility problems, resulting in degraded controller performance. We propose a new MPC framework that integrates CBF to tackle the issue of obstacle avoidance in dynamic environments, in which the infeasibility problem induced by hard constraints operating over the whole prediction horizon is solved by softening the constraints and introducing exact penalty, prompting the robot to actively seek out new paths. The efficacy of the proposed method is first shown through simulation experiments, in which a double-integrator system and a unicycle system are employed, and the proposed method outperforms other controllers in terms of safety, feasibility, and navigation efficiency.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning for Improved Alignment in Radiology Reports Generation
abstract: Chest X-rays are crucial for diagnosing various medical conditions, but generating accurate reports from them is challenging due to their complexity. Traditional models often miss critical anomalies and produce vague content, overlooking specific clinical signs. To address these issues, we introduce a reinforcement learning framework that improves alignment between radiology images and their corresponding reports. The framework leverages high-level concepts and uses a two-stage generation process combined with reinforcement learning fine-tuning to enhance the analysis of complex medical image patterns, achieving precise text-image alignment. Evaluations on the IU X-Ray and MIMIC-CXR datasets demonstrate our model's superior performance. Further analysis shows significant improvement in aligning information between X-rays images and textual reports, leading to more relevant medical reports.

articleTitle: An Oversampling Fault Detection Method for Unbalanced Industrial Process Data Based on Improved SVM
abstract: In order to solve the problem of unbalanced high-dimensional data in industrial process data, this paper proposes a sampling dimensionality reduction method. Firstly, the dataset is oversampled by a safe-level borderline SMOTE method, the number of fault samples is increased. Dimentionality of the data is reduced by the convolutional neural network with attention mechanism, and finally the fault detection of industrial process data is carried out through the parameters of the support vector machine optimized by Harris Eagle algorithm. The advantages of the algorithm are verified by comparing with several common machine learning algorithms in the relevant indicators of fault detection.

articleTitle: Enhancing NERF Rendering in Architectural Environments Using Spherical Harmonic Functions and NEUS Methods
abstract: Conventional neural radiation field (NERF) techniques suffer from color deviations and artifacts or false objects in the reconstruction results when fusing architectural view-points. Due to variations in lighting conditions and inconsistencies in multi-view image data, traditional neural radiation field methods tend to produce inaccurate color renderings and generate false objects. To alleviate these problems, we integrate a ball-harmonic function into the Neus method to represent illumination and color information more efficiently, thereby improving the robustness and accuracy of the reconstruction model. Our method utilizes the spherical harmonic function to efficiently model the lighting environment, which, combined with the geometric representation capability of the Neus method, significantly reduces color bias and eliminates artifacts in the reconstruction results. We conducted experiments on the mip-NERF360 dataset and a customized building dataset to validate our method. The results show that our method performs well in high-quality surface reconstruction, significantly reduces color bias and artifacts, and improves the accuracy and realism of reconstruction results. This study provides effective solutions to common problems in NERF reconstruction and demonstrates significant progress in the field.

articleTitle: Pointer-Type Meter Recognition Based on Elliptical Bounding Box Detection and Reading Regression
abstract: The automatic reading of pointer-type meters plays an important role in routine inspection of power substation. However, considering various factors such as meter types, shooting angles, and lighting conditions, the recognition of the pointer meters in natural environment is still a challenging task. To address this issue, an improved YOLOv5 algorithm that using elliptical bounding box instead of traditional rectangle one is utilized to detect and classify dials, and a deep regression model based on UNet is designed to achieve meter readings. This algorithm has many advantages, such as without the need of pre-processing and post-processing, the effective filtering of background information through elliptical bounding boxes, thus can significantly improve the accuracy of reading recognition. Experimental results demonstrate that, within a reading error of ±5%, the recognition accuracy reaches 87.33%, while within a reading error of 10%, the recognition accuracy reaches 96.54%.

articleTitle: Stackelberg Game-Based Optimal Scheduling Strategy for Multi-Microgrid Systems with Electricity-Heat Shared Energy Storage
abstract: To address the challenges of the complexity of electricity-heat coupling, the pollution of carbon emissions, the security of privacy information, and the uncertainty of renewable energy generations (REGs), this paper proposes a novel multi-microgrid electricity-heat shared energy storage system framework, considering that the integrated energy storage operator (IESO) is equipped with electric boiler and two types of energy storage (i.e., electrical energy storage and heat energy storage) devices, and each microgrid (MG) is equipped with combined heat and power system that coupled carbon capture system and power-to-gas device. Latin hypercube sampling is used to deal with the uncertainty of REGs. A distributed bi-level iterative algorithm based on Stackelberg game theory is designed, which effectively protects the users' privacy information, and finally a Stackelberg equilibrium strategy is obtained, where the IESO and each MG minimize its operating cost. Simulation results show that the proposed optimal scheduling strategy can effectively reduce the operating cost and carbon emissions of each MG, and increase the benefits of the IESO.

articleTitle: New End to End Trajectory Tracking Controller for Spherical Robot Based on Feedback Linearization and Singular Perturbation
abstract: The dynamic model of a spherical robot exhibits nonlinearity and underactuation, posing significant challenges for model-based trajectory tracking control. Previous control methods often required two cascaded controllers to compute the motor torques needed for trajectory tracking. Additionally, controllers using Taylor series expansion-based linearization methods could only maintain high accuracy near operating points. Therefore, previous control methods were complex and restricted to specific conditions. Addressing these issues, this paper proposes an end to end trajectory tracking controller based on feedback linearization and singular perturbation control. This new end to end controller directly computes the required motor torques using the desired trajectory instead of using two cascade controllers to track desired trajectory. By employing input-output feedback linearization, the nonlinear dynamic model is accurately transformed into a linear system, simplifying controller design and ensuring the convergence of the robot's motion trajectory to the desired path. Furthermore, singular perturbation control stabilizes internal dynamics without increasing control inputs, thereby ensuring the feasibility of the feedback linearization controller. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed controller effectively enables the spherical robot to track the given trajectory.

articleTitle: Quality-Related Fault Diagnosis Methods of Industrial Processes Under Variable Operating Conditions: A Review
abstract: As industrial systems expand in scale and production processes grow more complex, the safety and quality of products have become increasingly important. Consequently, fault detection and diagnosis have taken on greater significance. Traditional fault detection and diagnosis methods rely heavily on mathematical modeling, while data-driven approaches such as Partial Least Squares (PLS) have gained prominence with advancements in information and automation technologies. The impact of faults on product quality and Variable Operating Conditions (VOC) bring challenges to the industrial applications of fault detection and diagnosis methods. This review summarizes recent data-driven methods for quality-related and VOC scenarios. Firstly, we summarized recent quality-related fault detection and diagnosis methods centered around PLS. Then, we categorized recent fault detection and diagnosis researches for VOC scenarios and highlighted representative studies. Following this, we delved into specific scenarios to explore quality-related fault detection and diagnosis for VOC scenarios. Finally, on the basis of the remaining issues and challenges in quality-related fault detection and diagnosis for VOC scenarios, we discussed and envisioned future research directions.

articleTitle: Advanced Hierarchical Missile Guidance Strategies Based on Temporal Forecasting and Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: In response to the evolving requirements of modern combat scenarios, there is a growing emphasis on developing missile guidance systems that are more autonomous and capable of intelligently navigating and responding to challenging conditions. To address the challenges posed by increasingly complex target evasion patterns in modern warfare, this paper presents a novel hierarchical missile guidance strategy that integrates temporal forecasting with deep reinforcement learning. Our approach combines an Evasion Pattern Forecasting Network (EPFNet) with multiple reinforcement learning-based guidance policies, each tailored to a specific evasion pattern. The EPFNet, built on a bidirectional LSTM architecture, achieves a 97.5% accuracy in predicting target evasion patterns. We employ Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to train guidance policies, incorporating a Zero-Effort Miss (ZEM) guidance law to reduce the action space and enhance computational efficiency. Our hierarchical strategy demonstrates superior performance compared to traditional methods, achieving a 91.4% hit rate within a 10-meter tolerance across various evasion patterns. This significant improvement underscores the effectiveness of our approach in maintaining precise strike capabilities in challenging battlefield environments. The proposed method offers a promising solution for next-generation missile guidance systems capable of adapting to diverse and complex target behaviors.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimal Scheduling of Energy and Computational Workload in Green Data Centers Considering Waste Heat Recovery
abstract: Driven by the growth of the digital economy, the demand for computational performance of data centers (DCs) is growing exponentially, which leads to huge energy consumption in DCs. As such, this paper proposes a multi-objective optimal scheduling method for green DCs to jointly manage energy supply and computational workload. Firstly, an electricity-heat-computation coupling system model is constructed, which considers renewable energy sources (RESs), waste heat recovery and the temporal flexibility of DC workload. Then, a multi-objective optimal scheduling model is formulated with the comprehensive consideration of economic, environmental and energy efficiency indicators. Further, the power usage effectiveness (PUE) is modified to reformulate the objective as a linear function. Finally, the proposed solution is assessed extensively through a case study, and the numerical results confirm the efficacy of this method in reducing economic cost, carbon emissions and PUE.

articleTitle: Modeling, Computation and Analysis of Gaussian-Based Probability Density Function and Conflict Potential Field for Cooperative Overtaking
abstract: The collaborative overtaking framework presents significant potential for advancing road traffic safety and operational efficiency in intelligent transportation systems. By enabling instantaneous communication among roadway infrastructure, proximate vehicles, and other traffic entities, the framework facilitates the seamless exchange of critical information. Recognized for its superior performance, it is poised to play a pivotal role in the evolution of next-generation Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS), particularly with the proliferation of 5G communication technologies. This paper examines fundamental challenges associated with the modeling, computation, and analysis of Gaussian-based probability density functions and conflict potential fields, applying these methodologies to coordinated overtaking systems. Specifically, a Gaussian-based conflict potential field model is introduced alongside a risk assessment methodology designed to enhance overtaking safety by evaluating collision risks through vehicle-to-vehicle communication. Empirical experiments further substantiate the efficacy of the proposed approach, demonstrating notable performance improvements under dynamic and unpredictable driving conditions.

articleTitle: Dyna-OpenVINS: Dynamic Environment Visual-Inertial Odometry with Object Removal via Multi-Scale Semantic Segmentation
abstract: In many Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) systems, the assumption of a static environment is a common prior, which limits their performance in highly dynamic scenes. This paper introduces Dyna-OpenVINS, a lightweight Visual-Inertial odometry system built on the OpenVINS framework, specifically tailored for dynamic environments. Dyna-OpenVINS features a dynamic object removal module based on multi-scale semantic segmentation using the YOLOv8-seg model, effectively filtering out feature points associated with dynamic objects and mitigating their adverse effects. Additionally, the system is highly adaptable, supporting any number of cameras and incorporating a cross-camera feature tracking method to minimize redundant landmarks. We evaluated Dyna-OpenVINS using the dynamic VIODE dataset and in real-world scenarios. The results show that Dyna-OpenVINS achieves high localization accuracy while maintaining real-time performance, making it highly effective in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: A Transformer-Based Surrogate Model Predictive Control for Complex Chemical Processes
abstract: Quality of the Model Predictive Control (MPC) depends significantly on the predictive model. With the growing availability of industrial data, researchers are increasingly adopting data-driven methods, often using auto-regression and moving average model (ARMA) to accomplish multi-step prediction. However, these models can introduce cumulative prediction errors, affecting control performance. Recently, Transformers, originally designed for Natural Language Processing tasks, have been explored for surrogate MPC modelling. Because of a lack of effective guidance, they might introduce modelling errors caused by irregular temporal dependence and steady-state errors due to model mismatch. To address cumulative and modelling (CM) errors, a new Transformer-based predictive model named CMformer is proposed for MPC. CMformer employs an encoder-decoder architecture to reduce modelling errors and outputs multi-step predictions simultaneously to avoid cumulative errors. Additionally, to eliminate steady-state errors, a selector mechanism which can switch between PI control and MPC control is designed. Experimental validation on a Continuous Stirred Tank Reactor demonstrates superior prediction performance than the encoder-only Transformer, and a constrained closed-loop tracking control task demonstrates the controller's ability to reduce all three types of errors, achieving precise control performance.

articleTitle: Generation of Autonomous Vehicle Testing Trajectories for Cut-In Scenario Integrating Data and Kinematics
abstract: The assessment of autonomous vehicles (AVs) represents a pivotal aspect of technological advancement. However, the evaluation of AVs within a simulated environment presents a number of challenges, including ensuring compliance with physical laws and reflecting the naturalness and diversity observed in real-world driving, which makes simulated testing a challenging issue. In view of this, we introduce a novel approach that integrates data-driven methods with kinematic constraints to generate testing trajectories. Our method conceptualizes trajectory generation as a probabilistic process, using a Gaussian distribution to introduce variations. By incorporating fusion technology, this approach can rely solely on initial scene information, thereby enhancing the practicality and convenience of generating testing trajectories for AV applications. An ablation study of kinematic constraints and data is separately conducted, demonstrating the effectiveness of our model.

articleTitle: Non-Cooperative Game-Oriented Optimal Prescribed Performance Control for Underactuated Mechanical Systems with Asymmetric Constraints
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-cooperative game theory in achieving optimal prescribed performance control for uncertain underactuated mechanical systems. The study addresses scenarios characterized by time-varying (potentially rapid) and bounded uncertainties. Utilizing a constraint-following control design approach., we apply the prescribed transient and steady-state performance (TSSP) criteria to the constraint-following error. Additionally., we employ state transformation techniques to implement the prescribed performance control. We introduce a prescribed performance control methodology with two adjustable parameters and demonstrate the process of determining the optimal design for these parameters through Nash games. Our findings indicate a significant enhancement in the overall system performance., thus confirming the efficacy of the optimization method grounded in non-cooperative game theory.

articleTitle: A Hand Rehabilitation Device Based on Magnetorheological Three-Dimensional Soft Actuators TPU Exoskeleton
abstract: Addressing issues such as the complexity of hand rehabilitation device structures, difficulty in wearing, and weak grasping force at the end effector, a novel hand rehabilitation device based on magnetorheological three-dimensional soft actuators (TPU exoskeleton) is proposed. To enhance grasping force, this study utilizes magnetorheological elastomer as the base material for a three-degree-of-freedom fiber-reinforced magnetic-fluid hybrid soft actuator. To alleviate wearing difficulties, a modular TPU finger exoskeleton is designed. Finite element simulation is employed to optimize the winding turns of the fiber-reinforced layer. A maximum relative error of 28% between simulation-optimized soft actuators and actual values is observed. An improved whale optimization algorithm establishes a mathematical model with air pressure, magnetic induction intensity as inputs, and bending angle as output. Theoretical validations are conducted through performance testing on a comprehensive soft actuator experimental platform. Results demonstrate a maximum relative error of 16.0224% and an average absolute percentage error of 6.0874% in bending angle for the soft actuators. Experimental findings indicate that the hand rehabilitation device can grasp daily life items effectively and meet basic hand rehabilitation training requirements.

articleTitle: Target Recognition Inference Based on Knowledge Graph and Graph Neural Network
abstract: In complex environments with vast and diverse information sources, target recognition serves as a crucial precursor to situational analysis, providing the foundation for further decision-making and analysis. Traditional algorithms for target recognition often rely on human experience and rules, necessitating expert knowledge and subjective judgments, which introduces uncertainties. This paper introduces a method for target recognition inference, leveraging Situation Knowledge Graph Convolutional Neural Network (SKGCN). By employing active and passive radar sensor data in complex scenarios, the algorithm processes inputs within a self-constructed situational knowledge graph. It derives vector representations of target entities through aggregation operations among neighboring nodes and extracts perceptual data vectors using the embedding layer. The algorithm calculates the alignment between sensor data and target entities, facilitating target recognition and inference in complex scenarios. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Optimization Method of Wind Turbine Short-Circuit Current and Reactive Power Support Key Parameters Based on Trajectory Sensitivity
abstract: Direct-drive wind power generators(PMSG) have become mainstream models and are widely used in power grids due to their advantages. However, the lack of quantitative analysis methods makes it difficult to assess the impact of control parameters on short-circuit current and reactive power support capability. To address this issue, this paper first derives the analytical expression of three-phase short-circuit current through Park transformation based on the active and reactive current calculation method of PMSG. Then, based on the trajectory sensitivity method, it quantitatively analyzes the impact mechanism of different control parameters on short-circuit current from three aspects: generator parameters, voltage drop coefficient, and PI parameters. The parameters with higher sensitivity are selected as the dominant parameters. Finally, combined with simulation, the paper studies the impact of key parameters of short-circuit current on the reactive voltage support capability of wind turbines. Based on this, an optimization method for key parameters of short-circuit current and reactive power support of PMSG is formulated. The research results show that the proposed method can enhance the reactive voltage support capability of wind turbines while ensuring the level of short-circuit current.

articleTitle: High-Low Frequency Filtering Aware Graph Neural Networks with Representation Decoupling Learning
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) perform excellently in representation learning of graph data, attracting widespread attentions. Although, most GNNs with explicit graph convolution face the interference between attribute and topological structure, resulting in partial and compromise embedding representation. Most GNNs only capture the low-frequency information of graph signals and ignore the important high-frequency information. To address these issues, we propose a novel framework for GNNs, i.e., High-Low Frequency Filtering aware Graph Neural Network (HLFF-GNN). Under the designed optimization framework, HLFF-GNN learns various representations to fit attribute and graph structure with representation decoupling learning strategy, which obtains more comprehensive representation by concatenating them. High and low frequency information is simultaneously exploited, where especially the high-frequency information would be additional and useful supplement to low-frequency information. Further, diversity constraint is introduced to enhance complementarity of various embedding representations. The experimental results of node classification task on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the validity and superiority of our approach.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cyber-Security in Industrial Control: An Encrypted MPC Framework with Neural Network-Based Generalization
abstract: Cybersecurity presents a significant challenge in networked industrial control systems. To address this issue, we propose a fully homomorphic encryption scheme designed to secure control signals, thereby ensuring the network security of Model Predictive Control (MPC) systems. In response to the encryption requirements, the control output is approximated as a linear combination of basis functions which is realized by employing a neural network. This approach facilitates the computation of constrained approximate optimal solutions within the ciphertext space, therefore mitigating the computational overhead associated with online optimization in MPC and maintaining MPC's optimization performance. The basis functions are trained using data from multiple similar objectives, e.g. same type devices, or similar mechanisms, each under variant predictive control parameters. In practice, these basis functions can be reused, necessitating only the design of a set of weighting coefficients tailored to each device's performance requirements. The proposed method is demonstrated through its application to chemical process control. Simulation results validate the effectiveness and practicality of the approach.

articleTitle: Learning Representations of Tail Entities via Interactions and Scalar Fusions Among Subspaces of Head Entities and Relationships
abstract: In the past few decades, algorithms for chain prediction and knowledge graph completion tasks have been extensively studied. However, traditional methods based on geometric spatial embedding face challenges such as high dimensionality, high computational complexity, and poor scalability. To address these issues, we propose a novel model: Representations of Tail Entities from the Interactions and Scalar Fusions be-tween the Subspaces of Head Entities and Relationships (RTIFS). This model is based on a new assumption of the spatial relationship between head-relation-tail triples, embedding and abstracting tail entity information from the combined space. Experiments show that our model achieves competitive results compared to the latest eight state-of-the-art baselines, with an average reduction in embedding dimensions of 68.8%.

articleTitle: StableSort-CMC: A Tracking Algorithm for Robot Dog Based Orchard Fruit Counting
abstract: In recent years, the utilization of deep learning technology for fruit yield prediction methods using robot dogs equipped with cameras, along with target detection and tracking algorithms, has emerged as a research focus. However, the movement of robot dogs through undulating orchard terrain often induces vibration in the mounted cameras, which can significantly impact the performance of tracking algorithms. To address this issue, this paper proposes a tracking algorithm integrated with a camera motion compensation module. This module applies image rotation, scaling, and translation parameters to the tracking algorithm, enhancing its performance and counting accuracy in vibrated scenes. Utilizing nectarine data collected by a robot dog equipped with a gimbal camera, the proposed algorithm achieves a Multiple Object Tracking Accuracy (MOTA) of 63.4%. In ablation experiments, integrating the camera motion compensation module into the tracking algorithm improves MOTA by 2.9%. These results validate the efficacy of the proposed algorithm in mitigating the effects of camera vibration and enhancing tracking performance in dynamic orchard environments

articleTitle: Efficient Mobile Road Defect Detection with Parameter-Reduced AL-YOLOv8s
abstract: Road damage detection is crucial for timely maintenance and ensuring traffic safety. However, existing models often struggle to meet the required accuracy for defect detection operations and have large parameter counts, hindering deployment on mobile devices. This paper proposes an improved YOLOv8s-based road damage detection model, named AL-YOLOv8s, which incorporates several enhancements inspired Bi-directional Feature Pyramid Network (BiFPN) architectures. The Spatial Pyramid Pooling - Fast (SPPF) pooling layer is enhanced with a spatial pyramid pooling with edge localization and attention network (SPPELAN) module, while the network structure is reconstructed using a bidirectional feature fusion mechanism. Additionally, an exponential moving average (EMA) attention mechanism is integrated into the backbone, and a lightweight downsampling operation (Adown) is employed to improve Conv modules. Experiments on the RDD2022 road defect dataset demonstrate that our improved model achieves a mean average precision (mAP) of 93.8%, which is 3.1% higher than the current state-of-the-art model, while reducing the number of parameters by 12% to 6.88M. The proposed AL-YOLOv8s model addresses the critical need for accurate and lightweight road damage detection, enabling efficient deployment on mobile devices for real-time inspections and improved traffic safety.

articleTitle: Safety Risk Assessment in Fluid Catalytic Cracking Units Based on HAZOP and Knowledge Graph
abstract: The production process of the fluid catalytic cracking unit involves many hazardous factors and presents significant fire and explosion risks. Safety risk assessment can provide strong support for targeted protection of the system, effectively reducing the occurrence of safety accidents. To address the issue of the traditional hazard and operability analysis (HAZOP) ‘s difficulty in utilizing information, which results in a lack of research on risk assessment based on HAZOP, this paper fully considers the complexity and high risk of fluid catalytic cracking units and proposes a quantitative risk assessment algorithm based on a safety knowledge graph. Firstly, HAZOP is used to conduct a standardized analysis of the unit, integrating the analysis results with system process knowledge to construct a safety knowledge graph. On this basis, quantitative risk assessment is conducted for HAZOP deviation nodes, supplementing the evaluation rules of the risk priority number (RPN) algorithm and designing risk assessment functions to effectively improve the comprehensiveness and accuracy of risk assessment. Experimental results show that the risk sorting obtained through this method has high reliability and accuracy, providing strong support for targeted protection of the system.

articleTitle: Low-light Image Enhancement Algorithm Based on Adaptive Feature Decomposition and Parallel Dual Extractor
abstract: Many existing methods based on Retin-ex model mainly rely on convolution layer to process input features, which-h lack dynamic adjustment ability and are easily disturbed by redundant information. At the same time, when the local features are transferred to Transformer for modeling, the detailed information may be lost, which will lead to the decline of the visual quality of the image. In this paper, an Adaptive Feature Decomposition and Parallel Double Extractor (AFD-PDE) method is proposed to solve the problems of insufficient brightness, loss of details and increased noise in the process of weak light image enhancement. By combining the weak light image with illumination prior, this method extracts illumination features and illumination maps by convolution operation and channel attention mechanism, thus realizing adaptive feature decomposition. Then, the extracted features are denoised by Parallel Double Extractor module, and the image details are restored and noise is eliminated by down-sampling and up-sampling layer by layer. Finally, a high-quality image enhancement effect is achieved by combining Gamma correction and feature fusion. The experimental results verify the superior performance of AFD-PDE method in weak light conditions, and show its broad application prospects in the field of image enhancement.

articleTitle: Design of Motion Control System for Automatic Pusher Robot
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, industrial automation, and mobile communication, intelligent devices, represented by robots, are gradually integrating into people's work and life. This study focuses on the problem of grass accumulation in cattle sheds on ranches, and designs an Automatic Pusher Robot that can significantly improve production efficiency and reduce personnel labor intensity. The research content covers aspects such as dynamic model construction, automatic switching of multiple navigation methods, motion control methods, automatic charging, and safety protection. The research also involves motion control methods to ensure stable and precise movement and operation of robots, as well as efficient implementation of human-machine interaction, to achieve accurate understanding and response to the needs of the upper computer. Finally, to ensure the safety and smooth operation of the robot, the study also includes safety protection measures such as avoiding collisions with cattle and preventing misoperation. After careful testing, the robot's various functions are running normally and the expected goals have been achieved, providing a comprehensive innovative solution for Automatic Pusher Robot in animal husbandry cattle farms.

articleTitle: SWAFRET: A Temporal Convolutional Network Model Integrating Dynamic Sliding Window Technology
abstract: Accurate and reliable Electricity Load Forecasting (ELF) is of paramount importance for government decision making, market operation adjustment and optimization of consumers' electricity consumption behavior. In this study, Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) model incorporating dynamic sliding window technique is designed. Firstly, the feature importance analysis of raw electricity load data is carried out by the Random Forest algorithm, and the feature set is constructed accordingly. Subsequently, the time series data are segmented using the sliding window technology, and the TCN captures the intrinsic connection between the sequences and extracts the similar patterns from the historical load data, thus realizing the prediction. To verify the effectiveness of our proposed method, the study compared it with existing research that utilized three open-source datasets. The experimental results show that the SWAFRET model consistently outperforms other methods in terms of Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).

articleTitle: Enhancing the Adaptive Capability of Fuzzy Petri Net by an Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Fuzzy Petri Nets (FPNs) are an advanced topological model that extends traditional Petri nets (PNs) by integrating fuzzy theory. However, the generalization capability of FPN models is often limited due to their reliance on expert-driven parameter determination. This paper proposes an improved whale optimization algorithm (IWOA) for optimizing FPN models to address this challenge. The IWOA employs an adaptive weighting strategy, optimal search techniques, population grouping, and the Lévy flight strategy to dynamically adjust the search process, enhancing the WOA's effectiveness in handling complex problems and improving the balance between exploration and exploitation. The IWOA is tested on six classical benchmark functions in the experimental section and applied to the FPN model. The results demonstrate that the IWOA-FPN model exhibits strong generalization capabilities and superior convergence performance.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Task Assignment Algorithm for UAVs Cluster for Fast-Moving Targets
abstract: With its high flexibility, wide adaptability and controllable economy, UAVs cluster has more and more extensive application potential, and has been highly concerned at home and abroad. Task assignment is the top-level planning of UAVs cluster application, which is a comprehensive scheduling according to the requirements of mission environment situation, mission requirements, and own characteristics, so as to establish a reasonable mapping relationship between UAV and task, and maintain a reasonable cooperative relationship between aircraft. In this paper, dynamic model-based modeling and Kalman filter trajectory prediction for fast-moving targets are adopted to improve the accuracy and prediction ability of UAVs cluster on target trajectory. Then, an improved particle swarm optimization algorithm is proposed, which increases the global iterative optimization ability of the initial particle swarm by using linear decreasing parameter Settings and large inertia weights and learning factors as the beginning. And it ends with a small inertia weight and learning factor, which strengthens the final particle swarm to jump out of the local optimal solution. Intelligent cooperation and task allocation among UAVs cluster are realized, thus improving the efficiency and flexibility of the whole system. Finally, through task assignment, the UAVs cluster can track each fast-moving target autonomously.

articleTitle: Data-Driven $H_{\infty}$ Consensus Controller for Agents Under Disturbances and Model Uncertainty
abstract: We aim to study the application of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> consensus controller in the cooperative control of agents with disturbance, design a data-driven control algorithm for the scenario with unknown system model. Firstly, for the consensus problem of high-order linear multi-agent systems with disturbances, a distributed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> consensus control algorithm is proposed, which could not only ensure the consensus of multi-agent systems but also effectively improve the anti-disturbance ability of the system. Secondly, aiming at the consensus control problem of agent with disturbance and unknown model, a distributed consensus control algorithm based on data-driven approach is proposed, and it is combined with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> consensus controller, which could design appropriate control strategy by collecting agent information in real time. Finally the simulation results show that the Data-Driven <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> consensus Controller can effectively deal with the challenges caused by disturbances and model uncertainty, and achieve the stability and consensus of the agent consensus.

articleTitle: General Planning Method for Humanoid Collaborative Robots Using Large Language Models
abstract: Humanoid robots, capable of simulating human behavior and decision-making, have garnered extensive attention due to their anthropomorphic structures and versatile functional designs. Traditionally, actions and high-level decision-making in robots have been manually achieved by developers, requiring modifications and adaptations for different task requirements, thus lacking autonomous decision-making capabilities. With the rapid advancement of deep learning technologies, large language models trained on internet data have provided new solutions for robot intelligence, demonstrating effective applications in high-level task planning for robots. Based on this, we propose a general high-level task planning method using large language models, implemented on a mobile single-arm humanoid robot as the platform. This method consists of two core components: high-level decision planning and low-level action execution, coupled through the robot's atomic action interface. The robot autonomously completes sequential action planning by receiving natural language task instructions and executes long-term, complex, general indoor collaborative tasks. By deploying on a real robot, we conducted sub-module tests and overall system performance tests, successfully achieving the process of sorting and organizing tasks in an indoor experimental environment.

articleTitle: Fabric Defect Image Generation Based on Improved CycleGAN
abstract: The accurate detection of fabric defects remains a significant challenge, with the construction of the dataset being a major obstacle. To address the issue of insufficient data in fabric defect datasets, we have introduced a novel defect image generation algorithm called SA-CycleGAN. Initially, a residual module, SABlock, is incorporated with a self-attention mechanism to enhance the generator's ability to capture details. Furthermore, the generator is redesigned with an AutoEncoder and SkipConnection structure to improve the quality and diversity of image generation. Concurrently, we employ LPIPS as a cyclic consistency loss function to optimize the visual quality and realism of the generated images. Experimental results demonstrate that the SA-CycleGAN algorithm has brought about a significant data augmentation effect for fabric defect images. The effective application of the data generation method not only enriches the training dataset for fabric defect detection models but also contributes to enhancing the performance and generalization capability of the detection models.

articleTitle: Pseudo-Augmentation Entropy Domain Adaptation for Video Unsupervised Action Recognition
abstract: This research tackles the challenge of video unsupervised domain adaptation (VUDA) in human action recognition, focusing on deploying models trained in well-lit conditions to poorly-lit environments. Current unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) techniques mitigate performance degradation by aligning source and target domains through adversarial training. However, these approaches fail to enhance low-light images, resulting in information loss and suboptimal performance in dark settings. To address this issue, we introduce Pseudo-Augmentation Entropy Domain Adaptation (PANDA), an entropy theory-based method that simultaneously complements unsupervised adversarial alignment by incorporating image enhancement as an auxiliary task. Evaluations on the HMDB-ARID datasets demonstrate that proposed PANDA outperforms standard VUDA baselines, boosting action recognition accuracy by an average of 6.3%.

articleTitle: Semantic-Aware Monocular Point-Line Visual Odometry in Dynamic Environments
abstract: This paper introduces an enhanced visual odometry (VO) system tailored for robust performance in complex dynamic environments, specifically urban road scenarios with object motion and varying lighting conditions that challenge VO accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose an indirect VO approach integrating neural network-based feature detection and matching, coupled with the extraction of line features that have strong geometric constraints. Specifically, we employ a semantic segmentation network to categorize objects into three classes: artificial static, natural static, and movable. Line features are derived from the edges of artificial static objects' segmentation masks, while features within movable object segments are disregarded. By employing these techniques, our VO system effectively leverages both geometric and semantic cues to enhance scene understanding and camera motion estimation. Comparative experiments conducted on the KITTI dataset demonstrate the superior performance of our approach in dynamic environments, exhibiting enhanced robustness and accuracy compared to conventional indirect VO methods.

articleTitle: A Robust Feature Matching Method based on Semantic Geometric Constraints
abstract: Feature matching is crucial in computer vision applications, which aims to determine the correspondence between images. Different from traditional methods, this paper proposes a robust feature matching method based on semantic geometric constraints, which adopts the idea of two-stage matching. First, the image semantic information is used as a priori, and the region matching association is performed through the 3D-2D dual constraint method. On this basis, a matching trust factor is introduced, and a semantic geometric consistency feature matcher is constructed in combination with the VGG feature descriptor network to achieve robust feature matching. Experimental results show that this method has better matching performance for scenes with viewpoint changes and motion blur, and the AUC accuracy of relative pose estimation for indoor and outdoor scenes has been improved.

articleTitle: Single-Stage UAV Geolocation Enhancement with MaSA and Self-Homologous Loss
abstract: Visual Geo-localization plays a pivotal role in the domains of computer vision and image processing. In UAV nav-igation, high-precision localization can be achieved by matching the UAV's current viewpoint image with geo-tagged reference images, especially in scenarios where G PS signals are unavailable. However, conventional two-stage image retrieval methods, which initially employ global features for coarse retrieval followed by local feature-based re-ranking, are computationally intensive and demand substantial storage. To address these limitations, we propose a novel method that integrates explicit spatial priors from the Manhattan Self-Attention (MaSA) mechanism with the robust global modeling capabilities of Transformers, thereby streamlining the retrieval process into a single-stage. Furthermore, leveraging the unique pose characteristics of UAV-captured images, we refine the loss function and introduce a UAV-specific self-homogenous triplet loss to enhance the robustness of global feature extraction. Additionally, we have developed a new visual localization dataset comprising UAV and satellite images and validated our approach on this dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques, achieving improvements of 3.92% and 1.81% in top-1 and top-S retrieval accuracy, respectively.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Sensor Combination Optimization for Skiing Behavior Recognition
abstract: This paper presents a multi-sensor combination optimization algorithm based on the discrete particle swarm algorithm for addressing the multi-sensor redundancy problem in human skiing behavior recognition. A combination of sensor locations with better recognition and fewer sensor locations is selected from multiple sensor locations. The fitness function design is rooted in the concept of minimizing redundancy while maximizing correlation, considering both sensor correlations and redundancy, distinguishing it from previous studies. To evaluate the effectiveness of the chosen combination of sensor locations, acceleration data from 12 body part sensors during four basic snowboarding maneuvers were collected and classified on four classifiers: KNN, SVM, CNN and AlexNet. The experimental results indicate that the location combination of six sensors located at the left calf, right thigh, right calf, left thigh, hip and back achieves the highest effectiveness, with a recognition accuracy of 89.24%. Furthermore, a comparison with the RF method, which only considers correlation, demonstrates the effectiveness of the multi-sensor combination optimization algorithm designed in this study.

articleTitle: KANLINEAR: A Lightweight Model for Multi-Step Feedforward Prediction
abstract: This paper introduces KANLINEAR, a lightweight multi-step feedforward predictive model designed for monitoring the operational status of electrical equipment.
