KANLINEAR is based on a linear model framework and incorporates several innovative elements to enhance its predictive performance. Firstly, we introduced a linear layer based on the Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN), termed KANlayer, which significantly enhances the model's ability to express nonlinear relationships. Secondly, by designing a hybrid strategy for trend decomposition, we have overcome the limitations of traditional moving average methods. Moreover, we have developed a Temporal Volatility Capturing Loss function (TVCLoss), which further enhances the model's ability to capture fluctuations in time series data. Experimental results on an electrical data set demonstrate that KANLINEAR outperforms the baseline model, DLinear, across various performance metrics, particularly in capturing fluctuations in equipment operational status. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of these improvements. This research not only showcases the potential application of KANLINEAR in the field of electrical equipment status monitoring but also provides new directions and insights for related research areas.

articleTitle: SOFC System Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Maximum Mutual Information Coefficient and Particle Swarm Optimization Support Vector Machine
abstract: Solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) will degrade the performance of the battery stack due to fuel deficit failure, which will affect the performance of the whole system. As a result, there has been a growing focus on fault diagnosis technology to increase the stability and dependability of SOFC systems. This work proposes and introduces an efficient fault diagnostic model (FDM) for SOFC system failure diagnosis. In SOFC system, a large number of sample data are collected, the maximum information coefficient (MIC) method is used to reduce the dimension of the feature quantity and extract the feature quantity. Particle swarm optimization (PSO) is used to optimize the parameters of support vector machine (SVM), and the FDM of SOFC system based on MIC algorithm and PSO-SVM is established. To improve the accuracy of SOFC system fault diagnosis. The findings demonstrate the excellent accuracy and dependability of the FDM of the SOFC system, which is based on MIC and PSO-SVM. The accuracy of the training and test sets can both exceed 98%.

articleTitle: Design of User Experience Optimization System Based on Media Device Network Modeling
abstract: The media network faces challenges in systematically improving user experience due to the computational transmission tasks of massive data and highly coupled technical processes. Therefore, this paper designs a comprehensive user experience optimization system based on media device network modeling for key business scenarios, with user experience as the core, to achieve comprehensive user experience improvement for media device networks. We first use a network model to model the device network and achieve the mapping from physical space to mathematical space. Secondly we design a multi domain user experience model to map network capabilities to experience indicators. Finally, a multi-objective optimization method based on pareto optimality has been proposed for device networks to optimize their capabilities and achieve the goal of improving the overall quality of experience (QoE). We simulate weak network such as latency and packet loss in cloud gaming scenarios. When the user experience is poor, the proposed method is used to optimize the device network. The experimental results show that the user experience is significantly improved after optimization, proving the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: CNN-DBSCAN Intermittent Electricity Theft Detection Method for High Loss Station Areas Based on Correlation Analysis
abstract: The randomness of electricity theft behavior among intermittent electricity theft users results in data characteristics that differ from those of long-term electricity theft users. Consequently, directly applying the electricity theft detection method proposed for long-term electricity theft users to identify intermittent electricity theft users will result in a certain degree of error. The majority of existing methodologies for the detection of electricity theft under the assumption that the users under analysis and subsequent detection have engaged in electricity theft throughout the detection cycle. This approach, however, fails to account for the existence of intermittent electricity theft users within the actual system. In this paper, we put forward a correlation analysis-based CNN-DBSCAN method for the detection of intermittent electricity theft in high-loss stations with abnormal line loss rates. The method employs a multi-scale CNN model to identify the most probable time periods for all users under investigation for electricity theft. These time periods are then compared with the actual time periods when the line loss rate data exhibits abnormal behaviour. The Pearson maximum correlation analysis results are obtained under the time-distance weighting, and all the correlation analysis results for each user are clustered through the DBSCAN clustering algorithm. This process allows for the identification of outlier points, which are then classified as instances of electricity theft. The proposed method is evaluated using artificial electricity theft samples constructed based on real electricity consumption data, with a view to verifying its effectiveness in detecting intermittent electricity theft users. The superiority of the proposed method is demonstrated through comparison experiments with other methods.

articleTitle: Cloud-Aware Fusion of Infrared and RGB Images for Aerial Target Detection
abstract: Simultaneously utilizing the complementary information between infrared and RGB images for aerial target detection can improve the detection performance to a certain extent. However, cloud occlusion is difficult to avoid for aerial targets, which limits the upper limit of detection results to some extent. Therefore, in order to solve the problem of cloud occlusion, we have designed corresponding target detection methods for targets in cloud occlusion aerial environments. Specifically, firstly, we propose the Channel and Spatial Dimensions Fusion (CSDF) module, which extracts the differential features of two modalities in parallel from the channel and spatial dimensions, and uses them to enhance its own modality. Secondly, we propose the Convolutional Self Attention (CSA) module and Convolutional Mutual Attention (CMA) module, and use these two modules to form our Cloud-Aware Weight Generation (CAWG) module, which is used to solve the cloud occlusion problem in aerial target detection. We conducted experimental verification on our selfbuilt aerial target dataset, and the experimental results proved the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Data Enhancement and Named Entity Recognition Method for Water Intake Permit Management Information of Yangtze River
abstract: The Yangtze River is the longest river in Asia, with many abstraction users, making it difficult to manage abstraction permits. Water Intake Permits (WIPs) are mainly text-based, highly specialized and contain a large amount of content, which makes effective information extraction complicated. Named Entity Recognition (NER) is essential for identifying key entities in WIP texts. Aiming at the limited annotated corpus, nested entities and lengthy expressions for named entity recognition in water abstraction license materials, a data enhancement and named entity recognition method is proposed for WIP Management. According to the structure and linguistic characteristics of the Yangtze River WIP text, the data augmentation method is improved to solve the problem of annotated corpus scarcity. Comparison experimental results with other methods show that the proposed WIP model has accuracy and better generalization ability, and the F1 value on the WIP dataset reaches 89%, which provides an effective method for the recognition of named entities of water abstraction permits in the Yangtze River basin.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Method for Target Intention Recognition and Trajectory Prediction in Complex Aerial Combat Scenarios
abstract: With the development of new weapons such as decoy and self-defense interceptor, the air combat environment has become more complex. In this paper, an autoencoder intention recognition method is proposed to distinguish the types of targets. Additionally, a prediction method based on long short-term memory (LSTM) and convolutional neural network (CNN) is prosed for predicting target trajectories. Firstly, a three-degree-of-freedom relative motion model for missile-target interactions is established. Maneuver trajectories for target warplanes, decoys, and interceptors are designed using prior knowledge to establish the maneuver database. Secondly, an autoencoder is designed to compress and extract features from the trajectory data. Then, Softmax discriminant network is built to discriminate the intention of the trajectory data. Finally, the trajectory prediction network is designed based on LSTM and CNN to extract the features of the target trajectory from both temporal and spatial dimensions. The simulation results show that the intention recognition method proposed in this paper can accurately distinguish target warplanes, decoys and interceptors. And the trajectory prediction method can effectively improve the prediction accuracy compared with the traditional methods, which is suitable for the target prediction task in the complex air combat environment.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization of Two-Stage Scheduling for Aluminum Extrusion Machine Manufacturing Line
abstract: In view of the problems of high energy consumption, long inventory time and low production efficiency in the production process of traditional aluminum extrusion machine, this paper establishes an efficient two-stage parallel scheduling optimization model based on the integration of flexible job shop scheduling and assembly sequence planning (IFJSS-ASP). On this basis, an evolutionary algorithm combining strong dominance relationship and simple grouping method (SDREA-SGM) is proposed. The algorithm utilizes a two-stage hybrid chromosome encoding and decoding method to establish a rational mapping from the decision space to the solution space. Furthermore, in order to prevent the model from easily falling into local optima, an adaptive intra-class and inter-class pairing selection strategy has been adopted by the algorithm. This enhances global search and improves local search flexibility. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the algorithm are verified by solving problems of different scales.

articleTitle: HSTRL: A Hybrid Spatiotemporal State Model for Mobile Agent Autonomous Navigation
abstract: The field of intelligent robotic control has long been engaged in the study of autonomous navigation for mobile agent in complex dynamic environments. In order to address this significant challenge, a hybrid spatiotemporal enhanced reinforcement learning method (HSTRL) is proposed. The novel HSTRL model is designed to comprehensively extract and represent the spatiotemporal state information generated during agent-environment interactions. The model incorporates a network designed to extract both spatial and temporal states, thereby enabling an enhanced representation of hybrid spatiotemporal states, which is of paramount importance for the handling of the continuous changes inherent in complex dynamic environments. The HSTRL model employs value-based deep reinforcement learning to identify the optimal navigation strategy, thereby enabling agent to navigate safely and efficiently in such environments. The advantages of our method include the capacity to generate safe and efficient navigation strategies by leveraging comprehensive spatiotemporal information. A series of experiments have demonstrated the superiority of the proposed HSTRL model in agent navigation tasks, outperforming previous methods in both success rate and efficiency.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis and Optimization Design of Thermal Management Controller for Electric Trucks
abstract: To address the issue of performance degradation and potential failure of the thermal management controller in electric trucks caused by overheating of electronic components, this paper first analyzes the heat transfer mechanism of the controller from the hardware circuit design perspective, and then establishes a thermal model of the controller by adopting the computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation method, and finally tests the validity and accuracy of the thermal model through the temperature test. The simulation results indicate that when the ambient temperature is 25°C, the maximum temperature of the electronic components exceeds the design limit of 60°C, and the maximum temperature of the controller reaches 76°C. Therefore, this paper further proposes heat dissipation optimization based on thermal model in three aspects: optimizing the design of printed circuit board (PCB) vias, changing the PCB substrate material, and adding heat sink. These methods effectively reduce the maximum temperature of the controller to within the design limit of 60°C, significantly enhancing the reliability and safety of the controller during operation.

articleTitle: Predicting FEA Results of Cable Trays Using Machine Learning
abstract: In the design process of cable trays in nuclear power plants, mechanical analysis is a core technology used to ensure the safety and reliability of structural design. Traditional mechanical analysis methods, especially finite element analysis, although accurate, often incur high computational costs and time consumption. With the development of machine learning (ML) technology, it has shown potential in various engineering applications to effectively improve analysis efficiency and optimize designs. Particularly in addressing complex nuclear engineering problems, ML can learn from large datasets to predict system behavior under unknown conditions, thereby assisting in decision-making and design optimization. This paper focuses on a limited dataset of nuclear engineering cable trays. It first designs data augmentation algorithms to establish logical relationships between cable tray data, then proceeds with normalization and sample clustering. Multiple ML algorithms are experimented with, demonstrating effective prediction of output parameters of cable tray models within a certain margin of error.

articleTitle: Distributed Collaboration and Obstacle Avoidance Control of Multiple Omnidirectional Mobile Manipulator Assisted with Neural Networks
abstract: In this paper, a new distributed control scheme is proposed to realize the cooperative motion and obstacle avoidance control of multiple omnidirectional mobile manipulator (OMM) under the premise of limited communication. The proposed scheme enables multiple OMM to avoid end-effector squeezing phenomenon during cooperative load transportation, and to avoid point obstacles by introducing a cooperative repetitive motion planning and obstacle avoidance mechanism. Then, the proposed scheme ensures global convergence to the optimal solution by solving online utilizing noise suppression neural network (NSNN). Numerical simulation results verify the effectiveness of the control scheme to realize cooperative obstacle avoidance and efficient load transportation in complex environments.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Interpretable Vision Reasoning Driven Through a Multi-Modal Large Language Model for Depth Estimation
abstract: While the most advanced depth estimation methods currently achieve impressive results in ideal weather conditions, they are highly unreliable in adverse weather conditions such as night, rain, and snow. In this paper, we propose a hierarchical interpretable vision reasoning (HIVR) driven through a multimodal large language model (MLLM) that offers a simple and effective solution capable of reliable operation in adverse weather environments. First, we incorporate state-of-the-art image restoration and depth estimation models to construct a callable task model library, known as HIVR. Subsequently, we fine-tune an MLLM to identify weather conditions, automatically generate invocation programs, and drive HIVR by iteratively calling the relevant models until the depth estimation is completed. This approach enables rapid image restoration for different adverse weather conditions, followed by depth estimation, thereby realizing a universal depth estimation model. Additionally, we have utilized GANs to establish a large-scale synthetic KITTI dataset that includes six types of adverse weather conditions. In the comparison with the state-of-the-art models, the results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an obvious improvement in the comparison with the state-of-the-art models.

articleTitle: Location and Capacity Determination Method of Distributed Wind-Storage System in Distribution Network Considering Source-Load Uncertainty
abstract: The large share of distributed wind power integration brings many uncertainties to the planning of distribution network. In this paper, the energy storage is configured for the power generation side. In order to make the planning results more reasonable, the uncertainty of source and load is comprehensively considered, and the location and capacity planning model of wind storage system considering both technical and economic is constructed. Firstly, the results and working principle of the wind storage system are introduced. Secondly, the source-load uncertainty model based on multi-scenario analysis method is established. The Latin hypercube sampling is used to generate the initial scene, and the Kantorovich distance is used to reduce the scene, and then the planning scene is calculated with the scene probability as the weight. Finally, focusing on the economic performance of the wind energy storage system and the voltage stability of the distribution network, the linear weighting method is converted into a single objective. The particle swarm optimization algorithm, combined with the chaotic optimization algorithm, is used to solve the problem. The rationality and effectiveness of the proposed method are demonstrated through simulations of the IEEE 33-node power distribution system.

articleTitle: Trajectory Planning Towards Water-Air Trans-Media Motion for Robotic Dolphin
abstract: Water-air trans-media navigators have multi-media motion modes, breaking through the limitation that traditional robots can only operate in a single medium. Autonomous navigation is an indispensable component of the process of transmedia motion. Most of the current work has only completed the development and testing of prototypes, and the problem of task-oriented motion planning and control needs to be solved. In this paper, a safe and efficient hierarchical approach is proposed. First, a novel rapidly exploring random tree-based algorithm is proposed to search for a suitable path. Then, by fixing bound waypoints, the time-optimization trajectory is planned. Finally, the trajectory tracker is designed based on nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC). Simulation experiments numerically validate the proposed method, offering some new insights for further trans-media motions.

articleTitle: Tube-Based Distributed MPC for Heterogeneous Vehicle Platoons Subject to External Disturbances
abstract: This paper considers the platoon control problem with external disturbances and unknown desired set point in heterogeneous vehicles. To this end, this paper proposes a dis-tributed tube model predictive control method. First, the coupling factors between vehicles are treated as random disturbance and an error model for each vehicle is developed considering the expected distance and velocity. Then, for each vehicle that is dy-namically decoupled but spatially constrained, a linear feedback controller is used to maintain the actual trajectory within the pipeline around the nominal system trajectory. Second, in the implementation of the optimization problem, input saturation and string stability are considered as state constraints, and the DTMPC controller is designed and does not require all nodes to know the desired set point in advance. This approach significantly enhances computational efficiency and reduces inter-vehicle communication costs compared to previous methods. The simulation results show that the proposed method can ensure stability when the platoon is subjected to external disturbances.

articleTitle: Research on the Path of Manufacturing Digital Transformation and Upgrading Driven by Big Data Based on Knowledge Map Analysis
abstract: The digital transformation of the manufacturing industry is crucial for China to adapt to the new industrial revolution and achieve rapid economic development. This study explores the path of manufacturing digital transformation and upgrading driven by big data, utilizing a knowledge map analysis through CiteSpace. Key factors such as organizational structure, operational processes, and safeguard mechanisms are identified and integrated into a theoretical model. The model reveals how big data empowers various stages of manufacturing, from demand identification to intelligent production, enhancing decision-making and operational efficiency. Three transformation pathways are proposed, focusing on strengthening enterprise digital capabilities, fostering multi-stakeholder collaboration, and ensuring resource and policy support. This research offers both theoretical insights and practical guidance for the digital transformation of the manufacturing sector, addressing the needs of enterprises to improve competitiveness through innovation and data-driven strategies. The findings also provide a foundation for future studies to explore the evolving role of emerging technologies in this transformation process.

articleTitle: Seek-and-Take Games of Heterogeneous Agent Teams with Large Language Model
abstract: The problem of confrontation games between multi-agent teams has attracted considerable interest, and the question of how to ensure effective coordination of heterogeneous agents in dynamic and adversarial environments remains a significant challenge. In this paper, we present a decision-making methodology for a confrontation game between two teams, which is based on large language models (LLMs). The game is designed as a competitive Seek-and-Take task comprising three distinct robot types: reconnaissance, grabbing, and blocking robots. The LLMs enhance the robot team's decision-making efficiency, delivering high-level commands that significantly improve coordination and adversarial performance. The game is initially formalized as a partially observable Markov decision process. Subsequently, a systematic construction of the LLM agents is provided, enabling real-time decisions based on the state information of a heterogeneous robot team (HRT). Detailed prompt design and the “Zero-shot-CoT” procedure are provided, and a cue word iteration method with reflections is proposed as a means of enhancing the decision-making efficiency of the LLMs and generating optimal collaboration strategies. Finally, the efficacy of the methodology is validated through experimentation with multiple LLMs in a multi-robot simulation environment. The results demonstrate that LLMs improve the efficiency and adaptability of decision-making in dynamic environments by serving as a core decision module, generating optimal strategies through real-time analysis.

articleTitle: Discrete-Time Sliding Mode Predictive Control Based on Extended State Observer for Reference Tracking of Dynamic Positioning Ship
abstract: This paper introduces a sliding mode predictive control (SMPC) approach designed for the dynamic positioning of ships, addressing both model inaccuracies and environmental disturbances. The method combines sliding mode control with model predictive control (MPC) to achieve robust performance in the face of uncertainties. To further enhance system stability and convergence speed, an advanced nonlinear discrete-time sliding mode controller is proposed, incorporating an integral fast terminal term. This modification ensures quicker and more reliable convergence to the desired state, even under challenging conditions. In addition, an extended state observer (ESO) is employed to estimate the uncertainties in ship model parameters and external disturbances, enabling real-time adaptation to varying operational environments. The effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach are demonstrated through simulation results, which show significant improvements in positioning accuracy and disturbance rejection compared to traditional control strategies.

articleTitle: Collision Avoidance Path Planning Method Combining Improved DWA and A* Algorithms in Complex Sea Environments
abstract: This paper proposes a collision avoidance path planning method that combines the improved DWA algorithm with the A* algorithm to address navigation challenges in complex sea environments. First, a simplified grid map is constructed based on electronic chart data and the start and end points of the path planning, while the physical information of the ship is determined. The improved DWA algorithm is then used for collision avoidance path planning. When the ship reaches a safe distance from an obstacle, the improved A* algorithm is triggered to plan a path, and redundant points in the returned path are extracted to obtain key waypoints. These waypoints are used as temporary target points for the DWA algorithm, and the improved DWA algorithm is further applied for collision avoidance path planning. The improvements in the DWA algorithm mainly focus on the trajectory evaluation function, while the enhancements in the A* algorithm focus on the heuristic function. Finally, by combining the proposed algorithm with rich multi-source marine environment data and target fusion data, the ship's intelligent collision avoidance decision-making system is able to generate the optimal collision avoidance path in complex water environments. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively plan a safe and efficient collision avoidance path.

articleTitle: BMoE-AdaLoRA+: Parameter Efficient Fine-tuning for Segmenting Anything Model
abstract: Segment Anything Model (SAM), as a fundamental framework in the field of image segmentation, demonstrates excellent zero-shot capabilities in typical scenes. However, its advantages are diminished when it is applied to specialized fileds such as medical images and remote sensing, and Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) is a key way to solve this problem. On the basis of the pre-trained model, it provides a large amount of professional domain knowledge for the model and improves its domain-specific segmentation ability. However, we find that existing parameter efficient fine-tuning methods suffer from insufficient robustness, and the addition of multi-category domain data makes the model inevitably have the problem of inter-task interference. To address this challenge, we propose BMoE-AdaLora+. Firstly, we propose the concept of local smoothed sensitivity to enable the model to obtain stronger robustness during the training process. Secondly, we integrate the AdaLora+ module as an expert into the Balanced Mixture-of-Experts (BMoE), a MoE-style plug-in designed to motivate each expert to focus on a single type of data, which is used to minimize inter-task interference in multi-category fine-tuning by balancing the utilization of all experts. Experimental results show that BMoE-AdaLora+ can significantly improve the segmentation ability of the model in multi-category professional fields with the increase of domain knowledge data.

articleTitle: Vision-Based Automatic Constant Volume System for Volumetric Flasks
abstract: Aiming at the problems of cumbersome operation process, poor accuracy and low efficiency of manual volumetric flask constant volume in the process of chemical analysis, an automatic volumetric flask constant volume system based on machine vision is proposed. The vision-based volumetric flask calibration line recognition method and liquid level recognition method are designed, and the design and realization of the automatic volumetric flask setting system is completed by combining with the drip control device. The experimental results show that the proposed method has high accuracy and efficiency of constant volume, the absolute error of constant volume is within ±0.04 ml, 95.33% of which is within ±0.02 ml, and it can realize the automatic high-precision constant volume of volumetric flasks, which can meet the accuracy requirements of the actual test, and compared with manual constant volume, it improves the constant volume speed and saves manual operation, which has a good practical value.

articleTitle: Pulmonary Nodules Segmentation Based on Multilevel Fusion Path and Data Augmentation
abstract: Medical image segmentation is pivotal in computer-aided diagnosis. Although U-Net has been widely used in this field, its performance is limited by challenges such as the incomplete transmission of feature information in medical images, the lack of labeled data, and the imbalance between foreground and background pixel categories. To improve feature utilization and address issues of missing details, a segmentation method that incorporates multilevel fusion block, residual mixed attention, and data augmentation is proposed. The method includes a multilevel fusion path with a bottom-up path aggregation (BPA) branch and a complementary enhancement (CE) branch. The BPA branch optimizes the transmission of semantic and positional information, while the CE branch provides a richer feature basis for mask prediction. Furthermore, a residual block with directional edge support and mixed attention to focus on vital content units and boundary features is designed. In addition, the data augmentation strategy with local components improves the extraction of fine-grained foreground areas and enhances the diversity of data. Segmentation of pulmonary nodules in computed tomography (CT) images demonstrates a reduction in mis-segmented regions. The experimental results indicate improved segmentation performance and stability with the method. Overall, this approach is promising for pulmonary image segmentation applications.

articleTitle: Analysis and Scheduling for Flexible Job Shop Problem based on Unreliable Degraded Machine Model and Finite Buffers
abstract: In recent decades, the Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem (FJSP) has been widely studied. From a theoretical perspective, the FJSP with a fixed number of jobs has attracted significant attention. In actual production environments, machine performance can fluctuate due to factors such as workload and maintenance status, and machine performance does not remain constant but changes with the processing of workpieces. Therefore, it is necessary to study a FJSP model based on unreliable degraded machines and finite buffers. In this paper, a model of unreliable degraded machine is established, and the processing time of workpieces on degraded machines is calculated based on this model. Using the accurate processing times, an improved genetic algorithm is employed to solve the scheduling problem in flexible job shop production. The effectiveness of the algorithm is verified through numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Neuroadaptive Bipartite Consensus Control for Uncertain Networked Agent Systems Subject to Actuator Attacks
abstract: Uncertainties, such as modeling inaccuracies, external disturbances, and actuator attacks are widely spread in the control channels of the networked networked agent system, which affect the accuracy and reliability of the cooperative control to a certain extent. With this in mind, this paper focuses on the robust bipartite consensus control problem of uncertain nonlinear networked networked agent systems subject to actuator attacks. In particular, the communication topology among agents is described by a signed graph, which contains not only cooperative interactions but also competitive interactions among agents. Theoretically, the neural network-based robust consensus controller is designed. On the one hand, compound uncertainties, like modeling inaccuracies and external disturbances are approximated by interpolated fitting of Gaussian radial basis functions. The adaptive laws for approximate parameters are generated online based on the stability conditions of the closed-loop error system. On the other hand, the estimation of the unknown actuator attack factor is achieved based on the adaptive control technique, which results in the effective compensation of the attack-induced control attenuation. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed robust consensus control scheme is validated using some simulation examples.

articleTitle: CBMA-ViNet: A Path Planning Network Integrated with Attention Mechanism and Multi-Level Abstract Maps
abstract: This paper explores an improved path planning method based on Value Iteration Networks (VIN): CBMA-ViNet. This method combines attention mechanisms and multi-level abstract map mechanisms to optimize the reward function module in traditional VIN. Traditional Value Iteration Networks generate a reward map through a feature extraction network and perform value iteration on this map to learn policies. This process enables the network to flexibly adapt to different environments, learn complex decision rules, and effectively handle obstacle avoidance problems. However, VIN exhibits unstable performance and difficulty in utilizing long-range information in large maps and complex local environments. To address these issues, this study introduces the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), a lightweight and general-purpose attention module that enhances the network's expressive power. Additionally, this study proposes the Multi-Level Abstract Value Iteration Network (MutiA-VIN), which describes states at different resolutions and includes both global and local information, thereby effectively improving performance in large planning spaces. The CBMA-ViNet method combines CBAM and MutiA-VIN, enhancing the stability and accuracy of the reward function in large maps while strengthening the network's adaptability to complex environments and the algorithm's speed. Through these innovative improvements, CBMA-ViNet has become a powerful path-planning tool suitable for applications such as autonomous driving and robotic navigation.

articleTitle: An Unsupervised Leak Detection Method via Assembling Twin Attention-based Prediction Models for Natural Gas Gathering Pipelines
abstract: Accurately detecting leaks in natural gas gathering pipelines cannot only help enterprises and governments timely cope with the safety management problems, but also maintain the reliable operation of pipelines. The data-driven approaches for leak detection have become a preferred solution with the widely installation of sensors in pipeline network. However, these methods face challenges in achieving high identification accuracy due to the lack of labeled leak data and insufficient representation learning. To overcome this difficulty, an unsupervised leak detection method that leverages twin attention-based prediction models is proposed for these gathering pipelines in this article. First, attention-based point and sequence prediction approaches are designed by joint utilization of attention mechanism (AM) and the cascade of one-dimensional convolutional network (1D-CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) network, where the sequence one also employs the operation of sequence repetition and flipping for better prediction. Based on the designed attention-based point and sequence prediction approaches, an unsupervised twin attention-based prediction structure is then introduced to jointly establish the normal pipeline models. Specifically, the point prediction model is mainly used to learn the short-term dependency patterns whereas the sequence prediction model for the long-term ones from the multivariate time series. Next, a fusion strategy is presented to fuse the prediction errors generated from the twin attention-based models for the computing of overall leak scores as well as exploiting their complementary detection sensibility. To obtain clear status of pipelines without affected by abnormal points resulting from device anomalies or noises, the minimum covariance determinant (MCD) approach is adopted to attain the reliable leak scores of the fused errors. The experimental results on datasets derived from real-world gathering pipelines validate the effectiveness of the developed leak detection method.

articleTitle: SRECA: Style Remodeling and Essence Content Augmentation for Domain Generalization
abstract: Deep learning models have demonstrated a significant success across various visual tasks. However, their performance often significantly deteriorates when applied to unseen data distributions due to domain shift. In this paper, we investigate the combined aspects of style and content in the holistic visual representation of images, introducing a new method called Style Remodeling and Essence Content Augmentation (SRECA) for domain generalization. SRECA consists primarily of two components: Novel Style Learning (NSL) and Geometric Skeleton Generation (GSG). NSL identifies the most salient directions of style transition, crafting a diverse and plausible style distribution to maximize the generalization efficacy of style enhancement. Simultaneously, GSG emphasizes robust skeletal representations within the content to mitigate the adverse effects of spurious correlations, focusing on stable attributes conducive to accurate classification. This framework enhances model generalization by synergistically generating diverse styles while preserving essential content integrity. Extensive experimentation across two benchmark datasets validates the efficacy of our method.

articleTitle: Research on Improvement of Scanner System Based on Loongson 2P0500
abstract: In view of the high procurement cost in the domestic scanner market caused by high technical thresholds, market monopoly, and expensive prices, a brand-new scanner system is designed to promote the independent innovation and localization of high-speed scanners. Compared with the traditional ARM+FPGA development model, this scheme introduces the Loongson 2p0500 ASIC chip, which is based on the advanced LoongArch architecture, possesses powerful computing capabilities and high customization, and integrates widely used Linux and Free-RTOS systems, providing a stable and efficient operating environment for the scanner, significantly reducing development costs and shortening the product development cycle. Aiming at the problems of slow image transmission speed and image data processing speed in this design, algorithms based on the LoongArch architecture such as JPEG compression and efficient data sorting processing are also introduced, greatly improving the performance of this product. This efficient and economical development model has broad application prospects and can be promoted to other chip developments in the future.

articleTitle: VC-TGCN: A Novel Soft-Sensor Method of Silicon Content in Blast Furnaces
abstract: The soft sensor of silicon content in molten iron is crucial for the ironmaking process. Based on the temporal characteristic of the silicon content, several methods utilizing recurrent neural networks have been proposed and validated. Besides the temporal feature extraction in soft sensor, the inter-correlation of the variables in the ironmaking industry can be used to further improve the accuracy. But the existing methods for constructing graph structures using a single correlation metric limits the accuracy. To get the holistic correlation, we proposed a novel method called Vine Copula-Temporal and Graph Convolutional Network (VC-TGCN). We introduced the R-vine copula to model the correlations in multivariate joint distributions. The model combines the temporal and spatial feature extraction based on graph convolutional networks, time convolutional networks and the vine copula, which can obtain more comprehensive dynamic relationships and correlations between variables of the ironmaking process. Experiments validate the superiority of VC-TGCN over other models, demonstrating its feasibility in soft sensor of the silicon content.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation in Non-Cooperative Game Models with Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This study proposes a non-cooperative game model that includes a two-layer supply and demand relationship and employs reinforcement learning for its solution. The study takes the water resource allocation in Pujiang County, Jinhua City, Zhejiang Province, as a case study, constructing a non-cooperative game model with reservoirs, water plants, and fac-tories as the main entities. It simulates the strategic interactions among various water users to optimize the water resource allocation plan. This model takes into account the scarcity of water resources, the dynamic changes in demand, and the fairness of distribution. By introducing the CommFormer reinforcement learning algorithm, the model achieves policy optimization in complex and dynamic environments, reduces computational complexity, and speeds up decision-making response time.

articleTitle: Accurate Identification and Localization of Transmission Lines Under Complex Lighting for Distribution Network Power Supply Operation Robots
abstract: Accurate identification and position of transmission lines is critical for robots to safely and effectively perform distribution network operations. However, such tasks are often challenged by complex lighting conditions, where depth information can be easily lost. Transmission lines have limited texture features and reflective surfaces, making it difficult to match image feature points. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a visual perception system for weak texture targets under complex lighting, based on an “eye-on-hand” configuration and a depth complementation algorithm. Furthermore, a high-precision identification and localization method for transmission line grasping points is developed, utilizing the fusion of binocular visual color maps and depth maps. The proposed method has been shown to effectively solve the problem of identifying and localizing the grasping points of transmission lines under complex lighting conditions. Experiments demonstrated that the method can improve the localization accuracy to within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 4\text{mm}$</tex>, outperforming other algorithms. The method is characterized as simple and efficient, and it enhances the environmental adaptability of distribution network robots.

articleTitle: Multi-Robot Obstacle-Avoidance Formation Based on Graph Neural Networks and Imitation Learning
abstract: Obstacle avoidance is the basis for multi-robot systems to perform various tasks. Considering real-world scenarios where multi-robot formation has limited perception range and communication capabilities, achieving coordinated obstacle avoidance using decentralized control method while maintaining formation stability poses a significant challenge. In this paper, we propose a decentralized, learning-based control method using graph neural networks to achieve stable control of the formation. This method improves the convolution of the graph neural networks by combining the information of obstacles, and at the same time encodes the information of obstacles as the input of the graph neural networks as well. We use a modified artificial potential field method as an expert algorithm and train graph neural networks to imitate the outputs of the expert algorithm. This ultimately achieves obstacle avoidance for multi-robot formation, which is validated on physical robots. The experimental results demonstrate that the performance of our method is close to that of the expert algorithm, with a higher success rate of obstacle avoidance and a lower number of collisions. Moreover, it is more advantageous in maintaining the formation steady state, proving the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Temperature Prediction Method of Lithium-Ion Battery Pack Based on Attention Mechanism Optimized Convolutional Neural Network and Gated Recurrent Unit
abstract: Lithium-ion battery pack play a critical role in electric vehicles and renewable energy storage systems, with temperature regulation being crucial for their performance and lifespan. Elevated temperatures can expedite battery depletion, curtail cycle life, and heighten safety hazards. Consequently, precise temperature prediction and stringent control are essential. In this paper, we propose a temperature prediction method for lithium-ion battery pack based on convolutional neural network (CNN) and gated recurrent unit (GRU), with an integrated attention mechanism (AM) to augment the model's predictive prowess. Firstly, COMSOL Multiphysics software is used to simulate the operation process of lithium-ion battery pack, and a large amount of parameter data is collected as the training and testing set of the model. Subsequently, the CNN is combined with GRU, and the attention mechanism is introduced to enhance the prediction performance of the model. Empirical results demonstrate that the optimized CNN-GRU model exhibits high accuracy and reliability in temperature prediction of lithium-ion battery pack, with R2 values of more than 0.99, RMSE values of less than 0.08, and MSE values of less than 0.007 for both the training and test sets.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving in Data Aggregation for Smart Grid: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: The aggregation of smart grid data is essential for effective energy management and optimization. However, the aggregation process exposes data to risks such as network eavesdropping, data breaches, and malicious tampering, which can compromise user privacy and lead to data misuse. To address these privacy concerns in smart grid data aggregation, this paper introduces three evaluation criteria for assessing aggregation schemes and provides a comprehensive overview of existing solutions. The primary focus is on aggregation schemes based on homomorphic encryption, with a brief examination of alternative approaches. The methods and performance of each type of scheme are analyzed. In conclusion, the paper identifies the limitations of current schemes and offers suggestions for future research directions in privacy-preserving data aggregation within smart grids.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Economic Predictive Control for Coordinated Control System of Coal-fired Units
abstract: Coordinated control of coal-fired units is a key system to ensure the stability and economic operation of power supply. While the nonlinearity, strong coupling, and large inertia of coal-fired units bring about challenge for the model establishment resulting in unsatisfied control performance due to insufficient model accuracy. To address this issue, a novel data-driven economic predictive control method is proposed in this study. It utilizes a real-time updated dataset to affine the non-linear system as linear and predict the future trajectory of the system. In order to deal with the computational complexity caused by real-time updating of data sets and improve the computational efficiency, a two-stage algorithm is designed. The objective function of the first stage is replaced by an economic objective with real-time feedback instead of the original tracking objective, and the optimal solution is passed to the second stage, where it serves as a reference for tracking the economically optimal solution. Based on real data simulation, it is found that the proposed method efficiently responds to set point change as well as exhibits a small tracking error. It is also helpful for operating costs reduction, significantly improving the economic efficiency of the entire system.

articleTitle: Wide Area Ecological Environment Monitoring System Based on Cloud Platform
abstract: Ecological environment pollution events may seriously jeopardize industrial and agricultural production and people's lives. Such incidents will not only lead to a reduction in crop yields, a decline in soil quality, and the pollution of water resources but will also have a long-term impact on people's health. In addition, the deterioration of the ecological environment will destroy the natural ecological balance, leading to the reduction of biodiversity and the degradation of ecosystem function. To address the above problems, this paper designs a wide-area ecological environment monitoring system based on a cloud platform, including a low-power environment monitoring sensor node and a web-based monitoring interface based on a cloud platform. The environmental monitoring terminal node consists of an STM32F103VET6 microcontroller, a low-power narrowband IoT communication module, a positioning module, and a variety of specific sensors; the system adopts front-end and back-end separation technology to develop a Web-based monitoring interface, and builds an eco-environmental monitoring cloud platform through Tencent Cloud, and realizes data interaction between the sensing node and the cloud platform by using the message queuing telemetry transmission protocol so that the administrator can remotely view the data. The test results show that the system is suitable for ecological environment monitoring because of its wide monitoring range, high real-time transmission, and friendly user interface.

articleTitle: An Efficient Inductive Learning Model for Inferring Gene Regulatory Networks
abstract: Identifying gene regulatory networks (GRNs) from gene expression data has been a critical focus in systems biology. This paper proposes an efficient inductive learning framework based on a directed Graph Neural Network named GRDGNN_SP. This method, a significant departure from current GNN frameworks, provides a comprehensive and explicit regulatory relationship for a GRN. By combining StructPool for hierarchical pooling, GRDGNN_SP has shown impressive results across different datasets, species, and data types for inferring GRNs, demonstrating its effectiveness. It transforms the edge prediction task in GRNs into a graph multiclassification task, where subgraphs containing target nodes and their neighbors are classified. Furthermore, by using directed graph convolutional neural networks (DGCN), our model can infer the causal relationship in gene regulation. We improve the model's performance by integrating regulatory relationships from various heuristic methods through ensemble techniques. Experimental results demonstrate that the model proposed in this paper is highly effective in inferring the causal relationships of large-scale networks from gene expression data.

articleTitle: Robust Belief-Reward Approximate Value Iteration for Dynamic Detection Systems Allocation in Uncertain Counter-Drone Operations*
abstract: In the realm of counter-drone operations, adversaries introduce a spectrum of drone types and quantities across various sectors of the defended area. The high maneuverability inherent to drones leads to a dynamic and unpredictable evolution of threats within these regions. Concurrently, detection systems are subject to environmental influences, which introduce variability and incompleteness in the information they gather. To address these challenges, this study presents an enhanced Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) model, tailored for the complexities of drone countermeasures. The proposed model integrates a robust belief-reward frame-work and employs an approximation iteration method to refine strategic responses. This approach is designed to optimize the distribution of detection resources in countering drone threats. The experimental simulations illustrate a significant improvement in the precision of detection system allocation, achieving an enhancement of approximately 30% over standard methods. Additionally, the methodology proposed herein streamlines the dynamic deployment process of defensive systems, reducing the time expenditure in such operations.

articleTitle: Stochastic Configuration Networks for Data Augmented Seismic Magnitude Prediction
abstract: Geophysical exploration yields a vast amount of monitoring data that accurately captures the geological dynamics of areas under investigation, providing a rich dataset for the analysis of seismic events. Despite a growing interest in utilizing monitoring data for event-centric information learning, challenges such as data imbalance significantly pose formidable obstacle to accurate information learning. In this study, a novel data augmentation method termed Adaptive Feature Expansion (AFE) is proposed to mitigate data imbalance. Additionally, an innovative randomized learning paradigm with incremental model configuration mechanism, Stochastic Configuration Networks (SCNs), is employed to learn seismic information and predict magnitude ranges. The experimental results indicate that AFE can effectively balance seismic data in the feature space and present excellent scalability. SCNs outperform traditional machine learning algorithms in terms of predictive performance. This work makes insightful contributions to geological hazard assessment.

articleTitle: APF-RRT*: Sampling-Based Motion Planning via Artificial Potential Field
abstract: Path planning is a fundamental problem in the field of autonomous systems, particularly when it comes to navigating complex environments and avoiding obstacles. Traditional sampling-based algorithms like Rapidly-Exploring Random Trees (RRT) and its variants such as RRT* have been widely used for solving high-dimensional path planning problems. However, these methods often suffer from suboptimal path quality and high computational costs in cluttered environments. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel path planning algorithm, APF-RRT*, which combines the advantages of Artificial Potential Fields (APF) with RRT* to enhance convergence speed, path smoothness, and overall trajectory quality. By integrating APF's attractive and repulsive forces into the sampling process, the proposed method guides the random search towards feasible regions while maintaining trajectory smoothness. Experimental results demonstrate that APF-RRT* not only reduces the number of required nodes but also improves the path quality compared to conventional RRT* and APF-RRT algorithms. APF-RRT* achieves a 15.1% reduction in average convergence time and a 52.2% decrease in node count while delivering smoother paths. The proposed algorithm shows promise in addressing path planning challenges in dynamic and complex environments, providing a reliable solution for real-time navigation tasks in autonomous systems.

articleTitle: Intelligent Optimal Input-Constrained Control with Model Uncertainty and External Disturbance Applied to Robotic Manipulators
abstract: This paper investigates a novel critic optimal input-constrained control strategy with disturbance attenuation for robotic manipulators subject to model perturbation and external disturbance. Drawing upon the framework of a two-player zero-sum differential game initially designed to handle external disturbance, we incorporate an auxiliary boundary function into the performance index function to tackle model uncertainty. Notably, a nonquadratic utility is adopted to compensate for input saturation. Moreover, the approximate optimal control policy and the worst-case disturbance law are solved through the enhanced adaptive critic algorithm with an additional stabilizing component. Using Lyapunov theory, the stability of the system state and the convergence of network weight are thoroughly proven. Finally, comparative numerical simulation and Monte Carlo test are implemented to validate the effectiveness of the presented approach.

articleTitle: The Analysis and Research on the Effects Caused by the Pilot Model Parameters to the Pilot Induced Oscillation and Feasible Countermeasure of the Helicopter
abstract: The closed-loop stability analysis method on the pilot model parameters is proposed for pilot induced oscillation problem caused by the pilot in the closed loop of the helicopter. The control characteristics of the helicopter pilot coupling closed-loop system are studied with different pilot model parameters. Then feasible countermeasures to improve the stability, robustness as well as the flight quality of the helicopter in order to restrain the PIO are discussed from the perspectives of the pilot's manipulation and the flight control system. Results show that the increase of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{k}_{\boldsymbol{pl}}, \boldsymbol{T}_{\boldsymbol{L}}, \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\boldsymbol{pl}}$</tex> and the decrease of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{T}_{\boldsymbol{l}}$</tex> lead to larger probability of the PIO and more unstable and unrobust helicopter pilot coupling closed-loop system. The pilot should be well-trained and the manipulation should be moderate, the parameters of the flight control system should be adjusted properly in accordance with the demands of the mission in order to enhance the flight stability, robustness and quality, the improved performances of the helicopter pilot coupling closed-loop system are desirable. The analysis methods proposed in this paper reveal the physical nature of the research issue qualitatively and quantitatively, which is theoretically and practically referential to the helicopter flight.

articleTitle: Preference-Based Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning with Explicit Reward Modeling
abstract: Multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) often faces challenges in defining a single reward that captures complex real-world objectives. In this paper, we introduce Preference-based Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning (Pb-MORL), which addresses this challenge by utilizing human preferences, as a more intuitive and flexible alternative to reward functions. Our key contribution is the development of an explicit multi-objective reward model, which aligns with preference data through the Bradley-Terry model and cross-entropy optimization. This model serves as a bridge between qualitative preferences and the quantitative needs of MORL, facilitating policy optimization without predefined rewards. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Pb-MORL achieves comparable performance to state-of-the-art MORL methods, showcasing its potential for broader real-world applications.

articleTitle: Entropy-Guided Reinforced Open World Active 3D Object Detection Learning
abstract: Traditional fully annotated closed set 3D object detection methods improve model performance but are impractical in real-world settings due to the emergence of new categories and the complexity of 3D annotations. Open-World Object Detection (OWOD) addresses these issues but relies heavily on manual labeling, which is costly. This paper focuses on open world active learning and proposes an entropy-guided reinforced open world active 3D object detection (EROA). EROA regards active learning as a reinforcement learning problem tailored for open driving scenarios. We use entropy as a reward metric for efficient reinforcement learning. We also leverage knowledge from the 2D domain using object-level large-scale vision-language models to enhance sample selection. Extensive experiments evidence that the proposed EROA meets the dynamic and cost-sensitive requirements of autonomous driving, enabling real-time detection of both known and unknown objects.

articleTitle: Distributed State Estimation with Random Switching Topology Under Sensor Saturation Constraints
abstract: This paper presents a distributed robust filtering technique for sensor networks that incorporates randomly switching communication topologies and sensor saturation nonlinearities. In the sensor network, numerous sensor nodes are placed to detect and measure the target plant, transmitting data to a remote filter via the network. Among the filter network, each local estimator receives measurement data from sensor nodes and estimation data from neighboring nodes through a randomly varying topology. The sensor network employs a Bernoulli binary distribution to model random saturation nonlinearity, while random switching topologies are characterized using a non-homogeneous Markov chain. Next, a sufficient condition for the existence of a distributed filter is presented using the linear matrix inequality (LMI). Lastly, a numerical example illustrates the viability of the designed strategy.

articleTitle: Synchronous Control of H-type Linear Motor System via Super-Twisting Sliding Mode
abstract: In this paper, a synchronous control strategy based on super-twisting sliding mode algorithm is proposed to enhance the tracking accuracy and robustness of H-type linear motor systems. Such systems are widely utilized in precision manufacturing owing to their high precision and fast response. Firstly, the dynamic model is established based on the coupling dynamics analysis of the H-type system. Secondly, a supertwisting sliding mode controller (STSMC) with linear terms is designed, which effectively reduces the chattering associated with conventional sliding mode control, while maintaining good robustness. Thirdly, a super-twisting extended state observer (STESO) is introduced to handle large fluctuations in the early estimation process of linear extended state observer (LESO), so as to effectively observe and compensate the uncertainties and external disturbances. Finally, experimental results demonstrate that the STESO-based STSMC greatly improves the anti-disturbance ability and tracking accuracy of the H-type system.

articleTitle: LVIO-MOT: Online Lidar-Visual-Inertial Odometry with Multiple Object Tracking
abstract: Previous research has demonstrated that combining Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) and Multiple Object Tracking (MOT) yields better performance than using either one alone. In this paper, we present LVIO-MOT, an online stereo lidar-visual-inertial odometry which simultaneously tracks poses of objects while performing robot ego-motion tracking. LVIO-MOT consists of the visual-inertial system (VIS) and the lidar-Inertial system (LIS), and each subsystem includes both localization and MOT modules. The localization modules are connected through multi-sensor graph optimization, while the MOT modules extract new targets using VIS, and both systems collaborate to track the targets. Our experiments on the KITTI dataset demonstrate that our system has reached satisfying performance on both robot ego-motion and object tracking.

articleTitle: Effective and Robust Point Cloud Registration in Weak Texture Regions
abstract: Point cloud registration, a crucial component of 3D visual tasks such as AR, SLAM, and 3D reconstruction, aligns multiple point clouds by finding transformations. The success of point cloud registration largely hinges on finding high-quality point correspondences, which involves detecting overlapping regions between point clouds. While existing methods have demonstrated excellent performance in both indoor and outdoor scenes, they often falter in weak texture regions with similar structural features, producing numerous erroneous correspondences and leading to registration failure. In this paper, we propose a novel point cloud registration method aimed at reducing matching errors in weak texture regions. We introduce a weak texture score to identify regions with less distinctive structural features, and perform random downsampling based on this score to mitigate interference from weak texture regions. Additionally, we develop a new transformer-based matcher for the matching stage, which incorporates rotary position embedding and bidirectional attention to simplify calculations. This approach maintains high-speed computation while enhancing robustness and registration performance. Experimental results demonstrate that our method not only achieves superior matching accuracy compared to existing methods but also offers faster inference speeds, underscoring the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Combination Control Method of Multi-Link Flexible Manipulator
abstract: In order to overcome the position error caused by the characteristics of the flexible manipulator, a combination control method is proposed to distinguish the speed and slow variable sub-systems. Firstly, the elastic deformation of the flexible manipulator is described by the hypothesis mode method, and then the dynamic equation of the flexible manipulator is established by the Lagrange method. The flexible manipulator system is decomposed into a fast subsystem and a slow subsystem by the singular perturbation method. Combining adaptive control and synovial variable structure, a slow variable subsystem control method based on adaptive sliding mode variable structure control is proposed to solve the strong nonlinearity and parameter uncertainty of the slow variable subsystem. In view of the inaccuracy of the model of the fast variable subsystem, the fuzzy controller of the fast variable subsystem is designed because the fuzzy control has no requirement on the model precision. The simulation results show that compared with the traditional single control, the position error of the manipulator is greatly reduced, the response state and output torque of the system is more stable, and the control accuracy and stability of the flexible manipulator are greatly improved.

Author Keywords: adaptive sliding mode variable structure control

articleTitle: Privacy Preserving Second-Order Consensus by Adding Edge-Based Perturbations
abstract: Many works on privacy-preserving consensus of multi-agents are limited to first-order dynamics, and developing privacy-preserving consensus algorithms based on second-order dynamical network systems has a stronger need for engineering practicality and presents a greater challenge. In this paper, we propose a privacy-preserving second-order consensus algorithm based on strongly connected directed graphs. The algorithm avoids direct interaction of real states among individuals by adding well-designed perturbation signals based on commu-nication edges. Theoretical results indicate that the proposed algorithm is able to achieve accurate second-order dynamic consensus. Moreover, through rigid theoretical analysis, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for an agent to maintain its position and velocity privacy in the face of an internal honest-but-curious agent. Simulation examples verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Condition-Adaptive Dynamic Evolution Method for Digital Twin of Rolling Bearings Based on Continual Learning
abstract: As a common and key part of rotating machinery, rolling bearings mainly determine the health of the equipment. Digital Twin (DT) can help comprehensively monitor and predict the remaining useful life (RUL) of rolling bearings by generating a high-fidelity model of the physical object. Due to the varying working conditions faced in real industrial applications, the existing DT model of rolling bearings urgently needs continuous dynamic evolution ability and resource-efficient updating method. In this work, we propose an end-edge-cloud based DT architecture for rolling bearings, which includes two stages: DT construction and DT update. For adapting to dynamic changes of physical entities under various working conditions, a Condition-Adaptive Dynamic Continual Learning Digital Twin Model (CADCL-DTM) is designed, which applies different penalties to continual learning tasks in both intra-condition and intercondition scenarios. Furthermore, we apply the proposed DT methods to RUL prediction of rolling bearings, enabling the DT model to continuously learn new conditions while mitigating catastrophic forgetting of old ones. Comprehensive experiments have been carried out with FEMTO-ST bearing to verify the dynamic updating ability and forgetting performance under the same working conditions and different working conditions, respectively.

articleTitle: Object Recognition and Grasp Detection in Complex Scenarios for Home Service Robot
abstract: With the development of artificial intelligence, home service robots have been widely applied in daily life. As one of the fundamental functions of service robots, object grasping helps improve the level of unmanned and intelligent household. However, traditional robots still face challenges in flexibility and accuracy in complex home environments. In this paper, an object recognition and grasp detection system in complex scenarios for home service robots is proposed. The system consists of four modules: image acquisition, human-machine interaction software, RGB-D image processing, and robot control. The image acquisition module captures RGB and depth images of the work area and sends them to the software. The RGB-D image processing module begins with object recognition to obtain object categories and bounding box with the help of YOLOv8. The target point cloud is produced by combining the target subimage and corresponding depth information, followed by depth completion and plane expansion. Then the processed point cloud is fed into a Graspnet pose estimation network to calculate the 6D grasping pose for service robot. And finally, the robot control module is invoked to carry out the corresponding target grasping action. To evaluate the performance, an experimental platform for home service robot is built to grasp various daily necessities. The results tell that the average accuracy for object recognition reaches up to 98.3%, the success rate for single-target grasping is 94.4%, and the success rate for multi-target grasping can achieve 80%.

articleTitle: Carbon Tracing Method for Commercial and Office Park Distribution Networks Considering Load-Side Electricity Substitution
abstract: Electricity substitution is one of the main forms of energy transition. By replacing the combustion of traditional fossil fuels with electricity, it plays a significant role in achieving the “dual carbon” goals. However, electricity substitution loads in the power system still produce carbon emissions. To clarify the carbon reduction benefits before and after electricity substitution, a carbon tracing method for the distribution network in commercial and office parks considering load-side electricity substitution is proposed. Firstly, based on the iterative characteristics of carbon emission flow, a precise load-side carbon emission tracing model is established. Secondly, combining the carbon emission conversion mechanism of electricity substitution loads, the carbon emission factor is corrected to address the unfair problem of the carbon emission flow method allocating the carbon emissions of electricity substitution loads to various nodes, thus constructing a load-side electricity substitution model. Finally, a commercial and office park in a certain region is used as an example to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results show that this method is more equitable in measuring the carbon emissions of electricity substitution loads and can provide scientifically accurate quantitative results for assessing carbon reduction indicators and the effectiveness of energy-saving technologies in commercial and office park distribution networks.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Fault Diagnosis in Quadcopter Actuators: A CNN-LSTM Network with Bayesian Optimization
abstract: In recent years, deep neural networks have shown promising results in modern fault diagnosis. This paper focuses on diagnosing actuator faults in quadcopters using a deep learning strategy. Considering the dynamic and temporal characteristics of quadcopters, a deep neural network model consists of the convolution neural network and the long short-term memory network (CNN-LSTM) is designed with the exponential linear unit (ELU) activation function. To enhance the diagnostic capability, Bayesian optimization (BO) algorithm is utilized for selecting optimal hyperparameters of the designed deep neural network model. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve high accuracy in actuator fault diagnosis of quadcopters.

articleTitle: CG-YOLO: A Lightweight, High-Accuracy Gesture Recognition Method for Human-Computer Interaction
abstract: Although gesture recognition technology has made significant progress, its accuracy and robustness in practical applications are still insufficient due to factors such as complex environments, lighting variations, and background interference. This paper proposes a lightweight and high-accuracy humancomputer interaction gesture recognition method called CGYOLO to address these issues. We reconstruct the backbone network of YOLOv8s by introducing a Contextual Feature Aggregation Backbone Network (ContextRepViT) to enhance the model's accuracy in recognizing small-sized hand targets, thus solving the problems of missed and false detections in complex backgrounds. Additionally, we propose a lightweight feature extraction module (GSRepNCSP) to redesign the Contextual 2D Features (C2f) modules in the Head network of YOLOv8s, improving parameters utilization and reducing computational load. Experimental results on the public HaGRID dataset show that, compared to YOLOv8s, the CG-YOLO reduces the number of parameters by 1.3M, and improves Precision, Recall, mAP@0.5, and mAP@0.5-0.95 by 3.2%, 1.5%, 2%, and 3.9%, respectively. Moreover, the human-robot interaction experiments with the quadruped robot also verified the effectiveness of the CG-YOLO.

articleTitle: Adaptive Backstepping Fractional-Order Global Sliding Mode Control for Quadrotor Aircraft
abstract: In this work, an adaptive fractional-order sliding mode control method is illustrated of the quadcopter unmanned aerial vehicles where the perturbation is taken into consideration. The nonlinear mathematical model under external disturbances is established through the Newton-Euler mechanics theory. The fractional-order sliding mode control algorithm proposed in this paper not only reduces the chattering of the closed-loop system, but also guarantees the system converge to stable state within a finite time. In addition, the adaptive law estimates and compensates for the upper bounds of the disturbances and uncertainties. Furthermore, Lyapunov analysis is used to ensure the stability of the quadrotor UAV system and the robustness of the controller under external disturbances. Finally, different simulations are carried out in the MATLAB environment to verify effectiveness and advantages of the proposed strategy compared to the existed controllers. Moreover, a comparative result is accomplished to highlight the significant outperformance of the presented scheme.

articleTitle: Adaptive Tracking of Uncertain Markovian Jump Nonlinear Systems with Random Actuator Faults
abstract: This article deals with the adaptive fault-tolerant tracking problem for uncertain Markovian jump nonlinear systems (MJNSs) in a stochastic framework. A joint and a scalar Markovian process are employed to describe behaviors of the unknown parameters and actuator faults, respectively, thereby characterizing uncertainties in a random manner. With the aid of the backstepping technique, an adaptive tracking controller as well as the corresponding parameter update laws is constructed by treating the regimes of all Markovian variables as constants. It is shown that with appropriate design parameters, the output tracking error can converge into a small adjustable residual set in the sense of mean quadratic value while all closed-loop signals are bounded in probability, regardless of infinite number of random abrupt jumps in both uncertain parameters and the control input. An illustrative example is provided to show the effectiveness of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Human Arm Trajectory Prediction Framework for Safe and Efficient Human-Robot Collaboration
abstract: Accurately prediction of human arm trajectories is necessary to the safe and efficient execution of human-robot collaborative tasks. Traditional algorithms often struggling with low accuracy and uncertainty estimation. To address these challenges, a framework tailored for human arm trajectory prediction in collaborative scenarios is proposed. Firstly, one collects three-dimensional spatial data of trajectory points on the human upper limb by utilizing depth camera and complementary devices, and constructing a dataset with five operational tasks. Preprocessing involves outlier removal and, smoothing to enhance data quality. To bolster early-stage position estimation accuracy, one integrates observed and predicted arm trajectories, and employing Gaussian Mixture Model for current hand motion target prediction. Subsequently, one develops an Informer prediction model for human arm trajectories. Compared with related works, the result on predicted and actual data curves demonstrating superior performance over four alternative approaches.

articleTitle: Research on Competency of High-Speed Railway Train Dispatchers for Intelligent Dispatching System
abstract: To better evaluate the competency of high-speed rail (HSR) dispatcher within intelligent dispatch system, this paper first constructs a competency indicator system for HSR dispatchers, comprising 4 primary indexes and 18 secondary indexes. Interval-valued intuitionistic fuzzy sets (IVIF) are employed to represent competency indexes, addressing the fuzziness and uncertainty in the evaluation process. To enhance the accuracy of weight calculations, this paper integrates subjective and objective weights by leveraging game theory to calculate comprehensive weights. Additionally, regret theory is applied to model the psychological behavior of decision-makers, forming the basis for a competency evaluation method rooted in this framework. A case study verifies the practicality and scientific validity of this method. The research results indicate that this evaluation method can effectively assess the competency of HSR dispatcher, providing a new tool for performance evaluation within the dispatch departments of railway transport systems.

articleTitle: Integrated Anomaly Detection and Machine Learning Reconstruction for Offshore Wind Power Cleansing
abstract: Offshore wind energy, an efficient renewable source, has gained significant attention. However, its intermittency and data anomalies pose challenges for accurate power prediction. To address this, we propose an anomaly detection model based on power curve characteristics and domain knowledge. The model employs ensemble learning, integrating LOF, DBSCAN, and IF algorithms to overcome individual model limitations. We enhance raw multivariate features through feature engineering and use LightGBM for anomalous data reconstruction. Validated on a real-world dataset from a Fujian, China offshore wind farm, results show bin curve errors reduced by 11.8%-26.5% post-reconstruction.
