When applied to benchmark power prediction models, reconstructed data improves prediction accuracy by 4%-7%. Computational results confirm that our strategy accurately identifies and rectifies offshore wind power data anomalies, significantly enhancing prediction accuracy and ensuring efficient, stable wind farm operation.

articleTitle: Hybrid Attention DNN Capacity Prediction for Fast Charging Batteries Based on Partial Charging Data
abstract: To ease range anxiety and shorten recharging time, today's electric vehicles (EVs) often require large-capacity battery systems with fast charging. It is important to monitor and evaluate the battery state of health (SOH) for EVs' safe and durable operation. In this work, an attention-based hybrid deep neural network (DNN) is developed to predict battery charge capacity at the end of each charging cycle. First, correlation analysis is implemented to reveal the correlations of charging variables to the charge capacity. Second, the charging curves of all battery cells are extracted, and 90 points of charging data collected within 5 minutes are used as input to predict the charge capacity. Third, by using the charging time (t), charging current (I), and cell voltage (V) data on the early constant current charging stage as inputs, the proposed method generates charge capacity prediction with an average RMSE of 0.0205 Ah (1.86% of the nominal capacity of 1.1 Ah), which outperforms mainstream deep learning methods including solo and hybrid models.

articleTitle: SAVJTNNGAN: More Specific Information for Graph Structure Translation
abstract: Graph structure translation is an important re-search problem applicable in various scenarios, where graph translation models serve as advantageous tools for relationship prediction and network optimization. The application of graph translation in the field of drug molecules is a prominent area of deep learning implementation, focusing on optimizing target properties while maintaining a certain similarity between evolved molecules. To enhance the success rate of translation, we propose a new molecular translation model based on the VJTNNGAN model, which integrates SAGAN to optimize feature extraction using a message passing network combined with attention mechanisms. Additionally, we enhance the performance of the graph decoder by incorporating graph decoding information into GAN network training. Finally, we validate the translation performance of the SAVJTNNGAN network through testing on relevant datasets. And the translation success rate has improved on both the QED and Drd2 datasets.

articleTitle: KANMixer: A Fully Linear Network with Multi-Scale Feature Awareness for Power Quality Classification Tasks
abstract: This study introduces a novel power quality disturbance classification model, KANMixer, designed based on a fully linear KAN network with multi-scale feature perception. KAN-Mixer incorporates a multi-scale feature extraction mechanism that effectively captures the characteristics of input signals across different temporal scales. The model employs a fully linear layer architecture, founded on KANLinear, and combines piecewise polynomial interpolation with basic linear transformations to enhance the capture of nonlinear features. Experimental results demonstrate that KANMixer excels in power quality disturbance classification tasks, outperforming traditional methods across multiple evaluation metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and Fl-score. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of each component of the model, particularly highlighting the significant advantages of KANLinear over traditional MLPs. This research provides an efficient and accurate new method for power quality disturbance classification, which is crucial for enhancing the safety and stability of power systems.

articleTitle: Large Scale and High-Precision Crop Recognition Using Satellite Remote Sensing Images
abstract: Precise large-scale crop recognition is crucial for estimating crop yield and carbon assimilation. Current research on crop type recognition based on deep learning is often limited to a single crop and small areas, with poor model transferability. When performing multi-crop recognition over large areas, the accuracy significantly decreases. Therefore, it is necessary to establish a high-precision crop type recognition model with strong generalization capability. A deep learning model (LSTM-Transformer Parallel, LTP) based on the combination of LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) network and Transformer self-attention mechanism architecture is proposed in this paper. The model captures the dependencies among crop NDVI time series data to achieve high-precision recognition of large-scale crop types. Experimental results show that in crop recognition experiments using small-scale agricultural area data, the recognition results of the LTP, TSMixer, and SegRNN models all performed excellently, with average accuracies of 94.55%, 94.41%, and 94.79%, respectively. In contrast, in crop recognition experiments using large-scale agricultural area data, the average accuracy of the LTP model reaches 93.77%, while the accuracies of the TSMixer and SegRNN models are 82.30% and 84.13%, respectively. This indicates that the LTP model not only performs well on small-scale agricultural area datasets but also significantly outperforms models in the literature on large-scale agricultural area datasets, demonstrating strong generalization capability. It provides a reliable method for large-scale multi-crop recognition, contributing to global food security and carbon cycle assessment.

articleTitle: Hybrid Consensus-Based Cubature Information Filter and Covariance Intersection Strategy for Hierarchical Distributed State Estimation
abstract: In this paper, a novel hybrid consensus-based distributed cubature information filter and sequential covariance intersection estimator (CDCIF-SCI) is proposed for hierarchical distributed state estimation. A comprehensive hierarchical fusion structure is presented, utilizing the CDCIF filter at the local sensor layer and the SCI fuser at the cluster head layer. At the local sensor layer, the hybrid consensus strategy is integrated into the cubature information filter to achieve distributed state estimation. At the cluster head layer, the global fusion center employs a sequentially implemented multi-sensor covariance intersection fusion among the estimates from each cluster to enhance accuracy. Furthermore, an overall performance analysis of the CDCIF-SCI is provided, offering theoretical insights into the estimator's accuracy. Numerical simulation is conducted to validate the effectiveness of the estimator.

articleTitle: CFA: Consistent Feature Attribution for Black-Box Adversarial Attack Against Object Detection
abstract: Adversarial attack methods in black-box settings based on transferability have garnered significant attention. The inherent transferability of adversarial examples allows them to attack DNN models with unknown structures and parameters. Investigating the source of their transferability can help reveal the internal working mechanisms of DNN models and enhance their interpretability. Feature-level attack, a type to perform black-box adversarial attack, fully utilizes the internal information of models. To improve the transferability of feature-level attacks in the object detection task, this paper proposes to interact with the middle and deep feature maps of the backbone network of the object detector using the clean image and the corresponding gradients to explore the consistency of the model's inference logic reflected in the feature maps. We design a consistent feature attribution loss function to guide the adversarial patch to disrupt features that are beneficial for the model's correct predictions. We obtained transferable adversarial patches through this approach, and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method. Our project's code will be available at https://github.com/BUCT-IUSRC/Research_CFA.

articleTitle: A Scheduling Method for Blast Furnace Gas Systems Based on Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks and Process Rules
abstract: Blast furnace gas (BFG), a vital byproduct energy resource in the ironmaking process, can be efficiently managed through proper scheduling to minimize emissions and augment productivity. A novel scheduling method for BFG systems based on an improved Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (CGAN) and process rules is proposed. Based on the Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP) and the process production mechanism under ideal conditions, a scenario generative model is constructed to constrain the training process with the rules of the changes among scenario factors. Labels are used as condition information for CGAN to generate the corresponding labeled scenarios. Then, by matching real-time operational data with the generated scenarios, the scheduling solution is derived for the given condition. Using the actual data collected from a large steel enterprise, the validation experiments confirm that the scheduling scenarios generated by the proposed method are consistent with actual operational patterns. Moreover, it delivers viable and rational scheduling solutions for new operating conditions, safeguarding the safe operation of the BFG system.

articleTitle: YOLOv5-LF: An Optimized YOLOv5 Algorithm for Real-Time Automatic Tracking
abstract: Recent research has concentrated on enhancing robot visual tracking in dynamic settings. To boost real-time tracking capabilities, we introduce an optimized robot visual tracking control system that employs an advanced lightweight YOLOv5 algorithm. This system integrates the LCNet-a lightweight CPU-based Convolutional Neural Network-and a PConv-driven FasterNet module, both of which significantly enhance the detection of object features. Our experimental setup, which uses an industrial camera to acquire target pose data, demonstrates that after implementing the optimized model, the system efficiently detects and tracks moving objects in real-time from video streams. The gimbal's positioning is dynamically adjusted in response to the moving target's image displacement. The YOLOv5-LF network model, quantified with OpenVINO, has demonstrated a detection accuracy of 95.23% and a recognition rate of 90 frames per second (FPS) on Intel's NUC. This not only ensures seamless real-time system management but also enhances the precision of object detection. The refined detection algorithm notably outperforms the original network in terms of visual tracking efficacy on our experimental platform.

articleTitle: Constrained Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithm with Population Image Sharpening
abstract: Various real-world problems can be attributed to constrained multi-objective optimization problems, and many techniques have been proposed to deal with them. However, how to generate a promising offspring population according to the parent population is still a challenge. Given this, a constrained multi-objective evolutionary optimization method with population image sharpening is proposed. In this method, a column-oriented Sobel operator is introduced to participate in the population reproduction, which can be embedded into existing evolutionary algorithms easily. The proposed method is compared with seven state-of-the-art constrained evolutionary algorithms on two test suites and applied to the dispatch optimization problem of integrated coal mine energy systems. Experimental results verify the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method in solving constrained multi-objective optimization problems.

articleTitle: Neural correlation study of swinging and standing during dual-task walking-A pilot study
abstract: The walking process is often accompanied by other cognitive tasks, which will cause certain interference to the gait. It is important to explore the cognitive characteristics of brain at different stages during dual-task walking for the neural decoding of real gait features. By collecting and analyzing EEG signals of healthy subjects during walking of different cognitive tasks, this study completed the analysis of EEG characteristics during the standing and swinging stages of the whole gait cycle. The time-frequency characteristics of EEG signals on the main electrodes in the locomotor brain, the topological distribution of power spectral density in the swinging and standing phases, and the corresponding brain functional network structure were analyzed. The results showed that the temporal-frequency characteristics and brain functional network connections differed significantly between the non-cognitive and cognitive tasks, and the power spectral characteristics and network topological connections of the EEG signals also showed significant differences between the swinging and the standing phases. However, the power spectral values and functional brain connectivity relationships did not differ between arithmetic operation task and left and right brain task. There was no significant variability in the topological distribution of power spectrum values across brain regions. These results suggest that it is feasible to achieve effective recognition of swing and stand phases within the gait cycle based on EEG features analysis, and that the identification of EEG signals in different walking phases can contribute to the development of brain-computer interface-based rehabilitation and robotic assistive systems.

articleTitle: Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Generation Forecasting with Dynamic Decomposition and Digital-Analog Fusion
abstract: Accurately predicting photovoltaic (PV) power generation is crucial for energy companies to plan and conduct safety assessments. However, existing model-based methods are limited by low prediction accuracy, while data-driven methods also suffer from low accuracy due to the difficulty in extracting time series features from raw data. To address these issues, we developed a method based on improved moving average decomposition, which achieves short-term PV power generation prediction by integrating Unscented Kalman Filtering and an extended long short-term memory network (xLSTM). First, we used an exponentially weighted moving average method to decompose the data into seasonal and trend components, specifically modeling the trend component using a double exponential model. Second, the xLSTM consists of two improved LSTM modules, sLSTM and mLSTM, which enhance storage decision-making capabilities and storage capacity, respectively, and enable parallelization. Finally, through PV power generation prediction experiments, the results demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing methods in prediction accuracy, with an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> prediction result reaching 97%.

articleTitle: Research on the Regional Pricing Strategy of Electric Vehicle Aggregators Based on Master-Slave Game Theory
abstract: The primary active load on China's distribution network side is electric vehicles. As electric vehicles in China rapidly develop, their numbers are steadily increasing, allowing for more interactions with the power grid. Despite the widespread adoption, the scattered distribution of electric vehicles makes aggregating them through regional aggregators a new direction in smart grid development. However, as the demand for electric vehicle charging often fluctuates with electricity prices, formulating rational and mutually beneficial power purchase and sale strategies for aggregators has emerged as a new focus in regional integrated energy system research. This paper explores pricing strategies for electric vehicle aggregators, introducing a power purchase and sale pricing strategy based on a master-slave game. The pursuit of maximizing their respective interests by electric vehicle aggregators and owners is modeled as a master-slave game. Using an adaptive differential evolution algorithm combined with quadratic programming, the Nash equilibrium solution is determined, facilitating the derivation of the aggregators' optimal pricing strategy. Furthermore, through simulations and case studies, the impact of different electric vehicle user types on aggregators' pricing strategies and profits is analyzed.

articleTitle: Dynamic Real Time Event-Triggered Scheduling for Hydrogen-Based Integrated Energy System
abstract: The non periodic disturbance in hydrogen-based integrated energy system (HIES) pose a significant challenge in system scheduling. Traditional static event-triggered scheduling require a carefully designed of event-triggered boundaries. Over tightly boundaries can result in excessive computations, while over loosely may lead to non-optimal scheduling. In this paper, a optimized scheduling problem and a dynamic real time event-triggered approach is developed for real time scheduling of HIES to capture the non periodic disturbance. The scheduling problem can be divided into an upper-level primal problem and a lower-level fixed problem by fixing binary logic variables. The dynamic event boundaries include renewable, load and device operation boundaries, which is obtained by dual sensitivity analysis of a fixed scheduling problem. The developed approach ensures both optimality and real-time performance by solving the fixed problem through real-time computations and triggering the primal problem with dynamic boundaries. The numerical result shows that the scheduling can respond to promptly events, and the merits of obtaining method of event boundaries are also demonstrated.

articleTitle: CVaR-based Thompson Sampling for Factored Multi-agent Multi-Armed Risk-aware Bandit
abstract: Risk-aware online learning and bandit algorithms have been successfully applied in scenarios where optimizing the expected reward is not sufficient to achieve desired outcomes due to the presence of uncertainty. However, distributed decision-making under uncertainty in multi-agent systems has become increasingly important for addressing real-world tasks. Our research focuses on developing a distributed risk-aware decision-making approach that optimizes a shared objective in a network of loosely coupled agents. Specifically, we address the problem of regret minimization in the multi-agent multi-armed risk-aware bandit (MAMARAB) framework, where each arm follows a Gaussian distribution with bounded variances and is evaluated using Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR). To tackle this problem, we propose a novel CVaR-based multi-agent Thompson sampling (CVaR-MATS) algorithm, which selects actions based on the CVaR measure to balance exploration and exploitation while taking into account the risk associated with each arm. Moreover, to provide theoretical guarantees, we derive a regret bound for the CVaR-MATS algorithm that is sub-linear in time and exhibits low-order polynomial growth concerning the highest number of actions in sparse coordination graphs.

articleTitle: Towards Adaptive Cybersecurity: Implementing FedIDFR in Kubernetes for Enhanced Protection
abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has significantly enhanced agility and productivity in the industrial sectors by interconnecting smart sensors and actuators. However, this increased connectivity also broadens the attack surface and exposes traditionally isolated devices to evolving cybersecurity threats. Addressing this need, this paper facilitates a novel integration of Kubernetes' flexible container orchestration with the next-generation, learning-based firewall techniques, introducing the Federated Incremental Learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems and Dynamic Firewall Rule management (FedIDFR) framework. The FedIDFR framework harnesses Kubernetes' container orchestration capabilities to enhance the flexibility, scalability, and responsiveness of security services, providing a robust solution to the evolving industrial security needs. For the dynamic firewall management, we employ a federated incremental learning algorithm to enable real-time and adaptive security responses to a wide variety of threats. This incremental approach surpasses the static dataset limitations while preserving industrial business privacy. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate a significant 24.0% improvement in response times over traditional deployments, illustrating the benefits of our approach in the dynamic networked industrial systems. These results also establish a new benchmark for adaptive and resilient network security architectures, particularly in settings demanding high flexibility and rapid response to the emerging threats.

articleTitle: Indoor Temperature Field Modeling Based on Neural Network without Real Data
abstract: Accurately capturing and reconstructing the indoor temperature field is the key to meet the requirements of indoor environmental comfort and energy saving. Traditional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) methods and surrogate models are time-consuming and have challenges in simulating inlet and outlet boundary conditions and initial conditions, which may lead to inaccurate results. Artificial neural networks (ANNs) can reconstruct airflow fields directly from measurements, eliminating the need for large and potentially inaccurate CFD databases. However, because ANNs are purely data-driven, they can sometimes produce unphysical results. Incorporating physical laws into neural networks can address this issue. In this study, physical laws are integrated into ANN s. To improve the accuracy of ANN predictions, boundary conditions are strictly enforced using a hard constraint method, ensuring that the edge points comply with physical laws. This paper sets up a virtual indoor environment to determine the inlet and outlet positions as well as the fluid flow rate. The loss function is divided into the mean square error (MSE) of data and the losses of physical information calculated by different components. The experimental results indicate that, compared to the traditional CFD method, the neural network has higher prediction accuracy and faster calculation speed under hard constraint.

articleTitle: Unified DRL for Enhanced Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling with Transportation Constraints
abstract: In the domain of smart manufacturing systems (SMSs),the flexible job-shop scheduling problem with transportation constraints (FJSPT) represents a crucial challenge and holds the potential to significantly enhance production efficiency. Extending beyond the traditional job-shop scheduling problem (JSP), FJSPT incorporates the scheduling of automated guided vehicles (AGVs) to transport intermediate products between machines. Despite the promise of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) in solving combinatorial optimization problems, there remains a notable scarcity of research employing DRL to tackle FJSPT. To address this gap, this paper introduces an end-to-end DRL approach for simultaneous scheduling of machines and AGVs in FJSPT. The proposed method amalgamates operation selection, machine assignment, and AGV planning into a unified decision-making process, leveraging a graph attention network (GAT) and the proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm for efficient and stable training. Experimental evaluations conducted on synthetic data and public instances demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of scheduling performance and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: POPL-VIO: A Novel Pose-Only Measurement Model for Point-Line-Based Visual Inertial Odometry
abstract: The classical filter-based Visual Inertial Odometry (VIO) system, MSCKF, requires triangulation to obtain feature landmarks and constructs measurement equations on the historical co-visible frames. This approach introduces linearization errors from feature landmarks and delayed updates for the current frame state. Building upon the recent pose-only measurement model for point features, we propose a pose-only measurement model for line features and develop a point-line-based VIO system, denoted as POPL-VIO. This system eliminates both point and line feature landmarks in the measurement equations, thereby avoiding linearization errors from feature landmarks and providing immediate updates for the current frame state. Additionally, we propose a unified base-frame selection strategy specifically designed for the pose-only measurement model of both point and line features. Experiments on the EuRoC dataset show that POPL-VIO improves localization accuracy by 32% over MSCKF and outperforms both the point-based system, OpenVINS, and the state-of-the-art point-line-based system, EPLF-VINS.

articleTitle: An Experience Replay Approach Based on SSIM to Solve the Sparse Reward Problem in Pursuit Evasion Game*
abstract: Reward sparsity has always been a challenge in the field of reinforcement learning. Because of the complexity, dynamics, and uncertainty of the state space of the pursuit-evasion game, the problem of reward sparsity faced by agents in the learning process is more prominent. To solve this problem, we proposed an empirical replay method using the structural similarity measure (SSIM). The approach assesses the novelty of the current pursuit-evasion game screen, encouraging the agent to prioritize learning from states that appear less frequently but have greater learning potential. Simulation results illustrate that our approach outperforms both random sampling experience replay and prioritized experience replay methods in terms of training effectiveness and successful pursuit time within the pursuit-evasion game environment.

articleTitle: Minimal Controllability Problem of Structural Networked Systems with MIMO Singular Subnets
abstract: This paper explores the issue of identifying the minimum input matrices needed to guarantee the structural controllability of networked dynamic systems with MIMO singular subsystems, The global graph of the system is decomposed into a network topology graph and a node graph. Regarding the network topology graph, an algorithm is proposed to identify all possible controlled nodes and to further classify the system nodes. Additionally, necessary and sufficient conditions for achieving structurally controllable network topologies that satisfy both input connection and rank conditions are provided. Based on these conditions, we determine the minimum number of controlled subnets and the input configuration subnet set to achieve structural controllability of the network topology. As for the node graph, DM decomposition is employed to derive the minimum non-dedicated input matrix, ensuring the structural R-controllability of singular subnets. Finally, by combining the network topology graph with the node graph, we can determine the minimum input matrix required for achieving global network control.

articleTitle: Spectral Calibration for In-situ Measurement of Glycerol Fermentation Component Concentrations via Infrared Spectroscopy
abstract: For in-situ measurement of important component concentrations during a glycerol fermentation process via the near-infrared spectroscopy (NIR), this paper proposes a semi-supervised spectral calibration model building method based on the goose optimization algorithm (GO) for spectral data analysis to enhance in-situ measurement accuracy. To address the issue of very limited labeled samples as often encountered in practice, a semi-supervised approach based on combining the consistency regularization and pseudo-labelling strategy is presented, along with screening out reliable unlabeled spectra based on a wilcoxon signed-rank test for calibration model building. In addition, a comparative study on measuring the multiple component concentrations during a glycerol fermentation process is conducted in terms of using different modelling methods. Experimental results well demonstrate the measurement accuracy of the proposed spectral calibration method.

articleTitle: The Battery Management System with DNN Deployed in STM32
abstract: Accurate prediction of the state of charge (SOC) is crucial for extending the lifespan of batteries. While traditional ampere-hour integration methods are simple and practical, they suffer from large cumulative errors and are not well-suited for complex application scenarios. This paper presents a smart battery management system based on the STM32F407VET6 microcontroller, which incorporates a deep neural network (DNN) to effectively model the nonlinear relationship between key parameters such as current, voltage, and SOC. The system features autonomous operation without requiring a host computer, enabling precise measurement of remaining battery capacity and real-time data display on an OLED screen. Furthermore, it supports data transmission in industrial environments via an RS485 module using the Modbus RTU protocol, as well as communication through CAN bus and ESP8266-MQTT for IoT applications. Experimental results demonstrate that this system can accurately predict battery SOC while facilitating multiplatform data communication.

articleTitle: Task Planning for Dual-Arm Robot Empowered by Large Language Model
abstract: Autonomous decision-making capabilities are a key indicator of a robot's level of intelligence, requiring it to have scene understanding and reasoning abilities. Leveraging the powerful general intelligence of large language models (LLMs) for robot task planning has become an important approach in recent years. However, current research encounters several issues: (1) The output of LLM exhibits inherent randomness, making it challenging to ensure system stability and safety when directly executing LLM-generated code. (2) Existing frameworks are often designed for single-robot applications, and their direct application to multi-robot scenarios can lead to improper task allocation, task conflicts, and other issues. In this study, we propose DRTP-LLM, a framework that leverages LLM for reasoning and decision-making in dual-arm robotic tasks while ensuring system safety. This framework includes the prompt mechanism, a library of primitives, and the primitive sequence extractor, among other components. We deployed this method on a real dual-arm robot system and validated it in tabletop scenarios, evaluating the results with specific metrics. Compared to directly executing LLM-generated code, our method demonstrates a higher success rate. Additionally, the optimizations for dual-arm robot scenarios lead to more reasonable and efficient task allocations.

articleTitle: Convergence Analysis of Epidemic Models over Contact and Migration Graphs
abstract: In this paper, we study the susceptible-infected-susceptible (SIS) epidemic spreading model under population migration on multilayer networks. Specifically, we consider two-layer contact-migration networks, in which one layer of the multilayer networks describes the contact patterns between different populations and the other one captures the possible migration paths between any two sites. By using Lyapunov methods as well as Markov chain theory, we study convergence properties of the SIS epidemic dynamics on the two-layer contact-migration networks either by establishing the structural conditions under which the multilayer networked system always evolves into the disease-free equilibrium or by deriving the algebraic conditions below which the system converges to the disease-free equilibrium. Finally, two simulation examples are given to verify our theoretical results.

articleTitle: Dynamic Event-Triggered Predictive Control for Consensus of the Multi-Agent Systems with Disturbances
abstract: This paper combines the idea of Dynamic Event-triggered Control(DETC) and Tube-based Model Predictive Control(TMPC) to study the consensus control problem of continuous linear multi-agent systems(MASs). Considering that the system has bounded disturbance, under the DETC, the dual-mode MPC is used. Both the feasibility of DETC-TMPC and the stability of closed-loop system are guaranteed. At the same time, there is a minimum trigger time interval between two consecutive trigger moments, and the Zeno phenomenon is eliminated. Finally, this paper designs an adaptive trigger condition verification method to avoid continuously testing event trigger conditions. The proposed method can further save computing resources and improve system control efficiency.

articleTitle: Robust $H\infty$ Model Reference Tracking Control of Switched Time-Delay Systems with External Disturbances
abstract: This paper investigates robust <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H\infty$</tex> model reference tracking control for switched time-delay systems with external disturbances. To address common uncertainties in parameters, external perturbations, and delay issues in practical engineering, a model reference tracking control framework integrating performance metrics is proposed. This framework enables the closed-loop system to achieve state tracking of a reference model while managing switching control in the presence of delays. First, the average dwell time technique is employed to derive the stability of switched time-delay systems and simplify the design of the controller. Then, by utilizing Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional and robust <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H\infty$</tex> model reference tracking control technique, sufficient conditions are proposed to obtain the gains of the robust tracking feedback controller from solvable inequalities and ensure the global exponential stability of the switched time-delay system under external disturbances and actuator faults. Finally, a numerical simulation demonstrates that the proposed method significantly improves disturbance rejection and tracking accuracy.

articleTitle: SCINet for Mitigating Distributional Bias in Electric Coal Inventory Prediction
abstract: Accurately predicting coal storage in power plants is crucial for optimizing coal storage management and ensuring power supply security. The nonlinearity and non-stationarity of coal storage sequences pose challenges to coal inventory prediction. In response to this issue, Sampling Convolution and Interaction Networks (SCINet) combined with an Attention mechanism was used to extract multi-scale nonlinear temporal features and correlations between variables for prediction. An improved Reversible Instance Normalization (RevIn) was introduced during data preprocessing to help to mitigate the effects of the non-stationarity of the coal storage sequence on the prediction model. Finally, by utilizing the relationship between coal stored, consumed, and incoming, the prediction results were adjusted to yield the coal storage prediction sequence. Experimental results showed an average improvement of 4.98%, 5.56%, and 4.29% in terms of single-day, 7-day, and 10-day coal inventory prediction accuracy, compared to before the improvement.

articleTitle: MC-DQA: An Efficient Database Query Acceleration Architecture Based on FPGA
abstract: The data size and concurrent query probability involved in databases are growing rapidly, which leads to additional SQL query delay overhead, and it is becoming challenging to realize efficient database SQL query through FPGA heterogeneous design. In order to reduce the impact of this bottleneck on database performance, a novel Multi-card Collaborative Database Query Architecture (MC-DQA) based on FPGA is proposed to meet the requirements of high-performance database query processing. Unlike traditional heterogeneous acceleration methods, our architecture adopts a hardware design form of “single database server carrying multiple heterogeneous acceleration cards”. CPU executes MC-DQA scheduling strategy to allocate SQL query tasks to various acceleration cards, the cards and kernels parallel acceleration calculation cooperate, thus reducing the query processing time for high concurrency large-scale data. The MC-DQA we designed can be applied to current mainstream relational database management systems. On KaiwuDB, the SQL query experiment based on TPC-H benchmark and Inspur dataset proved the advantages and feasibility of our design architecture. Compared with the traditional “CPU-FPGA” scheme, MC-DQA can save up to 72.29% of query time overhead.

articleTitle: Research on Risk Accurate Prediction Method of Train Platoon Operation Based on KPCA-EBWO-SVM
abstract: In response to the problems of low utilization of monitoring data for platoon train operation, low accuracy in risk identification and prediction, as well as poor initiative in emergency response, a support vector machine hybrid prediction classification method based on KPCA and EBWO is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the multi-factorial nature of the risk encountered during operation in platoon is analyzed, and system risk levels are defined based on the operational status of platoon. Secondly, the KPCA method is used to perform data dimensionality reduction and feature extraction on operational data, quasi reverse learning and whirlwind foraging strategies are utilized to continuously update SVM model parameters, so as to achieve efficient processing of complex data and accurate prediction and classification of risk types. Finally, based on actual train parameters and simulated operation data, the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving the utilization rate of operation monitoring data, risk identification and prediction classification accuracy is verified. In turn, it provides a guarantee for the intelligent, reliable and safe operation in flexible platoon of rail transit.

articleTitle: A Hierarchical Energy Sharing Strategy for Multi-Communities with Heterogeneous Prosumers
abstract: Inter-community energy sharing is of positive significance in the energy transacion market, which can effectively reduce the cost of purchasing energy from the utility grid and improve the local consumption of renewable energy. In this study, a hierarchical energy sharing framework for multi-communities with heterogeneous prosumers is proposed. Each community consists of different types of prosumers, that is, photovoltaic (PV) prosumers, wind turbine (WT) prosumers and aggregate electric vehicle (EV) prosumers. A hierarchical energy sharing strategy based on Stackelberg game is proposed. In the inner cooperation stage, the total cost minimization model of operator cluster is established. In the outer non-cooperative stage, the Stackelberg game model between each operator and heterogeneous prosumers in each community is established, and the robust optimization method is adopted to solve the time-varying uncertainty problem of renewable energy generations. A hierarchical iterative algorithm is designed to solve the Stackelberg game equilibrium strategy, which maximizes each prosumer's income and minimizes the operators' total cost. The simulation results show that the proposed multi-community hierarchical energy sharing strategy can not only reduce the impact of load fluctuation on the utility grid, but also improve the income of prosumers.

articleTitle: PSNet: Local Context Perception and Global Semantic Information Extraction Based Detector for Power Scenario Defects Detection
abstract: The rapid development of power systems has made inspection tasks increasingly challenging. Effective intelligent detection methods for power system defects can significantly enhance the efficiency of power inspections. The complexity of power scenario images, the diversity of defects, and the low distinction between foreground and background all contribute to the difficulty of power system defect detection. Addressing these issues, this paper analyzes the characteristics of power scenario images collected by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and designs a defect detection network for the power scenario (PSNet). To mitigate the challenge of some objects being small and highly correlated with their surroundings in power scenario images, a Local Context Enhancement Block (LCEB) based on dilated convolutions is proposed. Given the typically complex backgrounds in power scenario images, a Global Weighted Attention Block (GWAB) is designed. Additionally, an Electric Power Scenario Defects Detection Dataset (EPSD) comprising images collected by UAVs is introduced, which contains defect information in various common power scenarios. Our method demonstrates superior performance in power scenario defect detection tasks compared to current advanced detection methods. We also conducted ablation experiments, and the results demonstrate that each proposed module enhances the model's performance. Additionally, experiments on public dataset further demonstrated the generalization performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Joint Prediction Method of Multi-Agent to Reduce Collision Rate
abstract: Predicting future motions of road participants is an important task for driving autonomously. Most existing models excel at predicting the marginal trajectory of a single agent, but predicting joint trajectories for multiple agents that are consistent within a scene remains a challenge. Previous research has often focused on marginal predictions, but the importance of joint predictions has become increasingly apparent. Joint prediction aims to generate trajectories that are consistent across the entire scene. Our research builds upon the SIMPL baseline to explore methods for generating scene-consistent trajectories. We tested our algorithm on the Argoverse 2 dataset, and experimental results demonstrate that our approach can generate scene-consistent trajectories. Compared to the SIMPL baseline, our method significantly reduces the collision rate of joint trajectories within the scene.

articleTitle: Self-Adaptive Dragonfly Optimizer with Random Forest and Kernel Principal Component Analysis for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: Optimization algorithms (OAs) frequently address complex industrial automation and system scheduling design problems. However, when handling high-dimensional complex problems, these algorithms often struggle to explore the entire solution space due to their reliance on extensive computational resources and significant time costs. Additionally, they are prone to becoming trapped in local optima when solving high-dimensional problems. To address these challenges, this work proposes a novel OA named Self-adaptive Dragonfly Optimizer with random Forest and kernel-Principal component analysis (SDOFP). The Self-adaptive Dragonfly Optimizer (SDO) is designed to dynamically adjust parameters for adaptive exploration of the decision space. Kernel-Principal Component Analysis (K-PCA) is a dimensionality reduction method, turning the high-dimensional search space into a lower-dimension one. It can effectively guide the population toward the global optimum. Random Forest (RF) is utilized as a surrogate model to balance training time and prediction accuracy, conserving computational resources and enhancing overall performance. The performance of SDOFP is evaluated by comparing it with several typical peers across eight high-dimensional benchmark functions. Further validation is conducted by applying SDOFP to a real-world flexible job shop scheduling problem, demonstrating its practical applicability.

articleTitle: HiCRISP: An LLM-Based Hierarchical Closed-Loop Robotic Intelligent Self-Correction Planner
abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into robotics has revolutionized human-robot interactions and autonomous task planning. However, these systems are often unable to self-correct during the task execution, which hinders their adaptability in dynamic real-world environments. To address this issue, we present an LLM-based Hierarchical Closed-loop Robotic Intelligent Self-correction Planner (Hi-CRISP), an innovative framework that enables robots to correct errors within individual steps during the task execution. HiCRISP actively monitors and adapts the task execution process, addressing both high-level planning and low-level action errors. Extensive benchmark experiments, encompassing virtual and real-world scenarios, showcase HiCRISP's exceptional performance, positioning it as a promising solution for robotic task planning with LLMs.

articleTitle: A Method for Scattering Removal in Three-Dimensional Fluorescence Spectra Based on Physics-Informed Neural Networks
abstract: Three-dimensional fluorescence spectroscopy offers high-dimensional information and rapid sensitivity, making it advantageous in fields such as environmental monitoring and food testing. However, scattering effects can hinder analysis accuracy, and traditional de-scattering methods often lead to signal loss and distortion. To overcome these issues, a denoising method based on a physics-informed neural network is proposed. This method includes a physical information reconstruction module that generates theoretical values approximating actual scattering values. Integrated into a GAN framework, this module uses physical quantities to guide the generator in producing physically consistent images, thus preserving material integrity after scattering removal. Tests on a self-built dataset show that this method achieves higher physical consistency compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: Thermal Management of Open-Cathode PEMFC Based on NMPC and EKF
abstract: The purpose of this study is to design a thermal management algorithm for open-cathode proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC). A nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) method is proposed for controlling the duty cycles of cooling fans. The electrochemical and thermal models of the open-cathode PEMFC are initially constructed. A further nonlinear control model is then developed based on the simplified fuel cell model. The system state variables are subsequently observed using the extended Kalman filter (EKF) method which are used as state inputs of NMPC. Finally, the fuel cell model, NMPC and EKF are constructed based on SIMULINK, and three simulations are conducted to assess the control effect. These simulations involved tracking constant temperature under constant current, tracking constant temperature under dynamic current, and tracking dynamic temperature under constant current, respectively. The results demonstrated that the control effect is superior to that of the PID algorithm in terms of tracking accuracy, response speed and robustness.

articleTitle: Active Disturbance Rejection Control of Dense Medium Separation Process Based on Improved PI-GPC
abstract: Aiming at the complex field environment of dense medium separation process and the large amount of matrix inversion calculation in the traditional PI-GPC solution process, an adaptive stepped generalized predictive control method with proportional-integral structure (PI-ASGPC-LESO) based on active disturbance rejection strategy is proposed. Considering the large amount of calculation when PI-GPC solves the optimal control rate, an adaptive step factor dependent on the system adjustment error is introduced to constrain the change of the control amount, which reduces the amount of calculation in the solution process. In view of the complex on-site environment of dense medium separation and the large interference in the system, LESO is added to the loop to suppress external disturbances and compensate the unmodeled error of the system. In order to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, a comparative experiment with traditional PI-GPC and PI-GPC-LESO was designed with the dense medium separation system of a coal preparation plant as the control object. The experimental results show that the proposed method effectively improves the dynamic performance of the system, with shorter adjustment time, smaller overshoot, and stronger anti-interference ability.

articleTitle: A Case Study of Liquid Cooling Modeling and Privacy Preserving LQR Design for Safe Management of Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: As a key component of electric vehicles, the life and safety of lithium-ion batteries are particularly important. How to prevent the thermal runaway of batteries and adjust batteries temperature reasonably are crucial to the daily use of batteries. This paper aims to design a fast and safe liquid cooling control system for lithium-ion batteries. Firstly, a linear electrothermal model is constructed to predict the thermal dynamics of batteries during operation. In order to simplify the calculation of model simulation tools, a resistance-capacitance heat transfer model was established to evaluate the thermal transference changes of batteries. Then, COMSOL multi-physical field simulation was used to simulate the actual heat transfer process of lithium-ion batteries and obtain the correlation coefficient of the thermal production model. The approximate discretization method is used to construct the lithium-ion batteries discretization mathematical model, and the steady state control quantity is obtained by linear quadratic regulator. At the same time, in order to prevent the system from being attacked by the network during operation, the control methods are encrypted. Finally, the simulation results show that the privacy preserving LQR model can ensure that the batteries temperature converges to the predetermined temperature faster and more smoothly in a short time.

articleTitle: Optimal Reconstruction of Active Distribution Network with Current Margin
abstract: In the process of distribution network reconstruction, the problem of nonlinear optimization is formed by connecting distributed power supply and dispatching controllable components. Using mathematical optimization method, the output state of switch and control unit is considered comprehensively to optimize the current margin and reduce the network loss. The node voltage constraint is effectively relaxed by large M constraint, and the initial model is transformed by Ll-box and second-order cone relaxation techniques, and a mixed integer programming model based on Ll-box is constructed. Yalmip toolkit is used for modeling, and Cplex algorithm package is called for efficient solution. The example shows that the method is reasonable and effective, which can not only reduce network loss and improve node voltage effectively, but also leave more safety margin for the system. It helps to improve the operation efficiency and reliability of the distribution network.

articleTitle: A Generalized Design for Database Heterogeneous Query Acceleration Based on FPGA
abstract: In recent years, the development of information technology has increased the performance demand of database. Improving the query efficiency of relational databases through FPGA heterogeneous design is becoming increasingly popular and has become an important direction for researchers in related fields to explore. This work deeply analyzes the principles and key steps of heterogeneous acceleration design for relational databases, and explores the compatibility and efficiency issues of existing FPGA heterogeneous query schemes in executing query applications. A generalized database heterogeneous query acceleration architecture based on FPGA is designed, and the database query operation mechanism of this architecture is introduced in detail. In order to further improve the efficiency of heterogeneous data query processing, we design a set of query acceleration kernel based on FPGA according to the practical application of database, which covers the common SQL query functions of relational database including sort, aggregation and join. In addition, the kernels involved in this work support variable width data queries, and multiple kernels adopt a pipeline design with high parallelism. The SQL query experiment on KaiwuDB platform, an open-source database, proves that the FPGA based heterogeneous database query acceleration architecture proposed in this work reduces the overall time overhead by up to 96.21 % compared to traditional software SQL query schemes.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Enhanced Dynamic Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithm for Cooperative Shovel Scheduling in Open-Pit Mining
abstract: Aiming at the ore blending problem in the open-pit mining scenario, the optimization objective is to minimize the grade variance of the sliding window of the ore flow, and a cooperative shovel scheduling model for real-time ore blending is established. A reinforcement learning-enhanced dynamic multi- objective evolutionary algorithm is proposed, where a Q-learning operator selection mechanism is introduced to reuse the information from the previous environment for tracking the optimal solution in the dynamic environment. Experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively control the grade fluctuation of the ore flow and dynamically respond to external events, and can find a better solution in real time compared with the traditional operator selection algorithm.

articleTitle: Grasp Trajectory Planning for Vehicle-Mounted Robotic Arm based on Improved DDPG Algorithm
abstract: In response to the problems of slow convergence and poor control effect when the traditional Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm is used to train the vehicle-mounted robotic arm, an improved DDPG algorithm is proposed in this paper. According to the control characteristics of the vehicle-mounted robotic arm, the state space, action space, and reward and punishment function are designed. Then the operation area is partitioned, and the baseline pose of each area is taught. A guidance function is designed and introduced to guide the algorithm training with the baseline pose to accelerate the algorithm's convergence. Finally, the traditional reward and punishment function is improved according to the guidance training characteristics. The simulation experiments show that the improved DDPG algorithm has significantly improved the convergence efficiency, planning success rate, and control efficiency compared with the traditional DDPG algorithm, especially since the planning success rate can reach about 93.8%.

articleTitle: Overlapping Region Estimation-Based Point Cloud Registration
abstract: Extracting overlapping regions is crucial for point cloud registration. Recently, coarse-to-fine approaches have gained popularity. These methods rely on highly accurate superpoint correspondences, which are then propagated to denser points. However, these correspondences inevitably introduce non-overlapping region superpoints, leading to a decrease in superpoint matching accuracy. To tackle this challenge, we introduce the Overlapping Region Estimation-Based (ORE-Based) Point Cloud Registration method, a novel approach designed to enhance matching accuracy by reducing the influence of non-overlapping points. Our method utilizes a learning model to predict whether each superpoint is situated within overlapping regions. By excluding superpoints outside these regions during correspondence extraction, we achieve improved matching accuracy. This approach ensures high registration precision regardless of the overlap ratio between the point clouds being registered. By specifically targeting overlapping regions, our method significantly enhances the robustness and reliability of point cloud registration across diverse scenarios. Although simple, our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on the challenging ModelLoNet benchmark, reducing Relative Rotation Error by 12.87 % and Relative Translation Error by 14.47 % under conditions of larger initial rotation error.

articleTitle: IROS: A Hard Real-time Intelligent Robot Operating System
abstract: This paper gives an overview of an intelligent robot operating system: IROS. Taking the open-source robot operating system (ROS) as a reference, the existing characteristics of the system and some difficulties in practical applications are summarized, and a complete IROS is redeveloped based on the problems encountered and the needs of users. Two versions of IROS have been publicly released: IROS V1 and IROS V2. And now, we are working on developing an upgraded version of IROS V3.x. IROS has excellent performance in real-time, stability, security, and other aspects. IROS particularly has hard real-time performance, which is a powerful improvement compared to ROS performance. This paper introduces the architecture, core functions, performance testing, and application scenarios of IROS. In addition, we also explain several core technologies in IROS, compare some technical indicators with ROS, and discuss future work.

articleTitle: Safety Equipment Wearing Detection Based on YOLO-MT in Coal Yards
abstract: Coal workers wear safety gear at the coal yard can greatly improve the personal safety of coal miners. But workers have weak safety awareness, often forget to wear safety equipment. To ensure production safety, a coal yard workers' safety equipment wearing detection problem is considered in this paper, and an improved YOLO-MT detection model was presented to address the issue of low detection accuracy of existing object detection algorithms in coal yard environment. Firstly, a neck network structure of YOLOv8 was strengthened by texture information to help the model better absorb texture information and enhance its positioning capabilities. Then, a macro residual backbone is created as the detection algorithm's backbone network to enhance the network's detection performance. Thirdly, the WMPDIoU loss function was created to enhance the network's regression efficiency and detection accuracy by integrating the benefits of the MPDIoU and WIoU loss functions. According to experimental data, the YOLO-MT algorithm improves mAP@0.5 by 2.5% when compared to the baseline model, and it can achieve an FPS of 203.2, which is sufficient for real-time detection.

articleTitle: Method of Parallel Robot Arm Positioning Based on Visual Guidance
abstract: Traditional manually taught robotic arms lack a certain level of adaptability in control and are unable to autonomously adjust when random situations occur, resulting in poor production line flexibility. To address this issue, a parallel robotic arm grasping control method based on YOLO vision is proposed. A hardware system consisting of parallel robotic arms, industrial cameras, Ubuntu servers, etc., is constructed, and each working module is encapsulated into independent ROS2 communication nodes. After training the model of the target object, pixel coordinates of the target object are converted into world coordinates of the robotic arm through data processing and message communication between nodes. Motion trajectories are generated based on the relationship between target points and placement point coordinates, and real-time inverse kinematics calculations of the robotic arm are performed to determine the angles of each motor at corresponding moments, thereby driving the robotic arm to perform grasping operations. The performance of the robotic arm control method is improved in terms of target detection accuracy and real-time performance. Experimental results indicate that the robotic arm grasping control method based on YOLO vision achieves high recognition accuracy for detecting targets, high efficiency in node-based development, strong portability, and has certain application value.

articleTitle: Multi-Behavior Euler Transformer for Click-Through Rate Prediction
abstract: Click-Through Rate (CTR) prediction is crucial for recommender systems, including e-commerce platforms. It estimates the likelihood of users clicking on recommended items, enabling more accurate and effective recommendations. Modeling user interests through behavior sequences has become the mainstream of CTR prediction task. In order to capture user interest preferences, models of the Transformer architecture have been widely used to model behavior data, and previous work has modeled semantic and positional differences in behavior data in different ways, inhibiting the expressive power of sequence modeling. User behaviors often show diversity, making it necessary to fuse multiple user behavioral data to provide more accurate recommendations. To address this challenge, we propose the Multi-Behavior Euler Transformer-based CTR prediction model (MBET). This model enhances multi-behavior interest modeling and adaptive fusion for better recommendation. Specifically: we introduce multi-behavior sequence data, enhance the representation of long-tailed distributed items using a contrast learning task. Utilize the Euler Transformer to transform representations into a complex vector space, unifying semantic and positional differences, and finally, design a multi-behavior adaptive fusion mechanism to dynamically adjust behavior weights based on different needs. Extensive experiments verify that MBET achieves the best performance on two real-world datasets.

articleTitle: Exchange Rate Forecasting with Fused Financial Exogenous Variables by CAE-SCINet
abstract: Exchange rate forecasting is essential to decision- making and optimization in various aspects, including international trade, investment decisions, and risk management within the financial domain. The most of existing methods focus on using historical data to predict future exchange rate, that is just using the temporal relation of time series without considering other exogenous variables such as some market sentiment and economic indicator. Recently, some researchers begin to introduce exogenous variables to exchange rate forecasting, while they neglect extracting the spatial relationships of them, resulting in suboptimal forecasting accuracy. This paper proposes an exchange rate forecasting model CAE-SCINet to capture the spatial nonlinear characteristics of multifaceted financial factors, and predict exchange rate by the captured features. Firstly, the spatial characteristics of multifaceted financial factors are extracted by convolutional autoencoder (CAE), and concatenated with exchange rate data. Then, the dynamic features of the joint time series are captured by sample convolution and interaction network (SCINet) at multiple temporal scales. Finally, the multi-resolution dynamic time features are sequenced, added to the original time series by residual connections, decoded by a fully connected network and utilized for predictions. We collected the daily exchange rate data of RMB against USD and related financial factors from August 11, 2015 to September 26, 2023 as the experimental data. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model by fusing multifaceted financial factors is effective for the exchange rate forecasting.

articleTitle: Multi-Dimensional Conflict Graph-Based Scheduling for Varied Deadline Requirements in IWSNs
abstract: Satisfying the end-to-end delay requirements of various real-time data flows is a critical challenge in industrial wireless sensor networks (IWSNs). Since each data flow has different deadline constraints, effectively utilizing network resources while ensuring that data flows meet their deadlines becomes an important problem to be addressed. This paper proposes a joint time slot and channel allocation algorithm based on a multi-dimensional conflict graph, aiming to minimize the total end-to-end delay of multiple data flows with different deadline constraints. First, the concept of a minimum integer scheduling unit (MISU) is introduced to represent the minimum transmission period based on the deadlines, allowing for a unified scheduling structure. Next, a flow-link-slot-channel tuple is proposed to describe potential scheduling schemes, and a multi-dimensional conflict graph (MDCG) is constructed based on the conflicts among tuples. The joint scheduling problem is then transformed into finding the optimal maximum independent set (MIS) in the MDCG. To reduce computational complexity, the original problem is decomposed into a series of maximum weight independent set (MWIS) subproblems using a greedy-based hop-wise scheduling algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in minimizing end-to-end delay compared to existing algorithms.

articleTitle: Prescribed-Time Adaptive Neural Tracking Control of Full-State Constrained Nonlinear Systems
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to propose a novel design algorithm based symmetric barrier Lyapunov function (BLF) and radial basis neural networks (RBF NNs) for nonlinear systems with full-state time-varying asymmetric constraints. First, we construct a new form of barrier Lyapunov function (BLF) such that the tracking error tends to a sufficiently small neighborhood of the origin with prescribed finite time and pre-given accuracy. Second, we propose a saturated filter to make virtual controllers naturally meet “feasibility conditions”. In addition, our approach can loosen the limitation of existing constraint boundaries, dealing with more general cases of time-varying state constraint. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed approach is further confirmed by simulation verification.

articleTitle: Practical Predefined-Time Consensus Control for High-Order Multiagent Systems via Output Feedback
abstract: This paper considers the problem of practical predefined-time (PPT) consensus control for a class of high-order nonlinear multiagent systems. With the help of the smooth time-varying function-based technique, the leader's state and the follower's unmeasurable states are estimated by introducing PPT observers. Then, a PPT output feedback consensus control algorithm with no singularity and discontinuity is proposed based on the observers. Finally, the effectiveness of the designed output feedback PPT consensus control scheme is validated by virtue of an illustrative numerical example.

articleTitle: Design and Control of a Novel 5-DoF Tilt-Rotor Quadcopter
abstract: This paper presents a novel 5-DoF (degrees of freedom) tilt-rotor quadcopter. Compared to traditional quadcopters, the vehicle offers more DoF by adding two servo-driven mechanisms. The extra DoF allow it to move at a constant pitch angle, thus adapting it to more scenarios, such as slope landings. In addition, the proposed tilt-rotor quadcopter can generate greater torque around the z-axis of the body coordinate system. This gives it an advantage in some scenarios, such as carrying a manipulator to turn valves in the air. In this paper, we first design and model the proposed tilt-rotor quadcopter. Then, we design the controller and control allocation algorithm for the proposed tilt-rotor quadcopter. The control allocation algorithm has clear analytical solutions, which benefits its implementation and deployment. Finally, the structure and control strategy of the tilt-rotor quadcopter are validated by an experiment.

articleTitle: Tenacity Prediction of Polyester Materials Based on an Ensemble Soft Measurement Model
abstract: In the development process of polyester powder coating materials, it has great guiding significance for the development of new materials as the polyester material properties can be predicted through the given monomer structure and formula. In order to meet the requirements of rapid development of polyester materials, this paper establishes a prediction method based on an ensemble soft measurement model (ESM) for one key property--tenacity in prompting the acceleration of development cycle of polyester products. The processed data employed to train and test the model were collected from a local material company, and it covers over 100 kinds of polymerized resins. Firstly, the molecular expressions of monomers are converted to SMILES codes and further translated to ECFP fingerprints. Then, the principal component analysis (PCA) method is adopted to extract the elements with higher importance in each fingerprint. Finally, the ensemble model that consists of 4 machine learning models was established to make the multiclassification decision in tenacity prediction. The effectiveness of the prediction model is evaluated by comparing the predicted and the practical tensile test results. The results demonstrate that this approach achieves better performance in the material property prediction as well as generalization capability.

articleTitle: Adaptive Cooperative Path Following Control for Autonomous Surface Vehicles via Path-Dependent Constraints
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive path-following co-operative control method for multiple underactuated autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs). To satisfy the feasible region constructed by the environment boundaries, the path-dependent constraints based on path parameters are designed, rather than depending on the time variable directly. The universal barrier function is incorporated with the control design to handle the prescribed performance requirements, which further ensures the satisfaction of position and heading angle constraints. The transversal function is employed to address the underactuation issue such that ASVs can follow the desired path while maintaining a predefined formation. With the use of radial basis function (RBF) neural network and adaptive control technology, the position and heading angle errors converge to the equilibrium point in the presence of internal uncertain dynamics and external time-varying disturbances. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Algorithm for Local Extrema Seeking of Black-Box Functions Based on Information Landscape Measure
abstract: This paper provides an introduction to the concepts of fitness landscapes and information landscapes(IL), and proposes an improvement to the IL measure, transforming it into an indicator for evaluating the ruggedness of landscapes. A novel extremum-solving algorithm based on the IL measure is introduced for the extremum seeking of high-dimensional functions. The algorithm incorporates Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) from spatial filling designs to sample high-dimensional spaces, thereby obtaining regional sample points in high-dimensional spaces. It then applies the IL measure to calculate intervals, facilitating the extremum solving process of the algorithm. Finally, by comparing this algorithm with other methods, it is demonstrated that the algorithm can find all solutions with fewer initial points, outperforming traditional methods in both speed and solution quality, thus providing a theoretical foundation for subsequent engineering applications.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization Method of Injection Molding Machine Temperature Control System Based on IK-SS
abstract: Injection molding, as a plastic processing technology, is widely used in the mass production of plastic products with high precision and automation. However, the performance optimization process of this system currently faces some prominent issues, such as time consumption, reliance on experience, and difficulty in achieving optimality. Traditional optimization methods typically rely on manual experience and rules, which are inefficient and time-consuming. To enhance the performance of the control system, this paper focuses on utilizing an improved simplex search method based on the data-driven optimization concept to optimize the parameters of the temperature control system of the injection molding machine. The method introduced in this paper is termed the Knowledge-Informed Simplex Search Method Based on Adjacent Historical Centroid Points Information (IK-SS). The IK-SS algorithm is a variant of the simplex search method that utilizes information from the centroids of neighboring simplices to evaluate the current state of the optimization process and dynamically adjust the iteration step size. This approach aims to improve optimization efficiency while reducing computational complexity and time costs. Simulation and experimental validation demonstrate that the IK-SS algorithm significantly enhances the temperature control performance of the injection molding machine (IMM). This demonstrates the potential of the IK-SS algorithm as a tool for optimizing the temperature control system of injection molding machines.

articleTitle: Optimization of Tiered Pricing Strategy for Smart Grid Considering Clean Energy
abstract: With the rapid development of new energy technology, it has become a trend to combine wind and solar power generation into the smart grid. In this paper, wind power generation and photovoltaic power generation are introduced into the smart grid, and taking into account the consumption capacity of consumers at different levels, a tiered pricing scheme considering the uncertainty of wind and solar energy is proposed. Firstly, we establish probability density functions of power generation for wind power generation and photovoltaic power generation respectively to express the uncertainty of wind energy and solar energy. To meet the energy demand of consumers at all levels, we present the energy demand model of consumers after considering their electricity demand and temperature influence. Then, we formulate the optimal pricing problem for the electricity market under the framework of tiered pricing, so as to make the energy market get satisfactory income while meeting the energy demand of consumers. Finally, we use the particle swarm optimization algorithm to determine the optimal pricing strategy of the energy market. The simulation results show that when meeting the energy demand of consumers in different temperature conditions, the optimal pricing can be found that meets the satisfactory income of the energy market.

articleTitle: Multi-UAV Cooperative Formation Control Considering Finite Time and Collision Avoidance
abstract: In this paper, the formation control problem for UAVs subject to model uncertainty and external disturbance is studied. To realize the control goals, the formation control problem of UAVs is decomposed into position consensus control and attitude consensus control. Firstly, a finite-time position consensus controller is developed for UAVs such that the desired formation can be formed in a finite time. In the position controller, a collision avoidance mechanism is designed on the basis of a novel artificial potential field function. Secondly, to handle dynamic model uncertainties and realize attitude tracking control, a robust filter based finite-time attitude tracking controller is developed. Finally, stability of the position control subsystem and the attitude control subsystem is analyzed using Lyapunov method. And simulation results on MATLAB and RflySim show that the proposed algorithm enables UAVs to form stable formation while avoiding collisions within a finite time.

articleTitle: Observer-Based Event-Triggered Formation Control of Multi-Agent Systems with External Disturbances Under Switching Topologies
abstract: The paper examines the time-varying formation control problem of multi-agent systems subject to external disturbances under switching topologies. The topologies considered are directed, and it is not required for each topology to have a globally reachable leader. Considering the unmeasurable states of agents, the present paper proposes formation control protocol that employ an observer and an event-triggered communication mechanism, along with sufficient conditions to guarantee the desired formation of the multi-agent systems. The introduced control protocol removes the requirement for agents to communicate continuously. Finally, a simulation example is furnished to substantiate the efficacy of the results.

articleTitle: Construction Method of a Virtual Debugging System for Equipment Based on Digital Twin
abstract: With the development of artificial intelligence, digital twins have further enhanced the level of industrial intelligence and informationization. However, achieving real-time interaction between virtual device information and physical device information, as well as managing the entire lifecycle of devices, are major issues in the application of digital twins. This paper introduces a construction method for a device virtual debugging system based on digital twins. The virtual debugging system is constructed using digital twin models, and by simulating the device operation process and comparing it with actual data, the efficiency and quality of device debugging are improved. Virtual debugging and verification are achieved through the combination of S7-PLCSIM Advanced, TIA Portal (TIA), and virtual simulation (PDPS). The effectiveness and practicality of virtual debugging based on this digital twin model are validated through the example of a dispensing system for a dispensing machine. Additionally, by designing a human-machine operation system, the actual debugging time and costs are significantly reduced, enhancing the performance and efficiency of the device.

articleTitle: Adaptive Utility Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning for Optimizing Batch-Fed Fermentation Processes
abstract: In industrial applications, many scenarios involve multiple conflicting objectives, such as yield, raw material consumption, and environmental protection in chemical production. To address this challenge, Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning (MORL) provides an effective solution by learning Pareto-optimal policies through multi-objective vector rewards. Despite these advances, a gap remains in accurately capturing and incorporating user preferences into the MORL framework. In response to this, a novel Adaptive Utility MORL algorithm (AU-MORL) is proposed to improve policy optimization in continuous fed-batch fermentation processes. This algorithm adaptively adjusts the utility between multiple objectives and uses reinforcement learning to generate policies aligned with user preferences. Extensive validation in the fermentation simulation environment demonstrates that the algorithm achieves a denser pareto front that more closely approximates the true front, while the resulting policies effectively align with user preferences.

articleTitle: Fourier-Based Formation Control of Multiple Unmanned Surface Vessels Using a State Error Port Control Hamiltonian Framework
abstract: Formation control of multiple unmanned surface vessels faces complex and changing environments and mission requirements, and the realization of efficient and complex formation control and the reduction of energy consumption have become key issues that need to be urgently addressed. In order to enhance system optimization, a state error port control Hamiltonian approach is employed to develop a Fourier-based controller for multiple unmanned surface vessels. It uses truncated Fourier series approximation curves and their finite coefficients to describe the shape of the curves in a state-error-port Hamiltonian framework. It automatically assigns multiple unmanned surface vessels to each of the formation control systems. The numerical and experimental results indicate that this approach not only simplifies the formation control process but also significantly reduces energy consumption. The algorithm has good tracking performance for closed boundaries of complex shapes, providing a novel and effective solution for complex formation tasks.

articleTitle: A Novel YOLOv5s-Based Tiny Object Detection Model for UAV
abstract: The diversity of target scales and the complex background interference present in UAV imagery pose significant challenges for UAV target detection. In response, this paper proposes a novel small object detection model built upon the YOLOv5s.
