We introduce a new layer, Head-P2, dedicated to detecting small targets within the YOLOv5s framework to enhance precision. Additionally, we incorporate a decoupled detection head to refine the model's target positioning capability. Further augmenting the model's capabilities, the SimAM attention mechanism is integrated into YOLOv5s' feature extraction and fusion network, amplifying feature attention on targets and improving overall feature extraction performance. To address the limitations of the CIOU loss function, particularly its inability to adapt to varying detection targets and challenges with learning difficult samples, we adopt the inner-CIOU loss function. This adaptation enhances both precision and training convergence speed of the YOLOv5s. The modified model is rigorously evaluated on the VisDrone2019 dataset, with ablation experiments confirming its efficacy. In comparative experiments, our enhanced model exhibits notable improvements over YOLOv5s, with a 6.7% increase in mAP@.5 and a 3.8% increase in mAP@.5:.95 values. Moreover, it outperforms YOLOv8s and other models, demonstrating its robustness in small target detection tasks.

articleTitle: Spatial-Temporal Graph-Based Distributed Optical Fiber Sensing Method for External Breakage Event Recognition
abstract: Improper construction poses a serious threat to the safety of communications cables. Therefore, continuous monitoring along the communication cable is essential to ensure the timely detection of any incidents that may compromise its security. Phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Phi$</tex>-OTDR) has been widely researched in the field of perimeter security due to its high sensitivity, fast response time and multi-point monitoring. However, the environment along communication cables is complex and variable, and long-distance detection often results in time-consuming recognition of external breakage signals and increased susceptibility to misjudgment. To address these issues, we developed a long-distance distributed fiber optic sensing external breakage recognition method based on Spatial-temporal graph. We propose a lightweight RT-DETR model, EFS-DETR, for efficient external breakage detection. The algorithm employs EfficientViT to reconstruct the feature extraction network of RT-DETR, enabling the extraction of deeper semantic features while reducing computational load and model complexity. Secondly, we introduce Fine-Grained Path Augmentation (FGPA) to address the issue of detail feature information loss in multi-level transmission of external breakage signals. Finally, the Shape-IoU loss function is introduced to make the bounding box regression more accurate by focusing on the shape and scale of the bounding box itself to calculate the loss. Additionally, this paper employs a combined threshold iteration and contrast enhancement denoising algorithm for data preprocessing, aiming to reduce various noise interferences while enhancing the external breakage signals of interest. We curated a real-world dataset of external breakage using a 40 km communication fiber optic cable from Guangzhou, China, to validate the efficacy of our proposed method. Multiple sets of experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses other vibration recognition techniques in fiber optic sensing.

articleTitle: Local Identification of Hammerstein Parameter Varying Systems with Asymmetric Noise Characteristics
abstract: The paper studies the multi-model structure parameter identification of the Hammerstein parameter varying system with asymmetric noise characteristics. And the multimodel structure is composed of weighted combinations of several local models, with the local model being the Hammerstein output-error model. We propose a variational Bayes robust identification algorithm based on a shifted asymmetric Laplace distribution (VBRIA_SAL). Firstly, the SAL distribution is used to describe the asymmetric noise. Then in variational Bayes (VB) framework, all unknown variables are seen as hidden variables and their prior information is introduced to iteratively update the estimates. In addition, to overcome the difficulty of directly obtaining the intermediate unmeasurable output, an auxiliary model is established using the measurement information of the system, including the calculated information. Its output replaces the intermediate output, enabling the algorithm procedure to execute smoothly. A numerical simulation has verified that the proposed algorithm is robust to the asymmetric noise compared to studies based on symmetric distributions.

articleTitle: Modelling of Forecasting Kiln Tail Temperature in Lime Calcination Process using Modified Physics-Informed Networks
abstract: In this work, we proposed a modified physics-informed long-short-term memory (LSTM) network for modelling the lime rotary kiln dynamics, which can maintain the physical information about certain inputs and outputs by inte-grating the mechanism during the learning process of neural networks to achieve reasonable control-oriented prediction. In the proposed method, a one-dimensional mechanism is firstly constructed based on the direction of the rotary kiln roll axis, which includes thermal exchange, lime generation, and combustion models. Utilizing these mechanism models, the constraints of certain physical inputs-output relationships are imposed on corresponding paths of the network during the LSTM learning process, while additional data is produced and employed for extending the generalization of the learned LSTM. Both the mechanism model and LSTM are updated synchronously and respectively. Finally, the experimental data demonstrates the effectiveness of the mechanistic model and the accuracy of the modified physics-informed LSTM model.

articleTitle: Topological-Semantic Structure and Attribute Representations Decoupling Learning for Improved Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have demonstrated strong embedding representation learning capabilities on graph with complex structure and have achieved significant success in many applications. The GNNs with explicit graph convolution usually learn a unified representation encoding both attribute feature and graph structure. However, attribute and graph structure are different characteristics of nodes. The unified representation is a compromised representation, which only contains partial information shared by attribute and graph. In addition, most current GNNs also suffer from the problem of ignoring semantic topology. In this paper, to alleviate the interference and redundancy of representation learning, as well as the problem of insufficient structural information, we propose a new Representation Decoupling Learning for Improved Graph Neural Networks (IGNN-RDL) with optimization framework, which learns various representations for attribute and topological-semantic graphs. Further, a diversity constraint is introduced to enhance the complementarity of various representations, resulting in a comprehensive embedding representation by concatenating them. IGNN-RDL iteratively updates attribute representation and graph embedding representation, which can avoid multilayer stacking of graph convolution and alleviate over-smoothing issue. Experimental results on multiple graph benchmark datasets validate the superiority of the proposed IGNN-RDL in node classification tasks.

articleTitle: Deployment of Dynamic Defense Strategies for Multiple Devices in the Industrial Internet Based on Zero Trust
abstract: This paper proposes an algorithm for deploying dynamic defense strategies on multiple devices in the industrial Internet based on zero trust, aiming at coping with complex and ever-changing security challenges. Malicious devices are identified through a submodular optimization algorithm, and defense strategies are dynamically allocated using mixed integer programming to ensure efficient protection of the system. This paper describes in detail the malicious devices feature analysis, the reverse strategy deviation algorithm, and the defense strategy allocation model, and verifies the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm through simulation experiments. The results show that the algorithm can maximize the security of the system under limited resources, respond to changes in device priorities and task requirements in real-time, and provide a new solution for security protection in the industrial Internet environment.

articleTitle: A Study on ECG Electrocardiogram Signal Classification Based on Improved CNN-LSTM
abstract: According to big data, about 17 million people develop arrhythmias every year, and timely diagnosis can effectively reduce the risk of disease. In this paper, we propose an automatic ECG signal detection algorithm based on a mixture of improved convolutional neural network (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) network, which can classify six different arrhythmic diseases. The ECA attention mechanism is introduced into the CNN-LSTM network, which avoids the dimensionality reduction of the module and improves the ability of the model to capture cross-channel interactive information. At the same time, the Hard Swish function was selected as the activation function of the model in the CNN network, which improved the accuracy of the model, and the experimental results showed that the accuracy of the improved model in the ECG signal classification task was 99.31%, F1 was 98.52%, and the recall rate was 99.01%. The method proposed in this study can efficiently and accurately identify different arrhythmic diseases.

articleTitle: Effective Scheduling for Distributed Flexible Job Shop with Heterogeneous Production Lines
abstract: With the development of modern manufacturing and a rising inclination towards multiregional collaboration, distributed flexible job shop problem (DFJSP) is becoming an emerging topic in the domain of production optimization. In this study, a brand-new model of DFJSP with heterogeneous production lines (DFJSP-HPL) is formulated. Driven by small-to medium-size production runs in modern manufacturing, heterogeneous production lines (HPL) comprised of Bernoulli machines and finite buffers operate mainly under transients. Therefore, transient behaviors of heterogeneous production lines are investigated using Markov chain. An improved genetic algorithm (IGA) is adopted to address scheduling problem of DFJSP-HPL for minimizing makespan. Methods of encoding, decoding and genetic operators are designed to ensure that individuals consistently correspond to feasible scheduling throughout the iteration. The effectiveness of adopted IGA is demonstrated through computational experiments.

articleTitle: Real-Time Scheduling for Multi-Cluster Tools with Residency Constraints by Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Multi-cluster tools are extensively utilized in semiconductor manufacturing. As these tools integrate more functionalities and handle increasingly complex processing recipes under numerous constraints, cyclic scheduling strategies become impractical. This poses challenges for non-cyclic scheduling approaches as well. This paper focuses on the non-cyclic scheduling problem of multi-cluster tools with residency time constraints. A generic model is developed to describe dual-armed multi-cluster tools and propose an optimization scheduling algorithm based on Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). This algorithm is designed to learn effective scheduling policies in environments with small batches of wafers and can scale to handle large batches. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm enables rapid scheduling, achieving scheduling performance close to optimal and minimizing residency time. Furthermore, comparisons with cyclic scheduling based on implicit enumeration methods show that our approach achieves shorter makespan.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Crop Planning Model with Interactive Multi-Stakeholder*
abstract: Current crop planning models aim to optimize planting schemes for farmers to maximize their social and ecological benefits within specified constraints, or to optimize planting structure schemes for related departments. However, farmers' planting strategy is closely tied to national planting subsidy policies, and governmental optimization and adjustment of planting structures require farmers' compliance. Focusing solely on the planting plans of either farmers or relative departments may not effectively address real-world scenarios. We propose an Interactive Multi-Stakeholder Crop Planning Model (IMSCPM) based on multi-agent reinforcement learning approaches. This model aims to provide specialized crop planning recommendations to individual farmers while simultaneously offering guiding policy suggestions to relevant regional departments. Stakeholders involved in the crop planning process are represented as multiple intelligent agents with specific objectives, allowing them to interact with each other. To address challenges posed by the proliferation of network input dimensions, the problem of strategy pursuit between two types of agents and the instability of the multi-agent environment caused by the excessive number of agents in the Regional-Farmer planting planning model, we introduce the methods of “Integrated observation”, “Asynchronous training” and “Planting consultant”. We constructed a multi-stakeholder interactive crop planning environment, and obtained strategies that are stable and consistent with the values pursued by each agent. The results demonstrate that our crop planning model based on this novel framework is effective for agricultural system with multi-stakeholders.

articleTitle: Merging on a Parallel-Type Entrance Ramp Using Hybrid-Action Reinforcement Learning
abstract: As the intelligent transportation system continues to evolve, the application of autonomous driving technology in the scenario of merging at parallel on-ramp entrances has become a research hotspot. However, current reinforcement learning-based merging methods only achieve merging with a fixed point at parallel on-ramp entrances and have not yet realized merging on the accelerating lane with undefined merging points, which is difficult to cope with in complex and variable real traffic environments. These traditional methods often use fixed control rules or a single action space (continuous or discrete), showing certain limitations when dealing with diverse road conditions and dynamic traffic flows. In response to the above issues, this study proposes a reinforcement learning strategy for automatic merging at parallel on-ramp entrances based on a hybrid action space. This method combines continuous and discrete action spaces, learning the optimal merging strategy autonomously through reinforcement learning algorithms, with outputs that include lane-changing decisions and longitudinal acceleration, to improve the system's flexibility and adaptability. The experimental results show that, compared with traditional fixed merging point meth-ods, the proposed method has significantly improved in terms of merging success rate, vehicle traffic efficiency, and comfort.

articleTitle: Visual Axis Control of Seeker Stabilization Platform Based on Super-Twisting Algorithm
abstract: The stabilization platform of the seeker is a key component of precision-guided weapons. Factors such as vibration shocks and enemy interference can severely impact the identification and tracking accuracy of the platform”s visual axis. The seeker”s stabilization platform is also a nonlinear system, making traditional PID control methods inadequate to meet performance requirements. Therefore, this paper proposes a terminal sliding mode-based super-twisting servo control method, with stability proven using Lyapunov functions. Additionally, to further enhance the seeker”s anti-interference capability, an extended state observer is incorporated into the visual axis angular velocity control loop to compensate for disturbances, allowing the seeker to maintain high-performance operation even under various interferences. Finally, simulations comparing a PID controller, a PID controller with an observer, a standalone super-twisting controller, and a super-twisting controller with an observer are conducted in MATLAB/Simulink. The results from dynamic tracking and disturbance experiments indicate that the combination of the super-twisting algorithm and the extended state observer significantly improves the dynamic tracking performance and anti-interference capability of the seeker.

articleTitle: Tightly-Coupled SLAM Algorithm Based on LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Fusion
abstract: This paper proposes a tightly-coupled SLAM algorithm based on LiDAR-inertial-visual fusion for the problem of reduced localization accuracy or even failure of single-sensor SLAM algorithms in complex environments. The algorithm splits the processing unit based on the point cloud, and performs state prediction and motion compensation through IMU integration. The image photometric error and the LiDAR point-to-surfel distance residual are fused to update the state, and the map is constructed using both dense point cloud and octree. Experiments on the public NTU dataset and self-built simulation environment show that our proposed algorithm outperforms other similar algorithms with improved localization accuracy and well map building capability.

articleTitle: DRE-xLSTM: Distributed Reversible Embedding Extended Long Short-Term Memory (xLSTM) for Complex Industrial Data Imputation
abstract: The large amount of sensor data poses a challenge for imputation in complex industrial processes. The prominent method of xLSTM can achieve highly accurate data imputation in time series, however, xLSTM is incapable of distributed imputation. To solve the problem in a distributed environment, a distributed reversible embedding xLSTM imputation method (DRE-xLSTM) is proposed. First, a reversible embedded xLSTM method is designed to scale the data and fuse complex features using reversible normalization and multilayer linear modules. Second, a searchable prototype federated learning method is developed to accomplish the distributed learning using searchable cell states in a reversibly embedded xLSTM for delivery. The proposed DRE-xLSTM produces more accurate imputation results than comparative methods on the QINGHE dataset.

articleTitle: Sparse Millimeter-wave Radar Point Clouds based Transformer for Human Activity Recognition
abstract: Compared to visual and wearable sensors, activity recognition based on millimeter-wave radar offers a better experience in terms of privacy and comfort. However, the point clouds generated by the millimeter-wave radar are sparse, and existing methods struggle to extract temporal and spatial features from the point clouds. To fully exploit the information in sparse point clouds sequences and accurately capture the spatiotemporal relationships within them, we propose Millimeter-wave radar-based Transformer for human Activity Recognition (MTAR), an innovative approach that achieves accurate human activity recognition by leveraging sparse point clouds as input through Transformers. This method enhances the identification and feature extraction of key channels in point clouds data by introducing PointNet with channel attention mechanisms. Additionally, we employ a dual-branch Transformer architecture, specifically designed to analyze the intrinsic connections within the temporal and spatial dimensions, and further optimize the integration of temporal and spatial features through an adaptive-weighted fusion Transformer, thereby improving the overall performance of the model. Comprehensive evaluations show that with fewer parameters and similar FLOPs, the MTAR outperforms the closest rival by 2.5% on the MM- Fi dataset and by 2.35% on the MMgesture dataset, showcasing its superior generalization performance in experiments with different individuals and environments as well.

articleTitle: GRRL: Goal-Guided Risk-Inspired Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Autonomous Driving in Off- Road Environment
abstract: When unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) are deployed for rescue, pathfinding, and other tasks in off-road scenarios, existing conventional path planners often fail to generate both feasible and efficient trajectories and also require high computational resources. To address these problems, this article introduces a goal-guided, risk-inspired reinforcement learning framework for efficient autonomous driving in off-road environments. This tightly coupled navigation framework integrates a perception network based on a Transformer feature extractor with an actor-critic reinforcement learning network. First, terrain risk maps are constructed from point clouds and converted into bird's-eye view risk images as the input of the learning framework. Then, terrain risk features and goal information are combined to generate safe actions for the UGV to move to the goal in off-road environments. Moreover, a joint reward function consisting of goal heuristic and driving feasibility is also designed to ensure both the efficiency and safety of the driving process. Sufficient experiments were carried out on simulated off-road terrains to verify the effectiveness of the proposed system. Experiment results show that, compared with other methods, our method achieves a higher success rate and enhances the UGV's risk avoidance ability in off-road scenarios.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Fractional-Order PI Control for Fractional-Order Optical Communication Systems
abstract: This study proposes a fractional-order control strategy for the Optical Communication Tracking System (OCTS) to enhance tracking accuracy and robustness in free-space transmission. Fractional order models capture the dynamic properties of OCTS more accurately than traditional integer-order models. Subsequently, a Fractional-Order Proportional Integral (FO-PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>) controller was designed based on finite-dimensional sampling data, which introduces the parameter λ to enhance control flexibility and precision. Simulation results demonstrate that the FO-PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>controller outperforms traditional integer-order PI controllers in terms of tracking accuracy and system stability.

articleTitle: Solving Distribution Shift in Quantization-Aware Training via Channel-Wise Standardization Distillation
abstract: With the continuous deepening of network models and the gradual increase of model parameters, model compression has become a necessary technology in the process of model deployment. Quantization of deep models can effectively reduce the computation and memory consumption based on low-bit parameters and bit-wise operations, and has recently attained much attention. However, due to quantization operations, quantized models are often affected by performance degradation. In this work, through extensive empirical analysis, we find that the performance degradation comes from the distribution shift between the Full Precision (FP) model and the quantized model. The distribution shift will lead to the continuous accumulation of quantization errors, which will affect the final performance of the model. In this paper, we address this issue from a distillation perspective to effectively eliminate such a shift. We present a simple and powerful method to eliminate the distribution shift via Channel-wise Standardization Distillation (CSD). CSD assumes that the quantized model and the FP model should have a similar distribution in the feature space. Our method generalizes well to different network architectures and various Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) methods. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms the current State-Of-The-Art (SOTA) QAT methods and even FP counterparts.

articleTitle: Prediction of Cement Combined Grinding Mill Bucket Elevator Current Based on Hybrid Neural Network
abstract: Cement combined grinding is one of the key links in the cement production process, and accurate prediction of mill bucket elevator current has an important impact on its control and stable operation. However, cement combined grinding is a nonlinear system with complex working conditions. In order to bring the predicted and actual values of the mill bucket elevator current closer together. In this paper, a hybrid neural network that combines Temporal Convolutional Network with Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory Network and introduces the Attention mechanism is utilized to predict the mill bucket elevator current. The model captures local features and long-range dependencies on the data and updates the model parameters using the Adaptive Moment Estimation optimization algorithm as the optimizer and the Mean Square Error as the loss function. Using the model to obtain the new current value, taking the standard error and the coefficient of determination as the evaluation metrics, and comparing the Convolutional Neural Network prediction model, the Long Short-Term Memory Network prediction model, and the Bi-directional Gated Recurrent Unit prediction model, it is verified that the present model outperforms the other several models, and exhibits a good performance in the current prediction of the mill bucket elevator.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Class Incremental Object Detection for Packaging Defects in Domain Transfer Scenerios
abstract: Few-shot class incremental learning presents a promising approach for the adaptation of detect models to evolving scenarios where the diversity of cigarette defect classes dynamically expands. While in practical production scenarios, the diversity of cigarette boxes may also alter due to production plan adjustments, with new brands potentially replacing old ones. This results in a domain shift within the training data, posing challenges for defect detection models. To circumvent the need for redundant training and reduce costs, we can transfer the detection model from old to new brand. We frame this challenge as a Domain-Transfer Few-Shot Class Incremental Learning (DT-FSCIL) problem, where the key difficulties stem from overfitting and catastrophic forgetting when learning from only a few samples of new defect categories within the newly introduced domain. To tackle these challenges, we devise a transfer strategy based on knowledge distillation to harness expertise from the source domain and propose a parameter update method guided by class sensitivity, which decouple the learning of classification and detection to avoid performance degradation of old class. We have verified the superiority of the proposed method through experiments and achieved good performance on the cigarette defect dataset.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation Method of Magnetic Levitation Train Suspension System Based on Operation Data
abstract: As a modern new type of rail transportation, magnetic levitation train has many technical advantages, such as safety, reliability, convenient maintenance, green and environmental protection, etc. The levitation system is the core key system of magnetic levitation train. The levitation system is the core key system of the maglev train, and its performance determines the overall performance of the maglev train. Currently, there are fewer studies on the performance evaluation of the levitation system of the maglev train. In this paper, on the basis of obtaining the actual running data of the train, two performance evaluation methods, namely the error integral index and the minimum variance index, are adopted to evaluate the levitation system of the normal-conducting magnetic levitation train. Firstly, maglev train levitation data acquisition system and the definition of the two evaluation indexes are introduced. Secondly, a single-point model of the levitation system is established, and a controller is designed to analyze the applicability of the two indicators in the performance evaluation of the levitation system. Finally, based on the actual running data of the train, the performance evaluation methods of the error integral index and the minimum variance index are experimentally verified and their correlation is analyzed.

articleTitle: An Efficient Transformer Incorporating a Spatial Decay Matrix and Attention Decomposition for Image Matching
abstract: Homography estimation has widespread applications in visual computing and image analysis. Current state-of-the-art Transformer-based image matching methods require computing all possible key-value combinations to obtain global information, resulting in high computational costs and slow inference speeds. This paper presents an enhanced Transformer-based approach for image matching, integrating a spatial decay matrix derived from Manhattan distance and leveraging attention decomposition. We introduce Manhattan Self-Attention (MaSA) to enhance the LoFTR framework. This approach maintains the integrity of the spatial decay matrix while reducing the computational burden of modeling global information. Through the incorporation of a spatial decay matrix and attention decomposition, explicit spatial priors can be seamlessly integrated into the visual backbone network, enabling the achievement of linear computational complexity. Thus, it improves decoding throughput, latency, and GPU memory usage without sacrificing performance. Experimental evaluations indicate that the proposed method substantially enhances matching accuracy while effectively reducing inference time and memory overhead, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches under consistent evaluation metrics.

articleTitle: A Complete Exploration and Mapping Algorithm for Robots in Unknown Obstacle-Cluttered Environments
abstract: This paper considers the problem of exploring an unknown, obstacle-cluttered, bounded environment and constructing a complete topological map using a robot equipped with range sensors. We propose an exploration and mapping algorithm for this problem utilizing a target obstacle selection rule and a sector selection rule. This algorithm aids the robot in making decisions to expand the explored area based on information obtained at each intersection, ultimately constructing a complete topological map within finite time. We demonstrate that this algorithm guarantees provable mapping completeness and provides an upper bound on mapping time in standard map environments. Compared to a previous complete map construction algorithm, our approach accelerates the exploration of unknown areas and reduces the number of revisits, thus im-proving exploration efficiency. Simulation experiments in various environments validate the completeness and efficiency of our algorithm.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Quasipolynomials with Complex Coefficients: A Frequency-Sweeping Approach
abstract: For real-coefficient quasipolynomials (RCQs), which always appear as the characteristic functions of time-delay systems, the complete stability problem has been fully investi-gated within the frequency-sweeping framework. In this paper, we further study the stability property of complex-coefficient quasipolynomials (CCQs), which are a straightforward extension of RCQs and, hence, correspond to a broader class of system dynamics subject to delays. However, to the best of the authors' knowledge, the complete stability problem for CCQs still remains unsolved. Unlike for an RCQ, the spectrum for a CCQ does not possess the conjugate symmetry property. Therefore, to analyze the stability, we have to (i) exhaustively detect the critical imaginary roots, including the ones with negative imaginary parts, and (ii) systematically study their asymptotic behavior. The current paper provides a complete solution to these technical issues by generalizing the frequency-sweeping framework.

articleTitle: Transition Flight Control of the Distributed Propulsion Tilt-Rotor Aircraft
abstract: Distributed propulsion tilt-rotor aircraft has multiple propulsion systems, which brings larger difficulties in the transition controller design. In this paper, the control for the transition flights of the distributed propulsion tilt-rotor aircraft is studied. A coordinated tilting strategy is firstly developed for distributed propulsion systems based on the Sigmoid function, which achieves smooth tilting thanks to the first increasing and then decreasing tilting angular velocity. Based on that, a discrete-time LQR controller with a predefined decay rate is designed for the transition flights, ensuring both a minimum decay rate and the desired pole configuration. Forward and backward transition simulation flights were conducted in the newly developed Matlab + X-plane platform to corroborate the effectiveness and robustness of the transition trajectory and the control law.

articleTitle: CBLN: A User Behavior Prediction Model Considering Content Correlation
abstract: The core of user behavior prediction is Click-through Rate (CTR) prediction, which requires deep analysis of user actions such as clicks and browse. It is crucial to model user behavior sequences, content attributes, and user attributes to understand user preferences and improve CTR prediction accuracy. While many CTR prediction models are based on historical behavior sequences, most treat historical behavior representations merely as preferences, neglecting the representation of correlations between users and content. To address this, we propose a new model called the Correlated Behavior Learning Network (CBLN), for the task of user behavior prediction. This model includes a User Behavior Tracking Network (UBTN) and a Content Relevance Network (CRN), which dynamically modeling the evolution of user preferences related to target content and introduce content relevance to more comprehensively capture user behavior, thus more accurate predictions of user behavior can be made. We conducted extensive experiments on two public datasets to validate the effectiveness of our model, and the results showed that our proposed model achieved better performance than many complex CTR prediction models.

articleTitle: A Time-Window Scheduling Method for Green Logistics Vehicles in the V2X Environment
abstract: Aiming at the problem of high energy consumption and high distribution cost of new energy logistics vehicles due to traffic congestion in the actual logistics distribution process. This paper firstly proposes the calculation method of road congestion coefficient, and combines the actual operation of new energy logistics vehicles to construct a nonlinear energy consumption model of new energy logistics vehicles considering traffic congestion; then, a mathematical model of green vehicle path optimization with time windows in the V2X environment is constructed by considering the relevant constraints and taking the optimization objective of minimizing the sum of fixed cost, time cost, and travel cost.; finally, based on the above model and combined with the improved Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search algorithm, we propose a green scheduling method for new energy logistics vehicles considering the time window. Experimental results show that the scheduling method in this paper can effectively reduce the distribution cost of new energy logistics vehicles, and the cost reduction is more significant with the increase of road congestion.

articleTitle: PSO-Based Modified Control Barrier Function to Avoid Collision of Vehicle
abstract: An efficient and stable algorithm for vehicle path following and obstacle avoidance is proposed in this paper. Firstly, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is used as the solver for the controller, combined with the modified Control Barrier Function (CBF), to propose the PSO-CBF controller. To ensure the safety of vehicle obstacle avoidance and solve the deadlock issue, we insert an additional local path planning layer after the global path planning, which enhances the stability of the controller. In addition, we optimize the initial state of the PSO solver, reduce the population size of PSO under the conditions of satisfying basic obstacle avoidance requirements and path following. This approach effectively improving the efficiency of the algorithm. Finally, the performance of the PSO-CBF controller is verified through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Machine Recognition and Subconscious Perception Characteristics of Musical Emotions
abstract: Music, an auditory art form abundant in emotional characteristics, plays a crucial role in human sensory experiences and psychological adjustments. Its emotional impact originates from the brain's emotional mechanisms, music appreciation education, as well as the surrounding environment and mental state. These effects involve subconscious perception and a complex interaction of emotions. In recent years, significant progress has been made in machine recognition of musical emotions, driven by the rapid development of artificial intelligence technologies. This paper presents a systematic review and analysis of relevant research, concentrating on aspects such as emotional feature extraction from music, emotional model construction, machine recognition methods, and the subtle perceptual characteristics of music. The paper proposes four classifications for music emotional features: basic acoustic features, music perception features, neural activity features, and multi-dimensional fusion features. Additionally, it summarizes four machine recognition methods based on audio data, lyrics, neural signals, and multimodal data. The discussion also addresses current challenges and outlines future research directions, aiming to provide insights for the advancement of music emotion research and intelligent recommendation technologies.

articleTitle: Research on Atmospheric Pollutant Concentration Prediction Model Based on the BO-GRU Neural Network with MIV Algorithm
abstract: The prediction of atmospheric pollutant concentrations is of crucial importance for environmental protection and safeguarding public health. However, there are some problems with the commonly used air quality prediction methods in China at present, including high model complexity, low prediction accuracy, insufficient spatiotemporal correlation, and poor real-time performance. To enhance the prediction accuracy and real-time capability of atmospheric pollutant concentration forecasting, this study employs the Mean Impact Value (MIV) algorithm for feature selection to determine input variables. Subsequently, a Bayesian Optimization Gated Recurrent Unit (BO-GRU) neural network prediction model is designed. Leveraging the advantages of GRU neural networks, this model fully explores the correlations between various meteorological factors and atmospheric pollutants. Moreover, an intelligent tuning mechanism based on Bayesian optimization is devised to optimize model parameters and structure intelligently, thereby improving the model's learning ability, generalization, and accuracy. Comparative analysis with similar models validates the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Discriminative Feature Aggregation Based Offline Handwritten Chinese Text Recognition
abstract: Connectionist temporal classification (CTC) based methods for offline handwritten Chinese text recognition (HCTR) have achieved remarkable progress recently due to their superiority in the robustness to varying sequence lengths and inference efficiency. However, CTC-based models still grapple with the attenuation of the feature representation degradation because of the collapse of height information of text images. To alleviate this issue, in this paper, we propose utilizing deep supervision technology and hierarchical feature aggregation to improve the CTC-based recognizers and construct a novel HCTR model, namely DSHctr. Concretely, DSHctr deploys multiple classifiers to directly supervise and optimize discriminative multi-scale features. Then these hierarchical discriminative are aggregated for the final recognition. The proposed DSHctr model exhibits remarkable performance on the publicly available ICDAR-2013 handwriting competition dataset, achieving an accuracy rate of 94.29% and a correct rate of 94.49% without a language model, surpassing its state-of-the-art counterparts. Extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments highlight the effectiveness of the proposed hierarchical discriminative feature aggregation.

articleTitle: 3D Face Reconstruction from Sketches with Hybrid Model Architecture
abstract: Recent advances in 3D face reconstruction have shown impressive results. However, these methods predominantly focus on real face images, leaving a gap in accessible and user-friendly 3D face modeling options. To address this challenge, we introduce our hybrid model approach, an end-to-end 3D generation framework tailored for sketching, enabling precise face reconstruction from a single sketch. Using a hierarchical approach, our system predicts missing facial geometry to enhance the extraction of fine geometric features. The resultant predictions combined with the original inputs guide the learning process of the 3D face model. To mitigate prediction uncertainty, our model incorporates a novel “predict consistent” loss, refining reconstruction outcomes with increased detail while closely adhering to the input sketch. Rigorous experiments demonstrate the capability of our method to produce high-quality face models from sketches.

articleTitle: Spatio-Temporal Wind Speed Prediction Model Based on Multi-Scale Fusion MambaFormer
abstract: In recent years, spatiotemporal wind speed prediction using deep learning methods has become a hot research topic. However, these predictions still face challenges as existing models primarily focus on spatial features and exhibit weaker capabilities in capturing temporal characteristics, failing to meet the efficiency and accuracy requirements of practical applications. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a novel method, the Multiscale Fusion MambaFormer spatiotemporal wind speed prediction model (MF-MambaFormer). This model integrates the Transformer with Mamba, leveraging the Transformer's ability to model long-distance dependencies and Mamba's capability to extract temporal features. By combining the strengths of these technologies, the model significantly enhances prediction accuracy. Additionally, through the Spatial Channel Gating Aggregation Module (SCGAM), which utilizes dilated convolutions to extract spatial features across different receptive fields and a channel attention module to capture channel weights, the model improves its ability to apprehend spatial and channel features. Moreover, by incorporating the Mam-baFormer module into the multiscale fusion, we propose a novel Multiscale Spatiotemporal Fusion Module (MSTFM) that integrates and effectively combines spatiotemporal features at various scales. We comprehensively evaluated our model's performance on the WeatherBench dataset, and extensive experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in spatiotemporal wind speed prediction.

articleTitle: Dynamic Event-Triggered H∞ Sliding Mode Control for Multi-Agent Systems Using a Dual Hidden Markov Model
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic event-triggered <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>∞ sliding mode control (SMC) issue for a class of linear multi-agent systems (MASs) with Markov jump parameters and Markov switching topologies. A mapping technique for continuous-time Markov chains is employed to address the challenge of MASs with dual Markov jumping process. Based on the hidden Markov model detector, the distributed event-triggered <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>∞ sliding mode controllers are constructed, and the dynamic event-triggering scheme (DETS) is introduced to reduce bandwidth pressure. By constructing mode-dependent Lyapunov- Krasovskii functionals (LKFs), the stochastic consen-sus conditions of MASs with prescribed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>∞ performance index are formulated by linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Finally, a numerical simulation is conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Improved Road Target Detection Approach Based on YOLO-v8
abstract: To address the challenges of high equipment demands, low detection accuracy, and high miss rates for overlapping and small targets in traditional road target detection models, we propose an improved detection method named YOLOv8-GPT. The C2f module in the backbone network is restructured with the inclusion of a lightweight attention mechanism, Triplet Attention, improving the model's feature extraction capabilities. Additionally, a new lightweight convolution accumulation technique, GSConv, is integrated into the Neck, reducing model burden while preserving accuracy and enhancing computational cost efficiency. Then, to better detect small vehicles in crowded traffic, a dedicated small target detection head has been added, aiming to capture detailed features and contextual cues effectively. Ultimately, the Wise-IoU, capable of adaptively adjusting weight coefficients, is employed as the loss function for the refined model, boosting the regression performance of bounding boxes and overall detection robustness. Experiments on the KITTI dataset show that the YOLOv8-GPT model significantly excels beyond the original, with a 3.5 percentage point increase in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> AP, a reduction of 1.3 million parameters, and superior performance in both volume and accuracy compared to other classic detection models, highlighting its strong practical applicability.

articleTitle: Cluster-Enhanced Federated Graph Neural Network for Recommendation
abstract: Personal interaction data can be effectively modeled as individual graphs for each user in recommender systems. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs)-based recommendation techniques have become extremely popular since they can capture high-order collaborative signals between users and items by aggregating the individual graph into a global interactive graph. However, this centralized approach inherently poses a threat to user privacy and security. Recently, federated GNN-based recommendation techniques have emerged as a promising solution to mitigate privacy concerns. Nevertheless, current implementations either limit on-device training to an unaccompanied individual graphs or necessitate reliance on an extra third-party server to touch other individual graphs, which also increases the risk of privacy leakage. To address this challenge, we propose a Cluster-enhanced Federated Graph Neural Network framework for Recommendation, named CFedGR, which introduces high-order collaborative signals to augment individual graphs in a privacy preserving manner. Specifically, the server clusters the pretrained user representations to identify high-order collaborative signals. In addition, two efficient strategies are devised to reduce communication between devices and the server. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets validate the effectiveness of our proposed methods.

articleTitle: Integrating Wavelet Reconstruction with Hybrid TCN-LSTM Model for Enhanced Fault Diagnosis in Distributed Photovoltaic System
abstract: As photovoltaic (PV) systems become more prevalent, effective fault detection and diagnosis in distributed PV systems (DPVS) are increasingly important. This study presents a novel approach combining Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for enhanced fault diagnosis in DPVS. By using wavelet transform-based signal denoising techniques, our method reduces noise and improves feature extraction. The TCN-LSTM hybrid model captures both long-term dependencies and sequential patterns, achieving a diagnostic accuracy of 99.33% on real-world PV fault datasets. This approach significantly enhances fault diagnosis, demonstrating strong performance and practical applicability in PV system maintenance.

articleTitle: MDAF: Enhancing Temporal Dynamics in CNNs for Action Recognition
abstract: Understanding temporal information in video sequences is crucial for various computer vision tasks, such as action recognition. Transformer-based methods and GCNs can effectively handle temporal information, but they suffer from high computational costs or poor generalization capabilities. Some research has shown promising results using 3D CNNs to process skeleton data instead of RGB data, but 3D CNNs may treat temporal dimension as a spatial one, limiting their ability to capture complex temporal dynamics. To address these issues, we propose the Multi-Dimensional Attention Fusion module (MDAF), which includes separate channel, spatial, and temporal attention computation modules, integrated through an attention fusion module. This design ensures the effective utilization of attention information across all dimensions. Our method enhances temporal dynamics, improving the recognition of complex actions. Experiments conducted on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving significant performance improvements.

articleTitle: Short-term Storm Surge Prediction based on Variational Mode Decomposition and Temporal Convolutional Network
abstract: Storm surges have caused severe casualties and economic losses. Accurate prediction of storm surge levels is crucial for disaster assessment, early warning, and effective disaster management. Compared to numerical simulation methods, machine learning approaches are relatively more efficient and direct. However, traditional machine learning models often fail to significantly remove noise and effectively capture long-term sequential dependencies. Therefore, this paper proposes a hybrid storm surge prediction model that combines Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) with Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN). By utilizing the VMD method, the model effectively decomposes storm surge signals into intrinsic mode functions (IMF) to enhance prediction accuracy by removing noise and extracting key features. The TCN component captures long-term dependencies in time series data, making the prediction of storm surge levels more precise. Upon comparison with conventional models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), and standard TCN, the proposed VMD-TCN model exhibits significant advantages. The forecasting performance metrics Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and Correlation Coefficient (CC) are 7.2254 cm, 9.4548 cm, and 0.9251 respectively, indicating that the model proposed in this paper performs well in predicting storm surges.

Author Keywords: Time Series Forecasting Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD)

articleTitle: Enhancing Dynamic Parameter Identification for Supernumerary Robotic Limbs Through Uncertainty Compensation
abstract: Accurate dynamic modeling is fundamental for wearable robotics, such as Supernumerary Robotic Limbs (SRLs), to ensure precise control and effective interaction with the environment. This paper presents an enhanced dynamic model for an SRL, incorporating uncertainty compensation to improve accuracy and robustness. The SRL dynamics are streamlined by linearizing the system and identifying a minimal set of inertia parameters. Using the Coot optimization algorithm, we refine the Fourier excitation trajectory parameters to optimize the condition number of the observation matrix, followed by parameter identification through the least squares method. To further reduce discrepancies between predicted and actual joint torques, an uncertainty term is introduced, validated through a neural network designed to predict torque variations. The method not only addresses but also compensates for uncertainties across various motion states of the SRL. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model improves prediction accuracy and robustness for our developed 6-DoF SRL compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: Analysis and Compensation of Object Surface Inclination Error Based on Line Laser Sensor
abstract: Base on the measurement principle of line laser sensor, when the surface of an object is tilted, the sensor will generate measurement errors, and for the same laser line, there will be deviation at different positions. To further enhance measurement accuracy, this paper examines the effect of the laser beam's optical path and the center of mass of the converging spot on the measurement accuracy on basis of the principle of laser triangulation, and establishes an object equation using the geometrical characteristics of the optical path, deduces the mathematical model of the tilting error at various positions on a laser line. Using the experimental platform for measuring tilting error, constructed with a robot, a sensor, and a tilting angle adjustment platform, the sensor error at different tilting angles is measured. The experiment takes the standard block as the measured object, and measures and compensates the data errors of different inclination angles and different positions on the laser line. The results show that the error can be controlled within 20 μ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> after model compensation, and the proposed error model is effective and accurate, which improves the measurement precision of the line laser sensor when the object surface is tilted.

articleTitle: Deep Feature Decomposition Autoencoder: Intelligent Fault Diagnosis for Unknown Faults in Landing Gear Systems
abstract: The landing gear system of civil aircraft has the design characteristics of high safety and reliability, which contributes to the scarcity of fault types and samples that can be obtained in practice. The incompleteness of fault labels and samples can not only cause the small sample problem but also lead to the zero-shot problem, meaning that traditional data-driven fault diagnosis models may not apply to identifying unknown faults. Aiming at this problem, a deep feature decomposition autoencoder (DFDAE) method is proposed to realize the unknown fault diagnosis of the aircraft landing gear system. Firstly, a set of parallel semi-supervised asymmetric convolutional autoencoders is constructed, combined with a deep feature decomposition strategy to extract features with interpretable differences from high-dimensional data. Secondly, an adaptive threshold strategy based on the distance difference ratio is proposed. The distance relationship between the test sample and the training set is analyzed to adaptively determine the threshold, avoiding the deviation caused by human subjective experience and realizing the diagnosis of unknown faults. In addition, a silhouette-density clustering evaluation strategy is used to predict the number of unknown fault categories. Finally, the performance of the proposed algorithm is analyzed using a simulation data set of the landing gear system. The results show that DFDAE can realize the unknown fault diagnosis of the aircraft landing gear system with little training in the fault category.

articleTitle: ATA -Net: Asynchronous Temporal Attention for Real-World Multi-Modal 3D Object Detection
abstract: Multi-modal fusion for 3D object detection exploits the benefits of various sensors, mitigating uncertainties arising from single-source sensor, rendering it crucial for visual perception in intelligent transportation. Addressing multi-modal fusion in real-world traffic scenes remains a significant challenge for existing methods, primarily due to issues such as temporal misalignment of data during actual collection and the sparsity problem associated with low-beam LiDAR or roadside LiDAR. To solve the above challenges., this paper proposes an asynchronous temporal attention model (ATA-Net) for achieving more robust multi-modal 3D object detection in real-world traffic scenes. To deal with the spatio-temporal asynchronous multi-modal data, a bi-directional interaction between image and sequential point clouds is realized in ATA-Net, enabling effective global and local feature fusion with spatio-temporal correlations. To mitigate the sparsity concern in point clouds within asynchronous multi-modal data, a object-level densification scheme, with an integration of visual guidance and optical flow estimation, is further designed for producing object-level pseudo point clouds. Experimental validation on the VANJEE real roadside dataset and the V2X-Seq temporal dataset demonstrates the effectiveness of proposed model. Our code will be available at https://github.com/BUCT-IUSRC/Research_ATA-Net.

articleTitle: Pixel Voting Network-Based Monocular Pose Estimation for Space Non-Cooperative Targets
abstract: This paper proposes a monocular pose estimation method for space non-cooperative target based on pixel-wise voting network (PVNet). By combining deep learning with geometric optimization, our approach can effectively improve the accuracy of pose estimation and solve the problems of low computational efficiency caused by train two networks: the object detection network and the key point regression network. In this paper, the 3D key points of the non-cooperative target are reconstructed by a multi-view triangulation, the 2D key point regression is performed using PVNet, and the non-cooperative target's pose is estimated using the Efficient Perspective-n-Point (EPnP) method. Experimental evaluation on a public dataset shows that the method in this paper can estimate the pose of non-cooperative targets efficiently and accurately.

articleTitle: DFE-SLAM: Dynamic SLAM based on improved feature extraction
abstract: Traditional visual localization algorithms often assume a static world, making them susceptible to inaccuracies and reduced robustness in real environments with dynamic objects. Additionally, these algorithms struggle to maintain high localization accuracy in low-texture settings. To overcome these challenges, we propose a dynamic SLAM system with enhanced feature extraction capabilities, called DFE-SLAM (Dynamic SLAM based on improved feature extraction). DFE-SLAM employs a lightweight YOLOv5s dynamic target detection network to filter out dynamic features from detection results. It also utilizes adaptive thresholding during the feature point detection stage to enhance accuracy. Moreover, the system incorporates a dense map construction thread, which creates dense point cloud maps using keyframes with corresponding bit poses. We evaluated DFE-SLAM using the TUM and Bonn datasets, benchmarking it against several advanced SLAM systems. The results demonstrate that DFE-SLAM excels in dynamic environments, delivering superior accuracy and robustness compared to most existing SLAM systems.

articleTitle: A Novel 3D Defect Detection System for Complex-Shaped Components
abstract: Accurate defect detection in high-end equipment components is essential for ensuring reliability and performance. This paper addresses the challenges of inspecting complex-shaped components, such as aviation core components, by developing an intelligent defect detection system based on human-like imaging principles. The system integrates a high-precision five-axis motion mechanism, a microscopic imaging system and a multi-spectral illumination system, enabling comprehensive and precise data acquisition. Additionally, we have constructed a small-scale 3D point cloud dataset specifically tailored for complex-shaped components. Furthermore, we propose a novel 3D anomaly detection method that combines coarse and fine registration strategies for point cloud alignment, utilizes the PointMamba for feature extraction, and employs a dual memory bank approach for defect identification. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in detection efficiency and accuracy, providing robust technical support for the high-end equipment manufacturing industry.

articleTitle: Takeoff Control for Variable-Sweep Wing Trans-Medium Aircraft Based on ADRC Extended State Observer and Backstepping Method
abstract: Addressing the challenge of low post-splashdown velocity and insufficient lift leading to potential water re-entry, a controller is designed using a backstepping approach enhanceed by an active disturbance rejection technique. This design enables the aircraft to maintain a set target angle of attack post-splashdown to sustain sufficient lift. Within the control strategy, the variations induced by wing deployment are treated as disturbances, effectively mitigated through observation using an extended state observer designed for active disturbance rejection, thereby addressing aerodynamic coefficient changes due to wing deployment. Simulation results confirm that the designed angle of attack tracking controller ensures successful take-off of the variable-sweep wing trans-medium aircraft post-splashdown.

articleTitle: Hybrid Algorithm on Timeline Matrix for Task Scheduling in Clouds
abstract: In recent years, cloud computing is an emerging industry that serves many people who do not own sufficient compute resources in a flexible and efficient approach. However, it is difficult to optimize the cost of computing while meeting the QoS requirements of users, especially for those time-constrained workflows. In this article, we present a hybrid particle swarm optimization (PSO) scheduling algorithm, called HPSOTM, which aims to optimize the scheduling strategy of workflows while meeting deadline constraints in a cloud environment. In HPSOTM, a more suitable and refined optimization and solution-repair strategy is constructed for the timeline matrix of the virtual machine pool to improve the efficiency. At the same time, it also enriches the diversity of solutions in particle swarms and improves the convergence speed of feasible solutions. It mainly contains two major highlight features: 1) design a new slot-aware rule to reduce VM idle time, which could reduce execution costs; 2) apply the concept of partial critical path to complete deadline distribution, which could fit to time constraints precisely. Extensive experiments are conducted and the results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms other existing algorithms that minimize the execution cost of scheduling workflows with deadline constraints.

articleTitle: Time-Varying Formation-Containment Tracking Control of Heterogeneous Multi-Agent System Under Denial of Service Attack and Sensor Fault
abstract: In this paper, the problem of output-feedback time-varying formation-containment tracking control for heteroge-neous multi-agent systems with sensor fault under distributed denial of service (DoS) attacks is studied. The leaders are non-cooperative, which are embedded with unknown input. Firstly, in order to estimate the sensor fault and the states of the followers, a distributed fault-detecting observer is designed. Secondly, in order to deal with distributed DoS attacks and the unknown input of the leaders, a leader state estimator is designed. Finally, a distributed output-feedback containment control law is proposed to realize the time-varying formation tracking of the convex hull of multiple leaders. It is proved that the proposed control scheme guarantees the exponential convergence of all errors of the multi-agent system, and the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed scheme are verified by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Integrated Train Timetabling and Rolling Stock Circulation Planning for Cross-Line Operation in Urban Rail Transit
abstract: With the rapid development of urban rail transit in China, cross-line operation is emerging as a key trend, offering passengers convenient travel and reducing operational costs for companies. However, scheduling effective train timetables while ensuring safety is crucial. This paper presents an integrated train timetabling and rolling stock circulation planning model for the cross-line operation of urban rail transit. The integrated problem aims to minimize three objective components, including the total turnaround operation time, the headway variations of train timetable and the number of rolling stocks required for operation. The constraints of the integrated optimization problem include running time constraints, dwell time constraints, turnaround operation constraints, headway constraints, and rolling stock circulation constraints. The resulting integrated optimization problem is nonliear programming problem, which is then transformed into a linear programming problem that can be solved using the commercial solver, e.g., Gurobi. Based on a small-scale case study, a set of numerical experiments are carried out to obtain the train timetable for cross-line operation during peak and off-peak hours, comparing departure interval with independent operation. It is concluded that cross-line operation are superior to independent operation, confirming the model's validity. This optimization model serves as an effective reference for preparing cross-line operation timetable.

articleTitle: SFMixer: Local Periodic Features in Frequency Domain and Global Features in Time Domain Modeling for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Considering the sophisticated interplay of features within time-series data, the fusion of local and global features is essential for effective long-term forecasting. While CNNs are adept at capturing local characteristics, they often fall short in encapsulating global features within time series when using simplistic model architectures or those with reduced complexity. Additionally, existing research on modeling dependencies between time-series data using frequency domain information, especially local periodic features, is insufficient. To address these issues, we propose the SFMixer model, which utilizes an improved CNN structure and MLP network to model and integrate both local periodic variations in the frequency domain, including intra-local and inter-local periodic variations, and global features in the time domain. The SFMixer model outperforms previous methods on eight benchmark datasets. In both multivariate and univariate forecasting experiments, SFMixer achieves significant reductions in MSE and MAE. Furthermore, SFMixer demonstrates higher capabilities in capturing temporal information and training efficiency. We will make our code and model publicly available.

articleTitle: Distributed Control of Vehicle Platoon with Input Saturation Under DoS Attacks
abstract: This paper focuses on the control of connected vehicle platoon when subjected to random Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks. Firstly, to better describe the impact of a random DoS attack, the attack is modeled as a random communication topology switching process using a stochastic Markov process. Then, to cope with the DoS attack, a security control law con-sidering the dynamic coupling between vehicles and the input saturation property is proposed on the basis of the recovery mechanism. After that, the relevant parameters of the proposed controller are calculated by solving the linear matrix inequality (LMI), while the Lyapunov- Razumikhin theory is applied to es-tablish a sufficient condition for the stabilization of the platooning system under DoS attack. Finally, the performance of the proposed control protocol is confirmed by the numerical simu-lation of a vehicular platoon system containing one leader vehi-cle and six follower vehicles.

articleTitle: Complex Industrial Process Monitoring using Improved Dynamic Latent Variables - Neighborhood Preserving Embedding
abstract: In complex industrial process monitoring, prevalent challenges include high dimensionality, extensive redundancies, and dynamic characteristics. In this paper, we propose an Improved Dynamic Latent Variable-Neighborhood Preserving Embedding (DLV -NPE) algorithm specifically designed to tackle these issues. The methodology begins with the implementation of a variance-covariance feature selection method to minimize redundancies among monitoring variables. This is followed using a dynamic latent variable algorithm to extract dynamic regression properties from the selected variables. Subsequently, the NPE algorithm is employed to preserve the residuals of high-dimensional dynamic latent variables and the high-dimensional residuals of selected variables, thereby preserving the integrity of the low-dimensional manifold structure. Finally, Bayesian inference is applied to develop comprehensive monitoring indicators. The efficacy of the DL V -NPE algorithm is validated through its application to the Tennessee Eastman (TE) process, where it demonstrates superior fault detection capabilities compared to other algorithms.

articleTitle: A Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Frequency Domain Convolution and Temporal Information Decoupling
abstract: In recent years, transformer family models have demonstrated excellent performance in time series data research, gradually becoming mainstream in time series analysis. However, due to their unique attention mechanisms, these models suffer from low computational efficiency and are significantly affected by noise. Conversely, convolutional methods have lost momentum in time series research due to their narrow receptive fields. This paper proposes a novel network for fault diagnosis in time series data, based on Fourier analysis and Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN). This network combines the global receptive field of Fourier analysis with the local receptive field advantages of convolutional methods. It filters out noise during the Fourier analysis phase to achieve better performance in fault diagnosis tasks. Additionally, this method decouples information from time series data, extracting information independently from the time, feature, and variable dimensions. This allows the network to learn complex dependencies among variables, building on previous research. Our study shows that our network can filter noise while capturing both long-term and short-term interactive information. Compared to previous models solely based on convolution, the network offers a broader receptive field and enhanced information decoupling. Experimental results demonstrate that this method achieves excellent performance in fault diagnosis tasks.

articleTitle: Point Cloud Segmentation Network Based on Multi-Scale Feature Fusion
abstract: Aiming at improving the local feature extraction for point cloud learning, we introduce a point cloud segmentation network that enhances the PointNet++ framework with a local feature transformation module and a multi-scale feature fusion module. The local feature transformation module employs operations akin to convolution to restructure the point cloud's local feature dimensions, thus boosting the network's ability to extract detailed local features. Additionally, the multi-scale feature fusion module integrates semantic features of point clouds across various scales using a layered network design, aiming to heighten segmentation precision. Experimental results indicate that the proposed network can achieve a robust point cloud segmentation accuracy, reaching an accuracy rate of 85.8%.

articleTitle: CaSTGCN: Deep Learning Method for Information Cascade Prediction
abstract: With the advancement of online social media technologies, a vast amount of information is constantly being spreaded and interacting with users on social networks. The diffusion of online information has a significant impact on individuals, organizations, and society. Thus, controlling and predicting information cascades are particularly important. Traditional information cascades prediction and pure sequence modeling methods struggle to both capture the temporal and structural information in cascades for accurate predictions. Recently, many studies have begun to explore deep learning algorithms, particularly graph neural networks (GNNs) and sequence modeling neural network algorithms in predicting information cascades. In this context, we introduce a novel prediction model named Cascade Spatio-Temporal Graphical Convolutional Network (CaSTGCN) based on an encoder-decoder structure to capture both structural and temporal features inherent in information cascades and make prediction of their future incremental size. CaSTGCN learns the representation of cascade sequence data combined with graph data through multiple Spatial Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (ST-GCN) modules, then employs Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) to further explore the temporal features and make predictions. Experimental results on real-world dataset and synthetic dataset indicate that our model surpasses existing models.

articleTitle: UAV 3D Path Planning Method Based on Multi-Strategy Improved Dung Beetle Algorithm
abstract: The objective of three-dimensional trajectory planning for UAVs is to efficiently navigate through obstacles while satisfying constraint conditions. To address the widespread application and computational complexity of UAV path planning, a multi-strategy improved dung beetle optimizer (MIDBO) algorithm is proposed to solve the three-dimensional path planning problem for UAVs under various scenarios and obstacle conditions. Firstly, addressing the shortcomings of the Dung Beetle Optimization (DBO) algorithm, such as low convergence accuracy and susceptibility to local optima, MIDBO improves the acceptance of both larvae and thief beetles to local and global optima. This allows for dynamic changes in their search capabilities based on their own abilities, thereby improving population quality while maintaining the good search capability of high-fitness individuals. Secondly, by integrating the follower position update mechanism from the sparrow search algorithm to perturb the algorithm and using a greedy strategy to update positions, the convergence accuracy of the algorithm is enhanced. Lastly, when the algorithm stagnates, the Cauchy-Gaussian mutation strategy is introduced to enhance the algorithm's ability to escape local optima. The results demonstrate that MIDBO can plan high-quality paths in complex multi-obstacle scenarios, with higher convergence accuracy and stability compared to control algorithms, showing significant advantages.

articleTitle: Multi-Stage Optimal Service Matching Framework for the Logistic Service Combination Problem with Spatio-Temporal Constraints
abstract: The fourth-party logistics service platform aims to integrate logistics services from various providers to offer a one-stop logistics solution to customers. However, constructing a logistics service combination scheme that maximizes overall profit while meeting the spatial and temporal constraints of the services is a significant challenge. Traditional heuristic algorithms face issues such as low computational efficiency and insufficient adaptability to dynamic environments and varying order demands when addressing logistics service combination problems with service temporal and spatial constraints. Therefore, we propose the Multi-Stage Optimal Service Matching framework (MOSM). Specifically, the MOSM framework achieves rapid and efficient allocation of logistics order service requirements through three stages: order screening, service provider selection, and service matching, thereby maximizing overall profit. Experiments conducted on nine sets of logistics order datasets demonstrate that the MOSM framework outperforms traditional baseline methods, thereby validating the effectiveness of the MOSM framework in solving logistics service combination problems with temporal and spatial constraints.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Intelligent Security Patrol Robot with Nighttime Dynamic Object Detection Functionality
abstract: Current intelligent security robots on the market capture images of relevant objects in patrol areas during inspections. However, they do not conduct real-time analysis of security events or detect dynamic object behaviors, making them challenging to use in nighttime environments. Based on this, this paper designs an intelligent security patrol robot with nighttime dynamic object detection capabilities. This robot can perform patrol tasks in nighttime environments while detecting and analyzing the dynamic behavior of pedestrians. In terms of hardware design, a four-wheel differential robot was designed; it uses a 3D LiDAR to obtain point cloud data, an IMU module to gather robot posture information, and an infrared camera to capture nighttime infrared images. The robot also has an embedded processor, providing a computing platform. In software design, based on the four-wheel differential chassis, the kinematic model of the robot was first constructed. Then, the robot's autonomous navigation functions were designed, focusing on localization and mapping, as well as integrated path planning algorithms. For nighttime detection, a dynamic object behavior detection algorithm was proposed. The algorithm was trained using a custom-built dataset, enabling the robot to perform visual security tasks in nighttime environments. Experimental results demonstrate that the robot designed in this paper can detect dynamic behavior objects in real-time during nighttime patrol tasks and maintain efficient security operations in low-light and no-light environments.

articleTitle: AMCF-CMV: Adaptive Mahony Complementary Filtering based Attitude Compensation for Cross-water-air Medium Vehicle
abstract: Due to the significant differences in the physical properties of water and air, the impact acceleration experienced by cross-medium vehicle during the transition between water and air could decrease the attitude measurement precision dramatically. To address this issue, this paper proposes an Adaptive Mahony Complementary Filtering (AMCF) to adjust the dynamic proportional and integral (PI) parameters of the complementary filter. Simultaneously, the effects of impact acceleration on the vehicle during cross-medium transitions are mitigated by combining impact acceleration compensation techniques. Furthermore, quaternion-based attitude updates are employed to enhance the real-time and reliability of attitude estimation. Finally, the accuracy of the proposed algorithm is verified through attitude measurement experiments in cross-medium environments. The experimental results demonstrated that the proposed attitude measurement method can eliminate the influence of cross-medium impact acceleration, ensuring the accuracy and stability of vehicle attitude measurement.

articleTitle: Multiple Adaptive Fuzzy Tracking Controller for Complex Models of Continuum Robot Based on Error Upper Bound Estimation
abstract: Continuum robots, owing to their exceptional structural features, find extensive application in rescue operations, medical procedures, and other specialized environments. Because the robot has nonlinear properties and redundant degrees of freedom, the robot dynamics modeling is difficult, and the choice of control method is also very important.
