This will lead to new application scenarios in intelligent drilling techniques along with supporting engineering applications; intelligent geological research; intelligent equipment; intelligent diagnosis; early warning systems; all aimed at driving innovation in the processes involved in oil and gas exploration. In conclusion, the paper discusses potential scenario designs for future digital transformation within both domestic & international contexts regarding smart field exploration & exploitation practices.

articleTitle: A Digital Twin-Based Path Planning Method for Bending Robot Feeding and Unloading
abstract: During bending operations, the narrow space between the upper and lower dies of a bending machine and the ever-changing shapes of the workpieces make them highly susceptible to collisions with the bending tool. Automatic path planning algorithms are crucial when using robot-assisted bending. This paper proposes an improved Synchronized Biased Greedy RRT -Connect algorithm (Improved SBG-RRT -Connect) for planning a bending robot's feeding and unloading paths. The algorithm addresses the issues of the standard RRT -Connect being easily attracted to low-value regions and having unstable convergence speed by introducing a synchronized biased greedy strategy, adaptive ellipsoidal region sampling, and an adaptive node growth strategy. Compared to the unimproved algorithm, the number of iterations and search time are optimized by 51.91 % and 67.6%, respectively, while achieving less costly paths. Additionally, the algorithm can be pre-tested on the digital twin platform designed in this study, allowing for further control of the physical robot through the virtual system. Experimental results demonstrate that the robot completes collision-free feeding and unloading operations, verifying the algorithm's feasibility.

articleTitle: Distributed Stochastic Averaging Gradient Algorithm over Directed Graph
abstract: This paper concentrates distributed stochastic opti-mization over directed network topology. In the network there is a collection of nodes that can access to their own local objective functions, and their target is to cooperate to minimize the sum of objective functions over multi-agent networks with directed network topology. For the large scale machine learning problems, the local objective functions are further assumed to be an average of a finite set of functions. We introduce a directed decentralized double stochastic averaging gradient method(DDSA) which utilizes the renowned push-sum protocol and stochastic averaging gradient to accelerate convergence in directed graph. DDSA can linearly converge in expectation to the optimal solution. We provide a numerical experiment based on logistic regression to illustrate the validity of DDSA.

articleTitle: Data-driven Speed Control for Permanent Magnet DC Motors of Sewing Machines
abstract: This paper studies a data-driven speed control issue for permanent magnet DC motors of sewing machines. Firstly, a model-free adaptive sliding mode control method is developed to manage the motor effectively without relying on a predefined system model. Then, an event-triggering mechanism is integrated into this control strategy to reduce the communication burden. Moreover, compensation algorithms for both input and output are designed to mitigate the impact of data dropouts in both feedback and forward channels. Finally, the convergence of the control error is theoretically validated, and simulation studies confirm the efficiency and robustness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Infrared Maritime Target Tracking Algorithm Based on Temporal Context
abstract: In territorial waters where suspicious incidents frequently occur, continuous tracking of vessels exhibiting suspicious behavior is necessary. However, most existing infrared image target trackers not only fail to fully utilize temporal information but also have insufficient infrared feature extraction capabilities. To address these issues, this paper proposes an infrared maritime target tracking algorithm based on temporal context. Building upon the OSTrack target tracking network, we propose using temporal contextual information for target tracking and add a time information fusion branch to leverage this information. Additionally, the CoTattention module is introduced to enhance the network's feature extraction capabilities. Finally, by introducing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha-CIoU$</tex> to optimize the IoU loss calculation, the accuracy of target bounding box prediction is improved. Our method is compared with other mainstream trackers on the LSOTB-TIR-BOAT dataset. Experimental results show that this algorithm can improve the accuracy of maritime infrared target tracking and effectively address the issue of poor robustness during tracking. This method overcomes the limitations of traditional self-attention mechanisms in feature extraction capability and the finite nature of sinale-frame infrared image information.
